title: Second-opinion engine lane in /code-review and /doc-review
idea: The ENGINE_INTENTS offer lives only in /plan's tier table and team-execution's worker table; it is absent from /code-review and /doc-review, which intake tension 2 explicitly designates as judgment stages defaulting to second-opinion. Today an operator wanting a codex/agy cross-read hand-copies the diff out and hand-reconciles findings back. Wire an optional second-opinion pass into both skills: call engine_resolver.resolve with role_kind='advisory-reviewer' (mode='advisory'), dispatch the merge-base diff or the plan doc to the configured engine as advisory input, and have Claude fold the engine's findings into its own review artifact with per-finding provenance. Claude stays verifier-of-record: engine verdicts are advisory rows, never gate-setters, and satisfy_gate() still requires verified_by_claude=True.
basis: Grounding brief correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow' and only rendered in /plan + team-execution; intake tension 2: 'Judgment stages (/ideate, /brainstorm, /doc-review, /code-review) -> default second-opinion, reconciled by Claude.' Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: engine is advisory-reviewer only, Claude adjudicates every finding, so the never-gatekeepers structure is preserved rather than crossed.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md and plugins/saga/skills/doc-review/SKILL.md plus a new plugins/saga/skills/*/references/external-engine-second-opinion.md; verified by a review artifact showing reconciled engine findings AND a drift-guard test asserting an engine advisory verdict can never flip the review gate (verified_by_claude gate held).

title: Blind external-engine divergent-generator lane in /ideate
idea: role_kind='generator' already exists in ROLE_KINDS (engine_resolver.py:18) but is wired into no lifecycle skill. /ideate's own divergent phase suffers novelty anchoring (intake pre-mortem 4: agents converge toward the Opus pool). Offer an optional blind engine-generator fan-out lane in /ideate: dispatch the theme+frame brief to a configured engine (Ollama at $0, DeepSeek cheap) as a generator that never sees the Claude pool, then merge its raw ideas into convergence exactly as the Fable novelty-hunters do in Phase D. This adds NO new chaperone intent (offload/second-opinion untouched) and no gate power: generator output is candidate ideas, killed or kept by the same basis-contract convergence as any Claude idea.
basis: engine_resolver.py:18 ROLE_KINDS includes 'generator', unused outside the resolver; intake Phase D layer 'Fleet-wide novelty hunters ... Blind Opus fleet; hunt only obvious pass won't find' establishes the blind-generator pattern this generalizes to attended /ideate runs. Does not cross {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (that binding governs team-execution worker residency; /ideate generation is neither a team worker nor a residency).
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/skills/ideate/SKILL.md adding an optional engine-generator lane in the divergent phase plus a references note; verified by a run producing engine-authored candidate ideas that carry an 'engine-generated' provenance tag and pass through convergence unprivileged (test asserts no gate/basis exemption).

title: A codified reconciliation ladder for converged vs divergent engine findings
idea: The second-opinion 'reconciliation' is asserted everywhere ('reconciled by Claude') but specified nowhere: external-engine-workers.md §5 only covers offload verify-apply of a patch, not what happens when a second-opinion engine DISAGREES with Claude's own judgment. The one real datapoint — Claude+Codex converging 15/17, hand-reconciled — was done by a human with no machinery. Define an explicit ladder: converged findings (both surface it) auto-merge into the artifact; engine-only findings become Claude-adjudicated rows ('engine claimed X; Claude accepts/rejects because Y'); Claude-only findings pass through unchanged. Every divergent claim carries a claim_provenance adjudication note so the artifact records WHY the two disagreed, not just the union.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' — direct evidence that reconciliation is manual and unspecified. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the ladder makes Claude's adjudication the load-bearing step for every divergence, tightening (not loosening) verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/engine-reconciliation.md and extending the manifest's claim_provenance handling in engine_dispatch.py; verified by a unit test asserting a divergent engine finding cannot enter the artifact without an accompanying Claude adjudication note.

title: Offload-review-failure recaptured as second-opinion signal instead of silently discarded
idea: When an offload engine returns a patch the chaperone reviews and rejects, external-engine-workers.md §2/§5 has the chaperone quietly do the unit itself — the operator paid for the engine AND paid Claude to redo it, and the divergence evaporates. That is the worst-case net-negative offload with zero salvage. Instead, on offload-review-fail, record the rejected engine output plus the chaperone's rejection reason as advisory evidence on the manifest (a new disposition, e.g. offload-rejected-recovered), and emit a LEARNINGS-eligible note capturing which capability class the engine got wrong. Over runs this builds a grounded fitness signal for the engine registry — the engine that keeps failing a capability gets down-ranked from real evidence, not vibes.
basis: First principles: offload's entire justification (execution_spec.py:67 comment) is that it is 'net-negative otherwise' — so a silently-discarded rejected offload is precisely the net-negative case the intent was built to avoid, and the sunk verification cost already produced a signal (why the engine was wrong) that costs nothing more to persist. Aligned with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the recaptured output stays advisory, never re-entering a gate.
outcome_shape: PR adding an offload-rejected disposition to engine_dispatch.py's Disposition set + build_dispatch_manifest mapping, and a LEARNINGS capture hook; verified by a test that a chaperone-rejected offload patch produces a manifest with the new disposition and a non-empty rejection note.

title: Evidence-size-adaptive chaperone tier escalation (surfaced, not silent)
idea: The chaperone tier is frozen at plan-time (sonnet/medium for offload) from a work-shape guess made before the engine has returned anything. But verification cost scales with the SIZE of the returned patch, not the plan-time guess: a 2000-line engine diff verified at sonnet/medium is under-chaperoned (the exact silent-no-op / rubber-stamp risk), and a 10-line diff at that tier is over-spent. Add a post-dispatch, pre-verify sizing gate: when returned evidence crosses a line/token threshold, the chaperone SURFACES a recommended tier escalation with the cost delta and proceeds only on the spend-lever's operator yes (unattended runs stay cache-tight per intake tension 1). This treats the offload tier as the low rung of an escalation ladder, not a fixed point.
basis: First principles: verification effort is a function of diff size, which is unknown at plan-authoring time, so a plan-time-fixed chaperone tier is systematically mis-sized in both directions. Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} (tier tuples are ordered escalation ladders, not closed sets) — the escalation rides that binding's revisit intent rather than crossing it — and honors intake tension 4 (escalation surfaced with cost delta, never a silent default).
outcome_shape: PR adding an evidence-size threshold + surfaced escalation step to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md §5 and a helper in engine_dispatch.py; verified by a test that an oversized evidence payload yields an escalation recommendation and that unattended mode records but does not auto-escalate.

title: Batched single-context chaperoning of same-engine offload units
idea: When several offload units in a segment all route to the same engine, external-engine-workers.md §1 hands the chaperone one context package per unit — the plan pointer and shared context get re-read for each, and read-only recon fan-outs already burned 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes. Let one chaperone verify a batch of same-engine offload outputs in a single context load: read the plan pointer and shared spec once, then verify-apply-test each unit's returned patch sequentially against that warm context. The per-unit apply/commit/manifest stays untouched (each unit still gets its own manifest and verified_by_claude bit); only the redundant context ingestion is amortized. This rides the settled residency (worker-cache-scheduling) — it adds no wave queue, just reuses one resident chaperone's already-loaded context.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)' — direct measured evidence that repeated context ingestion in verification fan-outs is the dominant cost. Does not cross {#worker-cache-scheduling}: batching reuses the existing resident chaperone's context and introduces no formal wave queue, so the binding's revisit-when (idle-poll justifying a wave queue) is not triggered.
outcome_shape: PR extending external-engine-workers.md §1/§5 with a batched-chaperone context-package variant and per-unit manifest preservation notes; verified by a test that N same-engine offload units under one chaperone still emit N distinct manifests each with its own verified_by_claude=True, from a single context load.

title: Per-repo engine-choice memory: recommended defaults, still confirmed
idea: Every run the operator re-answers the same questions — offload or second-opinion? which engine? — because nothing remembers the last answer; intake tension 2 says the choice is 'always operator-choosable, never assumed,' but choosable and pre-filled are not opposites. Add a per-repo engine-preference file (e.g. .saga/engine-prefs.json) recording the operator's last per-stage intent + engine selection. On the next run the tier-table row and stage-entry prompt arrive PRE-FILLED with that remembered choice as the recommendation, still requiring an explicit confirm — never auto-applied. This kills the repeated-identical-answer fatigue without ever assuming, honoring operator-choice-framework's doc-only/operator-confirmed posture.
basis: Grounding brief §2 alignment note quoting operator posture 'evaluated and incorporated based on the analysis of the main LLM' + intake tension 2 'always operator-choosable, never assumed.' Engages {#operator-choice-framework} revisit intent: preference memory is a doc-only recommended default surfaced for CLI-driven confirmation, not an autonomous fan-out decision, so the framework's operator-confirmed invariant holds.
outcome_shape: PR adding an engine-prefs schema + read/write helper (new plugins/saga/scripts/engine_prefs.py) wired into /plan's tier table and team-execution stage entry; verified by a test that a remembered choice pre-fills the recommendation row but a run cannot proceed without an explicit confirm token.

title: Cost-delta preview on every engine-lane offer
idea: The engine offer is presented as one undifferentiated row in the /plan tier table with a prose rationale but no number — the operator cannot see what offload actually SAVES or what second-opinion actually COSTS, so the spend lever intake tension 4 demands ('expensive never a silent default; recommendation plus cheaper fallback') is nominally present but blind. Attach a cost-delta line to every engine-lane offer: for offload, the estimated token/dollar saving vs Claude doing the unit; for second-opinion, the estimated added spend of the adversarial pass; both derived from the unit's size estimate and the resolved engine/variant's tier. The operator then chooses against numbers, not vibes, and the cheaper fallback is shown beside the recommendation exactly as tension 4 requires.
basis: Intake tension 4: 'Fable-tier line in any plan or issue carries recommendation plus cheaper fallback; expensive never a silent default' — the offer surface today (plan/SKILL.md tier table rows) carries rationale prose but no cost figure, leaving the spend lever unquantified. Aligned with {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}: the delta is computed from the already-locked offload->sonnet/medium and second-opinion->opus/high tier mapping, adding transparency without altering the mapping.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cost-delta estimator helper and rendering a saving/added-spend line into plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md's engine tier rows (and the team-execution stage-entry offer); verified by a test that each engine-lane offer renders a non-empty cost-delta with a named cheaper fallback.

title: Auto-injected per-stage engine offer — kill the /plan-only authoring bottleneck
idea: Today ENGINE_INTENTS units are authored only in /plan and merely rendered in team-execution; /ideate, /brainstorm, /work, /doc-review, /code-review never surface an engine offer at all, so an operator who wants a second opinion at code-review has to reach back into a plan. Remove that authoring detour: add one shared engine_offer.py helper that any stage skill calls to compute the resolver's already-available offer for the current work shape (judgment→second-opinion/opus-high, mechanical→offload/sonnet-medium) and render it inline as a one-line 'want an external engine here? [y/N/none]'. Each of the five stage SKILL.md files gains a single documented call site; no new resolver logic, it reuses engine_resolver.resolve. The step the operator does manually today (author an engine unit upstream) becomes a surface that offers itself where the work actually happens.
basis: Grounding brief corrections §9: ENGINE_INTENTS 'authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table ... /ideate, /brainstorm, /work NUANCE' — the offer is absent at those surfaces. engine_resolver.resolve (engine_resolver.py:79) already returns a complete Resolution given a capability/engine request, so the offer is computable at any surface with zero new resolver code.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/engine_offer.py (pure, tested) plus a single documented call site in each of ideate/brainstorm/work/doc-review/code-review SKILL.md; verified by a unit test asserting the helper returns second-opinion/opus-high for a judgment stage and offload/sonnet-medium for a mechanical stage, and by a marketplace metadata bump + CHANGELOG entry.

title: Remembered per-stage engine choice — invert 'ask once per run' into 'ask once, ever'
idea: Intake tension 2 settles the offer as 'always operator-choosable, asked once per run at start'. The inversion: the best re-ask is no re-ask. Persist the operator's per-stage decision (offload / second-opinion / none) to a durable per-repo .saga/engine-prefs.json keyed by lifecycle stage, seeded with the tension-2 recommendation. On the next run an unattended context reads it silently (matching the intake's cache-first unattended posture); an attended context shows 'using your remembered choice for code-review: second-opinion via codex — keep? [Y/change]'. Because everything the pref controls is reversible (it only picks who generates advisory evidence, never a gate), silent reuse is safe under the intake's reversible-proceeds rule. The manual step removed is re-answering the same question every session.
basis: Intake brief tension 2: 'always operator-choosable, never assumed ... Per-stage override offered at the prompt in both directions; "none" always available' and tension 3: 'Everything reversible ... proceeds without asking.' The engine offer is reversible (advisory-only per {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}), so a remembered default satisfies the reversible-proceeds rule rather than contradicting the once-per-run rule — it removes the re-ask, not the choice.
outcome_shape: PR adding a .saga/engine-prefs.json read/write path in engine_offer.py (or a small engine_prefs.py), the attended-vs-unattended branch, and a schema; verified by tests covering silent-reuse-when-unattended, prompt-when-attended, and 'none' round-trip; DECISIONS.md entry recording the remember-across-runs choice with revisit-when.

title: Chaperone break-even guard — auto-collapse an uneconomic offload back to inline
idea: The ENGINE_INTENTS comment states an offload 'wants a cheap chaperone (the delegation is net-negative otherwise)' — but nothing measures whether the chaperone's own resolve→dispatch→verify→apply→test cost actually beats doing the unit inline. Automate that check away as a decision: a chaperone_breakeven(unit) guard estimates chaperone overhead (payload assembly + verification of returned evidence + apply/test) against the inline cost of the unit, and when the offload is net-negative it turns the unit into the resolver's existing Claude-fallback Resolution (engine_id='claude', halt=None) rather than dispatching. The painful step removed is a human noticing 'this offload cost more than just doing it'; the machinery refuses the net-negative delegation automatically, emitting the standard downgrade note so /retro can see it.
basis: execution_spec.py:66-68: '``offload`` wants a cheap chaperone (the delegation is net-negative otherwise)'. engine_resolver.py:272-288 (_fallback_resolution) already produces a Claude-fallback Resolution with fallback set and halt=None — the collapse target exists; only the break-even predicate and the wiring are new.
outcome_shape: PR adding chaperone_breakeven() to engine_resolver.py (or engine_dispatch.py) plus a downgrade_note on collapse; verified by a test where a small unit with a large protocol/context estimate collapses to the claude-fallback Resolution and emits a downgrade note, and a large-benefit unit still dispatches; CHANGELOG + LEARNINGS entry.

title: Typed second-opinion reconciliation — remove freeform prose reconciliation
idea: Intake tension 2 makes judgment stages default second-opinion 'reconciled by Claude', but reconciliation today is unstructured prose, which is exactly where a real external finding gets silently dropped. Automate the reconciliation shape: a reconcile.py takes the AdvisoryEvidence from a second-opinion dispatch and Claude's own findings and emits a typed triage — agreements, conflicts, engine-only net-new findings — each requiring an explicit per-item Claude adjudication before verified_by_claude flips. This turns the blanket verified_by_claude stamp into a per-claim stamp, strengthening {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} rather than crossing it: the engine still never holds a verdict, but now no engine finding can be lost by a hand-wave. The manual step removed is the operator/Claude eyeballing two prose blobs and hoping nothing fell through.
basis: external-engine-workers.md:20: 'when a typed manifest carries claim_provenance, every gate-relevant claim must already be Claude-adjudicated (R11 extension)'. The typed-per-claim adjudication slot is already reserved; engine_dispatch.satisfy_gate (external-engine-workers.md:18-19) requires verified_by_claude, so per-claim stamping is a strict tightening of the existing gate, engaging never-gatekeepers by reinforcing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding reconcile.py producing a typed {agreements, conflicts, net_new} object with a per-item adjudicated flag, wired into the second-opinion path so verified_by_claude flips only when all items are adjudicated; verified by tests covering a dropped-net-new-finding-blocks-verification case; CHANGELOG entry.

title: Activate the deferred team-execution engine-worker slot — remove the 'dispatch is deferred' gap
idea: engine-dispatch.md explicitly defers team-execution dispatch because it 'needs an external-engine worker context-package slot that does not exist yet' — but external-engine-workers.md has since fully specified that context package (unit_ids, plan_pointer, selector, intent, plan_time_resolution_preview, write_set) and the chaperone protocol. The deferral is now a paper gap: the contract exists, the wiring doesn't. Remove the gap by implementing the context-package slot in team-execution Step B1 wave scheduling so a worker-<engine> chaperone actually resolves→dispatches→verifies→applies. This directly engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}'s revisit-when ('team-execution gains external-engine worker slot') — that condition has now fired, and the diff still routes every engine diff through the same reviewer-consensus/validator gates, so Claude stays verifier-of-record.
basis: engine-dispatch.md:62-66: 'team-execution dispatch (R10/R12) is deferred — it needs an external-engine worker context-package slot that does not exist yet'. external-engine-workers.md §1 now specifies that exact context package and §5 keeps the diff on the reviewer/validator critical path. Grounding brief binding {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} revisit-when names 'team-execution gains external-engine worker slot' — the trigger this idea satisfies.
outcome_shape: PR adding the external-engine worker context-package to team-execution SKILL.md Step B1 plus the chaperone spawn wiring and worker-manifest disposition handling; verified by an end-to-end test that a capability-routed unit spawns a chaperone, produces AdvisoryEvidence, and its diff clears the existing reviewer-consensus gate; version bump + CHANGELOG on team-execution.

title: Automated engine-registry staleness gate — remove the manual 'is this profile current?' check
idea: Registry.stale() compares an engine entry's last_validated against a known model-revision date, but nothing calls it, so an operator can dispatch a second opinion to a capability profile that predates the model's latest revision without any signal. Automate the check that a careful operator would otherwise do by hand: a small preflight that loads a known-model-revisions file, runs Registry.stale over every entry, and (a) warns at dispatch time when the resolved entry is stale and (b) fails a marketplace CI job when any registry entry is stale beyond a threshold. The manual step removed is a human remembering to re-validate capability ratings after a provider ships a new model.
basis: engine_registry.py:377-385 defines Registry.stale(entry, known_revision_dates) but no caller exists in the resolver or dispatch path (engine_resolver.py never references it). Grounding brief §5 lists {#marketplace-ci-guard} as a pre-grounded seed — this is its engine-registry-specific extension, not the general guard.
outcome_shape: PR adding a known-model-revisions data file, a stale-check preflight callable from dispatch (warn) and a CI job (fail), wired to Registry.stale; verified by a test with a stale entry producing a warn at dispatch and a nonzero CI exit, and a current entry passing; CHANGELOG entry.

title: Content-addressed payload cache — remove redundant re-assembly and re-reads on re-dispatch
idea: engine_resolver assembles the dispatch payload exactly once (protocol + context, byte-preserved) — but a retry, a panel re-run, or a round-N second opinion re-derives the identical payload and makes the chaperone re-read the plan/context to rebuild it. Remove the redundant work: have _assemble_payload write the assembled payload to a content-addressed cache keyed by (unit_id, protocol-hash, context-hash); any re-dispatch of an unchanged unit reuses the cached payload with zero re-assembly and zero chaperone re-read, and a changed context misses the cache so staleness is structurally impossible. This lives entirely within the settled {#worker-cache-scheduling} architecture (derive saga-side, reside team-side) — it caches a saga-side derived artifact, so it neither crosses nor needs that decision's residency revisit-when.
basis: First-principles: engine_resolver.py _assemble_payload (:313-317) is a pure function of (protocol, context); the assert_protocol_preserved contract (:320-334) guarantees byte-identity, so its output is safely content-addressable. A retry/panel/round-N re-run recomputes the same bytes and forces the chaperone to re-load plan+context to do so; caching keyed on the two hashes removes that recompute+reread with no correctness change, since a content hash miss forces fresh assembly. This aligns with {#worker-cache-scheduling} ('derive saga-side') without touching its residency boundary.
outcome_shape: PR adding a content-addressed payload cache behind _assemble_payload (keyed on unit_id + protocol-hash + context-hash) with hit/miss provenance; verified by tests asserting identical inputs hit the cache and a changed context misses it, and that byte-preservation still holds on a cache hit; CHANGELOG entry.

title: Opt-out offload for mechanical units — invert the default so the machinery, not the operator, tags offload
idea: The offload machinery exists but sits idle in practice (219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate; offload is opt-in per unit, so nobody opts in). Invert the default: at /plan authoring, units whose shape matches a mechanical fingerprint (scaffold, fixed transform, mechanical edit — the tiering vocabulary the org already uses) are auto-tagged engine_intent=offload with a sonnet/medium chaperone, and the operator removes the tag rather than adding it. Judgment-shaped units stay untagged (or default second-opinion per tension 2). The manual step removed is an operator remembering that offload is even available and hand-tagging each mechanical unit; the inversion turns 'offload if you ask' into 'offload unless you object', which is what actually gets the idle machinery used. Chaperone tier stays sonnet/medium, so {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} is honored, not crossed.
basis: Intake brief tension 2: 'Mechanical stages (/work implementation units, /plan grounding research) → default offload with a Claude chaperone.' Grounding brief §7 session-mining: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate' — offload machinery unused in practice. Binding {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} fixes offload→sonnet/medium, which this idea preserves verbatim.
outcome_shape: PR adding a mechanical-fingerprint classifier at /plan unit authoring (plan/SKILL.md + a small classifier in execution_spec.py) that defaults engine_intent=offload on matching units with an operator opt-out; verified by tests asserting a scaffold-shaped unit defaults to offload/sonnet-medium and a judgment-shaped unit does not; DECISIONS.md entry with revisit-when.

title: Second-opinion is a runtime judgment-skill offer, not a plan-authoring artifact
idea: The whole fleet treats 'which engine' as a decision authored once inside /plan's tier table and frozen into an ExecutionSpec; the grounding brief confirms ENGINE_INTENTS is 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow' (grounding line 27). That framing is a choice, not a law: the judgment stages are exactly where a fresh external read is most valuable and where Claude is already present to reconcile. Reframe one level up: expose a lightweight in-skill 'want a second opinion?' offer in /ideate, /brainstorm, /doc-review, and /code-review that calls engine_resolver.resolve({role_kind:'advisory', capability:'second-opinion'}, mode='advisory') and folds the engine's advisory output into the skill's own reconciliation, with Claude remaining verifier-of-record (the engine never gates the surfaced verdict). This makes the engine registry reachable from where operators actually deliberate, instead of only from a spec they author hours earlier.
basis: Grounding brief line 26-27: ENGINE_INTENTS 'authored in /plan ... rendered in team-execution Step A7 ... Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow.' engine_resolver.py exposes MODES=('advisory','dispatch') (external-engine-workers.md §2). Binding {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the added path is advisory-only, Claude reconciles and signs the skill's verdict — no revisit needed since the engine never satisfies a gate.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a shared 'external second-opinion' offer block to plugins/saga/skills/{ideate,brainstorm,doc-review,code-review}/SKILL.md, each calling engine_resolver in advisory mode and specifying the reconciliation fold; verified by a doc-review/code-review transcript showing an engine advisory surfaced and Claude's kept/rejected reconciliation recorded, plus a drift-guard test asserting all four skills reference the same advisory-resolve contract.

title: A third intent where convergence is the failure signal (red-team / divergence-seeking)
idea: ENGINE_INTENTS = ('offload','second-opinion') at execution_spec.py:68 is a closed binary that silently assumes every external call wants the engine's answer to either replace or corroborate Claude's. That hides a third intent: sometimes you dispatch precisely to manufacture disagreement — a red-team pass where the engine agreeing with Claude is a null result and its dissent is the entire product. Reframe intent-semantics as a spectrum of reconciliation postures rather than offload-vs-agree: add a 'divergence' intent whose reconciliation contract is inverted (surface only the delta, weight dissent, and flag suspicious full-convergence for a human look). Because engine_intent already resolves upgrade-only via ENGINE_INTENTS.index max (execution_spec.py:1478-1484), the new value must be placed deliberately in that ordered ladder and mapped to a chaperone tier consistent with {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}.
basis: execution_spec.py:68 ENGINE_INTENTS closed tuple; resolution ordering at :1478-1484 ('second-opinion beats offload'). Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} (tuples are ordered escalation ladders): 'divergence' slots above 'second-opinion' and inherits opus/high. Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by extending, not contradicting, its two mappings — divergence maps to opus/high like second-opinion, adding a third row rather than altering offload→sonnet/medium. Stays advisory ({#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}).
outcome_shape: A merged PR extending ENGINE_INTENTS to a 3-tuple in execution_spec.py with the ordering + chaperone-tier row documented in plan/SKILL.md's tier table and external-engine-workers.md's reconciliation section; verified by execution_spec.py validate accepting a divergence-intent unit, the ordering-resolution unit test covering the new max, and a reconciliation example showing dissent-weighted output.

title: Reconciliation is an implicit act — make the adjudication a durable ledger artifact
idea: The never-gatekeepers binding requires Claude to adjudicate every engine claim (verified_by_claude, claim_provenance in external-engine-workers.md), but the reconciliation of CONTENT — what the engine said, what Claude kept, what Claude rejected and why — is nowhere recorded; only substitution/fallback dispositions are tracked. That treats adjudication as a transient mental act rather than an auditable output, which is exactly the 'stale-claim asserted as fact' pattern the journal keeps catching. Reframe: every second-opinion/divergence dispatch emits a reconciliation-ledger fragment (engine_claim, claim_status ∈ accepted/rejected/partial, adjudication_reason, verified_by_claude) attached to the saga tick or review artifact. This turns the binding's abstract 'Claude is verifier-of-record' into concrete, greppable provenance and gives /retro real substrate on which engines actually earn their keep.
basis: external-engine-workers.md 'Never a gatekeeper' section: satisfy_gate() hard-requires evidence.verified_by_claude and per-claim claim_provenance, but only dispositions (fell-back-to-claude/substituted-engine) are recorded, not content reconciliation. Grounding §6.2 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified' (4 learnings). Reinforces {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} by making adjudication visible — no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: A merged PR defining a reconciliation-ledger fragment schema in external-engine-workers.md and wiring its emission in engine_dispatch.py's evidence path (attached to the manifest without bumping saga.manifest.v1); verified by a dispatch run producing a ledger with accepted/rejected claims and a test asserting a gate cannot pass with an unadjudicated engine_claim in the ledger.

title: Chaperone tier should key off verifiability, not just intent — a test is a cheaper verifier than a reasoner
idea: The tier table hard-maps offload→sonnet/medium with the rationale that 'a heavier chaperone erases the token savings' (plan/SKILL.md, KTD2). But that same rationale, followed one step further, exposes a hidden assumption: it treats a reasoning chaperone as the ONLY way to verify an offloaded output. When the offloaded unit is test-gated or deterministically checkable, the passing test IS the verification Claude ratifies, and a sonnet/medium reasoning pass is pure overhead. Reframe chaperone-economics: derive the chaperone tier from output verifiability (test-gated → haiku/low ratify-only; opaque prose → sonnet/medium reasoning verify), making sonnet/medium a default the KTD2 logic itself argues down, not a floor. This is a principled override lever consistent with the table's existing fable/xhigh per-unit override precedent.
basis: plan/SKILL.md tier table offload row: 'Chaperone is mechanical verify-apply-test; a heavier chaperone erases the token savings (KTD2)' with an existing per-unit override precedent (fable/xhigh for second-opinion). Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by treating offload→sonnet/medium as the default its own KTD2 rationale supports lowering when a test is the ratified verifier — extends the map's logic rather than contradicting its floor; Claude still ratifies the test result ({#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}).
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a verifiability qualifier to the offload tier-recommendation logic (plan/SKILL.md tier table + a Unit.verifiability signal in execution_spec.py) that recommends haiku/low ratify-only for test-gated offloads; verified by execution_spec.py validate accepting the qualifier and a plan-time tier-table render showing a test-gated offload dropped to ratify-only with the CI-gate cited as verifier.

title: One chaperone can verify a batch — amortize the tax across homogeneous engine outputs
idea: execution_spec.py:1403 fixes 'one resident chaperone per contiguous run of the same engine,' which reads as a residency-scoping rule but silently sets the verification GRANULARITY at one-chaperone-pass-per-unit. For a run of many small same-shape offloads (e.g. a dozen mechanical refactors), that pays the verify-apply-test reasoning cost once per unit even though the outputs are homogeneous and could be adjudicated in a single batched pass. Reframe: let the chaperone verify a batch of same-engine, same-capability outputs in one reconciliation, amortizing the chaperone tax across N units instead of paying it N times — the exact inverse of the 'heavier chaperone erases savings' worry, applied at the batch axis. This is the economic move that makes cheap $0 offload targets (Ollama, per intake §5) actually net-positive at volume.
basis: execution_spec.py:1403 'One resident chaperone per contiguous run [of the] same engine'; intake §5 'Ollama → $0 offload target.' Reinforces {#worker-cache-scheduling} (chaperone resides team-side, segment = plugin directory) by batching within an existing segment rather than adding residency; Claude still adjudicates each claim in the batch ({#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}), so no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a batch-verify chaperone protocol to external-engine-workers.md (one reconciliation over a same-engine/same-capability unit group, per-claim ledger entries preserved) and the batching boundary in execution_spec.py's chaperone-segment logic; verified by a dispatch test where a 4-unit offload group is chaperoned in one pass with 4 distinct ledger verdicts and a token-count comparison against per-unit chaperoning.

title: Remembered engine posture per repo/outcome — stop asking the same question every run
idea: The intake insists external-LLM use is 'always operator-choosable, never assumed' (intake §37-44), which the fleet currently satisfies by asking fresh at every plan/run — treating statelessness as if it were the same thing as operator control. It isn't: an operator who says 'in this repo, offload mechanical units to the cheap engine and always get a codex second-opinion on architecture' is expressing a standing posture, and re-prompting them each run is friction dressed as respect. Reframe operator-ergonomics: persist a per-repo/per-outcome engine posture (a CLI-managed .saga/engine-posture.json) that pre-fills the plan-time and judgment-skill offers as recommended defaults the operator can still override, so the choice is remembered but never silently forced. Control is preserved (every default is visible and overridable); only the redundant re-asking is removed.
basis: Intake §37-44 'always operator-choosable, never assumed' + §33 'Asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation' — establishes recommendation-with-override as the sanctioned shape. Engages {#operator-choice-framework} (operator-choice = doc-only, CLI-driven): the posture is a CLI-managed config file surfacing recommended defaults, not a hidden auto-select — stays within doc/CLI-driven choice.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a .saga/engine-posture.json schema + a mission-control/saga CLI to set/show it, consumed as the pre-filled default in plan/SKILL.md's engine offer and the judgment-skill offers from T1-F3-1; verified by a run showing the remembered posture surfaced as the recommended default and an explicit override recorded, plus a test that an absent posture file falls back to today's ask-fresh behavior.

title: The registry calibrates itself from real reconciliation outcomes — retro-gated, not an autonomous loop
idea: engine-registry.yaml declares its ratings 'SEED DATA (2026-06-27), not permanent ranking' and says staleness is 're-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by automated measurement loop' — which quietly accepts that the richest evidence (every real dispatch where Claude kept or rejected the engine's output) is thrown away, forcing hand re-authoring. Reframe: treat the reconciliation ledger (T1-F3-3) as passive benchmark telemetry — each accepted/rejected adjudication is a data point on that engine×capability cell — and have /retro INGEST the aggregated signal to propose rating and last_validated updates. This keeps the deliberate human gate (proposals surface in /retro, never auto-commit to the registry) while ending the pretense that hand-authored seed data stays honest on its own. It directly attacks the 'stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact' pattern by making the registry earn its ratings from use.
basis: engine-registry.yaml header: 'SEED DATA ... re-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by automated measurement loop' and per-row last_validated. Grounding §7.7 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact.' Engages that /retro-gate convention explicitly: ingestion is retro-gated and proposal-only (no autonomous measurement loop), preserving the deliberate human revalidation the comment protects; evidence originates from Claude adjudication ({#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}).
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a /retro sub-step that aggregates reconciliation-ledger outcomes into per-cell rating-drift proposals against engine-registry.yaml (proposal artifact only, human-applied), plus a script that maps ledger stats to capability_profile deltas; verified by a /retro run over seeded ledger fragments emitting a rating-change proposal with last_validated bumps and a test that it never writes engine-registry.yaml directly.

title: Adversarial second-opinion on the FINDING at the /work round-N review-failure boundary
idea: When /work's code-review gate returns a P0/P1 finding, the loop's only move is to re-spin Claude to fix it — the finding itself is treated as ground truth, and a false-positive finding silently costs a whole churn cycle. That assumes Claude's review verdict needs no second look, even though the journal shows external/cross-family review catches what a single family misses (team-execution consensus 'catching defects green suites missed', grounding line 61). Reframe the surface-point: at the review-failure boundary, offer a codex/agy adversarial-review second opinion aimed not at the code but at the FINDING — is this defect real, is the severity right — as advisory input Claude reconciles before deciding to churn. Claude remains verifier-of-record on the gate (never-gatekeepers holds: the engine cannot dismiss a P0, only inform Claude's re-adjudication), turning a blind re-spin into an evidence-weighed decision.
basis: Grounding §3.2 (line 61): 'team-execution consensus review catching defects green suites missed (2 independent repos, operator-praised).' saga:work review gate hard-blocks on P0/P1 (work SKILL description). Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the second opinion is advisory on the finding's validity; Claude re-adjudicates and the engine can never clear or suppress the gate — both revisit conditions (read-only-verify profile, external-engine worker slot) already shipped, but this idea deliberately stays advisory rather than invoking them.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a review-failure second-opinion offer to plugins/saga/skills/work/SKILL.md's round-N gate (advisory adversarial-review dispatch on the finding, reconciled into keep/downgrade/dismiss-with-reason, logged to the reconciliation ledger); verified by a /work transcript where a flagged finding gets an engine second opinion and Claude records its re-adjudication before the churn/no-churn decision.

title: One shared engine-offer partial every lifecycle surface includes
idea: Today the external-engine offer is hand-authored into the `/plan` tier table and rendered again in team-execution Step A7, but is absent everywhere else, so wiring it into /ideate, /brainstorm, /work, /doc-review, /code-review would mean five bespoke re-implementations that drift. Instead build ONE reusable primitive: `plugins/saga/references/engine-offer-block.md` plus a thin helper that calls `engine_resolver.resolve(..., mode='advisory')` and renders a consistent 'this stage can route offload→<engine> / second-opinion→<engine>' block. Each of the five surfaces gets a one-line include pointing at the partial rather than its own copy. Adding a sixth surface later becomes a single include, and a wording or tier-map change lands in one file for the whole fleet. Advisory-only framing is baked into the block so no surface can read it as a gate.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow' — authored in plan/SKILL.md:303-304, rendered only in team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233. Five surfaces each needing the same offer is the classic contract-mirror-drift disease (§3 finding 1).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/engine-offer-block.md + a render helper, with include references added to the five SKILL.md surface files, plus a drift-guard test asserting each surface references the single partial (not an inline copy). Verified by the test failing if any surface re-inlines the block.

title: Registry-driven surface×intent default matrix as a single retune lever
idea: The intake resolved that judgment stages (/ideate, /brainstorm, /doc-review, /code-review) should default to second-opinion while mechanical stages default to offload, but that policy exists only as prose in the intake brief with nothing machine-readable behind it. Encode it as a small `surface_intent_defaults` table (surface-key → default intent) shipped beside the engine registry and consumed by the shared offer block from T1-F4-1. Each surface then computes its default offer from one data row instead of hardcoding it. Retuning the whole fleet's posture — e.g. flipping /code-review from second-opinion to offload — becomes a one-cell edit rather than editing five skills. This is the compounding payoff: the policy lives as data, not scattered defaults.
basis: Intake brief §2 resolved tension: 'Judgment stages (/ideate, /brainstorm, /doc-review, /code-review) → default second-opinion, reconciled by Claude. Mechanical (/work /plan) → offload.' No machine-readable encoding of this exists (grounding §1: no dispatch-time lever outside saga plan vocab).
outcome_shape: PR adding a surface_intent_defaults data file (YAML/JSON beside engine-registry.yaml) + offer-block consumption + unit test asserting each named surface resolves its documented default. Verified by test coverage over every surface key.

title: Intent→reconciliation-recipe registry so the merge protocol is data, not prose
idea: ENGINE_INTENTS is a bare 2-tuple that fixes a chaperone tier but says nothing structured about HOW Claude reconciles the engine's output — offload implies verify-apply-test, second-opinion implies adversarial refute-and-reconcile, but that mapping is re-described ad hoc wherever an engine is dispatched. Add a `reconciliation_recipes` table keyed by intent that names the merge protocol each intent triggers, mirroring the ordered-escalation-ladder treatment tiers already get. The shared offer block and the chaperone both read the recipe from one place. Compounding: a future intent value (a 'cross-check' or 'tie-break' semantics) becomes one registry row every surface inherits, instead of a fleet-wide prose edit. Crossing {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}: any new intent stays a chaperone-tiered advisory recipe, never a second executor kind or git participant — its revisit-when (team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot) is not triggered because recipes only change reconciliation, not residency.
basis: execution_spec.py:68 `ENGINE_INTENTS = ("offload", "second-opinion")` carries only a tier implication; {#tier-vocab-ordering} establishes tier tuples as ordered escalation ladders — intents deserve the same structured treatment. {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) constrains new intents to chaperone dispatch.
outcome_shape: PR adding a reconciliation-recipe registry (reference doc + intent→recipe map) referenced by engine-offer-block.md and external-engine-workers.md §4, plus a test that every ENGINE_INTENTS value has exactly one recipe. Verified by parity test between ENGINE_INTENTS and recipe keys.

title: Reconciliation ledger that closes the registry's /retro re-validation loop
idea: The engine registry header states ratings are 're-validated by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop' — but no substrate carries what actually happened when Claude reconciled an engine's output, so /retro has nothing concrete to re-validate against and the loop has never fired (mirrors §3 finding 5: promote ledger never fired). Add a reconciliation-ledger primitive: every second-opinion reconcile and every offload verify-apply-test appends a typed record (engine_id, variant, capability, intent, agreed/disagreed/refuted, Claude's verdict, file scope) to a per-repo derived-on-read ledger. /retro reads it to propose registry rating and last_validated updates as gated suggestions. Compounding: each dispatch sharpens the next dispatch's routing, turning hand-seeded ratings into evidence-backed ones without building the forbidden automated measurement loop — the human /retro gate stays in charge.
basis: engine-registry.yaml header: 're-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by an automated measurement loop.' Grounding §3 finding 5: cross-repo learning loop 'exists but has never fired' for lack of substrate. This supplies the missing substrate while respecting the no-automated-loop decision.
outcome_shape: PR adding a reconciliation-ledger writer invoked at reconcile time (engine_dispatch or chaperone apply step) + a /retro read hook that emits gated registry-update proposals. Verified by an integration test writing a ledger record and asserting /retro surfaces a proposal from it.

title: Break-even estimator so offload is a checked economic decision, not a reflex
idea: KTD2 justifies the sonnet/medium offload chaperone by saying a heavier chaperone 'erases the token savings that motivated the delegation' — but nothing actually checks whether a given offload nets savings, so a tiny unit gets delegated at a loss (chaperone verify-apply-test cost exceeds just doing it in Claude). Build a break-even estimator primitive: given a unit's declared `files`/size and the resolved engine's cost_speed_rank, it recommends offload-vs-do-it-in-Claude and records predicted-vs-actual to the T1-F4-4 ledger. Surface the recommendation in the shared offer block. Compounding: the estimate self-corrects each run from ledger deltas, and it turns the offload tier from a fixed heuristic into a lever that pays back its own build cost across every future delegation decision.
basis: First principles: offload is net-negative when chaperone_cost > (claude_do_it_cost − engine_cost). The KTD2 tier rationale (plan/SKILL.md offload row: 'a heavier chaperone erases the token savings') asserts this economics verbally but installs no gate, so the break-even is never actually evaluated per unit — small units are structurally over-delegated.
outcome_shape: PR adding a break-even helper (in engine_resolver or a new estimator module) returning a recommend/skip signal from unit size + cost_speed_rank, surfaced in engine-offer-block.md and recorded to the reconciliation ledger. Verified by unit tests over boundary cases (tiny unit → skip, large unit → offload).

title: Self-sharpening cost_speed_rank from captured dispatch telemetry
idea: cost_speed_rank is the KTD9 tie-break key that decides which engine wins when two rate a capability equally, but it is hand-seeded SEED DATA that only staleness (last_validated) makes visible — nothing measures real cost/latency to refine it. Wire a lightweight per-dispatch capture into engine_dispatch (wall-time + token/turn count of the engine call and its chaperone) that appends to the same reconciliation ledger, and have /retro propose gated cost_speed_rank re-orderings plus last_validated bumps from the aggregate. Compounding: the tie-break key that silently steers every capability-routed resolution becomes evidence-backed and stops rotting, and because the refinement routes through /retro's gate it stays inside the 'no automated measurement loop' decision rather than violating it.
basis: engine-registry.yaml: 'cost_speed_rank is the KTD9 tie-break key: lower = cheaper+faster. It only breaks ties between variants that rate a requested capability EQUALLY' and 'SEED DATA (2026-06-27), not a permanent ranking... last_validated (R3) makes staleness visible.' No capture feeds it today.
outcome_shape: PR adding dispatch telemetry capture in engine_dispatch.py (cost/latency → ledger) + a /retro-gated proposal that re-orders cost_speed_rank and bumps last_validated. Verified by a test seeding two ledger cost samples and asserting the proposed rank ordering flips accordingly.

title: Once-per-outcome remembered engine posture instead of re-asking every stage
idea: If each of the five lifecycle surfaces asks the engine-offer question fresh, the operator re-answers the same choice repeatedly — the exact re-asking pattern the intake flagged and that drew documented operator fury elsewhere. Add an engine-posture primitive: a derived-on-read `.saga/engine-posture` value (never a committed status field) captured once at outcome/session start — 'default offload to X, second-opinion to Y, or ask me' — that the shared offer block consults so it RECOMMENDS from the remembered posture rather than re-prompting. Compounding: every current and future surface inherits the remembered choice for free, and the operator tunes the fleet's whole external-LLM behavior from one answer. Crossing {#operator-choice-framework}: posture stays doc-only / CLI-driven and advisory — it is a recommendation the operator can override at any surface, never a hidden auto-router that dispatches without a visible offer.
basis: Intake brief §1 resolved tension: 'Asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation.' Grounding §7 pattern 2 documents operator fury at gate primitives that treat silence as consent — re-asking the same choice per stage is the same ergonomic failure. {#operator-choice-framework} keeps it doc/CLI-driven.
outcome_shape: PR adding engine-posture derive/read (saga-side, derived-on-read per the /outcome campaign rule) + offer-block consultation so surfaces recommend from posture. Verified by a test asserting a set posture suppresses the re-prompt and yields a recommendation at a second surface.

title: /engines meta-command: one legible surface to inspect, pin, and deprecate engines
idea: The registry's ratings, cost_speed_rank, and last_validated staleness are only visible by reading raw YAML, and an operator who distrusts an engine for a repo has no lever short of hand-editing that file. Add an `/engines` saga skill subcommand (NOT a new plugin) that renders the live registry — capability ratings, tie-break order, staleness age per row — and lets the operator pin a preferred variant or deprecate an engine per repo, writing a small overlay the resolver honors. Compounding: the registry becomes operator-legible and tunable from one meta-tool that every surface's resolution then reflects, instead of scattered YAML edits. Crossing {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: this ships as a subcommand inside the existing saga plugin, carrying zero new-plugin sprawl — its consolidation burden of proof is met by adding no plugin at all.
basis: engine-registry.yaml exposes capability_profile ratings, cost_speed_rank, and last_validated but grounding §1 confirms the fleet's only operator-facing model/effort lever is saga /plan's tier table — the registry itself has no operator surface. {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} forces the subcommand-not-plugin shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding an /engines saga subcommand (skill + CLI) that reads the registry, flags stale rows, and writes a per-repo pin/deprecate overlay honored by engine_resolver. Verified by a test asserting a pinned variant wins resolution and a deprecated engine is skipped.

title: Engine point-out: per-finding second-opinion flag at judgment stages
idea: In air-traffic control a 'point-out' lets a controller flag one specific target to an adjacent sector without a full handoff of the aircraft. Today the external-engine offer is coarse: absent from /doc-review and /code-review interactive flow (grounding correction (c)), so the operator's only lever is offload-the-whole-review or nothing. Add a granular 'point-out' surface where, on a single review finding, the reviewer can dispatch just that finding to a second-opinion engine (intent=second-opinion, opus/high chaperone) and fold the returned advisory into the finding's verdict. Claude remains verifier-of-record: the engine's opinion is advisory evidence Claude adjudicates, never a gate. The point-out is scoped to one finding, so context cost is a single finding's frame, not the whole diff.
basis: Source domain: air-traffic control 'point-out' procedure (FAA JO 7110.65, controller flags one target to an adjacent sector short of a full handoff). Grounds a granular surface distinct from whole-review offload; engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} within its constraint (advisory-only, Claude adjudicates) so no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'point-out' interactive step to plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md and doc-review/SKILL.md that calls engine_resolver.resolve(role_kind='worker', intent=second-opinion) for one finding and records the advisory under that finding; verified by a doc-review/code-review fixture test asserting the returned opinion is stored as advisory evidence with verified_by_claude gating the verdict.

title: Andon-cord engine offer: one uniform primitive across every lifecycle surface
idea: Toyota's andon cord is a single standardized signal any worker can pull at any station on the line to summon help — the power is that it is identical everywhere, not reinvented per station. The engine offer today is the opposite: ENGINE_INTENTS is authored only in /plan and rendered only in team-execution's A7 table, absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, and /work interactive flow (grounding correction (c)), so each command would grow its own ad-hoc prompt. Instead ship one declarative engine-surface map (engine-surface-map.yaml) enumerating each lifecycle command as a station with its default intent (judgment stages default second-opinion, mechanical default offload), and a shared offer snippet each SKILL.md references. Coverage becomes a property you can lint, not a per-command accident.
basis: Source domain: Toyota Production System andon cord (a single standardized stop/help signal identical at every station, per Ohno's TPS). The value is uniformity-of-primitive across surfaces, which maps directly onto the correction (c) finding that the intent offer is present in only 2 of ~6 surfaces.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/engine-surface-map.yaml (command -> default intent) plus a drift-guard test in tests/ asserting every lifecycle command SKILL.md (ideate, brainstorm, work, doc-review, code-review, team-execution) references the map and has a surface entry; verified by the test failing when a command is added without a map row.

title: Maker-checker dissent record for second-opinion reconciliation
idea: Banking's four-eyes / maker-checker control does not silently absorb a checker's disagreement — the dissent is recorded and, above a threshold, escalated, so the audit trail shows where the second signer objected and how it resolved. Second-opinion reconciliation today has no structured place to record that the engine disagreed with Claude; the manifest only distinguishes disposition (ran-as-requested / substituted / fell-back), not agreement-vs-dissent on the substance. Add a 'dissent' leg to the reconciliation contract: when a second-opinion engine's advisory materially contradicts Claude's own conclusion, the chaperone records a typed dissent record (engine claim, Claude claim, resolution) on the manifest. This preserves never-gatekeepers (Claude still decides) while making the disagreement a durable, reviewable fact instead of a swallowed one.
basis: Source domain: banking maker-checker / four-eyes principle (payment and trade authorization where a second authorizer's objection is logged and escalated, not discarded — Basel operational-risk control practice). Maps onto second-opinion reconciliation, which the ENGINE_INTENTS comment (execution_spec.py:68) frames as 'adversarial verification IS the product' but which currently has no dissent-capture channel.
outcome_shape: PR adding a typed 'dissent' field to the reconciliation manifest emitted by plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py (record_dispatch_manifest path) and documenting it in references/external-engine-workers.md section 5; verified by a unit test that a contradicting advisory produces a manifest carrying both claims and Claude's resolution.

title: Acceptance-sampling verification for offload output
idea: Manufacturing incoming-inspection does not re-test every unit in a delivered lot; it draws a sample sized to the supplier's demonstrated quality (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 AQL tables) and accepts or rejects the lot on the sample. Offload reconciliation today is implicitly all-or-nothing: the chaperone reads the whole returned patch. For a large mechanical offload from a STRONG-rated engine, full re-read erases the savings the offload was for (KTD2). Make offload verification an acceptance-sampling policy: the chaperone samples N hunks of the returned diff, sized inversely to the engine's capability rating for that capability, and escalates to full review on any sampled defect. This stays inside never-gatekeepers because the offload is a non-gated worker and the resulting diff still clears reviewer-consensus and validator gates unchanged — sampling governs only the chaperone's own read effort, not the gate.
basis: Source domain: statistical acceptance sampling / AQL (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4, MIL-STD-105 lot-acceptance sampling where sample size tracks supplier quality history). Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} within its bound: offload is explicitly the non-gated-worker role, sampling touches only chaperone read-effort while the diff still clears consensus gates — so it does not cross the decision and needs no revisit.
outcome_shape: PR adding an offload sampling-policy function to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py keyed off the engine's capability_profile rating, wired into the chaperone verify step in references/external-engine-workers.md section 5; verified by unit tests mapping WEAK/MODERATE/STRONG ratings to sample fractions and asserting any injected defect forces full-review escalation.

title: Coase break-even gate: offload only when make-vs-buy pays
idea: Coase's transaction-cost theory of the firm says you outsource a task only when the market price plus the transaction cost of contracting-and-inspecting is below the cost of doing it in-house. The ENGINE_INTENTS comment already states the economic truth — offload 'wants a cheap chaperone (the delegation is net-negative otherwise)' — but nothing computes the break-even, so a plan can author an offload unit whose sonnet/medium chaperone cost plus engine cost exceeds just doing the unit at tier. Add a pure break-even function that estimates offload_cost (engine cost_speed_rank + chaperone verify-apply-test tokens, scaled by capability rating) versus do-it-yourself cost for the unit size, and surface a 'net-negative offload' warning in the /plan tier table when the buy side loses. This makes the intake's stated Fable-tier discipline ('expensive is never a silent default') computable for the offload path too.
basis: Source domain: Coase transaction-cost economics / make-or-buy boundary of the firm ('The Nature of the Firm', 1937). Directly formalizes the offload cost claim quoted at plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md:303 ('a heavier chaperone erases the token savings'); respects {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by deciding whether to offload at all, not by changing the offload->sonnet/medium mapping.
outcome_shape: PR adding a chaperone_economics break-even function (new module beside plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py) consumed by the /plan Step-1 tier-table renderer (SKILL.md:295-307) to flag net-negative offload rows; verified by unit tests over cost scenarios asserting the warning fires when engine+chaperone cost exceeds do-it-yourself.

title: Best-execution TCA ledger: realized chaperone cost corrects registry ratings
idea: Equity trading desks run Transaction Cost Analysis: they record realized slippage of each routed order against a benchmark and feed it back to bias future venue routing toward brokers that actually delivered. The engine registry's capability ratings (WEAK/MODERATE/STRONG in engine_registry.py) are hand-authored priors that never get corrected by outcomes, and the /outcome cost ledger treats cost as a leaf-produced fact but does not close the loop on chaperone efficiency. Extend each dispatch manifest to carry realized chaperone tokens, engine tokens, and disposition, then ship a report that computes realized offload savings per engine/capability and surfaces registry rows whose realized savings contradict their rating. Routing stays operator-chosen and Claude stays verifier-of-record; this only makes the empirical cost of each engine legible.
basis: Source domain: trading Transaction Cost Analysis / best-execution (MiFID II RTS 27/28 venue-quality reporting, realized-slippage-vs-benchmark feedback into routing). Maps onto the hand-authored, never-corrected capability_profile ratings in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py and the /outcome 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' binding, which it extends rather than crosses.
outcome_shape: PR adding realized-token fields (chaperone_tokens, engine_tokens) to the dispatch manifest in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py plus a report script that flags engine-registry.yaml rows whose realized savings contradict their rating; verified by a test feeding synthetic dispatch records and asserting the mismatch flag.

title: AI-Director engine memory: adaptive per-repo intent recommendation
idea: Left 4 Dead's AI Director does not ask the player a settings question every scene; it observes accept/override behavior and tunes the next offer to the player's demonstrated preference, keeping a light per-session memory. The engine offer today has no memory: every run re-presents the same static default, so an operator who always declines second-opinion on /doc-review in a given repo re-declines forever. Add a small per-repo engine-preference memory (.saga/engine-prefs.json) that records accept/override history per command+intent and pre-selects the recommended intent accordingly, always overridable and always showing the cheaper fallback. This operationalizes the intake's 'remembered' ergonomics axis without ever auto-proceeding — the recommendation is pre-filled, the operator still confirms.
basis: Source domain: video-game Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment / the Left 4 Dead 'AI Director' (Valve; adapts to observed player behavior with lightweight session memory rather than re-prompting). Novel against QUEUED/direct-to-candidate pools, which contain no engine-preference-memory item; keeps Claude as verifier and never auto-proceeds, so it does not touch the never-gatekeepers boundary.
outcome_shape: PR adding a .saga/engine-prefs.json read/write helper and wiring the recommended-intent pre-fill into the shared engine-offer snippet (or engine-surface-map consumer); verified by a test that a recorded override-history biases the next recommendation while leaving the operator confirmation step intact.

title: Challenge-response run-start intent manifest
idea: Aviation challenge-response checklists front-load configuration decisions into one structured pass before takeoff — the crew answers every item once, reads it back, and does not get re-interrupted mid-climb. The intake's resolved tensions already want intent captured 'once per run start' (PR-reviews-required, gate-or-auto-merge, per-stage engine intent), but there is no single artifact that captures them; the choices are scattered into whatever mid-run prompt happens to fire. Ship a run-start engine-intent manifest: one challenge-response block at the start of /outcome and /work that captures every intent question at once, stores the answers, and every downstream lifecycle surface reads them instead of re-asking. Mid-run stages consult the manifest silently for reversible choices and only re-prompt for a spend-increasing escalation the manifest did not authorize.
basis: Source domain: aviation challenge-response checklists (front-loaded, read-back-confirmed configuration before a phase of flight, per crew-resource-management standards). Directly operationalizes intake tensions 2/3 ('asked once per run start', reversible choices proceed without asking); respects {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by recording intent per stage, not by adding an executor kind.
outcome_shape: PR adding a run-start intent-manifest capture to plugins/saga/skills/outcome and work SKILL.md that writes a stored intent record, plus consumer reads in the engine-offer snippet; verified by a test asserting downstream surfaces read stored intent and only re-prompt on an unauthorized spend escalation.

title: Engine-offer at every judgment surface, not just /plan
idea: Flip the constraint 'engines are reachable at exactly one surface' to its extreme: EVERY lifecycle command offers an external engine. Today ENGINE_INTENTS is a producer/consumer pair authored only in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304) and rendered only in team-execution; /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive have no offer at all. The practical kernel is a single shared reference (plugins/saga/references/engine-offer.md) plus a 3-line offer block inlined into each judgment skill's flow, each tagging its default intent (offload vs second-opinion) per the split in intake tension 2. Claude stays verifier-of-record; the offer is advisory-only, never a gate. The offer resolves the engine via engine_resolver.resolve(mode='advisory') so it previews without dispatching.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): 'ENGINE_INTENTS ... Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow' and plan/SKILL.md:303-304 as the sole authoring site; engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} by keeping every new surface advisory-only.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/engine-offer.md plus offer blocks in ideate/brainstorm/work SKILL.md and a marketplace/CHANGELOG bump; verified by a drift-guard test asserting each of the three skills references the shared offer anchor and no offer sets verified_by_claude.

title: Always-on blind second opinion with a typed reconciliation record
idea: Flip 'second opinion is opt-in, explicit-request-only' to the extreme: every gated judgment ALWAYS gets a blind external second opinion. Mine the kernel: not the always-on part, but the reconciliation machinery that makes disagreement cheap. Add a reconciliation-record schema (agree / diverge / engine-only-finding) that Claude produces when it adjudicates engine advisory output, so a divergence becomes a durable structured artifact instead of prose the operator reconciles by hand. Claude remains verifier-of-record and adjudicates every cell; the engine's dissent is recorded, never counted toward a verdict. This directly generalizes the one-off Claude+Codex 15/17 hand-reconciliation into a repeatable protocol.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' — prior art living in the session-mining synthesis; the reconciliation was manual and unrepeatable. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: engine dissent is advisory, Claude adjudicates each divergence.
outcome_shape: PR adding a reconciliation-record.md schema under plugins/saga/references/ and wiring it into /doc-review and /code-review advisory paths; verified by a fixture test that feeds a synthetic engine/Claude disagreement and asserts a well-formed diverge record with Claude as adjudicator.

title: Chaperone-overhead ledger: prove offload was actually net-positive
idea: Flip 'chaperoning is free' to test its opposite: assume the chaperone costs nothing, and offload always wins — then measure to see whether that assumption holds. KTD2 asserts a heavy chaperone erases the savings that motivated an offload, but nothing in the fleet measures the chaperone's own token cost against the engine tokens saved. The kernel is a chaperone_token_cost field on the dispatch manifest plus a net_savings computation (engine_tokens_avoided minus chaperone_tokens_spent) recorded per offload dispatch. This turns KTD2 from an untested design premise into a per-dispatch fact that /retro can validate the registry against, and makes a silently-net-negative offload visible.
basis: plan/SKILL.md tier table (offload row): 'a heavier chaperone erases the token savings that motivated the delegation (KTD2)' — asserted but never measured; engine_dispatch.record_dispatch_manifest (engine_dispatch.py:124-161) is the existing manifest builder to extend. Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by keeping offload→sonnet/medium and only measuring it.
outcome_shape: PR adding chaperone_token_cost + net_savings to saga.manifest.v1 via build_dispatch_manifest and a computation in engine_dispatch.py; verified by a unit test asserting a net-negative offload yields a flagged manifest and the drift-guard on the manifest schema stays green.

title: Zero-question engine choice: remembered per-surface intent preference
idea: Flip 'the operator is asked every run' to its extreme: the operator is asked zero times ever. The kernel isn't silent autonomy (that would violate the choosable-never-assumed posture) but memory: a persisted .saga/engine-prefs.json recording, per surface and per intent, the operator's last choice plus a remembered recommendation, so the run-start question is pre-filled with 'last time you chose codex/second-opinion here — keep it?' rather than a cold prompt. The preference is a recommendation the operator confirms once per run, honoring intake tension 1's asymmetric approval (spend-increasing choices still need an explicit yes) while eliminating the cold-start friction of re-deciding identical choices every session.
basis: Intake brief §2: external-LLM purpose is 'always operator-choosable, never assumed' and §1: 'Asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation.' No persistence layer exists — every surface re-asks cold. Engages the choosable posture by keeping confirmation, only remembering the default.
outcome_shape: PR adding a .saga/engine-prefs.json schema + a read/write helper in engine_resolver.py and a prefs-aware recommendation line in the offer block; verified by a round-trip test (write choice, re-read, assert recommendation surfaces) plus a gitignore-hygiene check on the prefs path.

title: $0-engine cost class: zero-ledger offload accounting
idea: Flip the engine cost constraint to $0: what if the offload engine were entirely free? Intake §5 already names Ollama as the $0 offload target. The kernel is a cost_class registry field (free / metered / premium) that makes free-engine offloads accrue zero to the run's cost ledger, so an offload's only remaining cost is the sonnet/medium chaperone — inverting the economics so offload is near-always net-positive without touching the chaperone tier. This composes cleanly with the chaperone-overhead ledger (T1-F6-3): a free engine means net_savings equals the full engine-work token count minus a fixed cheap chaperone tax. cost_speed_rank already exists as a tie-break key; cost_class is the coarser gate above it.
basis: Intake brief §5: 'Ollama → $0 offload target; DeepSeek → cheap second opinion' and engine-registry.yaml's existing cost_speed_rank tie-break key (the registry already ranks cost). Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by leaving offload→sonnet/medium fixed and only zeroing the engine-side ledger.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cost_class field to engine-registry.yaml rows + resolver/ledger handling that zeroes free-class engine cost; verified by a test asserting a free-class offload contributes 0 to the cost ledger and the registry schema drift-guard passes.

title: External-engine advisory jury for the hardest calls (Claude foreman)
idea: Flip 'one engine per unit' to '100 engines': a whole panel of external engines gives independent second opinions on the single hardest judgment call. Mine the kernel: a bounded external-engine advisory panel (role_kind='panel', already in ROLE_KINDS at engine_resolver.py:18) for the rare architectural decision where Claude wants cross-family dissent, with the panel capped by a VERIFY_N_CAP analog so it can't reprise the 22-judge rate-limit incident. Claude is foreman: it reads all panelists' advisory output, adjudicates, and is the sole verifier-of-record. The panel never gates and never joins wave scheduling — it is N one-shot advisory dispatches Claude reconciles, cap-bounded and mode-aware.
basis: engine_resolver.py:18 ROLE_KINDS includes 'panel' (currently a HALT_ROLE_KIND with no resolution path) and execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP = 7 born from the 22-judge concurrency incident. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (advisory foreman) and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (second-opinion→opus/high chaperone).
outcome_shape: PR adding a capped 'panel' resolution path in engine_resolver.py wiring role_kind='panel' out of HALT into a bounded advisory fan-out + a reconciliation summary; verified by a test asserting N>cap halts and Claude adjudication is required before any panel output is recorded.

title: Auto-offer a second opinion when /work hits an uncertainty signal
idea: Flip 'engines never enter interactive /work' to 'the engine auto-offers itself the moment Claude is stuck.' The extreme is fully autonomous mid-work escalation; the kernel is a stuck-signal detector in the /work round-N continuation loop (repeated failed test cycles, an explicit low-confidence self-assessment, a thrash pattern) that surfaces a one-line second-opinion offer at exactly that moment instead of only at plan-time. The offer is advisory and operator-confirmed (attended) or logged-and-skipped (unattended, per the asymmetric rule); Claude adjudicates whatever the engine returns. This closes the last of the three surfaces the grounding brief flags as offer-less.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS 'absent from ... /work interactive flow'; work/SKILL.md owns the round-N continuation loop where the stuck signal is observable. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the mid-work offer is advisory, Claude adjudicates.
outcome_shape: PR adding a stuck-signal → second-opinion offer hook in work/SKILL.md's continuation loop + a reference describing the signals; verified by a scripted /work fixture that trips a repeated-failure signal and asserts the offer surfaces without auto-dispatching in attended mode.

title: Mode→intent default matrix: unattended runs pick their own posture
idea: Flip 'expensive is never a silent default' to its mirror — in fully unattended /outcome runs, let the engine posture default itself with no human in the loop. The kernel is a small mode→intent matrix: unattended runs default to cache-tight offload (cheap, may proceed silently per intake tension 1); attended judgment stages default to a second-opinion recommendation the operator confirms. This encodes intake's asymmetric approval rule as a machine-readable table the resolver consults, rather than prose each skill re-interprets. It never silently escalates spend in attended mode and never blocks an unattended run waiting for a human — the two failure modes the tension was written to avoid.
basis: Intake brief §1 asymmetric approval rule ('Unattended ... may proceed silently'; 'Attended ... any spend-increasing choice always requires explicit operator yes') and §2 judgment-vs-mechanical intent split. Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by mapping offload/second-opinion to the fixed sonnet/opus chaperone tiers.
outcome_shape: PR adding a mode→intent default matrix (reference doc + a resolver lookup) consulted at engine-offer time; verified by a test asserting unattended-mode resolves offload silently and attended judgment-stage resolves a second-opinion recommendation requiring confirmation.

title: Retro-exit promote tripwire: surface the pending-cluster count nobody ever sees
idea: The promote loop has never fired because it is manual-invoke-only and nothing ever tells the operator that candidates have piled up. Add a `promote_scan.py --check` mode that reports counts (recurrence clusters >= threshold, declared-Transcendent markers, candidates filtered by ledger) and returns a nonzero-signal exit code when clusters exist. Wire that count into `/retro`'s terminal advisory summary and a saga status line so every retro ends with a concrete nudge like 'N cross-repo clusters await /promote'. The friction is pure discoverability: the machinery computes `recurrence_clusters` and `marked` already; it just never reaches the operator's eye between runs.
