basis: promote_scan.py already computes `recurrence_clusters` (lines 302-330) and `marked` (line 278) but only prints them on manual invoke; promote/SKILL.md:48 frames it 'a manual, gated, agent-judged workspace pass'; grounding brief §3.5: '0 learnings ever promoted ... the cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `--check` subcommand/flag to plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py and a promote-readiness line to plugins/saga/skills/retro/SKILL.md's terminal summary; verified by a unit test in tests/ asserting `--check` exits nonzero and prints the cluster count on a fixture workspace with >=1 cluster, and the retro SKILL step referencing it.

title: Deterministic near-duplicate pre-clustering so the recurrence net actually catches anything
idea: The deterministic recurrence floor groups rules strictly by identical normalized-wording hash (`_recurrence_clusters`, `by_hash[c.hash]`), so the same lesson phrased differently in two repos never forms a cluster — which is exactly why the scan surfaces no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster and all weight falls on the judgment layer that only runs on manual invoke. Add a deterministic lexical pre-grouping (token-set Jaccard / MinHash over the already-normalized rule text) that emits `near_duplicate_groups` alongside the exact clusters, lowering the activation energy for the judgment pass without introducing any semantic index. This stays inside core principle 5 ('Judgment, not vectors. No embeddings, no RAG, no index to drift') because MinHash over normalized tokens is deterministic lexical set-overlap, not a learned embedding or a persisted index — recomputed from source each scan, nothing to drift.
basis: promote_scan.py:302-330 `_recurrence_clusters` groups by `c.hash` ('identical wording -> identical hash across repos'); promote/SKILL.md:45-46 core principle 5 forbids embeddings/RAG/index; grounding §3.5 'no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster' — the exact-hash floor is empirically empty. The idea engages the principle-5 revisit boundary by staying deterministic-lexical.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `near_duplicate_groups` field to promote_scan.py's ScanResult + a deterministic token-set grouping function, plus a Phase 2 note in promote/SKILL.md; verified by a unit test feeding two differently-worded expressions of one rule across two repo fixtures and asserting they land in one near-duplicate group while exact clusters stay empty.

title: Codex session miner: light up 219 dark sessions as /retro substrate
idea: 219 codex sessions ran in the 60-day window with zero mining substrate — /retro only distills Claude session skeletons, so every lesson learned inside a codex rescue or delegation is invisible to the learning loop. Add a codex-transcript reader that reads the local codex session store and emits the same skeleton shape /retro's Claude miner already consumes, so codex work feeds recurring-pattern distillation on equal footing. This is strictly read-only mining and never a gatekeeping surface, so it stays clear of the never-gatekeepers boundary: codex output becomes learning evidence, not a verifier-of-record. The codex plugin already knows where its runtime writes; the miner points at that path.
basis: Grounding brief §7: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10'; the codex plugin ships a runtime (codex:codex-cli-runtime skill) whose session store is a known local path. Binding `{#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}` is respected: mining is read-only, produces no gated decision.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a codex-session-to-skeleton reader script under plugins/saga (or the codex plugin) plus a retro/SKILL.md substrate note listing codex as a mined source; verified by a test that parses a captured codex session fixture into the retro skeleton schema and by a retro dry-run enumerating codex sessions in its session count.

title: Incremental mining watermark so /retro stops re-chewing the whole workspace every run
idea: Each /retro mining pass fans out over sessions from scratch with no memory of what it already distilled, and read-only recon fan-outs already burn 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes — so as the Claude-plus-codex session corpus grows, a full pass gets expensive enough that nobody runs it, which is one root of the never-fired downstream loop. Add a per-workspace last-mined watermark ledger (session id + timestamp of last distillation) so a pass mines only sessions newer than the watermark, with an explicit `--full` override. The cost of mining collapses from O(all sessions) to O(new sessions), making a cheap recurring pass viable and directly feeding the promote substrate more often.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)'; §7 session-mining synthesis distilled 70 skeletons in one pass with no incrementality; intake §1 unattended->cache-tight posture makes a cheap delta-only pass the aligned default.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a watermark ledger file + read/update helpers and a `--since`/`--full` toggle to the retro mining path, plus a retro/SKILL.md note; verified by a test asserting a second pass over an unchanged fixture corpus mines zero sessions and a pass after adding one session mines exactly one.

title: Anchor-drift linter for CLAUDE.md and journal claims that assert current system state
idea: Stale memory and CLAUDE.md claims get asserted as fact and are caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification — a documented multi-repo pattern and a repeated journal learning. Add a `check_claims.py` that scans CLAUDE.md, LEARNINGS.md, and DECISIONS.md for factual assertions carrying a verifiable anchor (a `file:line`, an enum name, a `command` fence) and flags every anchor that no longer resolves: dead `file:line`, a quoted enum value absent from the named source, a referenced script path that moved. Wire it into a saga preflight or CI so drift surfaces mechanically instead of by memory. This is deliberately narrower than evidence-artifact immutability (already a direct-to-candidate): it targets prose claims with backing anchors, not run-artifact chain-of-custody.
basis: Grounding brief §6.2 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state (4 learnings)' and §7.7 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification (2 repos) -> theme 10'; the intake brief itself spot-checks anchors (execution_spec.py:52-53) precisely because they drift.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/check_claims.py + tests/test_check_claims.py, plus a CLAUDE.md/CI hook invoking it; verified by a test where a fixture doc citing a nonexistent `foo.py:999` and a wrong enum value both raise flagged findings while a live-anchor doc passes clean.

title: As-of verification stamps on state-asserting journal entries
idea: The provenance failure is that a durable journal or memory claim about current system behavior carries no freshness signal, so a reader cannot tell a claim verified this week from one that rotted six months ago — both read as fact. Introduce a lightweight convention: any LEARNINGS/DECISIONS claim asserting current system state carries a `**Verified.** YYYY-MM-DD @ anchor` line, and a linter flags state-asserting entries whose stamp is missing or older than a configurable staleness horizon. Reasoning from first principles: re-verifying every claim continuously is infeasible and re-verifying none is what produces the stale-fact bug, so the tractable middle is to make staleness visible and let the operator re-verify on demand — the same derive-on-read discipline the fleet already prefers over committed truth, applied to knowledge freshness.
basis: First-principles: a claim's truth is time-varying but its text is static; without a captured as-of date, a reader cannot distinguish fresh from rotted, which is precisely the caught-only-by-recall failure. Continuous re-verification is cost-infeasible (see the 350-450k recon number) and zero re-verification yields the observed bug, so surfacing staleness is the only tractable lever — mirroring the fleet's stated derive-on-read-over-committed-state preference (grounding §6.5).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding the `**Verified.**` stamp convention to the engineering-journal README + docs/engineering-journal practice and a staleness linter script with a threshold flag; verified by a test asserting a state-asserting entry with a stamp older than the horizon is flagged and a freshly-stamped one passes.

title: Cost-bounded scheduled workspace learning pass with the write gate preserved
idea: The promote loop never fires largely because it depends on a human remembering to run a manual workspace pass; nothing schedules the mine-and-check cadence. Add a scheduled cost-bounded monthly workspace pass (via the schedule/cron surface) that runs the read-only half only — incremental retro mining of the delta plus `promote_scan.py --check` — and emits a digest (a mission-control prepared issue or a Discord nudge) when clusters cross threshold, while the actual context-library promotion write stays manual and operator-gated exactly as today. This crosses the intake tension-1 asymmetric-approval binding, and engages its revisit-when directly: the scheduled pass is read-only and cache-tight, so it may proceed silently in the unattended lane, but every spend-or-state-changing step (the promotion upsert) still requires an explicit operator yes.
basis: Grounding §3.5 never-fired loop; promote/SKILL.md:38-42 keeps every context-library write propose-diff-and-wait; intake brief §1 binding: 'Unattended runs -> cache-tight serial; may proceed silently' for read-only, 'any spend-increasing choice ... always requires an explicit operator yes'. The idea keeps the write gated, satisfying the revisit-when rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a scheduled-pass definition (schedule/cron config + a read-only runner wrapping incremental mining and promote_scan --check + a digest emitter) and a DECISIONS.md entry recording the read-only-silent / write-gated split; verified by a dry-run of the runner producing a digest artifact and asserting it performs no context-library write.

title: Mined-pattern to prepared-issue pipeline (dogfooding this very session's manual labor)
idea: This entire ideation session mines recurring patterns by hand and materializes them into GitHub issues through a bespoke multi-phase workflow — the pattern-to-issue path is real, valuable, and completely un-durable. Make it a repeatable saga->mission-control handoff: given a ranked recurring pattern from a retro mining pass (with its repo-spread count and mined `file:line` evidence), produce a prepared SDLC issue draft where the mined evidence auto-populates the outcome-generating basis and the repo-spread becomes the priority signal. The pain is that every future 'we keep hitting X across repos' insight either dies in a journal or gets hand-carried into an issue; this closes retro's advisory-terminal boundary to mission-control's issue intake without making retro itself a gatekeeper.
basis: Grounding §7 explicitly maps mined patterns to themes (pattern 1->theme 7, pattern 7->theme 10, etc.) by hand this session; retro/SKILL.md is terminal-advisory and does not route to issues; mission-control:issue already accepts source artifacts (saga:handoff exists). The manual pattern-to-issue labor is the reproduced-live evidence.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a retro-pattern -> mission-control prepared-issue handoff path (a handoff/SKILL.md or retro/SKILL.md step plus a serializer turning a ranked pattern + evidence into the prepared-issue schema); verified by a test converting a fixture ranked-pattern record into a valid prepared-issue payload carrying the mined file:line evidence as basis.

title: Codex-session mining adapter — end the 219-session dark zone
idea: Today /retro mines only Claude sessions; the ~224 codex .jsonl transcripts under ~/.codex/sessions are structurally invisible, so more than half the fleet's recent agent work never becomes learning. Remove the substrate blindness by adding a codex-session source enumerator to retro's mining backbone that normalizes ~/.codex/sessions/*.jsonl into the same skeleton shape Claude sessions produce, so one mining pass covers both engines uniformly. The read is strictly read-only over transcripts (no codex invocation), so it never makes codex a gatekeeper. The inversion: the best version of 'remember to run this inside Claude so it gets captured' is no such step — mine the artifact on disk regardless of which engine produced it.
basis: Grounding brief line 115: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10.' Verified live this session: `find ~/.codex/sessions -name '*.jsonl'` returns 224 files. Engages `{#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}` revisit-when: mining transcripts is read-only consumption, not gated decision authority, so the decision is respected not crossed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a codex-source enumerator to saga retro's mining backbone (new function + reference note in plugins/saga/skills/retro/references/retro-passes.md), plus a CHANGELOG/plugin.json version bump. Verified by running the mining pass against ~/.codex/sessions and observing skeleton count > 0 where it was previously 0.

title: Recurrence-triggered promotion — remove the human from the /promote trigger
idea: The promote loop has fired zero times ever, and the root friction is that firing requires a human to remember to type /promote. But the deterministic floor already exists: promote_scan.py._recurrence_clusters() finds any lesson recurring across >=2 repos with no judgment needed. Invert the trigger so recurrence detection, not human recall, initiates the loop — a thin runner executes `promote_scan.py scan --json` and, when it finds a non-empty cluster set, surfaces those clusters to the operator's review surface as pending promotion candidates. The gated write stays exactly as-is (propose-diff-and-wait, KTD6); only the 'notice there is something to promote' step is removed. The best version of a step nobody performs is a step that performs itself up to the gate.
basis: promote_scan.py:302 `_recurrence_clusters` computes the deterministic recurrence floor with zero judgment, yet promote/SKILL.md Phase 0 requires a manual operator invocation to reach it; grounding brief line 72 records '0 learnings ever promoted' — direct evidence the manual trigger never fires.
outcome_shape: PR adding a runner (e.g. plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py gains a `report` subcommand or a small wrapper) that emits found recurrence clusters as a digest, wired to a review surface; verified by seeding two repo journals with an identical rule and observing the cluster surface as a pending candidate without any /promote invocation.

title: Auto-suggest the Transcendent marker at capture time (remove the declare cognition)
idea: The 'declare' feeder — a human or /retro marking `**Transcendent.**` in Pass 5 — has produced zero markers, because noticing that a just-written lesson transcends repos is invisible cognition nobody performs. Remove the cognition: at retro capture time, hash the new LEARNINGS rule with the existing rule_hash() and check it against every other repo journal's rules; on a cross-repo hash collision (or near-collision the agent confirms), auto-suggest appending the Transcendent marker inline in the same edit. The operator only accepts or declines a concrete suggestion rather than originating the judgment. This automates the exact case promote/SKILL.md flags as the gap: 'the transcendent lessons no one thought to declare.'
basis: retro-passes.md:142-144 defines the manual `**Transcendent.**` declare step and its idempotency skip; promote/SKILL.md:27-28 names the unfilled gap ('catching the transcendent lessons no one thought to declare'); rule_hash()/normalize_rule() at promote_scan.py:82-102 already provide the cross-repo collision primitive to reuse.
outcome_shape: PR to plugins/saga/skills/retro/references/retro-passes.md Pass 5 plus a helper (reusing promote_scan.rule_hash) that flags cross-repo hash collisions at capture; verified by a unit test feeding two repos with an identical normalized rule and asserting a Transcendent-marker suggestion is emitted.

title: Provenance lint — remove the human re-verification of stale doc claims
idea: Stale CLAUDE.md and journal claims (file:line refs, version numbers, counts) are asserted as fact and caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification — the Validation Discipline burden is fully manual. Remove the re-verification step by making it a machine check: a claim_check.py script that extracts verifiable assertions from CLAUDE.md and the journal (path:line anchors, plugin version strings, enumerated counts) and re-verifies each against the live repo — does the file:line still exist, does the quoted version match plugin.json. Wire it as a pre-commit/CI check so a claim that has gone stale fails the build instead of surviving until an operator happens to remember. The best version of 'did I verify this from a current source?' is a gate that will not let an unverified claim through.
basis: Grounding brief lines 135-136: 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification (2 repos) -> theme 10.' Directly instantiates the global Validation Discipline mandate ('never assert without checking') as machinery rather than habit.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/claim_check.py plus a .pre-commit-config / CI hook entry; verified by seeding CLAUDE.md with a file:line ref to a deleted anchor and a wrong plugin version, running the check, and observing a non-zero exit that names both stale claims.

title: Append-only evidence artifacts — remove the overwrite that destroys chain-of-custody
idea: A probe/verify script currently overwrites a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS, silently erasing the audit chain-of-custody — the failure that a later re-run masks is gone. Remove the overwrite failure mode by construction: codify an append-only evidence convention where each probe writes to a timestamped, never-reused path and the 'latest' pointer is derived, not overwritten. A tiny helper plus a guard test enforces it so no evidence write can clobber a prior result. The inversion: the safest overwrite is no overwrite — make the artifact immutable and let history accumulate.
basis: Grounding brief lines 150-151: 'probe script overwriting FAIL evidence artifact later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)' — recorded as a structural background-automation constraint. This is a named, concrete evidence-integrity defect, not a hypothetical.
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only evidence-write helper + convention doc under plugins/saga/skills/qa (or verify) references, plus a guard test asserting a second write to an existing evidence path raises rather than overwrites; verified by the test and by a demo run producing two dated artifacts instead of one clobbered file.

title: Scheduled cost-bounded mining+promote-scan routine — the loop runs itself
idea: Both /retro mining and /promote are on-demand-only, and an on-demand loop that has never fired in months will keep not firing. Remove the on-demand dependency with a scheduled, cost-bounded routine (a committed cron/routine definition) that runs the mining backbone plus promote_scan on a cadence and emits a digest only when patterns or recurrence clusters cross threshold — otherwise silent. Because it runs unattended, it honors intake tension 1: cache-tight serial, cheap tier, concurrency <=3, may proceed silently, and it never performs the gated context-library write itself (that stays propose-diff-and-wait for an attended pass). The best version of 'remember to run the cross-repo pass' is a scheduled job that surfaces only when it has something worth an operator's attention.
basis: Grounding brief line 72: '0 learnings ever promoted' and line 73: 'cross-repo learning loop exists but never fired' — direct evidence the on-demand cadence never fires. Engages intake brief tension 1 revisit posture: unattended runs default cache-tight/serial and may proceed silently, which is exactly the cost-bounding this routine adopts, so the binding cost posture is satisfied not violated.
outcome_shape: PR adding a committed routine/schedule definition + a wrapper script that runs mining+promote_scan cheaply and emits a threshold-gated digest (no auto-write to context-library); verified by a dry-run schedule listing and a manual wrapper run producing a digest artifact on seeded data and silence on empty data.

title: Pattern-triggered issue drafting — automate the mined-pattern-to-backlog bridge
idea: The step this very ideation session performs manually — a mined cross-repo pattern hand-carried into a backlog issue — is the missing automation. When /retro surfaces a friction pattern recurring across >=N repos, auto-draft a mission-control prepared issue (extending the existing saga:handoff route) whose body passes card_validator, gated at the write. The operator reviews a ready draft instead of transcribing a finding into an issue from scratch. This removes the transcription step while keeping the human as approver, so a mined pattern becomes a backlog candidate by default rather than only when someone stages a whole session around it.
basis: Intake brief line 89: observed friction 'becomes direct-basis issue material'; grounding brief theme 10 line 172-173 frames the mined-pattern->issue feedback pipeline as the theme's slice. saga:handoff already routes lifecycle artifacts into mission-control prepared drafts, so this extends an existing seam rather than inventing a plugin (no `{#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}` burden).
outcome_shape: PR wiring retro's recurring-pattern output to a mission-control prepared-issue draft via the existing handoff route (edits under plugins/saga/skills/retro + handoff references); verified by a pattern fixture producing a draft issue body that passes mission-control card_validator.

title: Mined-session ledger — remove blind re-mining and make the dark zone countable
idea: Session mining has no idempotency ledger, so every run re-mines everything and there is no record of which sessions were covered — the '219 codex sessions dark' figure is only knowable by a one-off manual count. Borrow the exact idempotency pattern promotion already uses (the promote-keys ledger + parse_ledger) and give mining a mined-session ledger keyed on session id/hash: a run skips already-mined sessions, mines only the delta, and reports the unmined count (Claude + codex) as a standing coverage metric. This removes redundant re-mining work and makes the gap self-reporting instead of requiring an operator to go find it. The best version of 'figure out what still needs mining' is a ledger that already knows.
basis: promote_scan.py:202 `parse_ledger` and :74 the promote-keys ledger regex are a proven drift-stable idempotency pattern for exactly this shape; grounding brief line 115 shows mining has no such accounting ('219 codex sessions ... with no mining substrate'), so coverage is only knowable by manual count.
outcome_shape: PR adding a mined-session ledger + delta-skip and an unmined-count report to saga retro's mining backbone (reusing the promote-keys ledger idiom); verified by running the pass twice and observing the second run mines 0 new sessions while reporting the standing unmined count.

title: Codex substrate adapter — un-drop the handler that was deliberately removed
idea: extract_session_skeleton.py's docstring states 'The Codex and Cursor handlers (and their platform auto-detect / dispatch branches) are dropped — this plugin only mines Claude Code sessions.' That sentence is the assumption to break: 'mineable substrate = Claude transcripts under ~/.claude/projects' is a port-time convenience choice, not a fact of the domain, and it renders 219 codex sessions in a 60-day window completely dark. Restore a codex-session discovery+skeleton path as a registry-style substrate adapter: discover_sessions.py gains a --substrate {claude,codex} selector globbing ~/.codex/sessions, and extract_session_skeleton.py regains a codex JSONL shape handler behind the same file-mediated body-out-of-context contract. This is read-only mining of dark transcripts, not letting codex adjudicate anything — it stays clear of {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} because codex is a data source here, never a verifier.
basis: extract_session_skeleton.py:5-7 'The Codex and Cursor handlers ... are dropped — this plugin only mines Claude Code sessions'; discover_sessions.py:35,83 globs ~/.claude/projects only; grounding brief §7 '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate.'

title: Mine merged PR review threads as an already-durable, already-cross-repo substrate
idea: Session mining assumes the substrate is ephemeral local transcripts that must be caught inside a 60-day mtime window before they age out. Reframe one level up: the highest-signal learning substrate is already durable, server-side, and repo-tagged — merged PR review threads, especially team-execution consensus reviews that caught defects green suites missed (operator-praised in 2 independent repos). A gh-driven miner pulls resolved review comments across workspace repos and distills the 'reviewer caught X that tests didn't' pattern into journal-candidate findings, with zero dependency on a session file still existing on disk. This sidesteps the whole recency-cap fragility (discover_sessions caps at 5, newest-first) by mining a substrate that never expires.
basis: grounding brief §3.2 'team-execution consensus review catching defects green suites missed (2 independent repos, operator-praised)'; discover_sessions.py:35 MAX_CANDIDATES=5 recency-only cap shows the transcript substrate is lossy.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/mine_review_threads.py (gh API pull of resolved review comments, repo-tagged, distilled to findings JSON) plus a retro-passes.md reference for the new substrate; verified by running it over a repo with a known reviewer-caught defect and confirming that finding surfaces.

title: Flip promotion from opt-in marker to opt-out nomination ledger
idea: The promote loop has never fired, and the root friction is an opt-in default: promotion depends on a '**Transcendent.**' marker that /retro's gated single-repo Pass 5 must write and nobody ever does, while the deterministic recurrence floor requires *identical normalized wording* across repos — which real lessons never have because each repo phrases them differently. So the deterministic floor is chronically empty and the pass collapses to 'a human remembers to mark, then a human remembers to run /promote.' Reframe: make recurrence opt-out. promote_scan.py gains a persisted cross-repo nomination ledger where every ≥2-repo near-duplicate cluster (folded by a cheap-tier judgment pass, not exact-hash) is auto-enqueued as a standing nominee that survives across runs, so /promote becomes 'triage a pre-populated queue' instead of 'scan 19 repos cold and hope the marker exists.' The propose-diff-and-wait write gate and self-feed guards stay exactly as-is — only the nomination default inverts.
basis: promote/SKILL.md Phase 2 'The script clusters *exact* recurrences (identical normalized wording)' + 'Declared ... a human or /retro already vouched for it'; §8.10 + §3.5 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted ... The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.'
outcome_shape: PR to plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py adding a persisted nomination ledger + cheap-judgment near-dup fold, and a promote/SKILL.md Phase edit describing queue-triage; verified by a scan over the current 19 repos producing a non-empty nomination queue where today it produces zero.

title: Promotion as a derive-on-read view, not a copy-between-journals batch
idea: The deepest fixed assumption behind the never-firing promote loop is architectural: knowledge is sharded into ~19 per-repo LEARNINGS.md files and 'promotion' is a physical copy operation into a 20th journal, gated behind context-library being cloned and an operator running a manual pass. Reframe one level up and align with this repo's own recurring rejected-alternative signal ('derive-on-read over committed state'): treat the org-wide learning corpus as a single query surface computed on demand from the per-repo journals' Transcendent markers + recurrence clusters, rather than a materialized copy that must be kept idempotent via a promote-keys ledger. Promotion stops being a write event that never happens and becomes a `/promote --view` render that is always current, with the physical upsert reserved only for the truly frozen org-standard subset. This attacks the copy-is-the-unit default that makes the loop expensive-to-fire.
basis: grounding brief §6.5 'Derive-on-read over committed state — recurring rejected alternative' and §2 /outcome campaign 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields'; promote/SKILL.md Phase 4 idempotency-via-promote-keys ledger is the committed-copy machinery this reframes.
outcome_shape: A DECISIONS.md entry proposing derive-on-read promotion plus a PR adding promote_scan.py 'view' subcommand that renders the current cross-repo transcendent corpus without writing; verified by the view reflecting a freshly-marked learning with no upsert step.

title: Extend the source-stale provenance status from delegated outputs to standing docs
idea: provenance_manifest.py already models a ClaimProvenance record with a 'source-stale' status and a producer-claimed-vs-Claude-adjudicated split — but it is scoped entirely to per-execution delegated-output envelopes (saga.manifest.v1). The unexamined assumption is that standing documents (CLAUDE.md, agent memory, SKILL claims) are trusted-until-caught-by-luck, which is exactly the 2-repo mined pattern 'stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by operator recall.' Reframe the ownership boundary: durable-doc factual claims about system state carry a lightweight provenance stamp (verified-date + cited file:line anchor), and a lint reuses the existing source-stale vocabulary to flag any stamped claim whose anchor has moved/vanished or whose date exceeds a threshold. Provenance discipline stops being a human memory game and becomes a structurally detectable staleness signal, using the schema the fleet already ships.
basis: provenance_manifest.py:15-25 docstring 'ClaimProvenance — source-attributed claims ... producer-claimed vs Claude-adjudicated' + 'source-stale' status, scoped to delegated-output envelopes only; grounding brief §7.7 + §6.2 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by operator recall.'
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/provenance_lint.py (parses claim stamps in CLAUDE.md/SKILL docs, reports source-stale using provenance_manifest vocab) wired into a CI check or PreCommit hook; verified by seeding a claim with a moved anchor and confirming the lint flags it stale.

title: Replace human-memory cadence with a cost-bounded scheduled nomination digest
idea: /retro and /promote are on-demand skills — the implicit assumption is 'the operator triggers mining when they remember to,' which is precisely why the promote loop has fired zero times. Reframe: that is a cadence choice, not a law. journal_nudge_hook.py already proves the fleet accepts event-driven, non-blocking, cross-repo-safe automation. Stand up a scheduled cloud routine (cron/schedule) that runs a strictly cost-bounded cross-repo mining + promote-nomination pass on cadence — capped session count per repo, cheap tier, cache-first — and emits ONLY a nomination digest (never a write). This matches the intake's unattended→cache-tight-serial posture (tension 1): unattended runs may proceed silently precisely because they only produce a read-only digest, and any spend-increasing escalation stays gated. Cadence moves from 'never' to 'weekly, bounded, silent.'
basis: journal_nudge_hook.py:1-20 'PostToolUse hook ... NON-blocking ... Cross-repo-safe' proves event-driven fleet automation is accepted; intake brief tension 1 'Unattended runs → cache-tight serial; may proceed silently'; §3.5 promote never fired.
outcome_shape: A committed schedule/cron routine config plus plugins/saga/scripts/mine_digest.py (bounded session cap, cheap-tier, emits digest JSON, zero writes); verified by one scheduled run producing a nomination digest artifact within a declared token budget.

title: Auto-materialize mined recurring patterns into a draft backlog feed retro drains
idea: retro/SKILL.md is explicit that 'Surfaced follow-ups become a /handoff (new issue) or a QUEUED.md entry — /retro routes them, it does not file them.' That not-file boundary is the assumption to break: it means every mining→issue conversion is a bespoke heroic session (like this very 80-agent one) rather than a standing pipeline. The promote layer exists to close this loop for transcendent *learnings*, but nothing closes it for actionable *defects/enhancements* that recur across repos. Reframe the ownership boundary: retro's recurring-pattern output (≥N repos) auto-writes structured *draft* candidates into a durable cross-repo feed that mission-control:issue drains under the existing Gate, turning a once-per-quarter human ritual into a continuously-fed backlog. The human gate stays (drafts, not filed issues); only the manual transcription step is removed.
basis: retro/SKILL.md 'Surfaced follow-ups become a /handoff (new issue) or a QUEUED.md entry — /retro routes them, it does not file them'; grounding brief §7 lists 10 recurring cross-repo patterns produced by mining but no standing conversion path.
outcome_shape: PR adding a retro pattern-emit step writing structured draft candidates to a cross-repo feed file + a mission-control drain command that reads it; verified by a mining pass depositing a draft candidate that mission-control:issue then materializes behind its gate.

title: Closed-loop retirement — a merged fix must silence its originating pattern
idea: The mining→issue pipeline is assumed one-directional: patterns flow out, issues get filed, done. But nothing flows back, so the next mining run re-surfaces the same pattern (or the same stale claim) that a merged PR already resolved — pure re-work, and a provenance lie by omission. retro already 'diffs against the last retro so knowledge accumulates instead of repeating'; reframe that single-thread idea one level up into a cross-repo closed loop: when an issue born from a mined pattern reaches merged/closed, the originating journal finding or stale-claim record is auto-annotated as resolved (with the resolving PR as evidence) so subsequent mining passes de-prioritize or retire it. This makes provenance self-healing — the corpus records not just what was learned but what has since been fixed — and prevents the feedback pipeline from becoming a treadmill.
basis: First-principles: mining is stateless across runs (discover_sessions.py re-globs a raw mtime window every time with no memory of prior outputs), so any pattern that produced an issue last run re-appears this run until independently re-verified; retro's own 'diffs against the last retro' compounding principle (retro/SKILL.md core principle 1) is exactly this loop but scoped to one thread — generalizing it cross-repo is the missing back-edge that stops the pipeline repeating resolved work.
outcome_shape: PR adding a resolution back-annotation step (issue merged → mark originating finding resolved with PR evidence) plus a mining filter that de-ranks resolved findings; verified by a resolved-pattern issue causing its finding to be skipped/flagged on the next mining pass.

title: promote_scan diagnose: make the zero-promotion friction visible before fixing it
idea: The promote loop has fired zero times, but no one can name WHY from a current source — is the candidate pool empty, are there Transcendent markers nobody clustered, or does the exact-recurrence floor swallow every paraphrased match? Add a `promote_scan.py diagnose` subcommand that reports fleet-wide counts: total repos scanned, `**Transcendent.**` markers found, legacy `**Generalizable rule.**` lines, exact-recurrence clusters at threshold, and near-miss clusters one repo below threshold. Commit its output as a dated baseline doc so every later activation idea measures against a real number instead of a guess. This is the cheapest compounding move: it turns an untestable 'never fired' into an instrumented, re-runnable metric that all other T10 promotion work targets.
basis: grounding brief line 72 '0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster'; promote_scan.py READ backbone (U3) already parses the marker, the generalizable-rule variants, and groups exact-recurrence clusters at DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=2 — a diagnose mode reuses that exact parse path with no new contract surface.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py (new `diagnose` subcommand) + tests/test_promote_scan.py + a committed docs/engineering-journal/ baseline report; verified by running `promote_scan.py diagnose --workspace-root ~/workspace/infiquetra` and reading the actual fleet counts it prints.

title: Scheduled read-only promote-scan digest — a standing prompt for a pass nobody invokes
idea: The single biggest reason promote has never fired is nobody runs it: it is purely on-demand with no trigger, no cadence, no standing signal. Wire a cost-bounded weekly cron (via the schedule/cron primitive) that runs `promote_scan.py scan --json` read-only, and if candidate clusters exist, opens or upserts ONE standing GitHub issue in infiquetra-context-library listing the clusters awaiting the gated /promote pass. It writes zero journal entries — the propose-diff-and-wait promotion gate stays fully intact — it only manufactures the missing recurring prompt. The compounding payoff: a manual pass that fired zero times in the fleet's lifetime becomes a self-refreshing backlog item, and the same digest scaffold generalizes to any other gated-but-uninvoked workspace pass.
basis: promote/SKILL.md establishes promote as a 'manual, gated, agent-judged workspace pass' triggered only by an operator saying 'promote'; grounding brief line 72-73 confirms the loop 'exists but never fired'. First principles: a gate that requires human invocation, with no scheduled or event-driven prompt, has expected invocation rate approaching zero — restoring cadence without touching the write gate is the minimal fix. Engages {#outcome}-style reversibility: the digest writes only a reversible GitHub issue (mission-control owns SDLC), never a journal, so the KTD6 propose-diff-and-wait promotion gate is untouched.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/promote_digest.py (wraps scan, emits an idempotent issue body) + a cron/schedule config entry + tests; verified by a dry-run that prints the issue body from live scan output and a re-run showing idempotent upsert (no duplicate issue).

title: Session-substrate registry — light up 219 dark codex sessions and every future engine with one seam
idea: 219 codex sessions in the 60-day window have no mining substrate — completely dark to /retro's session mining, which only reads Claude transcripts. Rather than a one-off codex reader, introduce a session-substrate registry (mirroring the engine-registry seam the intake brief chose for provider routing): each agent runtime is a registry entry plus a small adapter that normalizes its native session logs into the same skeleton format the wf_7e5d77a2-5c0 workflow already consumed. Ship codex as the first non-Claude entry to prove the seam. The second-order win: antigravity/agy and any future runtime become a registry entry, not a retro-code change, so mining coverage compounds instead of being re-litigated per engine.
basis: grounding brief line 115 '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10'; brief line 113 shows the existing mining path distilled 70 Claude skeletons. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): mining codex transcripts is read-only data extraction with Claude doing all downstream judgment — codex is not a verifier or gatekeeper of any decision, so the decision's structural enforcement is preserved.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/session_substrates.py (registry + Claude and codex adapters) wired into the retro mining path, plus a references/session-substrates.md doc; verified by running it against the codex session directory and emitting N>0 normalized skeletons matching the existing format.

title: Mining-harvest writeback — stop letting 175 mined findings evaporate into a workflow journal
idea: The session-mining run produced 175 findings and 10 recurring patterns, but they live only in a one-off workflow journal (wf_7e5d77a2-5c0); none flowed back into any repo's durable LEARNINGS.md, so the promote layer that feeds on LEARNINGS never even sees them. Add a gated mining-harvest writeback: findings recurring above a repo-spread threshold auto-draft a LEARNINGS.md entry (with Evidence = session ids + repo list, Mechanism, and a Generalizable rule stub) behind propose-diff-and-wait, in the repo where the pattern concentrates. This closes the loop mining->journal->promote so mined signal becomes promotion fuel instead of dying in a scratch artifact. Compounding: every future mining run now deposits durable, promotable substrate automatically rather than requiring a human to retype findings.
basis: grounding brief lines 111-116: 70/70 skeletons distilled, 27 sessions yielded 175 findings -> 10 patterns, 'per-agent detail in workflow journal' — i.e. findings terminate in a transient workflow journal, not durable LEARNINGS. promote_scan.py enumerates only */docs/engineering-journal/LEARNINGS.md, so anything not landed there is invisible to promotion. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: writeback is gated propose-diff-and-wait with Claude authoring, no engine gatekeeps.
outcome_shape: PR adding a harvest-writeback step to plugins/saga/skills/retro (or a scripts/mining_harvest.py) that emits gated LEARNINGS.md draft entries from a mining-findings payload, plus references doc + test fixture; verified by feeding the 10-pattern payload and producing valid, Evidence-stamped draft entries that promote_scan then detects.

title: Claim-freshness linter — flag stale CLAUDE.md / memory assertions before an operator's memory has to
idea: Stale memory and doc claims are asserted as fact and caught only by operator recall or a lucky re-verification — a 4-session, 2-repo pattern. Build a `check_claims.py` linter that scans CLAUDE.md and auto-memory for factual assertions carrying resolvable anchors (file:line references, `plugin X.Y.Z` versions, named enums) and flags any whose anchor no longer resolves or whose version has drifted from plugin.json. Wire it as a pre-commit/CI check so a claim rots loudly instead of silently. This is deliberately broader than the direct-to-candidate evidence-artifact-immutability item (which guards probe outputs): it guards the standing-instruction and memory surface that agents treat as ground truth. Compounding: every future doc claim inherits a re-verification harness, so provenance discipline scales without operator vigilance.
basis: grounding brief lines 135-136 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification (2 repos)' and brief line 105 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state (4 learnings)'. Distinct from direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' (brief line 187), which covers probe FAIL/PASS chain-of-custody, not standing-doc/memory claim anchors.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/check_claims.py + hook/CI wiring + tests; verified by seeding a CLAUDE.md line citing a non-existent file:line and a drifted plugin version and showing the linter flags both, then passes after correction.

title: Promote-ledger backlink drift guard — make promoted org standards self-auditing in CI
idea: Promotion is keyed on a drift-stable source-key ledger (`<!-- promote-keys: ... -->`) in context-library, but nothing verifies those backlinks still resolve: a promoted org standard can outlive the source LEARNINGS entry it distilled, leaving the library asserting provenance that no longer exists. Extend context-library's existing check_docs.py (which already runs promotion-ledger checks in validate.yml) to validate that every promote-key still resolves to a live journal entry in its origin repo, warning on orphans. This binds provenance discipline directly onto the promote surface, so as promotion finally starts firing (ideas 1-2), it fires onto a self-auditing ledger instead of accumulating silent drift. Compounding: the guard makes every future promotion trustworthy by construction.
basis: grounding brief lines 77-79 'validate.yml CI runs check_docs.py ... + promotion-ledger checks'; promote/SKILL.md core principle 3 'idempotent upsert keyed on the drift-stable source-key ledger each entry carries'. The ledger check today confirms keys are present (dedup), not that their source anchors still resolve — that is the provenance gap this closes.
outcome_shape: Cross-repo PR to infiquetra-context-library extending check_docs.py with a promote-key backlink resolver + a test fixture with a deliberately orphaned key; verified by CI going red on the orphan and green once the key is reconciled.

title: Mined-pattern -> prepared-issue emitter — institutionalize the exact move this session performs
idea: This very session is the pattern: a mined recurring finding becomes a backlog issue/spec. But /retro today 'routes follow-ups to /handoff or QUEUED, does not file them' — the mining-evidence-to-issue step is manual retyping, which is precisely where the loop dies (219 dark sessions, 175 findings, zero issues auto-filed). Add a structured emitter that turns a mined pattern above a repo-spread threshold into a mission-control prepared-issue draft, carrying the mining evidence (repo list, session ids, finding count) as the issue's source-artifact so provenance travels with the work. Compounding: the fleet gains a standing mining->backlog conveyor, so future mining runs continuously fund the backlog instead of requiring a bespoke ideation campaign like this one.
basis: retro/SKILL.md: 'Surfaced follow-ups become /handoff (new issue) or QUEUED.md entry — /retro routes them, does not file them'; saga:handoff skill exists ('Route durable Infiquetra lifecycle artifacts into mission-control prepared issue drafts'). Existence proof: this ideation campaign is the manual instance of exactly this conveyor (intake brief describes mined-pattern -> gated GitHub-issue materialization).
outcome_shape: PR adding a mining-pattern -> handoff payload emitter in plugins/saga/skills/retro (or scripts/mining_to_handoff.py) that produces a mission-control:issue-compatible prepared draft with source-artifact provenance fields; verified by feeding a mined pattern and generating a draft that passes mission-control's card_validator.

title: Continuous transcendence declaration — accrue promotion candidates as a byproduct of normal journaling
idea: The declare feeder is dead because `**Transcendent.**` marking lives only in /retro Pass 5, a separate gated pass that rarely runs — so candidates never accrue and the recurrence net has nothing to cluster. Lower the activation energy: let any LEARNINGS.md entry self-declare transcendence inline at write-time, riding the always-on in-commit journal-capture rule the repo already mandates, via the same marker promote_scan already parses. A learning that an author judges org-wide gets marked the moment it is written, not months later in a pass nobody reaches. Add a lightweight journal-convention guard so the marker stays well-formed. Compounding: promotion candidates accumulate continuously as a free side effect of disciplined journaling, converting a rare gated event into an always-on stream.
basis: promote/SKILL.md 'Declare — /retro (or a human) marks a transcendent learning ... a local gated edit (retro-passes.md, Pass 5)'; CLAUDE.md always-on rule 'in the same commit that ships the change ... a dated LEARNINGS.md entry'. promote_scan.py already detects the marker at line-start regardless of who wrote it, so inline declaration needs no contract change — only guidance + a guard. Distinct from QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} (release-metadata drift), this guards journal-marker well-formedness.
outcome_shape: PR touching the engineering-journal practice doc + plugins/saga/skills/promote/references/promotion-contract.md (inline-declaration guidance) + a journal-marker guard test; verified by a test asserting an inline-marked LEARNINGS entry is picked up by promote_scan without a /retro pass.

title: Multi-instrument session federation: a codex-session substrate adapter
idea: The mining pipeline reads only Claude session skeletons, leaving 219 in-window codex sessions completely dark. Model this the way a multi-instrument astronomical survey federates optical, radio, and infrared telescopes: each instrument writes a native format, but a per-instrument adapter normalizes every observation into one shared calibration frame before science runs. Add a substrate-adapter registry (one entry per engine: claude, codex, and a stub for agy) that reads each engine's native session store and emits a normalized skeleton conforming to a single observation schema, so /retro and promote_scan consume all engines identically. The adapter for codex is the first non-Claude instrument to come online. This unlocks the dark 60-day codex corpus without the miner needing to know engine-specific formats.
basis: Grounding brief line 115: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10.' Source domain (F5): multi-instrument astronomical survey federation, where a per-instrument adapter normalizes native formats to one common calibration/coordinate frame so downstream science is instrument-agnostic — the structural analog to an engine-agnostic session-skeleton schema.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/session_substrate/ with an adapter registry (base interface + codex_adapter.py) and a normalized-skeleton JSON schema, wired into the mining workflow; verified by running the codex adapter over the in-window codex session store and asserting N>0 normalized skeletons emitted matching the schema, with a unit test fixture.

title: Bill-of-lading manifest: every mined session carries a chain-of-custody header
idea: Mined findings enter synthesis as free-floating text with no durable record of which engine, repo, session id, time window, or miner-tier produced them, so provenance is reconstructed by guesswork later. In freight logistics, no container moves without a bill of lading: a manifest that travels with the cargo naming origin, contents, handler, and timestamps, so custody is auditable at every transfer. Emit an analogous per-session mining manifest (engine, repo, session-id, window, miner model/effort, skeleton hash, extraction timestamp) that is attached to every finding and carried unbroken through synthesis into any downstream issue or promotion. Findings without a valid manifest are rejected at synthesis, exactly as unmanifested cargo is refused at the dock. This makes every mined claim traceable back to its exact source session.
basis: First-principles: the mining workflow (grounding line 113-114, 175 findings from 70 skeletons) produces findings but records per-agent detail only in an ephemeral workflow journal; once synthesized, a finding cannot be traced to its origin session for re-verification, which is precisely the substrate that lets stale claims (line 135-136) go unchecked. Source domain (F5): freight logistics bill-of-lading / manifest discipline — cargo without a manifest is refused at transfer, giving unbroken auditable custody; applied here, findings without a source manifest are refused at synthesis.
outcome_shape: PR adding a mining-manifest schema (JSON) plus emit/validate helpers under plugins/saga/scripts/, referenced by the /retro synthesis step, with a validation test asserting a manifest-less finding is rejected and a valid one round-trips engine+repo+session-id+hash.

title: Hippocampal replay: overnight pre-staging of ranked promotion candidates
idea: The /promote loop has never fired because it is a manual workspace pass that starts from a blank cursor — the human must hunt the whole cross-repo journal corpus before judging anything, which is high activation energy nobody pays. Mammalian memory consolidation solves the same problem differently: the hippocampus replays the day's salient traces during sleep and only the patterns that recur across replays get consolidated into neocortex, so the waking system inherits pre-selected candidates rather than re-deriving them. Add a cheap cadence-driven pre-staging pass that runs promote_scan, clusters recurring learnings across repos, ranks by repo-spread and recurrence, and writes a durable ranked candidate ledger. The human /promote pass then becomes a yes/no on a pre-ranked shortlist, not a cold hunt. Lowering activation energy is the whole point: the gate stays human, the search stops being human.
basis: Source domain (F5): neuroscience systems-consolidation / hippocampal replay (documented in the sleep-and-memory literature, e.g. Wilson & McNaughton replay findings) — recurring traces are auto-replayed and pre-selected before the slow cortical store commits them, the structural analog to auto-pre-staging recurrent cross-repo learnings before the human commit gate. Supports the fix because grounding line 72 states '0 learnings ever promoted' and the loop 'never fired' — a cold-start manual pass is the friction; pre-staging removes it without touching the human gate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a promote_scan pre-stage subcommand that writes a ranked candidate ledger (docs/engineering-journal/QUEUED-promotions.md or a JSON ledger), plus a /promote skill edit that reads the ledger first; verified by running the pre-stage over the workspace and confirming a non-empty ranked ledger with repo-spread scores.

title: Funnel conversion telemetry: instrument where promotion candidates die
idea: Zero promotions ever is not proof there are no transcendent learnings — it is an uninstrumented funnel with an invisible drop-off, exactly the failure a sales pipeline hits when top-of-funnel leads never convert and nobody can see at which stage they vanish. Revenue teams fix this by instrumenting each stage transition (lead → qualified → staged → won) and surfacing per-stage drop-off so the broken stage is named, not guessed. Instrument the promotion funnel the same way: count learnings captured, learnings clustered ≥N repos, candidates staged, candidates presented to the human, and candidates accepted, and emit the per-stage counts as a small dashboard line in /retro. If the corpus has 175 findings but 0 reach the ≥3-repo cluster stage, the threshold is the culprit; if candidates stage but are never presented, the /promote invocation is the culprit. The telemetry converts 'never fired' from a mystery into a diagnosed stage.
basis: Grounding brief line 72: '0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster' and line 73 'cross-repo learning loop exists but never fired.' Source domain (F5): sales/revenue pipeline conversion instrumentation — per-stage drop-off telemetry names the broken stage instead of leaving a zero-conversion funnel unexplained; applied here to the capture→cluster→stage→present→accept promotion funnel.
outcome_shape: PR adding a promote_scan funnel-metrics mode that prints per-stage counts (captured/clustered/staged/presented/accepted) and a /retro skill line that surfaces them; verified by a test asserting the counts sum consistently on a fixture corpus and the >=3-repo cluster stage reports its actual count.

title: Supply-chain attestation for durable claims: last-verified provenance on memory/CLAUDE.md facts
idea: Stale memory and CLAUDE.md claims get asserted as fact and are caught only by operator recall or a lucky re-verification, a 4-session mined pattern. Software supply chains hit the identical trust problem — a binary asserts it is what it says — and solve it with signed provenance attestations (SLSA / in-toto): every artifact carries a verifiable statement of what produced it and when, and consumers refuse artifacts whose attestation is missing or expired. Apply the same discipline to durable factual claims in CLAUDE.md and journal memory: a lightweight convention where a load-bearing state claim carries an inline provenance tag (source pointer + last-verified date), and a linter flags any tagged claim past a TTL as 'unattested — re-verify before relying.' This does not verify truth automatically; it makes staleness visible and refusable, the way an expired attestation blocks a deploy. Validation discipline stops depending on operator luck.
basis: Source domain (F5): software supply-chain provenance attestation (SLSA framework / in-toto, as implemented in sigstore/cosign and GitHub artifact attestations) — consumers refuse artifacts with missing or expired provenance statements. Named prior art lives in the SLSA spec and in-toto attestation format. Supports the fix because grounding lines 135-136 record 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification' — an expiry-aware attestation tag converts luck into an enforceable TTL check, mirroring the repo's own CLAUDE.md Validation Discipline mandate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a claim-provenance frontmatter/inline convention doc plus a linter script (scripts/) that scans CLAUDE.md and journal files for TTL-expired provenance tags and exits non-zero; verified by a test with a fresh tag (passes) and an expired tag (fails) and one seeded CLAUDE.md claim tagged.

title: Forensic chain-of-custody: append-only, hash-chained evidence ledger for verify runs
idea: A probe script was observed overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS, destroying the audit trail — the digital equivalent of tampering with a sealed evidence bag. Law-enforcement forensics and flight-data recorders both refuse mutable evidence: custody is preserved by append-only, write-once media and a tamper-evident hash chain where each entry seals the previous, so a later result cannot silently replace an earlier one. Generalize beyond the single probe fix into a verify-evidence contract: every verify/QA/deploy run appends its outcome to a hash-chained evidence ledger keyed by run-id, never overwriting a prior artifact, and a reader that finds a broken hash link surfaces tampering. A FAIL followed by a PASS then reads as two sealed, ordered entries — the true history — instead of one overwritten lie. This makes chain-of-custody a fleet property, not a one-file patch.
basis: Grounding brief lines 150-151: 'probe script overwriting FAIL evidence artifact later PASS (audit chain-of-custody).' This idea explicitly builds beyond the direct-to-candidate point fix by making the contract fleet-wide and hash-chained rather than patching one script. Source domain (F5): forensic evidence chain-of-custody plus WORM (write-once-read-many) / tamper-evident hash-chained logging (as in flight-data recorders and append-only audit ledgers) — a later entry can never silently overwrite an earlier sealed one.
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only hash-chained evidence-ledger helper under plugins/saga/scripts/ (append + verify-chain functions) and wiring the QA/verify writer to append instead of overwrite; verified by a test asserting a second write for the same run-id appends a new sealed entry, the chain hash validates, and an overwrite attempt is rejected.

title: Ground-delay flow metering: a cost-bounded mining scheduler under the concurrency cap
idea: Cross-repo session mining is expensive and today runs only as an ad hoc heavy pass, so the corpus goes stale between runs while a full re-mine risks a cost and rate-limit blowout. Air-traffic control faces the same demand-exceeds-capacity problem and does not simply queue everyone: a ground-delay program meters departures to downstream runway capacity, releasing aircraft in cost-bounded waves so the system never saturates. Build a mining flow controller that runs on a schedule, mines only sessions new since the last high-water mark (delta, not full re-mine), releases work in waves sized to a token budget, and holds strictly to the fleet concurrency cap. Unattended scheduled runs default cache-first and silent per the intake posture; any spend-increasing escalation (widening the window, more parallelism) is surfaced, never silently taken. Mining becomes a steady metered flow instead of a saturating flood.
basis: Source domain (F5): air-traffic-control ground-delay / traffic-flow-management programs (FAA TFM) — departures are metered to downstream capacity in cost-bounded waves rather than queued or flooded. Crosses the intake concurrency constraint (max 3 concurrent agents) and the unattended→cache-first posture: the idea explicitly engages them by holding the cap and defaulting scheduled runs to silent cache-first, escalations surfaced — so it complies rather than contradicts. Grounded by the stale-corpus / re-mine-cost tension implied by the 350-450k reconciliation cost number (grounding section 7).
outcome_shape: PR adding a delta-aware, token-budgeted mining scheduler config (cron entry + high-water-mark tracking) that batches to concurrency<=3 and defaults cache-first; verified by a dry-run showing only post-high-water sessions selected, wave sizing honoring the budget, and no batch exceeding 3.

title: Syndromic surveillance: an N-repo mined cluster auto-drafts a mission-control issue
idea: A mined pattern only becomes durable work when a human manually shepherds it into an issue or spec, so most of the 175 findings evaporate — this very session is the rare case where the loop closed by hand. Public-health syndromic surveillance solves the identical signal-to-action gap: individual symptom reports are noise, but when a cluster crosses a case threshold across enough sites, the system auto-generates a notifiable case report that triggers an investigation, no manual transcription. Build a feedback bridge where a mined pattern recurring across >=N repos automatically drafts a prepared mission-control issue (title, evidence pointers back to the source-session manifests, affected-repo list) staged for human approval — never auto-filed, only auto-drafted, preserving the human gate. The threshold is the case definition; the manifests are the line-list evidence. The mining corpus stops being a graveyard and becomes a monitored feed that raises its own tickets.
basis: Source domain (F5): epidemiological syndromic surveillance and notifiable-disease reporting (CDC/WHO systems such as NNDSS) — clustered case counts crossing a defined threshold auto-generate a case report that triggers investigation without manual transcription. Prior art also demonstrated live by this session's own mined-pattern→issue loop (intake brief calls this the feedback-pipeline exemplar). Grounded by grounding lines 113-114 (175 findings → 10 patterns) with no automated path to issues, and pairs with T10-F5-2's manifests as the evidence line-list.
outcome_shape: PR adding a feedback-bridge script that takes clustered mined patterns, filters by >=N-repo spread, and emits prepared mission-control issue drafts (markdown with evidence/manifest pointers) for human approval — not filed; verified by running it over the current mining synthesis and producing at least one draft whose evidence pointers resolve to real source sessions.

title: Break the exact-wording recurrence floor with lexical candidate clustering
idea: Flip the /promote 'sparing, never a harvest' constraint to its extreme opposite — promote all 899 accumulated rules — and mine the kernel from why that flip is absurd: the loop has fired ZERO times not from over-caution but because the deterministic recurrence floor (promote/SKILL.md:92) demands *identical normalized wording* across repos, which 899 independently-authored rules never satisfy, so the judgment layer that could fold near-duplicates never receives a single cluster. Add a `promote_scan.py cluster-candidates` mode that shingles every rule into cheap keyword-Jaccard similarity buckets (staying lexical — no embeddings, honoring KTD5 'judgment not vectors') and emits bucketed candidate groups for the Opus fold-and-split judgment pass. Rewrite promote SKILL Phase 1-2 to consume buckets instead of exact clusters. The point is to make a real >=2-repo transcendent cluster *surfaceable at all*, which today it structurally is not.
basis: grep across ~/workspace/infiquetra: 0 `**Transcendent.**` markers in any `*/docs/engineering-journal/LEARNINGS.md`, 899 `**Generalizable rule.**` lines, and 0 `promote-keys` entries in infiquetra-context-library/LEARNINGS.md — so the exact-recurrence floor at promote/SKILL.md:92 has never produced a cluster and nothing has ever been promoted. Stays lexical to satisfy KTD5 (promote/SKILL.md:46).
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py (new cluster-candidates subcommand) + plugins/saga/skills/promote/SKILL.md Phase 1-2; verified by running the scan over the live workspace and observing >=1 non-empty >=2-repo candidate bucket where the exact floor returns zero.

title: Make transcendence-marking a lifecycle byproduct, not a rare /retro Pass 5
idea: Flip 'one declare source' to the extreme 'every session declares' — that extreme is pure noise, but the kernel is real: the declare feeder produces 0 markers because it lives only in /retro Pass 5 (promote/SKILL.md:24-28), a pass rarely run to completion, so a cross-repo lesson is never marked at the moment it is actually felt (during /work or /code-review). Move the mark to the point of capture: extend the always-on journal-capture rule so that when /work or /code-review appends a LEARNINGS entry whose Mechanism is stack-agnostic, it emits a one-line `**Transcendent.**` self-assessment inline, and add a journal_triggers.py check that flags stack-agnostic entries missing the marker as promote-run candidates. This converts marking from a deferred harvest chore into a cheap per-entry reflex.
basis: 0 `**Transcendent.**` markers exist across all workspace journals despite 899 generalizable rules, and promote/SKILL.md:24-28 names /retro Pass 5 as the sole declare feeder — a pass that has never emitted a marker. journal_triggers.py (1000B) already exists as the capture-reflex hook to extend.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/journal_triggers.py (stack-agnostic-without-marker check), plugins/saga/skills/retro/references/retro-passes.md, and the repo CLAUDE.md capture rule; verified by a fresh stack-agnostic LEARNINGS entry surfacing the marker prompt and the trigger flagging an unmarked one.

title: Codex-session dark-substrate bridge into the existing skeleton pipeline
idea: Flip 'mine only the engine we own' to 'mine 100% of every engine's sessions': there are 509 codex JSONL rollouts on disk (219 in the 60-day window) completely dark while 2639 Claude sessions feed /retro. The kernel that survives the flip: discover_sessions.py + extract_session_skeleton.py already normalize Claude session JSONL into a skeleton envelope — codex writes its own JSONL rollout format under ~/.codex, structurally the same shape. Add a codex-format adapter to discover_sessions.py that maps ~/.codex/*.jsonl into the same skeleton envelope extract_session_skeleton consumes, so /retro's mining substrate covers both engines with one distiller. Deliberately NOT a new plugin — engaging {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}, this rides saga's existing discovery scripts, adding zero portfolio surface.
basis: `find ~/.codex -name '*.jsonl'` returns 509 files; grounding brief §7 states '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10.' extract_session_skeleton.py (8.8K) + discover_sessions.py (4.0K) already exist as the Claude-only pipeline to extend. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by extending, not adding, a plugin.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/discover_sessions.py + extract_session_skeleton.py with a codex-rollout fixture and a round-trip test; verified by the scan emitting >=1 codex-origin skeleton in the same envelope shape as a Claude skeleton.

title: Dual-engine adversarial session mining with Claude-reconciled diff
idea: Flip 'one miner' to 'a hundred independent miners' — the practical distillation is two: run Claude and codex as independent miners over the *same* session skeletons and diff their syntheses, because a single miner's blind spots are exactly the transcendent patterns that stay unmined. Extend /retro's session-mining step to optionally dispatch a codex second-miner over the identical skeleton set produced by extract_session_skeleton, then have Claude reconcile the two synthesis sets — converging findings gain confidence, divergent ones are surfaced for judgment. This is chaperone dispatch (codex = second-opinion offload, advisory only), so Claude remains verifier-of-record and never-gatekeepers is preserved. Prior art: this exact pattern already fired once by hand at 15/17 convergence.
basis: grounding brief §7 singleton: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art).' Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) by routing codex as second-opinion offload, advisory-only, with Claude reconciling — never a second executor or gatekeeper.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/skills/retro/references/retro-passes.md (session-mining pass) + plugins/team-execution references/external-engine-workers.md; verified by a reconciled-diff artifact over one real window showing converging vs divergent findings with the codex miner tagged advisory.

title: Claim-freshness receipts and a CI stale-claim linter on durable memory
idea: Flip 'verify every claim before every assertion' (100% verification tax) against '$0, never verify' — both extremes are wrong, and the kernel between them is that durable factual claims (counts, file:line refs, 'X has never happened') should carry an inline verification receipt so staleness is detectable without re-verifying everything continuously. Add a `claim_freshness.py` lint that scans CLAUDE.md and journal surfaces for claims stamped `<!-- verified: <date> via <probe> -->`, fails CI when a cited file:line has drifted or a stamp exceeds a TTL, and reports unstamped hard claims. This operationalizes the repo's own Validation Discipline ('never assert without checking') as machinery instead of hoping the operator remembers.
basis: grounding brief §6 item 2: 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state (4 learnings)' and §7 pattern 7: 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification (2 repos).' provenance_manifest.py (17.9K) exists as an adjacent provenance surface.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/claim_freshness.py + CI wiring + verification stamps on the fleet-map count claims; verified by CI going red when a stamped claim's cited file:line is deliberately drifted or its stamp aged past TTL.

title: Durable lineage records so every mined pattern is re-verifiable to source
idea: Flip 'every mined pattern is trusted as self-evident fact' to 'nothing is trusted without its chain' — the mining run that produced this backlog turned 175 findings into 10 patterns, but the per-agent lineage lives in an ephemeral workflow journal, so a claim like 'promote loop never fired' becomes a durable fact with no re-openable trail back to the source skeletons. The kernel: extend provenance_manifest.py to stamp each promoted mined pattern with the source session IDs plus skeleton content hashes it was distilled from, so any later reader can re-open the exact evidence and re-run the check. Distinct from evidence-artifact immutability (that guards against overwriting a FAIL with a PASS); this captures *lineage* at distill time so a pattern is never a bare assertion.
basis: grounding brief §7: '70/70 skeletons distilled... 27 sessions yielded 175 findings -> 10 recurring patterns... Per-agent detail in the workflow journal' — the lineage lives only in an ephemeral workflow journal, and §6 item 2 records provenance re-verification as recurring pain. provenance_manifest.py (17.9K) is the existing surface to extend.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/provenance_manifest.py adding a mined-pattern lineage record (source session IDs + skeleton hashes); verified by round-tripping one distilled pattern back to its exact source skeleton set from the durable manifest alone.

title: Nightly cost-bounded watermarked mine-and-nominate that never writes
idea: Flip 'on-demand, manually invoked' against 'fully autonomous, runs forever unattended' — /promote has fired zero times precisely because it depends on a manual invocation that never happens, yet the propose-diff-and-wait gate binding forbids autonomous *writes*. The kernel splits the two: nomination-accumulation is reversible and can run unattended; only the context-library write is irreversible and gated. Add a `--nominate-only` watermarked mode to promote_scan.py that a scheduled nightly routine (CronCreate) runs cost-bounded over sessions since the last watermark, appending to a standing PROMOTION-CANDIDATES.md — accruing nominations continuously so the eventual gated write starts warm instead of cold. This keeps KTD6 propose-diff-and-wait fully intact (nomination != write) and matches the intake's unattended->cache-first, reversible-proceeds-silently posture.
basis: 0 promote-keys entries in infiquetra-context-library confirms /promote has never completed, and promote/SKILL.md is entirely manual-invocation-driven with no cadence trigger. Engages KTD6 (promote/SKILL.md:38-40) by keeping every context-library write gated and only accruing reversible nominations unattended — consistent with intake §3 'everything reversible proceeds without asking.'
outcome_shape: PR adding a `--nominate-only` watermarked mode to plugins/saga/scripts/promote_scan.py + a scheduled routine config + a standing PROMOTION-CANDIDATES.md; verified by two consecutive nightly runs accruing distinct nominations under a bounded token budget with zero context-library writes.

title: Durable /mine-to-backlog harness so pattern-to-issue stops being a one-off
idea: Flip 'every mined pattern self-executes straight into a GitHub issue' (fully autonomous materialization) against '0 — patterns die inside a report' — the autonomous extreme violates the Gate E/F human-approval binding, but the kernel is sharp: this very ideation session ran pattern->theme->idea->candidate as bespoke one-off orchestration, and a loop that only exists as hand-built briefs decays into forgotten process (the exact QUEUED.md decay rationale). Build a re-runnable saga command `/mine-to-backlog` that takes a mining synthesis report and emits mission-control-ready issue drafts, halting at Gate E — never writing GitHub — so the monthly pattern-to-backlog transform is machinery, not a memory. A saga command extension, not a new plugin, engaging {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}.
basis: First-principles: this session materialized pattern->candidate via ad hoc intake/grounding briefs (one-off docs, not a re-runnable harness). QUEUED.md's own preamble states undocumented good ideas decay into forgotten good ideas; by identical logic an undocumented *process* decays into an unrepeatable one. An outcome-generating loop meant to run each retro cycle must be encoded as a command or it will not fire twice — the same failure mode as /promote's zero firings. Intake mandates all GitHub writes occur only after Gate E/F, so the harness halts at draft, preserving the binding.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/mine-to-backlog/ (command + reference) that consumes a synthesis report and emits mission-control:issue-ready drafts stopping at Gate E; verified by regenerating this session's candidate pool from its synthesis report with no GitHub writes.

title: Scored agent-prompt quality rubric + linter across the fleet
idea: The 34 agent files on disk (the brief's ~55 fleet-wide) are guarded only structurally: test_agent_registration_drift.py checks that frontmatter `name:` matches the file stem, nothing about prompt quality. Quality is wildly uneven — security-reviewer.md carries an explicit `NOT for:` boundary and negative-scope clause while others ship a bare description. Define a written rubric (role boundary present, at least one `Do NOT use / NOT for` clause, trigger examples, model-choice justification, least-privilege tool declaration) as docs/reference plus scripts/audit_agent_prompts.py that scores every agents/*.md against it and emits a ranked deficiency report. Wire it as an advisory (non-blocking) CI job first, then ratchet the passing bar per plugin. The annoyance being killed: no maintainer today can see which of ~55 prompts are underspecified without opening all of them.
basis: plugins/team-execution/agents/security-reviewer.md frontmatter carries `NOT for: code quality concerns; architecture patterns; test coverage` while plugins/mission-control/agents/sdlc-operator.md and most others carry none; tests/test_agent_registration_drift.py docstring states it guards name==stem discoverability only, explicitly not quality. 34 agent files enumerated under plugins/*/agents/.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/audit_agent_prompts.py + docs/engineering-journal or a plugins/*/references rubric doc + an advisory `agent-prompt-audit` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml; verified by running the script over all agents/*.md and by a meta-test asserting a synthetic under-specified agent is flagged.

title: Least-privilege tool-scope guard for review/verify-class agents
idea: readonly-verifier.md explicitly pins `tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob` precisely so a verifier cannot Edit/Write and clobber the tree — but security-reviewer.md and the other ~20 team-execution reviewer/tester agents omit `tools:` entirely, which inherits the full tool set including Edit/Write. A reviewer that can silently mutate code contradicts the verifier-of-record posture. Add a lint that classifies each agent by name/description as review-class, verify-class, or executor-class, and fails (or warns) when a non-executor agent lacks an explicit least-privilege `tools:` list excluding Edit/Write. Ship a companion doc mapping each class to its allowed tool floor. This makes the never-gatekeepers guarantee structurally visible at the prompt layer rather than assumed.
basis: plugins/saga/agents/readonly-verifier.md line ~3 declares `tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`; plugins/team-execution/agents/security-reviewer.md frontmatter has no `tools:` line (inherits all). Engages binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} + {#verify-agent-git-checkout-clobber}: those enforce read-only at spawn-time; this idea extends the same guarantee to the agent-definition layer without contradicting them (revisit-when untouched — it hardens, not loosens).
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/audit_agent_tools.py (or a case in test_agent_registration_drift.py) + a tool-floor reference doc + CI wiring; verified by a test asserting a review-class agent with no tools list or with Edit in its list is flagged, and that readonly-verifier passes.
