title: One-time comprehensive fleet code-review campaign, concurrency-batched
idea: No systematic code-review pass has ever swept the 8-plugin fleet; team-execution consensus review has caught defects green suites missed in 2 independent repos, so latent defect debt across unreviewed Python is a near-certainty. Author a durable campaign spec that partitions every plugins/*/scripts/*.py and scripts/*.py surface into review batches of at most 3 (honoring the operator's global concurrency cap), each dispatched to saga:readonly-verifier under worktree isolation producing a durable review artifact, with findings materialized into wave-tagged GitHub issues. The spec names the batch order (highest-blast-radius scripts first: execution_spec.py, engine_resolver.py, outcome_decompose.py, artifact_pointer.py), the review lenses per batch, and the stop/roll-up mechanism. The friction being fixed: reviews happen reactively per-PR and never over the accreted whole.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 2: team-execution consensus review caught defects green suites missed in 2 independent operator-praised repos. Concurrency cap of 3 mandated in intake brief 'Added constraint'. Spawn rule from repo CLAUDE.md: verify-class spawns outside a saga skill must use subagent_type saga:readonly-verifier + isolation worktree.
outcome_shape: Merged docs/plans/ campaign spec + a tracking Objective issue with per-batch sub-issues; verified by the spec enumerating every script path (cross-checked against `find plugins scripts -name '*.py'`) and each batch being <=3 files.

title: Declared-but-unwired seam (reachability) review lens + audit script
idea: A recurring, invisible defect class in this fleet is vocabulary/config that is declared but never reachable end-to-end: `fable`/`xhigh` exist in MODELS/EFFORTS yet are unreachable outside saga's plan vocabulary, and ENGINE_INTENTS is a producer/consumer pair authored in /plan and rendered in team-execution but absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, and /work. Add a reachability audit — scripts/audit_wiring.py — that walks a small registry of known contract symbols (MODELS, EFFORTS, ENGINE_INTENTS, artifact-pointer schema keys) and reports every symbol with a producer but no consumer reference (or vice versa) across the plugin corpus, plus a code-review lens doc teaching reviewers to trace producer→consumer for any new enum/config. This turns 'looks defined, silently does nothing' from a lucky catch into a CI signal.
basis: Grounding brief section 1: `fable`/`xhigh` unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary (execution_spec.py:52-53); correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS producer in plan/SKILL.md:303-304, consumer in team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233, absent from /ideate /brainstorm /work. Section 6 item 1: dead-wiring learnings (producer+consumer) are a named recurring pain.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/audit_wiring.py + a contract-symbol registry + a review-lens reference doc + advisory CI job; verified by the script reporting the known fable/xhigh and ENGINE_INTENTS gaps and by a meta-test on a synthetic producer-only symbol.

title: Producer-AND-consumer paired-test requirement for every contract symbol
idea: Dead-wiring keeps shipping because a test can exercise the producer side of a contract while no test ever asserts the consumer actually reads it (or vice versa). Establish a contract registry (a small YAML/JSON listing each cross-module contract: symbol, producer module, consumer module) and a meta-test that fails when a registered contract lacks BOTH a producer-side and a consumer-side test reference. Seed it with the known pairs — ENGINE_INTENTS (plan producer / team-execution consumer), artifact-pointer schema (producer script / consumer worker), MODELS/EFFORTS (plan producer / emitter consumer). The maintainer pain this kills: green suites that prove a value is written but never that anything downstream consumes it, so the wiring rots silently.
basis: Grounding brief section 6 item 1 lists 'dead-wiring producer+consumer' and 'test-shape-masks-dead-wiring' as distinct repo learnings; correction (c) documents ENGINE_INTENTS as an explicit producer/consumer pair. Existing tests (test_team_execution_pointers.py, test_saga_execution_spec.py) prove per-side coverage exists but no meta-test enforces the pairing.
outcome_shape: PR adding a contracts registry file + tests/test_contract_pairing.py (a meta-test) + CI coverage; verified by the meta-test failing when a seeded contract's consumer-side test reference is removed.

title: Fake-adapter suites must pin a golden fixture derived from the real producer
idea: Fake/stub adapters (30 of the test files use mocks, fakes, or monkeypatch) pass their suites while silently diverging from the real contract — the canonical failure being validate_card_body, a stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py that passed 343 'clean' cards which then failed the live contract (#222). Introduce a convention plus a lint: any fake/stub that stands in for a real schema or client must be paired with a golden fixture generated from the actual producer (checked in, regenerated by a script), and a test asserting the fake's shape still matches the golden. scripts/check_fake_fixtures.py flags fakes with no paired golden. This converts 'the fake and reality drifted' from an operator-recall catch into a failing check.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 1: validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of card_validator.py — 343 cards passed the fake, failed the live contract (#222). Section 6 item 1 names 'fake-adapter mismatch' as a repo learning. 30 test files under tests/ use Fake/Stub/Mock/monkeypatch (grep count).
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/check_fake_fixtures.py + a golden-fixture convention doc + at least one seeded golden pairing + advisory CI job; verified by the check flagging a fake whose golden is deleted/mutated.

title: Single-command local CI mirror generated-from and drift-tested against ci.yml
idea: CLAUDE.md's 'Running Quality Checks' section is a strict subset of ci.yml, which is exactly how 'CI red on checks local runs passed' happens (mined in 2 repos): the doc tells operators to run pytest, ruff check, mypy, bandit — but ci.yml also runs `ruff format --check .` (line 101), the standalone `check_issue_contract_parity.py` gate (line 40), `validate_plugins.py` (73), and `marketplace/validator/validate.py` (76), none of which the local guidance mentions. Ship scripts/ci_local.sh that runs the exact ordered step list from ci.yml, make it the one documented command, and add a drift test that parses ci.yml's `run:` steps and asserts the local script covers every one. Now local == CI by construction, and any new CI step that the mirror misses fails a test.
basis: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs ruff format --check (line 101), check_issue_contract_parity.py (40), validate_plugins.py (73), marketplace validate.py (76), pytest --cov (43); repo CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks' lists only pytest, ruff check, mypy, bandit — a strict subset. Grounding brief section 7 item 10: local-vs-CI parity gaps mined in 2 repos.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/ci_local.sh + tests/test_ci_parity.py (parses ci.yml run steps, asserts mirror covers each) + a CLAUDE.md edit pointing to the single command; verified by the parity test failing when a ci.yml step is added but not mirrored.

title: Four-surface release-parity CI guard (version + changelog + behavior diff)
idea: CLAUDE.md step 6 requires plugin.json, marketplace.json, CHANGELOG.md, and drift tests to tell the same story, yet release-surface drift persists despite the written rule, and the marketplace validator only checks required-field presence and semver format — never that the plugin.json version equals its marketplace.json entry version equals the top CHANGELOG.md heading. Add scripts/check_release_surface_parity.py + a CI job that, per plugin, asserts those three versions are identical AND that any PR touching a plugin's SKILL.md/scripts/agents without bumping its CHANGELOG fails. This is deliberately beyond the QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} seed, which only checks directory↔marketplace-entry presence — version/changelog/behavior parity is the drift class {#marketplace-ci-guard} does not cover.
basis: Repo CLAUDE.md 'Development Workflow' step 6 enumerates the four surfaces that must stay in sync; grounding brief section 6 item 3: 'release-surface drift persists despite CLAUDE.md step 6'. marketplace/validator/validate.py checks required fields (line 218) and semver (230) but no cross-surface version equality. Explicitly extends QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} (QUEUED.md:176-188), which covers only directory↔entry presence (PRs #110/#111/#112), not version/changelog parity.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/check_release_surface_parity.py + a CI job in ci.yml + a version-parity drift test; verified by the guard failing on a seeded plugin whose marketplace.json version lags its plugin.json, and on a scripts change with no CHANGELOG bump.

title: Single-source CI runner: delete the hand-maintained local check list
idea: The 'did I run every check CI runs?' step is manual and drifts — CLAUDE.md lists the commands prose-style and they can silently diverge from ci.yml. Invert it: make ci.yml and the local run read the SAME command list from one source. Extract the four job command sets (tests, validate, lint, type-check) into a `tools/ci-steps.sh` (or a `[tool.ci]` table in pyproject) that both ci.yml steps and a new `make ci` / `tools/ci-local.sh` invoke, so there is no second place to keep in sync. A drift test asserts every `run:` line in ci.yml resolves to a step in the shared script. The best local-parity step is no separate step — one definition, two callers.
basis: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines four jobs (tests:14, validate:53, lint:78, type-check:103) whose exact commands live only in the YAML; CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks' restates them by hand (uv run pytest / ruff check . / mypy plugins/ scripts/ tests/ / bandit). Grounding brief section 7 pattern 10: 'Local-vs-CI' parity failures mined in 2 repos (CI red on checks local runs passed).
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/ci-local.sh + tools/ci-steps.sh (or pyproject [tool.ci]), rewiring .github/workflows/ci.yml run: lines to call it, updating CLAUDE.md step to `tools/ci-local.sh`, and tests/test_ci_parity.py asserting no ci.yml run-line lacks a shared-script entry. Verified: CI green with rewired steps + parity test fails if a raw command is added to ci.yml.

title: Kill the uv-vs-python3 invocation split that reproduces differently locally
idea: CI runs the issue-contract parity check as bare `python3 plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py`, while every other check runs under `uv run` — so an operator reproducing locally under uv (the CLAUDE.md-blessed path) exercises a different interpreter/env than CI, the exact shape that makes CI red on a locally-green check. Remove the split: run every Python check through one invocation form (`uv run python ...`) so there is no second execution mode to reason about. Add a lint that flags any ci.yml step invoking bare `python`/`python3` instead of `uv run`.
basis: .github/workflows/ci.yml:40 runs `python3 plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py` while ci.yml:43 runs `uv run python -m pytest` and lint/type-check jobs all use `uv run` — a single interpreter-env divergence inside one workflow.
outcome_shape: PR normalizing ci.yml:40 to `uv run python ...` and adding a guard (extend tests/test_ci_parity.py or a ruff-style check) rejecting bare python invocations in ci.yml. Verified: grep of ci.yml shows zero non-`uv run` python calls; guard test red if one is reintroduced.

title: Version-bump generator: one edit regenerates all four release surfaces
idea: CLAUDE.md step 6 makes the human keep four surfaces in lockstep by hand (plugin.json, marketplace.json, CHANGELOG.md, drift-guard tests) on every behavior change — a four-file manual ritual that the {#marketplace-ci-guard} seed only proposes to DETECT after the fact. Go past detection to removal: a `tools/bump-plugin.py <plugin> <version>` that reads plugin.json as source of truth, rewrites the matching marketplace.json entry, scaffolds a dated CHANGELOG stub, and prints the exact drift-guard expectation — so the operator makes one intentional edit and the mechanical fan-out is generated, not remembered. The guard becomes a safety net over a generator, not the primary interface.
basis: CLAUDE.md 'Development Workflow' step 6 enumerates the four surfaces that must move together (plugins/<plugin>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, plugins/<plugin>/CHANGELOG.md, version/metadata drift guard tests); tests/test_agent_registration_drift.py already exists as the detection half, proving the generate half is absent.
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/bump-plugin.py + tests/test_bump_plugin.py, and a CLAUDE.md step-6 rewrite pointing to it. Verified: running the tool on a plugin produces a diff that passes existing drift-guard tests; test_bump_plugin.py asserts marketplace entry matches plugin.json after a bump.

title: Automate the agent-prompt quality rubric into a CI lint
idea: There is no repeatable audit of the ~34 agent prompt files — quality is whatever the last author remembered. Replace the periodic manual read-through with a machine-checkable lint: `scripts/audit_agents.py` walks every plugins/*/agents/*.md, parses frontmatter, and enforces a rubric (has model in the MODELS vocabulary, has a description with an activation trigger, declares a minimal tools list, no references to renamed/removed skills or plugins, sandbox-spawn rule present where the agent spawns verifiers). Wire it into the existing `validate` CI job so a prompt regression fails the PR. The recurring manual audit becomes no step — a gate.
basis: find plugins -path '*/agents/*.md' returns 34 files today; grounding brief section 1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model, zero effort fields' — confirming frontmatter is uniform enough to lint. ci.yml:53 'validate' job already runs scripts/validate_plugins.py + marketplace validate, an existing hook point for a new agent linter.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/audit_agents.py + a rubric doc (docs/agent-prompt-rubric.md) + a `validate`-job step calling it + tests/test_audit_agents.py. Verified: audit passes on the current 34 agents (or lists real gaps as the first backlog), and a deliberately broken fixture agent fails CI.

title: Opus rubric scorecard: automate the judgment half of the prompt audit
idea: The lint (T11-F2-4) catches structure but not prompt quality — clarity of trigger, absence of contradictory instructions, effort/model fit. Automate that judgment layer too: a saga:readonly-verifier-spawned pass (isolation worktree, per the repo's mandatory sandbox rule) scores each agent .md against a written rubric and emits a docs/agent-audit/scorecard.md artifact ranking the fleet, so the 'sit down and review all agents' step is replaced by a re-runnable command producing a durable, diffable scorecard. Because external engines are advisory-only here, Claude is verifier-of-record and the scorecard is advisory input to human triage, not a gate.
basis: First-principles: a structural lint (F2-4) is necessary but cannot judge prose quality; the only scalable way to audit ~34 prompts for judgment defects without a human re-reading all of them each time is to make an LLM pass produce a diffable artifact. This crosses {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} / {#readonly-verifier-fallback-ladder-325}: engaged by keeping the scorecard advisory (Claude/human is verifier-of-record, output never gates a merge) and mandating subagent_type saga:readonly-verifier + isolation worktree per CLAUDE.md's spawn rule — revisit-when not triggered because nothing here gatekeeps.
outcome_shape: PR adding a saga skill/command hook that runs the scored audit and writes docs/agent-audit/scorecard.md, plus the rubric it scores against. Verified: running it produces a scorecard listing all 34 agents with per-criterion scores; re-run on an unchanged fleet is stable (deterministic ranking sections).

title: Incremental changed-plugin review: remove the 'when do we review the whole fleet' decision
idea: A comprehensive one-time fleet code review is a painful, easily-deferred step that goes stale the moment it finishes. Invert the cadence: instead of a periodic big-bang pass, make review continuous and scoped — a workflow that on each PR detects which plugin directories changed (segment boundary = plugin directory, matching the settled worker-cache-scheduling architecture) and runs saga:code-review only over those segments, appending findings to a per-plugin review ledger. The 'schedule the big review' step disappears; the fleet is always reviewed at the granularity of what changed, and the ledger shows coverage/staleness per plugin.
basis: Grounding brief section 2 {#worker-cache-scheduling}: 'segment boundary = plugin directory' is already the settled unit; saga:code-review exists as a skill (SKILL.md, 'Run a structured Infiquetra code-quality review at the work-to-PR boundary'). Theme 11 explicitly scopes 'comprehensive code review'; no changed-scope automation exists in ci.yml (jobs are tests/validate/lint/type-check only).
outcome_shape: PR adding a review-orchestration script (tools/review-changed-plugins.py) that maps a diff to plugin segments and invokes saga:code-review per segment, writing docs/plugin-reviews/<plugin>.md ledger entries. Verified: a PR touching one plugin triggers review of only that segment; ledger records date + findings count per plugin.

title: Producer/consumer contract-parity tests: make dead-wiring fail CI instead of hiding
idea: Dead-wiring survives because a test can exercise a producer OR a consumer in isolation and pass while the two never agree on shape. Remove the blind spot by generalizing the existing vendored-parity gate into a producer/consumer contract-parity test suite: for each known wiring pair (e.g. ENGINE_INTENTS authored in plan/SKILL.md rendered in team-execution's worker table, plan unit-tier table consumed by execution_spec) assert the producer's emitted keys/vocabulary exactly equal what the consumer reads. A single fixture registry of (producer, consumer, shared-vocabulary) drives it, so adding a new cross-plugin wire forces a parity assertion. Dead-wiring becomes a red test, not a runtime surprise.
basis: Grounding brief section 1 corrections: 'ENGINE_INTENTS producer/consumer pair — authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233)'. ci.yml:33-40 already runs check_issue_contract_parity.py as a consumer-side vendored-parity gate — prior art proving the pattern; test-shape-honesty axis notes 'dead-wiring needs producer AND consumer'.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_wiring_parity.py + a fixtures registry of producer/consumer pairs, extending the existing parity approach beyond the vendored issue-contract. Verified: a deliberate edit desyncing plan's ENGINE_INTENTS from the team-execution worker table turns the parity test red.

title: Fake-adapter detector: lint away test suites that never touch real code
idea: Fake-adapter suites pass by asserting against a mock and never importing the module under test, so a whole file can be green while the real adapter is broken — the test-shape lie the axis names. Automate the smell out: a lint (`scripts/lint_test_shape.py`) that flags any tests/test_*.py whose assertions run only against locally-defined fakes/mocks with no import of the corresponding plugins module, and any test that patches the very function it claims to verify. Wire it into the lint CI job. The 'reviewer eyeballs whether this test is real' step becomes a mechanical gate.
basis: First-principles: a test file that imports no production symbol and only asserts on in-file fakes has, by construction, zero coverage of real behavior regardless of green status; this is statically detectable (AST: production-module imports vs assertion targets). Grounding brief section 5/7 names 'dead-wiring test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter' as a mined recurring pattern, establishing the failure exists in this repo's substrate. No such lint exists in ci.yml today.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/lint_test_shape.py + a lint-job step + tests/test_lint_test_shape.py with a fake-only fixture (flagged) and a real-import fixture (passes). Verified: running it over the current tests/ either passes clean or names the offending files as first backlog items; a fake-only fixture fails CI.

title: Agent prompts are untested code: executable quality-rubric linter, not a human doc
idea: The fleet treats each agent .md as prose a human reads and blesses one at a time. Reframe every agent frontmatter+body as a testable config artifact and ship scripts/audit_agent_prompts.py that enforces a machine-checkable rubric across all 34 agent files: declared model present, trigger/when-to-use section present, tool scope declared, a verification-discipline clause present, and no unbounded fan-out or unsandboxed verify-spawn language that violates the CLAUDE.md readonly-verifier+worktree rule. Wire it as a pytest module beside the existing test_agent_tiering.py / test_agent_registration_drift.py and as a CI step, with the rubric itself living as references/agent-prompt-rubric.md so failures cite a clause. This converts 'audit ~55 agents by hand' into a standing invariant that fails the PR that regresses a prompt.
basis: 34 agent .md files verified via `find plugins -path '*/agents/*.md' | wc -l` (team-execution alone 25); CLAUDE.md mandates 'Any verify/review-class Agent-tool spawn made outside a saga skill must pass subagent_type: saga:readonly-verifier + isolation: "worktree"'; existing tests/test_agent_tiering.py + test_agent_registration_drift.py establish the agent-as-testable-artifact pattern this extends.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/audit_agent_prompts.py + tests/test_agent_prompt_rubric.py + a rubric reference doc + a CI step in .github/workflows/ci.yml; verified by the test failing on a deliberately clause-stripped agent fixture and passing on the current fleet.

title: model: is not a fixed agent property — audit tier-appropriateness against a role-class policy
idea: Every agent hardcodes model: as if the model were an intrinsic, unquestionable property of that agent. Reframe it as a resolved consequence of a declared role class (judgment / mechanical / survey per the global effort-tiering guidance) and add an audit that flags mismatches: a survey-only readonly agent pinned to opus, or a judgment/adversarial-review agent pinned to haiku, is a defect the audit surfaces. The audit does not change dispatch (that is theme 12); it only asserts each agent's hardcoded model is defensible against a checked-in role-class table, turning 'is this the right model?' from an every-time ad hoc judgment into a reviewable policy diff. This attacks the closed default that model choice is settled at authoring time and never re-examined fleet-wide.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields ... no dispatch-time override lever anywhere'; global CLAUDE.md effort-tiering: 'judgment/design/adversarial review -> Opus; mechanical -> Sonnet or Haiku; read-only survey -> Sonnet'.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/<shared>/config/agent-role-classes.json (role class per agent) + scripts/audit_agent_tiering.py extension (or new check in test_agent_tiering.py) that fails on model↔role-class mismatch; verified by an oracle test with one intentionally mis-tiered agent.

title: A comprehensive review is not one heroic pass — segment the fleet into a standing review ledger
idea: 'Comprehensive code review' is framed as a single large scheduled event, which guarantees it rots the moment it finishes. Reframe it as a per-segment standing invariant using the plugin-directory segment boundary the fleet already settled for worker-cache-scheduling: each plugin is a review unit with a checked-in review-ledger entry recording last-reviewed commit SHA, the judgment lenses applied (reusing saga /code-review's ce-code-review lens spine), and open findings. A tiny CI check flags any plugin whose HEAD has drifted N commits past its last-reviewed SHA, converting 'did we review everything?' into a derivable, always-current answer instead of a memory. This dogfoods the fleet's own review engine's scope model rather than inventing a parallel one.
basis: Grounding §2 binding {#worker-cache-scheduling}: 'segment boundary = plugin directory'; QUEUED campaign record: /code-review shipped 0.8.0 as the ce-code-review 'findings/validator/judgment-lens spine'; pre-mortem #1 in intake brief: 'Backlog rot — generation outpaces execution bandwidth' — same rot risk applies to a one-shot review pass.
outcome_shape: PR adding docs/review-ledger.md (or per-plugin .review-ledger.json) seeded with current SHAs + scripts/check_review_staleness.py + a CI step; verified by the check going red when a plugin is edited without a ledger update.

title: CI is not the authority local approximates — one shared entrypoint both invoke, parity by construction
idea: The mined pain (CI red on checks a local run passed, 2 repos) is treated as an unavoidable fact of 'how CI works,' with the ci.yml job commands and the CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks' list maintained as two independent hand-copies. Reframe the drift as a defect in the environment contract: ship scripts/ci.py (or a Makefile) that defines the exact five gates (pytest+cov, validate_plugins + marketplace validate, ruff check + format, mypy plugins/scripts/tests, bandit) once, have ci.yml call scripts/ci.py <job> instead of re-typing the commands, and have a pre-push hook call the same script. Local and CI then run byte-identical command lines and tool scopes, so a green local run cannot diverge from CI by construction rather than by discipline.
basis: .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 42-43/72-76/97-101/122-123/144-145 each re-declare gate commands that are independently re-typed in CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks'; grounding §7 recurring pattern 10: 'Local-vs-CI verification parity gaps — CI red on checks local runs passed (2 repos)'.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/ci.py exposing named gates + editing .github/workflows/ci.yml to call it + a pre-commit/pre-push config + a CLAUDE.md pointer; verified by `python scripts/ci.py all` locally reproducing the full CI gate set and CI green through the same entrypoint.

title: Don't guard the copies — generate them: single-source release surfaces from plugin.json
idea: CLAUDE.md step 6 and the QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} seed both accept that release surfaces (marketplace.json entry, plugin.json version, CHANGELOG heading) are separate hand-maintained files whose job is to stay in sync — the seed's answer is a CI guard that detects drift. Reframe one level up: the drift surface exists only because the copies are authored independently; make plugin.json the single source and generate the marketplace.json plugin entries (name/version/description/path) from it via scripts/sync_marketplace.py, with CI running it in --check mode. This goes beyond the QUEUED drift-guard (which catches divergence after the fact) by removing the second author, so the class of bug that shipped in PRs #110/#111/#112 cannot recur. It engages the seed's 'guard the copies' framing directly rather than duplicating it.
basis: QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} (line 176) proposes 'assert plugin directories match marketplace.json entries' as a detection guard, citing 'the bug it prevents has shipped twice in a row (PRs #110, #111) and required a third PR (#112)'; marketplace/validator/validate.py validates schema shape but performs no plugin.json→marketplace.json value derivation (grep of validate.py functions confirms no generation path).
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/sync_marketplace.py (generate + --check) + a CI step + a CLAUDE.md step-6 rewrite pointing at the generator; verified by `--check` going red when a plugin.json version is bumped without regenerating marketplace.json, and green after regeneration.

title: Mock isolation is the bug at a wiring seam — force one shared contract fixture across producer/consumer
idea: The fleet's test culture treats unit isolation (each side mocked) as virtuous, which is exactly what let dead-wiring ship: a producer and its consumer each pass green against their own fakes while disagreeing about the contract. Reframe the seam itself as the unit under test and add contract tests keyed to the fleet's real producer/consumer pairs — starting with ENGINE_INTENTS, authored in saga /plan and rendered in team-execution Step A7 — where one shared fixture enumerates the contract's values and a single test fails if the producer can emit a token the consumer's table does not handle. A checked-in seam registry lists every such pair so new seams inherit the requirement, converting 'both sides green' from a false comfort into a real cross-side guarantee.
basis: Grounding §1 correction (c): 'ENGINE_INTENTS is a producer/consumer pair — authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233)'; grounding §6 pain: 'dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring' among 5+ learnings.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_contract_seams.py + docs/contract-seams.md (the pair registry) covering ENGINE_INTENTS producer↔consumer first; verified by the test failing when a new intent is added to the producer enum without a matching consumer handler.

title: A fake is not free to lie — collection-time conformance gate binding every stub to the real interface
idea: A green suite built on fakes is treated as evidence the adapter works, but the journal records fake-adapter suites hiding real mismatches: nothing forces a test fake to actually match the shape of the real thing it stands in for. Reframe the fake as a conformance obligation — every fake/stub used in tests must be registered against the real interface (ABC or a declared protocol signature) and a pytest collection-time check fails if a fake drifts from the real method/argument surface. This attacks the default that a stub can be hand-written to whatever shape makes the test pass; instead the stub inherits or is signature-checked against production, so a passing suite can no longer certify a mismatched adapter.
basis: Grounding §6 pain #1 lists 'fake-adapter mismatch' and 'test-shape-masks-dead-wiring' as distinct durable learnings requiring 'did it actually run/persist' verification for any bridge/delegation idea; CLAUDE.md requires fake plugins be tested but sets no fake↔real conformance rule.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/conftest.py conformance hook + a fakes registry + refactoring existing test fakes to register against their real ABC/protocol; verified by the collection-time check erroring when a fake's method signature diverges from the real interface.

title: Shared agent-spec registry primitive that every agent file is CI-validated against
idea: Extract the ad hoc frontmatter parsing (`_parse_frontmatter` currently duplicated inside `tests/test_agent_tiering.py:18-38`) into a reusable `tools/agent_spec.py` primitive and build a single fleet-wide rubric test that runs over all 34 `plugins/*/agents/*.md` files. The rubric asserts machine-checkable prompt-quality invariants that today are only conventions in some agents: `name:` matches the file stem, a model pin or a `tiering_exempt:` field is present, the description carries an explicit negative-scope clause (the `NOT for:` / `Do NOT use` pattern already in `security-reviewer.md` and `mechanical-executor.md`), and a `tools:` allowlist is declared for any Bash-capable agent. Because the registry is the one place the rubric lives, every future agent added anywhere in the fleet is audited for free — the second-order win is that agent quality stops depending on whether the author remembered the convention. This folds the existing tiering and registration-drift guards into one primitive instead of three parallel frontmatter parsers.
basis: `tests/test_agent_tiering.py:18-38` and `tests/test_agent_registration_drift.py` each re-implement frontmatter parsing; `plugins/team-execution/agents/security-reviewer.md` has an explicit `NOT for:` clause and `plugins/saga/agents/mechanical-executor.md` a `Do NOT use this agent for...` clause — the negative-scope convention exists but is unenforced across the other ~30 agents.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tools/agent_spec.py` (shared parser + rubric) and `tests/test_agent_prompt_rubric.py` parametrized over every `plugins/*/agents/*.md`; `test_agent_tiering.py` and `test_agent_registration_drift.py` refactored to consume the shared parser. Verified by CI green after the rubric flags and fixes any agents missing negative-scope / tool-allowlist fields.

title: One durable agent-prompt scorecard doc scoring all 34 agents on a written quality rubric
idea: Run a single comprehensive semantic audit pass over all 34 fleet agents and land a durable `docs/agent-prompt-audit.md` scorecard that scores each agent on dimensions a CI test cannot judge: output-contract explicitness (does the prompt say what shape it returns to its caller), model-tier justification (is `model: opus` earned or cargo-culted — 12 team-execution reviewers all pin opus), prompt-injection posture for channel-facing agents (redis-channel-coach, discord surfaces), and negative-scope sharpness. The scorecard becomes the reference rubric future agents are written against and the meta-tooling anchor idea T11-F4-1's machine checks point back to for rationale. The compounding return: the fleet gets a single canonical definition of 'a good agent prompt here' so review of new agents converges instead of re-litigating taste each time.
basis: First-principles: the fleet has 34 agents across 8 plugins with no shared quality definition — every team-execution reviewer hardcodes `model: opus` (per grounding brief §1 'zero effort fields, every agent hardcodes model'), which is either all-justified or partly cargo-culted, and only a written rubric can adjudicate. A scorecard is the cheapest artifact that makes the implicit rubric explicit and reusable; without it, agent-quality judgments are re-derived per review and drift.
outcome_shape: Merged `docs/agent-prompt-audit.md` with a per-agent scored table (34 rows) + a rubric section, plus a short PR fixing the lowest-scoring agents' output-contract clauses. Verified by the doc existing, every agent appearing exactly once (a trivial coverage test asserts row-count == agent-file count), and cross-links from the T11-F4-1 rubric test.

title: Shared review-lens catalog that both saga /code-review and team-execution reviewers draw from
idea: The fleet has two parallel, drifting review taxonomies: saga `/code-review`'s judgment-selected review lenses (`skills/code-review/SKILL.md`) and team-execution's ~12 standing reviewer agents (security-reviewer, api-reviewer, architecture-reviewer, code-quality-reviewer, testing-reviewer, clarity-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, infra-reviewer, devils-advocate-reviewer, ai-usefulness-reviewer, and the scanners). Author a single `plugins/saga/references/review-lens-catalog.md` registry — each lens defined once with its scope, trigger heuristic, and severity bands — and have both consumers reference it: saga selects lenses from the catalog, and each team-execution reviewer agent's frontmatter declares which catalog lens it embodies. The compounding win is that a new review concern (say, a new supply-chain lens) is authored once and immediately available to both the saga solo pass and the team consensus panel, instead of being added to one and forgotten in the other.
basis: `plugins/team-execution/agents/` contains 12+ distinct `*-reviewer.md` files (enumerated: ai-usefulness, api, architecture, clarity, code-quality, devils-advocate, infra, privacy, security, testing) and saga ships a separate judgment-lens `/code-review` skill (`plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md`) — two review vocabularies with no shared source of truth.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/review-lens-catalog.md` + a `lens:` field on each team-execution reviewer's frontmatter + `tests/test_review_lens_catalog.py` asserting every reviewer's declared lens resolves to a catalog entry and every saga-referenced lens exists. Verified by CI green and the catalog covering all 12 reviewers.

title: Single source-of-truth CI runner that both GitHub Actions and local invoke
idea: The parity gaps come from CI job definitions in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the human-run commands in CLAUDE.md's 'Running Quality Checks' block being two hand-maintained copies of the same command set — the tell is CLAUDE.md's own parenthetical 'match CI scope — CI checks plugins/ scripts/ tests/, not just plugins/', a note that only exists because they already drifted. Land a single `tools/ci_local.py` that defines the check matrix (pytest+cov, validate_plugins + marketplace validate, ruff format --check + ruff check, mypy over plugins/ scripts/ tests/, bandit) as data, and have both `ci.yml` steps and the local developer entrypoint call it. The second-order return: 'green locally, red in CI' becomes structurally impossible for the covered checks because there is exactly one definition of what the checks are.
basis: CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks' section explicitly annotates the mypy line 'match CI scope — CI checks plugins/ scripts/ tests/, not just plugins/' — a drift-repair note proving the doc and `ci.yml` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:123` runs `mypy plugins/ scripts/ tests/`) were already out of sync; grounding brief §7 pattern 10 records 'CI red on checks local runs passed' in 2 repos.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tools/ci_local.py` (data-defined check matrix + runner), `ci.yml` steps rewired to invoke it, CLAUDE.md pointing to `uv run python tools/ci_local.py`, and `tests/test_ci_local_matrix.py` asserting the matrix parses. Verified by running the runner locally reproducing all four CI jobs and CI staying green.

title: Drift guard that fails when CLAUDE.md's documented checks diverge from ci.yml
idea: Complementary to a shared runner but far cheaper: a meta-test that parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and CLAUDE.md's 'Running Quality Checks' block and asserts the set of check commands (pytest, ruff check, ruff format, mypy with its exact path scope, bandit) matches in both directions. This makes the reproduction instructions unable to lie — the moment CI gains or drops a check, or changes mypy's path scope, the doc must be updated in the same PR or CI fails. It is a lever because it protects every future contributor's ability to reproduce CI locally without any runtime coupling, and it can ship immediately (before the heavier T11-F4-4 runner) to stop the bleeding.
basis: Same drift evidence as T11-F4-4: CLAUDE.md's mypy line carries a manual 'match CI scope' correction, and `ci.yml` type-check job runs `mypy plugins/ scripts/ tests/ --ignore-missing-imports` — two independently-maintained copies that already diverged once.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tests/test_ci_command_doc_parity.py` that parses both files and diffs the command/scope set. Verified by the test failing on a deliberate injected mismatch (e.g., dropping `tests/` from the doc's mypy line) and passing on the reconciled state.

title: Diff-aware release-surface bump guard: touched a plugin's behavior, must bump its surfaces
idea: The existing static triad parity test (`tests/test_release_triad.py`) checks that a plugin's plugin.json / marketplace.json / CHANGELOG versions agree with each other, and QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} only checks directory↔marketplace presence — neither catches the actual recurring miss: changing a plugin's behavior/schema/prompt files and forgetting to bump anything (CLAUDE.md step 6 is a process rule with no enforcement). Add a git-diff-aware CI guard that, for each plugin whose non-doc files changed in the PR's merge-base diff, asserts that plugin's version bumped AND its CHANGELOG gained a top entry. This turns CLAUDE.md step 6 from an honor-system checklist into machinery, and because it keys off the diff it costs contributors nothing until they actually forget.
basis: CLAUDE.md Development Workflow step 6 mandates updating plugin.json + marketplace.json + CHANGELOG 'in the same PR' but is unenforced; QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} documents the same class of bug shipped in PRs #110/#111 needing #112 to fix; `tests/test_release_triad.py` covers only static cross-file version agreement, not 'you changed code without bumping'.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tools/release_surface_diff_guard.py` + a CI step (runs on pull_request against merge-base) + `tests/test_release_surface_diff_guard.py` with fixtures for changed-without-bump (fail) and changed-with-bump (pass). Verified by the guard failing a synthetic diff that edits a SKILL.md without touching CHANGELOG.

title: Boundary-crossing test convention + shared helper so round-trip tests actually cross persistence
idea: The dead-wiring learning {#test-shape-masks-dead-wiring-291} proved a green e2e test can hide a no-op consumer leg when producer and consumer share an in-memory value instead of reading back from the saved boundary. Turn the generalizable rule into meta-tooling: add a shared `assert_reads_from_boundary` fixture helper in `tests/conftest.py` (constructs the consumer's input from disk/DB/wire, never from the producer's return), a short `docs/test-shape-convention.md` codifying 'a round-trip test must re-read from the boundary it claims to validate', and an audit pass that finds producer/consumer round-trip tests in the suite that never re-read. Because the helper and convention are shared, every future persistence-crossing test is written honestly by default — the compounding return is that the whole suite's green becomes more trustworthy, not just one test.
basis: LEARNINGS `{#test-shape-masks-dead-wiring-291}` (LEARNINGS.md:92-99): 'A round-trip test only proves the round-trip if the consumer reads from the boundary it claims to validate. If producer and consumer share an in-memory value, the persistence layer is untested no matter how green the test is — assert the consumer derives its input from disk/DB/wire, not from the producer's return value.'
outcome_shape: PR adding `assert_reads_from_boundary` to `tests/conftest.py`, `docs/test-shape-convention.md`, and at least one existing round-trip test (e.g. an artifact-pointer or saga tick test) converted to re-read from disk. Verified by the converted test failing when the persistence write is stubbed out, proving it now crosses the boundary.

title: Real-adapter contract lane: a registry of fake-only seams gets one real-substrate test each
idea: The fake-adapter learning {#fake-adapter-hides-real-path-mismatch} showed an all-fake suite let the worktree liveness oracle read every live worktree as ABSENT under the real CLI because the fake keyed on the happy value and could not surface path canonicalization. Build a marked `tests/real_adapter/` lane plus a small registry doc enumerating the fleet's adapter seams that currently have only fake-backed coverage (worktree liveness oracle, engine bridges, redis client — fakeredis is present but does not exercise real filesystem path handling). Each registered seam gets one opt-in contract test that runs the production adapter against a minimal real substrate (a real tmp git repo for the worktree oracle, real fs paths). The registry is the lever: it makes 'which seams are still fake-only' visible and gives every future adapter a named slot to add real coverage, so path/format mismatches surface in CI instead of production.
basis: LEARNINGS `{#fake-adapter-hides-real-path-mismatch}` (LEARNINGS.md:417): 'An all-fake adapter test suite cannot catch a real-adapter path-canonicalization mismatch — the worktree liveness oracle read every live worktree as ABSENT under the production CLI'; existing suites like `test_outcome_worktrees.py` and the fakeredis-backed redis tests confirm the fake-first shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tests/real_adapter/` (pytest-marked lane), `docs/real-adapter-seam-registry.md` enumerating fake-only seams, and one seam converted — a real-tmp-git-repo contract test for the worktree liveness oracle. Verified by the new test passing against the real CLI and failing if pointed at a mis-canonicalized path.

title: Spectral-style declarative ruleset linter for agent frontmatter
idea: Adopt the API-governance pattern from Stoplight Spectral (a rulesets-as-data linter that lints OpenAPI/AsyncAPI documents against named, severity-tagged rules) and apply it to the 34 agent .md files. Ship tools/lint_agent_prompts.py plus a declarative agent-prompt-rules.yaml encoding the rubric: every agent must carry model:, a description with an explicit NOT-for / delineation section, at least one trigger example or <example> block for orchestrator-facing agents, and a tools: declaration for any read-only agent. The linter emits per-rule severity (error/warn) exactly like Spectral so the rubric is data, not code, and evolves without rewriting the linter. Wire it into the existing validate job in ci.yml beside validate_plugins.py.
basis: Source domain: API governance tooling. Stoplight Spectral (github.com/stoplightio/spectral) lints structured docs against a YAML ruleset of named rules with given/then/severity — the exact shape needed to turn an agent-prompt rubric into versioned data rather than imperative checks. Repo today has only test_agent_tiering.py pinning model: for 4 callable agents; no rubric covers description quality, NOT-for boundaries, or example presence across the other 30 agent files.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tools/lint_agent_prompts.py, config/agent-prompt-rules.yaml, a ci.yml validate-job step, and tests/test_agent_prompt_lint.py with a synthetic malformed-agent fixture. Verified: CI red on the fixture (missing NOT-for section) and green on the real 34-agent fleet.

title: Airworthiness-directive cycle: scheduled advisory LLM grade of every agent prompt
idea: Borrow the FAA Airworthiness Directive model, where each aircraft type undergoes recurring inspection at fixed intervals against a published standard and the finding is recorded even when no grounding is mandated. Stand up a scheduled (cron) Claude routine that grades all 34 agent prompts against the rubric an LLM can judge but a linter cannot — trigger-clarity, overlap with sibling agents, hallucination-prone instructions, missing failure-mode guidance — and writes a dated docs/agent-audit/REPORT.md with a per-agent score and delta from last cycle. This is strictly advisory and non-gating: Claude judging Claude's own prompts is verifier-of-record work, and no external engine gates. It complements the deterministic linter (T11-F5-1) by catching semantic rot the ruleset cannot express.
basis: Source domain: aviation maintenance regulation. FAA Airworthiness Directives (14 CFR Part 39) mandate recurring type-level inspection against a standard with a durable logbook entry — the recurring-cycle-plus-record shape, distinct from a one-time gate. Aligns with binding {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} because the grader is Claude, advisory-only, never a merge gate.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a scheduled workflow (or /audit-agents skill), a rubric doc, and the first committed docs/agent-audit/REPORT.md baseline. Verified: the routine runs, produces a scored report for all 34 agents, and a follow-up run shows a computed delta section.

title: Fleet C-check: scheduled heavy-inspection review campaign, one plugin at a time
idea: Aviation runs tiered maintenance checks (A/B/C/D) where the heavy C-check pulls one airframe out of service for a deep, checklist-driven teardown rather than reviewing the whole fleet superficially at once. Model a comprehensive code-review pass the same way: a tracked campaign that runs saga:code-review against exactly one plugin per cycle, against a fixed heavy-inspection checklist (dead-wiring, test-shape honesty, release-surface parity, error handling, security), and lands a dated docs/quality/fleet-c-check/<plugin>.md review artifact plus a rolling index. This gives the theme's comprehensive pass a bounded, resumable scope and a durable evidence trail instead of one unbounded review that never finishes.
basis: Source domain: aviation maintenance check cycles (A/B/C/D checks) — the C-check's one-airframe-deep-teardown scope is the structural answer to 'comprehensive review' without a fleet-wide-at-once cost blowout. Grounded need: theme axis asks for 'scope + mechanism for a comprehensive pass'; saga:code-review already exists (plugins/saga skill) but has no fleet-coverage tracking so no plugin is guaranteed reviewed.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding docs/quality/fleet-c-check/INDEX.md (per-plugin last-reviewed date + link), the first 1-2 plugin review artifacts, and tests/test_c_check_coverage.py asserting every marketplace plugin has an index row. Verified: coverage test passes; index shows dated artifacts.

title: Intermodal container: single-source check commands invoked by both local and CI
idea: Intermodal freight guarantees identical cargo behavior across ship, rail, and truck by putting the goods in one standardized container that every mode handles the same way — the interface, not the transport, is canonical. Apply that to check-command drift: create one canonical tools/ci.sh (or justfile) that defines each gate (pytest+cov, mypy over plugins/ scripts/ tests/, ruff, bandit, validate_plugins, marketplace validate) exactly once, then have both the developer and ci.yml invoke those named targets instead of each re-spelling the commands. Drift becomes structurally impossible because there is a single container for the check definitions.
basis: Source domain: intermodal containerization (one standardized interface across transport modes). Direct evidence of the drift it fixes: this repo's CLAUDE.md instructs `uv run mypy plugins/ scripts/ tests/ --ignore-missing-imports` with the parenthetical warning 'match CI scope — CI checks plugins/ scripts/ tests/, not just plugins/' — a documented prior instance of local and CI mypy scope diverging, and ci.yml (line 123) inlines that same command as a second copy.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tools/ci.sh with named targets, editing ci.yml to call them, updating CLAUDE.md to reference the targets, and tests/test_ci_parity.py asserting ci.yml invokes ci.sh rather than inlining pytest/mypy/ruff. Verified: parity test fails if a raw `uv run ... mypy` reappears inline in ci.yml.

title: Level-D simulator: hermetic locked-env pre-push run certified to match CI
idea: FAA Level-D full-flight simulators are certified to reproduce the real aircraft so precisely that training in them counts as flight time — the value is the certified fidelity of the environment, not just the checklist. The mined 'CI red on checks local runs passed' pain is usually environment fidelity (unlocked deps, Python patch version, runner) rather than command drift. Ship tools/ci-local.sh that runs the checks against a hermetic, `uv sync --locked` environment matching ci.yml's pinned Python 3.12, and a parity self-test that fails loudly if the local interpreter or the resolved lockfile hash diverges from what CI would use. A green local run then genuinely certifies the CI run.
basis: Source domain: FAA Level-D full-flight simulator certification (14 CFR Part 60) — certified environmental fidelity is what makes a local proxy trustworthy. Grounded pain: grounding brief §7 pattern 10 'Local-vs-CI verification parity gaps — CI red on checks local runs passed (2 repos)'; ci.yml pins `uv sync --locked` + Python 3.12 but nothing forces the developer's env to match.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tools/ci-local.sh (hermetic locked-env runner + interpreter/lockfile-hash parity assertion) and tests/test_ci_local_parity.py. Verified: script exits nonzero when run under a mismatched Python or a dirty lockfile, zero when matched.

title: cargo-semver-checks for prompts: behavior-surface change forces a version+CHANGELOG bump
idea: Rust's cargo-semver-checks and Elm's `elm diff` mechanically inspect a diff, detect that a public surface changed, and refuse a release whose version number does not reflect the change — the tool, not the author's memory, enforces the bump. The existing release-triad guard only checks that plugin.json, marketplace.json, and CHANGELOG versions agree; a PR that edits a SKILL.md, agent prompt, or script while leaving the version untouched sails through, which is exactly the persistent CLAUDE.md-step-6 drift. Add a guard that, when a PR touches a plugin's behavior surface (skills/**, agents/**, scripts/**, commands/**), asserts that plugin's version and CHANGELOG top entry also changed in the same diff.
basis: Source domain: package-ecosystem semver enforcement — cargo-semver-checks (github.com/obi1kenobi/cargo-semver-checks) and `elm diff` mechanically derive the required version bump from the diff. Distinct from QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} (registry presence) and from test_release_triad.py (version lockstep only): neither detects an un-bumped behavior change. Grounded by grounding brief §6.3 'Release-surface drift persists despite CLAUDE.md step 6'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tools/behavior_bump_guard.py, a ci.yml step (PR-scoped git diff), and tests/test_behavior_bump_guard.py with fixtures: SKILL.md edited + version bumped (pass) vs edited + version static (fail). Verified: guard red on the un-bumped fixture.

title: Pact-style producer/consumer contract test for cross-file wiring pairs
idea: Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact) verifies a producer and a consumer independently against one shared contract so a mismatch fails in CI without a live integration — the canonical defense against a producer emitting a field no consumer reads, or a consumer expecting one no producer sends. Repo's recurring dead-wiring learning is structurally identical: a wiring needs BOTH ends, e.g. ENGINE_INTENTS is authored in plan/SKILL.md but rendered in team-execution's worker table, and either half can silently rot. Ship a contract test that enumerates every declared ENGINE_INTENTS key on the producer side and asserts each is consumed on the render side (and flags orphan consumers), failing on any half-wired pair.
basis: Source domain: consumer-driven contract testing (Pact, pact.io). Direct anchor: grounding brief §1 correction (c) — 'ENGINE_INTENTS is a producer/consumer pair — authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233)'. Grounding brief §6.1 names 'dead-wiring producer+consumer' as a 5+-learning recurring pain with no producer/consumer contract test today.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tests/test_producer_consumer_contracts.py asserting ENGINE_INTENTS producer keys ↔ team-execution render coverage (both directions). Verified: test red when a key is added to plan/SKILL.md without a matching render row (and vice versa).

title: Chaos Monkey for drift guards: nightly mutation canary proving the guards have teeth
idea: Netflix's Chaos Monkey deliberately kills a live instance to prove the resilience machinery actually fires rather than being aspirational config; mutation testing does the same for a test suite by injecting a fault and demanding a test go red. The repo already worries about this — test_agent_registration_drift.py explicitly notes a test that 'stayed green under mutation' — yet no automated canary proves the drift/release/wiring guards would catch a real break. Add a nightly wiring-canary job that programmatically mutates one guarded invariant (rename a producer key, un-bump a version, corrupt an agent name) in a throwaway checkout and asserts the corresponding guard turns red; a guard that stays green is reported as a toothless test.
basis: Source domain: chaos engineering / mutation testing (Netflix Chaos Monkey; mutmut/cosmic-ray). Direct grounding for the fear it kills: tests/test_agent_registration_drift.py carries an inline note about a test that 'reimplemented the comparison inline and stayed green under mutation', and grounding brief §6.1 lists 'test-shape-masks-dead-wiring' and 'fake-adapter mismatch' as recurring learnings.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tools/wiring_canary.py (applies a known mutation, runs the target guard, asserts failure) and a scheduled workflow plus docs/quality/canary-log.md. Verified: canary reports RED-as-expected for each guarded invariant, and flags a deliberately weakened guard as toothless.

title: Release-surface parity gate: one source of truth, two generated mirrors
idea: Flip CLAUDE.md step 6 to its extreme: no human ever edits three release files by hand. Pick plugin.json version as the single source of truth and treat marketplace.json entries and CHANGELOG headings as derived mirrors. Ship scripts/check_release_surface_parity.py modeled exactly on the existing vendored-parity gate (ci.yml:33-40, which SHA256s vendored modules against a pinned manifest): for every plugin it asserts plugin.json version == its marketplace.json entry version == the top CHANGELOG.md heading version, and that a CHANGELOG entry exists for that version. Wire it as a named, dependency-free CI step beside the vendored-parity one so any drift red-flags the PR. The practical kernel of the impossible full-generation flip is a drift guard plus an optional --fix that regenerates the two mirrors from the source.
basis: ci.yml:33-40 already runs a stdlib-only SHA256-vs-manifest parity gate (check_issue_contract_parity.py) as reusable prior art; marketplace/validator/validate.py:249-275 checks entry required fields + semver but does NOT cross-check version equality across plugin.json/marketplace.json/CHANGELOG; CLAUDE.md step 6 mandates all four surfaces 'tell the same story' by prose only; QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} is the open seed. Builds beyond the seed by naming the exact three-way invariant and the ci.yml gate to clone.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding scripts/check_release_surface_parity.py + a named CI step in .github/workflows/ci.yml + a tests/test_release_surface_parity.py; verified by intentionally bumping one plugin.json version in a branch and confirming CI goes red on exactly that plugin.

title: Single-source CI matrix: local and CI run byte-identical commands
idea: Flip the constraint 'CI is the authority' to 'there is no CI, only one command that both a laptop and a runner invoke.' Today ci.yml hand-writes five jobs (tests, validate, lint, type-check, security) each re-declaring the same uv setup and its own command strings; a local dev reconstructs those commands from memory, which is exactly how CI goes red on checks that passed locally. Extract every check command into scripts/ci.sh (or a ci-matrix declarative file) with named stages, then have both ci.yml steps and a repo Makefile target `make ci` shell out to the identical stage definitions. The kernel: the check list stops living in two hand-synced places. Mirror CI's `uv sync --locked` locally so lockfile drift also fails locally, not only on the runner.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 10: 'Local-vs-CI verification parity gaps — CI red on checks local runs passed (2 repos)'. Directly corroborated by ci.yml:14-155 where 5 jobs each independently re-declare setup-uv + a bespoke command string (ruff check ., ruff format --check ., mypy plugins/ scripts/ tests/, bandit -r plugins/ scripts/ tests/, pytest --cov), with no shared source a local runner could invoke identically.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding scripts/ci.sh with named stages + a Makefile `ci` target + ci.yml jobs refactored to call the same stages; verified by running `make ci` locally and confirming each stage's command string is grep-identical to what CI executes (a test asserts the two references match).

title: CI-parity fingerprint doctor: autonomous red-vs-green environment diff
idea: Flip 'a human diagnoses CI failures' to 'CI diagnoses itself with zero operators.' When local is green and CI is red, the difference is almost always environment, not code: python patch version, uv.lock resolution, or tool versions (ruff/mypy/bandit) drifting between machines. Emit a deterministic parity fingerprint (tool versions + uv.lock content hash + python version) as a CI artifact on every run, and provide scripts/ci_fingerprint.py that a dev runs locally to print the same fingerprint. On a CI failure the doctor diffs the two fingerprints and surfaces the exact mismatched line instead of leaving the dev to guess. The impossible flip (fully self-healing CI) mines down to a cheap, always-on fingerprint + diff that converts an opaque red into a one-line environment delta.
basis: First-principles: ci.yml pins python 3.12 and uses `uv sync --locked` on the runner, but a laptop's resolved toolchain (ruff/mypy/bandit versions, python patch) is not asserted equal to the runner's; therefore a green-local/red-CI outcome is unattributable without capturing both environments' fingerprints. The parity gap pattern (section 7 pattern 10, 2 repos) is the recurring symptom this makes diagnosable rather than restating; no existing artifact in ci.yml captures a comparable fingerprint.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding scripts/ci_fingerprint.py + a ci.yml step uploading fingerprint.json as an artifact + a `make ci-fingerprint` target; verified by pinning a deliberately older ruff locally, running the doctor, and confirming it reports the ruff version delta as the divergence.

title: Agent-frontmatter lint gate: the invariants a single fleet-agent would still need
idea: Flip '34 bespoke agent prompts' to 'imagine one mega-agent served the whole fleet' and ask what frontmatter invariants would survive that collapse; then enforce exactly those across every real agent file. Ship scripts/check_agent_prompts.py as a CI gate over all agents/*.md fleet-wide: required frontmatter keys (name, description, model), name matches kebab-case + file basename, model is in the allowed enum {opus,sonnet,haiku}, description within sane length bounds, and — engaging the {#tier-vocab-ordering} decision — if an effort field is present it must be a valid EFFORTS value. This turns the currently prose-only prompt conventions into a machine-checked rubric and gives the fleet a single place to add new prompt-quality invariants.
basis: Verified: 34 agent definition files across the 8 plugins (25 in team-execution alone), and grounding brief section 1 states 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:, zero effort: fields' — meaning model values and frontmatter shape are load-bearing yet unchecked. No CI job in ci.yml lints agent .md frontmatter (validate_plugins.py and marketplace validate.py cover manifests/registry only). {#tier-vocab-ordering} is engaged (effort, if present, validated against the ordered ladder, not rejected).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding scripts/check_agent_prompts.py + a CI step + tests/test_agent_prompts.py; verified by introducing an agent file with model: gpt4 on a branch and confirming CI fails naming that file and field.

title: Semantic prompt-audit campaign: 100 reviewers collapsed into one batched scorecard
idea: Flip 'every agent prompt gets a live human reviewer (100 reviewers)' to a single offline batched audit that produces a ranked remediation backlog. Lint (idea 4) cannot judge role clarity, output-contract explicitness, failure-mode handling, or isolation directives — those need semantic reading. Run one readonly-verifier-driven pass that scores each of the 34 agent prompts against a five-point rubric and emits docs/audits/agent-prompt-scorecard.md plus a ranked list of the weakest prompts to fix. team-execution's 25 reviewer/validator agents are the dominant surface and the highest payoff, since a vague reviewer prompt silently weakens consensus review. The kernel of the 100-reviewer flip is that the audit runs once, cheaply, and converts subjective prompt quality into a triaged backlog.
basis: First-principles: 25 of 34 fleet agent files are team-execution reviewers/validators whose output quality is a direct multiplier on consensus-review value (section 3 finding 2: consensus review catches defects green suites miss, 2 repos, operator-praised) — a weak reviewer prompt degrades that silently and no lint can detect semantic vagueness, so a rubric-scored read is the only mechanism that closes it. Any verify-class spawn here must use saga:readonly-verifier + worktree isolation per CLAUDE.md.
outcome_shape: Merged docs/audits/agent-prompt-scorecard.md (rubric + per-agent scores) plus a prioritized set of follow-up issues for the lowest-scoring prompts; verified by the scorecard covering all 34 agent files and each low score citing a specific missing rubric element (e.g. no output contract).

title: Fleet code-review manifest: risk-tiered scope instead of uniform coverage
idea: Flip 'review every line of every plugin equally' (infinite reviewers) versus 'review nothing' and land on the practical middle: a declarative review manifest that assigns each plugin's review-critical surfaces a risk tier, which saga:code-review consumes to drive a comprehensive-but-scoped pass. The fleet's Python surface is uneven — mission-control's CLI + vendored issue-contract, team-execution's artifact_pointer.py and 25 agents, saga's execution_spec/lifecycle scripts, and marketplace/validator — and a flat pass wastes the budget the intake brief is trying to protect. The manifest (plugin -> {paths, risk_tier, review_lenses}) makes the scope explicit, repeatable, and auditable, and becomes the input to a first comprehensive campaign whose findings land as a triaged backlog.
basis: Directly grounded in the verified plugin/script inventory: 8 plugins, mission-control vendors an issue-contract with its own parity gate (ci.yml:33-40), team-execution carries artifact_pointer.py + 25 agents (CLAUDE.md hybrid note + verified count), saga carries execution_spec.py / lifecycle_state.py (grounding §1), marketplace/validator/validate.py exists — a heterogeneous risk surface that a uniform review under the intake brief's explicit budget-protection posture (tension 1/4) would spend against evenly and wastefully.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding docs/reviews/fleet-review-manifest.(toml|md) consumed by saga:code-review's scope selection, plus the first campaign's triaged findings as issues; verified by saga:code-review reading the manifest and producing a per-plugin scoped review rather than a flat diff pass.

title: Producer/consumer parity guard: no contract key alive on only one end
idea: Flip dead-wiring's core lesson to an absolute: every contract key must be proven present on BOTH the producer and the consumer, or CI fails. ENGINE_INTENTS is authored in saga /plan and rendered in team-execution's Step A7 worker table — a classic producer/consumer pair where a key added on one side and forgotten on the other is invisible to any green single-side test. Ship tests/test_producer_consumer_parity.py that statically extracts the ENGINE_INTENTS key set from execution_spec.py and cross-references the keys referenced by the team-execution worker-table renderer + references/external-engine-workers.md, failing if either side carries a key the other lacks. Generalize the harness to a small registry of (producer, consumer) pairs so future contracts inherit the same both-ends-proven guard.
basis: Grounding brief section 1 correction (c): 'ENGINE_INTENTS is a producer/consumer pair — authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233, -> references/external-engine-workers.md)'. Section 6 pattern 1: 'dead-wiring producer+consumer' is a recurring learning requiring 'did it actually run/persist' verification. This engages ENGINE_INTENTS without contradicting {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (it verifies wiring, not gatekeeper role).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tests/test_producer_consumer_parity.py + a small pairs registry; verified by adding a synthetic ENGINE_INTENTS key with no consumer reference on a branch and confirming the test fails naming the orphaned key.

title: Fake-adapter registry with mandatory real-contract shadow
idea: Flip 'tests may use any convenient fake' to the extreme 'zero fakes are allowed to exist unshadowed.' The mined failure is fake-adapter suites that stay green while the real interface has drifted, hiding a real mismatch. Introduce a convention + guard: every test double must be registered in tests/fakes_registry.py naming the real class/protocol it stands in for, and a signature-parity test asserts the fake's public method signatures match the real adapter's at import time — so a real adapter gaining or renaming a method makes the fake fail CI instead of silently lying. The kernel of the no-fakes flip is not deleting fakes but forbidding a fake from drifting away from the contract it impersonates.
basis: Grounding brief section 6 pattern 1 lists 'fake-adapter mismatch' and 'test-shape-masks-dead-wiring' among 5+ delegation/dead-wiring learnings, concluding 'any bridge/delegation idea needs did-it-actually-run/persist verification'. This targets that exact recorded learning: a fake adapter that outlives the real contract's shape. Reasoned mechanism (import-time signature parity) is the enforcement, but the supporting basis is the direct journal learning.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tests/fakes_registry.py + tests/test_fake_contract_parity.py + a CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md note on the convention; verified by renaming a method on a real adapter and confirming the registered fake's parity test fails.

title: Tier-lever decision contract cited by every judgment command, not just /plan
idea: Today the 'surface the tier table, confirm-or-override, do not lock silently' lever lives only inside /plan's ExecutionSpec authoring — /ideate, /brainstorm, and /work's interactive flow ask nothing about model/effort. Extract the decision-point behavior into a shared `plugins/saga/references/tier-lever.md` contract (auto-recommend + always-confirm, mirroring how `operator-choice.md` is cited fleet-wide) and add 2-3 line offer hooks to the other judgment-stage SKILLs so the operator meets the same lever wherever spend is committed. A drift-guard test asserts each named SKILL cites the doc, the way operator-choice offers are checked. This turns one buried lever into a fleet convention.
basis: `plan/SKILL.md:306-307` ('present the full tier table ... ask the operator to confirm or override before proceeding. Do not lock tiers silently') is the fleet's ONLY operator-facing tier lever (grounding brief §1); §1 also states ENGINE_INTENTS/tier surfacing is 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow.' Engages `{#operator-choice-framework}` revisit-when — its doc-first-then-cite pattern already fired across command rebuilds — extending the same auto-recommend+always-confirm contract to tiers is aligned, not contradicting.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/tier-lever.md` + offer-hook lines in `skills/ideate/SKILL.md`, `skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md`, `skills/work/SKILL.md`, plus `plugins/saga/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` + `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + `plugins/saga/CHANGELOG.md` version bump; verified by a new citation drift-guard test in tests/ asserting each SKILL references the doc anchor.

title: Run-start tier posture asked once, seeding the per-unit table instead of per-unit interrogation
idea: The per-unit confirm loop asks about tiers after the whole table is built, which is late and repetitive; the intake resolution says the spend lever should be 'asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation.' Add a single run-start posture selector (thrifty / balanced / premium, mode-aware: unattended defaults thrifty-silent, attended surfaces the choice) that seeds every unit's default tier before the table is rendered, so the operator confirms a table already shaped by their posture rather than reasoning rung-by-rung. The posture becomes a field on the ExecutionSpec so /work re-emits it and the choice survives. This moves the decision point earlier and collapses N per-unit micro-decisions into one.
basis: Intake brief §Resolved tensions 1: 'Asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation' and unattended→silent-cache-first / attended→always-ask asymmetry. Grounding §7 pattern 6: 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses' + 'manual per-unit tier tables' — the current per-unit locus (`plan/SKILL.md:306`) is the friction. Engages intake tension 1's mode-based rule directly.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `posture` field + validation to `plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py` and a run-start posture step to `plan/SKILL.md` §5.2a; verified by an execution_spec unit test asserting posture seeds per-unit defaults and round-trips through to_dict, plus release-surface bump.

title: Mandatory 'worth it, because…' + named cheaper fallback on every above-baseline tier row
idea: The /plan tier table has a Rationale column but no per-row cheaper fallback, and Fable appears only as 'available as a per-unit override, never a default' with no worth-it justification. Make every row above the sonnet/medium baseline (opus, fable, xhigh) carry two required fields: a one-line 'worth it because…' and the explicitly named adjacent-cheaper rung it beats, computed from the ordered tier ladder via the same index arithmetic segment_units() already uses. The validator hard-blocks an above-baseline unit that ships without both. This makes premium spend always self-justifying and always one keystroke from a documented downgrade.
basis: Intake brief §Resolved tensions 4: 'Fable-tier line in any plan or issue carries recommendation plus cheaper fallback; expensive never silent default.' `plan/SKILL.md:304` shows fable is mentioned but with no fallback field. `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` (LEARNINGS.md:164-179) confirms MODELS/EFFORTS are ordered ladders whose adjacent-cheaper rung is computable by index arithmetic — engaged directly as the mechanism for naming the fallback.
outcome_shape: PR editing `plan/SKILL.md` §5.2a tier-table spec + adding `fallback`/`justification` fields with validate() hard-block in `execution_spec.py`; verified by a new test asserting an above-baseline unit missing either field fails validate, plus release-surface bump.

title: tier_recommender.py — the work-shape→tier heuristic as a callable, killing ad hoc re-derivation
idea: The work-shape→tier heuristic lives as prose in `plan/SKILL.md:298-304` that the agent re-reasons from scratch every plan, which is exactly the mined 'ad hoc tier reasoning every time / hand-build tier tables' pain. Extract it into a deterministic `plugins/saga/scripts/tier_recommender.py` (work-shape signals → {model, effort, rationale, fallback}) — the tier analog of the already-shipped `recommend_execution_backend()` helper. /plan calls it to pre-fill the table the operator then confirms, so the reasoning is consistent, testable, and no longer hand-rebuilt. An oracle test pins the mapping so a future model addition surfaces loudly.
basis: Grounding §7 pattern 6: 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time; xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables (3 repos).' `{#operator-choice-framework}` revisit-when — 'wire the CLI-backed helper against this doc' — already fired for backend recommendation (`recommend_execution_backend()` shipped 0.10.0); this idea applies the same doc→callable maturation to the tier heuristic, engaging that decision's pattern rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: New `plugins/saga/scripts/tier_recommender.py` + oracle test in tests/, with `plan/SKILL.md` §5.2a Step 1 calling it instead of prose re-derivation; verified by the oracle test and a plan-SKILL citation, plus release-surface bump.

title: Validator-enforced spend asymmetry — cheaper moves silent, spend-increasing moves block for yes
idea: The intake rule says cheap/cheaper paths proceed silently while any spend-increasing choice always requires an explicit operator yes, but nothing enforces the asymmetry — an operator can silently escalate every unit to opus/xhigh. Add a spend-delta check to execution_spec validate: compare each authored unit's tier to the recommender's baseline via the ordered-ladder index arithmetic; a same-or-cheaper delta passes silently, any spend-increasing delta (up-ladder, or verify N above the recommended panel) emits a 'SPEND-INCREASE: requires operator confirm' band that mirrors the existing VERIFY_N_WARN 'surface, don't silently run' precedent. Unattended mode may auto-accept the cheaper side only; the increase always halts.
basis: Intake brief §Resolved tensions 1: 'any spend-increasing choice ... always requires explicit operator yes. Cache-first only silent default.' Existing precedent `execution_spec.py:111-118` (VERIFY_N_CAP/VERIFY_N_WARN — 'big panels are legal but smell like the overcorrection, so they are surfaced, not silently run') is the exact enforcement shape to mirror; `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` supplies the index arithmetic for computing the delta direction.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `spend_delta` warn-band to `execution_spec.py` validate() (baseline from tier_recommender) + doc in `plan/SKILL.md`; verified by tests asserting cheaper-move → silent, up-ladder-move → SPEND-INCREASE band, plus release-surface bump.

title: Per-repo tier defaults so the operator stops rebuilding the same table every run
idea: Operators hand-build the same per-unit tier table run after run because there is no place to remember 'in THIS repo, mechanical work is haiku/low and reviews are opus/high.' Add a committed, operator-owned `.saga/tier-defaults.json` (posture + per-work-shape overrides) that tier_recommender loads as its baseline before /plan surfaces the table, so a confirmed table is remembered and the next run starts from the operator's settled preference, not the generic heuristic. Because this is a preference config, not derived run state, it is git-committable and shareable — distinct from machine-local saga state.
basis: Grounding §7 pattern 6: 'manual per-unit tier tables ... ad hoc tier reasoning every time (3 repos).' Intake tension 1 wants a 'mode-based recommendation ... asked once per run start' — a remembered per-repo default is what makes 'asked once' stick across runs. Engages the `/outcome` campaign binding ('never committed status fields; derived-on-read') by being operator-authored preference config, explicitly NOT derived run/status state, so it does not cross that constraint.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `.saga/tier-defaults.json` loader to `tier_recommender.py`/`execution_spec.py` + `plan/SKILL.md` reading it as baseline + a documented schema/example file; verified by a test using a fixture defaults file asserting it overrides the generic heuristic, plus release-surface bump.

title: Relative-cost preview on the tier table plus realized-vs-estimated reconciliation after the run
idea: The operator confirms tier tables blind to spend: /plan shows no cost estimate before, and /work shows no realized cost after, even though /outcome already records leaf-produced cost.
