Add an index-weighted RELATIVE cost column (normalized to sonnet/medium = 1.0, deliberately not dollar-precise to avoid false precision) to the surfaced tier table so the operator sees the shape of the spend before confirming, and a post-run 'realized vs estimated' reconciliation line in the /work summary fed by the same leaf cost ledger. This closes the loop that lets 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' actually be seen and corrected.
basis: Grounding §1 + DECISIONS.md:735 revisit-when: `/outcome` `record_cost` produces per-leaf cost as a 'leaf-produced fact' — the realized-cost substrate already exists but is not surfaced at the tier-choice point. Engages the `/outcome` campaign binding ('cost ledger = leaf-produced fact', derived-on-read) by keeping the pre-run figure a non-committed ESTIMATE and the post-run figure the existing leaf-produced fact — never a committed status field. No-false-precision posture mirrors the ported qa_health_score restraint.
outcome_shape: PR adding a relative-cost estimator to the tier-table render (`plan/SKILL.md` + a helper in `execution_spec.py`/`tier_recommender.py`) and a realized-vs-estimated line in `work/SKILL.md`'s summary sourced from the leaf cost ledger; verified by a unit test on the estimator normalization, plus release-surface bump.

title: /retro tier-efficacy pass — evidence-tuned defaults from past cost-vs-outcome, not vibes
idea: Tier defaults are set by heuristic and gut; nobody checks whether the opus/xhigh units actually produced something the adjacent-cheaper rung would not have. Add a /retro pass that mines completed runs' recorded per-leaf cost against their outcomes (findings surfaced, review verdicts, rework) and proposes evidence-backed adjustments to the per-repo tier defaults — e.g. 'the last 6 mechanical units ran opus/high at 3x baseline cost with zero findings the recommender wouldn't have gotten at sonnet/medium; downgrade default.' Proposals are gated diffs to `.saga/tier-defaults.json`, never auto-applied. This is the compounding answer to 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' — the recommender learns from realized spend.
basis: First-principles: the mined claim 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' (grounding §7 pattern 6) is an assertion no current mechanism can confirm or refute, yet the two inputs to test it now both exist — per-leaf realized cost (`/outcome` `record_cost` ledger) and per-run outcome signals (/code-review findings, /qa verdicts). A /retro pass joining them turns a repeated gut complaint into a falsifiable, gated default adjustment; it rides /retro's existing tiered self-edit gate (pure-additive auto, modify-existing propose-and-wait) so no new approval machinery is needed and no binding decision is crossed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a tier-efficacy pass to `plugins/saga/skills/retro/SKILL.md` that reads the cost ledger + review/qa signals and emits a gated diff proposal against `.saga/tier-defaults.json`; verified by a fixture-driven test that a synthetic 'overspent, zero marginal finding' history yields a downgrade proposal, plus release-surface bump.

title: Auto-derived tier table: kill the hand-built ad hoc table
idea: Today /plan Step 1 tells the author to 'Apply the heuristic per unit' by hand and 'present the full tier table' before locking. Remove the hand-authoring entirely: a tier_recommender.py CLI reads the plan's Implementation Units (each tagged with a work-shape keyword) and deterministically emits the full tier table from the existing work-shape->tier heuristic (plan/SKILL.md:298-304). Every row is auto-populated with the recommended {model,effort}, a one-line 'worth it because...' rationale, and a cheaper fallback tier one rung down the MODELS/EFFORTS ladder. The operator reviews a generated table instead of building one, and the mined 'operators hand-build tier tables ad hoc' step disappears.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:296-307 'For each Implementation Unit... assign a {model, effort} tier from the work-shape heuristic... Apply the heuristic per unit, then present the full tier table... Do not lock tiers silently' — the manual step F2 removes. The cheaper-fallback column engages binding decision {#tier-vocab-ordering} (revisit-when: tiers stop being ordered ladders) by treating MODELS/EFFORTS index-1 as the fallback rung, which relies on the ordering being an escalation ladder — consistent, not crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_recommender.py + tests/test_tier_recommender.py, and rewriting plan/SKILL.md Step 1 to call it. Verified by unit tests asserting each documented work-shape maps to the exact tier + fallback in the heuristic table, and a golden-render test of a sample unit list.

title: Spend gate: silence the cheap path, only ask when spend rises
idea: The intake settled that cheap-or-equal choices proceed silently and only spend-increasing choices require an explicit operator yes — but that is prose, not machinery. Automate the classification away from human judgment: a spend_gate.py compares a proposed tier against the locked baseline using the ordered MODELS/EFFORTS indices; cheaper-or-equal auto-applies with a log line, spend-increasing (up the model ladder or up the effort ladder, and any fable/xhigh reach) halts for an explicit yes. Wire it into the plan tier-lock and any future dispatch override so the operator is never prompted for a downgrade and never NOT prompted for an escalation.
basis: Intake brief tension 1 lines 31-35: 'any spend-increasing choice (parallel fan-out, cache churn, tier escalation) always requires an explicit operator yes. Cache-first is the only silent default... This lever is itself a design requirement... plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded cache-first mandate.' Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} (revisit-when: tuples stop being ordered ladders) — the asymmetry IS the ladder comparison, so it depends on and reinforces that ordering rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/spend_gate.py (classify_change(baseline, proposed) -> 'silent'|'ask') + tests, plus integration at the plan tier-lock site. Verified by tests asserting haiku/sonnet-low downgrades classify 'silent' while opus, fable, and xhigh escalations classify 'ask'.

title: Per-repo tier defaults: stop re-asking the same question every plan
idea: Every plan re-derives tiers from scratch with zero memory, so the operator re-confirms the same overrides run after run. Remove the repeated confirmation: persist confirmed work-shape->tier overrides in a per-repo .saga/tier-defaults.json (doc/CLI-driven, git-ignorable), and have the recommender pre-fill from it, prompting only on deltas from remembered preference. The second plan in a repo reuses the operator's earlier judgment silently; the ad hoc re-derivation step is gone.
basis: Grounding brief session-mining pattern #6 (lines 132-134): 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking mid-run model-change pauses.' Engages binding decision {#operator-choice-framework} (revisit-when it stops being doc-only/CLI-driven): the defaults file is a CLI-read config artifact, not a runtime-injected blob, so it stays inside that decision's envelope.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a .saga/tier-defaults.json schema + read/write helpers in the recommender + plan/SKILL.md Step 1 wiring + tests. Verified by a test that runs the recommender twice: the second run reuses a stored override without re-emitting a prompt for that work-shape.

title: Pre-run cost preview beside the tier table (before AND after)
idea: The operator is asked to approve spend-increasing tiers with no spend magnitude in front of them — a yes/no on cost with no number. Invert the blind spend: a tier_cost_preview.py computes a relative-cost figure per unit (model price-weight x effort-weight x unit/target count), totals it, and renders it as a column in the tier table BEFORE lock; after the run, the /outcome leaf-produced cost ledger is diffed against the preview and surfaced as an estimate-vs-actual note. Cost becomes visible on both sides of the decision instead of only after the money is spent.
basis: First principles: tension 1's asymmetric-approval rule and tension 4's Fable-recommendation rule both demand the operator judge 'is this spend worth it,' yet no spend magnitude is surfaced at decision time — consent to cost without a number is uninformed. The /outcome binding decision fixes 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (derived-on-read); this idea explicitly keeps the preview a pre-run ESTIMATE (never a committed status field) and treats the leaf ledger as the authoritative actual it reconciles against, so it consumes the leaf fact read-only rather than crossing the derive-on-read rule.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_cost_preview.py + a cost column in the plan tier-table render + a post-run reconciliation note reading the leaf ledger + tests. Verified by unit tests on the cost-weight function and a golden estimate-vs-actual reconciliation over a sample ledger.

title: One dispatch-time tier resolver seam instead of N hardcoded model: fields
idea: The lever exists at exactly one authoring point (cc-workflows-ultracode plan tiers); every other spawn — team-execution workers, verify-panel judges, readonly-verifier calls — hardcodes model with no override. Rather than sprinkle a prompt at every spawn (noise the operator will hate), collapse the 'which decision points ask' question to ONE: a resolve_tier(unit, repo_defaults, session_override) resolver that all spawn sites funnel through, so the lever is set once at run start and applied everywhere. A drift-guard test enumerates spawn sites and asserts each routes through the resolver, mirroring the existing sandbox-spawn-sites.md inventory discipline.
basis: Grounding brief §1 lines 18-20: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields... no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern.' Engages {#operator-choice-framework} (revisit-when it stops being doc-only/CLI-driven): a single CLI-invoked resolver reading config keeps operator-choice CLI-driven and centralizes it rather than injecting runtime blobs.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_resolver.py, refactoring execution_spec._agent_opts and the team worker-table render to call it, plus a spawn-site drift-guard test (list of sites, each asserted to route through resolve_tier). Verified by that enumeration test and by existing emit/render tests staying green.

title: Hard-block any fable/xhigh line lacking a worth-it justification + fallback
idea: Fable and xhigh are the premium reaches, and the intake mandates every such line carry a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback — but nothing enforces it, so a wasteful premium default can still slip through silently. Remove the possibility: extend execution_spec.py validate so any unit whose tier is fable OR xhigh REQUIRES a populated tier_justification and fallback_tier, raising SpecError on emit otherwise (the same fail-loud posture as R3/R10 today). Premium spend can never be a silent default because an unjustified premium tier no longer emits.
basis: Intake brief tension 4 lines 60-63: 'every Fable-tier line in any plan or issue carries a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback; expensive is never a silent default (mirrors tension 1).' Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} (revisit-when tuples stop being ordered ladders): fallback_tier is validated to be a strictly-cheaper rung on the MODELS/EFFORTS ladder, which depends on the ordering being an escalation ladder — consistent with the decision.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a Tier/Unit validate rule in execution_spec.py (fable|xhigh => tier_justification + fallback_tier required, fallback must be a lower ladder rung) + tests + a plan/SKILL.md note + CHANGELOG/plugin.json version bump. Verified by tests asserting an unjustified fable/xhigh unit raises SpecError and a justified one validates.

title: /tier session ceiling: automate away the mid-run model-change pause
idea: Session mining caught operators pausing mid-run to ask for a model change — a manual interruption with no lever. Replace the pause with a persisted session ceiling: a /tier command writes a run-scoped cap (e.g. 'nothing above sonnet/medium this run') to a session-local override file, honored by the tier resolver so all subsequent spawns clamp to it without re-prompting. The operator sets intent once and the run self-enforces it; the recurring interrupt-and-negotiate step is removed.
basis: Grounding brief session-mining pattern #6 line 133: 'operator asking mid-run model-change pauses' (ranked recurring pain across 3 repos). Engages {#operator-choice-framework} (revisit-when it stops being doc-only/CLI-driven): /tier is a CLI command writing a config file the resolver reads, staying within the CLI-driven operator-choice envelope rather than introducing runtime injection.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a /tier command doc + a session-override file schema + resolver clamp logic + tests. Verified by a test that sets a sonnet/medium ceiling and asserts a subsequently-resolved opus/high unit is clamped to the ceiling with a logged downgrade and no prompt.

title: Spend retro: make 'xhigh-Opus is wasteful' a measured fact, not a belief
idea: The mined complaint 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' is an assertion nobody has measured — and the validation-discipline rule forbids asserting cost claims without a source. Automate the never-happens reflection: a spend_retro.py aggregates the /outcome leaf-produced cost ledgers across completed sagas into a per-repo engineering-journal summary — tier-mix vs outcome, premium spend vs delivered value — so the operator can see whether xhigh-Opus actually paid off historically. The output feeds sharper future recommendations, closing the loop that currently leaves the wasteful-default belief unfalsifiable.
basis: First principles: the theme's own mined premise 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' is a cost claim with no measurement behind it; under the validation-discipline rule (no cost claim without a current source) the fleet cannot even confirm the pain it is optimizing. The leaf cost ledgers already exist as facts; aggregating them read-only is the only way to falsify or confirm the belief. Engages the /outcome binding 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact / derived-on-read' — spend_retro consumes leaf facts read-only and writes a derived summary, never a committed status field, staying inside the decision.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/spend_retro.py that reads leaf ledgers and emits a docs/engineering-journal spend-summary table + tests over sample ledgers. Verified by a golden-summary test asserting the aggregate tier-mix and premium-share figures match a fixture set of leaf ledgers.

title: Lever-placement census: stop treating the tier prompt as a /plan-only afterthought
idea: T12 silently assumes the operator's model/effort lever belongs to /plan alone, because that is the one command that grew a tier table. Reframe one level up: every command that spawns agents is a lever-placement site, and the fleet has never audited which sites ask. Ship a lever-placement census doc that inventories every agent-spawn point across the 8 plugins (saga /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow, team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch) and marks each as asks / silent-hardcoded, then a follow-up PR that wires a single shared spend-posture prompt into the entry of the currently-silent judgment-stage commands. The census is the deliverable that turns 'we hardcode model everywhere' from folklore into a tracked gap list.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow.' Grounding §1: 'no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern.' Direct evidence the lever exists at exactly one placement site while judgment-stage commands spawn agents blind.
outcome_shape: A merged doc plugins/saga/references/lever-placement-census.md enumerating every agent-spawn site with an asks/silent column, plus a PR adding the spend-posture prompt to /ideate and /brainstorm entry. Verified by a drift-guard test that greps for Task/agent-spawn call sites and fails if a new spawn site is absent from the census table.

title: Extract the hand-authored work-shape tier table into a tier_resolver that emits 'because' + cheaper fallback
idea: The work-shape heuristic at plan/SKILL.md lines 298-304 is prose in a markdown file that an LLM re-interprets ad hoc every run — this is exactly the mined 'operators hand-build tier tables ad hoc' pain, just relocated into a skill. Reframe: the table is a pure function of task features (judgment vs mechanical vs read-only vs offload vs second-opinion), so stop asking an agent to re-derive it and ship a tier_resolver.py that takes a work-shape descriptor and returns {model, effort, rationale, cheaper_fallback}. The resolver makes the intake tension-4 rule ('recommendation plus cheaper fallback; expensive never silent default') machinery instead of a hope, and /plan renders resolver output rather than re-authoring prose. Every row carries a stated 'Fable, worth it, because…' plus the one-notch-cheaper alternative by construction.
basis: plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md:298-304 is a hand-embedded work-shape → tier prose table an LLM interprets each run; session-mining pattern 6 (grounding §7): 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time... manual per-unit tier tables.' Intake §4: cheaper-fallback must always accompany the recommendation.
outcome_shape: Merged plugins/saga/scripts/tier_resolver.py with unit tests over the five work-shape cases, and plan/SKILL.md §5.2a edited to call it. Verified by pytest asserting each shape yields a rationale string and a strictly-cheaper fallback tuple (by MODELS/EFFORTS index), respecting the tier-vocab ordering.

title: Budget envelope: replace per-decision yes/no with a once-set spend threshold
idea: The intake asymmetry rule treats approval as a binary asked at every spend-increasing choice, which quietly assumes the operator wants to be interrupted per decision. Reframe one level up: approval is a threshold policy, not a per-gate interrupt — the operator sets a run-scoped budget envelope once, spend-increasing choices below the remaining envelope proceed silently, and only a choice that would cross it asks. This preserves the asymmetry (cheap silent, expensive asks) while collapsing N interrupts into one up-front commitment, and it degrades safely: an unattended run with no envelope set falls back to the cache-tight silent default. The envelope is a first-class field on the run/spec, decremented by leaf-produced cost facts.
basis: Intake §1: 'any spend-increasing choice (parallel fan-out, cache churn, tier escalation) always requires explicit operator yes... Asked once per run start.' The 'asked once' aspiration is undermined the moment there are many spend-increasing choices; a threshold is the only shape that keeps 'asked once' literally true. Compatible with {#operator-choice-framework} (doc-only/CLI-driven): the envelope is a CLI-set field, not a new autonomous gate.
outcome_shape: A PR adding a spend_envelope field to the ExecutionSpec/outcome run spec plus gate logic that only prompts when a choice crosses the remaining envelope. Verified by a test simulating a sequence of sub-threshold choices (zero prompts) then a crossing choice (one prompt).

title: Give the repo a spend personality: persisted per-repo tier defaults that seed every run
idea: T12 assumes tier preferences are ephemeral — rebuilt from the prose heuristic every single run — which is why operators hand-assemble the same tables repeatedly. Reframe: the repo itself carries a durable spend personality. Ship a per-repo .saga/tier-prefs.json (git-ignored, machine-local like saga state) that records remembered defaults (default posture, a repo's habitual per-work-shape tier overrides, its attended/unattended lean), which the tier resolver reads to pre-seed the tier table so the operator confirms a remembered posture instead of rebuilding one. This is distinct from the QUEUED per-teammate-effort seed: that is plan-dictated per-agent effort inside one plan; this is a cross-command repo-level memory that outlives any single plan.
basis: Session-mining pattern 6 (grounding §7): 'manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses' — repeated re-derivation is the pain. Explicitly NOT the §5 QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} seed (that is plan-scoped per-teammate effort). Machine-local git-ignored file matches saga state convention (plan/SKILL.md §5.3: 'saga state is git-ignored, machine-local').
outcome_shape: A PR adding .saga/tier-prefs.json read/write helpers and resolver seeding, plus a documented schema. Verified by a test: a written prefs file changes the resolver's default output for a work shape, and an absent file reproduces today's heuristic exactly.

title: Cost as a forecast-then-variance loop, not a post-hoc receipt
idea: Today cost surfaces only as the /outcome leaf-produced ledger fact — a receipt you read after the money is gone. Reframe one level up: spend-observability is a feedback loop, not a receipt. Before a run, render a spend forecast from the resolved tier table (per-unit tier × expected calls) that the operator can veto; after, compute variance = forecast vs the actual leaf-produced ledger, and record it so the tier recommendations can be calibrated over time. This engages the /outcome binding: the actual cost ledger stays a leaf-produced fact and status stays derived-on-read — the forecast is a separate pre-run artifact and variance is a pure comparison, never a committed cost field. The payoff is that 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' becomes visible before the spend, not lamented after.
basis: Grounding §2 binding: /outcome campaign — 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (post-hoc only). Session-mining pattern 6 / theme constraint: 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' — waste is currently only discoverable retrospectively. Engaged constraint: forecast/variance are separate artifacts, so the leaf-produced-fact and derived-on-read invariants hold.
outcome_shape: A PR adding a pre-run forecast renderer (consuming resolved tiers) and a post-run variance line in the /outcome cost report, touching outcome cost-ledger code + report doc. Verified by a test asserting forecast is produced pre-dispatch and variance equals forecast minus the recorded leaf ledger.

title: Relative lever: 'one notch cheaper / dearer' instead of re-picking from a closed enum
idea: The lever forces the operator to pick an absolute tier out of the closed MODELS/EFFORTS enums, which assumes operators reason in absolute coordinates. But execution_spec.py comments say the tuples are load-bearing ordered ladders, and operators actually reason in deltas from the recommendation ('cheaper than you proposed'). Reframe: expose a relative lever at the decision point — as-proposed / one-notch-cheaper / one-notch-dearer — that walks the ladder by one index using the same min/max ordering the emitter already trusts, instead of demanding a fresh absolute selection. This engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} by making the ordering the interaction mechanism, not just an internal merge rule. It is a smaller, faster affordance that matches how the mined operators talk about tier.
basis: plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:49-53: 'ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING... MODELS is strongest-first and EFFORTS is weakest-first' via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index). Binding {#tier-vocab-ordering}: 'Tier tuples are ordered escalation ladders' — this idea uses that ordering as the lever's motion, not a contradiction of it.
outcome_shape: A PR adding a relative-adjust helper (tier, direction) → adjacent tier in execution_spec.py and a plan/SKILL.md override-step edit offering the three-way relative choice. Verified by unit tests over ladder boundaries (cheapest can't go cheaper; dearest can't go dearer).

title: Encode the mode→posture mapping as machinery, not prose buried in an intake brief
idea: The intake declares a mode-dependent spend posture (unattended → cache-tight silent; attended → throughput-recommended-but-always-ask), but that rule lives only as prose in a planning doc — nothing in the fleet resolves it, so every command re-improvises. Reframe: the (run-mode → default posture + approval asymmetry) mapping is itself a first-class policy object the intake even calls 'a design requirement,' so ship a spend_posture.py that takes run-mode and returns the default posture plus the asymmetric-approval rule, consumed uniformly by saga, team-execution, and /outcome. This makes the recommendation mode-aware by construction — the same work shape recommends differently unattended vs attended — instead of a mode-blind table. It is the connective tissue that idea T12-F3-1 (placement), T12-F3-2 (resolver), and T12-F3-3 (envelope) all consult.
basis: Intake §1: 'Unattended runs → cache-tight serial, may proceed silently. Attended runs → throughput recommended, but any spend-increasing choice always requires explicit operator yes... mode-based recommendation. This lever is itself a design requirement resulting in issues plugins encode as a question, not a hard-coded cache-first mandate.' The rule is explicitly designated machinery-to-be, currently unimplemented.
outcome_shape: A merged plugins/saga/scripts/spend_posture.py returning (default_posture, approval_rule) keyed on run-mode, referenced from saga + team-execution spawn docs. Verified by tests asserting unattended yields silent/cache-tight and attended yields ask-on-spend-increase.

title: Extract the work-shape tier heuristic into one shared tier-policy registry
idea: The fleet's only tier recommender is a prose markdown table hardcoded at plan/SKILL.md:298-305; execution_spec.py only validates that authored tiers draw from the closed MODELS/EFFORTS sets, it never recommends. Promote that heuristic into a single machine-readable registry (plugins/saga/references/tier-policy.json: work-shape key -> {default_tier, rationale, cheaper_fallback}) plus a thin tier_advisor.py resolver every lever calls. Any command that proposes a tier (/plan, /work, future /tier, team-execution worker table) renders identical 'tier X because <rationale>; cheaper fallback Y' lines from one source. Second-order compounding: sharpening a rationale once improves every operator-facing recommendation in the fleet at once, and new spawn sites inherit quality for free instead of re-deriving a table by hand.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:298-305 holds the heuristic as prose-only ('Judgment...opus/high','Mechanical...sonnet/medium'); execution_spec.py:46-53 comment states 'The emitter does not invent tiers; it only validates that authored tiers are drawn from these closed sets' — i.e. no recommender primitive exists, only a validator. Engages {#operator-choice-framework}: registry stays a doc/config artifact consumed CLI-side, not a runtime-injected mandate.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/tier-policy.json + plugins/saga/scripts/tier_advisor.py, refactoring plan/SKILL.md Step 1 to render from it, with a drift-guard test asserting the SKILL prose and JSON stay in sync. Verified: tier_advisor.py resolve('judgment') returns opus/high + rationale + fallback; drift test fails if the table and JSON diverge.

title: A model/effort lever-site inventory registry, mirroring sandbox-spawn-sites.md
idea: Grounding brief finds 'no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern' and every agent frontmatter hardcodes model with zero effort fields. The sandbox theme already solved the analogous problem with plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md — a canonical inventory of every spawn site and the containment each must satisfy, backed by a drift-guard. Build the tier analogue: a lever-sites.md registry enumerating every place a model/effort tier is chosen across all 8 plugins (agent frontmatter, plan tier table, team-execution worker table, readonly-verifier calls, /outcome dispatch), tagging each as lever-exposed or hardcoded and why. Compounding: it becomes the checklist a new spawn site must satisfy, converting 'we forgot to add a lever here' from a discovered defect into a failing test, and giving the whole fleet a single map of where operators can and cannot intervene.
basis: CLAUDE.md cites plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md as the existing 'full spawn-site inventory and rationale' pattern; grounding brief section 1 states the lever-placement gap ('no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier'). This is that proven inventory pattern applied to the tier axis.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/lever-sites.md (one row per tier-decision site: location, exposed?, rationale) + a coverage test that greps agent frontmatter/skill tables and fails if a tier-choosing site is absent from the registry. Verified: test flags an added agent that hardcodes model without a registry row.

title: A shared spend-delta classifier that derives silent-vs-ask from tier ordering
idea: Intake tension 1 mandates an asymmetric rule: cheapening paths proceed silently, spend-increasing paths always ask. The load-bearing insight is already in execution_spec.py: MODELS is strongest-first, EFFORTS weakest-first, and segment_units merges upgrade-only via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index). Reuse that exact ordering as a one-function primitive spend_delta(old_tier, new_tier) -> {cheapen|escalate|lateral} that every lever calls to decide whether to ask. Because the classifier is derived from the same ordered tuples the emitter already trusts, the asymmetric approval rule is enforced identically everywhere for free — no lever hand-rolls its own notion of 'more expensive'. Compounding: the intake rule stops being prose each plugin re-implements and becomes one tested function; adding a provider or an effort level updates the ordering once and every gate inherits it.
basis: execution_spec.py:49-53 'ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: segment_units() merges tiers upgrade-only via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index), so MODELS is strongest-first and EFFORTS is weakest-first'; intake brief tension 1 'any spend-increasing choice ... always requires an explicit operator yes. Cache-first is the only silent default'. Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} (tuples are ordered escalation ladders) — the classifier consumes that ordering rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding spend_delta() to execution_spec.py (or a shared tier module) + unit tests, and wiring plan Step 1 tier-override handling to gate on it. Verified: spend_delta('sonnet/medium','opus/high')=='escalate' (asks) while ('opus/high','sonnet/low')=='cheapen' (silent).

title: Per-repo tier defaults + remembered overrides so tier tables stop being hand-built each run
idea: Session mining ranks 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking mid-run model-change pauses' as a 3-repo recurring pain (grounding pattern 6). Add a per-repo .saga/tier-defaults.json that overlays the shared tier-policy registry: a repo can pin its own work-shape->tier defaults, and the last operator override per work-shape is remembered and re-proposed next run. The lever still asks on spend-increases (defers to idea T12-F4-3), but the starting table is the repo's accreted preference, not a from-scratch derivation. Compounding: each run's override makes the next run's table cheaper to confirm; a repo that has tuned its tiers reaches a near-zero-prompt steady state, which is the opposite of today's re-derive-every-time cost curve.
basis: Grounding brief section 6/7 pattern 6: 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos) -> theme 12'. Directly targets the persistence gap that makes each run pay the full derivation cost.
outcome_shape: PR adding .saga/tier-defaults.json schema + loader in tier_advisor.py (overlay precedence: repo defaults > shared registry) and remembered-override write-back, with a test that a pinned repo default overrides the shared table. Verified: two consecutive /plan runs — second proposes the first run's confirmed overrides without re-asking on unchanged shapes.

title: Estimate-then-reconcile spend envelope built on the leaf-produced cost ledger
idea: Cost today is invisible until after the fact. Add a two-sided observability lever: before tiers lock, tier_advisor renders an estimated relative-spend envelope from the proposed tier table (sum of per-unit tier weights); after the run, the /outcome cost ledger reconciles estimate-vs-actual and surfaces the delta, which also feeds the tier-policy sharpening loop. The estimate is strictly advisory and derived-on-read — it never commits a status/cost field — so it honors the outcome campaign's binding rule that the cost ledger is a leaf-produced fact, not an orchestrator-written one. Compounding: once every unit carries an estimate and reconciles against a real ledger, the fleet accumulates a growing corpus of estimate-vs-actual pairs that make both the estimate model and the tier recommendations progressively more honest.
basis: Grounding brief section 2 binding decision '/outcome campaign (U1-U11): ... cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' and 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields'. Idea explicitly engages that revisit boundary by keeping the pre-run estimate advisory/derived and reading (never writing) the leaf-produced ledger for reconciliation.
outcome_shape: PR adding an estimate renderer to tier_advisor.py + a post-run reconcile step that reads the existing cost ledger and prints estimate/actual/delta, with a test asserting no status field is written. Verified: a dry /plan prints an envelope; a completed /outcome leaf prints estimate-vs-actual from the ledger.

title: A mid-run /tier lever that re-emits from the canonical spec instead of restarting
idea: Mining records operators 'asking mid-run model-change pauses' — today changing a tier mid-flight means aborting and re-planning. But plan/SKILL.md:292 already establishes the ExecutionSpec JSON as 'the canonical artifact /work re-emits from ... the single source of truth'. Expose a thin /tier lever that, at a saga tick boundary, edits the tier of not-yet-run units in the spec JSON, re-validates, and re-emits the downstream workflow — leveraging the existing re-emit seam rather than building new machinery. It defers the ask decision to the spend-delta classifier (T12-F4-3) so a mid-run escalation prompts and a mid-run cheapen is silent. Compounding: because the lever rides the canonical-spec re-emit path, every backend that already re-emits from the spec inherits mid-run tier control with no per-backend work, and the spec stays the one diffable record of what tier ran what.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:291-293 'author a structured ExecutionSpec ... the spec JSON — not the prose plan — is the single source of truth (KTD1) ... the canonical artifact /work re-emits from'; grounding pattern 6 names 'operator asking mid-run model-change pauses'. The re-emit seam already exists; this places a lever on it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a /tier micro-command (or /work sub-action) that patches unrun units' tiers in the spec, runs execution_spec.py validate+emit, and gates via spend_delta. Verified: mid-run tier change on a pending unit re-emits a valid workflow and leaves already-run units untouched.

title: A tier-regret ledger that closes the loop from outcome back to the heuristic
idea: The tier heuristic never learns: it recommends the same thing regardless of whether last time opus produced a trivial diff or a haiku unit truncated. execution_spec.py:122 already bakes a BUDGET_RIDER into cheap-tier agents precisely because cheap tiers hit output budget — a truncated/partial emit under that rider is an observable under-provision signal, just as an opus unit finishing far under budget is an observable over-provision signal. Capture both as a per-unit tier-regret record (chosen_tier, shape, signal: over|under|right) appended when a unit completes, and periodically fold the aggregate back into tier-policy.json rationales and cheaper-fallback suggestions. This is the compounding engine behind the whole theme: recommendations get sharper because the fleet mines its own tier outcomes, turning 'xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful' from an operator complaint into a data-driven downgrade suggestion.
basis: First-principles: a recommender with no feedback signal cannot improve, so the heuristic table is frozen at authoring quality forever. Two concrete signals already exist in-code — the cheap-tier BUDGET_RIDER (execution_spec.py:120-128) makes truncation/partial-emit an under-provision tell, and an over-budget-headroom completion is an over-provision tell — so the regret signal is derivable without new instrumentation, only new capture. Feeds theme-12's mined 'xhigh-Opus wasteful' directly.
outcome_shape: PR adding a tier-regret record schema + an appender at unit completion + a fold-in script that proposes tier-policy.json rationale/fallback edits from aggregated regret. Verified: a seeded set of under-provision records makes the fold-in script emit a downgrade suggestion for that work-shape.

title: A shared ordinal cost-weight table so every plugin renders comparable spend
idea: For cost to be shown before and after in a comparable way, every lever needs a common unit — otherwise each plugin hand-rolls its own sense of 'expensive' (exactly the ad hoc reasoning mined in pattern 6). Add one shared cost_weights.json mapping each MODELS x EFFORTS cell to an ordinal relative-cost weight (consistent with the existing strongest-first/weakest-first ordering, so fable/xhigh is the ceiling and haiku/low the floor), plus a tiny helper that turns a tier list into a single comparable spend figure. This is deliberately ordinal (relative weights, not asserted dollar prices), so it stays a stable primitive independent of provider price changes. Compounding: the estimate lever (T12-F4-5), the spend-delta classifier (T12-F4-3), and any future provider-router all read the same weights, so 'how expensive is this' has exactly one fleet-wide answer and reachable fable/xhigh finally has a comparable cost position instead of being an unpriceable outlier.
basis: First-principles: comparable before/after cost display requires a shared unit; without one, each of the 8 plugins re-derives 'expensive', reproducing the mined ad hoc tier reasoning. Keeping weights ordinal (tied to execution_spec.py:52-53 ordering) rather than absolute prices avoids asserting provider pricing and makes the primitive stable across price changes. Engages the outcome cost-ledger boundary by being an estimate input only, never a written ledger fact.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/references/cost_weights.json (16 ordered cells) + a to_spend() helper, consumed by the estimate renderer, with a test asserting weight monotonicity along both ordered axes. Verified: to_spend of a fable/xhigh unit exceeds any haiku/low unit and ordering matches MODELS/EFFORTS indices.

title: Titrate-to-effect tier escalation: start cheap, climb only on a difficulty signal
idea: Borrow anesthesiology's titration-to-effect: rather than fixing the tier up front from a work-shape guess, every unit starts one rung below its heuristic default and the emitter watches a depth-of-difficulty signal (a verifier refute, a failed risk-gated test, or a unit's self-reported low-confidence return) as the escalation trigger. On a fired signal the unit re-runs at the next MODELS/EFFORTS index up the ordered ladder. This inverts the current lever placement from plan-time-only to signal-time, so cheap work that succeeds never pays for headroom it did not need. Because auto-escalation is spend-increasing, the intake asymmetric-approval rule applies: silent climb is permitted only in unattended/cache-tight runs; attended runs surface the escalation as an explicit ask before the re-run. The escalation ladder is exactly the ordered tuples the emitter already merges upgrade-only.
basis: Anesthesiology titration-to-effect: clinicians dose to the minimum effective level and escalate only on a monitored signal (Bispectral Index / depth-of-anesthesia monitors, standard in Miller's Anesthesia). Structurally analogous to escalating model tier only when a difficulty signal fires. Aligns with {#tier-vocab-ordering} (execution_spec.py:49-53 makes MODELS/EFFORTS ordered ladders merged upgrade-only) and engages the intake asymmetric-approval rule (silent only unattended) rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `escalate_on_signal` rung to execution_spec.py's segment/verify path plus a Step-1a subsection in plan/SKILL.md 5.2a; verified by a unit test asserting a refuted unit's re-emitted tier is exactly one index up MODELS or EFFORTS, and a second test asserting attended-mode escalation emits an ask gate rather than a silent re-run.

title: Sommelier tier rows: every tier carries a justification and a house-fallback
idea: Model the tier recommendation on a sommelier's pairing upsell, which never states a price without a reason and always offers a graceful cheaper pour. Restructure each row of the 5.2a tier table from a bare {model, effort} into a recommendation object: {tier, justification ('worth it because <specific reason grounded in this unit'), fallback_tier, fallback_tradeoff ('gives up X')}. The rule is absolute, mirroring intake tension 4: any Fable/xhigh line must carry both a spelled-out justification and a strictly cheaper fallback, so the expensive default is never silent. This turns the ad-hoc hand-built tier table into a schema the emitter can validate for completeness, killing 'xhigh-Opus on everything' by forcing the operator to see what each escalation buys and what the cheap path costs.
basis: Intake brief 2026-07-03-plugin-fleet-ideation-intake-brief.md lines 61-63: 'Fable-tier line in any plan or issue carries recommendation plus cheaper fallback; expensive never silent default.' Current plan/SKILL.md:298-307 rows carry a Rationale column but no structured fallback field and no schema enforcement, so the contract is prose-only and un-validated.
outcome_shape: PR converting plan/SKILL.md:298-307 rows to a recommendation schema and adding a `validate` check in execution_spec.py that a tier row at fable-or-xhigh without a populated fallback_tier + tradeoff fails emit; verified by a validator unit test on a fixture spec with a bare Fable row (expects non-zero exit) and a well-formed one (expects exit 0).

title: Delegation-of-authority matrix: per-repo signature thresholds for tier spend
idea: Import corporate procurement's delegation-of-authority (signature-authority) matrix, where a spend below a role's limit is auto-approved and anything above routes up for sign-off. Define a per-repo `.saga/spend-authority.json` that maps a tier ceiling to 'silent' and everything above it to 'ask', with optional per-lifecycle-stage overrides (e.g. code review may auto-approve opus/high, scaffolding may not). At emit time the resolver classifies every unit's tier against the matrix and stamps it silent or ask, making the intake asymmetric-approval rule a machine-checked property of the plan instead of an operator's memory. Cheap paths proceed with zero prompts; only the spend-increasing rows collect into a single batched approval, so the operator answers once for the whole escalation set.
basis: Corporate delegation-of-authority / signature-authority matrices (standard financial control; e.g. SOX-driven approval-limit tables documented in COSO internal-control frameworks) auto-clear spend under a threshold and require sign-off above it. Directly operationalizes the intake asymmetric-approval rule (intake §26-36) as config rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `.saga/spend-authority.json` schema, a resolver in execution_spec.py that stamps each unit {silent|ask}, and a docs section in plan/SKILL.md; verified by a unit test feeding a matrix + mixed-tier spec and asserting the exact silent/ask partition, plus a drift-guard test that an absent matrix defaults every above-sonnet tier to ask.

title: Pre-flight fuel plan + post-flight reconciliation for a run's spend
idea: Adopt aviation dispatch's fuel planning: before departure a dispatcher computes trip + contingency + reserve fuel and files it; after landing the actual burn is reconciled against the plan. Before a run, emit a spend flight-plan from the locked tier table (estimated tokens/cost per unit + a contingency reserve for the escalation ladder), shown to the operator up front. After the run, reconcile planned vs actual by reading the leaf-produced cost ledger and rendering a variance line per unit ('planned opus/high ~X, actual Y, +Z% because escalated'). This closes the loop the fleet lacks entirely today: operators see committed spend before they approve and real spend after, so the next run's estimates get grounded.
basis: FAA/ICAO fuel planning (14 CFR 91.167 / ICAO Annex 6): trip + contingency + reserve computed pre-flight and reconciled against actual burn post-flight. Engages the /outcome binding decision ('cost ledger = leaf-produced fact', derived-on-read) by sourcing post-flight actuals from the existing leaf-produced ledger and deriving the variance on read, never from a committed status field.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `spend-plan` render step to the plan/SKILL.md 5.2a emit flow and a reconciliation reader over the leaf cost ledger; verified by a golden test that a fixture plan produces a planned-cost table and, given a synthetic actuals ledger, emits a per-unit variance report with correct +/- deltas.

title: Level-of-detail tier policy: a per-repo file that remembers which work-zones run cheap
idea: Borrow real-time graphics' level-of-detail: distant/background geometry renders at low detail via a persisted LOD bias, foreground gets full detail, and the policy is a durable setting, not a per-frame decision. Replace the operator's ad-hoc, rebuilt-every-time tier table with a committed `.saga/tier-policy.json` that maps repo work-zones (path globs or unit labels: docs/ and scaffolding -> haiku/low, core service paths -> opus/high, tests -> sonnet/medium) to default tiers. The plan heuristic consults it before proposing, so a repo's learned tier preferences persist across runs and PRs. This directly attacks the mined pain 'operators hand-build tier tables ad hoc' by making the table a remembered, diffable, reviewable artifact that a new run inherits instead of reinventing.
basis: Computer-graphics Level-of-Detail / mipmap-bias rendering (Clark 1976, 'Hierarchical geometric models for visible surface algorithms', and standard GPU LOD bias settings): detail budget is a persisted per-object/per-distance policy, not a per-frame recomputation. A per-repo config file does not add a plugin (respects {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}) and is doc/CLI-shaped (respects {#operator-choice-framework}).
outcome_shape: PR adding a `.saga/tier-policy.json` schema + a resolver that lets a matched policy entry override the work-shape default in plan/SKILL.md 5.2a, with the override surfaced in the tier table so the operator sees policy-vs-heuristic; verified by a resolver unit test that a path-glob match overrides the default tier and an unmatched unit falls back to the heuristic.

title: Andon cord: a running cheap worker can stop and request escalation instead of failing silently
idea: Import the Toyota Production System andon cord and jidoka ('autonomation'): any worker who hits an abnormality stops the line and pulls the cord, surfacing the problem to a human rather than pushing defective work downstream. Give a cheap-tier worker a structured 'pull-cord' return disposition ('this unit exceeds my tier: <evidence>; recommend escalation to <tier> because <reason>') distinct from success or crash. The coordinator batches pulled cords into a single operator escalation ask, so the spend-increasing decision is worker-initiated at the point of real friction, not guessed at plan time. This is the asymmetric-approval rule inverted from a threshold policy (idea 3) to a runtime, evidence-carrying escalation request, and it kills the failure mode where a too-cheap agent silently returns thin work that passes shape checks but is substantively wrong.
basis: Toyota Production System andon cord + jidoka (Ohno, 'Toyota Production System', 1988): a worker stops the line on an abnormality and surfaces it to a human rather than passing defects downstream. Maps a worker-initiated stop-and-ask onto tier escalation; honors the intake asymmetric-approval rule (spend-increasing = always asks) and stays advisory-only, so no external-engine gatekeeping concern.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `pull_cord` disposition to the cheap-tier return contract (execution_spec.py BUDGET_RIDER / return schema) and coordinator handling that batches cords into one escalation ask; verified by a test that a unit returning pull_cord is not marked complete and produces a batched escalation entry rather than a silent pass.

title: Kelly-sized tier recommender: spend proportional to edge and remaining budget
idea: Replace the flat work-shape lookup with a bankroll-management recommender modeled on the Kelly criterion, which sizes a bet by expected edge times bankroll. Score each unit on two axes the flat table ignores: payoff-at-stake (blast radius / irreversibility / whether it feeds a gated decision) and remaining run budget (bankroll). A unit that is high-stakes and early in the budget earns a Fable/xhigh recommendation with an explicit 'edge' justification; a low-stakes unit late in a depleted budget gets pushed down the ladder even if its work-shape would default high. The recommendation stays a deterministic, Claude-side heuristic that the operator confirms, never an external-engine gate. This produces the 'worth it, because' justification as a computed edge score rather than a category label, and it naturally starves the 'xhigh on everything' pattern once the bankroll runs thin.
basis: Kelly criterion / bankroll management (Kelly 1956, 'A New Interpretation of Information Rate'; standard in gambling and quantitative finance position-sizing): stake ~ edge x bankroll. The recommender is deterministic and advisory (operator confirms), so it respects {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (no engine adjudicates a gated decision) and stays within {#tier-vocab-ordering} by only moving along the ordered ladder.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `tier_recommender` scoring function (payoff x remaining-budget -> tier + edge justification) wired into the plan/SKILL.md 5.2a heuristic step; verified by unit tests over a scoring matrix (high-stakes/full-bankroll -> top ladder rung with justification; low-stakes/depleted -> pushed down) and a test that the operator-confirm gate still fires.

title: Itemized spend receipt with a cheap-fallback counterfactual
idea: Borrow the utility itemized bill / smart-meter statement, which shows not just the total but line-item usage and a comparison against a cheaper plan. After a run, emit a receipt that breaks spend down per unit and per tier, then computes the counterfactual: 'this run cost X; the all-cheap-fallback plan (every unit at its declared fallback_tier from idea 2) would have cost ~0.4X and given up <named tradeoffs>.' Seeing the delta between what was spent and what the cheap path would have cost is the single most direct pressure against 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' -- it makes waste visible in retrospect and feeds the operator's next tier-policy edit. The counterfactual is computed from the same leaf-produced ledger the reconciliation reader uses, derived on read.
basis: First-principles: the mined waste pattern ('xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful', grounding brief §7.6) persists because spend is never contrasted against its cheaper alternative -- an operator sees only the absolute bill, not the counterfactual, so there is no felt cost to over-tiering. A receipt that renders actual-vs-cheap-fallback delta creates that missing feedback signal; it reuses the fallback_tier field (idea 2) and the leaf cost ledger, adding no new spend-tracking substrate and staying derived-on-read per the /outcome cost-ledger binding.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `spend-receipt` renderer (per-unit/per-tier actuals + a fallback-plan counterfactual delta) reading the leaf cost ledger, invoked at run end; verified by a golden test that a fixture ledger + fallback-annotated spec produces a receipt whose counterfactual total equals the sum of fallback-tier estimates and names each tradeoff.

title: Tier table gains a cost column: estimate before, actual after
idea: Flip the constraint to a hard $0 budget where every unit must justify its spend. The tier table at plan/SKILL.md:296-307 today shows U-ID, label, tier, rationale but NO cost signal, so the operator confirms tiers blind. Add a relative-cost estimate column derived at author time from a tier->cost-weight map over MODELS/EFFORTS (execution_spec.py:52-53), plus a run total, rendered into the same table the operator confirms. After the run, a second column reads the leaf-produced cost ledger and shows actual-vs-estimate per unit. The estimate is explicitly a modeled preview, never claimed to be the ledger fact; the actual column only READS the leaf ledger and never recomputes or overwrites it, preserving the /outcome 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' + derive-on-read invariants.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:306-307 'present the full tier table (U-ID, label, proposed tier, rationale) and ask the operator to confirm or override' has no cost dimension; binding /outcome decision 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (grounding brief section 2) is engaged by making the after-column a read-only projection of the leaf ledger, not a new committed field.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cost_weight(tier) helper + tier-table cost column to execution_spec.py and plan/SKILL.md Step 1, with a unit test asserting estimate ordering follows MODELS/EFFORTS ladder; verified by running validate/emit on a sample spec and confirming the rendered table carries estimate and (post-run) actual columns.

title: Every tier row carries a machine-readable cheaper fallback + one-line because
idea: Flip to fully autonomous with zero operator present: a recommendation nobody reads must still carry its own justification and a named cheaper path so an unattended run can downshift defensibly. Add an optional fallback_tier field and a rationale string to the Unit/Tier schema in execution_spec.py so each authored tier emits 'this tier because <reason>; cheaper fallback: <model/effort>' as a structured pair, not prose. The emitter renders the fallback as a comment beside each agent() call so /work (or an unattended loop) can mechanically apply it. This makes the intake tension-4 rule ('every Fable-tier line carries a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback; expensive is never a silent default') a schema property instead of an authoring convention that drifts.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:304 'fable/xhigh available as a per-unit override, never a default (KTD2)' + intake brief tension 4 'every Fable-tier line in any plan or issue carries a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback'. Distinct from QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} (that seed is who-picks-effort; this is the fallback-rationale schema on the tier itself).
outcome_shape: PR adding optional fallback_tier + rationale to Tier/Unit dataclasses in execution_spec.py, emitter rendering them as agent()-adjacent comments, round-trip + validation tests; verified by emitting a spec and grepping the .workflow.js for the fallback comment on a fable unit.

title: Re-tier direction gate: downgrades silent, upgrades always halt for yes
idea: Flip to every issue self-executing, where the only brake on runaway cost is structural. When a tier is changed (mid-run operator override, resume reconciliation, or a proposed default), classify the delta using the load-bearing MODELS/EFFORTS ordering (execution_spec.py:49-53, already used by segment_units for upgrade-only merges): a move toward cheaper (down MODELS index, down EFFORTS index) is spend-decreasing and proceeds silently; any move toward opus/xhigh/fable is spend-increasing and emits a HALT marker requiring an explicit operator yes. Encode this as a tier_delta_direction() helper feeding an emit-time / resume-time gate. This turns the intake asymmetric-approval rule into machinery instead of a prose posture.
basis: execution_spec.py:49-51 'ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: segment_units() merges tiers upgrade-only via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index)' + binding decision {#tier-vocab-ordering} 'Tier tuples ordered escalation ladders, not just closed sets' (grounding brief section 2) — this idea consumes that ordering as the direction oracle, exactly its intended escalation-ladder use.
outcome_shape: PR adding tier_delta_direction(old, new) to execution_spec.py returning increase/decrease/lateral and an emit/resume gate that marks increases as operator-approval-required, with unit tests over the ladder corners (haiku/low -> fable/xhigh, etc.); verified by a test asserting an upgrade trips the gate and a downgrade does not.

title: Per-repo remembered tier defaults so the table is never hand-built twice
idea: Flip run-scoped defaults (which die every run) to permanent memory. Operators hand-build tier tables ad hoc every single time (session-mining pattern #6, 3 repos). Add a git-ignored, machine-local .saga/tier-defaults.json (same residency class as saga state) keyed by work-shape that records the operator's CONFIRMED tier choices. On the next /plan, Step 1 pre-fills the tier table from this memory instead of re-deriving from the static heuristic, showing 'remembered from last run' provenance and still offering override. Over a few runs the ad-hoc table converges to the operator's actual preference for this repo, and confirmation becomes a glance instead of a rebuild.
basis: grounding brief session-mining pattern #6 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — manual per-unit tier tables ... (3 repos) -> theme 12'; residency respects the established machine-local git-ignored saga-state convention (plan/SKILL.md:361-362 'saga state is git-ignored, machine-local'), not the derive-on-read status invariant (this is a preference cache, not committed status).
outcome_shape: PR adding read/write of .saga/tier-defaults.json + a plan Step-1 pre-fill path with 'remembered' provenance annotation, plus a test asserting a confirmed tier persists and pre-fills; verified by running /plan twice on a fixture and confirming the second table pre-populates.

title: Fleet lever-placement inventory: name the ask-points and open the effort seam
idea: Flip from one lever to a lever at every spawn, then mine the practical middle. Today the fleet's ONLY operator-facing model/effort lever is saga /plan's tier table; every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: with zero effort: fields and no dispatch-time override anywhere else. Rather than sprinkle prompts everywhere (the extreme), publish a DECISIONS entry + a references/lever-placement.md that enumerates the 3-4 canonical decision points that SHOULD ask (plan-time tier table, resume re-tier, team-execution worker table, mission-control high-cost dispatch) and the rule at each, and add effort: to the agent-frontmatter schema so the seam exists to be filled per that inventory. No new plugin; a doc + schema seam, honoring the doc-only operator-choice framework.
basis: grounding brief section 1 'fleet's ONE operator-facing model/effort lever ... Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:, zero effort: fields ... no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern'; engages binding {#operator-choice-framework} (doc-only, CLI-driven) and {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by adding no plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md entry + plugins/saga/references/lever-placement.md enumerating canonical ask-points, and an effort: field admitted to the agent-frontmatter schema/validator; verified by a schema test accepting effort: on an agent and the DECISIONS entry linking each named ask-point to a file:line.

title: Spec-level cost budget that HALTs emit when the plan exceeds it
idea: Take the $0-budget flip literally as an operator-set ceiling. execution_spec.py already HALTs emit loudly when a structural bound is exceeded — VERIFY_N_CAP=7 fails validate rather than silently emitting an over-large panel (execution_spec.py:111-114). Reuse that exact 'fail emit loudly' pattern for spend: an optional spec-level cost_budget (in relative cost units) summed across the units' tier weights; if the authored plan's total exceeds it, validate/emit HALTS with a message naming the overage and the cheapest units to downshift. This gives the operator a single knob ('keep this run under X') that is enforced structurally, HALT-not-degrade, before any token is spent — never a silent trim.
basis: execution_spec.py:111-114 'Hard upper bound on a verify panel's verifier count. N above this FAILS validate/emit ... the bound directly guards the rate-limit overcorrection' — established emit-time HALT precedent; honors the /outcome binding decision HALT-not-degrade (grounding brief section 2) by halting rather than silently trimming units.
outcome_shape: PR adding optional cost_budget to ExecutionSpec + an emit-time check raising SpecError with overage detail (mirroring the VERIFY_N_CAP block), plus a test asserting an over-budget spec fails emit and an under-budget one passes; verified by validate exiting non-zero on a fixture over budget.

title: Mode-aware recommender: attended recommends throughput, unattended recommends cheapest-defensible
idea: Flip on the operator axis: design for both zero-operator and always-present-operator and let run mode pick the default. The intake settled a mode-dependent default (attended -> throughput recommended but spend-increases always ask; unattended -> cache-tight, may proceed silently). Encode that as a recommender that takes (work_shape, run_mode) and emits the tier row's default plus the 'Fable, worth it, because... (cheaper fallback: ...)' line CONDITIONED on mode: attended runs see the throughput-leaning recommendation with the ask, unattended runs default to the cheapest tier that still clears the work-shape bar, with the pricier option named as an available upgrade rather than the default. One heuristic, two framings, both surfaced.
basis: intake brief tension 1 'Mode-dependent default with an asymmetric approval rule ... Unattended runs -> cache-tight serial ... Attended runs -> throughput recommended, but any spend-increasing choice ... always requires an explicit operator yes ... Asked once per run at start, with a mode-based recommendation'.
outcome_shape: PR adding a recommend_tier(work_shape, run_mode) helper + plan Step-1 wiring that renders mode-conditioned rationale rows, with tests asserting the same work_shape yields a cheaper default under unattended than under attended; verified by comparing two rendered tier tables across modes on a fixture.

title: Move the lever upstream: issues carry a recommended tier band at handoff
idea: Flip to every issue self-executing — if an issue could dispatch itself, it would need its tier decided at creation, not at plan time. Mine that: have mission-control:issue stamp a recommended tier band on each issue derived from its type and labels (a defect-investigation issue -> opus/high judgment band; a mechanical context-update -> sonnet/medium; a read-only survey -> sonnet/low), written into the issue body as a structured field. Then saga /plan Step 1 pre-fills its tier table from the issue's band instead of re-deriving from scratch, and the operator confirms once. The lever moves upstream to where the work is first named, so the tier is a decision the whole lifecycle inherits rather than re-litigates per run.
basis: grounding brief session-mining pattern #6 'manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos) -> theme 12' + the 6-type issue taxonomy (capability/enhancement/defect/exploration/context-update/objective) already carried by mission-control:issue; no new plugin, so {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} is satisfied.
outcome_shape: PR adding a recommended-tier-band field to the mission-control issue template + a type/label->band mapping, and a saga /plan Step-1 reader that pre-fills the tier table from it; verified by creating a fixture defect issue and confirming /plan pre-fills the opus/high judgment band.

title: Wave-width cap in the saga emitter — turn the unbounded parallel([...]) wave into machinery
idea: The layer scheduler in execution_spec.py:1219-1225 renders every ready unit of a layer into one `parallel([...])` wave with no width bound — this is the literal 'emitter has no concurrency knob' finding, since VERIFY_N_CAP only guards a single verify panel, not the layer fan-out. Add a `WAVE_WIDTH_CAP` module constant (sibling to VERIFY_N_CAP at line 114) and have the wave renderer chunk any layer wider than the cap into sequential `await`-separated sub-batches inside the generated JS, preserving dependency order. Default the cap to 3 (operator's stated ideal), 4 only when every unit in the layer is read-only (mirroring the intake's '4 permitted for read-only scans' carve-out). This is the aspiration→machinery conversion the theme names.
basis: execution_spec.py:1219-1225 emits `parallel([...])` over all ready layer units with no width bound; VERIFY_N_CAP=7 (line 114) guards only a verify panel, per grounding brief §1 'team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded'. Operator: 'concurrency 3 ideal, maybe 4'.
outcome_shape: PR adding WAVE_WIDTH_CAP + read-only carve-out to plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py and chunking logic in the layer-wave renderer, with a unit test asserting a 6-unit layer emits two sequential 3-wide waves (and a 4-wide read-only layer stays single-wave). Verified by inspecting generated JS in the test golden + emit-time assertion.

title: A single concurrency-policy block in execution_spec with a resolution ladder (spec default → env → run override)
idea: Today the only cap lives as a bare `VERIFY_N_CAP` literal; there is no home for a general concurrency knob, so every proposal scatters magic numbers. Introduce a `ConcurrencyPolicy` dataclass in execution_spec.py carrying `max_wave_width` and `max_verify_n`, resolved through an ordered ladder — module default, then `SAGA_MAX_CONCURRENCY` env (the unattended/CI knob), then an explicit per-run authored override — so the knob has exactly one authoritative locus and the env path lets an overnight /outcome run tighten itself without code edits. VERIFY_N_CAP becomes a derived special case (a verify panel is just a wave), collapsing two caps into one policy object. Keep it validate-at-emit like the existing tier vocabulary so a bad override fails emit, not runtime.
basis: execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP is a lone literal with no policy home; grounding brief §1 names it 'the only orchestration-level cap'. execution_spec.py:46-53 establishes the 'validate authored values at emit, never invent' pattern this reuses.
outcome_shape: PR adding a ConcurrencyPolicy dataclass + resolve() ladder to plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py, VERIFY_N_CAP refactored to read from it, and tests covering each ladder rung (default, env, override) plus an invalid-override emit failure. Verified by the test suite and a grep confirming no remaining bare cap literals.

title: 429-aware bounded backoff-and-requeue wrapper around generated agent() thunks
idea: The mined kill was '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting' — a hard wave failure with no recovery — and HTTP-429 handling exists nowhere in the orchestration layer (only in the unifi and mission-control HTTP clients). Wrap each generated `agent()` thunk (the ones assembled at execution_spec.py:1016 and 1093) in a helper that catches a rate-limit/429 signal and retries with bounded exponential backoff + jitter, capped at a small retry count, so a throttled agent re-queues into a later slot instead of dropping the whole wave. Pair it with the wave-width cap (T13-F1-1) so backoff is the second line of defense when even a capped wave meets a busy account. Failures that survive the retry budget still surface — no silent swallow.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting'; §1: 'HTTP-level 429 handling exists only in unifi and mission-control clients'. Thunk assembly at execution_spec.py:1016/1093 is the injection point.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `__retryOn429` JS helper emitted alongside `__gate` in execution_spec.py and wrapping each agent thunk, plus a test asserting a simulated 429-then-success thunk resolves and a persistent-429 thunk fails loudly after the retry budget. Verified by generated-JS golden + a harness stub test.

title: Fleet-wide concurrency lease file so co-running workflows can't sum past the cap
idea: A per-workflow cap of 3 does not deliver the operator's actual constraint — 'maximum 3 concurrent agents at any moment, across all phases' — because two concurrently-running workflows (a saga emit and a team-execution review) each obeying their own cap of 3 still put 6 agents against the account. Introduce a shared on-disk slot lease (an flock-guarded `~/.saga/concurrency.lock` with N tokens) that every fleet spawn site — the saga emitter, team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges — acquires before spawning and releases on completion. The lease count is the fleet-wide knob; a workflow that can't get a slot waits rather than over-spawning. This is the only mechanism that makes 'across all phases' true rather than aspirational.
basis: First-principles: independent per-workflow caps of K compose additively — two workflows at cap 3 yield 6 concurrent agents, violating the intake's stated invariant 'maximum 3 concurrent agents at any moment, across all phases' (intake §91). Only a shared counting lease held across all spawn sites (enumerated in plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md) enforces a global ceiling; nothing in the fleet does this today.
outcome_shape: PR adding a concurrency-lease module (acquire/release with flock + stale-lock reclamation) plus adoption at each spawn site listed in sandbox-spawn-sites.md, with a doc note in that reference and a test spawning 5 mock acquirers against a 3-slot lease and asserting max-2 wait. Verified by the concurrency test + spawn-site grep.

title: Re-add a rescoped max_concurrent to /optimize, decoupled from the isolation+auto-merge apparatus it was shed with
idea: /optimize deliberately shed `max_concurrent` — but reading optimize/SKILL.md:17-18, it was shed as one item in a BUNDLE (git-worktree-per-experiment isolation + parallel fan-out + auto-commit/auto-merge of experiment branches), all of which 're-enter only' when the heavyweight ce-optimize path does. The revisit-when engagement: rate-limit governance is orthogonal to experiment isolation and branch merging — those were shed for safety/simplicity reasons that do not apply to a bare concurrency ceiling. Re-add ONLY a concurrency ceiling to the default /optimize path (no worktrees, no auto-merge), sourced from the shared ConcurrencyPolicy (T13-F1-2), so /optimize's experiment fan-out is rate-limit-safe without dragging back the apparatus that justified the shed. The knob's absence today is not a decision that concurrency is bad; it is a decision that the bundle was heavy.
basis: optimize/SKILL.md:17-18: 'The default path SHEDS ce-optimize's git-worktree-per-experiment isolation, its parallel / max_concurrent fan-out, and its auto-commit / auto-merge ... Those re-enter only [with the heavy path].' The shed is a bundle; concurrency governance is separable from isolation/merge — that is the revisit engagement.
outcome_shape: PR editing plugins/saga/skills/optimize/SKILL.md to reinstate a concurrency ceiling on the default path (explicitly NOT worktree isolation or auto-merge), wired to ConcurrencyPolicy, plus a DECISIONS.md entry recording the bundle-decoupling rationale and revisit condition. Verified by doc review + the SKILL.md diff showing isolation/merge remain shed.

title: Per-session AIMD concurrency governor that dials wave width to the observed 429 rate
idea: A static cap is a guess; the safe concurrency is a moving target that depends on account load at that moment. Borrow AIMD (additive-increase / multiplicative-decrease), the control law behind TCP congestion control and AWS SDK v2 adaptive retry mode: start at the cap (3), halve the effective wave width on a 429 burst (3→2→1), and add one slot back after a clean wave, persisting the governor state in saga session state so it survives across layers within a run. This turns the operator's 'maybe 4' from a static gamble into an earned ceiling — the governor probes up to 4 only when the account is demonstrably quiet, and retreats instantly under pressure. Bounds stay [1, ConcurrencyPolicy.max] so it never exceeds the hard cap.
basis: Prior art: AWS SDK v2 'adaptive' retry mode (client-side rate limiter using a token bucket + AIMD, in aws-sdk-java-v2 RateLimitingTokenBucket) and TCP congestion control's additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease. Both are documented, battle-tested control laws for exactly 'unknown server-side capacity, avoid overshoot'.
outcome_shape: PR adding an AIMD governor (state persisted in saga session state) that the wave-width renderer consults, bounded by ConcurrencyPolicy.max, plus a simulation test feeding a 429-burst-then-quiet trace and asserting width descends to 1 then recovers toward the cap. Verified by the deterministic trace test.

title: Concurrency-cap conformance drift-guard test over every fleet spawn site
idea: Caps are only real if new code can't route around them — and the fleet already has the exact pattern for this: the literal-consistency guard tests that assert READONLY_VERIFIER_AGENT_TYPE stays wired (execution_spec.py:87-94) and that the SANDBOX_PROFILES copies stay byte-identical across modules. Add a conformance test that walks the spawn-site inventory in plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md and asserts each fan-out site routes through the shared concurrency primitive (lease acquire or capped wave), failing CI the moment someone adds a fresh unbounded `parallel(` or raw multi-agent spawn. This is the cheapest, most durable way to keep 'aspiration' from creeping back after the machinery lands — the guard is the enforcement.
basis: execution_spec.py:80-94 documents existing drift-guard tests ('a cross-module drift-guard test asserts the two copies stay identical'; 'the literal-consistency guard test asserts this'). CLAUDE.md cites plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md as 'the full spawn-site inventory' — a ready enumeration to assert against.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_concurrency_conformance.py that parses the spawn-site inventory and asserts each site references the cap primitive (plus a negative test that an unbounded parallel( wave fails), wired into the pytest suite. Verified by CI green with the guard active and red when a stub unbounded site is introduced.

title: Emitter chunks wide fan-out waves so the cap is machinery, not a hand-batching ritual
idea: Today `_render_layer` renders every ready layer as one unbounded `parallel([...])` wave (execution_spec.py:1225), so a 10-unit layer spawns 10 agents at once and the only defense is the workflow author manually chunking fan-out into batches of ≤3 by hand. Invert it: add a module-level `CONCURRENCY_CAP` beside `VERIFY_N_CAP` and teach the emitter to split any wave wider than the cap into ceil(width/cap) sequential `parallel([...])` sub-waves in the generated JS. The best version of the hand-batching step is no step — the emitter emits the batching loop. This directly closes the mined 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery' pain by making the claimed cap live in the generated harness.
basis: grounding brief line 130: 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 aspiration, not machinery'; corroborated by execution_spec.py:1225 (`const [...] = await parallel([`) rendering one unbounded wave per layer, and intake brief lines 97-98 documenting that the ideation workflow itself must 'chunk every fan-out into batches of ≤3 (explicit sequential loop over parallel() batches)' by hand.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py (new CONCURRENCY_CAP constant + wave-splitting in the parallel()-emit path) and tests/test_execution_spec*.py; verified by a golden-file emit test asserting a 10-unit ready layer renders 4 sequential parallel() sub-waves of ≤3, and that a ≤3-unit layer is unchanged.

title: One authoritative concurrency-policy constant module, drift-guarded like the sandbox mirror
idea: The cap currently lives nowhere and everywhere — an aspiration scattered across prose and per-workflow hand-batching. Remove the scatter: create a single `concurrency_policy.py` exporting `MAX_CONCURRENCY = 3` and `READONLY_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4` as the one source of truth, imported by the execution_spec emitter, outcome dispatch, and referenced by team-execution's worker-fan-out docs. Follow the exact pattern already proven for SANDBOX_PROFILES, where a cross-module drift-guard test asserts two copies stay byte-identical (execution_spec.py:80-85). This makes 'where does the knob live' answerable in one file instead of re-derived per plugin.
basis: execution_spec.py:114 already houses `VERIFY_N_CAP = 7` as a module-level cap constant with a documented incident lineage; the same file at lines 80-85 shows the SANDBOX_PROFILES cross-module drift-guard pattern this idea extends. Intake brief line 103-104 names the gap: 'reviewer fan-out, workflow emitters, and /outcome dispatch currently have no shared cap policy'.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency_policy.py plus a drift-guard test in tests/ that fails if any other module hardcodes a concurrency integer literal (grep-based, like the existing literal-consistency guard); marketplace.json + saga CHANGELOG.md version bump per repo release-surface rule.

title: Auto-retry-on-429 wrapper in the emitted parallel helper so a rate-limited agent re-queues, not dies
idea: When a wave hits rate limits today, individual agents fail and a human re-runs them ('6-7 agents failed on rate-limiting'). Automate the recovery away: wrap each emitted `agent()` thunk inside the generated `parallel([...])` in a bounded exponential-backoff-on-429 helper (`__retryOn429`) that distinguishes a transient HTTP 429 from a real failure and re-attempts up to a small bound before surfacing. A transient rate-limit becomes an invisible retry instead of a manual re-run step. Crucially this respects the /outcome HALT-not-degrade decision: a 429 is a transient retryable, not a silent quality degrade, so only genuine (non-429) failures HALT the wave.
