basis: grounding brief line 129: 'Rate-limit fan-out kills — 6 7 agents failed on rate-limiting' (3 repos); the /outcome U-decision '{HALT-not-degrade}' (grounding line 48) is engaged directly — 429 is classified transient-retryable, not a degrade path, so its revisit-when is satisfied rather than crossed.
outcome_shape: PR touching the _JS_GATE_HELPER / parallel-helper emit region of execution_spec.py to inject a __retryOn429 wrapper into generated workflow scripts, plus a unit test asserting the emitted JS contains bounded 429 retry logic and that a non-429 error still propagates (HALT).

title: Resume-on-429: /outcome marks a rate-limited leaf dispatch retriable-pending, next advance re-picks it
idea: When a leaf-saga dispatch in the /outcome DAG hits a rate limit, remove the manual resume step entirely: instead of the leaf failing terminally, the advance loop classifies a 429 dispatch as `retriable-pending` (a derived-on-read status, never a committed field) so the next `advance` tick naturally re-picks it from the ready frontier. This extends the existing pattern where outcome reads already 'degrade safely if rate-limited' (outcome_github.py:10) from the read path to the dispatch path. The operator never hand-resumes a rate-limited outcome — the frontier heals itself on the next tick.
basis: outcome_github.py:10: 'Every read degrades safely: if gh is unavailable / rate-limited / the ref is unknown, the state is [degraded]' — this idea extends that same safe-degrade posture from reads to dispatch. Consistent with the /outcome 'derived-on-read status, never committed status fields' decision (grounding line 48), whose revisit-when is not crossed because retriable-pending is derived, not stored.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome.py advance/dispatch path to classify 429 as retriable-pending and re-include on next tick, plus a test simulating a rate-limited dispatch and asserting the leaf re-enters the ready frontier without operator action.

title: Session-scoped concurrency lease so two stacked workflows still sum to ≤3 fleet-wide
idea: Per-workflow caps do not compose: two workflows each self-capped at 3 run 6 agents concurrently — exactly the rate-limit kill. Invert the ownership of the cap from the workflow to the session: a shared token-bucket lease file in the scratch dir that every agent spawn across saga, team-execution, and /outcome dispatch must acquire-before-spawn and release-on-complete, so the operator's 'maximum 3 concurrent across ALL phases' holds even when independent workflows overlap. The cap stops being a property each workflow re-implements and becomes a session-global budget nobody can exceed by stacking.
basis: intake brief lines 91-93: 'Maximum 3 concurrent agents at any moment, across all phases' — an explicitly fleet-wide (cross-workflow) scope that no per-workflow knob can enforce; intake line 103-104 confirms the three surfaces (reviewer fan-out, emitters, /outcome dispatch) 'have no shared cap policy'. outcome_worktrees.py (R15 hard cap on concurrent live worktrees) is prior art that a session-global proliferation cap is already an accepted shape in this codebase.
outcome_shape: PR adding a lease-acquire/release helper (lease file under the scratch dir) plus spawn-site wiring at the three named surfaces, with a concurrency test spawning two overlapping mock workflows and asserting peak concurrent leases never exceeds 3.

title: Turn /optimize's narrated Phase-4 max_concurrent escalation into a real, defaulted-off spec field
idea: /optimize deliberately shed ce-optimize's max_concurrent fan-out to keep the loop serial and in working state, letting concurrency re-enter 'only by explicit operator-choice escalation (Phase 4), recorded narratively.' Narrated-in-prose is exactly the aspiration-not-machinery failure this theme targets. Reconcile it by promoting the escalation from narrative to a real experiment-log schema field (`max_concurrent`, default null = serial) that Phase 4 sets explicitly — the shed's intent (serial-default, working-state safety) is preserved because the field defaults off and only an operator yes activates it. Automate the narration into a typed, verifiable knob.
basis: optimize/SKILL.md:17-20: 'The default path SHEDS ce-optimize's ... parallel / max_concurrent fan-out ... Those re-enter only by an explicit operator-choice escalation (Phase 4), recorded narratively. The loop runs serial ... by default.' Revisit-when engaged: the shed's rationale (serial-default working-state safety) is honored because the new field defaults to serial and requires an explicit operator yes — re-adding the knob does not re-add the default parallelism the shed rejected.
outcome_shape: PR adding an optional max_concurrent field to the /optimize experiment-log schema (default serial) + SKILL.md doc update describing Phase-4 activation, verified by a schema test asserting default-serial and that the field only activates on explicit set.

title: Read-only waves auto-lift to cap 4 by reusing the existing mutation_policy axis
idea: The operator's rule has two tiers — 3 concurrent normally, 4 for short read-only scans — and today that distinction lives only in the operator's head and is applied by hand. Automate the judgment: since units already carry a `mutation_policy` axis (execution_spec.py:74, values read-only / read-write), the emitter can compute a wave's cap automatically — a wave whose units are ALL read-only gets cap 4, any wave containing a read-write unit gets cap 3. The 'is this scan safe to run 4-wide' decision stops being a manual operator call and becomes a derived property of data the spec already carries.
basis: intake brief lines 93-95: 'Maximum 3 concurrent ... 4 permitted only for short, read-only scans such as Phase B greps'; execution_spec.py:74 already defines MUTATION_POLICIES = ('read-only', 'read-write') as a per-unit axis, so the read-only/read-write signal needed to derive the cap already exists on every unit.
outcome_shape: PR extending the wave-chunking logic (built by idea T13-F2-1) so cap is derived per-wave from unit mutation_policy, plus a test asserting an all-read-only layer chunks at width 4 and a mixed layer chunks at width 3.

title: CI drift-guard that fails when any emitted workflow script contains an over-wide parallel wave
idea: Even with an emitter that chunks waves, nothing structurally prevents a hand-authored or regressed workflow script from shipping an over-wide `parallel([...])`. Remove the human review step that would otherwise catch it: add a CI test that parses every emitted / committed workflow script under docs/plans and fails if any `parallel([...])` wave exceeds CONCURRENCY_CAP. The 'eyeball the generated script for a too-wide fan-out' review step becomes no step — a machine asserts the invariant on every PR, mirroring how literal-consistency guard tests already protect the readonly-verifier agentType wiring.
basis: execution_spec.py:90-92 documents the existing 'literal-consistency guard test' pattern that 'asserts this, so a rename ... fails a test rather than silently spawning verifiers unrestricted' — this idea reuses that guard-test idiom for concurrency width. Grounding brief line 130 ('KTD6 aspiration, not machinery') is the aspiration this converts into an enforced invariant.
outcome_shape: PR adding a test (tests/test_workflow_concurrency_guard.py) that scans committed .workflow.js scripts and fails on any parallel() wave wider than CONCURRENCY_CAP; wired into the existing pytest CI scope (plugins/ scripts/ tests/).

title: One fleet concurrency governor, VERIFY_N_CAP derived not declared
idea: The assumption baked into execution_spec.py:114 is that a concurrency limit is a per-concern literal scattered across the fleet (VERIFY_N_CAP here, nothing in team_emitter, nothing in outcome dispatch). Reframe one level up: there is exactly ONE fleet concurrency budget, and every cap is a view onto it. Add plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency_governor.py exposing a single resolved cap with an explicit resolution ladder (env SAGA_MAX_CONCURRENCY > session marker > default 3) plus a pure chunk(seq, cap) helper. Rewire VERIFY_N_CAP so it is DERIVED from the governor (or a drift-guard test asserts they agree), killing the 7-vs-3 split brain where a legal verify panel already violates the operator's stated ceiling.
basis: execution_spec.py:114 `VERIFY_N_CAP = 7` is the fleet's only orchestration-level cap; grounding brief §1 states team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded. Operator seed: concurrency 3 ideal, maybe 4 — directly contradicts a standalone 7.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency_governor.py (resolution ladder + chunk helper) and a tests/ drift-guard asserting VERIFY_N_CAP is consistent with the governor default. Verified by the new unit test plus mypy/ruff green on scripts/.

title: Emit chunkedParallel so a wide layer cannot spawn a wide wave
idea: The mined finding is that the emitter has no concurrency knob — the claimed cap is aspiration, not machinery. Confirmed: emit_workflow_script renders a topological layer as one full-width `parallel([...])` (execution_spec.py:1225), so a 10-unit layer spawns 10 agents at once regardless of any stated cap. Reframe: emitted machinery, not prose promises. Add a `__chunkedParallel(thunks, cap)` runtime helper alongside the existing `__gate` helper (line 132) that loops the thunk list in slices of `cap`, and have the layer emitter call it instead of raw `parallel`. Now the cap is enforced by the generated harness itself — a script that structurally cannot exceed the governor's cap.
basis: execution_spec.py:1225 `const [...] = await parallel([` emits the entire layer as one wave; `_JS_GATE_HELPER` at line 132 is the existing precedent for a baked-in runtime helper. Grounding §7 pattern 4: "the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery."
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching execution_spec.py (new _CHUNKED_PARALLEL_HELPER + layer-emit call site) with a test asserting a >cap layer emits a chunked loop, not a single parallel of >cap thunks. Verified by emitting a fixture spec and grepping the output for the chunk helper.

title: Chunk the refute-N verifier fan-out so a legal panel obeys the cap
idea: VERIFY_N_CAP=7 treats "how many verifiers may exist" and "how many may run at once" as the same number — a false collapse. _emit_panel_reconciliation spawns all n verifiers in one `parallel([...])` (execution_spec.py:943-949), so a fully-legal n=7 panel breaches the operator's concurrency-3 ceiling the instant it runs. Reframe the two axes apart: keep the panel-SIZE cap for statistical validity, but emit the verifier spawn through the same chunkedParallel path so at most `cap` verifiers are live at once. The 22-judge incident was a concurrency spike, not a headcount problem; fixing headcount alone never addressed the actual failure.
basis: execution_spec.py:943-949 spawns `range(n)` verifiers in a single `parallel([...])`; the cap comment at line 112-114 attributes it to "the 22/23-judges panel that tripped the concurrency cap" — a runtime-concurrency event, yet the guard is a static count.
outcome_shape: Merged PR modifying _emit_panel_reconciliation to route verifier thunks through chunkedParallel(cap), plus a test that an n=7 panel emits no single parallel wave wider than cap. Verified by fixture emission + assertion.

title: Promote per-client 429 handling up to the orchestration tier
idea: Today a 429 at the orchestration layer is terminal — "6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting" — while the fleet ALREADY owns retry-with-backoff logic, just buried in the unifi and mission-control HTTP clients where the emitter can't reach it. The fixed assumption is that rate-limit resilience belongs to leaf HTTP clients. Reframe: a 429 on an agent spawn is a schedulable signal, and the retry/backoff pattern is a fleet capability that belongs in the concurrency governor. Lift a small exponential-backoff-with-jitter + requeue wrapper into the governor and bake it into the emitted thunk runner, so a rate-limited agent re-enters the queue rather than dropping its slice of a fan-out.
basis: Grounding brief §1: "HTTP-level 429 handling exists only in unifi and mission-control clients." Grounding §7 pattern 4: "6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting." The capability exists; it is just scoped to the wrong layer.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a backoff+requeue helper to concurrency_governor.py and wiring it into the emitted thunk-runner, plus a reference doc plugins/saga/references/concurrency-governance.md documenting the 429 policy. Verified by a unit test simulating a 429 and asserting requeue-then-succeed.

title: AIMD auto-discovery of the true concurrency ceiling
idea: The operator's "3 ideal, maybe 4" is a hand-tuned guess, and it is treated as a fixed constant. But the real ceiling is a discoverable, time-varying property of the current rate-limit tier and the mix of agent tiers running. Reframe the static number as a converged equilibrium: an additive-increase / multiplicative-decrease governor that starts at the operator floor (3), probes upward one slot at a time while waves complete cleanly, and halves on a 429 — exactly TCP congestion control applied to agent dispatch. The operator sets a floor and a hard ceiling; the governor finds the sweet spot without a human re-tuning a magic number every rate-limit change.
basis: Additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease (AIMD) congestion control — the canonical TCP Reno / Jacobson algorithm (RFC 5681) — is proven prior art for converging on an unknown, time-varying throughput ceiling from a conservative floor. Applies directly to unknown API rate ceilings.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an opt-in adaptive mode to concurrency_governor.py (floor/ceiling params, AIMD state) behind an env flag defaulting off, with a test driving simulated 429/clean sequences and asserting convergence between floor and ceiling. Verified by the simulation test.

title: Cross-process concurrency lease so parallel sagas share one budget
idea: Every cap in the fleet is scoped to a single workflow run — the hidden assumption is that one process is the whole world. But two concurrent /outcome leaves, each internally respecting cap=3, together put 6 agents against the same account rate limit; the ceiling is an account-wide resource, not a per-run one. Reframe the cap as a fleet lease: a well-known lock/token file (or the existing outcome coordinator-lease seam) that all live orchestrations acquire slots from, so total live agents across ALL processes stays within budget. It must HALT-and-surface when the lease is exhausted, never silently degrade — aligning with the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade rule.
basis: Grounding §2 (/outcome campaign row): "HALT-not-degrade" is the binding rule a cross-process governor must honor — this idea explicitly adopts it rather than crossing it. Grounding §1: reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are independently unbounded, so per-run caps cannot bound the account-level total.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a file-lease slot acquisition to concurrency_governor.py (reusing the outcome lease pattern in outcome.py:119-120), with a HALT-on-exhaustion path and a doc note. Verified by a test spawning two governor instances against a shared lease and asserting the combined live count never exceeds budget.

title: DECISION: /optimize's shed max_concurrent is not precedent against a rate governor
idea: A future contributor will cite optimize/SKILL.md:18 ("the default path SHEDS ... max_concurrent fan-out") as evidence the fleet decided AGAINST concurrency knobs, and use it to block the governor. That reads a specific decision as a general one. Engage it head-on: /optimize shed max_concurrent because its experiments must run serial-in-working-state and one-variable for measurement validity — an experiment-ISOLATION concern (worktree-per-experiment, auto-merge) — which is orthogonal to a rate-limit GOVERNOR that bounds live agents. Write the DECISIONS.md entry that names both axes, records the rejected conflation, and sets the revisit-when so the two are never re-collapsed.
basis: optimize/SKILL.md:18 and experiment-loop.md:59 shed `max_concurrent` as part of "git-worktree-per-experiment isolation ... auto-commit/auto-merge of experiment branches" — explicitly an isolation/measurement bundle, re-entering only via operator escalation (Phase 4). No rate-limit rationale is stated.
outcome_shape: Merged docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md anchor {#concurrency-governor-vs-optimize-shed} with rationale, rejected-conflation, and revisit-when, cross-linked from a note in plugins/saga/skills/optimize/references/experiment-loop.md. Verified by the anchor resolving and the cross-link present.

title: Weight the cap by tier: concurrency is rate cost, not headcount
idea: Both the count cap and the operator's number assume every agent weighs the same against the rate limit. It does not — the 22-judge incident was cheap judges, and 7 haiku/low agents and 3 opus/xhigh agents are completely different rate loads. Reframe the closed assumption "concurrency = bodies": the governor admits by SUMMED tier weight against a budget, not by count. Reuse the already-ordered MODELS/EFFORTS ladders (execution_spec.py:52-53) to derive a per-tier weight, so a wave of cheap agents can run wider while a wave of expensive ones stays narrow — the same rate ceiling expressed as an economic budget instead of a blunt integer.
basis: First-principles: a rate limit is denominated in tokens/requests per minute, not agent instances. VERIFY_N_CAP=7 was set by a cheap-judge incident (execution_spec.py:112-113); applying that same integer to opus/xhigh fan-out both under-caps the cheap case and over-caps the expensive one. MODELS/EFFORTS are already ordered escalation ladders (line 49-53, {#tier-vocab-ordering}), so a monotone weight is derivable without a new enum.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a tier->weight table to concurrency_governor.py and a weight-summing admission function, plus a test asserting a cheap-tier wave admits more slots than an expensive-tier wave under the same budget. Verified by the unit test.

title: Single shared concurrency-resolver primitive every fan-out site imports
idea: Add a `concurrency.py` module beside `execution_spec.py` exposing one `resolve_max_concurrent()` with a documented precedence ladder (env `SAGA_MAX_CONCURRENT` > session state file > `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 3`) and a hard `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_CEILING = 4`. Every current unbounded spawn site (team-execution reviewer fan-out, `/outcome` leaf dispatch, engine bridges) imports this one resolver instead of hardcoding or ignoring a cap. The leverage is second-order: today VERIFY_N_CAP is the fleet's ONLY orchestration cap and it governs one site; this makes the cap a shared lever so any future emitter inherits governance for free rather than re-litigating it. Operator's '3 ideal, maybe 4' becomes the default+ceiling pair, changeable in one constant.
basis: grounding brief §1: 'only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7 (execution_spec.py:114)... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, engine bridges unbounded.' Operator (intake §added constraint): 'Maximum 3 concurrent agents... 4 permitted only for short read-only scans.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency.py (resolver + FLEET_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT/CEILING constants) plus tests/test_concurrency_resolver.py asserting the precedence ladder and ceiling clamp; verified by unit tests covering env>session>default resolution and a >ceiling input being clamped.

title: Bake a runtime batching semaphore into the emitted workflow, not a hoped-for chunk loop
idea: The emitter already injects a `__gate` JS helper verbatim into generated scripts (execution_spec.py:132). Add a sibling `__concurrencyGate(items, capFn)` helper the emitter bakes in, that chunks any `parallel()` fan-out into sequential batches of ≤cap at RUN time, reading the cap from the resolver at execution. This converts the mined 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery' into actual machinery: the generated script physically cannot exceed the cap, versus today's reliance on the authoring workflow to hand-chunk. Leverage compounds because every future emitted workflow inherits enforced batching from the same helper the way it inherits `__gate`.
basis: Session-mining pattern 4 (grounding §7): "'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery' (3 repos)"; existing injected-helper pattern at execution_spec.py:132 (_JS_GATE_HELPER).
outcome_shape: Merged PR extending execution_spec.py with a _JS_CONCURRENCY_HELPER emitted into generated workflows + a golden-output test asserting a multi-branch fan-out emits batched dispatch capped at the resolved value; verified by running a generated script fixture and observing ≤cap concurrent dispatch.

title: Extract the 429-backoff logic into one shared retry primitive the whole fleet reuses
idea: 429 handling exists today only inside the unifi and mission-control HTTP clients, duplicated and invisible to the agent-dispatch and engine-bridge paths that actually hit rate limits. Extract a single `retry_with_backoff(fn, *, on_status=429)` primitive (exponential backoff + jitter + cap) into a shared scripts location and have both existing clients plus the engine bridges adopt it. Leverage: one hardened backoff implementation becomes the fleet default, so the next bridge added inherits 429 resilience instead of re-implementing (or omitting) it. This is the adaptive counterpart to the static cap — caps prevent overshoot, backoff recovers from the 429s that slip through.
basis: grounding §1: 'HTTP-level 429 handling exists only in unifi mission-control clients.' Session-mining pattern 4: 'Rate-limit fan-out kills — 6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a shared retry/backoff helper module + tests (backoff schedule, jitter bounds, max-attempts, non-429 passthrough) and refactoring the unifi + mission-control clients to import it; verified by the existing client tests still green against the shared helper.

title: Session-wide concurrency budget ledger so nested caps compose instead of multiply
idea: Independent per-layer caps do not give a fleet-wide cap: an `/outcome` leaf (cap 3) that spawns a team-execution run (cap 3) that fires a verify panel still yields far more than 3 truly-concurrent agents because the caps multiply across nesting depth. Introduce a session-scoped concurrency-budget ledger (a small file in the same spirit as the /outcome cost ledger 'leaf-produced fact'), where every spawn site acquires a slot before dispatch and releases on completion, so the operator's global '≤3 at any moment' holds across the whole nested tree. Leverage: turns N independent local knobs into one enforced global invariant — the compounding win is that adding a new spawn site anywhere just calls acquire/release and the global cap stays true.
basis: First-principles: intake sets '≤3 concurrent agents at any moment, ACROSS ALL PHASES.' Grounding §1 confirms three independent unbounded fan-out sites that nest (/outcome leaf → team-execution fan-out → verify panel). Independent caps of k at depth d compose to worst-case k^d simultaneous agents, so a per-site cap of 3 cannot satisfy a global 'at any moment' bound — only a shared budget acquired/released across sites can. Engages the /outcome campaign 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' pattern as the storage precedent rather than a new committed-state field.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a session concurrency-budget acquire/release helper + ledger file format doc, wired into the three spawn sites, with a test spawning a nested fan-out and asserting peak concurrent slots never exceeds the global cap; verified by the peak-slot assertion.

title: Encode /optimize's deliberate serial=1 as a first-class exception in the cap registry, not a re-added fan-out knob
idea: /optimize SHED its `max_concurrent` fan-out on purpose: parallel experiments contaminate one-variable measurement, so it runs serial in working-state by design and re-adds parallelism only via explicit Phase-4 operator escalation. Rather than re-introduce a fan-out knob, record this as a DECISIONS.md entry and give the shared concurrency registry an explicit `serial-by-design` marker for /optimize, so the fleet-wide cap primitive treats /optimize's concurrency=1 as an intentional invariant, not a site that 'forgot to cap.' Leverage: the shared primitive gains a vocabulary for deliberate exceptions, so future serial-by-design loops declare intent once instead of looking like governance gaps. This explicitly engages the shed rather than reversing it.
basis: optimize/SKILL.md:18-20: 'The default path SHEDS ce-optimize's... parallel / max_concurrent fan-out... Those re-enter only by an explicit operator-choice escalation (Phase 4)... runs serial and in working state by default.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md entry (why /optimize stays serial; revisit-when = Phase-4 escalation demonstrably needed) plus a `serial-by-design` field/marker in the shared concurrency registry for /optimize; verified by a test asserting the resolver returns 1 for the /optimize context.

title: Drift-guard test that fails CI when any fan-out site bypasses the shared cap
idea: The codebase already uses cross-module drift-guard tests that fail when a mirrored constant diverges (execution_spec.py:80-81, SANDBOX_PROFILES mirror). Apply the same discipline to concurrency: a guard test that scans the spawn-site inventory (references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md already enumerates them) and fails if any emits a raw unbounded `parallel(` / batched Agent spawn without going through the shared resolver/gate. Leverage: prevents aspiration from silently re-creeping — the cap stays machinery permanently because a regression turns CI red rather than shipping an un-governed fan-out that surfaces only as a 429 storm months later.
basis: execution_spec.py:80-81: 'a cross-module drift-guard test asserts the two copies stay identical.' CLAUDE.md references plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md as 'the full spawn-site inventory.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding tests/test_concurrency_governance_drift.py that enumerates spawn sites and asserts each routes through the shared cap primitive, plus any doc update to the spawn-site inventory; verified by the test failing on an injected unbounded-fan-out fixture and passing on the governed tree.

title: Promote max_concurrent to a validated ExecutionSpec field alongside tier
idea: Concurrency should be an authored, validated dimension of a workflow the same way model/effort tier already is. Add `max_concurrent` to the ExecutionSpec dataclass so a /plan can author per-workflow concurrency, validated at emit against a hard `FLEET_CONCURRENCY_CEILING` exactly as VERIFY_N_CAP validates panel N today (author above the ceiling → emit FAILS, not silently runs). Leverage: concurrency joins tier in the one operator-facing lever surface, so the same authoring+validation+drift-guard machinery that already governs tiers now governs concurrency — no parallel governance stack. This extends the existing VERIFY_N_CAP pattern the theme names as the seam to build on.
basis: execution_spec.py:111-114: 'Hard upper bound on a verify panel's verifier count. N above this FAILS validate/emit... VERIFY_N_CAP = 7.' Theme constraint: 'VERIFY_N_CAP is the existing pattern to extend.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a validated max_concurrent field to the ExecutionSpec dataclass + emit-time ceiling check + to_dict serialization, with tests asserting over-ceiling authoring fails emit and a valid value round-trips; verified by the emit-fails-on-over-ceiling test.

title: AIMD rate-limit weathervane: cap that multiplicatively backs off on observed 429s
idea: Borrow TCP congestion control's additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease (AIMD) discipline: persist a session-scoped 429-incident signal, and have the shared resolver return a reduced cap (e.g. 3→2) for subsequent batches after a 429 is observed, recovering additively toward the default on clean runs. This makes the cap self-tuning rather than a static guess, so a rate-limited window automatically throttles the whole fleet and a calm window restores throughput — without an operator babysitting. Leverage compounds because the signal is fleet-shared: one bridge hitting 429 protects every other concurrent spawn site through the same resolver. It stays a safety floor (reliability), not a spend/tier lever, so it sits beside — not inside — the operator-choice model/effort framework.
basis: Prior art: TCP congestion control AIMD (Van Jacobson, RFC 5681 congestion window) — additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease is the canonical proven-stable feedback rule for shared-resource contention; lives in the TCP/IP stack every OS ships. Applied here to the shared concurrency resolver's cap value.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an AIMD adjustment layer + 429-signal state file to the shared resolver, with tests asserting multiplicative decrease on a simulated 429 and additive recovery over clean cycles, clamped to [1, ceiling]; verified by the decrease/recover trajectory test.

title: bounded_parallel(): a semaphore/bulkhead helper that chunks every emitted wave
idea: Today segment_units renders a layer of >1 ready unit as one unbounded parallel([...]) wave (execution_spec.py:1219-1225); VERIFY_N_CAP only bounds verifier-panel width, not layer width, so a wide dependency layer can spawn N agents with no ceiling. Borrow the bulkhead/semaphore pattern from resilience engineering (Netflix Hystrix, and the classic counting-semaphore that guards a fixed pool of resources): add a bounded_parallel(thunks, cap) codegen helper that splits any wave wider than cap into sequential sub-batches of <=cap, awaiting each before the next. The cap becomes machinery the generated workflow physically cannot exceed, converting KTD6's aspiration into an emitted structural bound identical in spirit to how VERIFY_N_CAP already fails-closed. Emit the helper once at script top and route both layer waves and verify panels through it.
basis: Source domain: resilience engineering / concurrency primitives (Hystrix bulkhead + counting semaphore). execution_spec.py:1219-1225 emits 'const [...] = await parallel([' for any layer of >1 ready unit with no width bound; line 112 comment scopes VERIFY_N_CAP to 'a verify panel's verifier count' only. Grounding brief: 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery.'
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py (new _emit_bounded_parallel helper + rewrite of the layer-wave and verify-panel renderers to route through it) plus a test in tests/ asserting an emitted script with a 5-wide layer at cap=3 produces two sub-batches. Verified by rendering a fixture spec and grepping the generated JS for the sub-batch loop.

title: concurrency_cap as a validated execution_spec field, filed at plan time like a flight plan
idea: Air-traffic flow management sets a single authoritative flow rate when the flight plan is filed (the Ground Delay Program / metering-fix rate), not renegotiated per aircraft mid-air. Mirror that: add a concurrency_cap field to ExecutionSpec, authored in /plan alongside the unit tier table, default 3 (operator's stated ideal), validated against a closed sane range exactly as MODELS/EFFORTS tiers are validated at emit so a typo fails emit rather than silently uncapping. This settles the cap-policy-architecture question in favor of spec-resident (the same layer that already owns tiers and VERIFY_N_CAP) rather than env or session, giving one diffable, reviewable knob per workflow that bounded_parallel then enforces.
basis: Source domain: air-traffic flow management (FAA Ground Delay Program / metering-fix rate set at flight-plan filing). Grounding brief section 1: 'only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP'; execution_spec.py:46-53 establishes the closed-set-validated-at-emit pattern the cap field would join; operator statement 'concurrency 3 ideal, maybe 4.'
outcome_shape: PR touching execution_spec.py (ExecutionSpec dataclass field + validate() range check), plan/SKILL.md:296-352 unit-tier-table section documenting the knob, and a drift-guard test asserting cap outside range fails validate. Verified by unit test on validate() and a rendered fixture carrying the field.

title: AIMD congestion governor: start at 3, multiplicatively back off on 429, additively probe back up
idea: A static cap of 3 is either too timid when the account is quiet or too aggressive under contention. TCP congestion control (Reno's additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease) solves exactly this: probe capacity by slowly raising the window, and halve it instantly on a loss signal. Emit a small runtime governor into the generated workflow that holds a live concurrency window (init 3), and on any agent() throwing a 429/rate-limit error, multiplicatively drops the window (e.g. to 1-2) and re-queues the failed unit, then additively increments back toward the ceiling after a clean batch. The 429 is the 'packet loss' signal; the cap field (idea T13-F5-2) is the ssthresh ceiling. This makes the fleet self-tune to whatever headroom actually exists instead of guessing.
basis: Source domain: distributed-systems / networking congestion control — TCP Reno AIMD (Jacobson 1988) and its modern reuse in client-side adaptive rate limiting (AWS SDK 'adaptive' retry mode, which literally runs a token-bucket AIMD loop client-side). Lives in the AWS SDK retry documentation and boto3 adaptive retry implementation.
outcome_shape: PR touching execution_spec.py to emit an _adaptive_governor JS shim wrapping bounded_parallel, plus a reference doc plugins/saga/references/adaptive-concurrency.md explaining the AIMD contract, and a test simulating a 429-throwing thunk asserting the window halves and the unit re-runs. Verified by the simulation test observing window trajectory.

title: Circuit breaker + backoff-with-jitter at the unbounded engine bridges
idea: The engine bridges (codex/agy and future registry providers) are called out as unbounded, and HTTP-429 handling today exists only in the unifi and mission-control clients. Netflix Hystrix's circuit breaker plus the canonical exponential-backoff-with-full-jitter (AWS 'Exponential Backoff and Jitter' article) is the standard remedy: on a run of 429s the breaker trips OPEN and short-circuits further calls for a cooldown, retries individual calls with jittered backoff (avoiding thundering-herd synchronization), then HALF-OPENs a probe before closing. Add a shared bridge_call() wrapper in the engine-bridge layer that all provider scripts route through, so a second opinion or offload that hits a limit degrades to backoff-then-resume instead of a hard fan-out kill.
basis: Source domain: resilience engineering — Netflix Hystrix circuit breaker + AWS 'Exponential Backoff and Jitter' (Marc Brooker). Grounding brief section 1: 'engine bridges unbounded... HTTP-level 429 handling exists only in unifi mission-control clients'; session-mining pattern 4: '6/7 agents failed on rate-limiting.'
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared bridge_call helper (backoff-with-jitter + breaker state) consumed by the codex/agy bridge scripts under plugins/, a reference doc, and a test injecting sequential 429s asserting the breaker trips and a later call succeeds after cooldown. Verified by the fault-injection test.

title: Fleet-wide slot coordinator: one finite pool of dispatch slots across saga, teams, and bridges
idea: Per-workflow caps still let three concurrent surfaces (/outcome leaf dispatch, team-execution reviewer fan-out, engine bridges) each open 3 agents and collectively blow past the account limit. Congested airports solve the identical multi-actor shared-scarce-resource problem with IATA slot coordination: a finite pool of takeoff/landing slots that every airline draws from through one coordinator, so aggregate flow is bounded regardless of how many airlines want to fly. Stand up a fleet-wide concurrency ledger (Redis-backed via the existing redis-channel substrate, or a lockfile fallback) exposing acquire/release slot primitives; every fan-out site acquires before spawn and releases on completion. The pool size is the true fleet cap; individual workflows compete for slots rather than each assuming private headroom.
basis: Source domain: aviation logistics — IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines (coordinated-airport slot pools) and distributed rate-limiters (Redis token pool). Grounding brief section 1: 'team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, engine bridges unbounded'; intake §92-104 promotes 'fleet-wide rate-limit-aware concurrency governance... currently have no shared cap policy.'
outcome_shape: PR adding a slot-coordinator module + a redis-channel-backed (with lockfile fallback) acquire/release CLI, wiring the emitter's bounded_parallel and team-execution spawn sites to acquire slots, a reference doc, and an integration test showing two concurrent workflows never exceed the pool. Verified by the concurrency integration test.

title: Re-admit /optimize's max_concurrent as a risk-budget draw against the fleet cap, not a private knob
idea: /optimize deliberately SHED ce-optimize's max_concurrent fan-out (optimize/SKILL.md:17-20) because its default must be serial-safe and crash-safe in working state; re-adding a naive knob would reopen exactly that. Engage the revisit-when honestly: the shed was about the DEFAULT, and the SKILL already documents that parallel fan-out re-enters only via an explicit operator-choice Phase-4 escalation. Finance risk budgeting is the reconciling frame: an experiment desk does not get its own uncapped position size; it draws down against a firm-wide risk budget (VaR limit). Re-admit max_concurrent to /optimize solely as a Phase-4 escalation that acquires slots from the fleet slot-coordinator (idea T13-F5-5) or, absent that, is clamped to the spec concurrency_cap — so the escalation can never exceed the fleet-wide ceiling and the serial default is untouched.
basis: Source domain: finance risk management (firm-wide VaR / position-limit budgeting). Direct: optimize/SKILL.md:17-20 'The default path SHEDS... its parallel / max_concurrent fan-out... Those re-enter only by an explicit operator-choice escalation (Phase 4)' — the revisit-when is the documented escalation seam itself; this idea binds re-entry to the fleet cap rather than reverting the shed.
outcome_shape: PR touching optimize/SKILL.md Phase-4 escalation section to add a max_concurrent option explicitly clamped to the fleet cap / slot pool, plus CHANGELOG and a doc-review-checkable narrative note. Verified by doc-review confirming the escalation cannot exceed the ceiling and the serial default is unchanged.

title: Per-session cgroup-style cap: a nice-level wrapper all spawns consult
idea: Between per-workflow and fleet-wide sits the session: one Claude Code session may run /outcome while the operator also fires an ad-hoc team-execute, and neither knows about the other. Linux cgroups solve the analogous problem for processes: a cpu.max / pids.max ceiling attached to a control group that every child process inherits regardless of who spawned it. Emit a per-session concurrency ceiling written once at session/run start (a small state file in the saga scratch dir) that every fan-out primitive reads and decrements against before spawning, inheriting the cap the way a process inherits its cgroup. Cheaper than a distributed coordinator (no Redis dependency), it closes the same-session double-dispatch gap and gives the operator one place to raise 3->4 for an attended run.
basis: Source domain: operating systems — Linux cgroups v2 pids.max / cpu.max inherited ceilings (kernel cgroup-v2 documentation). This is a strictly cheaper, single-host variant of the fleet coordinator, chosen because a session is a single-host boundary where a shared state file suffices and a network round-trip does not.
outcome_shape: PR adding a session-cap state file (written at run start, default 3) + a read-and-acquire helper consumed by the emitter and team-execution spawn sites, a reference doc, and a test asserting two same-session fan-outs share the ceiling. Verified by the shared-ceiling test.

title: Poka-yoke drift guard: emit fails when any fan-out site lacks a cap
idea: VERIFY_N_CAP became real machinery because a validate() check fails emit when a panel exceeds it (execution_spec.py:355-358); the wider fan-out surfaces stayed aspirational because nothing fails when they omit a cap. Toyota's poka-yoke (mistake-proofing) principle is to make the defect physically impossible to ship, not to remind people to avoid it. Add a preflight/emit-time guard plus a repo-level drift-guard test that enumerates every fan-out spawn site (the same inventory already maintained in references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md) and FAILS if any emits an unbounded parallel([...]) or spawns without acquiring a slot. This converts 'we should cap concurrency' from prose into a red test, exactly the mechanism that made VERIFY_N_CAP trustworthy, and prevents a future spawn site from silently reintroducing the unbounded path.
basis: Source domain: manufacturing quality — Toyota Production System poka-yoke (mistake-proofing / jidoka). Direct: execution_spec.py:355-358 shows the fail-closed guard pattern that made VERIFY_N_CAP machinery; CLAUDE.md references plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md as the maintained spawn-site inventory this guard would enumerate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a drift-guard test in tests/ that scans the emitter output and the spawn-site inventory for uncapped parallel/spawn calls and fails on any, plus a short note in sandbox-spawn-sites.md. Verified by deliberately introducing an unbounded wave in a fixture and observing the test go red.

title: WAVE_WIDTH_CAP: chunk emitted parallel() waves into batches of ≤3
idea: Flip the constraint to '100 agents fire at once' — which is exactly what emit_workflow_script does today: dependency_layers returns a layer, and line 1225 renders `const [...] = await parallel([...thunks])` with one thunk per independent unit and ZERO width bound, so a 22-target fan-out layer spawns 22 concurrent agents. Mine the kernel: add a WAVE_WIDTH_CAP sibling to VERIFY_N_CAP and rewrite the layer emitter to chunk thunks into sequential batches of ≤cap (an explicit `for (const batch of chunk(thunks, CAP))` loop over parallel() calls), turning the claimed concurrency cap from prose into emitted control flow. This is the direct 'make KTD6 machinery, not aspiration' move.
basis: execution_spec.py:1225 emits `await parallel([` with no width bound for a >1-unit layer; grounding brief §1 line 34-39 'team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded' and §7 line 130 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery'.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py (new WAVE_WIDTH_CAP const beside VERIFY_N_CAP; a _emit_batched_wave helper; emit_workflow_script layer loop rewritten to chunk) + tests/test_execution_spec.py. Verified: emit a spec with a 22-target fan-out layer, assert the generated JS contains N sequential `parallel([...])` calls each with ≤CAP thunks and NO single parallel() with >CAP thunks.

title: One fleet knob: shared concurrency.py resolver read by all three emitters
idea: Flip 'the cap lives in one hardcoded constant' to the opposite extreme — exactly ONE authoritative knob for the entire fleet, resolved through a strict precedence ladder rather than duplicated per emitter. Extract a plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency.py exposing resolve_concurrency_cap(spec_value, session_env, default=3) with precedence spec > SAGA_MAX_CONCURRENT env > default 3 (the operator's stated ideal). execution_spec.py's emitter, team_emitter.py (U11 team protocol), and outcome_spec.py all import it instead of inventing their own bound, so a single change moves the whole fleet's ceiling. The kernel: cap policy is a resolved value with a documented precedence, not a scattered literal.
basis: Intake brief line 93 (operator, mid-intake): 'Maximum 3 concurrent agents any moment, across all phases (4 permitted only for short, read-only scans)... 3 ideal historically.' The default=3 and env-override ladder encode that statement directly.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency.py + tests/test_concurrency.py, with execution_spec.py / team_emitter.py / outcome_spec.py importing resolve_concurrency_cap. Verified: unit test asserts precedence (spec beats env beats default) and that default==3; a drift-guard test asserts no emitter defines its own separate cap literal.

title: __withBackoff harness helper: unattended runs self-survive 429
idea: Flip to 'zero operators, fully autonomous' — an overnight /outcome or workflow run has nobody to hand-restart the '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting' wipeout. Inject a _JS_BACKOFF_HELPER beside _JS_GATE_HELPER: agent() calls are wrapped so a rate-limit error triggers exponential backoff with jitter and bounded retries, and a partially-429'd parallel wave re-queues ONLY the failed thunks rather than failing the whole layer. The kernel is that adaptive backoff belongs in the emitted machinery, not left to the operator — today 429 handling exists only in the unifi and mission-control HTTP clients, nowhere in orchestration.
basis: Grounding brief §7 line 130 'Rate-limit fan-out kills — 6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting' and §1 line 38-39 'HTTP-level 429 handling exists only in unifi and mission-control clients' (absent from all orchestration emitters).
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py (new _JS_BACKOFF_HELPER string; thunk/agent emission wrapped in __withBackoff) + tests/test_execution_spec.py. Verified: emit any multi-unit spec and grep the JS for the __withBackoff wrapper around every agent() call; a JS-level unit test drives the helper through a simulated 429 and asserts it retries on the documented backoff schedule and re-queues only failed thunks.

title: Fleet-wide concurrency lease: cross-session token bucket
idea: Flip 'each workflow caps itself' to 'the cap is fleet-wide across every concurrent process'. The pre-mortem's own arithmetic exposes the hole: three unattended workflows each individually capped at 3 still sum to 9 in-flight agents against one shared Anthropic rate limit — a per-workflow cap cannot hold the operator's fleet-wide ceiling. Mine the kernel: a filesystem-based (flock'd counter file) or redis-channel-backed concurrency LEASE that every saga/team-execution/outcome dispatch must acquire before spawning and release on completion, so the sum across all sessions is bounded. Even the degenerate v1 — a documented single-writer lease file with acquire/release — closes the multi-session summation gap the per-workflow caps miss.
basis: First-principles: the operator's constraint is 'Maximum 3 concurrent agents any moment, ACROSS all phases' (intake line 93), but every other T13 idea caps per-emitter; N independently-capped-at-3 processes yield up to 3N concurrent against a single provider quota. Only a cap whose scope is the shared resource (the provider token bucket), not the workflow, satisfies the stated invariant — hence a cross-process lease is required, not optional.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency_lease.py (flock counter with acquire/release + stale-lease reaper) + a DECISIONS.md entry recording fleet-scope-vs-workflow-scope rationale + tests/test_concurrency_lease.py. Verified: a test spawns 6 mock acquirers against a lease of 3 and asserts never more than 3 hold simultaneously and stale holders are reclaimed.

title: Decouple /optimize's shed knobs: re-add bounded parallelism WITHOUT worktree isolation
idea: /optimize shed three things as a bundle — worktree-per-experiment isolation, parallel/max_concurrent fan-out, and auto-commit — defaulting to serial-in-working-state, with re-entry only via an explicit Phase 4 operator-choice escalation. Flip the bundling assumption: the reason to shed worktrees (working-state simplicity, avoiding the stale-worktree disease) is NOT the reason to shed parallelism (rate-limit fear). Engage the shed by UN-bundling: define a Phase 4 escalation that re-adds ONLY bounded-parallel experiment fan-out (capped by the shared concurrency resolver from T13-F6-2, default 3) while keeping working-state serial commit — honoring 're-enter only by explicit operator-choice, recorded narratively.' This reconciles the shed knob instead of blindly re-adding it.
basis: optimize/SKILL.md:17-20 'The default path SHEDS ce-optimize's git-worktree-per-experiment isolation, its parallel / max_concurrent fan-out, and its auto-commit... Those re-enter only by an explicit operator-choice escalation (Phase 4), recorded narratively.'
outcome_shape: PR editing plugins/saga/skills/optimize/SKILL.md Phase 4 escalation section to document a bounded-parallel-experiments option (worktree isolation stays OFF; cap sourced from concurrency resolver, default 3) + a DECISIONS.md entry on un-bundling the shed knobs. Verified via /doc-review that the escalation path renders and the concurrency-cap reference resolves; no code path enables parallelism without the recorded operator choice.

title: Aggregate in-flight guard: widest layer × verify panels, checked at emit
idea: Flip 'one cap dimension is enough'. VERIFY_N_CAP bounds a single panel to 7, but panels run INSIDE parallel layers: a layer of 3 units each carrying verify n=7 puts up to 3 + 21 = 24 agents in flight simultaneously — the exact magnitude of the 22-judge incident VERIFY_N_CAP was born to prevent, reconstituted along an axis the cap never measured. Mine the kernel: add a pure function max_concurrent_agents(spec) that computes the true simultaneous ceiling (widest dependency layer, plus each unit's verify panel width where panels co-run), and FAIL or WARN at emit time when it exceeds the fleet cap. This makes the AGGREGATE a machinery check, not a per-panel one.
basis: First-principles from the code: VERIFY_N_CAP=7 (execution_spec.py:114) bounds one Verify.n, but dependency_layers can place multiple verify-bearing units in one parallel wave (emit_workflow_script line 1194-1229), and each _emit_verify_panel spawns n concurrent verifiers — so simultaneous in-flight = layer_width + Σ(co-running panel widths), which no current check bounds. The 22-judge failure recurs whenever that product exceeds the provider limit.
outcome_shape: PR adding max_concurrent_agents(spec) to plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py with an emit-time warn/fail against the fleet cap + tests/test_execution_spec.py. Verified: a spec whose widest layer×panel product exceeds the cap trips the guard (SpecError or stderr WARN), and a within-cap spec emits clean.

title: Per-lane concurrency: max_concurrent as an engine-registry field
idea: Flip 'the cap is one global number' — that is wrong the moment provider routing lands: a local Ollama lane ($0 offload target) can run 100 concurrent while the Anthropic lane must stay ≤3, because rate limits are per-provider, not fleet-uniform. Mine the kernel: the concurrency knob belongs BESIDE each provider entry. Add a max_concurrent field to engine-registry.yaml's schema (engine_registry.py), and have the batched-wave emitter (T13-F6-1) partition thunks by their resolved engine lane and batch each lane against its own cap — so Anthropic units serialize at 3 while Ollama units flood freely in the same wave. Cap granularity follows the rate-limit boundary, which is the provider.
basis: Intake brief lines 80-83: 'extend existing engine-registry seam (engine_resolver.py / engine_registry.py); each provider a registry entry + bridge script. Ollama → $0 offload target; DeepSeek → cheap second opinion.' Per-provider entries are the natural home for a per-provider concurrency bound.
outcome_shape: PR adding an optional max_concurrent field to plugins/saga/references/engine-registry.yaml + its parse/validate in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py + lane-partitioned batching in execution_spec.py's wave emitter + tests. Verified: registry-load test accepts/rejects the field per schema; emit test asserts a mixed-lane layer serializes Anthropic thunks at the lane cap while local-lane thunks are unbatched.

title: Upstream-live parity job: close the #222 disease the current gate leaves open
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py only recomputes the SHA256 of the vendored bytes and compares it to a pinned SHA vendored alongside them, so it catches hand-edits to the vendored copy but is structurally blind to the source moving ahead - its own docstring says 'a match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator LAST produced and pinned.' That is exactly the #222 stale-mirror failure (343 cards passed a mirror while the live contract had changed): if infiquetra-sdlc's gen_issue_contract.py evolves and nobody re-vendors, the gate stays green forever. Add a scheduled (nightly / weekly) CI job that checks out infiquetra-sdlc at HEAD, runs the generator, and diffs its output against the vendored artifacts, opening or updating a 'contract drift' issue on mismatch. This is opt-in and cannot block PRs (no sdlc checkout in the fast path), preserving the KTD3 hermetic design while finally detecting the drift direction that matters.
basis: plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py:15-21 docstring: 'Design (deliberately does NOT run the sdlc generator)... A match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator last produced and pinned' - upstream advance is undetectable. Origin pain: grounding brief section 3, card_validator.py 343 cards / #222 stale hand-mirror.
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-upstream-drift.yml (schedule: cron) plus a check_upstream_parity.py that clones infiquetra-sdlc, runs gen_issue_contract.py, and diffs; verified by a red run against a deliberately-reverted vendored artifact opening a labeled drift issue, and a green run when in sync.

title: Bring sdlc-schema.json under the parity umbrella it is currently exempt from
idea: config/sdlc-schema.json is vendored from infiquetra-sdlc (the docstrings and migration_notes say so) yet, unlike the two issue-contract modules, it carries NO .sha256 sidecar and is absent from VENDORED_ARTIFACTS, so a hand-edit or a silent stale copy of the canonical board/routing/schema contract flips nothing red. This is the single largest un-guarded contract in the plugin: teams, boards, phase_board_map, wip_limits, review models all resolve from it. Emit a pinned sdlc-schema.json.sha256 at vendor time and add the file to the VENDORED_ARTIFACTS tuple so the existing gate and test_issue_contract_parity.py cover it with zero new machinery. The generalizable rule: every vendored contract artifact gets a sidecar the moment it lands, never bolted on per-incident.
basis: ls of plugins/mission-control/config/generated/ shows .sha256 sidecars only for issue_contract_data.py and issue_contract_shim.py; VENDORED_ARTIFACTS in check_issue_contract_parity.py:40-43 lists exactly those two; sdlc-schema.json lives in config/ with no sidecar and is unguarded despite being vendored (its own migration_notes describe source-derived snapshots).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/sdlc-schema.json.sha256, extending VENDORED_ARTIFACTS, and a test asserting the gate now covers three artifacts; verified by hand-editing the schema in a test fixture and observing parity_errors() flag it.

title: A contract-consumer registry so a source change knows who it breaks
idea: The parity gate lives only inside mission-control and enumerates only mission-control's own vendored copies - nothing in the fleet records which OTHER repos vendor sdlc-schema.json or the issue contract, so when infiquetra-sdlc regenerates a contract, the blast radius is discovered by memory and grep, per-incident. Ship a machine-readable contract-consumers manifest (a consumers.json listing each contract artifact -> [repo, vendored-path, parity-gate-present?]) checked into infiquetra-sdlc as the source-side truth, plus a mission-control command that reads it to answer 'if I change this field, which repos re-vendor?' The manifest is the substrate idea T14-F1-1's cross-repo job iterates, and it makes the 4-repo contract-mirror pain from the grounding brief a queryable fact instead of tribal knowledge.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:40-43 VENDORED_ARTIFACTS is a per-repo local tuple with no cross-repo consumer list; grounding brief section 3 'Rename/vocabulary contract-mirror (4-repo)' and 'Consumer-side (cross-repo)' name the 4-repo hand-copy spread with no registry enumerating it.
outcome_shape: PR (mission-control + a proposed infiquetra-sdlc consumers.json) adding a contracts/consumers.json manifest and a mission-control:contract-consumers command; verified by the command listing all vendored copies of a named contract and flagging any consumer lacking a parity gate.

title: A vocabulary-rename campaign runner for lockstep cross-repo landings
idea: The Olympus->CAMPPS retirement and the saga rename were executed as hand-copy lockstep landings; the schema's migration_notes record the human doing it by prose ('2026-06-17: Retired Mount Olympus... phase_board_map now projects only...'). There is no tool that takes a term mapping (old->new, plus a retire-vs-rename disposition) and drives it: grep every consumer surface, generate a per-repo diff, and produce an ordered landing plan that respects the additive-then-remove sequencing a live board needs. Build it as a mission-control command (NOT a new plugin - honoring {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}, whose revisit-when is a genuine consolidation-burden proof: this rides existing mission-control CLI + the section-3 four-repo mirror pain rather than adding plugin #9). Output is a reviewable campaign plan, not auto-applied edits, keeping Claude the verifier-of-record.
basis: sdlc-schema.json migration_notes (lines 4-6) show Olympus retirement done as hand-written prose across phase_board_map/wip_limits; grounding brief section on T14 axes: 'rename-campaign-tooling (saga rename, Olympus->CAMPPS lockstep landings).' Binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} engaged: implemented as a mission-control command, no new plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding a mission-control:rename-campaign command + skill doc that emits an ordered per-repo landing plan from a term-mapping input; verified by feeding it a synthetic old->new mapping and asserting the plan enumerates every consumer file and sequences additive-before-removal.

title: Declare pin-vs-float compat instead of the brittle exact-literal assertion
idea: sdlc-schema.json carries schema_version '2026-06-17' and migration_notes that carefully distinguish 'strictly additive' from breaking changes, but the ONLY consumer of that field pins it as a hardcoded exact string (test_prompt_alignment.py:121 asserts schema['schema_version'] == '2026-06-17'). So a legitimate additive bump - the very thing the migration_notes say is safe - breaks the test, while there is no logic that would reject an actually-incompatible schema. Replace the exact-literal pin with a declared compat contract: the schema gains a compat_floor / breaking-since field, and consumers assert 'vendored schema_version >= my required floor' rather than '== a frozen string.' This turns the migration_notes' additive-vs-breaking prose into enforced version-coupling semantics and stops additive bumps from tripping a false failure.
basis: plugins/mission-control/tests/test_prompt_alignment.py:121 'assert schema["schema_version"] == "2026-06-17"' is the sole consumer and is an exact-literal pin; sdlc-schema.json migration_notes (lines 4-6) explicitly classify changes as 'strictly additive' vs breaking with no machine-readable compat field.
outcome_shape: PR adding a compat block to sdlc-schema.json and replacing the exact-literal test with a floor/range assertion helper; verified by bumping schema_version additively in a fixture and observing the test pass, then bumping past the declared breaking-since and observing it fail.

title: Cosmetic-vs-substantive drift classifier to kill false re-vendor churn
idea: The parity gate is pure SHA256 byte-identity, so a purely cosmetic upstream regeneration (a reordered comment, a reflowed docstring, a trailing-comma change) flips the hash and screams 'drifted - re-vendor' even when the actual DATA surface (the tuples and dicts the shim imports) is byte-for-byte semantically identical. That is friction: the operator burns a re-vendor cycle to chase a no-op change. Since issue_contract_shim.py and issue_contract_data.py are PURE DATA modules (REQUIRED_H3_HEADERS, SEMANTIC_CHECKS, EXECUTABLE_CHECKS, PLACEHOLDER_LINES), add a semantic-diff companion that, on a hash mismatch, imports both the vendored and the freshly-generated module and compares the exported __all__ objects, reporting 'cosmetic-only' vs 'semantic' drift. The SHA gate stays the hard invariant; the classifier just tells the human whether the re-vendor is load-bearing.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:64 hashes raw bytes (hashlib.sha256(artifact.read_bytes())); issue_contract_shim.py:89-100 __all__ exports are pure tuples/dicts, making value-level comparison feasible - so byte drift and semantic drift are conflated today.
outcome_shape: PR adding a classify_drift() helper + CLI flag to the parity tooling that reports cosmetic-vs-semantic on mismatch, plus a unit test with a comment-only-changed fixture asserting 'cosmetic'; verified by the test distinguishing a whitespace change from a header-set change.

title: Executable retired-vocabulary invariant: make the migration_note a test
idea: After a rename/retirement the schema keeps the old term as deliberate historical context (teams.olympus is status 'retired_historical', and there is a retired_patterns list) - correct, but the promise that no ACTIVE surface still routes through the retired term is enforced only by a hand-written migration_note sentence, not by code. Nothing asserts that phase_board_map, active board keys, cross_team_transfer targets, and wip_limits contain zero references to any status=retired_historical team or any retired_patterns entry. Add a guard test that derives the retired-vocabulary set from the schema itself (teams with retired status + retired_patterns) and asserts every active routing surface excludes it. This converts every future retirement's core promise into an executable invariant, so an incomplete rename campaign fails CI instead of silently leaving a live edge pointed at a dead term.
basis: sdlc-schema.json: teams.olympus status 'retired_historical' with board null (verified via json load); retired_patterns list at line 218; cross_team_transfer_rule line 205 states 'Mount Olympus is retired historical context and is not an active target' as prose with no test enforcing active surfaces exclude the retired set.
outcome_shape: PR adding a test_retired_vocabulary_isolation.py that derives the retired set from the schema and asserts active routing surfaces exclude it; verified by injecting a retired-team reference into a phase_board_map fixture and observing the test fail.

title: Provenance sidecars: record which upstream commit produced each vendored artifact
idea: The .sha256 manifests contain only a bare 64-char digest - they pin what the vendored bytes are but record nothing about WHERE they came from, so the question 'is this vendored copy stale?' cannot even be posed without guessing which infiquetra-sdlc commit generated it. Emit a .provenance.json beside each vendored artifact capturing {source_repo, source_commit_sha, generator_path, generated_at} at vendor time, and have the parity gate print it on both pass and fail. This is the missing coupling metadata that makes T14-F1-1's upstream-live check cheap (compare recorded source_commit to sdlc HEAD before doing any expensive regen) and gives every drift report a precise 're-vendor from commit X' instruction instead of 'go figure out the source state.'
basis: ls shows the two .sha256 files are 65B each (a bare hex digest + newline) with no upstream reference; check_issue_contract_parity.py:64-65 reads only expected = sha_path.read_text().strip() - there is no source-commit provenance anywhere in the vendoring surface.
outcome_shape: PR adding .provenance.json sidecars for each vendored artifact + gate output that prints provenance, and updating the vendoring generator contract to emit them; verified by the parity gate printing the recorded source commit and a test asserting each vendored artifact has a well-formed provenance sidecar.

title: Upstream-staleness guard: turn the half-parity gate into a whole gate
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py only proves vendored bytes equal what the source generator LAST produced and pinned — it cannot see that upstream has moved on, which is exactly the staleness class that let 343 cards pass a stale hand-mirror. Invert the manual 'did we re-vendor recently?' question into an automated freshness gate: a CI job (scheduled + PR) that reads the current pinned SHA from infiquetra-sdlc over `gh api` and compares it to each vendored `.sha256` manifest, failing loud when the source repo's fingerprint has advanced past the vendored one. This removes the human re-vendor cadence entirely — the gate tells you the moment a consumed contract goes stale, instead of a lucky re-verification catching it months later. Pair it with an auto-opened 're-vendor' PR body listing the changed artifacts.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring: 'A match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator LAST produced and pinned ... No sdlc checkout, no generator run -- just stdlib hashlib.' The gate structurally cannot detect upstream advance; grounding brief §3 records the 343-card stale-mirror (#222) as staleness-vs-live-contract, precisely this blind spot.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_upstream_freshness.py + a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow, verified by tests/test_upstream_freshness.py that mocks a source SHA ahead of the vendored manifest and asserts non-zero exit; workflow run visibly fails on injected staleness.

title: Close the unpinned-vendor hole: SHA-pin sdlc-schema.json itself
idea: The consumer-side parity gate vendors and hash-pins two generated modules (issue_contract_data.py, issue_contract_shim.py) but sdlc-schema.json — vendored by the SAME fetch-dont-copy pattern and explicitly named as a re-vendored artifact after the disaster — carries only prose migration_notes and NO .sha256 manifest. That leaves the single largest vendored contract able to drift silently under a hand-edit, the exact failure mode the parity gate was built to kill. Remove the gap by generating and committing sdlc-schema.json.sha256 and adding the file to check_issue_contract_parity.py's VENDORED_ARTIFACTS tuple, so a hand-edit to the schema flips its hash and fails the gate like the two modules already do.
basis: `find plugins -name '*.sha256'` returns only issue_contract_data.py.sha256 and issue_contract_shim.py.sha256; sdlc-schema.json has no pin. check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring names sdlc-schema.json as the same vendoring pattern ('the same vendoring pattern the plugin already uses for config/sdlc-schema.json') yet it is absent from VENDORED_ARTIFACTS.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/sdlc-schema.json.sha256 + extending VENDORED_ARTIFACTS in check_issue_contract_parity.py; verified by test_issue_contract_parity.py gaining a case that mutates one schema byte and asserts parity_errors() is non-empty.

title: One registry-driven vendored-artifact guard replacing bespoke per-contract checkers
idea: Today each vendored contract gets its own hand-written parity checker (check_issue_contract_parity.py is bespoke to two modules), so every new vendored artifact re-implements hashlib boilerplate and the next one is likely to ship unguarded — as sdlc-schema.json already did. Remove the per-artifact hand-authoring step: declare all vendored contracts once in a `vendored_manifest.json` ({consumer_path, upstream_repo, upstream_path, pinned_sha}) and drive a single generic check_vendored.py over it. Adding a new consumed contract becomes a one-line registry entry that is guarded by construction, and the fleet gains a single source of truth for 'what do we vendor and from where.' The best per-artifact guard is no per-artifact guard.
basis: First-principles: the parity gate's own docstring frames mission-control as 'a CONSUMER of the issue-contract pipeline ... the same vendoring pattern the plugin already uses for config/sdlc-schema.json' — i.e. the pattern is already repeated by hand, and sdlc-schema.json fell through the gap (idea T14-F2-2 evidence). A declarative manifest makes 'guarded' the default state rather than an act of remembering to hand-write a checker.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/vendored_manifest.json + generic check_vendored.py that supersedes check_issue_contract_parity.py's artifact list; verified by test asserting every *.sha256 on disk is referenced by exactly one manifest entry (no unguarded vendor, no orphan manifest row).

title: Collapse the four-format CHANGELOG heading parser to one canonical format
idea: test_release_triad.py must support FOUR distinct CHANGELOG version-heading formats (bracketed/bare crossed with hyphen/em-dash) because the fleet never standardized the vocabulary of a release heading. That per-plugin format freedom is silent drift: the parser is fragile and a fifth variant would slip a version past the triad guard undetected. Invert freedom into a single canonical form — pick one heading grammar, add a lint that rejects any NEW heading not matching it, and shrink the release_triad parser toward one branch as plugins migrate. The best release-heading parser is a single regex because there is only one legal heading shape.
basis: test_release_triad.py docstring enumerates four supported formats: '## [1.2.0] - 2026-06-21', em-dash variant, '## 0.1.2 - 2026-06-21' (deploy, saga bare version), and bare em-dash — 'first match wins'. Four accepted grammars for one concept is vocabulary drift the guard tolerates rather than prevents.
outcome_shape: PR adding a CHANGELOG-heading lint (pre-commit hook + tests/test_changelog_heading_format.py) rejecting non-canonical new headings, plus a DECISIONS.md entry fixing the canonical grammar; verified by a test that feeds a non-canonical heading and asserts rejection.

title: Rename-campaign engine: replace hand-grep lockstep landings with a token-pair driver
idea: The Olympus→CAMPPS retirement and the saga rename were executed as hand-copied lockstep landings — manual grep, manual replace, manual verification that nothing was missed. Automate the campaign: a saga-hosted `rename-campaign` skill that takes old→new token pairs, walks the vendored-consumer blast radius across workspace repos, emits a lockstep PR set, and installs a reappearance guard that fails CI if the retired token resurfaces in live (non-historical) surfaces. The best rename step is no manual sweep — the operator declares the pair and the tooling proves completeness. To respect the portfolio-groom decision this lands as a skill inside the existing saga plugin, not a new plugin.
basis: Grounding brief §3: 'Rename/vocabulary contract-mirror ... Olympus→CAMPPS, hand-copy' and 'saga rename ... lockstep landings'; sdlc-schema.json migration_notes shows the Olympus retirement landed as a hand-edited note ('2026-06-17: Retired Mount Olympus as an active board projection'). Engages binding {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} revisit-when by shipping as a saga skill (no new plugin, carries no consolidation burden).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/rename-campaign/SKILL.md + a scripts/rename_sweep.py driver and a reappearance-guard test template; verified by a fixture repo where an injected stray old-token occurrence fails the guard.

title: Vocabulary-sunset guard: retired tokens live only in history blocks, never in live keys
idea: After a rename, retired vocabulary lingers — 'Mount Olympus' survives in sdlc-schema.json as historical context inside migration_notes, which is correct, but nothing enforces that it stays confined there. Remove the manual 'did any live routing key still reference the retired token?' review by asserting, in a guard, that each sunset token appears ONLY inside designated historical/migration blocks and never in live routing keys (phase_board_map, wip_limits, project mappings). A sunset registry lists retired tokens and their permitted historical homes; the guard fails if one leaks into a live surface. The best 'did we miss a reference?' review is the one a test performs for you.
basis: sdlc-schema.json migration_notes: '2026-06-17: Retired Mount Olympus as an active board projection. phase_board_map now projects only Jeff Intent, Asgard, and CAMPPS' — the retired token is deliberately retained as history, but no guard confines it; a future live reference would be silent drift.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/sunset_vocabulary.json + tests/test_vocabulary_sunset.py asserting each retired token occurs only within whitelisted historical JSON paths; verified by a case that plants the token in a live key and asserts failure.

title: Machine-checkable contract-coupling policy: what pins, what floats, stated once
idea: The fleet silently mixes three pinning strategies with no stated coupling policy: semver in plugin.json, a date-string schema_version ('2026-06-17') in sdlc-schema.json, and SHA256 manifests on vendored modules. Which contracts must pin, which may float, and how a bump in one couples to another is re-decided ad hoc every time — the operator carries the rules in their head. Remove the recurring judgment call: write the coupling policy as a DECISIONS.md entry and encode it as a contract_coupling.json manifest (each contract → pin-kind + coupling rule + revisit condition), then validate on-disk reality against it. The best per-bump coupling decision is one already written down and enforced.
basis: Three distinct pin kinds observed: marketplace.json/plugin.json semver (verified via jq: saga 0.51.0 etc.), sdlc-schema.json 'schema_version': '2026-06-17' date string, and issue_contract_*.py.sha256 byte manifests. No document states which is authoritative or how they couple.
outcome_shape: PR adding a DECISIONS.md coupling entry + config/contract_coupling.json + tests/test_contract_coupling.py that asserts each declared contract's on-disk pin matches its declared pin-kind; verified by a case that swaps a pin-kind and asserts failure.

title: Auto-generated reverse-dependency map: which repos consume which contracts
idea: When a contract changes, the operator hand-reasons the blast radius — the consumer side is per-repo ad hoc across ~19 consumer repos, so 'who breaks if I change this?' is answered by memory and grep. Invert the investigation into a generated artifact: a blast_radius.py that scans every workspace repo for vendored .sha256 manifests and upstream declarations, builds the reverse-dependency graph (contract → consuming repos), and emits a committed CONSUMERS.md plus a PR comment listing affected repos whenever a source contract's fingerprint moves. This is the reverse-dependents view that `cargo tree -i` / npm dependents give for packages, applied to hand-vendored contracts. The best 'who consumes this?' step is a map that is always current because a job regenerates it.
basis: Prior art: Cargo's reverse-dependency resolution (`cargo tree --invert`) and npm's dependents graph both make impacted-consumer discovery a query, not a manual audit; they live in those package managers' resolver cores. Applied here to the vendored-contract seam the parity gate already treats as a producer/consumer pipeline (check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring frames mission-control as 'a CONSUMER of the issue-contract pipeline whose source of truth is infiquetra-sdlc').
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/blast_radius.py + a generated CONSUMERS.md and a CI step that regenerates and diff-checks it; verified by running the scanner over the workspace and asserting the mission-control issue-contract consumer edge appears in the generated map.

title: Upstream-currency job: the parity gate proves frozen-copy stasis, not upstream truth
idea: check_issue_contract_parity.py deliberately never contacts infiquetra-sdlc; it recomputes each vendored artifact's SHA256 and compares to a .sha256 sidecar that is ITSELF vendored. So the gate is green whenever the copy matches its own frozen pin — even after upstream has advanced. This is the validate_card_body disease one level up: the pin is a hand-mirror of a moment in time. The fix is not to weaken the hermetic blocking gate but to add a SEPARATE scheduled, non-blocking CI job that fetches infiquetra-sdlc HEAD's generated artifact, recomputes its SHA, and opens or updates a tracking issue when the live upstream hash differs from the vendored pin. Blocking parity stays hermetic; currency becomes observable instead of silently stale.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:15-21 'Design (deliberately does NOT run the sdlc generator)... recomputes the SHA256 of each vendored module and compares it to its vendored .sha256 manifest.' Nothing in the gate detects upstream advancing past the pinned hash — a stale-but-green window is structurally invisible.
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-currency.yml (scheduled) + plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_upstream_currency.py that fetches the sdlc-published artifact hash and diffs against the vendored .sha256, emitting a gh issue payload on mismatch. Verified by a fixture test that feeds a divergent upstream hash and asserts a drift-issue body is produced (and a matching hash produces none).

title: Collapse the deliberate parallel houses: one ordered vocabulary source, not N mirrored tuples
idea: MODELS, EFFORTS, PASS_RULES, ENGINE_INTENTS, MUTATION_POLICIES, WORKSPACE_ISOLATIONS and SANDBOX_PROFILES are hand-typed Python tuples in execution_spec.py, and the module's own comment admits outcome_spec.py 'mirrors these three names verbatim (deliberate parallel house)' guarded by a cross-module drift test. F3 attacks the word 'deliberate': a drift TEST is a confession that two sources exist where one should. Reframe to a single ordered vocabulary module (tier_vocab.py) that both execution_spec.py and outcome_spec.py import, deleting the verbatim copies. The drift test degenerates into a one-line 'both import the same symbol' assertion. Crucially this must preserve {#tier-vocab-ordering}: the source stays ORDERED arrays (strongest-first MODELS, weakest-first EFFORTS) so index-based upgrade-only merges keep working — the manifest declares ladders, not sets.
basis: execution_spec.py inline comment on SANDBOX_PROFILES: 'outcome_spec.py mirrors these three names verbatim (deliberate parallel house, different error type) -- a cross-module drift-guard test asserts the two copies stay identical.' Engages binding {#tier-vocab-ordering} by keeping ordered arrays and index-merge semantics intact.
