outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocab.py as the single ordered source; execution_spec.py and outcome_spec.py import from it; the verbatim literals deleted. Verified: existing tests/test_saga_execution_spec.py passes, the cross-module drift test collapses to an identity-of-import assertion, and grep confirms no second literal copy of the enums remains.

title: Guard the guard: auto-discover every vendored artifact instead of trusting humans to register it
idea: The parity gate's coverage is a hand-maintained tuple — its own docstring says 'Adding a future vendored artifact here extends the gate with no other change,' i.e. it relies on a human remembering to append. So a newly vendored copy with no .sha256 sidecar is invisible to the drift guard: the drift-guard itself can drift. F3 reframes one level up — coverage should be discovered by convention, not enumerated by hand. Add a meta-guard that scans every plugins/*/config/generated/** file and every file bearing a SOURCE-OF-TRUTH provenance header, and asserts each has both a pinned sidecar and membership in the parity manifest. A vendored contract added without a pin fails CI immediately rather than riding along unguarded.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:38-39 'Adding a future vendored artifact here extends the gate with no other change' — coverage is enumerated in VENDORED_ARTIFACTS by hand; nothing forces a new vendored file to be registered, so the guard's completeness is unverified.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_vendored_artifact_coverage.py that walks config/generated/** plus provenance-header-tagged files and asserts each has a .sha256 sidecar and appears in a parity manifest. Verified: a fixture generated file dropped in without a sidecar makes the test fail with the offending path named.

title: Renames as an aliasable deprecation window, not a big-bang lockstep landing
idea: Cross-repo evidence shows renames executed as simultaneous lockstep landings (saga rename, Olympus->CAMPPS across 4 repos). F3 attacks the fixed assumption 'a rename is one synchronized edit event.' Reframe: a rename is a declarative ledger entry (old term, new term, alias-until date, forbid-after date). During the window both terms are accepted; a CI vocabulary lint only FAILS when a retired term reappears past its forbid-after date, and warns during the grace window. This converts a fragile all-repos-at-once landing into add-alias -> deprecate -> forbid, so no single PR must touch every consumer atomically and stragglers are surfaced by date-aware lint rather than by a production surprise.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 finding 1: 'Rename/vocabulary churn... saga rename lockstep landings, Olympus->CAMPPS' recurring across 4 independent repos — the lockstep posture is the documented pain. Distinct from {#marketplace-ci-guard} (that seed guards dir-vs-marketplace, not vocabulary terms).
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/vocabulary-ledger/renames.jsonl + check_forbidden_vocabulary.py wired into CI, scanning plugins/ for retired terms with grace-date awareness. Verified: a fixture ledger entry whose forbid-after date has passed plus a lingering old-term occurrence makes CI fail citing the ledger line; the same term inside its grace window only warns.

title: Make contract consumption a declared edge, and generate the blast-radius graph from it
idea: Today 'which repos consume which contract' is tribal knowledge rediscovered by hand-grepping at rename time, even though vendored artifacts already carry a prose source comment (issue_contract_shim.py names infiquetra-sdlc as its origin) and tests/test_provenance_manifest.py already exists. F3 reframes: consumption is invisible because it is written as an unstructured comment, not a machine-readable edge. Promote every vendored artifact's provenance to a structured record (source repo, source path, generator, pinned SHA, declared consumers) and generate a fleet-level contract-graph.json answering 'if sdlc card_validator changes, who breaks?' Blast radius stops being rediscovered and becomes a queryable artifact regenerated in CI.
basis: tests/test_provenance_manifest.py already exists and issue_contract_shim.py:6 carries a prose 'source of truth is infiquetra-sdlc' header — the provenance data exists but is unstructured and ungraphed, so blast radius cannot be computed.
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/contract-graph/build_graph.py that reads structured provenance headers and emits contract-graph.json (source->consumer edges) + a short docs/ query note. Verified by a test asserting the sdlc card-validator node lists mission-control as a consumer and the graph regenerates deterministically.

title: SHA pins conflate byte-identity with compatibility; separate them with explicit version bands
idea: The drift gate keys entirely on SHA256 byte-equality. F3 exposes the buried assumption: byte-identity is being used as the coupling primitive, but compatibility is a different relation. Byte-equality is a total order on bytes; compatibility is a partial order on semantics. So the gate cannot tell a whitespace/cosmetic upstream change from a required-field addition — it either cries wolf (blocks and forces a re-vendor on harmless drift) or, if relaxed, misses a breaking change that happens to look small. Reframe: each contract carries a declared semver + compatibility band, and the consumer declares 'I require issue-contract >= 2.1, < 3.' The currency check then classifies upstream movement as compatible-advance (auto-ok, informational) versus band-breaking (must act), instead of treating every byte as equally alarming.
basis: First principles: the parity gate compares hashlib.sha256 digests, a total order on bytes. Semantic compatibility is a partial order on meaning. A single-primitive gate keyed on bytes therefore cannot separate cosmetic drift from a required-field addition — the two produce indistinguishable hash flips — so it is forced to be either over-strict or unsafe. An explicit version band restores the missing semantic axis the hash cannot carry.
outcome_shape: PR replacing each .sha256 sidecar with a .contract.json (contract-version, compat-band, pinned SHA) and upgrading check_issue_contract_parity.py to enforce band membership alongside byte pinning. Verified by tests where an additive upstream minor bump passes the band check while a major bump fails it, with the SHA still pinned for exact-copy integrity.

title: Byte-parity is not behavioral-parity: lock the validator against a real-card verdict corpus
idea: The 343-card disaster was not a byte problem — the mirror parsed fine and passed its own tests; it simply DISAGREED with the live contract on real inputs, surfacing only when real cards hit production. Byte/SHA parity guards the copy's identity but says nothing about the copy's BEHAVIOR, and today's test_card_validator.py exercises only a handful of hand-written bodies (VALID_BODY, OLYMPUS_BODY) — not the real-card distribution that actually broke. F3 reframes drift as a behavioral question: freeze a golden corpus of real (anonymized) card bodies paired with their captured live-contract verdicts, and assert the vendored validator reproduces every verdict. This catches the exact 343-card class of semantic drift that byte-identity and synthetic samples both miss.
basis: Grounding brief section 3: 'validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract, -> #222)'; and tests/test_card_validator.py:63 asserts on a hand-authored VALID_BODY sample rather than a real-card corpus — the existing tests cannot reproduce the failure that shipped.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/fixtures/card_corpus/ (real anonymized card bodies + captured expected verdicts) and a differential test asserting sdlc_manager.validate_card_body matches every captured verdict. Verified: mutating one regex in the shim makes the corpus test fail on the specific cards that regex governs, not just a synthetic sample.

title: Generic vendored-contract parity primitive + registry (one gate, N contracts)
idea: Today the SHA256-pinned parity guarantee is a bespoke module: check_issue_contract_parity.py hardcodes VENDORED_ARTIFACTS = the two generated issue-contract modules, and the sibling vendored artifact config/sdlc-schema.json rides the 'same vendoring pattern' but carries no equivalent SHA-pinned parity gate. Extract the recompute-SHA-vs-pinned-manifest logic into one generic check_vendor_parity.py driven by a vendored-contracts.toml registry where each row is (artifact_path, sha256_manifest_path, source_repo, gen_command, re-vendor_hint). Migrate the issue-contract entries and ADD sdlc-schema.json as the first newly-covered artifact. Second-order: vendoring the next generated contract becomes a one-line registry row that auto-inherits the parity gate, the drift-failure message, and the re-vendor instructions instead of a new hand-written module + test pair.
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:1-27 is a per-contract bespoke gate ('the WHOLE validator data surface (U1)... TWO generated modules are vendored here') covering only issue_contract_data.py + issue_contract_shim.py; its docstring names config/sdlc-schema.json as vendored under 'the same vendoring pattern' yet sdlc-schema.json has no .sha256 manifest or parity assertion (test_issue_contract_parity.py pins only EXPECTED_DATA_SHA256 / EXPECTED_SHIM_SHA256).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/vendored-contracts.toml + scripts/check_vendor_parity.py, deleting the bespoke check_issue_contract_parity.py, adding a config/sdlc-schema.json.sha256 manifest, and a parametrized test_vendor_parity.py. Verified: test iterates every registry row, hand-editing any vendored byte flips its hash and fails the gate; sdlc-schema.json now fails on silent edit where it previously passed.

title: Declarative intra-fleet mirror-drift registry (kills the ad-hoc guard-per-pair habit)
idea: The fleet already relies on 'X mirrors Y verbatim' invariants but each is a separately-remembered hand-test: execution_spec.py's SANDBOX_PROFILES/axis names are asserted identical to outcome_spec.py's copy, the readonly-verifier agentType has a literal-consistency guard, and test_template_sync.py guards templates — yet execution-spec.md:138 re-types the tier vocabulary `fable|opus|sonnet|haiku` with NO guard, exactly the class of stale hand-mirror that let 343 cards pass a dead validator. Build a drift_pairs registry (source locator, mirror locator, extractor fn) + one parametrized test_fleet_mirror_drift.py that asserts every registered pair stays byte-equal on the extracted slice. Second-order: every future 'mirrors verbatim (deliberate parallel house)' comment becomes a registry row nobody can forget, and the currently-unguarded code→prose vocab pairs get covered on day one.
basis: execution_spec.py comment 'outcome_spec.py mirrors these three names verbatim (deliberate parallel house)... a cross-module drift-guard test asserts the two copies stay identical' (GUARDED) contrasted with execution-spec.md:138 re-listing `fable|opus|sonnet|haiku ×` (UNGUARDED); grounding brief §3 finding 1 (validate_card_body stale hand-mirror → 343 cards → #222).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/drift_pairs.py (or tests/drift_pairs registry) + tests/test_fleet_mirror_drift.py, registering the execution_spec↔outcome_spec pair, the readonly-verifier agentType pair, and the NEW execution_spec.py↔execution-spec.md tier-vocab pair. Verified: editing the tier tuple in code without updating the doc fails the new parametrized test (currently green).

title: Release-surface version tri-lock: plugin.json == marketplace.json == CHANGELOG head
idea: CLAUDE.md step 6 demands plugin.json + marketplace.json + CHANGELOG.md move in lockstep on any behavior/schema change, but it is prose-only and the journal records that release-surface drift persists despite it. The QUEUED marketplace-ci-guard seed only asserts directory↔entry membership, not version agreement. Add a CI gate that, for every plugin, asserts the three version tokens are byte-identical (plugin's .claude-plugin/plugin.json version, its marketplace.json entry version, and the top-most CHANGELOG.md heading version) and emits a release-surfaces.lock snapshot. Second-order: the recurring 'code says the same story as installed metadata' review burden becomes machine-checked, so the version lever becomes trustworthy enough to build later automation (auto-bump, changelog gen) on top of.
basis: Grounding brief §6 item 3 'Release-surface drift persists despite CLAUDE.md step 6 — room for automation'; QUEUED.md:176 marketplace-ci-guard covers only 'plugin directories match marketplace.json entries' (membership), NOT the version tri-match this adds. CLAUDE.md dev-workflow step 6 lists all three surfaces as required-in-same-PR but is unenforced.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_release_surface_versions.py (or a scripts/check_release_surfaces.py wired into CI) + a generated release-surfaces.lock. Verified: bumping plugin.json version without touching marketplace.json or CHANGELOG head fails the gate; the current fleet (8 plugins) passes as the baseline snapshot.

title: Contract-consumer manifest + change-time re-vendor checklist generator
idea: When validate_card_body drifted, the failure was invisible because nobody could enumerate who consumed the live contract — 343 cards passed a mirror while failing source. Author a machine-readable contract-consumers manifest mapping each fleet contract (issue-contract, sdlc-schema, tier-vocab, sandbox-profiles/axes, readonly-verifier agentType, project-mappings) to its source-of-truth locator AND every file/plugin that consumes it. A scripts/contract_impact.py <contract> prints the exact ordered re-vendor/update checklist for a change to that source. Second-order: every contract change now emits its own blast-radius checklist, converting the 'I didn't know that copy existed' failure mode into a generated to-do, and the manifest becomes the substrate idea T14-F4-7's coverage gate reads.
basis: Grounding brief §3 finding 1 (validate_card_body stale hand-copy, 343 'clean' cards failed the live contract → #222, re-vendored sdlc-schema.json) and finding 3 ('mission-control/saga contract copies drifting from source of truth', 2 repos); check_issue_contract_parity.py:72 already hand-writes a single re-vendor hint proving the checklist need is real but per-contract today.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/contract-consumers.toml (source + consumers per contract) and scripts/contract_impact.py. Verified: contract_impact.py issue-contract lists the two vendored modules + shim consumer sdlc_manager.validate_card_body + parity test; a test asserts every locator path in the manifest actually exists (no dead entries).

title: Guarded rename-campaign executor with historical-journal allowlist + atomic PR
idea: The plugin family has already absorbed four hand-done token renames (infiquetra-lifecycle→saga, sdlc-manager→mission-control, infiquetra-deploy→deploy, blueprint-reviewer folded into saga) plus the Olympus→CAMPPS lockstep landings recurring across repos, each a manual multi-file sweep. Build a tools/rename_campaign.py that takes an old→new token map + an allowlist of paths where the OLD token must survive verbatim (ARCHIVE.md historical entries, CHANGELOG history), performs the repo-wide guarded replace, and emits a single atomic PR plus a post-rename assertion that no stray old token leaked outside the allowlist. Second-order: renames stop being a bespoke error-prone ceremony and become a declarative map + review, making the fleet cheap to re-brand and lowering the cost of every future vocabulary migration.
basis: ARCHIVE.md:9 naming note enumerates the four hand-done family renames ('infiquetra-lifecycle->saga, sdlc-manager->mission-control, infiquetra-deploy->deploy, and blueprint-reviewer was folded into saga'); grounding brief §3 finding 1 names 'saga rename lockstep landings, Olympus→CAMPPS' as the top 4-repo recurring churn.
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/rename_campaign.py + a rename-allowlist.txt + a dry-run test fixture. Verified: running it on a synthetic old→new map in a test dir rewrites consumers, leaves allowlisted historical strings intact, and the leak-assertion fails if a non-allowlisted old token remains.

title: Generate the tier-vocabulary prose tables from execution_spec.py (docs-follow-code)
idea: The fleet's one operator-facing lever — the model/effort tier vocabulary — is authored in execution_spec.py (MODELS/EFFORTS/ENGINE_INTENTS/PASS_RULES/sandbox axes) and then re-typed by hand in execution-spec.md:138 and in the /plan unit tier table, a classic fetch-don't-copy hazard. Instead of only DETECTING that drift (T14-F4-2), eliminate the second source: a scripts/gen_tier_docs.py reads execution_spec.py's tuples/dicts and regenerates the vocabulary table blocks inside execution-spec.md between GENERATED markers, with a CI check that the committed doc equals the freshly generated one. Second-order: prose can never again outlive the code it documents for the fleet's most-touched contract, and the same generate-between-markers primitive is reusable for the sandbox-profile and engine-intent tables.
basis: execution_spec.py:52-53 defines MODELS/EFFORTS as the authority ('ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING'); execution-spec.md:138 re-types `fable|opus|sonnet|haiku ×` by hand; grounding brief §1 confirms /plan's unit tier table (plan/SKILL.md:296-352) is a third hand-copy of the same vocabulary.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/gen_tier_docs.py + GENERATED markers in plugins/saga/references/execution-spec.md + a CI test asserting generated==committed. Verified: adding a hypothetical fifth model to MODELS and regenerating updates the doc table; skipping regeneration fails CI.

title: Contract census + guard-coverage gate (every contract must declare a guard)
idea: infiquetra-context-library already runs the org's canonical meta-pattern: context_census.py --check keeps llms.txt honest and CI-fails on an undescribed doc. Port that discipline to contracts: a scripts/contract_census.py --check reads the contract-consumers manifest (T14-F4-4) and the vendored-contracts registry (T14-F4-1), then asserts every enumerated contract maps to at least one registered guard (parity gate, mirror-drift pair, or generator) — and CI FAILS if a contract exists with guard status UNGUARDED. It also emits a CONTRACTS.md self-describing index. Second-order and the deepest compounding lever of the theme: introducing an unguarded contract becomes structurally impossible, so drift-prevention scales automatically with the number of contracts instead of depending on whoever remembers to write a guard.
basis: infiquetra-context-library's validate.yml CI runs context_census.py --check to 'keep llms.txt honest' (grounding brief §4) — the exact self-describing-index + census-gate pattern this ports to the contract surface; prior art lives in that repo's CI + check_docs.py/context_census.py.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/contract_census.py (--check mode) + a generated CONTRACTS.md + a CI job. Verified: adding a contract row with no guard reference to the manifest makes --check exit 1; the current fleet passes once every existing guard is registered.

title: Retired-vocabulary reverse guard (cheap durable residue of every rename)
idea: A rename campaign's real failure mode is silent regression — an old token creeping back months later in a new file. Ship the cheap durable complement to the executor (T14-F4-5): a retired-vocabulary.txt listing dead tokens (infiquetra-lifecycle, sdlc-manager, infiquetra-deploy, blueprint-reviewer, Olympus) + a CI check that fails any PR reintroducing a retired token outside a historical-journal allowlist (ARCHIVE.md, CHANGELOG history). Second-order: each completed rename leaves behind a one-line registry entry that permanently defends the new vocabulary at near-zero cost, so the fleet's naming stays coherent without vigilance — compounding cleanliness from a trivial gate.
basis: ARCHIVE.md:9 names the retired tokens explicitly ('infiquetra-lifecycle->saga, sdlc-manager->mission-control, infiquetra-deploy->deploy, and blueprint-reviewer was folded into saga') and already carves out a historical-naming exception, evidencing both the retired set and the allowlist need.
outcome_shape: PR adding tools/retired-vocabulary.txt + scripts/check_retired_vocab.py wired into CI + an allowlist for historical journal files. Verified: a test that adds `sdlc-manager` to a non-allowlisted file trips the gate; the current tree (old tokens only in ARCHIVE/CHANGELOG) passes.

title: mRNA half-life: give every vendored contract mirror a self-expiring transcript
idea: In molecular biology's central dogma the genome (DNA) is never edited by the ribosome; the cell transcribes short-lived mRNA copies on demand, and each transcript carries a half-life so stale copies self-degrade rather than accumulate. Apply this to the fleet's hand-vendored contract mirrors (the class of failure behind `validate_card_body`, where 343 cards passed a stale hand-mirror while failing the live contract): every derived artifact under `plugins/mission-control/config/generated/` gets a header stamping (source-hash, derived-at, half-life-days) at generation time. A CI guard fails when any mirror outlives its half-life without a fresh re-derivation from `sdlc-schema.json`, forcing transcription rather than letting a copy silently ossify. This turns 'someone forgot to re-vendor' from an invisible latent bug into a scheduled, loud expiry.
basis: Molecular biology, central dogma: transcription produces short-lived mRNA with a defined half-life (see any cell-biology text, e.g. Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell, ch. on RNA and protein synthesis). The genome is the single source; transcripts are disposable and time-bounded. Directly analogous to fetch-don't-copy with enforced expiry on `config/generated/*.py`.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `--stamp` half-life header emitter to the generation step and a `test_contract_mirror_freshness.py` (beside `test_issue_contract_parity.py`) that fails when a stamped mirror's derived-at + half-life is exceeded; verified by deliberately back-dating a stamp in the test and observing CI red, then a re-derivation turning it green.

title: ATC positive handoff: no vocabulary term is retired until every consumer sector acknowledges
idea: Air-traffic control never assumes a flight left its sector; a controller retains responsibility until the next sector gives a positive two-way 'radar contact' acknowledgment, and only then is the aircraft dropped. The Olympus->CAMPPS rename was a hand-copy lockstep landing across ~4 repos with no positive-ack protocol, so a term could be assumed retired while a consumer still spoke the old vocabulary. Build a `rename_campaign.py` orchestrator backed by a `rename-manifest.json` that tracks, per consumer repo, an explicit adoption ack (new term present + old term absent, machine-verified via `gh` grep). The old vocabulary stays live and dual-accepted until the manifest shows every sector has acked; only then does the campaign tool authorize decommissioning the old term. Retirement on silent assumption becomes structurally impossible.
basis: Air-traffic control positive handoff / positive two-way communication transfer (FAA JO 7110.65, controller handoff procedures; 'radar contact' acknowledgment). Responsibility is never released without positive acknowledgment from the receiving sector. Maps to per-consumer-repo ack gating before old-vocabulary decommission.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/scripts/rename_campaign.py` + `rename-manifest.json` schema + a `--status` dry-run that lists unacked repos; verified by running against a synthetic two-repo fixture where one repo still contains the old term and confirming the tool refuses the decommission step and names the laggard.

title: Procurement three-way match: reconcile schema, generated shim, and live GitHub before trusting a field
idea: Accounts-payable controls fraud and error with a three-way match: a payment clears only when the purchase order, the goods receipt, and the invoice all reconcile; any two agreeing is not enough. The current `check_issue_contract_parity.py` is a two-way match (source schema vs generated shim), but the schema itself declares that live GitHub Projects field option IDs must be resolved at runtime and are deliberately absent from the file, so the actual failure surface is a third leg nobody reconciles. Extend the parity check into a three-way match: (1) `sdlc-schema.json`, (2) the generated shim, (3) a live `gh` resolution of the project's field options. CI passes only when all three agree, catching the board/field drift pattern (hardcoded aliases, nonexistent fields assumed) at its true source.
basis: Procurement/finance internal control: the three-way match (PO + receipt + invoice) in accounts payable (standard AP control, e.g. GAAP internal-control practice). Two-way reconciliation misses the third document; analogously the current two-way parity check misses the live-GitHub leg that `sdlc-schema.json`'s own description says tooling must resolve at runtime.
outcome_shape: PR extending `plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py` with a third live-resolution leg (guarded behind a `--live` flag for offline CI) and a `test_issue_contract_parity.py` case asserting a divergence in any single leg fails the match; verified by mocking a live field-option rename and observing the three-way check flag it.

title: Structural expansion joints: declare which contract edges are welded and which are designed to move
idea: Civil engineers do not rigidly weld every joint in a bridge or rail line; uniform rigidity buckles under thermal expansion. They deliberately place expansion joints where movement is expected and rigid connections where load must not shift, and the drawings say which is which. The fleet has no declared coupling semantics: it is implicit and per-consumer whether a repo pins an exact contract version or floats on a compatible range, so CI cannot tell designed movement from dangerous drift. Introduce a `coupling-policy.yaml` at the contract-owner (mission-control) that declares, per consumer-contract edge, welded (exact pin, drift is a hard failure) vs expansion-joint (compatible-range, drift within range is expected and allowed). Drift guards then read the policy: buckling fails the build, designed movement passes quietly.
basis: Structural / civil engineering: expansion joints in bridges and continuous-welded rail deliberately allocate movement vs fixity (AASHTO bridge design practice; rail thermal-expansion joint design). The engineering insight is that uniform rigid coupling is a failure mode, not a virtue. Directly reframes version-coupling from 'pin everything' to a declared welded-vs-joint policy per edge.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/config/coupling-policy.yaml` (schema + per-edge welded|expansion-joint declarations) and teaching the drift guard to consult it; verified by a test with one welded and one expansion-joint edge, asserting an in-range float on the joint passes while the same float on the welded edge fails.

title: Epidemiological contact tracing: rank exposed consumers by which fields they actually touch
idea: Public-health contact tracing does not treat all contacts equally; it computes an exposure graph and ranks contacts by proximity and duration so scarce attention goes to close contacts first, not everyone in the city. A contract change today has no blast-radius map across the ~19 independent consumer repos, so a schema diff is merged blind to who it exposes. Build a `blast_radius.py --diff <schema-change>` that treats the change as an infection origin, walks the consumer graph (repos + the specific fields each repo references, discovered by grep over consumer usage), and emits an exposure-ranked report: repos touching a changed field are close contacts, repos importing the schema but not the field are distant. The report attaches to the contract-change PR so reviewers see the true reach before merge, not after breakage.
basis: Epidemiology: contact tracing and exposure-risk stratification (WHO/CDC contact-tracing methodology ranks contacts by proximity/duration, not flat enumeration). The non-obvious import is exposure-weighting by which specific field a consumer touches, mirroring proximity-weighting of contacts, rather than a flat dependency list.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/scripts/blast_radius.py` producing a field-level exposure-ranked markdown report from a schema diff plus a consumer-usage index; verified against a fixture of three mock consumer repos (one touching the changed field, one touching an unchanged field, one not importing) confirming the ranking order.

title: Aviation NOTAM broadcast: consumers subscribe to a contract, the owner broadcasts changes to them
idea: Aviation inverts the burden of staying current: pilots do not poll every airport for changes; the system maintains a subscription of relevant airspace and broadcasts a NOTAM (Notice to Airmen) to exactly the affected operators when something changes. The fleet's propagation is the opposite and broken: consumers hand-copy contracts and have no way to learn a source changed, so drift is discovered by accident (the `validate_card_body` class of latent staleness). Invert it: each consumer repo declares a `contracts.lock` manifest naming the contracts and versions it consumes; a fleet-level GitHub Action, triggered when a contract in mission-control changes, reads all registered `contracts.lock` files and opens a targeted NOTAM issue in each affected repo describing the change and the fields impacted. Propagation becomes push-based and addressed, not pull-based and forgotten.
basis: Aviation NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system (FAA/ICAO Annex 15): a push-based, subscription-scoped broadcast of changes to exactly the affected operators, replacing per-operator polling. The non-obvious move is inverting propagation direction (owner-broadcasts vs consumer-polls) via a `contracts.lock` subscription registry.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `contracts.lock` manifest schema, a repo-scanning registry builder, and a `.github/workflows/contract-notam.yml` that fans out targeted issues on contract change; verified end-to-end by editing a contract in a fixture and confirming a NOTAM issue is opened only in the repo whose `contracts.lock` names it.

title: RTS lockstep desync checksum: halt the fleet on first contract divergence, do not degrade
idea: Real-time-strategy multiplayer engines run lockstep simulations and exchange a per-frame checksum of world state; the instant any client's checksum diverges the session halts with a desync error rather than letting clients drift into silently different worlds, because a degraded shared reality is worse than a stop. Contract mirrors across the fleet have no such tripwire, so divergence (a re-vendored `sdlc-schema.json` in one place, a stale copy in another) accumulates unseen. Add a `contract_checksum_lockstep.py` fleet job that computes a normalized checksum of each consumer's effective contract and compares against the canonical source; on the first mismatch it HALTS by opening a single blocking issue naming the diverged repo, rather than auto-reconciling or warning-and-continuing. This deliberately mirrors the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade decision, extending that same posture from run status to contract integrity.
basis: RTS lockstep networking desync detection: per-frame world-state checksums that halt on first divergence (well-documented in Age of Empires / StarCraft lockstep engineering writeups, e.g. Bettner & Terrano, 'GDC 2001: 1500 Archers on a 28.8'). The engineering principle is halt-on-desync over silent drift, which aligns with the fleet's binding {#outcome HALT-not-degrade} decision rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/mission-control/scripts/contract_checksum_lockstep.py` + a scheduled workflow that opens one blocking issue on first checksum mismatch; verified by injecting a one-field divergence into a fixture consumer and confirming the job halts and files exactly one issue naming that repo, and stays green when all checksums match.

title: Live-source liveness gate: fetch-don't-pin contract verification
idea: Flip the cache constraint to zero: instead of trusting the vendored SHA pin, fetch the CURRENT source contract at check time and diff against it. The existing parity gate only recomputes the SHA256 of vendored modules and compares to their pinned .sha256 sidecars — it proves the vendored bytes equal what was LAST pinned, never that they equal live source. A source that advanced without re-vendoring stays green, which is exactly the #222 failure mode (343 cards clean locally, failing the live contract). Add a scheduled workflow that git-fetches infiquetra-sdlc HEAD, re-runs gen_issue_contract.py, and diffs against the vendored artifacts, decoupled from the fast per-PR byte gate so the expensive checkout only runs nightly. The practical kernel even without full liveness is the diff-against-live signal that the pure byte gate structurally cannot produce.
basis: plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py docstring: 'recomputes the SHA256 of each vendored module and compares it to its vendored .sha256 manifest. A match means the vendored bytes equal what the source generator last produced and pinned' — explicitly last-pinned, not live. Wired at .github/workflows/ci.yml:33-40. Grounding §3.1: re-vendored sdlc-schema.json after 343 cards failed live contract (#222).
outcome_shape: PR adding .github/workflows/contract-liveness.yml plus a fetch-and-diff script beside check_issue_contract_parity.py; verified by advancing the source generator without re-vendoring and observing the nightly job report drift that the existing SHA gate misses (green byte-gate + red liveness-gate on the same commit).

title: One canonical ref, N zero hand-mirrors: contract resolved from a single pinned subtree
idea: Flip 'every consumer keeps its own copy' to 'nobody keeps a copy — all resolve one canonical artifact.' Today each repo hand-vendors sdlc-schema.json and the issue-contract modules, and each copy is an independent drift surface. Replace the N hand-mirrors with a single source ref (git subtree / submodule pin, or a single fetched URL resolved at CI time) that the parity gate dereferences, so there is exactly one place a version can be wrong. This respects the org's binding convention that contracts are schema-validated-in-CI with a self-describing index, NOT runtime-injected blobs (grounding §4) — the resolution happens at CI time against a pinned ref, never injected into an agent prompt at runtime. The kernel: collapse the drift surface from N copies to one pin, so a re-vendor is a single ref bump instead of a per-repo hand-copy.
basis: Grounding §4: 'org convention is schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index, not runtime-injected blobs' — idea engages this by keeping resolution CI-time, not runtime. §3.3: 'mission-control/saga contract copies drifting from source truth (2 repos)'; §3.1 validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py.
outcome_shape: PR converting plugins/mission-control/config/generated/ vendored copies to a single pinned source ref (subtree or fetched-at-CI artifact) plus the parity gate rewired to dereference it; verified by a single ref bump propagating without any per-file hand-edit, and the parity test passing against the resolved ref.

title: Continuous cross-repo drift sweep: contract drift hunted, not stumbled upon
idea: Flip 'drift caught reactively on someone's PR or by lucky recall' to 'drift continuously hunted across the whole fleet.' A scheduled routine walks all consumer repos, diffs each vendored contract copy against source, and files a mission-control defect issue per drift with the offending file, pinned SHA, and live SHA. Today drift surfaces only when an operator remembers or gets lucky (stale-claim pattern, 2 repos) and contract copies silently diverge from source truth (2 repos). Extreme framing (check every hour, every repo) mines the kernel: a cron-scheduled sweep + a precise per-drift issue emitter so the fleet's contract health is a live dashboard, not tribal memory. Cheap-tier agents author the issues; nothing merges autonomously, only reversible issue creation.
basis: Grounding §7 pattern 7: 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted fact, caught only by operator recall or lucky re-verification (2 repos)'. §3.3: 'mission-control/saga contract copies drifting from source truth (2 repos)'. §3 scanned 19 repos reactively to find this.
outcome_shape: PR adding a scheduled workflow + drift-sweep script that enumerates consumer repos and emits one mission-control defect issue per detected contract drift; verified by seeding a deliberate drift in a test repo and observing a correctly-scoped defect issue filed.

title: Zero hardcoded board vocabulary: every field/option resolved live before any write
idea: Flip 'author-time knowledge of board fields' to zero — assume NOTHING about the Projects schema is known until resolved live. mission-control still assumes nonexistent fields, uses hardcoded field aliases, and truncates item lists at 200/375 via silent pagination stops (4 repos). Recent work already schema-resolved /outcome board status instead of hardcoding 'In Progress' (commit 71faf92); generalize that to a mandatory preflight: every field-set and option write first resolves the live GraphQL field/option ids, fails closed if absent, and every item-list fetch pages to completion. The extreme (trust no cached vocabulary) yields the kernel: a single resolve-then-write guard that structurally cannot set a field that does not exist or act on a truncated page.
basis: Grounding §7.3: 'mission-control board/field drift — nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases, item-list pagination silently truncating at 200/375 items, create/board-add/field-set racing (4 repos)'. Repo commit 71faf92 'schema-resolve /outcome board status instead of hardcoded In Progress' establishes the pattern to generalize.
outcome_shape: PR touching mission-control flow/board scripts to route every field-set through a live schema-resolver + complete-pagination fetch with fail-closed guards; verified by a test that renames a field option upstream and confirms the write resolves the new id (or fails loud) rather than setting a stale alias.

title: Manifest-driven autonomous rename campaign with all-green lockstep landing
idea: Flip 'one rename hand-copied across repos' to '100 renames, zero manual edits, landed atomically.' The saga rename and Olympus→CAMPPS were hand-copy lockstep churn across 4 repos — slow, error-prone, and leaving windows of a half-renamed fleet. Declare {old→new} tuples in one rename-manifest; a codemod engine applies them across every consumer repo, opens lockstep PRs, and a landing-coordinator merges in dependency order ONLY when all are simultaneously green, so the fleet is never partially renamed. Housed inside the existing saga or mission-control plugin (not a new plugin) to avoid consolidation burden. The kernel even if landing stays operator-gated: a dry-run codemod from a single manifest replaces the hand-copy dance and makes the blast radius explicit before a single PR opens.
basis: Grounding §3.1: 'saga rename lockstep landings, Olympus→CAMPPS' listed as top independent-repo recurrence (4 repos) of rename/vocabulary churn. Binding {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} engaged: idea deliberately extends an existing plugin rather than adding one, carrying no new-plugin consolidation burden.
outcome_shape: PR adding a rename-campaign skill+script (rename-manifest.json schema + codemod runner + landing-coordinator) under plugins/saga or plugins/mission-control; verified by dry-running a sample rename across two repos and diffing the generated PRs, then a coordinator test that refuses to merge while any member PR is red.

title: Pin-vs-float compat manifest: auto-adopt additive contract changes, gate only breaking ones
idea: Flip both extremes — 'everything pinned' vs 'everything floats' — to mine the middle kernel. The SHA parity gate is binary: identical or drift. It cannot tell an additive, backward-compatible source change (a new optional field, safe to auto-adopt) from a breaking one (a removed/renamed required field, must gate). Byte-identity conflates 'changed' with 'incompatible,' forcing a manual re-vendor even for harmless additions and equally red-flagging both. Declare per-contract coupling semantics: a semver-style contract version plus a compat-mode (pinned = breaking-change gate; floating = auto-adopt additive) so CI auto-adopts additive diffs and halts only on breaking ones. The #222 incident was a genuine breaking divergence that SHOULD gate; the point is to stop treating every additive change with the same manual ceremony.
basis: First-principles: the parity gate recomputes and compares SHA256 (check_issue_contract_parity.py) — a pure byte comparison has no notion of backward compatibility, so an additive schema change (new optional enum value) and a breaking one (removed required field) both flip the hash identically and both demand a manual re-vendor. A declared contract-version + compat-mode is the minimum structure that lets CI distinguish safe-to-float from must-gate, eliminating manual ceremony for the safe majority while preserving the #222 gate for the breaking minority.
outcome_shape: PR adding a contract-version field + compat-policy manifest to plugins/mission-control/config/sdlc-schema.json and teaching the parity gate to auto-adopt additive diffs vs gate breaking ones; verified by two fixtures — an additive change that passes without re-vendor and a field-removal that fails the gate.

title: Self-registering consumer graph: instant who-consumes-X blast radius
idea: Flip 'zero knowledge of who consumes a contract' to 'every consumer known, 100% mapped.' Today discovering which repos vendor a given contract requires scanning 19 repos by hand (how the grounding pass itself found the drift). Make each vendoring gate self-register its copy — (repo, contract name, path, pinned SHA) — into one central consumers.json in infiquetra-sdlc (or context-library), so a source change instantly enumerates its exact blast radius and the drift sweep (T14-F6-3) fans out to precisely the affected repos instead of scanning the world. The kernel even at partial adoption: a queryable 'who consumes sdlc-schema' answer that replaces a full-fleet grep, turning contract-change planning from archaeology into a lookup.
basis: Grounding §3: 'Consumer-side signal (cross-repo journals, 19 repos scanned)' — the blast radius was established only by an expensive manual 19-repo scan, and §3.3 notes contract copies drift with no consumer inventory to target. No central registry of which repos consume which contract exists today.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consumers.json registry convention + a register-consumer step invoked by each vendoring/parity gate + a blast-radius query script; verified by querying 'which repos consume sdlc-schema' and matching the manually-scanned known set from grounding §3.

title: runner_receipt: hard subprocess proof before RAN_AS_REQUESTED
idea: team-execution's engine dispatch declares a codex run RAN_AS_REQUESTED purely by inspecting evidence.halt, with no proof the codex subprocess ever executed. A chaperone that fabricates evidence.evidence (patch/output) and leaves halt=None is indistinguishable from a real invocation. Add a mandatory runner_receipt on AdvisoryEvidence carrying the subprocess PID, resolved argv, exit code, stdout byte count, and wall-clock start/end, captured by the runner wrapper itself. build_dispatch_manifest must refuse to emit RAN_AS_REQUESTED (downgrade to a halted/unproven attribution) when the receipt is absent or shows zero bytes / nonzero exit. This is proof-of-invocation, not gatekeeping: Claude remains verifier-of-record, we only prove the engine actually ran.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md:158-161 maps `evidence.halt is not None -> HALTED ... -> RAN_AS_REQUESTED; attribution is kind=EXTERNAL_ENGINE, identity=f"{evidence.engine_id}/{evidence.variant}"` — the RAN verdict is derived from halt inspection alone, with no captured invocation receipt. Compatible with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): proving the engine ran does not make it a gatekeeper.
outcome_shape: PR adding a runner_receipt dataclass/field to AdvisoryEvidence in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py, populated by build_codex_invocation's runner path, plus a guard in build_dispatch_manifest that downgrades attribution when the receipt is missing/empty; verified by a new tests/test_engine_dispatch_receipt.py asserting a fabricated-evidence-with-no-receipt case cannot reach RAN_AS_REQUESTED.

title: Wire agy transcript audit into every live delegation, not just the release gate
idea: audit_harness_transcript.py — the independent classifier that proves an agy bridge agent invoked the wrapper and used no direct Claude file tools — only runs as a manual release-gate ceremony (harness-proof.md). Live /agy:delegate runs instead trust the wrapper's own self-reported _real_agy_verdict computed from its own run_result, so the one component that could have silently no-op'd is the one grading itself. Have the /agy:delegate skill run audit_harness_transcript.py against the just-produced turn transcript at delegation exit and fold its independent verdict into projection.md, flagging any divergence between the wrapper's self-verdict and the transcript audit as a loud DELEGATION_INTEGRITY warning.
basis: plugins/agy/docs/harness-proof.md:5-8 frames the transcript audit as a release gate ('gate requires Claude Code transcripts showing packaged agents invoked agy_delegate.py'); plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py:1015 shows the live verdict is self-computed: `"real" if agy_command_seen and not claude_file_tool_seen else "fallback_suspected"` from the wrapper's own run_result, never independently audited on live runs.
outcome_shape: PR extending plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/SKILL.md to invoke audit_harness_transcript.py on the live turn transcript and reconcile its verdict into projection.md; a test in tests/ asserting a transcript with a direct Edit tool call yields fallback_suspected in the live path; CHANGELOG + plugin.json version bump per release-surface rule.

title: Attributed verify-spawn fallback ladder — descent must be visible to the consumer
idea: The readonly-verifier fallback ladder lets a verify-class spawn silently descend to a weaker tier (Explore-first fallback) when saga:readonly-verifier is unavailable, and the consuming gate treats the result as a clean verify with no idea which rung produced it. This is the {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} disease in the verify bridge: a 'verified' verdict can be a degraded chaperone. Require every verify spawn to return a verifier_identity plus fallback_depth marker, and require the consuming gate to render 'verified by fallback tier N' rather than an unqualified pass — a tier>0 verify cannot be laundered into a clean gate signal. Does not weaken the ladder or drop sandbox isolation; it only makes the descent auditable.
basis: CLAUDE.md project instructions: verify-class spawns 'use the fallback ladder documented in that file... never fail the spawn outright or revert to unsandboxed' — the ladder is mandated but its descent carries no attribution to the consumer. Crosses binding decision {#readonly-verifier-fallback-ladder-325}; engaged on its revisit-when by preserving the ladder + worktree isolation intact and only adding attribution, not altering fallback behavior.
outcome_shape: PR adding a verifier_identity/fallback_depth field to the verify-spawn projection in plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md contract + the readonly-verifier agent output shape, and a gate-side render rule; verified by a doc-review checklist item and a fixture test that a tier-2 verify surfaces as 'fallback tier 2' in the gate summary.

title: Propagate resolver Claude-fallback reason to the merged artifact and operator
idea: When engine_resolver returns a Claude-fallback Resolution (engine_id='claude', fallback='<reason>'), the chaperone silently does the unit itself and the operator never learns their 'offloaded' unit was actually Claude — the reason string dies inside the resolver. Thread that fallback reason all the way to the unit's run report and the merged artifact's provenance, and emit a session-end DELEGATION_NOOP summary counting units that requested an engine but ran on Claude fallback. Cheap-tier offload silently becoming premium-tier Claude work is exactly the spend/trust leak the intake brief's fail-loud posture wants eliminated.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md:60-61 — 'the resolver itself returns a Claude-fallback Resolution (engine_id="claude", halt=None, fallback="<reason>") ... The chaperone does the unit itself'; the fallback reason is captured but never surfaced to the operator or artifact. Supports {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} recurring-pain no-op evidence (grounding brief section 5).
outcome_shape: PR that carries resolver `fallback` reason into the unit run-report schema and a session-end DELEGATION_NOOP roll-up in team-execution/SKILL.md's manifest step; verified by a test asserting a forced unavailable-engine offload produces a non-empty fallback reason in both the run report and the roll-up.

title: Provenance trailer on the delivered artifact, not just the sidecar manifest
idea: Engine-vs-chaperone-vs-Claude-fallback attribution today lives only in the provenance manifest sidecar; the actual delivered thing (the run report, the diff, the commit body) carries no visible marker, so a reviewer reading the PR cannot tell which content came from codex under a read-only sandbox versus Claude self-authoring. Attach a compact Provenance block to the delivered artifact itself — engine_id/variant, sandbox, RAN vs fallback — rendered into the unit run report and optionally a commit trailer, sourced verbatim from the manifest's attribution so the two can never drift. Makes provenance survive outside the run directory into the review surface where humans actually look.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md:108-110 — the leaf's declared sandbox 'is recorded on the provenance manifest as pre-hoc attribution ... attribution.sandbox string'; attribution lives in the manifest, never on the delivered artifact/review surface.
outcome_shape: PR adding a Provenance-block renderer that reads the attribution from the provenance manifest and injects it into the unit run report (and an opt-in commit trailer) in team-execution; verified by a test asserting the rendered block's engine identity matches the manifest attribution field byte-for-byte.

title: Write-once evidence artifacts — a later PASS must never overwrite an earlier FAIL
idea: Session mining caught a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS, destroying the audit chain-of-custody: the durable record lied because the failing state was silently replaced. Make delegation/verify evidence artifacts write-once — bundle files land under a content-addressed or run-id-scoped immutable path, a second write to the same logical slot appends a new versioned artifact rather than clobbering, and the audit view shows the full FAIL->PASS sequence. The truth of 'it failed, then a rerun passed' must survive; a bare final PASS with no history is the exact failure mode observed.
basis: Grounding brief section 7: 'probe script overwriting FAIL evidence artifact later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)' — direct mined evidence of a clobbered durable evidence artifact.
outcome_shape: PR adding write-once semantics (refuse-overwrite + versioned suffix) to the evidence-bundle writer shared by agy_delegate.py evidence bundles and engine_dispatch manifests, plus an audit-view rule that renders the full artifact history; verified by a test asserting a second write to an existing evidence slot is rejected/versioned and both FAIL and PASS remain retrievable.

title: Unified cross-bridge delegation receipt ledger + /delegation-audit reconciliation
idea: Three bridges record integrity three incompatible ways — agy writes .claude/agy/runs/<id>/ bundles with real_agy_verdict, team-execution writes provenance manifests with RAN_AS_REQUESTED, and saga verify spawns write essentially nothing — so no single place answers 'did every delegation this session actually invoke its engine?' Define one shared delegation.receipt.v1 schema (bridge, run_id, engine_id, invoked, proof_artifact_path, verdict, fallback_reason) that all three bridges append to a per-session delegation-receipts.jsonl, plus a /delegation-audit reconciliation that lists every delegation and flags any invoked=false or missing-proof entry. This lives in the existing saga scripts lib shared into team-execution — no new plugin — so the {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} consolidation burden is met by folding three ad hoc records into one seam.
basis: Three distinct integrity vocabularies exist with no common reader: agy's real_agy_verdict / fallback_suspected (plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py:1015, evidence under .claude/agy/runs/), team-execution's RAN_AS_REQUESTED attribution (external-engine-workers.md:158-161), and verify spawns with no record at all. First-principles: silent-no-op detection 'across all bridges' is unachievable while each bridge self-reports in a private format and no aggregate audit exists — a shared append-only receipt schema is the minimal structure that makes a single session-wide 'was anything a no-op?' query decidable. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by extending an existing shared lib rather than adding a plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding a delegation.receipt.v1 schema + append helper in the shared saga scripts lib, emit-calls from agy_delegate.py and engine_dispatch.py and the verify-spawn path, and a /delegation-audit skill that reconciles delegation-receipts.jsonl; verified by an integration test that runs one real + one forced-fallback delegation and asserts /delegation-audit flags exactly the fallback as a no-op.

title: Run-lease fencing so a late orphan runner cannot clobber the retry's evidence
idea: When a delegation runner is presumed dead on timeout and re-spawned, the orphaned first runner can still be alive and write its evidence bundle late — landing stale output over the retry's fresh, correct result (the idle-without-delivering / late-writer pattern reproduced live in the ideation session). agy already writes a run-lease.json per bundle; make it a real fencing token: every evidence write validates it holds the current lease epoch, and a write from a superseded lease is rejected and logged as ORPHAN_WRITE_BLOCKED. The retry owns a fresh epoch, so the zombie's late write is fenced out instead of silently winning.
basis: plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/references/delegation-contract.md:103-113 lists run-lease.json in the minimum evidence bundle but it is not used as a fencing token on writes; grounding brief section 5 pattern 9 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications ... also reproduced live in this very session' evidences the orphan/late-writer liveness failure.
outcome_shape: PR that turns run-lease.json into a monotonically-epoched fencing token checked on every evidence write in agy_delegate.py (and the shared bundle writer), rejecting superseded-lease writes as ORPHAN_WRITE_BLOCKED; verified by a test simulating a stale-lease late write and asserting it is rejected while the current-lease write persists.

title: Unified bridge_receipt.v1 invocation-evidence contract across all delegation bridges
idea: Today proof-of-execution is fragmented per bridge: saga/codex emits a saga.manifest.v1 via engine_dispatch.py/provenance_manifest.py, while agy proves itself with a wholly separate post-hoc audit_harness_transcript.py transcript-grep plus run bundle, and a future router provider (ollama/deepseek) would ship with nothing. Invert this from N incompatible proof mechanisms to ONE: define a bridge_receipt.v1 schema (engine_id, argv fingerprint, pid, exit code, wall-time, bytes-written) that every bridge script MUST emit at invocation, stored beside the existing manifest tree. Add a static drift test that enumerates every registered bridge script and fails CI if any lacks a receipt-emit call. This removes the per-bridge bespoke audit step and makes 'did the external process actually run' a single queryable fact rather than a forensic grep. The receipt is evidence only, never a gate input, so Claude stays verifier-of-record.
basis: Two disjoint proof mechanisms exist today: agy `plugins/agy/scripts/audit_harness_transcript.py` (transcript grep + run-bundle `PASS_STATUSES`) vs saga `plugins/saga/scripts/provenance_manifest.py` + `engine_dispatch.py` `build_dispatch_manifest`. external-engine-workers.md:6 shows worker-manifest reserves `fell-back-to-claude`/`substituted-engine` only for the codex path. Intake brief §5 adds a THIRD bridge kind (registry-driven providers) with no proof obligation. Does not cross {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: receipt is evidence, not a verdict.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_receipt.py` (schema + emit helper) wired into `engine_dispatch.py`, `agy_delegate.py`, plus `tests/test_bridge_receipt_drift.py` enumerating registered bridges and asserting each emits a receipt. Verified: drift test red when a bridge lacks the call; a live codex + agy run each produce a conforming receipt file.

title: Provider-registry receipt guard: no bridge enters the router without proof-of-execution wiring
idea: The planned router plugin (intake §5) makes adding a provider as cheap as a registry entry plus a bridge script extending engine_resolver.py/engine_registry.py. That cheapness is exactly how {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} is reborn: a new bridge with no invocation-evidence obligation silently lets Claude do the work. Remove the possibility at the source by making a receipt-emitter a REQUIRED field of every registry entry, validated at registry-load time and by a CI guard that walks engine_registry entries and fails if any names a bridge script that does not import/call the receipt helper. The best defense against a silent provider is a registry that refuses to register one. This is the marketplace-drift-guard pattern applied to the delegation seam.
basis: Intake brief §5: 'one router plugin, registry-driven — extend existing engine-registry seam (engine_resolver.py / engine_registry.py); each provider = registry entry + bridge script.' LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:305 'Delegated to an external CLI is a claim to verify per run.' The new providers would inherit that failure mode unless proof is a registration precondition. Builds beyond QUEUED {#delegate-agents-plugin} which does not address proof-at-registration.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `receipt_emitter` required key to the engine_registry entry schema plus `tests/test_engine_registry_receipt_guard.py` asserting every entry's named bridge script references the receipt helper. Verified: adding a dummy provider without a receipt-emitter turns the guard red.

title: Real-time fail-loud tripwire: PreToolUse hook kills the manual verify-agy-ran step
idea: The {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} fix added a MANUAL 'mandatory verify-agy-ran' post-hoc step: after a delegated run, grep the transcript for the actual agy/codex process call. A manual verification step is a step to remove. Invert it into a PreToolUse hook that watches the active delegation session and fails LOUD the instant Claude issues a Write/Edit on a repo file while the current unit is marked delegated and zero engine process calls have been observed for it. Rather than discovering the Claude-clone substitution days later in commit-provenance archaeology, the session halts at the first illegitimate keystroke with a typed error naming the unit. The hook reads the delegation state the wrapper already writes; no engine becomes a gatekeeper because the hook gates CLAUDE's own tool use, not an external verdict.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:301,305 — the discriminator (real agy → Bash `agy --model` + Claude touches only prompt.txt; clone → Write/Edit on repo files + zero agy calls) is documented but enforced only by a manual post-run grep. #279/#278 shipped false Claude-authored provenance because nothing caught it in real time. Frame F2 inverts the manual step to an automated harness gate. Engages {#manifest-full-loop-one-pr} revisit-when ('a gate needs verification logic that does not already exist') — this is new real-time logic.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/agy/hooks/delegation_tripwire_hook.py` (PreToolUse) plus a delegation-active state file written by agy_delegate.py, and `tests/test_delegation_tripwire.py` simulating a zero-engine-call Write and asserting a blocking error. Verified: a scripted clone-fallback session halts; a genuine agy run (writes only prompt.txt) passes clean.

title: Empty-delivery HALT at every unit boundary — automate 'commit each unit as it lands'
idea: The n=2 agy finding names the expensive failure precisely: F6 silent no-op, where a delegate finishes, writes nothing, emits no error, and Claude silently writes the unit by hand. The catch is trivial (`git status` empty) but today it is a discipline the operator must remember. Automate it: at each delegated unit boundary the wrapper runs a write_set delta check and HALTs with an empty-delivery error if the engine produced no in-scope change, instead of letting the flow slide into hand-authoring. Pair it with an auto-commit of each unit the moment it passes its gate, so a clean tree is the enforced precondition to advancing — closing both the no-op slide and the late-write clobber window in one guard. The best version of the 'did it deliver' check is one that cannot be forgotten.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-flash-coder-review-fix-n2}:331,333 'The real tax was F6 silent no-op... the verifier catch is trivial (git status empty) but the cost is the whole unit' and 'commit each unit the moment it passes its gate'; {#delegate-orphan-late-write}:345 'a clean tree at commit-time is the cheap defense.' Both are currently manual habits, not machinery.
outcome_shape: PR adding a unit-boundary `check_empty_delivery()` + auto-commit hook to the agy/team-execution delegated-build path plus `tests/test_empty_delivery_halt.py`. Verified: a delegated unit that writes nothing produces a HALT (not a silent hand-off); a delivering unit auto-commits and advances.

title: First-class SUBSTITUTED disposition — remove the hand-built fallback manifest
idea: When an engine is silently replaced by Claude, the manifest layer cannot express it: build_dispatch_manifest only inspects evidence.halt and maps to RAN_AS_REQUESTED, so the chaperone must HAND-CONSTRUCT a provenance_manifest.Manifest to record substitution. A manual escape hatch beside the machinery is exactly the seam where substitution goes unrecorded. Remove the hand-build: teach build_dispatch_manifest a first-class SUBSTITUTED disposition driven by the bridge receipt (zero engine invocations observed) so engine-vs-chaperone authorship is attributed automatically and uniformly. This makes 'who actually wrote this output' a computed field of the standard manifest path rather than a chaperone's remembered courtesy.
basis: external-engine-workers.md:163-164 (direct quote): 'Substituted: build_dispatch_manifest has no way to express this disposition (it only inspects evidence.halt), so the chaperone constructs provenance_manifest.Manifest [by hand].' engine_dispatch.py:124-161 maps halt→RAN_AS_REQUESTED with attribution kind=EXTERNAL_ENGINE. Does not cross a binding decision: attribution is provenance/evidence, not a gate verdict, consistent with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}.
outcome_shape: PR extending `build_dispatch_manifest` in `plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py` with a SUBSTITUTED disposition keyed off the bridge receipt, deleting the chaperone hand-build path, plus a `tests/test_provenance_manifest.py` case. Verified: a zero-invocation run yields a SUBSTITUTED manifest with kind=CLAUDE attribution automatically.

title: Provenance-claim vs proof reconciliation in /retro — flag manifests that lie about attribution
idea: manifest_reader.py already surfaces delegation manifests to /retro, and audit_harness_transcript.py already extracts the real process calls, but nothing cross-checks the two: a manifest can assert attribution=EXTERNAL_ENGINE while the transcript shows zero engine invocations. Automate the reconciliation the operator did by hand in the #279 provenance correction: a /retro-surfaced reader that joins each manifest's claimed attribution against its bridge receipt and lists every run where the claim and the proof disagree. This turns 'we later discovered the n=4 Pro data was invalid' from an archaeology episode into a standing report, so false-provenance datapoints are caught the same cycle they are produced. The reader is advisory-only and never mutates the manifest.
basis: manifest_reader.py exists (DECISIONS {#manifest-reader-sibling-override-rate}, #285 KTD8) and audit_harness_transcript.py exists, but LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:301 shows the claim-vs-reality check was a manual per-transcript classification that only ran after false 'n=4 Pro' provenance had already been logged. Nothing joins the manifest's attribution against the receipt automatically.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `provenance_reconcile.py` reader (sibling to manifest_reader.py) invoked by /retro, plus `tests/test_provenance_reconcile.py`. Verified: a fixture manifest claiming EXTERNAL_ENGINE with a zero-invocation receipt appears in the mismatch list; a genuine run does not.

title: Bridge-run liveness leases + late-write quarantine — automate the git-status defense against orphans
idea: A thrashing delegate runner spawned an orphan that ran ~72 minutes and, after the PR was already open, appended 5 unreviewed assertions to a test file — caught only by a routine git status. saga already has outcome_liveness.py for /outcome leaves but bridge runs (agy, codex) have no liveness contract. Extend leases to every bridge run: each run holds a time-bounded lease keyed to its unit, and a post-run guard quarantines (moves aside, does not accept) any write from a runner whose lease has expired or whose parent unit is already committed/closed. Invert the manual 'git status before trusting done' habit into a guard that structurally refuses late orphan writes into a tree the operator has moved past. The orphan can still finish; its output simply cannot land.
basis: LEARNINGS {#delegate-orphan-late-write}:341,345 — orphan ran ~72 min, appended 5 assertions to tests/test_team_execution_plugin.py after PR #303 opened, 'caught by a routine git status.' saga `plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_liveness.py` provides leases for /outcome leaves only, not for agy/codex bridge runs. Engages that gap directly.
outcome_shape: PR adding a bridge-run lease + `quarantine_late_write()` guard (reusing outcome_liveness patterns) wired into the delegated-build path, plus `tests/test_bridge_orphan_quarantine.py`. Verified: a simulated write from an expired-lease runner is quarantined, not merged; a live-lease write lands.

title: Cross-bridge append-only chain-of-custody ledger for delegation evidence
idea: A probe script overwrote a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS — evidence with no chain of custody. Beyond per-artifact write-once immutability (already a narrow direct-to-candidate), give the whole delegation fleet an append-only hash-chained ledger: each bridge receipt, manifest, and evidence artifact is content-addressed and linked to its predecessor by hash, so any silent overwrite, reordering, or deletion breaks the chain and is detectable. The ledger rides the existing git-common-dir saga-manifests tree, so it inherits the manifest carrier's storage without a new store. This converts 'trust the latest artifact' into 'verify the unbroken custody chain', making a swapped or clobbered FAIL structurally impossible to hide. Verification is a pure chain-walk, never a gate on an external verdict.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody).' manifest_store.py + DECISIONS {#manifest-carrier-git-common-dir} (#285 KTD1) provide the git-common-dir saga-manifests carrier this ledger rides. Explicitly supersets the narrow 'evidence-artifact immutability' direct-to-candidate by adding cross-bridge linkage, so it is not a duplicate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `custody_ledger.py` (content-address + hash-chain append) layered over manifest_store.py, a `verify_chain()` entrypoint, and `tests/test_custody_ledger.py`. Verified: overwriting or deleting a prior evidence entry makes verify_chain fail; an honest append-only sequence verifies clean.

title: Make the inert `provenance_required` field fail-loud instead of decorative
idea: The agy wrapper already parses, validates, stores, and serializes `provenance_required` (default True) but NEVER reads it in the supervised run path — it is a dataclass slot + argparse flag + JSON key with zero consumer, the exact dead-wiring anti-pattern the journal warns against. The field NAMES the protection against silent Claude-fallback yet enforces nothing: `main()` returns exit 0 on `success` even when `real_agy_verdict` is `unproven`. Reframe: proof-of-invocation is treated as advisory metadata when it is actually the contract. Wire `provenance_required` so that when it is True and `_real_agy_verdict()` returns `unproven` (or the log shows no genuine agy process), the wrapper coerces status to `fallback_suspected` and returns non-zero — a HALT the delegating skill cannot mistake for success. Claude stays verifier-of-record; the bridge just refuses to LIE about having run an engine.
basis: agy_delegate.py: `provenance_required` defined/validated/stored at lines 100,137-139,154,261 but grep shows ZERO reads in `create_supervised_bundle`/run logic; `main()` returns 0 on `success` (line 1161); `_real_agy_verdict()` already computes `unproven` (lines 1592-1600) but only writes it into run-lease.json, never gates. Matches LEARNINGS {#dead-wiring-needs-producer-and-consumer} (a consumer-less field is silently inert) and {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py (gate on provenance_required in the supervised status decision) + a new oracle test in tests/ asserting an unproven run with provenance_required=True yields status fallback_suspected and exit!=0 + CHANGELOG/plugin.json version bump. Verified by the test going red on today's code and green after the wiring.

title: Harness-enforce the transcript audit via a Stop hook instead of a remembered manual step
idea: Today proof-of-execution lives in `audit_harness_transcript.py`, run BY HAND per the harness-proof doc's 'Audit command' — which means the one time it matters (a real delegation in a working session, not the release gate) nobody runs it, and the silent-fallback shipped as '#279 n=4 Pro data' that was actually Claude. Reframe the 'that is just how delegation works — you audit afterward if you remember' default: attach the classifier to a Stop / SubagentStop hook in the agy plugin's settings so that after ANY session that invoked `/agy:delegate`, the harness auto-classifies the subagent transcript and surfaces `fallback_suspected` loudly before the turn closes. Proof stops being a discipline the orchestrator must remember and becomes a property of the harness.
basis: plugins/agy/docs/harness-proof.md:15-19 documents the audit as a manual `python3 audit_harness_transcript.py ...` command; LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} shows the fallback was caught only by an after-the-fact full audit ('The only trustworthy signal is the transcript itself'), i.e. exactly the step a human forgot mid-build.
outcome_shape: PR adding a hook entry to plugins/agy settings + a thin wrapper script that runs classify_transcript over the latest subagents/*.jsonl and prints a HALT banner on fallback_suspected, plus a test exercising the wrapper against a known Claude-clone transcript fixture and a known real-agy fixture. Verified by the fixture pair classifying correctly and the hook firing in a scripted session.

title: A fleet delegation-receipt contract so every bridge emits the same invocation evidence
idea: agy has a rich, proven evidence vocabulary — `agy.result.v1`, `agy.git-proof.v1`, run-lease with `agy_launched`/`real_agy_verdict` — but it is ENTIRELY agy-private. team-execution's external-engine workers (chaperone dispatch) and saga's readonly-verifier spawns produce no comparable receipt, so 'the offload engine reviewed this' is an unfalsifiable claim for every bridge except agy. Reframe the assumption that each bridge owns its own (or no) evidence shape: define one `delegation.receipt.v1` schema (engine, resolved_bin, launched:bool, invocation_proof, changed_paths, verdict) and require every in-repo bridge to emit it. This is a shared reference doc + validator, NOT a new marketplace plugin — so it discharges the 17→7 consolidation burden by REDUCING per-bridge bespoke evidence to one contract rather than adding surface.
basis: agy_delegate.py emits agy-only schemas `agy.result.v1` (line 1399), `agy.git-proof.v1` (line 1437), run-lease `real_agy_verdict` (line 1587); grep of plugins/team-execution/.../external-engine-workers.md and plugins/codex found ZERO transcript/proof/receipt machinery. Binding {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} revisit-when engaged: this is a schema+validator reference, not a plugin, and it consolidates rather than sprawls.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/agy/references/delegation-receipt.md (the v1 schema) + a scripts/validate_receipt.py + a drift test in tests/ asserting agy's emitted result validates against the shared schema. Verified by validate_receipt.py passing on a real agy bundle and rejecting a receipt missing invocation_proof.

title: Give team-execution's external-engine workers the same fail-loud discriminator agy has
idea: team-execution runs external engines as chaperone dispatch (offload→sonnet/medium, second-opinion→opus/high) via the Step A7 worker table, but that path has NO invocation proof: a worker slot that silently degrades to plain Claude looks identical to a genuine engine offload, and the consensus record will attribute a 'second opinion' that never happened. Reframe 'external-engine workers are just prompt-configured teammates, trust the label': port agy's discriminator idea — the worker must surface an invocation-proof line (engine process seen vs not) and, when absent, the chaperone marks the contribution `unproven` so it cannot count as an independent opinion in the 15/17-style convergence. This stays inside {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}: no second executor kind, no git participant — only an honesty flag on the existing chaperone contribution.
basis: Grounding §1 confirms 0 of 24 team-execution agents carry proof machinery and §6 lists silent-no-op as a 5+-learning pattern; {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) fixes the shape (offload/second-opinion, never a second executor) which this idea explicitly respects — it flags, it does not re-architect. external-engine-workers.md grep returned zero proof/transcript hits.
outcome_shape: PR editing plugins/team-execution/.../external-engine-workers.md + the Step A7 worker contract in SKILL.md to require an invocation-proof field and an `unproven`→not-counted rule, plus a version-metadata drift-guard test update. Verified by a scripted worker run whose missing proof downgrades its consensus weight.

title: Machine-checked engine-vs-chaperone authorship ledger, replacing the manual commit-provenance correction
idea: When #279's commits were mis-attributed as 'agy Pro authored', the fix was a HUMAN correcting commit messages after the fact. Reframe the assumption that authorship attribution is a manual after-thought bolted onto commit text (and note CLAUDE.md bans attribution TRAILERS, so this must NOT touch commit trailers): derive a per-unit authorship ledger from evidence already in the run bundle — changed_paths that crossed the wrapper's `git apply` gate are engine-authored; anything Claude Write/Edit'd (from the transcript classifier) is chaperone-authored. Write it as a `provenance.json` in the bundle, not into git. This turns 'who wrote this unit' from a claim someone must remember to correct into a fact the bridge computes, and lets a datapoint ('n=4 agy') be auto-invalidated when the ledger shows chaperone authorship.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} Fix (1): 'Commit provenance corrected — #279 commits say Claude-authored (the n=4 Pro data is invalid)' — a manual correction. agy_delegate.py already has both signals: apply-gate changed_paths (apply_patch_to_live_repo, line 969) and Claude-file-tool detection (classify_transcript, line 1010). CLAUDE.md Prohibited-Content ban engaged: ledger is a bundle artifact, never a commit trailer.
outcome_shape: PR adding a provenance.json emitter to plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py that joins apply-gate paths (engine) with transcript file-tool paths (chaperone) + a test asserting a Claude-clone run produces an all-chaperone ledger. Verified by the fixture run's ledger matching known authorship.

title: Fencing-token tree guard that rejects writes from an expired delegation lease
idea: A thrashing agy:runner spawned an orphan that ran ~72 minutes and appended unreviewed test assertions AFTER PR #303 was open; the only defense was 'commit each unit immediately so the late writer has nothing to clobber'. Reframe the accepted fatalism that 'a teammate's descendants have lifetimes decoupled from the orchestrator's turn — that is just how the harness works': the wrapper ALREADY writes run-lease.json (run_id, ended_at, shutdown) but nothing enforces it. Add a fencing-token pre-commit / pre-write guard that reads the active lease and REFUSES to accept tree mutations tagged to a run whose lease is `exited`/`terminated` — an expired-lease write is rejected at the boundary, not discovered later by a lucky `git status`. Attacks the orphan-write class structurally rather than relying on orchestrator vigilance.
basis: LEARNINGS {#delegate-orphan-late-write}: orphan ran ~72 min and wrote after PR open, caught only by routine git status. agy_delegate.py already produces run-lease.json with shutdown/ended_at (lines 598-604, 1559-1589) but no code consumes it as a liveness fence — a producer with no enforcing consumer.
outcome_shape: PR adding a pre-commit hook (or wrapper-owned guard script) + tests that, given a lease marked exited and a subsequent write tagged to that run_id, rejects it. Verified by a scripted late-write against a closed lease being blocked while an in-lease write passes.

title: Hash-chained chain-of-custody manifest so a later PASS cannot bury an earlier FAIL
idea: A probe script overwrote a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS — the audit trail was mutable, so absence of the FAIL read as never-failed.
