The direct-to-candidate pool already has the narrow 'make evidence files immutable' seed; go one level up: reframe evidence as an APPEND-ONLY hash-chained manifest per run. Each artifact write (envelope, agy.log, git-proof, checks, result) records its sha256 and the prior entry's hash into a manifest.jsonl; any overwrite breaks the chain and is detectable, and the FULL history (FAIL then PASS) is preserved rather than clobbered. This is chain-of-custody, not just file locks — an independent verifier can replay the manifest and prove no artifact was silently swapped.
basis: Grounding §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'. Distinct from the §8 direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' seed — this is a hash-linked append-only ledger with replay verification, one level up from per-file immutability. agy already writes discrete bundle artifacts (agy_delegate.py _write_json throughout) that this would chain.
outcome_shape: PR adding a manifest.jsonl hash-chain emitter to the agy bundle writer + a verify_custody.py that recomputes the chain and flags any broken/overwritten link, plus a test that mutating an artifact post-hoc trips the verifier. Verified by the verifier detecting a swapped FAIL→PASS artifact.

title: Relocate delegation evidence out of the disposable-worktree blast radius
idea: agy run bundles live under `.claude/agy/runs/<run_id>` inside the working repo — the same tree that gets reaped when a saga worktree is torn down (grounding found 15 stale abandoned worktrees inflating the repo 10x, and teammate work uses disposable clones). Reframe the assumption that proof belongs next to the workspace it proves: co-locating immutable evidence with a disposable workspace GUARANTEES eventual loss — the moment teardown finally works, the audit trail dies with it. Route delegation receipts to a durable per-host audit store (e.g. ~/.claude/delegation-audit/<repo>/<run_id>, gitignored, teardown-exempt) keyed by run_id, so chain-of-custody survives worktree reclamation and the eventual Step B8 teardown that theme 6 is chasing.
basis: agy_delegate.py builds bundle_path as `repo_root/.claude/agy/runs/<run_id>` (lines 279, 353); grounding §4 documents 15 stale worktrees under .worktrees/ as the teardown/reclamation disease and §6 ties delegation integrity to 'did it persist'. Evidence under the disposable tree is lost on the very teardown theme 6 wants to make work.
outcome_shape: PR adding a --audit-store path (default ~/.claude/delegation-audit) to agy_delegate.py that mirrors the receipt+manifest to the durable store + a test asserting the receipt exists in the store after the working bundle dir is deleted. Verified by removing the bundle dir and still resolving the receipt by run_id.

title: Fleet-shared delegation-receipt primitive (generalize agy's transcript auditor)
idea: agy already ships a per-plugin proof-of-execution auditor (plugins/agy/scripts/audit_harness_transcript.py) that greps a transcript for the real `agy --model` Bash call. Extract its core into a fleet-shared `scripts/delegation_proof.py` library that defines one receipt schema — {bridge, engine, argv_fingerprint, external_pid, external_tokens, exit_status, artifact_paths, ts} — plus an `assert_ran(receipt)` gate. Every bridge (agy, team-execution external-engine workers, saga engine_resolver) emits a receipt into a canonical `.delegation-receipts/` path on each call; the shared verifier reads receipts instead of each bridge reinventing transcript-grepping. Compounding payoff: any future bridge or provider-registry entry (theme 2's router plugin) gets silent-no-op detection for free by emitting the shared receipt.
basis: plugins/agy/scripts/audit_harness_transcript.py exists (115 lines, `PASS_STATUSES = frozenset({'success','patch_ready','applied'})`, BUNDLE_RE bundle-path extraction) but is agy-only; LEARNINGS.md:305 rule: "'Delegated to an external CLI' is a claim to verify per run from the transcript"; grounding brief theme 15 lists 5+ silent-no-op learnings across distinct bridges needing one 'did it actually run/persist' check.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/delegation_proof.py (receipt schema + assert_ran) with unit tests in tests/test_delegation_proof.py, refactoring plugins/agy/scripts/audit_harness_transcript.py to consume it, plus a DECISIONS.md entry. Verified: agy audit tests still pass green and a second bridge (team-execution external worker) emits a schema-valid receipt in a fixture test.

title: Bridge-signature registry with a fail-loud post-run HALT gate
idea: The silent Claude-fallback ({#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}) is undetectable because 'the name of the spawn is NOT a reliable discriminator' — only the transcript's external process call is. Ship a declarative `bridge-signatures.json` registry where each bridge declares its required external-process signature (agy: `agy --model`; codex: `codex exec`; each theme-2 provider: its bridge argv) and its clone tell (Write/Edit on repo files + zero external calls). A shared post-run gate loads the registry, checks the emitted receipt/transcript against the declared signature, and HALTs loud (nonzero exit, explicit 'DELEGATION DID NOT RUN — Claude clone detected') rather than letting the unit pass. Registry-driven so a new provider adds one entry, not new detection code.
basis: LEARNINGS.md:299 "the name of the spawn is NOT a reliable discriminator... The only trustworthy signal is the transcript itself"; LEARNINGS.md:301 documents the discriminator (real agy → `agy --model` Bash call + Claude touches only prompt.txt; Claude-clone → Write/Edit + `★ Insight` + 0 agy calls). Does not cross {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: gate makes Claude MORE the verifier-of-record, not less.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/bridge-signatures.json + a `assert_bridge_ran` gate in scripts/delegation_proof.py, wired as a HALT step in plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/SKILL.md and team-execution's external-engine-workers.md worker flow. Verified: a fixture transcript with zero external calls makes the gate exit nonzero with the clone-detected message.

title: Engine-vs-chaperone authorship stamp computed from the receipt
idea: When a delegated unit lands, the journal repeatedly has to reconstruct 'was this engine-authored or Claude-authored?' from commit messages after the fact — the #279 invalid 'n=4 Pro' datapoint is exactly this failure. Add a `provenance-stamp` step that, from the shared receipt, writes a sidecar `.delegation-provenance/<unit>.json` recording author-engine, chaperone-fix-delta (what Claude changed post-hoc), and external-token count — a first-class provenance fact, not a commit trailer (repo bans attribution trailers). team-execution and agy both stamp through the same helper so experiment datapoints (n=2, n=3...) are measured, not narrated. Compounds theme 10's provenance discipline: every future delegated run self-attributes.
basis: LEARNINGS.md:295 #279 'agy teammates behaved exactly like Claude', commit provenance had to be corrected post-hoc (LEARNINGS.md:301 fix #1 'Commit provenance corrected — #279 commits say Claude-authored'); LEARNINGS.md:333 'raw drafts were not archived, so this delta is reconstructed from commit messages, not measured'. CLAUDE.md prohibits commit attribution trailers — sidecar avoids that.
outcome_shape: PR adding a provenance-stamp helper to scripts/delegation_proof.py writing .delegation-provenance/<unit>.json, invoked from agy-delegate SKILL.md and team-execution SKILL.md post-unit steps, plus a schema doc. Verified: an integration fixture produces a stamp whose author-engine field flips correctly between a real-engine receipt and a clone receipt.

title: Shared runner-liveness heartbeat + orphan reaper across teammate bridges
idea: Two live-observed failure modes share a root: agy's `--background` runner spinning nested poll loops it can never block on, and 'subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications' reproduced in this very session. Build a shared liveness primitive: every teammate-model bridge (agy runner, team-execution reviewer fan-out, saga readonly-verifier spawns) registers a runner entry {bridge, runner_id, mailbox, last_heartbeat, expected_artifacts} in `.delegation-runners/`; a shared `reap_orphans.py` marks a runner stalled when heartbeat ages past a threshold with no artifact, and detects late-writing orphans (a runner that writes after the coordinator moved on). The coordinator re-pings or HALTs off one shared signal instead of each bridge hand-rolling idle detection.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 9 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications — coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session)'; LEARNINGS.md:311-315 {#agy-delegate-plain-is-the-path} '--background... runner spun firing nested auto-backgrounded poll loops it could never block on', 'agy produced 0 bytes for 21 minutes'. Builds on the mailbox/teammate substrate LEARNINGS.md:321 names as 'the coordination substrate to build the later distributed-delegation issues on'.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/delegation_runners.py (register/heartbeat) + scripts/reap_orphans.py with tests, referenced from plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/SKILL.md and plugins/saga/references/sandbox-spawn-sites.md. Verified: a test simulating a stalled runner (aged heartbeat, empty artifacts) is flagged, and a late-write-after-close runner is flagged as orphan.

title: Write-once receipt store as a fleet chain-of-custody spine
idea: The direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' item is narrow (fix one probe script that overwrote a FAIL with a later PASS). Go beyond it: make the shared receipt store itself append-only and content-addressed — every delegation receipt is written under a hash-named path that a later run physically cannot overwrite, and a `verify_custody.py` walks the chain to detect any in-place mutation of a prior receipt. This turns immutability from a per-script discipline into a fleet primitive every bridge inherits, so no future bridge can silently clobber its own evidence. The chain-of-custody log becomes the audit substrate theme 10's provenance discipline needs.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'; §8 direct-to-candidate pool lists only the narrow 'evidence-artifact immutability' fix — this idea is the generalized primitive beyond that item, satisfying the no-duplicate-of-pool requirement by shifting from one-script-fix to fleet write-once store.
outcome_shape: PR adding content-addressed append-only write in scripts/delegation_proof.py (hash-named receipt paths, refuse-overwrite) + scripts/verify_custody.py + tests asserting an overwrite attempt raises. Verified: test writes a FAIL receipt then attempts a PASS overwrite at the same logical key and the store rejects it, preserving the FAIL.

title: Marketplace-CI delegation-proof gate for any bridge-carrying version bump
idea: agy's release gate already requires a live harness-proof transcript (plugins/agy/docs/harness-proof.md) — but it is a manual, agy-only ritual documented as 'passed live run on 2026-06-30'. Promote it to a fleet marketplace-CI guard: a check that, whenever a plugin declaring a bridge bumps its version in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, requires a committed, schema-valid delegation-proof receipt/transcript for that bridge in the PR — otherwise CI fails. This makes 'proof of real external execution' a release-surface obligation (extending CLAUDE.md step 6's release-surface discipline) rather than a hand-run ceremony one plugin remembers. Compounds: theme 2's new providers cannot ship green without proving they actually invoke their engine.
basis: plugins/agy/docs/harness-proof.md:5-8 'Static tests are not enough for this plugin: the gate requires Claude Code transcripts showing that the packaged agents invoked plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py'; it is a manual live-run doc (line 3 'Status: passed live run on 2026-06-30'). CLAUDE.md step 6 already mandates release-surface parity incl. marketplace.json and drift-guard tests — this extends that machinery.
outcome_shape: PR adding a CI job (e.g. .github/workflows/) + scripts/check_delegation_proof.py that fails when a bridge-declaring plugin's marketplace.json version changed without an accompanying valid proof artifact, plus a registry of which plugins declare bridges. Verified: CI red on a fixture PR bumping agy's version with no proof; green when the proof artifact is present.

title: External-token accounting as the fail-loud silent-fallback discriminator, wired to the cost ledger
idea: The cheapest unforgeable proof that an external engine actually ran is that it burned external tokens: zero external-engine tokens on a 'delegated' unit is proof Claude did the work. Have the shared receipt record external_tokens per call, and add an `assert_external_spend(receipt)` gate that HALTs when a delegated unit reports zero external tokens. Then feed those same per-leaf token facts into the /outcome cost ledger, which the U1–U11 campaign already treats as a leaf-produced fact — so the silent-fallback discriminator and the cost-accounting number are the same measurement, computed once. One lever, two payoffs: fail-loud on no-ops and honest delegation spend.
basis: Grounding brief §2 binding decision '/outcome campaign (U1-U11): cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' — this idea engages it by making external-token spend a leaf-produced fact feeding that ledger, not a committed field. LEARNINGS.md:331 names 'F6 silent no-op' as the expensive failure; a zero-external-token reading is the crisp machine signal the current `git status`-empty heuristic approximates.
outcome_shape: PR adding external_tokens to the receipt schema + assert_external_spend gate in scripts/delegation_proof.py, with a ledger-adapter that emits the same number into the /outcome cost ledger path, plus tests. Verified: a zero-external-token receipt trips the HALT gate, and the same value appears once in a cost-ledger fixture.

title: Auto-archived raw delegate drafts as an immutable experiment-measurement corpus
idea: The journal's own process gap: 'raw drafts were not archived, so this delta is reconstructed from commit messages, not measured' — so every agy/codex coder experiment (n=1..3) loses its ground truth. Add a shared pre-fix hook to the delegation primitive that, before the Claude chaperone touches a delegated draft, snapshots it write-once into `.delegation-drafts/<run>/<unit>/` (the `git stash`/copy the learning prescribes, done automatically). This makes the engine-vs-chaperone fix-delta a durable, replayable measurement across every future run and every provider, compounding the provenance and proof axes into a permanent evidence corpus rather than a one-time reconstruction.
basis: LEARNINGS.md:333 'Process gap to close at n=3: raw drafts were not archived, so this delta is reconstructed from commit messages, not measured — git stash/copy each draft before fixing it.' This is an explicit named process gap the operator's own journal prescribes closing.
outcome_shape: PR adding a pre-chaperone snapshot step to scripts/delegation_proof.py writing immutable .delegation-drafts/ copies, wired into plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/SKILL.md's verify-and-fix flow, plus a LEARNINGS.md entry closing the named gap. Verified: a fixture run leaves an unmodified draft snapshot whose diff against the fixed file equals the chaperone fix-delta.

title: Bridge transponder ledger: no squawk, no radar contact
idea: Air-traffic control does not trust a pilot's radio 'I am here' — an aircraft with no transponder return is treated as no contact and the sector controller acts on that absence. Generalize agy's agy-only, post-hoc classify_transcript (agy_delegate.py:989-1022) into a fleet primitive plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py: every bridge dispatch (agy, codex, team-execution external-engine worker, /outcome leaf) must open an append-only 'squawk' record with a unique code before launch and close it with process-level evidence (the resolved engine binary in argv + a nonzero-duration exit) after. A returned result whose squawk never closed is 'no radar contact' — the caller HALTs loudly rather than attributing the work. This makes invocation evidence a shared contract instead of one plugin's private grep.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} (LEARNINGS.md:293-305): '#279 (4 units) and #278 (5 units) made zero agy calls'; the discriminator today lives only in agy's classify_transcript (agy_delegate.py:1014-1015, agy-local, returns advisory 'fallback_suspected'), while grounding brief §1 confirms team-execution fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch and engine bridges are unbounded with no shared proof.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py (open_squawk/close_squawk + an append-only per-call JSON ledger) and wiring the call into plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py, plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md, and the /outcome leaf-dispatch path; verified by tests/test_bridge_proof.py asserting a stubbed dispatch that never invokes the engine leaves an unclosed squawk and forces a nonzero exit.

title: Server-authoritative output attestation: the delivered diff must be one only the engine's run could emit
idea: Online-chess anti-cheat does not merely confirm 'an engine binary was open' — it checks the moves correlate with engine output, because a process can run yet contribute nothing. A silent no-op passes a naive 'did the process run?' check: agy U4 'finished, wrote nothing, no error/escalation, then thrashed.' Make every bridge return a server-authoritative attestation: the engine's run bundle must contain a non-empty diff.patch whose hash equals the patch actually applied/committed for that unit. Empty bundle diff, or a committed change that does not match the bundle, means the delivered output did not come from the claimed producer — reject the unit. This closes the gap idea T15-F5-1 leaves open (process ran but produced null).
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-flash-coder-review-fix-n2} (LEARNINGS.md:329-331): 'U4 (prose protocol + doc test): silent no-op — finished, wrote nothing, no error/escalation, then thrashed → hand-written ... the verifier catch is trivial (git status empty) but the cost is the whole unit'; delegation-contract.md already emits diff.patch + git-proof.json in the run bundle, so the correlation check has real inputs to bind.
outcome_shape: PR extending plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py (derive_diff_evidence / apply_patch_to_live_repo) to assert bundle-diff hash == applied-commit hash and reject on empty bundle diff, plus a shared assertion in plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py for non-agy bridges; verified by a test feeding an empty-diff bundle and asserting rejection with a distinct exit code.

title: Jidoka andon cord: pull the line the instant a delegation cannot prove it ran
idea: Toyota's jidoka stops the whole line the moment a defect is detected rather than passing it downstream, and poka-yoke makes the defective path physically impossible to continue. Today agy classifies 'fallback_suspected' but the run can still complete and Claude can silently finish and attribute the unit. Convert the documented-but-manual 'verify-agy-ran' step into an enforced andon: any bridge classification that is not provably 'real' halts the delegated unit loudly and refuses to record authorship, forcing an explicit operator decision (re-dispatch, scrap, or accept-as-Claude). Because Claude remains verifier-of-record, the halt is Claude-driven — consistent with never-gatekeepers, which the issue text must state explicitly.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} (LEARNINGS.md:301): the fix was a documented 'mandatory verify-agy-ran step' — still a doc instruction, not machinery; binding {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) is engaged: the andon halt is executed by Claude as verifier-of-record, so external engines gain no gate authority, satisfying that decision's constraint without touching its revisit-when.
outcome_shape: PR making plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py exit nonzero when classification != 'real' and provenance_required is true, plus a SKILL.md andon-halt clause in plugins/agy/skills/agy-delegate/SKILL.md and plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md; verified by a test asserting fallback_suspected + provenance_required forces the halt exit and emits no authorship record.

title: Two-signal co-stimulation: a delegation is 'accepted' only when engine and observer signals corroborate
idea: Immunology's two-signal model holds that a lymphocyte receiving antigen (signal 1) without an independent co-stimulatory signal 2 goes anergic rather than activating — a deliberate guard against false-positive self-attack. Apply the same to delegation acceptance: a bridge 'success' requires TWO independent signals that must agree — the engine's own exit/self-report AND an external observer's transcript/process classification. If only one fires, the unit is marked 'anergic' (unverifiable) and re-queued, never silently accepted on the engine's word alone. This is the dead-wiring 'producer AND consumer' discipline lifted onto the proof-of-execution boundary: one signal proves nothing.
basis: Two-signal / co-stimulation model of lymphocyte activation (Bretscher-Cohn 1970; Lafferty-Cunningham) — established immunology, the canonical anergy-without-second-signal guard; adapted here as the acceptance rule for a delegated unit, directly paralleling this repo's {#dead-wiring-needs-producer-and-consumer} (LEARNINGS.md:471) which already treats a single-direction signal as inert.
outcome_shape: PR adding an 'anergic/re-queue' acceptance state to plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py requiring agreement between engine exit-report and observer classification, wired into agy and the team-execution worker table; verified by a test where the two signals disagree and the unit lands in re-queue rather than accepted.

title: Certificate of conformance: taggant-bound authorship no downstream reader can fake
idea: Aerospace supply chains fight counterfeit parts with taggants (DNA marking, holograms) plus a certificate of conformance traceable to the OEM — a part with no verifiable taggant is quarantined, never installed as genuine. Every delegated artifact (commit, saga tick, experiment datapoint) should carry a provenance taggant derived from its bridge run bundle (engine id + git-proof.json hash). Any downstream reader that records a producer — the engineering journal, an experiment log, a saga attribution — MUST resolve the taggant; if it cannot, it records 'provenance: unverified' rather than a confident engine attribution. This structurally prevents the '#279 commits say Claude but were logged as n=4 Pro' class of false datapoint. The taggant is a provenance record bound to the run bundle, NOT a marketing trailer, so it does not violate the no-attribution-lines rule.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} (LEARNINGS.md:301): 'Commit provenance corrected — #279 commits say Claude-authored (the n=4 Pro data is invalid)'; binding {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) is engaged — the taggant encodes exactly the engine-vs-chaperone attribution that decision governs, adding no second-executor kind.
outcome_shape: PR emitting a taggant field (engine id + bundle hash) from plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py run bundles and a resolver in plugins/saga/scripts/ that any producer-recording site calls, defaulting to 'unverified' on miss; verified by a test that an unresolvable taggant yields 'provenance: unverified' instead of an engine name.

title: Fencing tokens: a stale orphan's late write is rejected at the boundary, not caught by vigilance
idea: Distributed-systems leasing (Kleppmann's fencing tokens) solves exactly the late-writer problem: a paused/slow process resumes after its lease expired and tries to write stale data. The defense is not the client behaving — it is a monotonically increasing token stamped on every write, with the resource rejecting any write bearing a token older than the last it accepted. A thrashing runner's orphan already reproduced this: it ran ~72 minutes and appended 5 unreviewed assertions AFTER the PR was open. Give each bridge dispatch a monotonic fencing token tied to a TTL lease; the write target (worktree, saga tick, evidence ledger) refuses writes carrying a superseded token. The orphan is fenced out at write time — structural, replacing 'git status before trusting done state' vigilance.
basis: LEARNINGS {#delegate-orphan-late-write} (LEARNINGS.md:337-345): the orphan 'ran ~72 minutes and, after PR #303 was already open, completed and appended 5 unreviewed test assertions ... Caught by a routine git status'; binding {#verify-agent-git-checkout-clobber} is engaged — the fence sits at the worktree/saga write boundary the isolation profile already defines.
outcome_shape: PR adding a monotonic fencing-token + TTL-lease field to plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py dispatch records and a reject-on-stale-token guard at the saga-tick / evidence-ledger write path; verified by a test where a superseded-token write is rejected while the current-token write succeeds.

title: WORM chain-of-custody ledger: a later PASS cannot bury an earlier FAIL
idea: Financial-records compliance (SEC Rule 17a-4 WORM storage) plus RFC 3161 trusted timestamps plus legal chain-of-custody together guarantee that an audit record, once written, cannot be silently altered and every handoff is logged with who held it. A probe script already overwrote a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS. Beyond the narrow 'make the file immutable' candidate, bind every bridge's evidence artifact (qa health score, verify verdict, agy run bundle) into a hash-chained, write-once ledger where each entry records its producing bridge's identity/taggant and links the prior entry's hash. A FAIL-then-PASS becomes two ordered, tamper-evident entries — the earlier FAIL is provably still there — rather than one overwritten file. Custody (which bridge produced/handled it) is the piece the immutability-only candidate omits.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'; DECISIONS.md:932 already establishes the O_EXCL per-leaf immutable-file pattern for /outcome completions — this extends that proven pattern to fleet-wide evidence artifacts. Binding /outcome campaign (derive-on-read, HALT-not-degrade) is engaged: this ledger holds evidence facts, not status fields, so it complements rather than reintroduces committed status.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/evidence_ledger.py (O_EXCL write-once entries, prev-hash chaining, producer-identity/taggant field) and routing plugins/saga/scripts/qa_health_score.py + verify-verdict + agy bundle writes through it; verified by a test where a second write of the same logical artifact appends a new chained entry and the original FAIL entry remains readable and unmodified.

title: Zero-trust bridge contract: no delegated output counts until it proves it ran
idea: Flip the trust default to 0% — assume EVERY bridge call is a Claude-clone lie until a proof artifact refutes it, exactly as we now do for agy but nowhere else. Extract agy's proof machinery (agy_delegate.py:989 classify_transcript, the agy_launched flag, result.json bundle) into a bridge-agnostic plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py that defines a single ProofOfExecution schema (engine_id, launched:bool, invocation_evidence, transcript_classification). Make every dispatch seam — build_codex_invocation, engine_dispatch, team-execution external workers, saga readonly-verifier spawns — return this record, and make the consuming code (/work attribution, /outcome leaf ledger, team-execution consensus) refuse to attribute authorship or log an experiment datapoint without a launched=true proof. The practical kernel even if universal zero-trust is heavy: the proof schema is the reusable seam; sites adopt it incrementally.
basis: agy carries the full proof stack (plugins/agy/scripts/agy_delegate.py:989 classify_transcript -> agy_command_seen/claude_file_tool_seen/'real'|'fallback_suspected'; agy_launched at :792; audit_harness_transcript.py PASS_STATUSES gate) yet build_codex_invocation (plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py:41) returns a bare invocation dict with no launched flag. LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:305 'Delegated to an external CLI is a claim to verify per run from the transcript, never an assumption from the invocation.' Strengthens {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (Claude stays verifier-of-record), so no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/bridge_proof.py (shared ProofOfExecution dataclass + classifier interface), wiring engine_dispatch.build_codex_invocation and team-execution worker dispatch to emit it, plus tests/test_bridge_proof.py asserting a fallback/clone transcript classifies as launched=false. Verified by a red-then-green test that feeds a zero-engine-call transcript and asserts attribution is refused.

title: Codex bridge parity: the untested twin gets agy's transcript auditor
idea: Flip 'many bridges, one audited' to 'every bridge audited identically.' agy earned a transcript classifier and a release-gate auditor after the #279 silent-fallback burn; the codex bridge shipped later with zero equivalent, so codex delegation sits in exactly agy's pre-#279 blind spot. Give codex a classify_transcript analog that greps the harness transcript for the real codex process invocation (mirroring agy's `agy --model` Bash-call grep) and emits a codex_launched proof, plus a codex arm in audit_harness_transcript.py so the release gate proves codex ran rather than Claude finishing read-only. The kernel: parity of proof, not parity of engine — an unaudited bridge is a latent false-provenance datapoint.
basis: engine_dispatch.build_codex_invocation returns {'via':'codex:codex-rescue','sandbox':'read-only'} with NO launched flag or classifier, while agy_delegate.py exposes classify_transcript (:989) and audit_harness_transcript.py gates on agy_launched. external-engine-workers.md:104-106 confirms codex is a live dispatch target. LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} shows the exact failure this closes for codex. Honors {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318): codex output stays advisory; the proof only attests it was codex, not Claude.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a codex transcript classifier (plugins/saga/scripts/ or a codex bridge module) + a codex branch in plugins/agy/scripts/audit_harness_transcript.py, with a fixture transcript test proving a Claude-finished read-only run classifies as codex_launched=false. Verified by the auditor exit code (1) on the clone transcript.

title: $0 fallback budget: the resolver may never silently return Claude
idea: Flip the Claude-fallback budget to $0 — the resolver is forbidden from silently substituting Claude for an unavailable engine. Today engine_resolver returns a Resolution with engine_id='claude' and a string `fallback` reason for worker role_kinds, and the chaperone quietly does the unit itself; a consumer that ignores the fallback field never learns the engine no-op'd. Convert `fallback` from a passively-ignorable string into a loud, first-class event: dispatch emits a distinct FALLBACK signal that must be recorded in the saga/manifest and surfaced to the coordinator ('engine X unavailable -> Claude authored this unit') before any output is accepted. Fail-loud, not fail-silent. The kernel survives even if hard-blocking is too strict: the fallback becomes an attributed, logged, acknowledged fact instead of a silent substitution.
basis: engine_resolver returns a Claude-fallback Resolution (engine_id='claude', halt=None, fallback='<reason>') at engine_resolver.py:272-288 per external-engine-workers.md:60-61, and 'the chaperone does the unit itself.' LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:299 'the spawned teammate is effectively a Claude clone... never shelling out.' Aligns with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (Claude may do the work; it just may not do it silently) and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} #318 (fallback stays chaperone, not a second executor) — strengthens both, no revisit-when triggered.
outcome_shape: Merged PR making the resolver/dispatch fallback path emit a typed FallbackEvent persisted to the provenance manifest and returned as a non-silent status, with tests asserting a worker-role resolution with an unavailable engine produces a recorded fallback event (not a null-ish string a consumer can drop). Verified via test that a consumer reading the dispatch result sees fallback=true.

title: Every token attributed: engine-vs-chaperone stamp on every committed unit
idea: Flip to 'every artifact carries its true author or it cannot merge.' The #279 disaster was commits that SAID agy-authored while Claude wrote them; provenance was reconstructed forensically after the fact. Instead, derive an author-stamp at commit-time from the bridge proof (T15-F6-1): each delegated unit's commit trailer / saga record carries {authored_by: engine|chaperone, proof_ref: bundle_path, classification}. A pre-PR check (saga /code-review or a marketplace-CI guard) cross-checks every 'delegated to X' claim in the PR body against the proof classification and fails if a claim of engine authorship lacks a launched=true proof. The kernel: attribution becomes a derived-on-read fact from evidence, never an operator-typed claim — matching the fleet's derive-on-read posture.
basis: LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback}:301 'Commit provenance corrected -- #279 commits say Claude-authored (the n=4 Pro data is invalid)'; the discriminator (real agy -> transcript has agy --model + Claude touches only prompt.txt) is documented but applied only in a manual post-hoc audit. Derive-on-read is a settled fleet stance (grounding brief 6.5). Does not cross a binding decision; complements {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} by making advisory-vs-authored explicit in the artifact.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an author-provenance trailer derived from the proof bundle + a pre-PR claim-vs-proof cross-check (extending saga:code-review or the marketplace CI guard), with a test where a PR body claiming 'agy-authored' but backed by a fallback_suspected transcript fails the check. Verified by the check's non-zero exit on the mismatched fixture.

title: Assume every runner is thrashing: a fenced orphan reaper for delegate descendants
idea: Flip to 'every delegate runner WILL spawn a late-writing orphan' and design as if that is certain. A thrashing agy:runner spawned an orphan that ran ~72 minutes and appended 5 unreviewed test assertions AFTER the PR was already open — caught only by a lucky git status. Give each delegation a liveness fence: at dispatch, stamp a run-token into the tree/bundle; on turn-end, a reaper checks for any tree mutation carrying no live run-token (or a stale one) and quarantines it loudly instead of trusting a clean-looking 'done'. Pair with an auto commit-on-gate-pass so the orchestrator's work is never exposed to a late writer. The kernel even if full fencing is heavy: a cheap end-of-turn 'unexpected-write detector' keyed on delegation tokens.
basis: LEARNINGS {#delegate-orphan-late-write}:337-345 — orphan ran ~72 min, appended to tests/test_team_execution_plugin.py after PR #303 opened, 'caught by a routine git status; discarded with git restore', mechanism: 'a delegate launched as a session teammate can spawn descendants whose lifetime is decoupled from the orchestrator's turn.' No binding decision crossed; reinforces sole-committer posture. Distinct from the direct-to-candidate worktree write-routing seed (that is Edit-after-worktree-removal; this is late-orphan write detection).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a delegation run-token + an end-of-turn reaper/unexpected-write detector (saga or team-execution script) that quarantines untokened tree mutations, with a test simulating a post-dispatch write landing without a live token and asserting it is flagged not trusted. Verified by the detector surfacing the injected late write.

title: Append-only chain-of-custody ledger linking every bridge proof to its merged commit
idea: Flip to 'nothing about a delegation can ever be un-said or overwritten.' Beyond making a single evidence file read-only (already a direct-to-candidate seed), build a tamper-evident chain-of-custody: extend the existing provenance_manifest/manifest_store seam into an append-only ledger where each delegation writes a hash-linked entry (task packet hash -> proof classification -> bundle path -> resulting commit sha), each entry referencing the prior entry's digest. A later PASS can never silently replace an earlier FAIL because both are chained and the break is detectable. /retro and release gates can then walk the chain to reconstruct 'who really did what' without forensic transcript archaeology. The kernel: chaining, not just immutability — the audit trail proves ORDER and non-replacement, not merely that one file didn't change.
basis: engine_dispatch.py imports provenance_manifest and manifest_store (existing seam, extend not invent — respects {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}). Grounding brief 7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'; brief explicitly names 'evidence-artifact immutability' as the narrow direct-to-candidate — this idea deliberately exceeds it with hash-chaining and cross-bridge linkage. LEARNINGS {#agy-delegate-silent-claude-fallback} shows provenance was reconstructed forensically, which a durable chain removes.
outcome_shape: Merged PR extending plugins/saga/scripts/provenance_manifest.py + manifest_store.py with an append-only hash-linked delegation ledger (prev-digest per entry, task-hash -> classification -> commit-sha), plus a chain-verify command and tests where replacing an earlier entry breaks verification. Verified by the verify command failing on a tampered/overwritten entry.

title: Every-issue-self-executing flip: a bridge is 'wired' only if producer AND consumer both fired
idea: Flip to 'assume every bridge is dead-wired until both ends prove live.' The dead-wiring lessons show a seam can pass tests while one leg is inert — a producer with no consumer, or an e2e-green consumer whose persisted leg is a no-op. Apply that framing directly to delegation bridges: define a bridge-liveness assertion that fails loud unless a real producer (a launched engine invocation, per the proof record) AND a real consumer (the output actually read/committed/attributed downstream) both fire on the same run. A serializer slot, an unread result.json, or an engine that launched-but-nothing-consumed each trip the assertion. The kernel: the two-axis dead-wiring test, generalized from saga fields to cross-plugin delegation, closes the 'looked delegated, was inert' class end-to-end through the real entrypoint.
basis: LEARNINGS {#dead-wiring-needs-producer-and-consumer}:471-481 'A field is live only when a real producer writes it AND a real consumer reads it... Test the seam end-to-end through the real entrypoint, not via a fixture that fabricates the on-disk shape'; {#test-shape-masks-dead-wiring-291}:92 'An e2e test can be green while a persisted-field consumer leg is a no-op.' Applies to the delegation bridge, not a saga field. Distinct from T15-F6-3 (resolver Claude-substitution) — this catches the both-ends-inert case. No binding decision crossed.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a producer-and-consumer bridge-liveness assertion (in bridge_proof.py or the dispatch consumer path) + an end-to-end test through the real dispatch entrypoint proving a launched-but-unconsumed result and a consumed-but-unlaunched result both fail. Verified by both negative fixtures tripping the assertion.

title: Zero operators watching: a fleet-wide continuous delegation-integrity monitor in CI
idea: Flip to 'no human will ever eyeball a git status again' — full autonomy, so the machine must catch every silent no-op unattended. Add a CI job (and a scheduled sweep) that walks all harness transcripts / proof bundles produced in a run across every bridge (agy, codex, saga spawns, team-execution workers) and asserts fleet-wide invariants: every 'delegated' unit has a launched=true proof, every fallback is recorded, no orphan write lacks a token, no ledger chain is broken. It is the audit_harness_transcript.py idea promoted from a manual release ritual to an always-on, all-bridge gate — because the intake's unattended/overnight runs (/outcome, /loop) are exactly where a silent no-op ships unseen. The kernel: continuous, cross-bridge integrity enforcement rather than per-plugin, human-triggered spot checks.
basis: audit_harness_transcript.py exists but is invoked by hand (plugins/agy/docs/harness-proof.md 'Audit command' run manually at release). Intake brief 22-32: unattended /outcome and /loop runs 'may proceed silently' — the exact context a silent no-op ships unwatched. Grounding brief 6.1 names 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings)' as theme 15's core. Delivered as CI + a shared audit script, not a new plugin ({#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} honored).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a .github/workflows delegation-integrity job + a fleet-audit script that aggregates all bridge proof bundles/transcripts in a run and fails on any un-launched delegation, unrecorded fallback, untokened orphan write, or broken ledger chain, with a fixture run exercising each failure. Verified by CI red on a seeded silent-no-op transcript.

title: OpenAI-compatible HTTP bridge + substrate-keyed dispatch adapter table
idea: Today `_build_invocation` (engine_dispatch.py:323-327) hardcodes an if-ladder for `codex`/`agy` and raises `DispatchError` for any other engine, while `invocation.via` can only name marketplace-plugin recipes (`codex:codex-rescue`, `agy:delegate`) -- so Ollama and DeepSeek, which both speak the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` shape, have no path in. Add ONE bridge script `plugins/saga/scripts/engine_bridge_http.py` plus a `substrate`-keyed adapter table that replaces the if-ladder, so a registry row with `invocation.via: saga:http-bridge`, an `endpoint`, and a `model` dispatches uniformly and returns the unchanged `AdvisoryEvidence(status/output)` contract. The Ollama adapter reads `/api/show` to honor the row's `context_window` against the daemon's actually-served `num_ctx`, so a local model quantized to a smaller window HALTs instead of silently truncating. Bridge output stays advisory-only with `write_capable:false`, so a provider never becomes a gatekeeper -- #external-engines-never-gatekeepers (#283) is not crossed and its revisit-when is not triggered -- and the whole thing lives inside saga's existing seam, minting no new plugin (serves #plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7).
basis: engine_dispatch.py:327 `raise DispatchError(f"unsupported external engine {resolution.engine_id!r}")` sitting under the hardcoded codex/agy branches at 323-326, plus engine_resolver.py:22-25 `ENGINE_CLI = {"agy":"agy","codex":"codex"}` -- the seam structurally admits only two CLI-plugin engines and refuses a third.
outcome_shape: PR touching engine_dispatch.py (`_build_invocation` -> substrate-keyed adapter dict), new `plugins/saga/scripts/engine_bridge_http.py`, engine-registry.yaml (Ollama + DeepSeek rows), and tests. Verified by a dispatch unit test that runs an Ollama row through a fake HTTP runner and asserts a byte-identical AdvisoryEvidence shape, plus an availability-gated live smoke against localhost:11434 that records status:ok.

title: Provider credential-resolution model (env/secret-ref) with secret redaction
idea: `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` (engine_resolver.py:27-36) hardcodes agy/codex dotfile locations and `_default_config_exists` (resolver:140-142) treats 'a config file exists' as 'authenticated' -- but an API-key provider like DeepSeek authenticates from an env var or secret manager with no dotfile, and local Ollama needs no auth at all. Add a per-row `auth:` block (`kind: none|env|config-file|command`, `env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `probe`) parsed into `EngineEntry`, and a `resolve_credentials(entry)` in engine_resolver that returns availability plus a REDACTED source label and never emits the secret value into provenance or logs. `preflight` consults it instead of the hardcoded path map. This is what actually unblocks 'DeepSeek -> cheap second opinion' (needs a key present) and 'Ollama -> $0' (needs none) without a new plugin, and keeps the existing halt-on-unavailable behavior honest for credential-shaped providers.
basis: engine_resolver.py:27-36 `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS = {"agy": (...), "codex": (...)}` plus `_default_config_exists` at resolver:140-142 -- availability is modeled as dotfile-existence for exactly two named engines, with no env-var or secret-ref concept that an API-key provider requires.
outcome_shape: PR touching engine_registry.py (EngineEntry gains `auth`), engine_resolver.py (`resolve_credentials` + preflight rewire), engine-registry.yaml (DeepSeek row with `auth.kind: env`), and tests. Verified by a unit test asserting a missing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY yields `available:False` with a reason, plus a redaction test that greps the emitted preflight/provenance output and asserts the key VALUE never appears.

title: Measured cost/latency dispatch ledger + cost_speed_rank drift report
idea: The registry header (engine-registry.yaml:1-9) admits `cost_speed_rank` is hand-authored seed data 're-validated by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop', and `build_dispatch_manifest` (engine_dispatch.py:163-202) records status/disposition but zero tokens, latency, or dollars -- so nobody can answer what a dispatch actually cost or whether 'Ollama is the $0 offload target' is even true. Extend the manifest/AdvisoryEvidence with a measured `usage` block (prompt+completion tokens, wall-ms, computed $ from a per-provider price table in the registry) that the HTTP bridge populates from the provider response, persisted per dispatch. Add `engine_cost_report.py` that aggregates the ledger and FLAGS any row whose measured cost/latency ordering contradicts its authored `cost_speed_rank`. It reports drift for human/Claude review; it never auto-reorders, so `cost_speed_rank` stays an authored ordered ladder per #tier-vocab-ordering.
basis: engine-registry.yaml:6 `... re-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by an automated measurement loop`, and the manifest Attribution (engine_dispatch.py:189-197) carrying kind/identity/effort/protocol/sandbox but no token/latency/cost field -- the seam has no measured cost surface at all.
outcome_shape: PR touching provenance_manifest.py (typed `usage` block), engine_dispatch.py (populate usage from the runner result), a per-provider price table in engine-registry.yaml, new `plugins/saga/scripts/engine_cost_report.py`, and tests. Verified by feeding two fake dispatches with known token counts and asserting the report computes the right $ and flags an inverted-rank fixture as drift.

title: Policy-driven recommend() -- ranked provider routing with free-first / cheapest-viable
idea: `by_capability` (engine_registry.py:336-352) returns exactly ONE winner (min by rating -> cost_speed_rank -> registry_order) and exposes no rationale -- so the intake's 'Ollama -> $0 offload target; DeepSeek -> cheap second opinion' cannot be expressed, because that is a COST POLICY over the same capability, not a different capability. Add `recommend(capability, policy)` with policy in {best-quality, cheapest-viable, free-first}, returning a ranked candidate list, each with a one-line rationale (rating, rank, why-not-chosen), and a `min_rating` floor so free-first never routes a WEAK provider. The recommendation is advisory input to the chaperone-dispatch split (#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch #318: offload -> cheap, second-opinion -> strong): it makes the PROVIDER pick inside that posture explicit and reproducible while Claude/operator still decides, so no provider becomes an executor kind, a residency, or a gatekeeper -- the decision is engaged, not crossed.
basis: engine_registry.py:346-352 `return min(candidates, key=lambda entry: (-_RATING_SCORE[...], entry.cost_speed_rank, entry.registry_order))` -- a single-winner selector with no policy input and no top-N/rationale, so a $0-preferred offload cannot be routed differently from a best-quality pick.
outcome_shape: PR touching engine_registry.py (`recommend` alongside `by_capability`), a new `plugins/saga/references/routing-policy.md`, and tests over a fixture registry. Verified by unit tests asserting free-first prefers an Ollama MODERATE row over a DeepSeek/codex pick for an offload capability, refuses to return a WEAK row under free-first, and best-quality stays byte-identical to today's `by_capability`.

title: Provider-onboarding scaffolder + registry conformance CI gate
idea: Adding a provider today means hand-authoring a registry row with every closed-vocab capability key, prompting_protocol, sources, cost_speed_rank, context_window, last_validated, and model_identity, AND extending `_build_invocation`, AND wiring preflight/auth -- with no template and no pre-flight check that the row is well-formed before a live run. Ship `tools/add-engine.sh <engine_id> <variant>` that emits a registry-row stub plus a bridge skeleton, and `tests/test_engine_registry_conformance.py` (backed by the existing `Registry.validate()`) that every row must pass in CI: all capabilities present, sources non-empty, `auth` block valid, and `invocation.via` resolvable to a known adapter. This turns onboarding from tribal knowledge into a checklist + gate, and by making a correct registry row cheap it directly serves the consolidation posture (#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7): providers stay rows, not new plugins.
basis: First-principles from the onboarding surface: `EngineEntry.from_dict` (engine_registry.py:187-231) requires ten-plus fields per row, `_build_invocation` needs a matching adapter branch, and `preflight` needs an availability model -- three files, no scaffold, no conformance test, and the only current safety net is a live-run failure. The marginal cost of a correct row is the exact lever that decides whether a contributor adds a row or reaches for a new plugin; lowering it is what makes 'registry-driven, one router' actually hold as the provider set grows.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tools/add-engine.sh`, `tests/test_engine_registry_conformance.py`, and `plugins/saga/references/adding-a-provider.md`. Verified by running the scaffolder for a fake `deepseek/chat`, asserting the emitted row passes conformance, and asserting a deliberately-broken row (missing capability, empty sources) fails it with a precise message.

title: Dispatch-adapter contract + fake-runner no-op guard
idea: The repo's #1 recurring journal pain is silent no-ops in delegation and dead wiring (agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, fake-adapter mismatch), and a new HTTP bridge is exactly the adapter that can be registered-but-never-called or return a fake-shaped result that mismatches the real provider. Write `plugins/saga/references/dispatch-adapter-contract.md` fixing the exact runner input/output schema (`{status, output, usage?}`, the `FAILURE_STATUSES` vocabulary, byte-preservation of the payload) and ship a shared `FakeHttpRunner` plus a contract test every adapter must pass -- including a 'did it actually reach the network' liveness assertion on the smoke path, so a wired-but-dead bridge fails loudly instead of silently downgrading to Claude. This hardens every current and future provider adapter against the precise failure mode the journal already burned on, before the fleet grows more of them.
basis: Grounding brief section 6 finding 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings: agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter mismatch) -- any bridge/delegation idea needs "did it actually run/persist" verification', and the only current adapter contract is the undocumented `FAILURE_STATUSES` frozenset at engine_dispatch.py:18.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/dispatch-adapter-contract.md`, a shared `FakeHttpRunner` test double, and `tests/test_dispatch_adapter_contract.py`. Verified by the contract test failing a deliberately dead adapter (returns without ever touching its runner) and passing a conformant one, plus a liveness assertion exercised on the smoke path.

title: Automated provider-benchmark harness proposing registry rating/cost updates
idea: The registry header explicitly chose manual re-validation ('re-validated by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop'), a stance seeded 2026-06-27 for two slow-moving CLI engines -- but Ollama tags and DeepSeek versions churn weekly, so manual /retro cannot keep capability_profile ratings or cost_speed_rank honest for local/API providers. Build a scheduled `engine_benchmark.py` that runs a small fixed eval suite per capability against each provider variant, measures pass-rate + tokens + latency + $ via the cost ledger, and emits a DIFF PROPOSAL against engine-registry.yaml (rating changes, rank reorderings, last_validated bumps). Critically it never auto-commits: it proposes, and Claude/operator adjudicates the diff -- preserving #external-engines-never-gatekeepers (#283: the harness is a generator of evidence, not a decider) and #tier-vocab-ordering (rank stays an authored ladder a human approves). This is the automated measurement loop the seam deliberately deferred, now earning its keep because the provider set it routes over is no longer slow-moving.
basis: engine-registry.yaml:3-6 SEED DATA note: 'The architecture does not depend on any cell being eternally correct -- last_validated (R3) makes staleness visible, and the data is re-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by an automated measurement loop.' I engage that stance directly: it was set for codex/agy, but local/API providers churn far faster, so an evidence-proposing (never auto-committing) loop is the honest evolution that keeps last_validated from silently rotting.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/engine_benchmark.py`, a per-capability eval-suite fixture, and `plugins/saga/references/benchmark-loop.md` documenting the propose-not-commit gate. Verified by running the harness against a fake provider whose measured rating contradicts its authored one and asserting it emits a registry diff PROPOSAL (not a write) that a human/Claude step must approve before it lands.

title: Per-provider budget ceiling with halt-not-overspend
idea: DeepSeek and other API-key providers cost real money per call, yet the seam's only dispatch ceilings are context-window (`_context_window_halt`, engine_resolver.py:353-360) and preflight availability -- there is no spend concept anywhere (`cost_speed_rank` is an ordinal, not dollars), so a misrouted fan-out (the intake's Phase-D cost-blowout pre-mortem, and the mined '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting') could quietly rack up API charges. Add a per-row `budget:` (max $/dispatch, max $/day) enforced by the HTTP bridge against the measured usage ledger: when a dispatch's projected or cumulative cost would breach the ceiling, HALT visibly with a 'budget ceiling $X reached' note that routes back to Claude -- never silently downgrade AND never silently overspend. This applies the seam's existing halt-not-degrade posture, and the /outcome campaign's 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact', to money.
basis: First-principles: the registry encodes cost only as the ordinal `cost_speed_rank` (engine-registry.yaml:8-9), and the dispatch path's sole ceilings are `_context_window_halt` (resolver:353-360) and preflight availability -- so an API-key provider has an unbounded-spend surface the seam never guards, which is exactly the Phase-D cost-blowout pre-mortem left unmitigated at the provider layer. The seam already halts-not-degrades on context and availability; extending the same posture to a measured dollar ceiling is the minimal consistent fix.
outcome_shape: PR touching engine-registry.yaml (per-row `budget`), engine_bridge_http.py / engine_dispatch.py (ledger-backed ceiling check that emits a HALT resolution), and tests. Verified by a unit test that drives cumulative fake usage past a $/day ceiling and asserts the next dispatch HALTs with a budget note and falls back to Claude rather than calling the provider.

title: Kill the CLI-only invocation assumption: a transport discriminator + one generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP bridge
idea: Today every engine row is a shell recipe (`invocation.via`/`recipe`, validated as required strings) and `preflight` resolves availability with `shutil.which` against ENGINE_CLI. Ollama and DeepSeek have no CLI binary, so they cannot even be expressed. Invert the contract: add an `invocation.transport` discriminator (`cli` | `http`) to the registry schema and ship ONE generic bridge script speaking the OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` shape that both Ollama (`/v1`) and DeepSeek already implement. A new HTTP provider then becomes a registry row plus a base_url, never a new script. HTTP rows stay `write_capable: false` worker/generator/advisory-reviewer only so Claude remains verifier-of-record.
basis: engine_resolver.py:22-25 `ENGINE_CLI` + line 55 `which=shutil.which` make preflight CLI-only; engine_registry.py:197-199 `_require_string(invocation,'via')`/`'recipe'` force a shell recipe with no HTTP representation. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): the new http transport dispatches only non-gated worker/generator/advisory roles, Claude stays verifier-of-record, so no gatekeeper crossing.
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py (schema: `transport` enum on invocation), plugins/saga/scripts/http_bridge.py (new generic OpenAI-compatible bridge), plugins/saga/references/engine-registry.yaml (one ollama row + one deepseek row), and tests/test_engine_registry.py. Verified by a unit test that loads a transport:http row and by a live `preflight`+dispatch against a local Ollama returning a completion.

title: Availability without a paid call: HTTP preflight that halts (not silently degrades) for advisory/panel roles
idea: `preflight` promises 'cheap engine availability without live API calls' but only knows how to check a CLI binary and a config file's existence. For HTTP providers, invert the manual 'is the endpoint up?' guesswork into a typed, no-cost probe: Ollama exposes a free local `GET /api/tags`; DeepSeek availability is decided purely on env-key presence, never a billed completion. Wire these into `preflight` so the existing HALT_ROLE_KINDS path (advisory-reviewer/panel) halts the whole panel when an HTTP provider is down rather than substituting Claude, preserving HALT-not-degrade. Removes the step where an operator discovers a dead provider only mid-dispatch.
basis: engine_resolver.py:57-58 preflight docstring 'Return cheap engine availability without live API calls'; line 20 `HALT_ROLE_KINDS = frozenset({'advisory-reviewer','panel'})`. Engages the /outcome U1-U11 binding decision (HALT-not-degrade): the HTTP probe must halt panels, never silently downgrade, and must stay zero-cost, so no billed liveness call.
outcome_shape: Merged PR extending preflight() in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_resolver.py with a transport-aware availability branch + a `preflight_http()` helper, plus tests/test_engine_resolver.py cases asserting (a) Ollama-down yields halt for a panel member and (b) DeepSeek missing key yields halt without any network call (mocked to raise if called). Verified by those tests passing.

title: Automate away the hand-authored provider row: a scaffold generator that emits an UNVERIFIED draft PR
idea: Onboarding a provider today means hand-writing an ~40-line YAML row (7-capability profile, sources, protocol, cost_speed_rank, context_window) and getting the closed-vocabulary schema exactly right. Remove the blank-page step: `scaffold_provider.py <engine_id> --base-url ... --model ...` probes the OpenAI-compatible `/models`, stubs a full capability_profile at a conservative rating, tags every source `UNVERIFIED`, sets last_validated to today, and opens a PR. Crucially it does NOT benchmark or assert real ratings; it produces a draft whose ratings are confirmed by use through /retro, honoring the registry's explicit 'not an automated measurement loop' design.
basis: engine-registry.yaml header comment (lines 3-6): 'SEED DATA... re-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by an automated measurement loop.' The scaffold therefore emits UNVERIFIED stubs requiring human/`/retro` confirmation rather than an authoritative auto-rating loop, engaging that revisit condition instead of crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/scaffold_provider.py + tests/test_scaffold_provider.py. Verified by running the generator against a local Ollama and confirming the emitted row passes `Registry.load().validate()` and carries `corroboration: UNVERIFIED` sources plus today's last_validated.

title: Remove the manual schema-review step: run Registry.validate() on engine-registry.yaml in CI
idea: `Registry.load()`/`validate()` already enforce the full closed-vocabulary schema (unique variants, one default per engine, role members exist, all capabilities present) but nothing runs them in CI, so a malformed provider row is caught only by a human reviewer or at runtime. Automate the review away: a CI job (and a pre-commit hook) that loads the registry and fails the build on any RegistryError. This makes provider onboarding cheaper because the schema polices itself, and it closes the same class of drift that bit the marketplace registry. Distinct from the marketplace-ci-guard seed, which guards marketplace.json, not the engine registry.
basis: engine_registry.py:305 `def validate(self)` and :273 `Registry.load` exist and raise RegistryError on schema violations, yet CLAUDE.md 'Running Quality Checks' and the CI scope reference no engine-registry lint. This builds beyond {#marketplace-ci-guard} (grounding s5), which targets .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, a different file.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `validate-engine-registry` step to the repo CI workflow (.github/workflows) + a tests/test_engine_registry_lint.py that calls Registry.load on the real references/engine-registry.yaml. Verified by CI going red when a deliberately broken row is pushed and green once fixed.

title: No more hand-picking an engine: auto-render the capability fit-matrix and feed /plan + team-execution
idea: `by_capability()` already computes the best engine per capability (rating dominates, then cost_speed_rank, then registry order), but the team-execution worker table in external-engine-workers.md is hand-maintained, so operators still reason about task-provider fit manually and the doc drifts from the code. Invert it: a `engine_resolver.py --recommend <capability>` command plus a generated fit-matrix reference rendered directly from the registry, consumed by /plan's unit tier table and team-execution's Step A7 worker table. The recommendation is advisory-only (Claude reconciles) and respects chaperone-dispatch shapes: offload leans cheap providers, second-opinion leans the strongest-rated. The hand-authored step is removed.
basis: engine_registry.py:336-353 `by_capability()` computes best-fit deterministically; team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md is hand-maintained (grounding s1 corrections: rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table). Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318): recommendations map offload->cheap and second-opinion->strongest, never introducing a second executor kind.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `--recommend` subcommand to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_resolver.py, a generated plugins/saga/references/engine-fit-matrix.md, and a generator invoked in CI to assert the checked-in matrix is not stale. Verified by a test comparing generated-vs-committed matrix and by /plan referencing the matrix.

title: Delete the credential dance: env-var-first resolver, Ollama as zero-auth default, redaction guard on the bridge
idea: `_default_config_exists` and ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS decide availability purely by whether fixed files exist (`~/.codex/auth.json`), which cannot express API-key providers keyed on env vars (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, OLLAMA_HOST). Invert the auth step for the common case and automate the rest: make Ollama the zero-auth $0 offload default so the most-used offload path needs no secret at all, and add a per-provider credential resolver that accepts env-var OR file, reports a typed missing-credential reason from `preflight --explain` without a live call, and passes the key only via request headers with a redaction guard that forbids interpolating any secret into the logged `recipe`/payload string.
basis: engine_resolver.py:27-36 `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` and :140-142 `_default_config_exists` are file-existence-only, with no env-var path; DeepSeek/Ollama credentials are env-var-based, so they are unrepresentable today. Ties to grounding s6 recurring-pain 1 (silent no-ops) by requiring a redaction guard so a leaked/interpolated key cannot masquerade as a working dispatch.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a credential-resolver + `preflight --explain` to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_resolver.py, an Ollama zero-auth default row in references/engine-registry.yaml, and tests/test_engine_resolver.py asserting (a) missing DEEPSEEK_API_KEY yields a redacted 'missing credential' reason and (b) no secret ever appears in the assembled payload. Verified by those tests.

title: Stop hand-seeding cost_speed_rank: let the HTTP bridge emit measured latency/cost as leaf facts
idea: cost_speed_rank is a hand-maintained integer explicitly flagged as 'SEED DATA, not a permanent ranking' and is the sole tie-break between equally-rated providers, so a wrong seed silently misroutes offload. Invert the guesswork into observation: have the HTTP bridge emit measured wall-clock latency and token cost per dispatch as leaf-produced facts (matching the /outcome cost-ledger discipline), accumulated into a telemetry sidecar the tie-break can read. This does not auto-rewrite capability ratings, honoring 'not an automated measurement loop'; it surfaces the accumulated evidence into /retro so a human confirms the re-rank, turning the tie-break from a guess into a re-validated fact.
basis: engine-registry.yaml comment (lines 8-9): 'cost_speed_rank is the KTD9 tie-break key... SEED DATA... not a permanent ranking.' Engages the /outcome U1-U11 decision (cost ledger = leaf-produced fact) and the 'NOT an automated measurement loop' revisit-when: telemetry informs /retro's human re-validation, it does not auto-mutate ratings.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding per-dispatch latency/cost emission to plugins/saga/scripts/http_bridge.py, a telemetry sidecar reader consulted by cost_speed_rank tie-breaks, and a /retro reference that surfaces the accumulated deltas. Verified by a test that dispatches twice and asserts the sidecar records monotonic call counts + measured latency, and that ratings remain untouched.

title: Remove the blind offload: a break-even guard that halts an external dispatch that isn't actually cheaper than Claude
idea: The intake posture is that any spend-increasing choice needs an explicit operator yes and cache-first is the only silent default, yet nothing checks whether routing to an external provider actually beats just using Claude for a given payload size. Automate the spend decision: a break-even guard that, using the telemetry sidecar's measured cost+latency, compares the external dispatch against the Claude-equivalent and halts (surfacing the recommendation + cheaper fallback) when the offload is not cheaper. This inverts the current implicit 'external is assumed cheaper' into a checked fact, and makes DeepSeek/Ollama routing self-justifying rather than faith-based.
basis: Intake brief tension 1: 'any spend-increasing choice... always requires an explicit operator yes. Cache-first is the only silent default'; tension 4: 'every Fable-tier line... carries a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback; expensive is never a silent default.' The guard encodes that lever at the router seam instead of leaving offload cost unverified.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a break-even check to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_resolver.py (or http_bridge.py) that reads the telemetry sidecar and returns a halt+recommendation Resolution when external is not cheaper, plus tests/test_engine_resolver.py asserting a small payload routes to a halt-with-cheaper-fallback and a large one proceeds. Verified by those tests.

title: Generic OpenAI-compatible `via` bridge kind — a provider is a registry row, not a plugin
idea: Today every `invocation.via` value is a Claude Code plugin skill (`codex:codex-rescue`, `agy:delegate`), silently making 'add a provider' mean 'author a plugin.' Break that: add a second `via` dispatch kind, `bridge:openai-compat`, backed by one new bridge script `plugins/saga/scripts/openai_bridge.py` that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions protocol against a per-row `base_url`. Ollama (`localhost:11434/v1`), DeepSeek (`api.deepseek.com`), and any API-key provider then onboard as pure registry rows with zero new plugin. This is the load-bearing move that makes 'one router plugin, registry-driven' true rather than aspirational, and it is the answer to the consolidation burden of proof.
basis: engine-registry.yaml:27,57,83,113 — all four `via` values are plugin skills; engine_registry.py:197 validates `via` only as a non-empty string, so a `bridge:*` indirection is schema-compatible today. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} revisit: a bridge collapses N providers into 1 plugin + N data rows, which is the consolidation the decision demands rather than violates.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/openai_bridge.py`, a `bridge_kind` branch in engine_resolver.py dispatch, and one Ollama + one DeepSeek row in engine-registry.yaml; verified by a new tests/test_openai_bridge.py asserting a mocked chat-completions round-trip produces a valid U2 Resolution and that `resolve()` routes a `bridge:openai-compat` row without a plugin skill present.

title: Provider-declared preflight — kill the hardcoded 2-engine, file-on-disk availability model
idea: `preflight()` treats availability as a closed problem: `ENGINE_CLI` and `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` are hardcoded to only agy and codex, and `_default_config_exists` only checks `path.exists()`. That silently assumes every engine is a CLI whose auth is a file on disk — false for an API-key provider (DeepSeek authenticates from `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the env) and for a local daemon (Ollama is available iff `GET /api/tags` returns 200). Reframe availability as provider-declared: add a `preflight` block per registry row with a kind (`cli-config` | `env-var` | `http-health`) so each provider states how it proves it is reachable, and the resolver dispatches on that instead of a hardcoded map.
basis: engine_resolver.py:22-36 hardcodes ENGINE_CLI/ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS to agy+codex only; engine_resolver.py:140-142 `_default_config_exists` checks only `path.exists()`. Neither can represent env-var auth or a live health endpoint, which are the exact auth shapes DeepSeek and Ollama require.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `preflight` schema block to EngineEntry (engine_registry.py) with three kinds and a dispatcher in engine_resolver.py replacing the hardcoded dicts; verified by tests/ cases: env-var-present→available, env-var-absent→unavailable-with-reason, and a mocked http-health 200/connection-refused pair.

title: Widen the capability vocabulary to what local models are actually for
idea: CAPABILITIES is a closed 7-value set (code-generation, adversarial-review, second-opinion, debug, refactor, scaffold, long-form-writing) — every one of them a frontier-Claude-competitor task. That framing structurally hides the real $0-offload value of a local model: bulk cheap work. Add capability classes `bulk-classification`, `structured-extraction`, and `embedding` to the vocabulary so Ollama can register a STRONG profile on the work it genuinely wins, and task-provider-fit routing can send high-volume mechanical passes to $0 instead of forcing everything through a frontier-shaped lens. The closed vocab is a choice, not a law of the harness.
basis: engine_registry.py:13-21 CAPABILITIES is a 7-value closed tuple, all frontier-competitor tasks; engine-registry.yaml:11-18 mirrors it. Nothing represents high-volume cheap-mechanical work, which is precisely the intake's stated Ollama role ('$0 offload target'). Per-engine `capability_profile` is already allowed to be partial (_parse_capability_profile needs only ≥1), so new capabilities add no burden to existing rows.
outcome_shape: PR extending CAPABILITIES in engine_registry.py + engine-registry.yaml with the three cheap-bulk capabilities and an Ollama row rating them, plus a references/engine-dispatch.md note on when to route bulk work local; verified by a tests/ case asserting `by_capability('bulk-classification')` resolves to the local row and existing 7-capability tests still pass.

title: Make cost_speed_rank earned, not guessed — a dispatch telemetry sink
idea: The registry header openly admits cost_speed_rank is 'SEED DATA... re-validated by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop.' That is a defensible bootstrap, but it treats a measurable quantity as a permanent human guess. With metered DeepSeek and $0 Ollama in the fleet, cost and latency are directly observable at every dispatch. Add an append-only JSONL telemetry sink written by the bridge on each call (engine_id, variant, capability, tokens_in/out, wall_ms, est_cost_usd) plus a small `rank_report` reducer, so /retro re-ranks cost_speed_rank from real evidence instead of vibes. This closes the measurement loop the header explicitly left open.
basis: engine-registry.yaml:1-9 — 'cost_speed_rank is the KTD9 tie-break key' and the file states re-validation is 'by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop'; the seam is named as deliberately-open in the source. Does not cross {#worker-cache-scheduling} (that governs residency/segments, not per-call cost facts).
outcome_shape: PR adding telemetry emission to the dispatch path (openai_bridge.py / engine_resolver.py) and a `plugins/saga/scripts/rank_report.py` reducer, plus a docs/ note wiring it into /retro; verified by a tests/ case asserting a simulated dispatch appends a well-formed JSONL row and rank_report aggregates two rows into a per-variant median-latency + total-cost table.

title: `provider onboard` scaffolder + golden contract-test — turn a plugin task into data entry
idea: Onboarding a provider today is tribal knowledge: know the recipe string, hand-write a prompting_protocol, guess ratings, remember last_validated. Reframe onboarding cost as a single command: `saga provider onboard <base_url>` probes the endpoint's model list, scaffolds a registry row with placeholder ratings and `last_validated: today`, and immediately runs a golden contract-test that dispatches a fixed prompt through the bridge and asserts the U2 Resolution round-trips. The consolidation burden of proof from the plugin-groom decision is only payable if provider N+1 is near-zero marginal cost — this is the machinery that makes it so.
basis: First-principles: {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} makes any new-plugin proposal owe a consolidation burden of proof; a router plugin only discharges that burden if adding a provider is cheaper than adding a plugin. Onboarding currently requires authoring a recipe + protocol + ratings by hand (see the four hand-authored rows in engine-registry.yaml), which is plugin-authoring-grade effort. A scaffolder+contract-test converts it into probe-then-verify data entry, collapsing the marginal cost and making 'one router plugin' provably non-sprawling.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/provider_onboard.py` (endpoint probe → scaffolded row) and a reusable golden contract-test in tests/test_provider_contract.py parametrized over registry rows; verified by running the contract-test against a mocked OpenAI-compatible endpoint and asserting a scaffolded row validates against Registry.from_dict.

title: Cheapest-sufficient escalation ladder instead of single-best routing
idea: `by_capability` returns exactly one engine — `min(...)` over rating-then-cost. That bakes in 'routing = pick the single best,' which is wrong once a $0 tier exists: for non-gated offload work the right move is try Ollama, escalate to DeepSeek on a failed quality-bar, then Claude. Add `by_capability_ladder(capability) -> list[EngineEntry]` ordered cheapest-sufficient→strongest, and a resolver `ladder` mode that walks it with a caller-supplied acceptance predicate. This applies strictly to worker/generator (non-gated) dispatch; Claude stays verifier-of-record, so it does not touch the gatekeeper boundary.
basis: engine_registry.py:346-353 `by_capability` returns a single `min(...)` entry. {#tier-vocab-ordering} binding: tier tuples are ordered escalation ladders, not just closed sets — so a ladder resolver is the aligned extension of the existing tie-break ordering, not a new concept. {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} is respected because the ladder runs only for FALLBACK_ROLE_KINDS (worker/generator), never advisory-reviewer/panel gated roles.
outcome_shape: PR adding `by_capability_ladder` to engine_registry.py and a `ladder` resolve mode in engine_resolver.py gated to FALLBACK_ROLE_KINDS; verified by a tests/ case asserting the ladder for a capability is ordered cheapest→strongest and that a predicate rejecting the cheap tier escalates to the next entry, while advisory-reviewer requests still get single-entry HALT semantics.

title: An egress axis — route sensitive context to local-only, not just to cheap
idea: The registry's `substrate` enum ('external' | 'in-repo') models where the engine's *code* lives, never where the *data* goes. But the whole reason to add Ollama beyond price is that context never leaves the host, while DeepSeek ships it to a third-party API. Add an `egress` field per row (`local-only` | `third-party-api`) and a per-dispatch data-classification gate so a task tagged sensitive can only resolve to `local-only` engines. Without this, quietly adding cloud API providers silently expands the fleet's data-egress surface with nothing in the schema able to honor 'this must not leave the machine.'
basis: First-principles: engine-registry.yaml `substrate` values are external/in-repo — a code-provenance axis. Egress (localhost vs third-party network) is an orthogonal, unmodeled property: Ollama is localhost/no-egress, DeepSeek is a third-party API round-trip. Once T2 introduces API-key cloud providers, every dispatch becomes a data-egress decision the router cannot currently reason about, so the privacy value of the local tier is unrepresentable and un-enforceable. An explicit egress field is the minimal schema change that makes 'route sensitive work local' a routing constraint rather than a hope.
