outcome_shape: PR adding an `egress` field to EngineEntry (engine_registry.py) with validation, a `max_egress` constraint honored in engine_resolver.py resolution, and egress values on all registry rows; verified by a tests/ case asserting a request with max_egress='local-only' HALTs rather than resolving to a third-party-api row, and resolves to the Ollama row.

title: Staleness-to-freshness CI guard — stop passively hoping ratings are current
idea: `Registry.stale()` compares `last_validated` to a `known_revision_dates` dict that nothing populates — staleness detection exists but is inert. As providers multiply, hand-seeded ratings rot invisibly. Add a small `model-releases.yaml` watch file plus a CI check that fails (or annotates) when a registry row's `last_validated` predates a newer known release of its `model_identity`, emitting a /retro re-validation task. This reframes freshness from 'someone will remember to re-benchmark' into a mechanical drift guard — the same release-surface-drift discipline the repo already applies to plugin metadata.
basis: engine_registry.py:377-385 `Registry.stale()` takes a `known_revision_dates` mapping that no caller in the codebase populates, so the staleness API is dead wiring; engine-registry.yaml:3-6 admits data is re-validated only 'by use through /retro' with no automated loop. This mirrors grounding-brief §6.3 ('release-surface drift persists despite CLAUDE.md step 6 — room for automation').
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/model-releases.yaml` and a CI check (script + workflow step) that calls Registry.stale() over the registry and fails on any row stale against a newer known release; verified by a tests/ case with a seeded newer release asserting the check flags exactly the stale row and passes when last_validated is current.

title: One generic OpenAI-compatible HTTP dispatch substrate, so every future provider is a registry row
idea: engine_dispatch.py today hardcodes exactly two dispatch paths keyed on `resolution.engine_id == "codex"` and `== "agy"`, each forwarding to that engine's own wrapper plugin; there is no path for an engine that lacks a wrapper plugin. Ollama, DeepSeek, Together, Groq, and vLLM all speak the identical OpenAI `/v1/chat/completions` contract, so add a single `substrate: http-openai-compatible` dispatch adapter that reads `base_url` + `model_identity` + `auth.api_key_env` from the registry row and returns the same `AdvisoryEvidence(verified_by_claude=False)` the existing paths return. The compounding payoff: onboarding the Nth OpenAI-compatible provider becomes a registry-row-only change against one adapter, not a new keyed branch and not a new wrapper plugin. This deliberately stays inside {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the adapter emits advisory evidence with no gated-verdict field, so `satisfy_gate` still requires a distinct Claude verification stamp exactly as the codex/agy paths do.
basis: engine-dispatch.md: "a wrapper subagent shells out to the engine's CLI" and "team-execution dispatch ... deferred"; engine_dispatch.py dispatches only on `engine_id == "codex"`/`"agy"` (grounding §1 + engine-dispatch.md 'The two dispatch paths'). No HTTP/wrapper-less substrate exists, so Ollama/DeepSeek (intake §5 scope) are currently unroutable. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} revisit-when by keeping write_capable=false + advisory-only, not crossing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `http-openai-compatible` branch to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py, a `substrate`/`base_url` schema extension in plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py, and a new tests/test_saga_engine_http_dispatch.py asserting (a) payload forwarded byte-for-byte, (b) result is AdvisoryEvidence with verified_by_claude False, (c) non-ok HTTP status yields a halt+downgrade note. Verified by the new test suite + a mocked-transport round trip; no live API call in CI.

title: Ollama as the first $0 offload row — proving the http substrate and the local-model chaperone mapping in one landing
idea: Once the generic http substrate (T2-F4-1) exists, register a local Ollama variant as a concrete `engine_id: ollama` row with `substrate: http-openai-compatible`, `base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1`, `cost_speed_rank: 0` (cheaper than every cloud row), and a capability_profile honestly seeded WEAK/MODERATE for offload-class work only. The second-order leverage is that this row is the reference implementation every future local-model row (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM) copies, and it makes `by_capability` tie-breaks actually prefer the free local engine for offload the moment it is installed and preflight-available. Per {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} this row is dispatched offload-intent only, paired with a sonnet/medium chaperone, and is never a residency/git participant — the registry `engine_intent: offload` guard already carries that constraint, so the local model enters strictly as an evidence-returning offload worker.
basis: Intake brief §5 operator statement: "Ollama -> $0 offload target; DeepSeek -> cheap second opinion." Crosses {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318); engaged by registering Ollama as offload-intent only (chaperone = sonnet/medium), evidence-only, no second-executor residency — exactly the decision's offload branch.
outcome_shape: PR adding one `engine_id: ollama` engines[] entry to plugins/saga/references/engine-registry.yaml (with sources + last_validated) plus an ENGINE_CLI/availability entry in engine_resolver.py so preflight reports not-installed when Ollama is absent. Verified by extending tests/test_saga_engine_registry.py::test_shipped_seed_registry_loads_and_resolves to assert the ollama row resolves for an offload capability and its preflight halts cleanly when localhost:11434 is unreachable.

title: An engine-onboarding conformance test that makes a half-wired provider fail CI instead of failing at dispatch
idea: Adding a provider today silently spans four surfaces — the engine-registry.yaml row, a keyed branch in engine_dispatch.py, an ENGINE_CLI/preflight entry in engine_resolver.py, and the capability_profile schema — with nothing asserting they stay in lockstep, so a registry row with no dispatch path resolves fine and then explodes at dispatch: the producer-without-consumer dead-wiring failure class the journal repeatedly burns on. Ship a single parametrized conformance test that iterates every engines[] row and asserts each has a reachable dispatch substrate, a preflight/availability entry, and every capability_profile it advertises is resolvable, plus a `references/engine-onboarding.md` contract that the test is the executable checklist for. The F4 win is that onboarding cost drops from tribal-knowledge archaeology to "make the failing conformance test green," and every future provider inherits the same guarantee for free.
basis: Grounding §6 pattern 1 ("dead-wiring producer+consumer", "test-shape-masks-dead-wiring") and §15 delegation-integrity theme: a registry engine_id with no engine_dispatch.py branch is a producer with no consumer that resolves then fails at dispatch. No existing test cross-checks registry rows against dispatch/preflight coverage (verified: tests/test_saga_engine_registry.py covers schema only).
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_saga_engine_onboarding_conformance.py (parametrized over registry rows, asserting dispatch-path + preflight + capability resolvability coverage) and plugins/saga/references/engine-onboarding.md. Verified by the test going red when a row is added without its dispatch/preflight wiring (demonstrated with a deliberately-partial fixture row).

title: A single recommend() primitive that hands authors the ranked engine AND its prompting protocol at plan time
idea: engine_registry.by_capability already computes the correct rating-dominant, cost_speed_rank-tie-broken pick, but that ranking is invisible to the humans and agents authoring units — the grounding correction confirms engine routing is "absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow." Expose one pure `recommend(capability, intent) -> {engine, variant, rationale, prompting_protocol}` helper and wire that ONE source into three consumers: saga /plan's unit tier table, team-execution's Step A7 worker table, and the doc-review panel, so none of them re-derives fit and all of them auto-inject the provider-specific prompting_protocol lines (e.g. "assign an explicit adversarial role," "reserve xhigh"). The compounding effect: a registry rating change instantly re-routes every consumer, and prompt-quality guidance for each provider stops being copy-pasted lore.
basis: engine_registry.py by_capability() implements the ranked lookup (rating score, then cost_speed_rank, then registry_order) and each row carries a prompting_protocol list; grounding §1 correction (c) states this routing is still "absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow." The ranking primitive exists but is not surfaced to authors.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `recommend()` function + CLI subcommand to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_resolver.py, and edits to plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md and plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md Step A7 to consume it. Verified by a new test asserting recommend() returns the same variant by_capability picks plus the row's verbatim prompting_protocol, and a SKILL.md render check.

title: A registry-declared secret-reference contract with redaction-safe preflight for API-key providers
idea: Preflight today only runs shutil.which on the engine's CLI ("CLI and config present; no live API call made") because codex and agy both authenticate through their own CLI's stored login — there is no notion of an API-key env var, which every HTTP provider (DeepSeek, Together, Groq) needs. Add an `auth` block to the registry schema with two shapes, `auth: cli-managed` (today's engines) and `auth: {api_key_env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}`, and extend preflight to report `not-configured` (reusing the existing halt/downgrade-note machinery) when a declared api_key_env is unset — while structurally guaranteeing the key value is never echoed into a note, log, or ledger. The leverage: every future API-key provider gets uniform "is it configured?" answering and a single audited redaction guarantee, so secret handling is solved once at the seam instead of per provider.
basis: engine_resolver.py preflight (line ~75) reports "available: CLI and config present; no live API call made" and checks only shutil.which(cli) (lines 55-60); there is no env-var/API-key auth path. Current registry rows have no `auth` field. Direct gap for the DeepSeek/API-key providers named in intake §5.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `auth` schema field to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py, extending preflight in engine_resolver.py to surface not-configured on a missing api_key_env, and tests/test_saga_engine_auth_preflight.py asserting (a) missing key -> not-configured halt, (b) present key -> available, (c) the key value never appears in any emitted reason/note string. Verified by the redaction assertion in the new test.

title: Dispatch-fed engine-usage ledger — turn every advisory call into a leaf-produced cost/latency fact
idea: The registry's ratings are seed data explicitly "re-validated by use through /retro, NOT by an automated measurement loop," which means today no call leaves a trace and revalidation is memory-based. Since engine_dispatch already returns AdvisoryEvidence carrying provenance, have it append one append-only JSONL fact per call — engine_id, variant, capability, intent, token-in/out estimate, wall-time, and terminal status — mirroring the /outcome cost-ledger pattern (leaf-produced fact, never committed status). This is the foundational primitive the whole telemetry axis compounds on: with it, /retro and /optimize can point at real corroboration instead of recalled impressions, and downstream routing can eventually become cost-aware. It respects the /outcome campaign binding by making the ledger a produced fact rather than a mutable status field, and stays advisory-only so it touches no gated verdict.
basis: Grounding §2 binding — /outcome campaign: "cost ledger = leaf-produced fact" (the pattern this idea mirrors, not contradicts). engine_dispatch.py already returns AdvisoryEvidence with provenance but persists nothing; engine-registry.yaml comment confirms there is "NOT an automated measurement loop." Engaged by making the ledger append-only leaf-produced facts, never a committed status field (derive-on-read discipline, §6.5).
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only JSONL writer to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py (guarded, disable-by-default flag) and tests/test_saga_engine_ledger.py asserting one well-formed record per dispatch and no record on a short-circuited halt. Verified by the test plus a schema doc line in engine-dispatch.md.

title: Ledger-fed staleness report that arms /retro to revalidate registry ratings from evidence, not recall
idea: This is the compounding second-order payoff of the dispatch ledger (T2-F4-6): a `engine_registry stale-report` reader that joins the usage-fact ledger against the registry's per-row last_validated and corroboration tags, and emits, for each (engine, capability) cell, whether real observed usage now corroborates, contradicts, or has never exercised the seeded rating. That report becomes a first-class /retro input, closing the loop the yaml deliberately left open ("re-validated by use through /retro (R21)") with evidence instead of memory — directly countering the stale-claim-asserted-as-fact pattern the journal keeps catching. The leverage is that the registry stops rotting silently: every dispatch quietly buys down the cost of the next revalidation, and a rating with zero exercised evidence is flagged as pure seed rather than passing as fact.
basis: engine-registry.yaml header comment: "the data is re-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by an automated measurement loop" and last_validated "(R3) makes staleness visible." Grounding §6 pattern 2 / §7 pattern 7: stale-memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by luck. The revalidation hook (last_validated, /retro) exists but has no evidence feed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `stale-report` subcommand to plugins/saga/scripts/engine_registry.py that reads the ledger + registry and emits per-cell corroborated/contradicted/unexercised, plus a bullet in plugins/saga/skills/retro/SKILL.md wiring it as a /retro input. Verified by tests/test_saga_engine_stale_report.py over synthetic ledger+registry fixtures covering all three cell verdicts.

title: Intermodal-container substrate adapters: decouple capability payload from transport (CLI vs HTTP)
idea: Today `preflight()` hard-assumes a binary on PATH (`shutil.which(cli)`, engine_resolver.py:59-60) and `ENGINE_CLI` lists only agy/codex, so an HTTP API-key provider (DeepSeek, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama) is unrepresentable — it has no binary to `which`. Borrowing intermodal shipping containerization, where an ISO container (the payload) rides truck, ship, or rail via a standard corner-casting interface, introduce a `transport` field on each EngineEntry (`cli-subprocess` | `http-openai-compatible` | `http-ollama`) and make `preflight`/dispatch dispatch on transport, not on an implicit binary. The EngineEntry `invocation {via, recipe, write_capable}` payload stays transport-agnostic (the container); only the corner-casting adapter differs. This keeps chaperone-dispatch #318 intact: an HTTP provider is still a dispatch adapter, never a second executor kind, residency, or git participant.
basis: engine_resolver.py:59-60 `if which(cli) is None` and ENGINE_CLI={agy,codex} (lines 21-25) make CLI-on-PATH a structural assumption no HTTP provider can satisfy. Source domain: intermodal freight containerization (ISO 668 corner castings) — a single standardized interface lets one payload ride any transport mode, which is exactly the CLI-vs-HTTP decoupling the registry lacks.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `transport` enum field to EngineEntry in engine_registry.py + a transport-dispatch table in engine_resolver.py/engine_dispatch.py, with two seed HTTP rows (ollama, deepseek) in engine-registry.yaml. Verified by new cases in test_saga_engine_resolver.py asserting an http-transport row preflights without any `which` call and dispatches through the http adapter.

title: Service-mesh bridge contract: a stdio JSON data-plane behind a saga control-plane
idea: Rather than compiling each provider into resolver Python, define a language-agnostic bridge as a thin stdio JSON contract (request envelope in on stdin, U2 resolution/response out on stdout), mirroring a service mesh where a sidecar data-plane speaks a uniform internal protocol and the control plane (Envoy's xDS) pushes it config. Saga's registry + resolver become the control plane that emits a fully-resolved dispatch envelope; the per-provider bridge script is a swappable sidecar that translates to the provider's native API. A new provider ships one small bridge executable conforming to the stdio contract — no edits to resolver internals — and bridges are hot-swappable and independently testable with a golden fixture. Stays within the sanctioned one-router shape; adds no new plugin.
basis: Source domain: distributed-systems service mesh — Envoy's control-plane/data-plane split with the xDS discovery protocol (envoyproxy.io docs) lets a stable control plane drive many heterogeneous data-plane proxies via one wire contract. The EngineEntry.invocation {via, recipe, write_capable} triple (engine_registry.py:193-199) is already the seam a stdio bridge contract can formalize into a data-plane protocol.
outcome_shape: A reference doc plugins/saga/references/bridge-contract.md specifying the stdio JSON request/response schema + a conformance fixture, plus a `bridge_protocol.py` shim in plugins/saga/scripts wired into engine_dispatch.py. Verified by a fixture-driven test that runs a stub bridge subprocess end-to-end and asserts protocol byte-identity of the envelope.

title: UL-listing conformance harness: no provider row merges without passing golden-transcript certification
idea: Onboarding a provider today is trust-me hand-authoring of a registry row (capability_profile ratings, prompting_protocol, last_validated) with nothing that proves the provider actually behaves as claimed — the same class of failure as 343 'clean' cards that failed the live contract (#222). Borrowing product-safety certification (UL listing / CE marking), where a device cannot be sold until it passes a standardized conformance battery and carries the mark, add a `provider-conformance` harness: a golden-transcript suite (protocol byte-identity, a capability probe per claimed capability, refusal/format checks) a candidate must pass before its row is accepted, stamping `last_validated` + a conformance report path. This makes onboarding cost explicit and bounded, and gives `stale()` real teeth.
basis: Source domain: product-safety certification — Underwriters Laboratories listing requires a device pass a fixed conformance battery before it carries the mark; the mark is a portable trust token. Maps directly onto engine_registry.py's `last_validated`/`stale()` (lines 176, 377-385) which currently record a date with no evidence that any test was run.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/provider_conformance.py (golden-transcript runner) + a CI gate in the marketplace/registry validation path that fails if any engine row's last_validated lacks a passing conformance report. Verified by a red/green test: a row with a fabricated capability the provider fails to demonstrate is rejected.

title: Quarantine-then-immune-tolerance: new providers enter offload-only shadow mode and earn advisory standing
idea: Drawing on immunology — a novel antigen is not immediately trusted; it passes through quarantine and only earns tolerance after repeated benign exposure — a newly onboarded provider should not land straight into second-opinion panels. It enters a `probation` tier: offload/non-gated worker only, optionally shadow-mode (its output logged and scored against Claude's but not consumed), and is promoted to advisory-reviewer standing only after N conformance-clean, reconciliation-agreeing exposures. This lowers the risk of onboarding a cheap-but-erratic provider and gives a principled promotion ladder rather than a hand-flip of capability ratings.
basis: Source domain: immunology — quarantine plus acquired immune tolerance (repeated benign exposure builds trust before full participation). This explicitly engages `{#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}` (#283): probation keeps a new provider as a non-gated worker and, even at promotion, only to advisory-reviewer — Claude stays verifier-of-record, so no revisit of the decision is triggered; it strengthens the decision rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `probation`/`trust_tier` field to EngineEntry + resolver logic that refuses probation providers for panel/advisory-reviewer role_kinds and a promotion-threshold check reading the telemetry ledger. Verified by resolver tests asserting a probation row resolves for offload but halts (or is excluded) for a panel role.

title: Elo-rated capabilities: replace static WEAK/MODERATE/STRONG with ratings that learn from reconciliation outcomes
idea: capability_profile ratings are static, hand-authored WEAK/MODERATE/STRONG values, and `resolve_capability` routes by them (engine_registry.py picks min by -rating_score then cost_speed_rank). Borrowing chess Elo, where a rating updates from actual match results and converges on true strength, treat each second-opinion reconciliation (Claude accepts or rejects a provider's finding) as a match result and update a continuous per-(provider,capability) Elo score that feeds routing. Ratings then track real observed fit instead of a stale guess, and a provider that degrades after a model swap decays automatically. Routing still only informs which advisory engine to call — Claude remains verifier-of-record, so this never becomes gatekeeping.
basis: Source domain: competitive-matchmaking Elo (Arpad Elo's chess rating system; expected-score update from observed win/loss). The static rating→routing path in engine_registry.py resolve_capability (min by -_RATING_SCORE then cost_speed_rank, lines ~342-352) is precisely a fixed-strength ranking that Elo generalizes to an observed-outcome-updated one. Engages `{#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}`: Elo informs routing, not gating — Claude still adjudicates, so the decision is not crossed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a scripts/capability_elo.py updater + an optional `elo` field consulted (with static rating as prior/fallback) in resolve_capability, fed by reconciliation-outcome records from the telemetry ledger. Verified by a test that a provider losing repeated reconciliations drops below a rival and stops being selected.

title: Envelope-encryption key handles: registry references secrets by handle, preflight validates presence+shape without a live call
idea: HTTP providers need API keys, but the config layer only knows file-existence (`_default_config_exists`, engine_resolver.py:140-142) and preflight deliberately makes no live API call (lines 73-76). Borrowing KMS envelope encryption, where you never store or embed the data key — you store a wrapped reference/handle and resolve it at use — registry rows reference a secret by handle only (an env-var name or vault path), never a value. Preflight is extended to validate the handle resolves and the resolved value matches a provider-declared key-shape regex (e.g. `sk-...`), preserving the no-live-call invariant while catching the most common misconfig (missing/typo'd key) before dispatch. Keys never enter the registry, logs, or the cost ledger.
basis: engine_resolver.py:73-76 asserts preflight makes no live API call, and lines 140-142 only check local file existence — neither can express an HTTP API key held in an env var or vault. Source domain: cryptographic envelope encryption / KMS key handles — store a reference and validate its shape, never the secret itself — which fits the existing no-live-call preflight contract exactly.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `secret_ref` + `key_shape` field to the http-transport EngineEntry and a handle-resolution+shape-validation branch in preflight() (engine_resolver.py), with a redaction guard. Verified by tests: a present-but-malformed key fails preflight with a redacted reason; the key value never appears in any preflight output.

title: SPC control charts for providers: detect cost/latency drift and auto-flag rows for re-validation
idea: engine_dispatch.py emits no cost or latency telemetry, so a provider whose latency triples or whose cost-per-token jumps after a silent model swap is invisible until it hurts. Borrowing manufacturing statistical process control (Shewhart control charts + Western Electric run rules), have dispatch record per-call (provider, tokens, wall-time, cost estimate) and a small analyzer maintain rolling per-provider control bands; a provider drifting beyond its band (e.g. latency > 3σ, or sustained one-sided run) is auto-flagged for re-validation and optionally deprioritized in routing. This turns cost-speed-rank from a static hand-set integer into a monitored, drift-aware signal.
basis: Source domain: manufacturing quality control — Shewhart SPC control charts with Western Electric run rules distinguish common-cause noise from a real out-of-control shift, exactly the signal needed to tell provider jitter from genuine degradation. It also gives the `/outcome` 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' principle (grounding brief §2) a concrete producer, since engine_dispatch.py currently produces no such fact.
outcome_shape: PR adding a telemetry-record emit in engine_dispatch.py (append to a per-run ledger) + scripts/provider_control_chart.py computing bands and a drift flag consumed by resolver deprioritization. Verified by a test feeding a synthetic latency spike series and asserting the provider is flagged out-of-control.

title: Flight-data-recorder cost ledger: append-only, tamper-evident per-call records
idea: A provider cost/latency ledger is only trustworthy if a later run cannot silently overwrite an earlier fact — the exact failure the grounding brief records where a probe script overwrote a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS, breaking chain-of-custody. Borrowing the aviation flight-data recorder, which is crash-survivable and append-only precisely so the record cannot be doctored after the event, make the per-call provider telemetry ledger append-only and hash-chained (each record carries the prior record's hash), so any edit or gap is detectable. This makes `/outcome`'s leaf-produced cost facts auditable rather than merely present.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)' is direct evidence that mutable evidence artifacts are an active repo failure mode. Source domain: aviation flight-data recorders — append-only, tamper-evident capture designed so the record survives and cannot be retroactively altered — is the mechanism that closes it for the provider cost ledger.
outcome_shape: PR making the telemetry ledger writer (scripts) append-only + hash-chained, with a `verify_ledger` check wired into the /outcome cost-ledger read path. Verified by a test that mutating or deleting an earlier record fails the chain-verification.

title: Collapse to ONE stdio bridge contract every provider must conform to
idea: Flip the constraint to its extreme: there may be only ONE provider abstraction, ever. Today invocation is heterogeneous per row (agy uses `via: agy:delegate`, codex uses `via: codex:codex-rescue`) and `ENGINE_CLI`/`ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` are hardcoded Python dicts limited to two engines, so onboarding provider N means editing `engine_resolver.py`. Define a single `EngineBridge` stdio contract: stdin receives the byte-preserved payload, stdout returns AdvisoryEvidence JSON, exit code signals availability/halt. Each provider (codex, agy, ollama, deepseek) becomes one conforming executable named by `invocation.via` with zero resolver code changes. The practical kernel even if the 1-provider flip is absurd: the seam that varies per provider must be data + a conforming script, not a branch in resolver code.
basis: engine_resolver.py:22-36 hardcodes `ENGINE_CLI = {"agy","codex"}` and `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` per-engine; the never-gatekeepers DECISION already fixed `registry home = saga` and rejected a new plugin (DECISIONS.md:2001-2005), so this stays in saga and satisfies {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}'s consolidation burden — one router, one contract, no 9th plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/engine-bridge-contract.md` (the stdio spec) plus a conformance shim in `engine_dispatch.py` and a golden `tests/test_engine_bridge_conformance.py` that runs a stub bridge and asserts stdin-payload byte-identity, stdout AdvisoryEvidence shape, and exit-code→availability mapping. Verified: existing codex/agy rows pass the conformance test unchanged.

title: Add an `http` substrate kind so keyed API providers (DeepSeek) route without a CLI
idea: Flip the implicit constraint that every provider ships a CLI binary: assume the opposite — most future providers are pure HTTP endpoints with an API key and no binary at all. Current rows carry `substrate: external|in-repo` but BOTH are invoked through a shell `recipe` and `preflight()` gates on `shutil.which(cli)`, so an OpenAI-compatible provider like DeepSeek is unrepresentable. Introduce a third `substrate: http` whose bridge is a single generic keyed HTTP caller (base_url + model + auth-env from the row), and teach `preflight` to check key-presence + a cheap reachability probe instead of PATH. Seed it as DeepSeek = cheap cross-family second-opinion, write_capable false, advisory-only per chaperone-dispatch.
basis: engine_resolver.py:52-76 `preflight` gates on `shutil.which(cli)` and a config file; engine-registry.yaml recipes are all shell CLIs (`recipe: "codex -s read-only --effort high"`). Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (DECISIONS.md:2021): the HTTP provider stays evidence-only (write_capable false, advisory-reviewer/second-opinion role), never a git participant, so the trust boundary is preserved.
outcome_shape: PR extending `engine_registry.py` substrate validation to accept `http` + an `http_bridge.py` generic caller + a DeepSeek row in engine-registry.yaml + `tests/test_http_bridge.py` mocking the endpoint. Verified: `preflight('deepseek')` returns available=false with a key-absent reason when the env var is unset, and a resolved second-opinion request round-trips through the mocked endpoint.

title: Move credential preflight from hardcoded Python into a per-row `auth:` block
idea: Flip 'zero operators touch code to add a provider' to the extreme: onboarding a provider must require editing NO Python, only the YAML. Right now `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` and `_default_config_exists` live in `engine_resolver.py`, so every new provider's credential location is a code change and a code-review round. Add an `auth:` block to each registry row declaring either an env-var name (for keyed HTTP providers) or a config-path glob (for CLI providers), and rewrite `preflight` to read that block instead of the module-level dicts. The kernel: credential-presence is provider data, not resolver logic — this is the precondition that makes both the bridge contract (T2-F6-1) and the HTTP substrate (T2-F6-2) actually zero-code to extend.
basis: engine_resolver.py:27-36 (`ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS`) and :140-142 (`_default_config_exists`) are module-level code, not registry data; `preflight` at :66-71 consults them, so adding a provider's secret location today is a Python diff, contradicting the 'registry-driven' Gate-A shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding `auth:` schema + validation to `engine_registry.py`, refactoring `preflight`/`_default_config_exists` in `engine_resolver.py` to read row.auth, migrating the codex/agy rows in engine-registry.yaml, and updating `tests/test_engine_resolver.py` preflight cases. Verified: deleting `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATHS` leaves the existing preflight tests green because behavior is now data-sourced.

title: Ollama as the $0 keyless local offload provider — the concrete zero-budget flip
idea: Flip the inference budget to $0: assume ALL offload-class work must run on free local models. Ollama is a localhost daemon with no CLI-config-file and no API key, which breaks every preflight assumption (`which` + config-file exists), so wiring it end-to-end is the honest stress test of the data-driven auth (T2-F6-3) and HTTP substrate (T2-F6-2) seams. Register `ollama` with `substrate: http`, `auth:` = none, preflight = a cheap GET to `localhost:11434/api/tags`, and seed it as the default $0 offload target for scaffold/refactor/code-generation at MODERATE. Even if a fleet never goes fully local, the kernel is a proven no-secret, no-binary provider path and a real dollar-zero fallback when keyed providers are unavailable.
basis: Intake brief line 83-84: 'Ollama -> $0 offload target; DeepSeek -> cheap second opinion' — direct operator scope statement. The preflight mismatch is real: engine_resolver.py:59-71 requires a CLI on PATH and a config file, neither of which a localhost Ollama daemon provides.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `ollama` row to engine-registry.yaml (substrate http, auth none, localhost probe recipe) + a preflight reachability branch + `tests/test_ollama_preflight.py` mocking the :11434 endpoint (reachable / connection-refused). Verified: with the daemon mocked down, an offload capability request falls back to Claude with a recorded reason; mocked up, it resolves to the ollama row.

title: Capability-profile family inheritance so onboarding a variant isn't 7 hand-authored cells
idea: Flip to 100 providers: if the registry had to hold a hundred rows, hand-authoring seven capability cells (rating + note + sources) per row is the bottleneck that kills the whole idea. Introduce `model_identity` family defaults: a variant that shares a `model_identity` with an existing row inherits its capability_profile unless it overrides specific cells, so a new `gpt-5.5-medium` or `deepseek-chat-v2` variant declares only what differs. The validator still enforces the closed capability vocabulary on the resolved (merged) profile. The kernel even at realistic scale: onboarding cost drops from a full benchmark-authoring exercise to a delta, which is what makes a genuinely multi-provider registry maintainable.
basis: engine_registry.py `_parse_capability_profile` (:106+) requires a full mapping and `_parse_capabilities` (:97-103) enforces the closed 7-value vocabulary per row; two agy variants and two codex variants in engine-registry.yaml already duplicate near-identical profiles by hand — evidence the per-row cost is real and repeated.
outcome_shape: PR adding an inheritance-merge step in `engine_registry.py` (resolve family defaults before validation) + a `references/engine-registry.yaml` refactor collapsing the duplicated codex/agy variant cells to deltas + `tests/test_capability_inheritance.py`. Verified: merged profiles are byte-identical to the pre-refactor validated profiles (golden snapshot), and an override cell wins over the family default.

title: Passive dispatch telemetry ledger that feeds /retro — not an auto-ranking loop
idea: Flip 'nothing is measured' to 'everything is measured': assume every dispatch must emit a cost/latency fact. Today `cost_speed_rank` and `last_validated` are hand-assigned integers and dates with no observed evidence behind them. Have `engine_dispatch` append one JSONL record per call (engine_id, model_identity, wall-latency, token_estimate, availability, halt/fallback reason) to a ledger. Crucially this is NOT the automated measurement-and-reranking loop the DECISION forbids — the ledger is inert data that /retro reads during its human-gated re-validation pass, exactly the 'seed capability data drifts materially -> re-validated by use via /retro' revisit path. The kernel: staleness and mis-ranking become visible with evidence instead of by operator recall.
basis: DECISIONS.md:2016 and the engine-registry.yaml header both state ranking is 're-validated by use through /retro (R21), NOT by automated measurement loop.' This idea crosses that stance and engages its revisit-when by staying a PASSIVE ledger feeding /retro's human gate — it never mutates cost_speed_rank or last_validated automatically, so the no-measurement-loop rule holds.
outcome_shape: PR adding a telemetry-emit call in `engine_dispatch.py` writing to a gitignored JSONL ledger, a `/retro` reader section that surfaces rows whose observed availability/latency contradicts their registry rank, and `tests/test_dispatch_telemetry.py`. Verified: a dispatch produces one well-formed record; the /retro reader flags a seeded stale row and proposes (does not apply) a last_validated bump.

title: Per-run resolution+preflight memoization for the everything-cached flip
idea: Flip to 'everything is cached': assume no route resolution or availability probe may ever be computed twice in a run. A 100-leaf /outcome campaign currently re-runs `shutil.which` + config-file stats on every `resolve`, and panel resolution re-preflights every member on each call, so provider availability is probed hundreds of times against an answer that cannot change within a run. Add a per-run memo cache keyed on (engine_id) for preflight and (capability, token_estimate) for route resolution, invalidated only at run boundary. The kernel even short of total caching: filesystem-probe latency and syscall noise collapse to one probe per provider per run, which matters most exactly in the large unattended cache-tight runs the intake brief's tension-1 default targets.
basis: engine_resolver.py:231 calls `preflight(entry.engine_id)` inside `_resolve_entry`, and `_panel_availability_halt` (:416-428) loops role members re-calling `preflight` each time; nothing memoizes, so a multi-leaf run repeats identical `shutil.which`/`path.exists` probes.
outcome_shape: PR adding an opt-in memo (a resolver-level cache object threaded through resolve/resolve_role, or lru_cache with an explicit run-scoped clear) + `tests/test_preflight_memo.py` asserting `shutil.which` is invoked once per engine across N resolves via a call-counting fake. Verified: probe count for a 10-resolve loop drops from 10 to 1 per engine.

title: `route explain` — a read-only recommendation dry-run over capability x rating x cost
idea: Flip to fully-autonomous, zero-operator routing: if the operator never picks a provider, the router's silent choice must at least be auditable. `by_capability` picks the winner with a bare `min()` over (rating, cost_speed_rank, registry_order) and the operator sees only the final Resolution, never the runner-up or the reason. Add a read-only `explain(capability, token_estimate)` that returns the chosen engine, the runner-up, the exact tie-break chain that decided it, and any context-window halt or WEAK-fit fallback — without dispatching. This turns the autonomous route into a defensible recommendation surface and is the natural place to render the telemetry-flagged staleness from T2-F6-6. The kernel: even under full autonomy, capability->provider fit becomes explainable rather than a magic min().
basis: engine_registry.py:346-352 `by_capability` returns a single `min(...)` result with no surfaced runner-up or rationale; the resolver embeds fallback/halt as opaque strings (engine_resolver.py:272-289) but nothing exposes the WHY of a successful pick, so an autonomous route is currently unauditable.
outcome_shape: PR adding `Registry.explain_capability()` (or a resolver `explain()`) returning chosen/runner-up/tie-break-chain/halt + a thin `python -m ... explain` CLI + `tests/test_route_explain.py`. Verified: for a tie between two variants the output names cost_speed_rank as the deciding key; for a WEAK-only capability it reports the Claude fallback and reason without invoking any engine.

title: One canonical tier-palette module the whole fleet imports (kill the literal-string scatter)
idea: Today `MODELS`/`EFFORTS` live only in `execution_spec.py:52-53`, while the same vocabulary is re-typed as English in the `/plan` tier table (`plan/SKILL.md:298-304`), the team-execution A7 worker table (`team-execution/SKILL.md:226-234`), and 25 agent-frontmatter `model:` literals — so `fable`/`xhigh` were reachable in exactly one of those surfaces. Extract the ordered tuples into a single `plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocab.py` (models strongest-first, efforts weakest-first, with the ORDERING-IS-LOAD-BEARING contract as module docstring), have `execution_spec.py` import from it, and add a repo-wide drift-guard test that greps for any bare model literal (`"opus"`, `'haiku'`, ...) outside `tier_vocab.py` and fails the build. This makes the palette a propagated fact rather than a copy that drifts. It is the enabling substrate every other idea in this theme leans on.
basis: grounding brief §1: 'fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary'; `execution_spec.py:52-53` defines MODELS/EFFORTS as sole source; consumer-side signal §3 finding 1 (contract-mirror drift, `validate_card_body` stale hand-copy → #222) is the exact failure mode a single-source palette prevents.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocab.py` + rewiring `execution_spec.py` import + `tests/test_tier_vocab_single_source.py` (asserts zero bare model literals outside the module, mirroring `tests/test_operator_choice_drift.py`). Verified: test red before the extraction, green after; `uv run pytest tests/test_tier_vocab_single_source.py` passes; existing `test_saga_execution_spec.py` unchanged.

title: Tier-resolution shim so the 4 single-agent plugins stop hardcoding model in frontmatter
idea: mission-control, unifi, deploy, and home-lab-ops each ship exactly one agent whose `model:` is a frozen frontmatter literal (verified: 1 each), with no way to run them at a cheaper or heavier tier for a given invocation. Add a lightweight `tier:` frontmatter convention (`tier: judgment|mechanical|survey`) plus a resolver that maps the semantic tier to a concrete `{model, effort}` from the canonical palette at spawn/skill-load, so a home-lab preflight can drop to survey-tier and a deploy gate can escalate to judgment-tier without editing frontmatter. The mapping table is one file; the operator overrides per run. This propagates the effort dimension (absent everywhere outside saga) into the single-agent plugins for the first time.
basis: grounding brief §1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields ... no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier'; verified fleet count (1 agent each in deploy/unifi/mission-control/home-lab-ops via `grep ^model: plugins/*/agents/*.md`).
outcome_shape: PR adding a `tier:` convention doc + `resolve_agent_tier()` helper reading the canonical palette, applied to the 4 single-agent plugins' frontmatter, with CHANGELOG + plugin.json bumps per CLAUDE.md step 6. Verified: a unit test asserts each semantic tier resolves to a palette-valid pair, and one plugin's skill demonstrably spawns at a survey tier in a smoke run.

title: Make effort a first-class authored field in the team plan A7 worker table, not a comment
idea: The A7 Team-Structure worker table renders a `Tier` column as `opus/high` prose (`team-execution/SKILL.md:226-234`), but `team_emitter.py` never parses model/effort out of it (verified: zero tier/model/effort references in the emitter) — so the effort half of every teammate's tier is decorative today. Give the emitter a real parse of the `{model, effort}` pair per worker row into a structured field on the emitted team plan, and add an emit-time validator (mirroring `execution_spec.Tier.validate`) that rejects a malformed or off-palette effort so a typo fails loudly instead of being silently ignored. Effort becomes a carried, validated fact on the team artifact — the precondition for ever honoring it at spawn. This is the authoring-layer half; it does not itself change the spawn path.
basis: grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS producer/consumer pair rendered in team-execution A7; verified `team_emitter.py` has 0 matches for tier/model/effort, so the A7 `Tier` column is unparsed prose. QUEUED `{#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}` states 'effort is not [settable per agent] ... all teammates inherit one session-global effort' — this idea structures the authored value without re-architecting the spawn (distinct from that seed's Workflow-engine re-host).
outcome_shape: PR extending `plugins/saga/scripts/team_emitter.py` to parse+validate per-worker `{model, effort}` into the emitted plan, with `tests/test_team_emitter.py` cases for a valid pair and an off-palette effort (must raise). Verified: new tests green; a golden team plan shows structured effort fields.

title: Effort-honored reconciliation: detect when a teammate silently ran at session-global effort
idea: Because team-execution spawns subagents by type, every teammate inherits one session-global effort regardless of its planned tier — a silent mis-tier exactly like the fable-weaker-than-haiku bug, but at run time and invisible. Add a post-run reconciliation step that compares each teammate's planned effort (from idea T3-F1-3's structured field) against the effort actually in force, and emits a `tiering-drift` note naming any worker whose planned effort could not be honored, so 'I asked for xhigh on the security reviewer' is a reported gap, never a silent downgrade. This turns the current invisible coarseness into an audited fact and gives the per-teammate-effort push a verification spine before its expensive re-architecture lands.
basis: grounding brief §6 finding 1 (silent no-ops in delegation; 'did it actually run/persist' verification demanded) + QUEUED `{#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}` ('all teammates inherit one session-global effort'). Builds BEYOND the seed: the seed sets effort, this audits whether it was honored — not a duplicate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a reconciliation emitter section + `honored_effort` check to team-execution's post-run flow, with a test asserting a planned-vs-actual mismatch produces a named `tiering-drift` line. Verified: test with a divergent plan yields the drift note; a matching plan yields none.

title: An escalate-one-rung primitive for the operator's mid-run 'bump the model' ask
idea: Session mining recorded operators 'asking for mid-run model-change pauses' and 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' — but the only tier levers are full-table re-authoring; there is no cheap 'take this unit up one rung' move even though the tuples are explicitly ordered ladders. Expose a `bump_tier(tier, model_steps=0, effort_steps=0)` helper in the palette module that walks MODELS/EFFORTS by index (respecting strongest-first / weakest-first) and clamps at the ends, plus a `/work` operator affordance to escalate or de-escalate a named unit by one rung between rounds. This makes the ladder semantics of `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` operable rather than merely documented. It is the minimal lever the ad-hoc-tier-reasoning pain keeps re-inventing by hand.
basis: grounding brief §7 pattern 6: 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses'; 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful'. Crosses binding `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` — engaged by building the primitive ON its ordered-ladder contract (min-index-strongest / max-index-weakest) and honoring the `.index(`-has-two-contracts rule from LEARNINGS.md:164 rather than treating the tuples as unordered sets.
outcome_shape: PR adding `bump_tier()` to `tier_vocab.py`/`execution_spec.py` + a `/work` between-rounds escalate affordance, with tests covering up/down steps and end-clamping (fable can't bump stronger; low can't bump weaker). Verified: `uv run pytest` on the new cases; a `/work` transcript shows a one-rung escalation applied.

title: A per-unit tier floor so upgrade-only segment merge can't cheap out a must-be-deep unit
idea: `segment_units()` derives a segment's tier by upgrade-only index arithmetic — `min(MODELS.index)` / `max(EFFORTS.index)` (`execution_spec.py:1474-1475`) — which means a cheap unit sharing a segment can only ever be pulled UP, but there is no way to assert 'this adversarial-review unit must never resolve below opus/high' as an invariant the merge respects. Add an optional `min_tier` on `Unit` that `segment_units()` clamps the merged tier up to, and fail emit if a declared floor is itself off-palette. This gives the ordered ladder a floor concept to complement its ceiling, so a security or design unit carries a guaranteed minimum through segment collapse instead of hoping the merge math lands high enough.
basis: `execution_spec.py:1473-1475` (upgrade-only max merge, no floor). Crosses `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` — engaged by implementing the floor as index arithmetic over the SAME ordered tuples (clamp = max over MODELS-strength index), preserving the load-bearing ordering contract the learning at LEARNINGS.md:164 protects rather than adding an unordered override.
outcome_shape: PR adding `Unit.min_tier` + clamp in `segment_units()` + validate + round-trip in `to_dict`, with `tests/test_saga_execution_spec.py` cases: floor pulls a cheap segment up, off-palette floor fails emit, absent floor round-trips byte-identical. Verified: new tests green, existing spec golden tests unchanged.

title: A 'new model onboarding' kit that makes adding Claude 6 a one-file change with a self-arming guard
idea: The `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` learning exists because enabling `fable`/`xhigh` LOOKED like 'append two tuple entries' but a wrong insertion point silently mis-tiered every merge and passed validation. Ship a runbook (`plugins/saga/references/tier-palette.md`) plus a generated guard-test template that, for any model/effort tuple, asserts the intended strength ordering AND greps for every `.index(` call over the tuple so a future addition that breaks a second (ordering) contract fails loudly. The kit encodes the learning's own generalizable rule ('grep for `.index(` before extending a closed vocabulary') as executable machinery, so the next model arrives without a fleet-wide manual audit. This is the drift-proofing that turns a remembered gotcha into a standing gate.
basis: LEARNINGS.md:164 `{#tier-vocab-ordering}` — Evidence cites `execution_spec.py:49-56`, `segment_units()` merge, and guard test `test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh`; Generalizable rule: 'grep for `.index(` on it — a tuple used for membership and ordering has two contracts.' This idea operationalizes that exact rule; it honors, not contradicts, the binding learning.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/tier-palette.md` (onboarding runbook) + a parametrized ordering/`.index(`-coverage guard test in `tests/test_team_emitter.py`/`test_tier_vocab_single_source.py`. Verified: intentionally mis-inserting a fake `"model6"` at the wrong index makes the guard test red; correct prepend makes it green.

title: Per-teammate tier variants minted at team-scaffold so effort ships as frontmatter today
idea: The per-teammate-effort seed is blocked on re-hosting team-execution onto the Workflow engine (where `agent()` accepts effort) — a multi-day rebuild. A cheaper reachable path: since model IS settable per agent via frontmatter, and the seed notes 'if Claude Code adds an effort: frontmatter field most of this collapses to a cheap frontmatter edit', add a scaffold-time generator that materializes per-teammate agent variants from a plan's `validator → tier` table — emitting distinct frontmatter (model now, effort the moment the harness field lands) rather than one shared subagent type. The generator writes the drift-guard alongside so the variant set can't silently desync from the plan table. This delivers concentrated deep-reasoning-on-security-reviewer today for the model axis and is effort-ready by construction, without the full Workflow re-architecture.
basis: QUEUED `{#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}`: 'Model is settable per agent because it is frontmatter; effort is not ... or Claude Code adds an effort: agent-frontmatter field (at which point most of this collapses to a cheap frontmatter edit mirroring the model tiers).' Builds BEYOND the seed: the seed's target design routes through the Workflow engine; this delivers the frontmatter-variant path the seed names as the collapse case, ahead of the harness field.
outcome_shape: PR adding a per-teammate variant generator (reads a plan `validator → tier` table, emits frontmatter variants + a registration drift test like `tests/test_agent_registration_drift.py`). Verified: generator produces variants whose model matches the table, drift test catches a hand-desynced variant, CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bumped per CLAUDE.md step 6.

title: Tier-enforceable-by-backend matrix: halt, never silently degrade a fable/xhigh unit
idea: A plan-authored `fable/xhigh` unit validates fine (MODELS/EFFORTS accept it, execution_spec.py:52-53) but when team_emitter renders it to team-execution markdown the runtime spawns teammates by agentType and inherits the session-global tier, so the fable/xhigh the worker table shows is cosmetic — the unit silently runs at session default. Invert the silent degrade into a visible halt by mirroring the existing SANDBOX_ENFORCEABLE_BY_BACKEND pattern (execution_spec.py:105) with a TIER_ENFORCEABLE_BY_BACKEND matrix: backends that cannot spawn at an arbitrary {model,effort} (team-execution today) HALT at emit time when a unit's tier exceeds what they can honor, rather than emitting a table they will not obey. This makes fable/xhigh honestly reachable-or-refused everywhere the spec flows, closing the 'unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary' gap by removing the fake reachability.
basis: Grounding §1: 'fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary' and team-execution 'enforces neither restrictive axis... residents run bypassPermissions'. execution_spec.py:96-109 already implements the halt-not-degrade pattern for sandbox axes (SANDBOX_ENFORCEABLE_BY_BACKEND, 'unknown never permissive R4') — a directly reusable template for a tier axis.
outcome_shape: PR adding TIER_ENFORCEABLE_BY_BACKEND + a tier_unenforceable(backend, tier) helper to execution_spec.py, wired into team_emitter emit-path to raise SpecError on an un-enforceable tier; verified by a new test in tests/test_team_emitter.py asserting a fable/xhigh unit routed to team-execution FAILS emit while the same unit to cc-workflows-ultracode passes.

title: Single-source palette manifest that every emitter and lint reads (kill the copy-paste vocabulary)
idea: The MODELS/EFFORTS vocabulary lives only in execution_spec.py; team_emitter, agent-frontmatter, and single-agent plugins each re-state model strings by hand, so fable/xhigh never propagate. Remove the duplication step entirely: extract the ordered palette to one exported artifact (a `palette.py`/`palette.yaml` re-exported by execution_spec so nothing else redefines the tuples) and have team_emitter and a new frontmatter lint import it. Any place that needs the vocabulary now references the single source instead of restating it, so 'add fable everywhere' becomes 'it is already everywhere.'
basis: LEARNINGS #tier-vocab-ordering:178-179 generalizable rule — 'a tuple used for membership and ordering has two contracts, and only one shows up in the validator'; grounding §1 confirms the vocabulary is defined once (execution_spec.py:52-53) and re-stated nowhere as a shared import, which is why fable/xhigh do not propagate.
outcome_shape: PR extracting MODELS/EFFORTS (+ ordering comment) into plugins/saga/scripts/palette.py, re-exported by execution_spec.py for backward compat, with team_emitter importing it; verified by a drift test asserting no plugin file outside palette.py hardcodes the literal model-tuple, and existing execution_spec tests stay green.

title: Effort field becomes real: generalize the readonly-verifier per-call effort pattern into an `effort:` frontmatter convention + spawn shim
idea: Across all 8 plugins agent frontmatter carries `model:` but zero `effort:` fields; the ONLY place effort is set per-spawn is saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern (execution_spec bakes effort into the agent() call). Automate effort into first-class existence everywhere by (1) adopting an `effort:` frontmatter key convention and (2) a thin spawn wrapper that reads it and injects effort at dispatch — the same move that already works for readonly-verifier, generalized fleet-wide so agy/deploy/mission-control agents stop inheriting one session-global effort. This removes the 'effort is unsettable outside a Workflow script' constraint by making the one working pattern the fleet default.
basis: Grounding §1: 'zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution), no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern.' That existing per-call pattern is the proof the mechanism works; the idea is to lift it out of one call site into a convention.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `effort:` frontmatter key to the plugin agent-authoring convention doc + a spawn-shim helper (mirroring READONLY_VERIFIER per-call effort injection) applied to at least agy and deploy agents; verified by a test asserting an agent frontmatter `effort:` value reaches the dispatch opts, and CHANGELOG/plugin.json release surfaces updated.

title: Derive effort from role_kind so the manual per-unit effort column disappears
idea: Step 1 of /plan authoring makes the operator hand-assign a {model,effort} tier per Implementation Unit and confirm the whole table ('Do not lock tiers silently', plan/SKILL.md:307) — effort is picked by hand every run. Automate the effort half away: an effort_resolver that deterministically derives effort from the work-shape/role_kind already implied by the heuristic table (judgment→high, mechanical→medium, read-only survey→low), so the tier table pre-fills effort and the operator only overrides exceptions instead of choosing every cell. The manual per-unit effort decision becomes a confirmable default, collapsing a repeated authoring step.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:296-307 — the work-shape→default-tier heuristic is already written as a deterministic table ('Apply the heuristic per unit, then present the full tier table... ask the operator to confirm or override'); the effort column is derivable from the same work-shape key that already sets the model, so hand-assigning it is redundant.
outcome_shape: PR adding an effort_resolver(work_shape)->effort function to execution_spec.py plus a plan/SKILL.md edit that has the tier table pre-fill effort from work-shape; verified by a unit test mapping each heuristic row to its derived effort and a plan-doc example showing operator overriding one cell.

title: Auto-escalate one rung up the ladder on unit HALT instead of manual re-tiering
idea: Tier tuples are ordered escalation ladders (#tier-vocab-ordering), and segment_units already steps them via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index) index arithmetic — but when a unit HALTs or its output fails the gate, escalation is a manual operator act: notice, re-tier, re-run. Automate it: an opt-in escalation policy on a unit that, on gate failure, retries once at the next rung up the ladder (stronger model or higher effort via the existing index math) before surfacing the HALT to the operator. The best version of 'operator manually bumps the tier and reruns' is no step — the ladder that already exists in code drives the retry.
basis: LEARNINGS #tier-vocab-ordering:172-174 — 'segment_units() derives a segment's upgrade-only tier by index arithmetic over the tuples: MODELS strongest-first (min index wins), EFFORTS weakest-first (max index wins)'. The ordered ladder is already load-bearing machinery; auto-escalation reuses it rather than adding new ordering semantics, so it builds on the binding decision rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding an optional `escalate_on_halt` policy to Unit + an emitted retry-at-next-rung block in the workflow harness (execution_spec.py emitter), bounded to one escalation; verified by a test that a failing unit's retry renders at the correctly-incremented ladder rung and that a top-of-ladder unit surfaces the HALT instead of looping.

title: Grep-for-.index drift guard: new-model additions fail loudly fleet-wide, no manual audit
idea: Adding Claude 5's fable/xhigh looked like 'append two tuple entries' but silently mis-ranked fable weaker than haiku because the tuple is used for BOTH membership and ordering; the fix was a hand-remembered rule ('before extending a closed vocabulary, grep for .index'). Remove the manual grep-and-remember step by encoding it: a CI drift guard that (1) asserts every `.index(` consumer of the palette is covered by an ordering-assertion test and (2) fails when a model string appears in any file other than the single palette source. The next model (Claude 6) then cannot be added wrong — the guard forces the ordering decision instead of trusting an operator to recall the learning.
basis: LEARNINGS #tier-vocab-ordering:169-179 — 'Appending fable would have validated fine but made every merge rank fable weaker than haiku — a silent mis-tier, not a validation failure' and generalizable rule 'grep for .index( on it'. The learning explicitly names a manual discipline; the idea machine-enforces it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a drift-guard test (tests/) that scans for palette model-string literals outside the single source and asserts an ordering test exists for each .index consumer, plus a CI hook; verified by the test failing on a deliberately mis-ordered fixture branch and passing on main.

title: Per-model effort-capability matrix that fails loudly instead of silently clamping a teammate's effort
idea: The per-teammate-effort seed's own open question is 'Haiku may clamp the top effort tiers; verify per-model effort support when built' — meaning a per-teammate effort assignment can silently clamp with no signal. Build beyond the seed by removing the silent clamp: a per-model effort-capability matrix (which {model} honors which EFFORTS rungs) validated at author time, so a teammate assigned haiku/xhigh (or any model/effort the model cannot honor) FAILS validate with a SpecError rather than quietly running at a clamped tier. This is the guardrail the seed defers; it makes per-teammate effort trustworthy the moment the seed's spawn-path work lands, and it does not touch external-engine chaperone dispatch (offload→sonnet/medium, second-opinion→opus/high stay fixed), so it respects {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}.
basis: QUEUED #team-execution-per-teammate-effort:420 — 'Note Haiku may clamp the top effort tiers; verify per-model effort support when built.' The seed itself leaves this as an unbuilt TODO; the idea materializes it as an author-time validation, which the seed does not specify.
outcome_shape: PR adding EFFORT_SUPPORTED_BY_MODEL to execution_spec.py + a Tier.validate() check raising SpecError on an unsupported model/effort pair, with the matrix documented; verified by a test asserting haiku/xhigh (or the real clamp pairs) fails validate while opus/xhigh passes, and the guard leaves ENGINE_INTENTS chaperone tiers untouched.

title: Agents declare a role-tier intent, not a concrete model string
idea: Today every teammate hardcodes (or omits) a concrete `model:` string, so the palette word `fable` can never appear in an agent file and a model swap is a 24-file edit. Reframe one level up: an agent should declare WHAT KIND of thinking it does (`role-tier: adversarial-review`, `role-tier: mechanical-scan`, `role-tier: contract-test`), and a single fleet-shared resolver maps each role-tier to a concrete `{model, effort}` drawn from the saga palette. This makes fable/xhigh reachable everywhere by changing one map entry, and it turns the currently-implicit convention (reviewers=default, testers=sonnet, scanners=haiku) into an explicit, greppable contract. The resolver reuses saga's MODELS/EFFORTS as the value space so the two never diverge.
basis: grep of plugins/team-execution/agents/*.md shows the role/tier decision is ALREADY implicit-and-scattered: reviewers (ai-usefulness-reviewer, api-reviewer, architecture-reviewer, clarity-reviewer, code-quality-reviewer, devils-advocate-reviewer, infra-reviewer, privacy-reviewer) carry NO model field and silently inherit session default, while api-compat-scanner/dependency-scanner/deploy-watcher=haiku and concurrency-tester/event-flow-tester/performance-tester=sonnet. Grounding brief §1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:, zero effort: fields ... fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary.'
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/team-execution/references/role-tier-map.yaml (role-tier → {model,effort}) + a resolver in artifact_pointer.py-adjacent script, migrating all ~24 agent frontmatters from model: to role-tier:, and a drift-guard test in tests/ asserting (a) every agent's role-tier resolves and (b) resolved values are members of saga MODELS/EFFORTS. Verified by pytest going green and grep showing zero bare model: strings remaining.

title: Surface the tier palette in the judgment flows where xhigh actually pays — /ideate, /brainstorm, /work
idea: The tier/effort vocabulary is treated as a /plan-authoring-only concern: it lives in the unit tier table and nowhere in the interactive judgment surfaces. But xhigh-Opus and fable are most valuable exactly in adversarial judgment (ideation divergence, brainstorm depth, work-phase review), and those flows expose no tier lever at all. Reframe: judgment stages are first-class tier-consumers, not tier-blind. Add a lightweight tier-selection preamble to /ideate, /brainstorm, and the /work interactive path that names the palette (including fable/xhigh) with a cheaper fallback per the intake §4 spend-lever rule, so the operator can dial reasoning depth at the moment it matters instead of only when authoring a plan spec.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS/tier vocabulary is 'authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 ... Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow.' Intake §2 splits judgment stages (/ideate,/brainstorm,/doc-review,/code-review) as the second-opinion-default set — exactly the stages missing a tier lever.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/skills/ideate/SKILL.md, brainstorm/SKILL.md, and work/SKILL.md to add a per-run tier-selection step (palette + cheaper-fallback recommendation line). Verified by a docs/behavior test or SKILL-lint asserting each of the three flows references the shared palette and carries the spend-lever fallback sentence.

title: Stop waiting for the harness — inject effort at spawn via a prompt-preamble shim now
idea: The QUEUED seed treats 'effort isn't a frontmatter field' as a hard harness fact and parks per-teammate effort behind a multi-day re-route onto the Workflow engine. Attack that default: effort is a fleet-owned concept we can carry in our own metadata and REALIZE at spawn today, without any harness change, by appending a normative effort directive to the agent prompt at dispatch (the same mechanism BUDGET_RIDER already uses to bend cheap-tier behavior). A fleet `effort:` convention plus a spawn-time preamble ('Operate at HIGH effort: reason exhaustively before emitting...') gives operators an effort lever now; if/when Claude Code ships a real effort: field, the shim collapses to a frontmatter edit and the convention already exists.
basis: QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}: 'effort is not [frontmatter] ... per-agent effort only exists inside a Workflow script (agent(..., {effort})) ... Feasibility hinges on the spawn path exposing effort — today that means routing team-execution through the Workflow engine.' Precedent that prompt-appended riders steer tier behavior: execution_spec.py:122-129 BUDGET_RIDER is baked into cheap-tier agent prompts at emit.
outcome_shape: PR adding an EFFORT_RIDER table + spawn-preamble injection to the team-execution dispatch path and a fleet effort: convention doc, mirroring BUDGET_RIDER. Verified by a unit test asserting an agent authored with effort: high receives the corresponding rider text in its assembled prompt, and by a live team-execute run whose reviewer prompt visibly carries the directive.

title: Make effort a required, greppable field — zero-effort-field is a lint failure, not a default
idea: The fleet currently has 0 of 24 team-execution agents carrying any effort signal, so effort silently defaults to session-global and no one can audit it. Reframe the absence from 'reasonable default' to 'a hole in the tier contract.' Introduce a fleet rule that every agent must declare an effort (or a role-tier that resolves one), enforced by a marketplace-CI guard the same way plugin.json fields are checked. This makes effort a first-class, auditable property of the fleet — you can answer 'what effort does the security reviewer run at?' from the file, not from whatever session happened to spawn it.
basis: Intake brief §9 spot-check: '0 of 25 team-execution agents carry an effort field'; grounding §1: 'zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution)'. CLAUDE.md step 6 already mandates release-surface/metadata drift guards, so a required-field CI guard is an established repo pattern to extend.
outcome_shape: PR adding an effort-presence check to the marketplace/agent-metadata CI guard (tests/ or tools/) that fails when any agent lacks effort/role-tier, plus a one-time migration filling all agents. Verified by the guard test failing on a deliberately effort-less fixture agent and passing on the migrated fleet.

title: Promote the ladder from tuple-index-arithmetic to an explicit named-rung data structure
idea: {#tier-vocab-ordering} establishes that MODELS/EFFORTS are ordered ladders, but the ordering is encoded only as position in a tuple plus a load-bearing comment, and 'is A stronger than B' / 'escalate one rung' are re-implemented as scattered min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index) arithmetic. That near-miss (appending fable would have silently ranked it weaker than haiku) is the tell that index-in-a-tuple is the wrong representation. Reframe the palette as a first-class ladder: an ordered list of rungs each with an explicit rank and a strength comparator, exposing rank(model), stronger_of(a,b), and escalate(tier, rungs=1) as functions. segment_units and any future consumer call the ladder API instead of doing index math, so adding a model can never silently invert strength.
basis: LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering} (LEARNINGS.md:164-179): 'Appending fable would have validated fine but made every merge rank fable weaker than haiku — a silent mis-tier, not a validation failure' and 'a tuple used for membership AND ordering has two contracts, and only one shows up in the validator.' Binding register affirms tiers are ordered escalation ladders; this idea structurally encodes that decision rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR refactoring plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py to derive an explicit ladder object (rank + comparator API) from the palette, replacing the min/max .index() call sites in segment_units, plus a test asserting a new model inserted at any rung yields the intended strength order. Verified by existing test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh plus a new insert-a-model regression staying green.

title: Climb the ladder at runtime — auto-escalate one rung on budget-exhaustion or refutation instead of halting
idea: The ordered ladder exists but is only ever read at authoring time; at runtime the machinery only halts. When a cheap-tier agent exhausts its StructuredOutput budget or a verify panel refutes a unit, the run stops rather than doing the one thing an escalation LADDER is for: retry the same unit one rung stronger. Reframe the ladder as a dynamic climb, not a static label. Add an opt-in escalation policy: on a bounded set of failure signatures (budget-exhaustion, verifier-disagreement), re-dispatch the failed unit at the next rung up (haiku→sonnet→opus, effort medium→high→xhigh) once, then halt if still failing. This spends premium tokens only where cheap tiers demonstrably failed — the inverse of xhigh-Opus-on-everything.
basis: First-principles: execution_spec.py bakes BUDGET_RIDER precisely because cheap-tier agents exhaust budget (lines 122-129), and the emitter throws verifier-disagreement / missing-output on refutation or short output — both are terminal halts today. An ordering that is defined (MODELS/EFFORTS, {#tier-vocab-ordering}) but never traversed at runtime is latent capability: the same index-arithmetic that computes a merged tier can compute 'the next rung,' so escalate-and-retry is a small addition atop existing structure, and it directly answers the session-mining pain 'xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful' by escalating reactively rather than pre-emptively. Extends, does not contradict, {#tier-vocab-ordering}.
outcome_shape: PR adding an opt-in escalate-on-failure policy (config flag + next-rung helper) to the emitted workflow harness / team-execution retry path, bounded to one climb, emitting a visible escalation log line. Verified by a test where a unit fails at haiku, is re-dispatched at sonnet, and the run continues; and a second test asserting the climb halts after one rung.

title: One fleet tier-palette source of record; new model = one edit, guarded fleet-wide
idea: The palette is a saga-private Python constant, so 'which models/efforts exist' has a different answer in every plugin that hardcodes a model string, and a new Claude model (the next fable) means hunting edits across saga, team-execution agents, and docs. Reframe the palette as fleet currency owned by no single plugin: extract MODELS/EFFORTS + the load-bearing ordering into one machine-readable tier-palette manifest that saga imports (not redefines) and that CI reads to assert no plugin names a model outside it. Adding a model becomes a one-line manifest edit; the drift guard catches any file that hardcodes a stale or off-palette model.
basis: execution_spec.py:52-53: MODELS = ("fable","opus","sonnet","haiku"); EFFORTS = ("low","medium","high","xhigh") — a saga-private constant. Grounding §1: 'The fleet's ONE operator-facing model/effort lever' is saga's plan table and 'fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary.' Consumer-side signal §3 finding 1: contract-copies drifting from source of truth is the top cross-repo recurrence (validate_card_body stale hand-copy → #222) — same disease a single palette source prevents.
outcome_shape: PR extracting a tier-palette manifest (module or JSON) as the single definition, changing execution_spec.py to import it, and adding a marketplace-CI guard test asserting every plugin's model references resolve to the manifest. Verified by pytest + a deliberately off-palette fixture tripping the guard.

title: Invert ownership: teammates declare a tier FLOOR; the plan may escalate above it but never under-tier it
idea: The QUEUED seed assumes the plan (or operator) is the sole authority that assigns each teammate its effort. But the real failure mode is the opposite: reviewers carry no model field and silently inherit whatever the session default is, so a cheap session can run the security or architecture reviewer at haiku without anyone deciding to. Reframe WHO owns the tier: let each teammate declare its own minimum-viable tier FLOOR in its frontmatter (security-reviewer floor = opus/high), and let the plan's per-teammate table only escalate above that floor, never below. This flips the seed from 'plan dictates effort down' to 'agent guarantees a floor, plan tunes up' — so under-tiering a judgment reviewer becomes structurally impossible rather than a silent session accident.
basis: grep confirms the silent-under-tier hole: architecture-reviewer, code-quality-reviewer, devils-advocate-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, infra-reviewer and other reviewers carry NO model field and inherit session default, while only scanners/testers pin a model. QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} frames the ask as plan-dictated-downward per-teammate effort; this idea builds beyond it by adding an agent-owned floor the plan cannot violate.
outcome_shape: PR adding a tier-floor: field to teammate agent frontmatter (min model + effort), a clamp in the team-execution spawn/spec path that raises any plan-assigned tier to the floor and refuses to go below, and a test asserting a plan that assigns haiku to a floor=opus reviewer is clamped up (or fails loudly). Verified by that clamp test plus a live team-execute run showing the reviewer spawned at its floor despite a cheaper session default.

title: Extract tier vocabulary into a shared importable primitive every plugin script reuses
idea: Today MODELS/EFFORTS/ENGINE_INTENTS/_CHEAP_MODELS live inside execution_spec.py, and other modules re-declare overlapping tuples verbatim guarded only by cross-module drift-guard tests. Extract the tier vocabulary (models, efforts, cheap-model set, engine intents, ordering contract) into a single `plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocab.py` primitive that execution_spec.py and outcome_spec.py import rather than mirror. This turns 'add a model' from an N-file hand-copy-plus-drift-test dance into a one-file edit that propagates by import. Every downstream tier consumer (validator, emitter, resolver preview) inherits the change for free.
basis: execution_spec.py:79-81: 'outcome_spec.py mirrors these three names verbatim (deliberate parallel house, different error type) -- a cross-module drift-guard test asserts the two copies stay identical.' The verbatim-mirror-plus-drift-guard pattern is the exact hand-maintenance cost a shared import removes.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocab.py exporting MODELS/EFFORTS/_CHEAP_MODELS/ENGINE_INTENTS; execution_spec.py and outcome_spec.py import from it; the verbatim-mirror drift-guard test is replaced by an identity-by-import test. Verified: existing tier tests in tests/test_team_emitter.py stay green and a new test asserts both modules reference the same object.

title: Registry-driven model palette (models.json) so new models arrive as data, not code
idea: Replace the hand-ordered MODELS/EFFORTS tuples with a `plugins/saga/scripts/models.json` registry where each model carries an explicit integer rank (and each effort its rung index), from which the loader builds the ordered tuples at import. A new Claude model becomes a registry row with a rank, never a code edit whose ordering must be reasoned about. Encoding rank as an explicit data field directly defuses the dual-contract trap the ordering learning warns about: membership and ordering stop being two hidden contracts riding on tuple position.
basis: LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering}: 'Before extending a closed vocabulary constant, grep for .index( on it -- a tuple used for membership and ordering has two contracts, and only one shows up in the validator.' Engages that decision's revisit condition (the next model addition should fail loudly): an explicit-rank registry makes ordering a validated data field instead of positional lore, so the guard becomes a schema check.
