outcome_shape: PR adding models.json + a loader in tier_vocab.py/execution_spec.py that derives MODELS/EFFORTS from rank; a drift test asserts derived tuple order equals registry rank order. Verified: test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh passes against the registry-derived tuples.

title: Declare-and-validate effort: in agent frontmatter now, ahead of the spawn-path consumer
idea: The 33 model-bearing agents (25 in team-execution) carry `model:` but zero carry `effort:`, so effort is invisible until spawn-time and impossible to lint. Add an `effort:` field to agent frontmatter as a declarative, validated contract and ship a frontmatter linter that checks every value against the canonical EFFORTS tuple. The value stays inert for spawn until the Workflow-engine path lands, but declaring and drift-guarding it now means the eventual consumer inherits a fleet already annotated and validated. This is the cheap-frontmatter-edit half of the per-teammate-effort work, decoupled from the multi-day engine re-architecture so it can land first and compound.
basis: QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}: 'Priority P3 (-> P2 if Claude Code ships an effort: agent-frontmatter field)... at which point most of this collapses to a cheap frontmatter edit mirroring the model tiers.' Engages its worth-it-when by pre-landing the declarative field and its validator, so only the spawn wiring remains; does not duplicate the seed's engine re-arch.
outcome_shape: PR adding effort: to agent frontmatters + tests/test_agent_frontmatter_tiers.py asserting every effort value is in EFFORTS and every model in MODELS. Verified: the lint test fails on an out-of-vocab value and passes on the seeded fleet.

title: Ship escalate()/downgrade()/clamp() ladder operations as a reusable primitive
idea: segment_units() encodes ladder movement as inline min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index) arithmetic that no other caller can reuse, so any future 'bump this one unit up a rung' re-implements the index math and risks the same silent mis-tier the ordering learning describes. Expose the ladder as named operations in tier_vocab.py: escalate(tier, steps), downgrade(tier, steps), and clamp(tier, floor, ceiling), each honoring the load-bearing ordering. Mid-run operator moves ('take this to xhigh', 'shed to sonnet') and cache-tight downgrades become one call fleet-wide instead of bespoke arithmetic per site.
basis: execution_spec.py:49-53 ordering comment ('segment_units() merges tiers upgrade-only via min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index)') plus LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering} showing the index arithmetic is the exact place a silent mis-tier hides -- centralizing it as tested named ops removes per-site re-derivation.
outcome_shape: PR adding escalate/downgrade/clamp to tier_vocab.py with unit tests covering ladder bounds and ordering; segment_units() refactored to call them. Verified: existing merge tests green + new bound tests (escalate past strongest is a no-op, not an error).

title: Shared tier-resolution precedence primitive consumed by both /work and team-execution
idea: The per-teammate-effort seed will need identical precedence logic in two places: saga /work and team-execution both must decide how a plan-dictated override, a per-teammate override, a frontmatter default, and a work-shape default combine. Left implicit, the two consumers will drift exactly like the SANDBOX_PROFILES verbatim mirror already does. Extract that precedence FIRST as a single `resolve_tier(plan, teammate, frontmatter, workshape)` primitive with a documented precedence order, so the eventual per-teammate feature is a thin caller in both engines rather than two divergent implementations. This is the compounding substrate underneath the seed, not the seed's per-teammate table itself.
basis: First-principles: the grounding brief shows two independent tier consumers (/work re-emitting the ExecutionSpec, team-execution's worker table) and one already-realized cost of parallel un-shared vocab (execution_spec.py:79-81 drift-guard on a verbatim mirror). Two future callers of the same precedence rule, with a demonstrated in-repo history of copy-drift, make a shared resolver strictly cheaper than the eventual duplicate-and-guard path. Engages the QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} worth-it-when by supplying the precedence layer its implementation presupposes without duplicating its engine re-arch scope.
outcome_shape: PR adding resolve_tier() to tier_vocab.py + a precedence-order reference doc; unit tests asserting each layer wins in the documented order and absent layers fall through. Verified: table-driven tests cover all precedence permutations.

title: Fleet-wide agent-frontmatter tier lint wired into CI
idea: The execution_spec validator only guards tiers authored in a spec JSON; the 33 agent frontmatters that hardcode model: are unchecked, so a typo or a retired model name ('opus-4', 'med') sits latent until spawn. Add scripts/lint_agent_tiers.py that scans every plugins/*/agents/*.md model:/effort: value against the canonical MODELS/EFFORTS vocabulary and fails CI on drift. This makes future fleet-wide model renames safe: rename in the registry, and the lint immediately flags every stale frontmatter instead of leaving silent landmines. Compounds directly with the shared-vocab and registry ideas by giving them a fleet-wide enforcement surface.
basis: Verified in-repo: grep shows 33 agents carry model: and 0 carry effort:, while execution_spec.py:46-53 states the validator only 'validates that authored tiers are drawn from these closed sets' for spec-emitted units -- agent frontmatter is outside that guard entirely.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/lint_agent_tiers.py + a CI step + tests/test_agent_tier_lint.py; the lint fails on a seeded out-of-vocab frontmatter fixture and passes on the real fleet. Verified: CI job runs the lint on plugins/*/agents/*.md.

title: Single-source the operator-facing tier tables via a --check doc generator
idea: The tier/intent guidance exists as two hand-maintained tables: /plan's per-unit tier table and team-execution's worker table, wired by the same ENGINE_INTENTS producer/consumer pair but kept in sync by hand. Drive both from a shared tier_catalog data structure and add a context_census-style --check mode that fails if the rendered docs drift from the catalog. A new model, effort, or intent then updates one catalog and both operator-facing tables regenerate, so the palette can grow without a fleet-wide manual doc sweep.
basis: Grounding brief Corrections intake: 'ENGINE_INTENTS producer/consumer pair -- authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233)'. Two hand-maintained renderings of one vocabulary is the drift surface; the library already uses the schema-validate-in-CI + --check pattern (context_census.py --check).
outcome_shape: PR adding tier_catalog.py + a --check mode + a CI test asserting plan/SKILL.md and team-execution/SKILL.md tier tables match the catalog. Verified: mutating a table without updating the catalog fails --check.

title: Model-aware ladder: encode per-model effort ceilings in the registry so escalate() skips unreachable rungs
idea: The ladder today treats EFFORTS as uniformly reachable for every model, but the per-teammate-effort work already flags that Haiku may clamp the top effort tiers. Add a per-model effort-ceiling field to the models registry and have clamp()/escalate() consult it so 'bump to xhigh' on a haiku unit resolves to that model's real ceiling instead of an un-runnable tier. Encoding the capability map as data now means the eventual per-teammate spawn path reads a validated ceiling rather than rediscovering clamp behavior at run time, and every ladder operation becomes model-truthful fleet-wide.
basis: QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}: 'Note Haiku may clamp the top effort tiers; verify per-model effort support when built.' Engages its worth-it-when by pre-encoding the per-model effort-support map as registry data, de-risking the later spawn-path build; builds beyond the seed (which stops at a warning note) into an enforced capability map.
outcome_shape: PR adding effort_ceiling per model in models.json + clamp()/escalate() consulting it; tests asserting escalate on a clamped model stops at its ceiling. Verified: a haiku/xhigh request resolves to haiku's ceiling with a surfaced note, not a silent un-runnable tier.

title: Tier vocabulary as an authoritative DNS zone with generated resolvers
idea: Extract MODELS/EFFORTS (and the ordered ladder metadata) out of execution_spec.py into one authoritative tier_vocabulary.py module that both execution_spec.py and outcome_spec.py import, instead of hand-maintaining parallel copies guarded by a drift test. Model it on DNS: one authoritative zone-of-record, and every other consumer is a read-only resolver that imports rather than redeclares. Ship a tiny `tier_resolver.py resolve <alias>` CLI so any plugin's agent-loader or team-execution emitter can query the canonical set at load time rather than embedding a literal. The current drift-guard test that asserts two copies stay byte-identical becomes an import assertion — the mirror stops being a copy and becomes a pointer, which is the DNS 'single record, many caches' invariant.
basis: Source domain: DNS authoritative-zone + caching-resolver architecture (RFC 1035) — a single record of authority, arbitrarily many read-only resolvers, drift structurally impossible because caches never redeclare. Seam it attaches to: execution_spec.py:52-53 defines MODELS/EFFORTS as module-local tuples, and the module docstring at :80-81 documents that outcome_spec.py mirrors SANDBOX_PROFILES verbatim behind a cross-module drift-guard test — i.e. the fleet already pays the hand-copy-plus-guard tax the DNS pattern eliminates.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_vocabulary.py, rewiring execution_spec.py + outcome_spec.py to import it, and adding tier_resolver.py CLI; verified by the existing drift-guard test converting to an identity/import assertion (both modules reference one object) plus a new test that `tier_resolver.py resolve fable` exits 0 and an unknown alias exits non-zero.

title: Effort as a DSCP class marking carried in agent frontmatter
idea: Add an `effort:` field to agent frontmatter across the fleet as a first-class dimension alongside `model:`, borrowing the DiffServ/DSCP model from packet networks: every packet carries a small class marking (a first-class header field) that routers honor per-hop rather than re-deriving it. Today every one of the 24 team-execution agents (and all frontmatter fleet-wide) hardcodes `model:` and carries zero `effort:`, so effort is invisible until saga's plan tier-table re-invents it per run. Give each agent a declared effort marking that the dispatch/agent-loader honors, defaulting to the model's historical effort when absent (Postel-style graceful default). Add a loader lint that rejects an effort value outside EFFORTS — the DSCP 'unknown class → drop or default, never silently misroute' rule.
basis: Source domain: DiffServ/DSCP per-hop-behavior class marking (packets self-describe their service class in a header field honored downstream). Direct anchor: grounding brief §1 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution), no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern' — effort exists as a tier axis in execution_spec.py:53 but has no frontmatter representation to carry it.
outcome_shape: PR adding `effort:` to team-execution agent frontmatter (all 24) plus a frontmatter-schema lint in tests that asserts every effort value ∈ EFFORTS and defaults-when-absent; verified by the lint test going green over the whole agents/ tree and a fixture agent with `effort: bogus` failing it.

title: Iterative-deepening escalate() primitive that walks a HALT up the tier ladder
idea: Make the tier ladder's ordering an operational primitive, not just implicit index arithmetic buried in segment_units(). Borrow iterative deepening from game-tree search: start at a shallow (cheap) tier and, on an inconclusive/HALT result, re-run one rung deeper until a budget stop — chess engines do exactly this with search depth. Add `tier_ladder.next_rung(tier)` returning the next stronger model / higher effort per the load-bearing ordering, and a bounded retry policy in the workflow harness so a cheap unit that HALTs escalates one rung and re-runs instead of failing the whole spec. This turns {#tier-vocab-ordering}'s 'tiers are ordered ladders' from a documented fact into executable behavior, and gives cost-optimal 'cheapest tier that succeeds' rather than pre-committing xhigh-Opus on everything.
basis: Source domain: iterative-deepening depth-first search (start shallow, deepen on inconclusive result until a resource bound). Builds on (does not cross) binding decision {#tier-vocab-ordering}: LEARNINGS.md:164 states tier tuples are ordered escalation ladders, and execution_spec.py:1474-1475 already does min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index) upgrade-only merge — the ordering primitive exists for merging but is never exposed as a step-up-on-failure operation.
outcome_shape: PR adding tier_ladder.next_rung() to the tier module + a bounded escalate-on-HALT retry in the emitted harness/emitter, gated by a per-unit max_escalations cap; verified by a unit test asserting next_rung(sonnet/medium) == the next stronger rung per ordering and a harness test that a HALTing cheap unit re-emits at the next rung then stops at the cap.

title: Model palette as a HAL driver-registry with explicit rank, not positional tuples
idea: Replace the positional MODELS/EFFORTS tuples — whose ordering is silently load-bearing — with an explicit ordered registry of rows, each declaring model id + rank + capability flags, modeled on an operating-system Hardware Abstraction Layer driver table: new hardware ships as one new driver row, the kernel is untouched. Adding Claude 6 (or a new fable-class model) becomes a single registry row with an explicit rank, not a fleet-wide edit where getting tuple position wrong silently mis-ranks the model below haiku (the exact #285 failure where appending 'fable' would have ranked it weaker than haiku with no validation error). Add a CI guard `check_tier_registry.py` asserting ranks are total-ordered and unique so a mis-ranked new entry fails loudly rather than mis-tiering merges.
basis: Source domain: OS Hardware Abstraction Layer / driver-registration table (new device = new driver row with declared attributes; core code never edited). Direct anchor + engages binding {#tier-vocab-ordering}: LEARNINGS.md:164 records that enabling Claude 5 tiers 'looked like append two tuple entries' but appending fable would have made segment_units() rank it weaker than haiku — a silent mis-tier, not a validation failure, because ordering and membership are two contracts in one tuple. Explicit rank rows separate the two contracts.
outcome_shape: PR converting MODELS/EFFORTS to an explicit ranked registry (rows with id+rank), updating segment_units() index arithmetic to read declared rank, plus tests/check_tier_registry.py CI guard; verified by the existing test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh still passing and a new test that a duplicate/gapped rank fails the guard.

title: Per-teammate effort as cascading score dynamics with a resolved-tier provenance trail
idea: Go beyond the QUEUED 'plan can dictate per-teammate effort' seed by giving the override a resolution cascade and a provenance record, borrowing from an orchestral score: the ensemble carries a default dynamic (mezzo-forte) but each part's staff can carry its own marking that overrides locally, and a reader can always see which layer set a note's dynamic. Define a three-layer cascade — plan default tier → team default → per-teammate override — where most-specific wins, and emit a resolved-tier audit line per teammate recording which layer set it ('teammate worker-saga: effort=high, source=per-teammate override; model=opus, source=team default'). This makes the override auditable and prevents the silent-mis-tier failure mode the fleet already fears, rather than a bare unlabeled effort knob.
basis: Source domain: orchestral score dynamics — an ensemble default overridden per-part on each staff, with every marking's origin visible on the page (a cascade with provenance). Direct anchor: grounding brief §5 names {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} as 'plan-dictated per-teammate effort — exactly the why-cant-I-pick-effort ask', and §1 confirms 0/24 team-execution agents carry effort; this idea supplies the cascade-resolution + provenance the bare seed lacks.
outcome_shape: PR extending the team-execution worker table / .team-execution.json shape with an optional per-teammate effort override, a resolver that computes final tier by most-specific-layer-wins, and an emitted per-teammate resolved-tier provenance line; verified by a unit test of the cascade (per-teammate beats team beats plan) and a golden-file test that the emitted worker table shows the source layer per teammate.

title: Fleet-wide tier-vocab parity guard modeled on ISO 4217 currency-code validation
idea: Treat the tier palette as the theme's own metaphor makes literal — a currency — and enforce it the way payment systems enforce ISO 4217 currency codes: a central code registry plus validators everywhere that reject any code not in it. Add a repo-level test that statically scans every plugin's agent frontmatter, SKILL.md tier tables, and any config carrying model/effort strings, and asserts each string is a member of the canonical vocabulary module (from idea 1) — so the day fable/xhigh or a Claude 6 tier lands, any plugin still carrying a stale or misspelled tier fails CI instead of silently dispatching to a nonexistent model. This is the propagation enforcement layer: it does not centralize the vocabulary, it proves every consumer actually tracks the center.
basis: Source domain: ISO 4217 currency-code registry + ubiquitous validators (any system touching money validates the 3-letter code against the central list; an unknown code is rejected at the boundary, never processed). Attaches to the grounding-brief §1 finding that fable/xhigh are 'unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary' and model strings are hardcoded per-frontmatter fleet-wide — there is no fleet-wide validator asserting those scattered literals track a single source. Distinct from the QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} seed, which guards marketplace registry metadata, not tier-vocabulary parity.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/test_tier_vocab_fleet_parity.py that globs plugins/**/agents/*.md frontmatter + known tier-table/config sites, extracts model/effort tokens, and asserts membership in the canonical set; verified by the test going green across the current tree and a deliberately-planted stale tier ('opus-high') in a fixture failing it.

title: Effort as a spendable budget under a Kubernetes-style ResourceQuota per run
idea: Give the effort dimension a cost weight and a run-level ceiling, borrowing Kubernetes ResourceQuota + QoS classes (Guaranteed/Burstable/BestEffort): pods declare resource requests, a namespace quota caps total spend, and the scheduler refuses admission past the cap. Attach an estimated relative cost weight to each (model, effort) rung and let a plan/run declare a budget ceiling; dispatch sums the declared unit tiers and HALTs (never silently downgrades) if the spec would exceed the ceiling, surfacing the cheaper-fallback recommendation the intake §4 fable-spend lever already mandates. This turns effort from a per-unit label into a fleet-wide accounting unit — the operator sees 'this spec costs 4.2 budget units, ceiling 3.0' before it runs, matching the HALT-not-degrade posture from the /outcome campaign binding.
basis: Source domain: Kubernetes ResourceQuota + QoS classes (declared per-object requests, namespace-level ceiling, admission refused rather than silently throttled). First-principles argument: effort is already an ordered ladder (execution_spec.py:53) and intake §4 requires every fable-tier line to 'carry a recommendation plus cheaper fallback; expensive never silent default' — a ladder with an ordering but no magnitude cannot answer 'how much does this whole spec cost'; assigning each rung a relative weight is the minimal addition that makes a run-level ceiling computable, and the /outcome binding's HALT-not-degrade rule dictates the over-budget behavior (refuse, not downgrade) rather than my inventing one.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cost-weight table per (model,effort) rung + an optional run-level budget ceiling in the execution-spec, with validate() summing declared unit tiers and raising SpecError when the ceiling is exceeded; verified by a unit test that an over-ceiling spec fails validate with a message naming the total vs ceiling, and an under-ceiling spec passes.

title: Single-source tier palette registry with fleet-wide drift guard
idea: Flip the palette-churn constraint to the extreme: assume a new Claude model lands every day, so zero fleet-wide edits can be tolerated per arrival. Today MODELS/EFFORTS is a hardcoded tuple at execution_spec.py:52-53 and 33 agent frontmatters independently hardcode `model:`, so a new tier means editing the validator and hunting every consumer. Extract the palette into one source-of-truth module (tier_palette.py or a JSON the module imports) that preserves the load-bearing ordering (strongest-first models, weakest-first efforts), and add a CI drift-guard test asserting every `plugins/*/agents/*.md` `model:` value is a member of the palette. Absorbing a new model becomes one registry edit plus an auto-passing guard; a typo like `opus-high` (the failure execution_spec.py:48 explicitly fears) fails the guard loudly.
basis: execution_spec.py:52-53 `MODELS=("fable","opus","sonnet","haiku")` / `EFFORTS`; grep found 33 independent `^model:` lines across plugins/*/agents/*.md; LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering} shows a naive append silently mis-tiered fable weaker than haiku. Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} revisit by making the registry itself carry the ordering contract, not contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/tier_palette.py (or palette JSON) as SoT, execution_spec.py importing MODELS/EFFORTS from it, and tests/test_tier_palette_drift.py asserting frontmatter model membership. Verified: add a fake model to one agent frontmatter -> drift test goes red; add it to the registry -> green.

title: Per-phase tier declaration blocks in the interactive judgment skills
idea: Flip zero-operator to fully-autonomous: imagine each judgment skill must self-declare the tier it wants for every internal phase, with no operator present to pick. Grounding correction (c) confirms the {model,effort} tier vocabulary and fable/xhigh reachability live ONLY in /plan's unit table (plan/SKILL.md:296-352) and are absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work's interactive flow. Add a compact `## Tier vocabulary` front-block to each of those SKILL.md files naming the recommended {model,effort} per sub-phase (e.g. divergent frames -> opus/max, blind novelty hunt -> fable/xhigh, mechanical dedup -> sonnet/medium), making fable/xhigh citeable and reachable in the judgment flows rather than only in plan. A doc-lint asserts the block exists and every tier string it cites is in the canonical palette.
basis: Grounding brief correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS/tier vocab is 'Still absent from /ideate, /brainstorm, /work interactive flow'; grounding §1: /plan's unit tier table is 'the fleet's ONE operator-facing model/effort lever'. fable/xhigh 'unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary'.
outcome_shape: PR editing plugins/saga/skills/{ideate,brainstorm,work}/SKILL.md to add a Tier-vocabulary block, plus a doc-lint test (grep-based) asserting block presence and palette-membership of cited tiers. Verified: lint fails a branch that cites `opus-max-plus`.

title: Effort as a first-class frontmatter and worker-config field, at model parity
idea: Flip the axis count to one: imagine effort is the ONLY tier axis operators touch and model is derived. That extreme exposes that today effort has no independent home at all: grounding confirms 0 of 24 team-execution agents carry an `effort:` field and every frontmatter carries only `model:`, while the A7 worker table renders tier as a fused `opus/high` string with no separable effort knob. Give effort parity with model: add an optional `effort:` key to the agent frontmatter schema (documented in CLAUDE.md's plugin structure), an `effort` key in the `.team-execution.json` worker spec, and split the A7 Tier column so effort is explicit and independently overridable. The ExecutionSpec unit already carries {model,effort}; this closes the loop so effort survives from spec through team rendering instead of collapsing into a fused label.
basis: Grounding §1: 'zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution), no dispatch-time override lever anywhere'; team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233 A7 worker table renders Tier as fused `opus/high`; execution_spec.py:10-11 states units carry per-unit {model,effort}.
outcome_shape: PR adding optional `effort:` to agent frontmatter (schema + CLAUDE.md doc), an `effort` worker key in team-execution SKILL.md/references, and a split Tier/Effort column in the A7 table, with a frontmatter-schema test. Verified: rendered worker table shows per-worker effort; schema test rejects an unknown effort value.

title: Gated auto-escalation one rung up the tier ladder on unit failure
idea: Flip to fully-autonomous retry: every failing leaf climbs the tier ladder by itself. {#tier-vocab-ordering} establishes that MODELS/EFFORTS are ordered escalation ladders and segment_units() already does index arithmetic (min(MODELS.index)/max(EFFORTS.index), execution_spec.py:1474-1475) to pick the stronger tier for merges, but that ordering is never used for retry. Add an `escalate_tier(tier)` helper returning the next rung (bump effort first, then model), and offer it as /work's round-N recovery when a unit fails validate/verify. Because tier escalation is spend-increasing, intake tension 1 and {#operator-choice-framework} require it stay operator-gated in attended runs; the design surfaces the proposed next rung and its cost delta and only escalates on explicit yes (or silently in unattended cache-tight runs). The autonomy flip is unrealistic as a silent default, but its kernel - a reusable ladder-walk primitive - is the missing piece the ordering was already built for.
basis: LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering} + execution_spec.py:49-53 (ordering load-bearing) and :1474-1475 (min/max index merge). Crosses {#operator-choice-framework}: engaged via its spend-gate revisit - escalation stays doc-only/operator-gated in attended runs per intake tension 1, silent only in unattended cache-tight mode.
outcome_shape: PR adding escalate_tier() to execution_spec.py with a unit test walking each rung to the top, plus a /work SKILL.md recovery step that proposes the next rung on failure (gated). Verified: unit test asserts sonnet/high -> sonnet/xhigh -> opus/low ladder walk; doc step shows the gate.

title: Ladder-monotonicity invariant test generalizing the tier-vocab guard
idea: Flip the ordering constraint to nothing: pretend tiers are an unordered flat set and ask what silently breaks. The answer is exactly the {#tier-vocab-ordering} incident - appending fable validated fine but ranked it weaker than haiku in every merge. That regression is currently guarded by a single example test (test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh). Generalize it into a parametrized ladder-invariant contract test that, for every adjacent pair in MODELS and in EFFORTS, asserts segment_units()'s merge picks the stronger member, so ANY future reordering or mid-tuple insertion fails loudly rather than shipping a silent mis-tier. This turns the LEARNINGS rule ('grep for .index( before extending a closed vocabulary') from tribal knowledge into an executable invariant.
basis: LEARNINGS {#tier-vocab-ordering}: guard is one example test `test_segment_tier_merge_prefers_fable_and_xhigh` in tests/test_team_emitter.py; execution_spec.py:49-53 ordering comment + :1474-1475 merge arithmetic. Directly implements the decision's intent (tiers are ordered ladders) at fleet-guard strength.
outcome_shape: PR adding a parametrized ladder-monotonicity test over all adjacent MODELS/EFFORTS pairs and a CONTRIBUTING note pointing to it. Verified: reorder MODELS (swap opus/haiku) on a scratch branch -> the invariant test fails.

title: Per-teammate effort backed by a model x effort support matrix that halts on invalid combos
idea: Flip to 'every model supports every effort': assume a teammate can be set to any {model,effort} freely. The QUEUED seed {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} already asks for plan-dictated per-teammate effort but flags the real hazard - 'Haiku may clamp top effort tiers; verify per-model effort support when built.' Build beyond the raw seed by encoding a MODEL_EFFORT_SUPPORT matrix as first-class data and wiring the per-teammate override through it: when a teammate is assigned a {model,effort} its model cannot honor (e.g. haiku/xhigh), validate HALTS visibly rather than the harness silently clamping, matching the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade posture. This both unblocks the seed's stated feasibility risk and makes per-teammate overrides safe. Engine-owned workers stay pinned to their chaperone tiers per {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}; the override applies to Claude teammates only.
basis: QUEUED {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}: 'Haiku may clamp top effort tiers; verify per-model effort support when built.' Extends beyond the seed (which only asks for plan->ingest) by adding the support matrix + halt. Honors {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (engine workers excluded) and /outcome HALT-not-degrade binding.
outcome_shape: PR adding MODEL_EFFORT_SUPPORT to execution_spec.py, a validate() check that halts on unsupported combos, a per-teammate `effort` field in team-execution consuming it, and a test asserting haiku/xhigh exits non-zero. Verified: set a worker to haiku/xhigh -> validate fails loudly.

title: Shared work-shape -> tier resolver callable from every plugin
idea: Flip to 100 citation sites: imagine the work-shape-to-tier heuristic had to be restated in a hundred places across the fleet. Today it lives only as prose in one table (plan/SKILL.md:298-304 - judgment->opus/high, mechanical->sonnet/medium or haiku/low, read-only survey->sonnet/low, offload->sonnet/medium, second-opinion->opus/high). Propagate it as callable data: add a WORK_SHAPE_TIERS mapping plus an `execution_spec.py tier <shape>` subcommand so any plugin (team-execution, office-hours, mission-control triage spawns) resolves a tier from one source instead of re-deriving the heuristic by hand and drifting. This is the tier-vocabulary analog of the contract-mirror-drift pain grounding §3 ranks the #1 cross-repo recurrence.
basis: plan/SKILL.md:298-304 heuristic exists only as prose in the ONE lever (grounding §1); grounding §3 ranks contract-mirror/hand-copy drift the #1 cross-repo recurrence (validate_card_body stale copy -> #222), so a callable resolver is the drift-proof shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding WORK_SHAPE_TIERS dict + `execution_spec.py tier <shape>` subcommand, citing it from team-execution and office-hours docs, with a test covering every shape key. Verified: CLI returns the correct {model,effort} for each shape; test fails if a shape is dropped.

title: Spend-posture as a first-class handoff field every fan-out site reads
idea: Today the time-vs-money posture lives only in an operator's head at run start, and each fan-out site (team-execution reviewer spawn, saga verify panel, /outcome leaf dispatch, workflow emitter) silently defaults to whatever the author hard-coded. Add one `spend_posture` field to the saga->team handoff envelope and the workflow/outcome dispatch context, carrying the once-per-run answer (`cache-tight-serial` | `throughput`) plus a `mode` tag (unattended|attended). Every spend-increasing branch (parallel fan-out, cache-churning re-spawn, tier escalation) reads that field: unattended proceeds cache-first silently; attended requires an explicit operator yes before widening. The intake resolved this lever to be encoded in the plugins, not hard-coded cache-first, so the deliverable is the encoding itself.
basis: Intake brief section 1 (tension 1): 'This lever is itself a design requirement... plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded cache-first mandate,' with the asymmetric approval rule (unattended->cache-tight-serial silent; attended->any spend-increasing choice always requires explicit operator yes). This is the resolved tension, not a crossing of any binding DECISION.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `spend_posture` field to the saga execution envelope (`plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py`) and reading it at the reviewer-fan-out / verify-panel / outcome-dispatch prose (`consensus-protocol.md`, `outcome/SKILL.md`), plus a schema drift-guard test asserting each spend-increasing site consults the field; release surfaces (plugin.json/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json) updated. Verified by a dry-run under each mode showing the attended path halts for confirmation and the unattended path proceeds silently.

title: Derive a per-segment reuse-gap estimate so shed/keep-warm is deterministic, not a blanket heuristic
idea: The settled architecture derives (segment+agent+tier) saga-side and resides team-side, but R11's shed rule ('shed rather than keep warm across blocks expected to exceed the ~5-min TTL') is a single global judgment call with no per-segment input. Extend the derive side: from the segment-level dependency graph (R8) compute each segment's expected reuse-gap — the wall-clock distance between its first unit-wave and its next same-segment re-engagement along the critical path — and carry it on the per-segment worker row (R7). The reside side then sheds exactly those segments whose estimated reuse-gap exceeds the 5-min TTL and keeps the rest warm, replacing one blanket rule with a per-segment decision. This extends {#worker-cache-scheduling} inside its own derive-saga/reside-team seam rather than revisiting it.
basis: `docs/plans/2026-06-27-worker-model-cache-scheduling-plan.md` R7 (one worker row per resident segment carrying segment-level Depends-on), R8 (segment deps collapsed from the unit graph; reactive unblocking), R11 (shed across blocks expected to exceed the ~5-min cache TTL). The ~5-min horizon matches Anthropic's default ephemeral cache TTL (claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md). Extends the settled derive-side; does not cross the revisit-when.

Verified against a two-segment plan whose dep ordering forces one long gap.

title: Order the coordinator->worker context package stable-first, volatile-last, by contract
idea: Prompt caching is a prefix match: render order is tools->system->messages and any byte change in the prefix invalidates everything after it, so stable identifiers must physically precede volatile deltas. The chaperone context-package contract lists its fields (plan_pointer, unit_ids, selector, intent, plan_time_resolution_preview, write_set) with no stability ordering, and the consensus re-engagement payload interleaves stable criteria with per-cycle deltas. Rewrite both contracts to mandate stable-first assembly — frozen plan_pointer / unit_ids / criteria ahead of the last cache boundary, per-cycle deltas and run-specific resolution after it — so a worker re-engaged via SendMessage reuses the maximal cached prefix. This preserves the chaperone-dispatch contract (it only reorders fields, never grants the engine executor/residency status).
basis: `external-engine-workers.md` section 1 context-package table (fields enumerated, no stability order) and `consensus-protocol.md:207` (delta-only re-engagement) against the prefix-match render-order invariant in claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md ('any change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it; keep stable content first, volatile last').
outcome_shape: Merged PR reordering and annotating the context-package field table in `external-engine-workers.md` and the re-engagement payload spec in `consensus-protocol.md` to a stable-first / volatile-last contract, plus a lightweight assembly-order assertion in the coordinator handoff test. Verified by a review pass confirming no volatile field precedes a stable one in either contract.

title: Silent-invalidator lint: no volatile token ahead of stable prose in any injected skill/reference
idea: Residency only pays off if the injected prefix is byte-stable across re-engagements; a single timestamp, run-id, UUID, or unsorted-JSON blob interpolated ahead of stable prose silently invalidates the cache for everything after it and turns the whole residency protocol into a silent no-op — the repo's dominant failure class. Build a `check_docs`-style lint that scans SKILL.md files, injected references, and the context-package assembly sites for volatile interpolation placed ahead of stable content, mirroring the context-library's schema-lint-in-CI precedent. It reports each offending site and, where safe, moves the volatile piece after the last stable block. This makes 'did residency actually cache?' auditable statically instead of discovered by a mystified operator staring at token spend.
basis: Anthropic prompt-caching silent-invalidator audit table (claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md): datetime.now()/UUID/unsorted json.dumps/per-request IDs early in the prefix each break caching; 'if cache_read_input_tokens is zero across identical-prefix requests, a silent invalidator is at work.' The lint pattern mirrors named prior art `check_docs.py` (infiquetra-context-library validate.yml CI, grounding brief section 4).
outcome_shape: New `tools/`-hosted lint script + CI wire (matching the check_docs.py schema-lint pattern) that fails on any volatile-token-before-stable-prose finding in `plugins/*/skills/**` and context-assembly modules, plus the fixes it surfaces on first run. Verified by a red/green CI run: a seeded volatile interpolation fails, its relocation passes.

title: Every spawn exits with a residency+cost fact; the coordinator aggregates a run ledger
idea: A read-only recon fan-out burned 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes with no ledger recording where it went, so nobody can tell a cache-warm reuse from a cold re-pay after the fact. Extend the worker-exit provenance manifest — which already carries `effort` — with a residency disposition (`cold-spawn` | `warm-reuse`) and a coarse cost fact (token estimate + wall-clock) produced by the worker/leaf at exit, exactly as /outcome's cost ledger is a leaf-produced fact. The coordinator aggregates these on read into a per-run cache-economics ledger (segments, tiers, cold vs warm, total tokens), never a committed status field, honoring derive-on-read. That turns the 350-450k datum from an anecdote into a per-run measured artifact the operator and /retro can act on.
basis: Grounding brief section 2: '/outcome cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' and 'derived-on-read status, never committed status fields'; `worker-manifest.md` shows the provenance manifest already carries `effort` at worker exit. The 350-450k-tokens-in-<20-min recon datum is the mined measurement-ledger number (grounding brief section 7 singletons). Aligns with the /outcome campaign binding decision rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR extending `provenance_manifest.py` (+ `manifest_store.py` write path) with `residency_disposition` and a coarse `cost_fact`, a coordinator-side aggregator that derives the run ledger on read, and prose in `worker-manifest.md`; producer+consumer+real-CLI e2e test per the dead-wiring rule. Verified by a run whose ledger shows cold-vs-warm segment breakdown and a token total.

title: Residency-benefit regression guard: prove the warm reuse actually cached
idea: The residency protocol claims to re-pay context creation once per reuse boundary, but if a silent invalidator or a byte-unstable prefix creeps in, a 'warm-reuse' spawn silently pays full cold cost every cycle while still reporting reuse — a textbook silent no-op. Using the run ledger's cold/warm dispositions plus the coarse token deltas, add a guard that flags any segment tagged `warm-reuse` whose observed re-engagement cost is indistinguishable from its cold-spawn cost (the ledger's analog of 'cache_read_input_tokens is zero'). The guard surfaces the offending segment and points at the likely cause (prefix drift, below-floor prefix, tool set change) so the residency win is verified, not assumed. This applies the repo's 'did it actually run/persist' discipline to cache economics.
basis: Grounding brief section 6.1: silent no-ops are the dominant failure class and 'any bridge/delegation idea needs did-it-actually-run/persist verification' (agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring learnings). Operationalizes the verified cache-hit check 'if cache_read_input_tokens is zero across repeated identical-prefix requests, a silent invalidator is at work' (claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md). Consumes the ledger from T4-F1-5.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a warm-reuse-benefit assertion over the run ledger (in the coordinator aggregator + a `/retro`-consumable check), with a LEARNINGS.md entry recording the mechanism. Verified by a synthetic ledger where a prefix-drifted segment tagged warm-reuse trips the guard and a genuinely-cached segment passes.

title: Stagger-warm parallel dispatch: fan-out sites fire one, warm the cache, then release the rest
idea: A cache entry is readable only after the first response begins streaming, so N parallel spawns sharing a prefix (a saga verify panel up to VERIFY_N_CAP=7, an /outcome ready-frontier wave, a workflow emitter batch) all pay full price for that shared prefix — the concurrent recon fan-out's exact waste. Propagate the stagger-warm pattern beyond team-execution: fire one spawn, await its first token (or a short warm delay), then release the remaining N-1 so they cache-read the prefix the first one just wrote. The global concurrency cap of 3 makes this natural — the first-of-batch warms while the batch stays within cap. This is orthogonal to residency (it addresses parallel cold-start, not warm reuse), so it extends the cache-economics theme to sites the worker-cache-scheduling decision never touched.
basis: Anthropic concurrent-request timing + fan-out pattern (claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md): 'A cache entry becomes readable only after the first response begins streaming. N parallel requests with identical prefixes all pay full price... send 1 request, await the first streamed token, then fire the remaining N-1.' Fan-out sites verified in grounding brief section 1 (VERIFY_N_CAP=7; unbounded team-execution/outcome/emitter fan-out) and intake concurrency-cap-3.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a stagger-warm dispatch helper and wiring it at the three fan-out site classes: saga verify-panel dispatch (`execution_spec.py` VERIFY path), `/outcome` ready-frontier release (`outcome/SKILL.md` / `outcome_spec.py`), and the workflow emitter batch loop; test asserting batch member 2..N is released only after member 1 streams. Verified by a run whose ledger (T4-F1-5) shows shared-prefix cost paid once, not N times.

title: 1-hour-TTL wave queue for /outcome idle-poll gaps (engaging the revisit-when)
idea: The /outcome coordinator advances a ready frontier across leaves that can sit idle far longer than the 5-min ephemeral TTL between advances, so a resident leaf's cache is dead by the time its next same-segment work arrives — the idle-poll case the worker-cache-scheduling decision explicitly names as its revisit trigger. Engage that revisit-when with a formal wave queue for /outcome dispatch: batch ready leaves into temporally-tight waves to stay inside the 5-min window where possible, and where a gap is unavoidable, offer (as a spend-increasing choice, so attended runs must say yes) an escalation to the 1-hour `ttl:"1h"` cache posture whose doubled write cost only pays off across the bridged gap. Either way the operator sees the cold-re-warm cost coming instead of eating it silently. This is the first cache-economics extension that crosses {#worker-cache-scheduling} rather than living inside it, and it does so through the decision's own named revisit condition.
basis: {#worker-cache-scheduling} revisit-when (grounding brief section 2, verbatim): 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient, or idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue.' The 1-hour TTL economics (`ttl:"1h"`, 2x write vs 1.25x, needs >=3 reads to pay off; keeps entries alive across bursty gaps) are from claude-api shared/prompt-caching.md. /outcome ready-frontier idle-poll is the U-series dispatch path (`outcome_spec.py:531` ready_frontier).
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a wave-queue batching layer to `/outcome` dispatch (`outcome/SKILL.md` + `outcome_spec.py`) that groups ready leaves into TTL-tight waves and, on an unavoidable gap, surfaces the 1-hour-TTL escalation as an attended spend-yes gate (reusing T4-F1-1's posture field); DECISIONS.md entry recording the revisit-when engagement. Verified by an /outcome run with an induced >5-min frontier gap showing the queue either batches within the window or halts for the spend decision.

title: Kill the post-hoc "did caching help?" question — resident workers self-emit a cache-economics ledger line
idea: Today the only cache-economics datum in existence (350-450k tokens in <20min for a recon fan-out) is a mined singleton because there is no standing measurement — KTD4 leaves residency validation to "operator runs + headroom telemetry," i.e. a manual after-the-fact human notice. Invert that step out of existence: every resident worker emits one structured cache fact (cache-creation tokens, cache-read tokens, reuse count, shed events) into the /outcome cost ledger, which grounding brief section 2 already defines as a leaf-produced fact. The retro/operator never has to reconstruct token spend by hand; the ledger already carries it, and reuse-effectiveness becomes a queryable column instead of a lucky recollection. This is a fact-emission line, not the pulse-live-telemetry UI QUEUED seed.
basis: Grounding brief section 2: "/outcome ... cost ledger = leaf-produced fact"; DECISIONS.md:1965-1967 KTD4 leaves residency effectiveness to markdown prose + "operator runs + headroom telemetry" with no standing ledger; section 7 singleton "350-450k tokens in <20 min ... (cache-economics number)" exists only because it was manually mined once.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cache-economics fact schema to the /outcome leaf cost-ledger emitter (plugins/saga/scripts, ledger writer) + a resident-worker emit contract line in team-execution/references/*, verified by a test asserting one cache-fact row per resident worker per run and a real /outcome run showing populated rows.

title: Remove the runtime shed judgment — saga emits an explicit shed/summary-handoff marker per segment boundary
idea: R11 and KTD7 admit there is no live context-GC lever, so shedding is a runtime judgment a resident worker must make from markdown prose — a manual, untestable decision KTD4 concedes is "markdown protocol only." Automate the step away by moving the decision to where the data already lives: saga's segmentation derivation stamps each emitted worker row with an explicit boundary action — reuse, summary-handoff, or shed — so team-execution executes a derived instruction instead of re-deciding at runtime. The A7 worker table (currently Agent|Units|Tier|Mode|Depends-on|Engine|Intent, no boundary column) gains a Boundary column, making the previously prose-only R11/R8 behavior a testable emitted artifact. This extends worker-cache-scheduling's settled "derive saga-side" seam rather than crossing it.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1965-1968 KTD4/KTD5 ("behavioral residency is markdown protocol... R15a context-GC excluded — no harness lever"); worker table at team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md:226-230 has no shed/boundary column; plan R11 (shed at boundary expected to exceed ~5-min TTL) and R8 (segment-dep collapse) are derivable saga-side.
outcome_shape: PR threading a per-segment boundary action through the saga emitter and adding a Boundary column to the A7 worker table + external-engine-workers.md, verified by team_emitter round-trip tests asserting the derived action and a doc-review of the updated protocol.

title: Ban prefix-busting volatile tokens — a stable-prefix lint so cached prompt prefixes never silently invalidate
idea: Prompt-cache economics collapse the moment a volatile token (timestamp, run-id, live board status) sits above the stable content in a prompt, because it invalidates the whole 5-min-TTL prefix for every reuse — and nobody checks this by hand today. Remove the manual audit by making it a lint: a marketplace-CI-adjacent guard scans agent frontmatter and skill prompt templates and fails when volatile markers appear before the stable-reference block, forcing stable content (skill body, references/) into the cacheable prefix and volatile context into the shed tail. The best version of "remember to keep prefixes stable" is a check that makes forgetting impossible. Distinct from the marketplace-ci-guard QUEUED seed (that guards registry drift; this guards prompt-cache prefix stability).
basis: First-principles: Anthropic prompt caching keys on an exact prefix match under a ~5-min TTL (plan R11 cites the same window); any token that varies per-turn placed before the stable block forces a full cache-creation instead of a cache-read, so a single misplaced timestamp erases the reuse win worker-cache-scheduling was built to capture. No lint enforces prefix ordering across the 8 plugins today.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/lint_prompt_prefix_stability.py wired into CI, plus a test_prompt_prefix_stability.py fixture over agents/*.md and skill templates; verified by the lint failing on a seeded volatile-prefix agent and passing the current tree after any fixes.

title: Stop re-reading the whole diff every review round — hand reviewers a derived delta packet via typed artifact pointer
idea: consensus-protocol re-spawns fresh reviewers each consensus round, each cold-reading the whole plan + diff + criteria; R5 says sub-threshold reviewers should instead be re-engaged with only the delta, but that is prose today and untested. Remove the cold re-read step: saga derives the review delta since the last round and passes it as a typed artifact pointer (the #291 seam that just merged), so the resident reviewer consumes a handed delta packet instead of reconstructing context from scratch. This turns R5 from markdown aspiration into an emitted, testable artifact and compounds the residency win worker-cache-scheduling already banked. It extends the settled architecture (reuse via SendMessage) rather than engaging its revisit-when.
basis: Plan R5 (docs/plans/2026-06-27-worker-model-cache-scheduling-plan.md:52-54: "re-engagement context SHALL carry delta since last review, not full diff") is prose-only; typed artifact-pointer passing merged as #291 (docs/plans/2026-07-02-typed-artifact-pointer-passing-plan.md) provides the handoff seam; consensus-protocol.md re-spawn cited at plan:26.
outcome_shape: PR wiring a saga-derived review-delta artifact-pointer into the team-execution review-loop residency path + reference update, verified by a test asserting round N>=2 reviewers receive a delta pointer (not full diff) and the delta artifact round-trips.

title: Remove the coordinator's idle-poll-and-re-ping ritual — a within-run wave queue that dispatches the instant a resident frees
idea: worker-cache-scheduling's revisit-when explicitly names this: "a single team-execution run shows enough internal idle-poll to justify a formal within-run wave queue" — and section 7 pattern 9 (subagents idle without delivering; coordinator must detect and re-ping) was reproduced live in the very ideation session. Automate the manual poll away: a formal segment wave queue holds ready segments and dispatches the next one the moment a resident worker completes and frees a slot, under the global concurrency-3 cap, so no human or coordinator loop babysits idleness. This is the sanctioned revisit path, not a contradiction of the settled architecture — it fires exactly the condition the decision reserved. The queue subordinates to saga's coordinator-level ready_frontier (R10) so leaf ordering stays source-of-truth.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1970-1971 revisit-when: "or a single team-execution run shows enough internal idle-poll to justify a formal within-run wave queue"; grounding section 7 pattern 9 ("Subagents idle without delivering... also reproduced live in this very session"); plan R10 (segment frontier subordinate to outcome_spec.py:531 ready_frontier).
outcome_shape: PR adding a within-run wave-queue scheduler to team-execution (reactive segment dispatch under concurrency cap, subordinate to ready_frontier) + tests covering free-slot dispatch and cap enforcement; verified by a test simulating a resident completing and the next ready segment dispatching without a poll.

title: Stop each /outcome leaf from spawning its plugin-segment worker cold — a cross-leaf resident crew
idea: worker-cache-scheduling's residency lives inside one team-execution run; across an /outcome DAG, sibling leaves that touch the same plugin-directory segment each spawn a fresh worker, re-paying full context creation per leaf — the exact "named-teammate residency proves insufficient (revisit warm-pool / crew-pairing)" condition the decision reserved. Remove the per-leaf cold spawn: a cross-leaf resident crew keeps a named worker per plugin-directory segment alive across the DAG's ready frontier, reusing the SendMessage handle and accumulated segment summary so leaf N inherits leaf N-1's warm context instead of rebuilding it. The honest limit is that raw prompt-cache hits decay past the 5-min TTL between leaves, so the reused asset is the warm teammate + carried segment summary, not a guaranteed cache-read — the win is worker reuse, not TTL magic. This engages the revisit-when directly rather than silently crossing it.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1970 revisit-when: "Named-teammate residency proves insufficient (revisit warm-pool / crew-pairing)"; grounding brief §1 corrections (h): /outcome leaf dispatch is the real decomposition path and each leaf currently spawns independently; segment boundary = plugin directory (KTD2, DECISIONS.md:1962).
outcome_shape: PR extending the /outcome dispatch spec (outcome_spec.py / dispatch reference) with a per-segment cross-leaf resident-crew registry keyed on plugin directory + reuse protocol doc, verified by a test asserting two sibling leaves on the same segment reuse one worker id and a DECISIONS entry recording the revisit-when firing.

title: Collapse the recon fan-out's N cold repo reads into one shared context pack
idea: The 350-450k-tokens-in-<20min datum comes from read-only recon fan-outs where N agents each cold-read the same repo survey (inventory, journal, seam files) — N independent cache-creations of a near-identical prefix. Remove the duplication: pre-assemble the common repo-survey once into a shared context pack that every fan-out worker receives as an identical stable prefix, so the fleet pays one cache-creation and N-1 cache-reads instead of N creations. This propagates worker-cache-scheduling's reuse principle from team-execution into the recon/ideation workflow surface that produced the datum in the first place, and it is the highest-leverage attack on the one measured cache number the fleet has. Under the attended-run posture, spinning the fan-out at all stays a spend-increasing choice needing explicit yes; the pack only changes the per-worker cost, not the fan-out decision.
basis: First-principles on the section-7 singleton (350-450k tokens, <20min recon fan-out): recon workers share a near-identical read-only prefix; N separate spawns each trigger a full cache_creation of that prefix, whereas one pre-assembled shared prefix under the 5-min TTL converts N-1 of them to cache_read — a linear-to-constant reduction in creation cost with no change to the fan-out decision or its outputs.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared recon-context-pack builder used by recon/ideation fan-out dispatch (scripts + workflow reference) so all workers receive one identical prefix, verified by a ledger-instrumented before/after run showing a single cache-creation with N-1 cache-reads on the shared block.

title: Turn the time-vs-money posture from aspiration into machinery — a guard that blocks silent spend-increase
idea: The intake resolves posture as "asked once per run, cache-first the only silent default; any spend-increasing choice always requires explicit operator yes" — but section 7 pattern 4 records the twin finding that such caps are "aspiration, not machinery" (the emitter had no concurrency knob). Remove the silent-spend path entirely: a run-start posture prompt writes one run-scoped posture token (cache-tight-serial | throughput) that saga /work, team-execution fan-out, and /outcome dispatch all read, and a guard intercepts any fan-out / cache-churn / tier-escalation that exceeds the cache-tight default and blocks it unless the throughput token is set. The operator is asked exactly once and is never silently over-spent; the resolved tension becomes enforced plumbing instead of a prose promise. Unattended runs (/outcome, /loop) default to cache-tight and proceed silently, matching tension 1.
basis: Intake brief tension 1 ("Cache-first only silent default... any spend-increasing choice ... always requires explicit operator yes... Asked once per run") + "This lever is itself a design requirement... plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded cache-first mandate"; grounding §7 pattern 4 ("the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery").
outcome_shape: PR adding a run-scoped posture token (written by a single run-start prompt) read by saga /work, team-execution fan-out, and /outcome dispatch, plus a guard hook that blocks spend-increasing dispatch without the throughput token; verified by a test asserting a cache-tight run blocks an unapproved fan-out and a throughput run permits it.

title: Prime-then-fill batch dispatch: make the cache-first posture a real cache mechanic, not a vibe
idea: The time-vs-money posture (intake tension 1) is treated as a scheduling choice about serial-vs-parallel, but its actual cache lever is left unstated: N same-agent workers fired simultaneously all pay full price for their identical system-prompt/tool prefix because none can read a cache the others are still writing. Reframe the posture one level up as a dispatch-ORDERING decision the harness already permits without any cache_control API: under cache-first, spawn one worker of a segment/agent-type, wait for it to establish (first output), then release the rest of the batch so they read the just-written prefix; under attended/throughput, fire the whole batch. Encode `posture` as a machine-checked enum on the execution spec (asked once per run per tension 1) that the fan-out loop and verify-panel spawn read, rather than leaving 'cache-first' as prose nobody can enforce. This turns the operator's once-per-run answer into a concrete spawn schedule.
basis: Anthropic prompt-caching guidance (claude-api skill, shared/prompt-caching.md §Concurrent-request timing): 'N parallel requests with identical prefixes all pay full price — none can read what the others are still writing... send 1 request, await the first streamed token, then fire the remaining N−1.' Plus §Pre-warming (max_tokens:0 prime). The 350–450k recon fan-out fires same-agent workers in parallel, exactly this waste shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `posture` enum + resolver to plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py (ordered per {#tier-vocab-ordering} conventions) and a prime-then-fill dispatch step to team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md + saga verify-panel spawn prose; verified by a unit test on the posture resolver (defaults: unattended→cache-first, attended→ask) and a doc-review pass confirming the dispatch protocol.

title: Cache-clustering topological order: unit ordering is a choice segment_units silently obeys
idea: segment_units() groups CONTIGUOUS units only — 'a non-contiguous re-appearance of the same engine/segment opens a new resident (worker-agy-2)' — so the authored unit ORDER, not just the plugin-directory boundary, determines how many residents exist and thus how much cache reuse is possible. The plan currently treats unit order as fixed-as-authored; it is actually free within the dependency DAG. Add a dependency-respecting topological reordering that clusters same-segment units adjacent before segmentation, collapsing interleaved re-appearances (worker-x ... worker-y ... worker-x) into a single resident run. This extends {#worker-cache-scheduling} rather than contradicting it — same plugin-directory boundary (KTD2), same derive-saga-side seam — it just stops the contiguity rule from leaking scheduling cost onto arbitrary authoring order.
basis: plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:1399-1435 (segment_units contiguous grouping) with the inline comment at :1404-1408: 'One resident chaperone per contiguous run... a non-contiguous re-appearance of the same engine... opens a new resident (worker-agy-2).' Resident count is therefore order-sensitive, and Unit.depends_on gives the freedom to reorder safely.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `cluster_order(spec)` topological pre-pass in plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py invoked before segment_units, with a pytest asserting interleaved same-segment units collapse to one resident when deps allow (and are left untouched when deps forbid); resident-count reduction shown in test fixtures.

title: Crew-pairing by context-overlap: retire plugin-directory as the residency proxy (gated on evidence)
idea: KTD2 fixes segment = plugin directory as a static proxy for 'units that share cache-warming context,' but the real cache benefit is context OVERLAP — the files and references a resident teammate has already read — which the plugin directory only approximates. Two units in the same plugin touching disjoint files share little warm context; two units across plugins reading the same shared references share a lot. Reframe residency scheduling around a context-overlap graph over Unit.files (added in the doc-review addendum precisely to enable file-level segmentation), pairing high-overlap units onto one resident — the crew-pairing path the decision itself names. This crosses the binding {#worker-cache-scheduling} KTD2, so it is explicitly gated: it ships only if the T4-F3-6 A/B benchmark shows flat plugin-directory residency underperforming its potential reuse.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1970-1971 revisit-when: 'Named-teammate residency proves insufficient (revisit warm-pool / crew-pairing).' KTD2 (DECISIONS.md:1962) grounds segment=plugin-dir on 'Single monorepo; VECU's repo-change proxy never fires,' and the addendum's added Unit.files field is the overlap-computation substrate.
outcome_shape: Gated PR (blocked on T4-F3-6 evidence) adding an overlap-graph crew-pairing mode to segment_units in execution_spec.py behind a resolver flag, plus a DECISIONS.md addendum recording the revisit trigger and the measured insufficiency; verified by pytest on the pairing over synthetic file-overlap fixtures.

title: Prefix-stability lint: cache economics is set at authoring time, not just runtime
idea: KTD5 excludes context-GC as 'no harness lever (Messages-API-only),' and the team treats cache economics as a runtime concern the harness owns — but the agent frontmatter and the emitter-generated worker prompts ARE the cache prefix, and their byte-stability is fully within our control at authoring time. A date, run-id, epoch, or unsorted-JSON blob interpolated EARLY in an agent's system prompt silently busts the shared-prefix cache for every parallel spawn of that agent, and nothing checks for it today. Reframe cache economics one level up as a design-time discipline: a prefix-stability lint that scans agents/*.md frontmatter and the team_emitter worker-prompt template for volatile-content-in-prefix (timestamps, UUIDs, per-run ids, non-deterministic serialization) and flags anything cache-hostile placed before the stable body. This sidesteps the harness-lever constraint entirely because it operates on files we author, not on Messages-API calls.
basis: claude-api skill shared/prompt-caching.md §Silent invalidators table (datetime.now()/uuid4()/unsorted json.dumps()/session-id-in-system-prompt each 'Prefix changes every request') and §'Keep the system prompt frozen.' KTD5 (DECISIONS.md:1968) confirms no runtime lever — which is why the lever must move to authoring.
outcome_shape: PR adding a prefix-stability lint (new check in an existing marketplace/CI guard or a tools/ script) over plugins/*/agents/*.md frontmatter and the emitted worker-prompt template, wired into CI; verified by a fixture agent with a volatile prefix that the lint fails on, and a clean agent that passes.

title: Cache-economics ledger: make KTD4's named telemetry loop actually exist
idea: KTD4 asserts residency is 'validated by /doc-review + operator runs + headroom telemetry,' but the residency architecture shipped with no ledger that decomposes token spend into cache_read / cache_creation / uncached-input per segment — so the 350–450k recon-fan-out number is an undifferentiated anecdote nobody can attribute to cache behavior. The theme treats that headline number as a fixed cost of recon; it is actually an un-decomposed measurement. Build the ledger substrate: a per-run artifact that harvests the headroom telemetry (headroom_stats) / usage split and rolls it up by resident segment, so residency's token savings become a measured fact rather than a design claim. This makes {#worker-cache-scheduling}'s own validation loop real and is the evidence source that gates T4-F3-3 and T4-F3-6.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1965-1967 KTD4: residency reuse is 'validated by /doc-review + operator runs + headroom telemetry.' The headroom MCP surface (headroom_stats) exists but no ledger consumes it; the 350–450k recon datum (grounding brief §7 singletons) is recorded with no cache_read/creation/input breakdown.
outcome_shape: PR adding a cache-ledger emitter (a tools/ or saga/scripts script) that writes a per-run JSON ledger keyed by resident segment with cache_read/cache_creation/input token columns sourced from headroom telemetry; verified by a unit test over a captured telemetry fixture producing the expected per-segment rollup, aligned with /outcome's 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' contract.

title: Residency A/B benchmark: prove the recon fan-out cache claim before scaling the architecture
idea: The whole residency architecture rests on an unverified belief that keeping same-segment workers resident meaningfully lowers tokens, but no controlled measurement has ever isolated residency-ON vs residency-OFF on a fixed recon fan-out — the community's own validation-discipline rule ('never assert without checking') is being violated by the cache-economics theme itself. Reframe the 350–450k number from a fixed cost into a testable hypothesis: run one representative read-only recon fan-out twice, once with contiguous residency and once with positional worker-{i} (the pre-KTD3 baseline), and read the cache_read/input split from the T4-F3-5 ledger. The output is a decision-grade finding that either validates {#worker-cache-scheduling} as-shipped or fires its revisit-when — becoming the evidence gate for T4-F3-3's crew-pairing. This is a one-shot experiment, not permanent machinery, and it is the honest 'measure before building' move the theme has skipped.
basis: First-principles: residency only saves tokens if same-segment spawns actually achieve cache_read>0; the harness's cross-subagent cache behavior is unverified from inside the fleet, and the concurrent-timing rule means naive parallel spawns can achieve zero reuse even WITH residency. No repo artifact measures the ON/OFF delta, so the architecture's core premise is currently asserted, not checked — a direct conflict with the repo's stated validation-discipline norm.
outcome_shape: Merged benchmark harness (a tools/ script that runs a fixed recon fan-out under residency-on/off) plus a dated LEARNINGS.md entry (Evidence/Mechanism/Generalizable-rule) recording the measured cache_read split and an explicit verdict: KTD confirmed, or revisit-when fired for T4-F3-3.

title: Residency manifest: unlock the derived schedule for /outcome dispatch and verify-panels
idea: segment_units() already produces a structured Segment mapping saga-side, but KTD4 renders residency as 'markdown protocol' — prose in the team-execution worker table — so the derived schedule is machine-readable exactly nowhere except team-execution, and /outcome leaf dispatch plus saga verify-panels (which fan out many same-agent-type workers) get zero residency benefit. The ownership boundary 'reside team-side' is being read as 'residency data is team-execution's alone,' but the derive/reside seam is a producer/consumer pattern like ENGINE_INTENTS; the fix is to widen the consumers, not the producer. Emit the Segment mapping as a structured residency manifest (JSON) alongside the prose table, then have /outcome frontier dispatch cluster same-segment ready leaves into consecutive warm windows and have verify-panel spawn prime-then-fill same-type verifiers. This EXTENDS {#worker-cache-scheduling} (propagation, explicitly permitted) and respects /outcome's derived-on-read rule because the manifest is computed at dispatch time, never committed as status.
basis: plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:1384 segment_units returns list[Segment] (structured, saga-side), but DECISIONS.md:1965 KTD4 states 'behavioral residency is markdown protocol' — so no non-team-execution dispatcher can read it. /outcome verify-panels spawn up to VERIFY_N_CAP=7 same-type readonly-verifiers (execution_spec.py:114) sharing a byte-identical prefix.
outcome_shape: PR adding a residency-manifest emit (Segment mapping → JSON) in execution_spec.py and consumers in /outcome frontier-dispatch and saga verify-panel spawn that read it for segment-clustered ordering; verified by a pytest that the manifest round-trips the segmentation and a doc-review confirming derived-on-read compliance (manifest recomputed, never persisted as board status).

title: Shared run-posture primitive (execution_posture.py) every fan-out site imports
idea: Codify intake tension-1's asymmetric approval rule as reusable machinery instead of prose that each dispatch site re-implements. A single saga-side resolver `execution_posture.py` takes (mode: unattended|attended) and returns a posture object: unattended -> cache-tight-serial, may proceed silently; attended -> throughput recommended but every spend-increasing choice (parallel fan-out, cache churn, tier escalation) requires an explicit operator-yes token or it raises. team-execution wave scheduling, /outcome leaf dispatch, and recon fan-outs all import the one primitive rather than hardcoding a policy. The compounding return: once the lever exists, every future fan-out site inherits the operator-yes gate for free, so the fleet can add dispatch surfaces without re-litigating spend posture each time.
basis: Intake brief section 1 (lines 26-35): 'Unattended runs -> cache-tight serial; may proceed silently... Attended runs -> throughput recommended, but any spend-increasing choice... always requires explicit operator yes. Cache-first only silent default.' Grounding section 1 confirms no shared cap/posture policy exists across team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges (all 'unbounded').
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/execution_posture.py` (pure resolver + `PostureError` on unapproved spend-increase) plus wiring one consumer (team-execution Step B1 wave scheduling reference). Verified by a pytest that the attended+spend-increasing path raises without an approval token and the unattended path returns cache-tight silently, plus release-surface bump per CLAUDE.md step 6.

title: Data-backed posture prompt: emitter computes parallel-width vs critical-path depth
idea: The posture question is 'asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation' but today it would be a blind prompt with no numbers behind it. Extend the emitter so that when it derives segments it also computes the two figures that make the time-vs-money tradeoff concrete: parallel width (count of independent, dependency-free segments) and critical-path depth (already computable via the `critical_path_wall` logic in outcome_costs). The once-per-run posture prompt then shows real stakes: 'N independent segments; throughput spends ~N cold-starts, cache-tight-serial adds ~M min of wall.' This makes the lever from idea T4-F4-1 an informed decision, and the derivation reuses primitives that already exist, so it compounds rather than adds a new estimator.
basis: Intake brief section 1 line 33 ('Asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation'); `critical_path_wall(spec, wall_by_sid)` already exists at `plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_costs.py:134`; segment DAG collapse (parallel width) is produced by `segment_units` (`execution_spec.py:1384`, KTD4 segment-level deps).
outcome_shape: PR extending `team_emitter.py` / a small helper to emit `parallel_width` and `critical_path_estimate` alongside the segment table, surfaced in the team-execution Step A7 worker table and the posture prompt copy. Verified by a unit test over a fixture spec with a known independent-vs-chained mix asserting both numbers, plus a doc-review of the prompt-copy change.

title: Non-contiguous segment re-pairing: reorder-or-warm-pool to stop worker-N cold restarts
idea: segment_units groups strictly contiguous units, so a non-contiguous re-appearance of the same plugin-directory or engine opens a fresh resident (worker-agy-2) that re-pays the full cold context/cache cost even when the same segment key returns within the 5-minute TTL. This is direct evidence that named-teammate residency, as shipped, is insufficient for interleaved unit orderings. Engage the decision's own revisit-when (warm-pool / crew-pairing) with the cheapest form first: a saga-side reorder pass that, among units whose dependencies already allow it, sorts by boundary key so same-key units become contiguous and collapse into one resident. Only where reordering is dependency-blocked does the coordinator keep a resident warm across the gap (crew-pairing). The reorder is a pure saga-side transform with no harness lever, so it lands testably and every future run with interleaved segments inherits the saving.
basis: `plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:1405-1421` comment: 'a non-contiguous re-appearance of the same engine (e.g. interleaved with a Claude unit) opens a new resident (worker-agy-2).' Explicitly engages `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` revisit-when: 'Named-teammate residency proves insufficient (revisit warm-pool / crew-pairing)' (DECISIONS.md:1970).
outcome_shape: PR adding a dependency-preserving reorder step inside/ahead of `segment_units` (stable-sort by boundary key within each dependency-equivalence class) plus a residency-prose note for the blocked-reorder warm-pool fallback. Verified by a pytest fixture with interleaved plugin-dir units asserting the resident count drops from 3 to 2 and no dependency edge is violated.

title: Computable shed trigger: emitter stamps per-segment TTL budget
idea: The context-shedding rule (R11) tells the coordinator to shed a resident 'when a block of time is expected to exceed the prompt cache TTL horizon (~5 minutes),' but leaves 'is expected to exceed' as unaided judgment the coordinator must guess run to run. Give the residency protocol a computable trigger: the emitter stamps each segment with an estimated wall budget (from its tier and unit count) and a boolean `shed_after` when that budget alone exceeds the TTL horizon, so shedding becomes data-driven rather than eyeballed. This turns a soft markdown heuristic into a stamped field that /retro can later audit against realized wall time, compounding the residency plumbing's testable surface (KTD4) rather than adding more prose to interpret.
basis: team-execution `SKILL.md:311` (R11): 'Shed a resident worker at its segment boundary, or when a block of time is expected to exceed the prompt cache TTL horizon (~5 minutes).' KTD4 (DECISIONS.md:1965) makes 'the testable surface the saga-side plumbing,' which a stamped `shed_after` field extends.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `estimated_wall_seconds` + `shed_after` field to the emitted segment row (`team_emitter.py`) and a reference to it from R11 in the residency protocol. Verified by a unit test over a tier/unit-count matrix asserting `shed_after` flips at the ~300s boundary, plus release-surface bump.

title: Stable-prefix context-package primitive shared by seed, re-engagement, and chaperone dispatch
idea: Cross-segment summary handoff (R4), reviewer delta-only re-engagement, and chaperone dispatch all assemble a worker prompt, but nothing enforces the ordering that actually lands a cache hit under the 5-minute TTL: stable/cacheable content (plan, standards, segment brief) must sit BEFORE volatile content (the delta, prior output) so the cacheable prefix is byte-identical across reuses. Build one `context_package` assembly primitive that partitions blocks into stable and volatile and always emits stable-first, and have all three reuse sites call it instead of hand-concatenating. Because prompt-cache hit rate is governed by prefix stability, a single well-ordered assembler lifts cache reuse across every current and future reuse site at once, which is the compounding win.
basis: First-principles prompt-cache mechanics: Anthropic prompt caching keys on the longest byte-identical prefix, so a hit requires stable content to precede volatile content; today R4 (SKILL.md:310), reviewer delta re-engagement (consensus-protocol.md:207), and chaperone dispatch (external-engine-workers.md:27) each assemble context independently with no shared stable-first ordering, so any volatile block placed early silently voids the cacheable prefix for that reuse.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/context_package.py` (stable/volatile partition + stable-first serialize) and switching the three assembly sites to it, with the ordering contract documented in `consensus-protocol.md`. Verified by a unit test asserting two calls that differ only in the volatile block share a byte-identical stable prefix.

title: Add cached-vs-fresh token fields to the cost ledger so residency's value is falsifiable
idea: The residency protocol's entire justification is cache reuse, yet KTD4 says it is validated only by 'operator runs + headroom telemetry' — nothing durable. The cost ledger records tokens, wall, operator_touches, and retries per subplot, but not the split between cached-read tokens and fresh tokens, so the ledger cannot answer 'did residency actually save cache?' Extend `_NUMERIC_FIELDS` and the rollup with `cached_tokens` / `fresh_tokens` (or a reuse ratio), sourced from the worker-exit manifest.
