The DAG-vs-one-thread proof then gains a second axis (cache-reuse ratio), and every residency/cache idea in this theme becomes measurable against a durable number instead of a slogan — turning an unmeasured markdown protocol into a self-auditing one.
basis: `plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_costs.py:41` — `_NUMERIC_FIELDS = ('tokens', 'wall_seconds', 'operator_touches', 'retries')` (no cache split); KTD4 (DECISIONS.md:1965-1967) validates residency only via 'operator runs + headroom telemetry,' i.e. nothing in the durable ledger.
outcome_shape: PR extending `record_cost` / `_NUMERIC_FIELDS` / `rollup` in `outcome_costs.py` with `cached_tokens`+`fresh_tokens` and a reuse-ratio line in the rollup output, plus the worker-exit manifest carrying the split (`worker-manifest.md`). Verified by a pytest over multi-subplot fixtures asserting the reuse ratio is computed and 'no data yet' is preserved when the fields are absent.

title: Grounding-pack shared prefix: one warm read-cache for N-agent recon fan-outs
idea: Pure recon fan-outs burned 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes, and they are the worst cache offenders in the fleet: /ideate divergent agents, /resume forensics, and this very ideation run each spawn N cold agents whose read sets massively overlap (every agent re-reads the same briefs and source files) with zero cache sharing. Assemble the common read set once into a 'grounding pack' — a single stable prefix injected verbatim into every fan-out agent's context — so N agents share one cached prefix instead of paying N cold reads. This propagates the segment-residency cache thesis outward from team-execution to the recon fan-out sites that dominate the token bill, and because it is a shared assembler, every future fan-out command inherits the multiplier.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 singleton: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number).' Grounding section 1: /outcome leaf dispatch and engine bridges are 'unbounded'; recon fan-out sites (/ideate, /resume) carry no residency or shared-prefix mechanism (verified absent — worker-cache-scheduling scope is team-execution only, DECISIONS.md:1955-1956).
outcome_shape: PR adding a `grounding_pack` assembler (saga-side) plus wiring it into one fan-out command's dispatch (e.g. /ideate divergent agents) so each agent's prompt opens with the identical pack prefix. Verified by driving a small fan-out and confirming a shared byte-identical prefix across two spawned agents' assembled prompts, plus a doc note in the command's SKILL.md.

title: Reuse segment_units at /outcome leaf dispatch to group ready-frontier leaves cache-tight
idea: The segment-boundary primitive (segment = plugin directory) already exists and is battle-tested in the emitter, but /outcome leaf dispatch is a separate, unbounded cold-spawn path that ignores it — each ready-frontier leaf saga launches cold even when several leaves touch the same plugin directory and could share a warm resident. Propagate the settled primitive to a second consumer: at the /outcome coordinator, group the ready frontier by `segment_units`-style plugin-directory key into cache-tight dispatch waves, so co-located leaves reuse context. This is high-leverage because the derivation is already written and tested; extending worker-cache-scheduling to /outcome is reuse of an existing seam, not a new architecture, and it aligns with (extends) the binding decision rather than contradicting it.
basis: `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` KTD2 (DECISIONS.md:1962): 'segment boundary = plugin directory'; `segment_units` at `execution_spec.py:1384`. Grounding section 1: '/outcome leaf dispatch ... unbounded' with no residency/cache grouping. This extends the settled architecture to a new consumer (aligned, not a revisit-when trip).
outcome_shape: PR adding a plugin-directory grouping step to the /outcome coordinator's ready-frontier dispatch (reusing the `segment_units` boundary-key logic) and a residency note in the /outcome SKILL.md dispatch section. Verified by a unit test over a ready frontier with two same-plugin + one cross-plugin leaf asserting the same-plugin pair is grouped into one cache-tight wave.

title: Run-start posture as a capacity-reservation class (spot vs on-demand vs reserved)
idea: Model the once-per-run time-vs-money decision on AWS EC2's purchasing classes: a RunPosture declared at saga run start that behaves like choosing spot (cache-tight serial, cheap, may stall on rate limits, silent default for unattended), on-demand (throughput fan-out, guaranteed, requires explicit operator yes), or a middle reserved tier (bounded parallelism at a pre-approved ceiling). The posture is a typed value threaded from saga into team-execution dispatch, not re-negotiated per unit. Every spend-increasing transition (spot->on-demand mid-run) re-prompts, exactly as reserving extra capacity does. This turns intake tension 1's prose rule into a single machine-readable knob instead of scattered per-call judgment.
basis: Source domain = cloud capacity economics. AWS EC2 purchasing model (spot / on-demand / reserved instances, documented in AWS EC2 pricing) solves exactly this: a workload declares its cost-vs-availability posture once at launch, spot is the silent-cheap default that may be preempted, and stepping up to guaranteed capacity is an explicit, priced act. Maps 1:1 onto intake §1's unattended->cache-tight-silent / attended->throughput-with-explicit-yes rule.
outcome_shape: PR adding a RunPosture enum + resolver to plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py, surfaced at run start and emitted through team_emitter.py into the team-execution dispatch context; verified by a pytest asserting unattended runs resolve to the cache-tight class without a prompt and any escalation raises a confirm-required signal.

title: Cache-affinity wave ordering: schedule segments to keep the 5-min TTL warm (NUMA affinity)
idea: Treat each resident teammate like a CPU core with a hot L2 cache and each segment (plugin directory) like a thread's working set. Order the within-run wave so segments that share a stable prompt prefix run back-to-back on the same named teammate, landing subsequent dispatches inside the 5-minute cache TTL before it decays, exactly as a NUMA-aware scheduler pins a thread to the core whose cache already holds its data instead of paying a cold refill. Today team_emitter emits one row per segment with no ordering intelligence about prefix reuse or TTL windows. This adds a deterministic ordering pass that minimizes cache-cold refills across the wave. It deliberately materializes the formal within-run wave queue that the worker-cache-scheduling decision left for later.
basis: Source domain = OS/CPU scheduling. NUMA locality and cache-affinity scheduling (Linux CFS sched_setaffinity, cache-hot thread placement) minimize cold cache refills by co-scheduling work with warm state. Engages the {#worker-cache-scheduling} revisit-when clause verbatim: 'a single team-execution run shows enough internal idle-poll to justify a formal within-run wave queue' — this idea IS that wave queue, ordered by TTL/prefix affinity rather than arrival.
outcome_shape: PR adding a TTL-aware wave-ordering pass to plugins/saga/scripts/team_emitter.py (segment ordering by shared-prefix affinity) plus a DECISIONS.md entry recording the revisit-trigger firing; verified by a pytest that a wave of prefix-sharing segments is emitted contiguously and a golden test comparing cold-refill count before/after.

title: Crew-pairing: a reviewer+worker teammate pair that travels together to keep both caches warm
idea: Borrow airline crew pairing, where a cockpit crew is scheduled as a bonded unit across a multi-leg trip to avoid deadheading and repeated re-briefing. Bind a worker teammate and its consensus reviewer into a resident pair that persists together across all review/remediation cycles for a segment, so neither re-pays its full context on each cycle. Currently residency is per-teammate; the reviewer re-warms independently and the review loop (up to three cycles) can force cold reviewer refills. A pair contract keeps the reviewer's segment-context cache warm exactly as the crew stays together through the trip's legs. This directly answers the residency-insufficient half of the worker-cache-scheduling revisit condition.
basis: Source domain = airline crew scheduling. Crew-pairing optimization (bonding a crew across a trip's legs to minimize deadhead/re-brief cost, a classic set-partitioning problem in airline operations research) maps onto reviewer+worker residency across consensus cycles. Engages {#worker-cache-scheduling} revisit-when explicitly: 'Named-teammate residency proves insufficient (revisit warm-pool / crew-pairing)' — this is the named crew-pairing path.
outcome_shape: PR adding a crew-pairing residency protocol to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md and residency prose, with the saga-side pair-derivation plumbing (paired agent-ids) in team_emitter.py carrying pytest; verified by /doc-review readiness plus a test asserting a paired reviewer id is emitted alongside its worker for each segment.

title: Edge-Side-Includes prompt layout: cached shell first, volatile task payload after the breakpoint
idea: Adopt the CDN Edge Side Includes pattern, where a page is a static cacheable shell with small dynamic holes filled at the edge, so the expensive shell is cached once and only the volatile fragment varies. Restructure agent prompts fleet-wide so the stable plugin/segment context (skill body, references, role) forms an immutable cached prefix and the volatile per-task payload sits strictly after an explicit cache breakpoint. Any volatile token that leaks into the prefix silently busts the whole cache for that agent, the way a dynamic value bleeding into the cached shell defeats CDN caching. This is a layout convention plus a reordering pass across the 24+ team-execution agent prompts and saga panel prompts.
basis: Source domain = CDN/web edge caching. Edge Side Includes (ESI, the Akamai/Varnish standard) and HTTP cache-key stability solve exactly the stable-prefix/volatile-tail split: cache the invariant shell, isolate volatility behind a boundary. Anthropic prompt caching is prefix-matched with a 5-min TTL, so the ESI shell/hole discipline is the direct analog for maximizing cache-read hits.
outcome_shape: A prompt-architecture convention doc under plugins/team-execution (or saga references) plus a PR reordering agent .md prompts to stable-prefix-first with an explicit breakpoint marker; verified by /doc-review and a lint check that flags known-volatile tokens appearing before the breakpoint.

title: Token disaggregation ledger: NILM-style attribution of cache-write vs cache-read vs fresh input
idea: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) disaggregates a whole-house smart-meter reading into per-appliance draw without a sensor on each appliance. Apply the same to the fan-out token meter: consume headroom telemetry and disaggregate a run's aggregate burn into cache-write (1.25x), cache-read (0.1x), and fresh-input (1x) buckets attributed per segment and per teammate, surfacing a cache-hit-rate the operator can act on. The 350-450k-tokens-in-under-20-min recon datum is currently a single opaque number; NILM-style disaggregation reveals how much of it was avoidable cold refill versus irreducible fresh work, making the cache architecture measurable rather than asserted.
basis: Source domain = utility metering / energy informatics. Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (Hart's NILM, deployed in smart-meter disaggregation) turns one aggregate meter into per-source attribution. Grounds the measurement need in the mined datum '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs' (grounding brief §7 singletons), which is exactly the aggregate this ledger would decompose.
outcome_shape: PR adding a token-disaggregation ledger script (headroom-telemetry consumer) under plugins/saga/scripts plus a ledger schema doc; verified by reproducing the recon fan-out and asserting the cache-read/write/fresh buckets sum to the metered total with a reported hit-rate.

title: Intermodal container: extract segment+residency derivation as a shared primitive for /outcome and panels
idea: Shipping containerization won by standardizing one box that moves unchanged across ship, rail, and truck, so each mode reuses the same handling instead of re-packing at every transfer. Cache scheduling currently only rides the team-execution rail; /outcome leaf dispatch and saga verify-panels re-pack their own spawn logic and get zero cache reuse. Extract the saga-side (segment + agent-id + tier) derivation into one shared module that /outcome leaf dispatch and panel spawns consume unchanged, so the same warm-residency contract travels across all three dispatch modes. This extends worker-cache-scheduling to the modes it never reached rather than contradicting it.
basis: Source domain = logistics / freight. ISO intermodal containerization (the standard container that transfers across ship/rail/truck without re-packing) is the canonical case of one interface unlocking reuse across formerly siloed transport modes. Maps onto extracting one derivation seam consumed unchanged by team-execution, /outcome dispatch, and saga panels — a pure extension of {#worker-cache-scheduling}, whose segment=plugin-directory boundary already generalizes.
outcome_shape: PR extracting the segment/residency/tier derivation from team_emitter.py into a shared saga module imported by the /outcome leaf-dispatch path and the verify-panel spawn path; verified by pytest that all three call sites derive identical segment ids for the same ExecutionSpec.

title: Append-only prefix with generation rotation: an LSM-tree drift guard for cached prompt regions
idea: Log-structured merge trees and append-only logs never mutate written data in place; new state is appended and the old immutable segment stays valid until a deliberate compaction rotates a new generation. Apply this to the cached prompt prefix: treat each agent's stable-prefix region as immutable, forbid in-place edits that silently bust the cache mid-fleet, and require any real change to bump an explicit prefix-generation marker (a deliberate compaction). A CI lint guards that no PR mutates a cached-prefix region without rotating its generation, turning invisible cache-busting drift into a reviewable, versioned event — the same discipline this repo already applies to release-surface drift.
basis: Source domain = storage systems. Log-structured merge trees / append-only logs (LevelDB/RocksDB, log-structured file systems) achieve stable-read performance by never mutating in place and rotating generations via explicit compaction. Anthropic prompt caching invalidates the entire suffix on any prefix byte change, so immutable-prefix + generation-rotation is the direct structural remedy for silent cache-busting drift.
outcome_shape: PR adding a CI lint (under scripts/ or the marketplace guard suite) that fails when an agent prompt's cached-prefix region changes without a bumped generation marker, plus a short convention doc; verified by the lint failing on a seeded in-place prefix edit and passing when the generation marker is rotated.

title: Cache-efficiency ledger: measure what fork_is_cheap only assumes
idea: Flip the constraint to 'everything is measured': today `fork_is_cheap()` (outcome_dispatcher.py:309) decides cheapness from four boolean signals but nothing ever records whether the warm cache actually hit, and the 350-450k-token recon fan-out is an aggregate guess with no per-spawn breakdown. Add a cost ledger that captures `cache_read_input_tokens` vs `cache_creation_input_tokens` per agent spawn, keyed on (segment, resident_id, tier), emitted as a leaf-produced fact into the saga/outcome cost ledger. This turns the mined 350-450k datum from folklore into a per-run measured cache-hit-rate, and lets convergence rank other T4 ideas against real numbers. The ledger is append-only and derived-on-read, honoring the /outcome cost-ledger-is-leaf-fact rule.
basis: outcome_dispatcher.py:309-318 `fork_is_cheap` returns cheapness from model/system/tools/TTL booleans with zero post-hoc measurement; grounding brief section 7 '350-450k tokens in <20min pure recon fan-out' is an unattributed aggregate; /outcome campaign binding decision 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (grounding brief section 2) supplies the emission shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/cache_ledger.py` + wiring into the emitted cost-ledger artifact, with a golden test asserting cache_read/cache_creation fields are recorded per resident_id; verified by running a 2-segment emit and diffing the ledger artifact for populated token-class fields.

title: Ask time-vs-money once, thread the answer through every spend gate
idea: Flip to 'the operator is asked exactly once, never again': the fleet's only spend lever today is /plan's per-unit tier table (plan/SKILL.md:296-352) — there is no run-level posture that a downstream fan-out can read. Add a single run-start posture capture (throughput vs cache-tight) with a mode-based recommendation, persisted into the saga/outcome state, and have every spend-increasing site (parallel fan-out, tier escalation, fork-vs-fresh) read it: unattended defaults cache-tight silently, attended requires an explicit operator yes to increase spend. This encodes the question rather than hard-coding cache-first, exactly as the intake demands.
basis: Intake brief section 1 'Time vs money (decomposition posture)': 'Asked once per run at start... any spend-increasing choice always requires an explicit operator yes. Cache-first is the only silent default... plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded cache-first mandate.' Grounding brief section 1 confirms the plan unit tier table is the fleet's ONE operator-facing spend lever.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `posture` field to saga/outcome state (execution_spec.py or outcome_spec.py) plus a run-start capture prompt in /work and /outcome SKILL.md, with a test asserting spend-increasing recommenders read the persisted posture; verified by starting a run in each mode and confirming the silent-vs-ask branch.

title: Wave queue: residents pull the next unit instead of idling
idea: Flip to 'zero idle workers': when the ready frontier is wider than the segment count, `segment_units()` (execution_spec.py:1384) currently maps each unit to a resident but there is no mechanism for a finished resident to pick up an unstarted same-segment unit — it idles while a fresh spawn pays a full cache miss elsewhere. Build a lightweight wave queue where a resident, on finishing its unit, pulls the next queued unit whose segment matches its warm prefix, so the plugin-directory segment's cache is amortized across many units. This directly engages the worker-cache-scheduling revisit-when ('idle-poll justifies formal wave queue'), which the mined 'subagents idle without delivering' pattern (grounding section 7, pattern 9) demonstrates is now justified.
basis: Binding decision `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` revisit-when: 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient, or idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue' (grounding brief section 2); grounding section 7 pattern 9 'Subagents idle without delivering... reproduced live in this very session' supplies the justifying evidence; execution_spec.py:1384 `segment_units` is the seam.
outcome_shape: PR extending `segment_units`/team_emitter.py with a per-segment wave queue + resident pull protocol in consensus-protocol.md, plus a test that a 3-unit single-segment spec dispatches all three to one resident sequentially; verified by emitting and asserting one resident_id owns multiple unit rows.

title: Stable-prefix audit of all agent system prompts
idea: Flip to 'every prompt is a perfect cache prefix': Anthropic prompt caching keys on the longest stable prefix, so any volatile token (timestamps, run-ids, per-call context) placed early in an agent's system prompt poisons the cache for everything after it. Audit all agents/*.md across the 8 plugins for cache-hostile ordering — stable role/instructions must come first, volatile injected context last — and add a cache-block boundary convention (`cache_control` breakpoint marker) at the stable/volatile seam. Re-engaged residents then reuse the maximal warm prefix. This is the cheapest structural win in T4: it costs no new runtime machinery, only prompt reordering.
basis: Anthropic prompt caching documentation (docs.claude.com Build-with-Claude 'Prompt caching'): cache hits require an exact-match prefix from the start of the prompt; up to 4 cache breakpoints via `cache_control`, 5-minute default TTL. Grounding brief section 1 confirms 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:, zero effort: fields' — the prompts are static assets ripe for a prefix audit.
outcome_shape: PR reordering agents/*.md that place volatile content early + a `scripts/check_prompt_prefix.py` lint added to CI that flags volatile tokens before the first stable-block boundary; verified by the lint passing on the reordered set and failing on a deliberately poisoned fixture.

title: Carry fork_is_cheap into the recon and verify fan-out spawn sites
idea: Flip to 'every spawn asks whether a warm fork is cheaper than a fresh worker': the fork cost lever `fork_is_cheap()` lives only in outcome_dispatcher.py — the readonly-verifier verify-class spawns (sandbox-spawn-sites.md) and the ideate/recon fan-out that burned 350-450k tokens each pay a cold cache miss with no cheapness check. Propagate the fork-cost helper into a shared `cache_lever` module that every spawn site consults: when model+system+tools match a warm parent within TTL, fork; else spawn fresh. Because verify-class spawns must stay readonly+worktree-isolated, the lever only chooses fork-vs-fresh, never relaxes the sandbox — preserving the readonly-verifier fallback-ladder decision.
basis: outcome_dispatcher.py:309-318 `fork_is_cheap` is the only cheapness gate and is outcome-local; grounding brief section 7 '350-450k tokens in <20min pure recon fan-out' shows recon spawns are uncached; binding decision `{#readonly-verifier-fallback-ladder-325}` requires verify spawns keep readonly+worktree isolation — the lever chooses fork-vs-fresh only, not sandbox posture, so no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: PR extracting `fork_is_cheap` into `plugins/saga/scripts/cache_lever.py` and referencing it from sandbox-spawn-sites.md guidance + the recon fan-out dispatch, with a test that a TTL-expired candidate is not recommended as fork; verified by unit tests over the four boolean signals plus the readonly invariant.

title: Ship KTD5 context-GC for resident teammates
idea: Flip to 'nothing is cached that a resident no longer needs': delta-only re-engagement already lands (consensus-protocol.md:57 reuses the named teammate via SendMessage), but the worker-cache-scheduling KTD5 context-GC (Messages-API-only) was left unshipped — a long-lived resident accretes transcript that inflates every subsequent cache-creation cost. Ship an explicit context-GC protocol: after a unit completes and its artifact-pointer is emitted, the resident sheds the completed unit's working context down to a compact summary before pulling the next, keeping the warm prefix stable while bounding the volatile tail. This extends residency rather than contradicting it, so it stays inside the settled architecture.
basis: DECISIONS `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` KTD5 names 'context-GC (Messages-API-only)' as an un-shipped residency refinement (DECISIONS.md worker-cache-scheduling block); consensus-protocol.md:57 'RE-ENGAGE the same named reviewer via SendMessage' is the residency seam being extended, not crossed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a context-shedding step to consensus-protocol.md after artifact-pointer emit + a shed-summary helper, with a test asserting the resident's carried context shrinks to a bounded summary between units; verified by a two-unit resident run showing the volatile tail reset while the stable prefix is unchanged.

title: TTL-aware batch scheduling under the concurrency cap
idea: Flip to 'the 5-minute TTL is a hard scheduling deadline': with the operator's max-3-concurrent cap, a wide ready frontier is dispatched as sequential batches — but if batch N+1 lands more than 300s after batch N warmed the shared prefix, the cache has expired and every worker pays a cold miss. Add TTL-aware batch ordering to the frontier scheduler so same-segment units are grouped into adjacent batches that land inside the TTL window, and surface a 'cache will expire in Xs' signal when the serial queue can't keep up (the point where the cost ledger, idea T4-F6-1, would justify a refresh ping or a posture downgrade). This makes the concurrency cap and cache economics coexist instead of fighting.
basis: First principles: prompt cache TTL is 5 minutes (300s); the intake concurrency cap of 3 forces a wide frontier into serial batches (intake 'Added constraint: concurrency cap'); if inter-batch latency exceeds the TTL the warm prefix is evicted and cache_read drops to zero, so batch ordering that clusters same-segment units within one TTL window is the only way to preserve cache under the cap — an ordering choice with no new primitive, purely a scheduler heuristic over already-emitted segments.
outcome_shape: PR adding TTL-window batch grouping to the frontier/emit scheduler (team_emitter.py / outcome frontier dispatch) + a 'cache-expiry-risk' note in the emitted plan, with a test that same-segment units are placed in adjacent batches; verified by emitting a >3-unit multi-segment spec and asserting segment-contiguous batch order.

title: Cache-prefix stability regression guard in CI
idea: Flip to 'a refactor can never silently break the cache': resident cache reuse depends on `segment_units()` producing byte-stable resident prefixes across runs, but nothing pins that — a benign refactor to the emitter or an agent prompt can reorder a prefix and quietly convert every re-engagement from a cache hit to a cache miss, invisible until a token bill spikes. Add a golden regression test that snapshots the stable-prefix bytes for a fixture ExecutionSpec and fails CI on drift, plus a marketplace-style version-bump note when a prefix change is intentional. This is the cheap guardrail that protects every other T4 investment from silent decay.
basis: First principles: prompt caching is prefix-exact — a single reordered or newly-injected early token invalidates the cache with zero functional test failure, so cache economics have no protecting signal unless prefix bytes are explicitly pinned. execution_spec.py:1384 `segment_units` and agents/*.md are the prefix-determining inputs; both change routinely (grounding section 1 notes prompts are edited freely with no cache-awareness), making silent drift the default failure mode absent a guard.
outcome_shape: PR adding `tests/test_cache_prefix_stability.py` with a committed golden snapshot of resident prefix bytes for a fixture spec + a CONTRIBUTING note on the intentional-change bump; verified by the test passing on HEAD and failing when a fixture prompt prefix is perturbed.

title: Portable consensus-invocation contract so /work and /outcome can call the panel team-execution proved
idea: team-execution's review-revise consensus (consensus-protocol.md Step B3) is the fleet's proven defect-catcher, but it is trapped inside one plugin's Step B3 prose: no other lifecycle stage can invoke it as a primitive, so saga /work reaches for a DIFFERENT protocol (/code-review's P0/P1 findings gate) and /outcome leaves run their own verify. Extract a stable 'Consensus Invocation Contract' section — declared inputs (participants, threshold-profile, governance-mode) and outputs (verdict + persisted evidence) — that any stage invokes without re-deriving the cycle, reusing the existing recommend_execution_backend team-execution routing as the transport. This makes consensus a callable capability rather than a copy-paste pattern, and gives saga /work a real gated-consensus backend instead of a second review shape. Portability is the whole point of the theme: the value must travel out of team-execution intact.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:10-62 defines the B3 cycle as team-execution-internal; plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md reimplements a distinct findings-based gate (no numeric threshold); grounding brief section 3 finding 2 records this consensus catching defects two green suites missed in 2 independent repos (operator-praised) — proven value with no invocation seam out of the plugin. No new plugin is created (avoids {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} burden); the contract lives in existing team-execution + saga references.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'Consensus Invocation Contract' section to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md and a pointer from plugins/saga/references/operator-choice.md + saga work/SKILL.md routing /work's gated path at it; version surfaces bumped (team-execution plugin.json/CHANGELOG, marketplace.json). Verified by a doc-lint test asserting both /work and /outcome-leaf reference the contract anchor and that the contract enumerates the three declared inputs.

title: Single-source the consensus threshold constants that are hand-copied into ~24 reviewer prompts
idea: The acceptance math (>= 9.0 overall, < 7.0 blocking, < 5.0 severe, max 3 iterations) is not defined once — it is retyped as prose into every reviewer agent and every reference file, so changing the bar means a 20-plus-file hand-edit and guarantees the exact contract-mirror-drift disease the journal already logged. Extract one canonical consensus-thresholds reference and rewrite each reviewer's ACCEPT/BLOCKING/SEVERE line to cite it symbolically ('apply the thresholds in consensus-thresholds.md') rather than inline a literal. Add a drift-guard test asserting no bare 9.0/7.0/5.0/max-3 literal appears in any reviewer frontmatter or reference except the canonical file. This is the precondition for T5-F1-5's tunable profiles: you cannot vary a constant that is smeared across 24 files.
basis: Identical literals duplicated at security-reviewer.md:64-65, devils-advocate-reviewer.md:62-63, architecture-reviewer.md:120-121, consensus-protocol.md:70-78, review-criteria.md:5; grounding brief section 3 finding 1 + section 6 finding 3 name contract-mirror drift / release-surface drift as a top recurring, multi-repo pain (343 'clean' cards failed the live contract, #222).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-thresholds.md (single source), editing all reviewer agents/*.md + review-criteria.md + consensus-protocol.md to cite it, and adding tests/test_team_execution_threshold_drift.py asserting zero stray threshold literals. Verified: grep-based test is green; version surfaces (plugin.json/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json) bumped.

title: Carry gated-vs-advisory as a mode field on the consensus artifact so the split survives porting
idea: The governance split lives ENTIRELY on saga's side (operator-choice.md / recommend_execution_backend) and is enforced by forking to two different engines — gated to team-execution, advisory to ultracode's judge-panel — so team-execution's protocol has no concept of 'advisory' at all and cannot express a record-don't-block run. That means the superior named-reviewer roster is only reachable in gated mode; an operator who wants an advisory second opinion is forced into ultracode's shape, and if consensus is ported to any new stage the split does not travel with the protocol. Make consensus_mode (gated|advisory) a first-class field on the invocation contract and give consensus-protocol.md an 'Advisory mode' path: same scoring, verdict recorded as advisory-evidence, never sets a blocking gate on Step B4. Claude stays verifier-of-record in both modes, so this preserves the split's essence (does the verdict need to stick) while decoupling it from the engine fork.
basis: operator-choice.md:81-95 defines the split saga-side and routes advisory to cc-workflows-ultracode, gated to team-execution; consensus-protocol.md contains zero mention of advisory/gated (grep = 0 hits) — the downstream executor is blind to the mode. Engages the binding {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} directly (its 'must survive porting' revisit is the theme mandate) and keeps advisory Claude-reconciled, consistent with {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus_mode field to the team-execution handoff schema (worker-manifest.md) and an 'Advisory mode' section to consensus-protocol.md; a test asserting advisory mode never emits a blocking gate and gated mode still does. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: Fix the 3-cycle terminal action: a gated consensus that fails to converge must HALT, not silently ship
idea: The 3-cycle cap has a governance contradiction baked into the docs: consensus-protocol.md says 'proceed with the best available version regardless of scores', while the README and the validator path say 'escalate to the user'. Under the gated contract ('the verdict must BLOCK a merge/deploy'), proceed-with-best silently ships sub-9.0 code — the gate is a paper gate. Fork the cap's terminal action on governance mode: gated -> HALT + escalate with evidence (mirroring the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade rule), advisory -> proceed-with-best-and-record (which is fine because nothing was blocking). This also reconciles the three drifted docs into one behavior. It is a near-standalone quick-win: even before T5-F1-3's mode field lands, gated is today's default and the only mode reaching team-execution, so the fix is to make the default terminal action HALT.
basis: Direct contradiction: consensus-protocol.md:17 + :61 'proceed with the best available version regardless of scores' vs README.md:99 'before escalating to the user' vs validator-execution-order.md:30 'escalate to the user' vs operator-choice.md:86 gated = 'must BLOCK a merge/deploy and PERSIST'. Engages {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} (terminal action forks on mode) and the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade principle (grounding section 2).
outcome_shape: PR rewriting the 'After 3 Cycles' section of consensus-protocol.md to fork on mode (gated->HALT+escalate, advisory->proceed+record) and reconciling README.md:99 + validator-execution-order.md:30; a test asserting a gated cycle-3 non-convergence returns HALT/escalate, not COMPLETE. Verified via that test + CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace.json bump.

title: Risk-tiered threshold profiles set by /plan, defaulting to today's 9.0/7.0/5.0
idea: A single global acceptance bar cannot be right for both a typo-fix and a payments migration: consensus cost is roughly fixed while its value scales with blast radius, so 9.0-on-everything overpays on trivia and under-demands on critical paths, with no operator lever either way. Introduce named threshold_profiles (relaxed / default / strict) where default is exactly today's 9.0/7.0/5.0/max-3 and strict raises the accept bar and the severe floor for load-bearing work. /plan sets the profile from risk signals it already computes (parse_issue.py deployment_sensitive / has_security) plus an operator confirm, and it travels on the same handoff as consensus_mode. This is distinct from the QUEUED per-teammate-effort seed — that tunes model/effort, this tunes the score gate — and it depends on T5-F1-2 having made the constants tunable in the first place.
basis: First-principles: consensus panel cost is a near-fixed function of roster size and iteration cap, independent of the change's risk; therefore a fixed acceptance threshold necessarily mismatches value on both tails (wasted rigor on trivia, insufficient rigor on high-blast-radius work). The plan already carries the right discriminators — parse_issue.py surfaces deployment_sensitive and has_security (operator-choice.md:98-100) — so a profile can be derived, not invented. Never downgrades a gated critical diff (ties to the governance split).
outcome_shape: PR adding a threshold_profile field to the plan->team-execution handoff (worker-manifest.md), a profiles table in consensus-thresholds.md with default == current numbers, and a /plan interrogation step; test that 'strict' propagates the raised accept bar and default equals 9.0/7.0/5.0. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: An advisory external-engine reviewer slot in the panel — the 15/17 Claude+Codex synthesis, made protocol
idea: The strongest observed consensus signal in the fleet — Claude and Codex producing independent syntheses that converged 15 of 17 — was reconciled BY HAND, because there is no protocol slot for an external engine to contribute an independent review into a consensus panel; the roster is Claude-only and adding a second opinion is manual every run. Add an 'advisory external reviewer' role: spawned through the existing engine-dispatch as advisory-evidence (engine-registry.yaml verdict: advisory, verifier: claude), it produces a synthesis that enters the score-display step as a NON-scoring advisory column, which Claude reconciles into the gated verdict. The external voice can never flip consensus by itself, so Claude remains verifier-of-record. This turns a hand-reconciliation ritual into a repeatable, bounded panel member.
basis: Named prior art: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' (grounding brief section 7 singletons; lineage in section 3 finding 2). Crosses {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318): the #283 revisit-when is precisely 'team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot' — this idea IS that slot, kept advisory (non-scoring, Claude reconciles, verifier-of-record). #318 is honored: the slot is a second-opinion->opus/high chaperone dispatch producing advisory evidence, never a git participant or second executor. engine-registry.yaml:143 already types this result as 'advisory / never gated'.
outcome_shape: PR extending plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md + consensus-protocol.md with the advisory-reviewer role (enters B3c as a non-scoring column), wired through the existing advisory-evidence dispatch; a test asserting the external column can never move a verdict from NEEDS-REVISION to ACCEPT on its own. Verified via that never-gatekeeper test + version-surface bump.

title: Diversity-aware panel composition: port saga's judgment-selection so team-execution stops spawning reviewers that find nothing
idea: The two sibling plugins hold opposite philosophies on who sits on the panel: saga /code-review explicitly refuses 'a fixed specialist roster that re-opens reviewers that find nothing on this diff' and spawns only lenses with real work, while team-execution always spawns its 3 base reviewers regardless of the diff. The fixed roster both overpays (a security reviewer on a docs-only diff) and under-diversifies (3 correlated lenses can jointly miss a domain the diff actually needs). Port saga's judgment-selection into consensus-protocol.md — treat the base 3 as candidates, spawn those with real work on THIS diff, and add an explicit diversity-coverage check so the panel spans the domains the change touches rather than re-running the same three. Give reviewer-registry.md a 'when NOT to spawn' column so the selection rule is legible, not implicit.
basis: plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md:48-50 rejects the fixed-roster pattern by name; plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/reviewer-registry.md defines 'Base Reviewers (Always Spawned)' regardless of content — two sibling plugins, contradictory panel-composition philosophies. Diversity, not just cost, is the frame: the risk is correlated lenses missing a domain, addressed by the coverage check.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'Panel composition' step to consensus-protocol.md adopting judgment-selection + a domain-coverage check, a 'when NOT to spawn' column in reviewer-registry.md, and a cross-reference to code-review/SKILL.md; a doc example (docs-only diff => security-reviewer skipped) + a consistency test asserting both plugins cite the same selection principle. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: A consensus-worthiness pre-gate: decide BEFORE spawning whether the diff earns a full panel
idea: Consensus scales its cost only AFTER the fact — the re-review-scoping optimization re-runs just the sub-9.0 reviewers, but the INITIAL pass always spawns 'all reviewers in parallel' with no floor logic asking whether this change is worth any panel at all. So a 3-line README fix triggers the same 3-reviewer by up-to-3-cycle machine as a payments migration, and the only cap in the fleet (VERIFY_N_CAP=7) bounds the top, never the bottom. Add a Step B2.5 worthiness pre-gate: a cheap classifier (diff size, parse_issue.py risk signals, the active threshold_profile) picks a panel scale of none / single-lead-check / full-panel, defaulting to full-panel whenever gated risk signals are present so a security or deploy diff is never downgraded. This makes the cost of consensus proportional to blast radius while the governance split still forces the full machine where the verdict must stick.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:26 (B3a) spawns 'all reviewers IN PARALLEL' unconditionally; the only cost lever, the 'Re-review Scoping' section, is post-hoc (re-runs only <9.0 reviewers) — there is no pre-spawn floor. Grounding brief section 7 finding 6 ('xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful') and the 350-450k-token recon fan-out singleton establish that unscaled full-fan-out is a live cost pain. Never downgrades a gated critical diff, honoring the governance split.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'Step B2.5 — Consensus worthiness' pre-gate to consensus-protocol.md + team-execution/SKILL.md selecting panel scale {none|single-check|full-panel} from diff size + risk signals + threshold_profile; a test that a small no-risk diff selects single-check and a deployment_sensitive diff forces full-panel. Verified via that test + version-surface bump.

title: Extract consensus contract into a saga-side consensus_spec.py, delete the prose-as-source-of-truth
idea: Today the entire consensus contract (thresholds 9.0/7.0/5.0, 3-iteration cap, re-review scoping, exclusion vocabulary) lives as prose in team-execution's consensus-protocol.md, and DECISIONS.md:88 records that test_team_execution_consensus.py pins the contract *text*, not the behavior. Invert the source of truth: author the numeric/structural contract once as a data module (plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py) sitting beside execution_spec.py, exporting PASS_THRESHOLD, REVISION_BAND, BLOCKING_FLOOR, MAX_ITERATIONS, and the static-non-applicable exclusion enum. consensus-protocol.md then renders those constants rather than hardcoding them, and a drift-guard test fails if the prose and the module disagree. This removes the per-plugin reimplementation step so saga review and team-execution consume one contract. It stays in saga (not a new plugin) because execution_spec.py, ENGINE_INTENTS, and the recommender seam already live there.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17,74 hardcodes '9.0'/'7.0'/'5.0'/'Maximum iterations: 3'; DECISIONS.md:88 states the existing consensus test 'pins the contract *text*, not whether a given' behavior holds — an extracted module makes the numbers testable, not just quotable. Honors {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by landing as a script inside saga, not an 8th plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py + a drift-guard test (tests/test_consensus_spec_prose_parity.py) that parses the thresholds out of consensus-protocol.md and asserts equality with the module; consensus-protocol.md edited to cite the module as source of truth. Verified: test red if a threshold is edited in only one place.

title: Make the gated-vs-advisory split un-loseable by porting: a typed gating flag every consensus record carries
idea: The governance split survives today only because humans remember it — when consensus is ported to a new plugin or a new participant kind, nothing structurally stops an external engine's score from being counted toward the 9.0 gate. Invert 'remember the rule' into 'the type system forbids the violation': give every consensus participant record a structural shape mirroring #283's AdvisoryEvidence (which has no verdict field), where engine != claude participants are constructed as advisory-only and a validator raises if any advisory record is folded into the gating average. The manual vigilance step is removed; a ported consensus loop that tries to gate on Codex fails a test at author time, not in production. This rides the exact mechanism #283 named ('the gated-vs-advisory consensus split is the mechanism this rides on', DECISIONS.md:1999).
basis: DECISIONS.md:1994-1996 ({#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}) enforces non-gating 'structurally, not asserted' via an AdvisoryEvidence value with no verdict field; DECISIONS.md:1999 names the gated-vs-advisory consensus split as the mechanism it rides on. This idea extends that same structural guarantee to the consensus record type so the split cannot be dropped when the protocol is ported. Reinforces the decision rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a ConsensusParticipant dataclass (in consensus_spec.py) with a non-settable gating property keyed on participant engine, plus tests/test_consensus_governance_split.py asserting an external-engine participant raises when added to the gating denominator. Verified: attempting to gate on a non-claude participant raises in the test.

title: Automate away the prose-edit: consensus thresholds become a .team-execution.json dial with today's values as defaults
idea: Changing consensus rigor today means editing prose in consensus-protocol.md — a code-change ceremony for what is really a per-run policy choice (a spike wants 7.0/2-iter; a payments change wants 9.5/no-cap). Automate the edit away: surface pass_threshold, revision_band_floor, blocking_floor, and max_iterations as optional keys in .team-execution.json, defaulting to exactly the current 9.0/7.0/5.0/3 so behavior is unchanged when unset. The lead sets rigor per run instead of forking the doc. Because the defaults equal the hardcoded values, this is behavior-preserving and the existing text-pinning test still passes; a new test asserts the loader honors overrides and rejects out-of-band values (e.g. blocking_floor > pass_threshold).
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3') and :74 ('Overall score ... >= 9.0 AND no individual applicable dimension < 7.0') are hardcoded with no configuration seam; grounding brief §2 notes .team-execution.json exists as the run-config surface (external_second_opinion key, DECISIONS.md:2041) — the same file is the natural home for threshold overrides.
outcome_shape: PR editing consensus_spec.py loader + consensus-protocol.md + validator-registry docs to read optional threshold keys from .team-execution.json, plus tests/test_consensus_threshold_override.py (defaults unchanged; overrides honored; invalid ordering rejected). Verified: a run with pass_threshold 9.5 blocks a 9.2 reviewer that previously passed.

title: Consensus off by default: no panel unless a cheap triage signal earns it
idea: The best version of the consensus step, for a 3-line typo fix, is no step — yet the lead spins a multi-reviewer, up-to-3-iteration panel regardless of change shape, and read-only fan-outs already burn 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes (grounding §7). Invert the default: consensus is OFF unless a cheap, deterministic triage function trips it, reusing the exact signal set that already gates team-execution offering (file_count>=8, phase_count>=4, has_security, has_infra, cross_repo, deployment_sensitive — DECISIONS.md:1611). Below the bar, ship with a single lead review and log 'consensus skipped: change below triage bar'; above it, run the full panel. This removes the panel as a mandatory step and scales token spend to actual risk, while leaving the operator a one-flag force-on override so the gate is never silently weakened on something that matters.
basis: DECISIONS.md:1611 enumerates the should_offer_team_execution trigger constants (file_count>=8, phase_count>=4, has_security, has_infra, cross_repo, deployment_sensitive) — a proven, reusable triage seam; grounding §7 singleton records 350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs, evidencing that panel spend on trivial diffs is real waste.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus_required(change_signals) function to consensus_spec.py wired into SKILL.md Step B3, with a documented operator force-on flag, plus tests/test_consensus_triage_gate.py (typo diff -> skipped+logged; security-touching diff -> panel runs). Verified: a below-bar run produces the skip log and no reviewer spawns.

title: Automate the hand-reconciliation: an advisory convergence-diff between Claude and an external synthesis
idea: The 15/17 Claude+Codex independent-synthesis convergence was computed by hand — a person diffed two independent reviews and reconciled the 2 divergences. Automate that manual reconciliation into a convergence step: an external advisory reviewer runs the SAME review-criteria.md rubric independently, and the lead auto-computes a convergence-diff (dimensions where Claude and the external engine agree vs the specific divergences) surfaced as a table for the human. The external engine stays strictly advisory — its scores never enter the 9.0 gating average and it can never block completion, exactly per the chaperone-dispatch second-opinion contract. What is removed is the manual diffing labor; what is kept is the diversity signal that caught defects green suites missed (grounding §3 finding 2).
basis: Prior art: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' (grounding brief §7 singletons) — the reconciliation is the manual step this automates. Constrained by {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (DECISIONS.md:1985) and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} KTD5 (DECISIONS.md:2041: advisory validators 'structurally incapable of gating'); the idea keeps the external synthesis advisory-only, so it satisfies rather than crosses those decisions.
outcome_shape: PR adding a convergence-diff section to consensus-protocol.md + external-engine-workers.md (advisory-only, no gating denominator entry), and a computed divergence table format, plus tests/test_convergence_advisory_nongating.py asserting external scores never alter the gating pass/fail. Verified: a run where the external engine scores 6.0 still passes if all Claude reviewers are >= 9.0.

title: Collapse saga /code-review lenses and team-execution reviewers into one portable lens registry
idea: saga's /code-review selects judgment-picked review lenses and team-execution maintains its own reviewer-registry.md roster of ~14 reviewer agents with review-criteria.md rubrics — two parallel reimplementations of 'a set of review lenses scored against a rubric'. Remove the double-maintenance: extract a single portable lens registry (name, dimensions, rubric pointer, applicability precondition) that both surfaces consume, so a lens defined once (e.g. security, concurrency, api-compat) is available to both the saga review gate and the team-execution consensus panel. Porting consensus to a third surface then means pointing at the registry, not re-authoring lenses. This is the protocol-extraction axis applied to membership rather than thresholds: the review-lens roster becomes a shared primitive instead of a per-plugin copy.
basis: team-execution ships ~14 reviewer agents (plugins/team-execution/agents/*.md: security-reviewer, concurrency-tester, api-compat-scanner, architecture-reviewer, etc.) with rubrics in review-criteria.md; the saga:code-review skill description states it runs 'judgment-selected review lenses' — two independent lens rosters, no shared registry. Grounding §3 finding 3 (mission-control/saga contract copies drifting) is the same drift disease a shared registry prevents.
outcome_shape: PR adding a lens-registry reference (plugins/saga/.../review-lens-registry.md or a data file) referenced by both reviewer-registry.md and the saga /code-review lens selection, plus a drift-guard test asserting no lens is defined in two rosters with divergent dimensions. Verified: test red if security lens dimensions differ between the two consumers.

title: Remove the arbitrary 3-cycle cap: stop on convergence, not on a counter
idea: The fixed 'Maximum iterations: 3, then proceed with best version regardless of scores' cap either wastes a cycle on a change that already converged at cycle 2 or guillotines a change still climbing at cycle 3. Invert the counter into a convergence test: stop when the cross-cycle score delta for every still-open reviewer falls below an epsilon (converged — no further motion) OR a hard ceiling is hit, and when the ceiling is hit escalate to the human instead of silently proceeding. The manual 'count to 3 and give up' step is replaced by measured convergence. The hard ceiling defaults to 3 so this is behavior-preserving at the boundary, and it pairs with the threshold-config seam (idea T5-F2-3) so both epsilon and ceiling are dials, not constants.
basis: First-principles: a fixed iteration count is a proxy for 'reviews have stopped improving', and the proxy is wrong in both directions — a 9.4->9.4 pair at cycles 1-2 has converged and cycle 3 is pure token waste, while an 8.0->8.6->8.9 trajectory is still climbing and cycle-3 cutoff discards a review that would have passed at cycle 4. consensus-protocol.md:61 literally says 'proceed with best version' regardless of scores, i.e. it already admits the counter is not a quality signal. Measuring inter-cycle delta directly replaces the proxy with the thing it approximates.
outcome_shape: PR editing consensus-protocol.md 'Cycle Structure' + 'After 3 Cycles' sections to a convergence-or-ceiling rule, adding convergence_epsilon + iteration_ceiling to consensus_spec.py, plus tests/test_consensus_convergence_stop.py (converged pair stops early; still-climbing trajectory hits ceiling and escalates to human, not silent proceed). Verified: a 9.4/9.4 cycle-2 run spawns zero cycle-3 reviewers.

title: Consensus is one algebra, reimplemented three times — extract it
idea: The fleet treats 'consensus lives in team-execution' as fixed, but the same algebra (a panel of scorers -> aggregation -> verdict -> bounded re-review of only the dissenters) is written as prose in team-execution's consensus-protocol.md AND as separate code in saga's verify-panel (execution_spec.py VERIFY_N_CAP) AND implicitly in code-review lens selection. Reframe one level up: there is a single consensus primitive the fleet re-derives per plugin. Extract a machine-readable `consensus_spec.py` into the existing saga scripts substrate (NOT a new plugin) that names the panel/aggregate/verdict/re-review contract once, and have team-execution's SKILL and saga verify both reference it. A drift-guard test asserts the prose threshold table and the code constants stay in lockstep.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:24-62 encodes the review-revise loop as prose; execution_spec.py:111-114 encodes a parallel but separately-chosen panel bound (VERIFY_N_CAP=7) for the same 'panel of scorers' concern. Two surfaces, one algebra, zero shared definition. Honors {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} by extracting into saga scripts, adding no plugin.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py (panel/aggregate/verdict/re-review contract), edits to team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md pointing at it, and tests/test_consensus_spec_drift.py asserting the prose 9.0/7.0/5.0/max-3 values equal the module constants. Verified: drift test red if either surface changes alone.

title: 9.0 is not a constant — it is a risk-tier function masquerading as one
idea: The protocol treats 9.0/7.0/5.0 as universal constants applied identically to a README typo and an auth-boundary rewrite. That uniformity is a hidden choice, not a law. Reframe: the acceptance threshold is a function of the change's risk-tier, resolved from the same plan metadata that already drives tier tables. A docs-only change convenes at a lower bar and lower panel; a security-touching change raises the bar and lowers the escalation floor. Encode a named threshold-profile table keyed by risk-tier and thread the resolved profile through the review cycle so the number is derived, never hardcoded.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('>= 9.0/10'), :40, :74 ('Pass threshold ... >= 9.0'), :232 ('< 5.0 severe') hardcode one global bar. No risk input exists anywhere in the cycle. saga plan/SKILL.md:296-352 already carries per-unit tier metadata that could key the profile.
outcome_shape: PR adding a risk-tier -> {accept, revise, blocking} threshold-profile table to consensus-protocol.md and review-criteria.md, plus a resolution note in team-execution SKILL Step B3, and a validator asserting every profile row is a monotonic ladder. Verified: a docs-tier and a security-tier run resolve different bars in the same protocol.

title: The 3-cycle cap silently ships — but HALT-not-degrade is the house posture
idea: 'After 3 cycles, proceed with the best available version regardless of scores' treats forced-ship as the fixed terminal default. That contradicts the fleet's own settled /outcome posture of HALT-not-degrade. Reframe the cap's outcome as a configurable disposition — {ship-best, halt-and-escalate, extend-with-approval} — defaulting to halt so non-convergence surfaces rather than silently degrading a merge. The max-3 count itself becomes a floor the operator can lift with explicit approval, mirroring the attended spend-increase rule.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 and :61 ('proceed with best version ... regardless of scores') vs grounding-brief §2 /outcome binding: 'HALT-not-degrade'. Crosses the /outcome campaign decision; engaging its revisit-when: HALT-not-degrade is the settled campaign posture, so consensus non-convergence should default to HALT, not silent ship-degrade — the current auto-ship is the drift this decision exists to prevent.
outcome_shape: PR rewriting consensus-protocol.md 'After 3 Cycles' section into a disposition enum (default halt-and-escalate), team-execution SKILL Step B3 wiring, and a test asserting default disposition != silent-ship. Verified: a 3-cycle non-convergence run halts and escalates instead of merging best-effort.

title: Split consensus into an advisory layer and a gated layer so porting can't leak the boundary
idea: Today 'reviewer score' and 'gate' are conflated in one flow, so every plugin that ports consensus must re-derive where advice stops and adjudication begins — the exact seam an external engine could slip a gate through. Reframe consensus as two explicit layers: an advisory-synthesis layer (any scorer, including external engines, contributes evidence) and a gated-adjudication layer (Claude verifier-of-record alone converts evidence into a verdict). Make the layer boundary a first-class artifact in the shared spec so the gated-vs-advisory governance split survives any port by construction, not by each plugin re-reading the prose.
basis: external-engine-workers.md 'Never a gatekeeper' section: engine_dispatch.satisfy_gate() (plugins/saga/scripts/engine_dispatch.py:238-258) hard-requires evidence.verified_by_claude before advisory evidence counts. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): this idea structurally encodes the split rather than relying on prose, so external participation stays advisory across every ported instance.
outcome_shape: PR/spec defining a two-layer consensus contract (advisory-evidence vs gated-verdict) in the shared consensus_spec, referenced by both consensus-protocol.md and saga verify docs, with a test asserting no advisory-source verdict lacks a verified_by_claude adjudication. Verified: an external-engine advisory score cannot flip a gate without Claude adjudication in either plugin.

title: Make the 15/17 Claude+Codex independent-synthesis convergence a repeatable membership mode
idea: The reviewer panel assumes membership = a set of Claude lenses scoring one shared artifact. But the fleet has proven prior art for a different, stronger consensus shape — two engines producing fully independent syntheses that converged 15/17, hand-reconciled. Reframe independent-synthesis-then-reconcile as a first-class panel membership mode, not a one-off manual event: an external engine produces a blind parallel synthesis, Claude produces its own, and Claude reconciles the divergences (advisory only, Claude adjudicates). This ports the mined win into the standing protocol.
basis: Grounding-brief §7 line 148 singleton: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' (theme-5 prior art), lives in workflow wf_7e5d77a2-5c0 session-mining synthesis. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}: the external synthesis is advisory input; Claude remains verifier-of-record for the reconciled result.
outcome_shape: PR adding an 'independent-synthesis' membership mode to consensus-protocol.md and external-engine-workers.md (blind parallel synthesis -> Claude reconcile -> advisory evidence only), with a worked convergence-rate example. Verified: mode produces a reconciliation artifact where every accepted divergence carries a Claude adjudication line.

title: Correlated lenses fake agreement — measure panel independence, don't assume it
idea: Panel membership is chosen by judgment from a fixed reviewer registry, and consensus is read off the average as if every lens were an independent vote. But two reviewers with correlated lenses (e.g. security-reviewer and privacy-reviewer overlapping on data-handling) inflate apparent agreement — the number looks like consensus when it is one viewpoint counted twice. Reframe consensus quality as a function of lens independence: annotate each reviewer's lens with its correlation neighbors and add a selection guard that flags a panel whose accepting lenses are not genuinely independent, so a 9.2 average from three correlated lenses is not treated as strong consensus.
basis: First-principles: averaging correlated scorers overstates agreement — the 15/17 convergence number is meaningful precisely because the two syntheses were independent; strip independence and the same 15/17 is uninformative. reviewer-registry.md lists lenses with no independence metadata, so overlap is invisible to the aggregator today.
outcome_shape: PR adding lens-independence/correlation annotations to reviewer-registry.md and a panel-selection guard in consensus-protocol.md that warns when accepting lenses share a correlation cluster. Verified: a panel of three correlated lenses raises the independence warning; a diverse panel does not.

title: Consensus should have to earn its convene — add an entry gate, not just exit scoping
idea: The protocol optimizes cost only on the way out (re-run only reviewers scoring <9.0) but always convenes the full panel on the way in, spending a multi-reviewer fan-out on trivial diffs. That 'always convene' is an unexamined default. Reframe: convening consensus is itself a cost decision that must clear an entry threshold on change risk/size — below it, a single-lens or no-panel path; above it, a panel whose size scales with risk. This makes consensus worth its tokens by construction and composes with the risk-tier thresholds (T5-F3-2).
basis: consensus-protocol.md:113-126 ('To minimize cost, only re-run reviewers that scored < 9.0') is the ONLY cost lever and it is exit-only; nothing decides whether to convene a panel at all. Grounding-brief §7 records 350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs — evidence that unconditional fan-out is the dominant spend.
outcome_shape: PR adding a 'convene decision' pre-step and a panel-size-by-risk table to consensus-protocol.md, plus a validator asserting sub-threshold changes take the single-lens path. Verified: a docs-only diff resolves to a single lens; a multi-file risky diff convenes a scaled panel.

title: Two plugins picked two different bounds for the same panel-blowup fear — reconcile them
idea: saga hard-caps a verify panel at 7 (VERIFY_N_CAP, born from a real 22-judge blowup) while team-execution independently caps review at 3 iterations, with no shared reasoning. Both constants exist to bound the same failure — a panel that costs more than the decision is worth — yet they were chosen separately and drift independently. Reframe: bounded-panel-cost is one governance policy accidentally split across two plugins. Unify it into a single bounded-panel policy in the shared consensus spec, expressing both the participant cap and the iteration cap as instances of one 'panels are bounded' rule with documented per-context values.
basis: execution_spec.py:111-114: VERIFY_N_CAP = 7, comment 'born from a real 22-judge panel incident'; consensus-protocol.md:17: 'Maximum iterations: 3'. Same concern (unbounded panel cost), two constants, no shared home. Honors {#tier-vocab-ordering} by keeping the caps as an ordered/bounded policy rather than ad hoc numbers.
outcome_shape: PR/doc reconciling both caps under a single bounded-panel policy in consensus_spec (participant-cap + iteration-cap as one rule with per-context values), cross-referenced from execution_spec.py docstring and consensus-protocol.md, plus a test asserting both caps resolve from the shared policy. Verified: changing the bounded-panel policy moves both caps.

title: Single consensus-contract source of truth both plugins conform to
idea: Today two divergent consensus implementations exist with no shared primitive: team-execution scores dimensions 0-10 against a 9.0/7.0/5.0 rubric (consensus-protocol.md), while saga /code-review emits findings from judgment-selected lenses (code-review/SKILL.md:145-167) with no scores at all. Extract one machine-readable contract — verdict vocabulary (ACCEPT/NEEDS-REVISION/BLOCKING), the score/finding adapters, consolidation-and-dedup rules, and the escalation ladder — into a single reference (e.g. plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md promoted to a shared contract) that saga /code-review and team-execution both point at. Add a conformance drift-guard test asserting neither plugin's prose restates the thresholds independently. This makes every future consensus change (a new verdict state, a new consolidation rule) a one-file edit instead of an N-plugin hand-copy.
basis: Two non-conforming implementations verified: team-execution consensus-protocol.md:67-78 (score table + 9.0 pass rule) vs saga plugins/saga/skills/code-review/SKILL.md:145-167 (findings-based judgment lenses, no scoring). Grounding brief section 3 finding 1 names 'contract-mirror drift' as the #1 cross-repo pain (validate_card_body stale hand-copy → 343 cards failed live contract, #222) — a shared consensus contract is the same drift-prevention pattern applied to consensus.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared consensus-contract reference doc, updating saga code-review/SKILL.md and team-execution SKILL.md + consensus-protocol.md to cite it, plus tests/test_consensus_contract_conformance.py asserting no independent threshold restatement; verified by the test failing when a threshold is edited in only one location.

title: Plan-authored consensus thresholds via a .consensus.json registry
idea: The 9.0 pass, 7.0 blocking-dimension, 5.0 severe-stop, and max-3-iteration values are hardcoded in prose across SKILL.md:249/345/346 and consensus-protocol.md:17/74 — an operator cannot tighten a security-critical run to 9.5 or loosen a docs run without editing plugin markdown. Introduce an optional .consensus.json config (mirroring the plan-authored per-teammate lever pattern) whose keys — accept_threshold, blocking_dimension_floor, severe_stop_floor, max_iterations — default to today's values when absent, are resolved once at Step A and echoed into the run header. The protocol reads resolved values, never literals. This turns every future threshold-policy question into a config edit and lets /plan dictate consensus rigor per outcome the way it already dictates tier.
basis: Hardcoded literals confirmed at plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md:249 ('>= 9.0/10 from every reviewer'), :345-346, and consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3') / :74. Grounding brief section 5 carries {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} as a direct operator ask for plan-dictated per-teammate knobs — thresholds are the same 'why can't I pick?' shape applied to consensus rigor rather than effort.
outcome_shape: PR adding .consensus.json schema + resolver, rewriting consensus-protocol.md and SKILL.md to reference resolved values, a defaults-preserve test, and release-surface updates (team-execution plugin.json, marketplace.json, CHANGELOG); verified by a test asserting an absent config reproduces byte-identical 9.0/7.0/5.0/3 behavior and a present config overrides the run header.

title: Stamp the gated/advisory governance bit onto the consensus verdict artifact
idea: The gated-vs-advisory distinction currently lives only as a routing INPUT in lifecycle_state.py (consensus_is_gated selects team-execution vs the advisory ultracode branch) — it is consumed at dispatch and then lost. When a consensus verdict is later ported to a new locus (an /outcome leaf, a resumed saga, a code-review escalation), nothing on the produced artifact records whether that verdict was gating a merge or was throwaway advisory, so the governance split cannot survive the port. Stamp governance_mode (gated|advisory) plus consensus_is_gated onto the consensus verdict/completion record itself, and add a guard that refuses to treat an advisory-stamped verdict as a merge gate. This makes the split a durable property of the evidence, not a transient dispatch decision — the compounding win is that any future consumer of a consensus artifact inherits its governance semantics for free.
basis: Crosses binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) and directly operationalizes {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split}. Engaging the split's own evidence: lifecycle_state.py:164-165 computes gated_consensus/advisory_consensus at dispatch but LEARNINGS.md:523-533 documents the split as governance-not-depth; the never-gatekeepers revisit-when ('team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot') is respected because stamping mode makes advisory verdicts structurally non-gating, reinforcing rather than relaxing Claude-as-verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: PR extending the team-execution completion report + lifecycle_state.py verdict record with a governance_mode field, adding a guard that rejects an advisory-stamped verdict used as a merge gate, and a test proving the ported artifact retains its mode; verified by a round-trip test (produce advisory verdict → consume in a merge-gate path → guard blocks).

title: External-engine advisory reviewer slot in the consensus panel (non-scoring)
idea: The consensus panel is Claude-only (reviewer-registry.md base 3 + keyword-optional), yet mined prior art shows a Claude+Codex independent synthesis converging 15/17 with hand reconciliation — a diversity signal currently thrown away. Add an advisory reviewer slot that dispatches one external engine (Codex offload, or Ollama at $0) as a non-scoring lens whose findings feed the fix-consolidation step but NEVER count toward the 9.0 consensus and never block. The panel gains a genuinely independent perspective (different model family catches what a monoculture green suite misses) while Claude stays verifier-of-record. The slot reuses the existing external-engine-workers.md chaperone-dispatch plumbing, so it is a registry entry, not new machinery — every future consensus run can opt in a second opinion for the price of one config flag.
basis: Prior art: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' — grounding brief section 7 singletons (theme 5 prior art), plus section 3 finding 2 (team-execution consensus caught defects green suites missed, 2 repos, operator-praised). Binding-decision engagement: {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) revisit-when is literally 'team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot' — this idea IS that condition, and stays compliant by making the slot advisory/non-scoring per {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318, second-opinion→opus/high dispatch, never a second executor).
outcome_shape: PR adding an advisory-reviewer registry entry + dispatch wiring reusing external-engine-workers.md, updating consensus-protocol.md so external findings route to consolidation but are excluded from the score denominator, plus a test asserting an external verdict never moves the 9.0 gate; verified by a run where a low external 'score' cannot block consensus.

title: One shared lens/reviewer registry feeding both consensus loci
idea: Reviewer membership is defined twice with divergent selection models: team-execution's reviewer-registry.md (keyword-triggered optional reviewers atop a fixed base 3) and saga /code-review's judgment-selected lens-catalog (4 always-on + conditional). A lens authored for one is invisible to the other, so adding e.g. a 'concurrency' or 'privacy' perspective is a two-place job that drifts. Merge them into one shared lens/reviewer registry keyed by domain-trigger, with a per-locus selection adapter (keyword-match for team-execution, judgment for code-review) reading the same catalog. Define a reviewer once, both consensus surfaces can draw on it — the compounding return grows with every lens added and eliminates a standing drift source.
basis: Two independent membership definitions verified: team-execution reviewer-registry.md:9-42 (base 3 + keyword-optional table) vs saga code-review/SKILL.md:147-149 ('4 always-on lenses ... plus conditional lenses ... Load references/lens-catalog.md'). Grounding brief section 3 finding 3 (mission-control contract copies drifting, overlaps finding 1) establishes duplicated-definition drift as an active repo disease; a shared registry is the same source-of-truth consolidation applied to review membership.
outcome_shape: PR introducing a shared lens/reviewer registry + two thin selection adapters, repointing reviewer-registry.md and lens-catalog.md at it, with a drift-guard test asserting a lens added once appears in both loci's selectable set; verified by adding a probe lens and asserting both adapters can select it.

title: A consensus-worth-it estimator that recommends inline vs advisory-N vs gated-team
idea: There is no lever telling an operator WHEN consensus earns its tokens — the choice between inline self-review, an advisory throwaway N-vote panel, and a full gated team is made ad hoc. Build a small pre-consensus estimator that takes blast radius (files touched, security surface, whether the verdict gates a merge) and the mode-dependent spend posture and outputs a recommendation with a cheaper fallback always surfaced: e.g. 'docs-only, non-gating → inline; security surface + merge gate → gated team.' It reuses the triage-escape-hatch signals already in reviewer-registry.md and the governance bit from idea 3, and encodes the intake's asymmetric-approval rule (attended spend-increases need explicit yes) as machinery rather than prose. Every future run inherits a defensible, cheap-first consensus-cost decision instead of re-litigating it.
basis: Intake brief tension 1 (asymmetric approval: attended spend-increasing choices 'always require explicit operator yes ... Cache-first only silent default') and tension 4 (Fable spend lever: 'expensive never silent default') are direct operator statements demanding this lever be encoded, not hardcoded. The triage-escape-hatch qualifying criteria (reviewer-registry.md:61-76: single-config-change, no security surface, <3 files) already enumerate the blast-radius signals the estimator needs.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus-worth-it estimator (script or SKILL step) reading blast-radius + governance signals and emitting a recommendation-with-fallback into the run header, updating reviewer-registry.md triage section to route through it; verified by table-driven tests mapping (docs/no-gate)→inline, (security+merge-gate)→gated-team and asserting the cheaper fallback is always printed.

title: Convergence-driven iteration cap replacing the flat max-3
idea: The 'Maximum iterations: 3, then proceed with best version regardless' rule (consensus-protocol.md:17,61) wastes cycles when reviewers already agree and truncates when they are still moving. Replace the flat cap with a convergence stopping rule: stop early when inter-cycle score deltas fall below an epsilon (reviewers have stabilized) AND all pass, and allow a bounded extra cycle when scores are still climbing steeply toward the threshold — with the hard ceiling (from idea 2's max_iterations config) preserved as a backstop. This ports the 15/17 convergence concept from ad-hoc hand-reconciliation into the loop's own stopping logic, spending iterations where they change the verdict and skipping them where they don't. Compounding: the same convergence primitive later informs the advisory-N vote count and the external-slot reconciliation.
basis: First-principles: the current cap conflates a cost bound with a stopping criterion. A fixed N is optimal only if marginal iteration value is constant, but review-revise value is monotonically decreasing (each cycle resolves the largest-remaining fixes first per the consolidation/dedup step, consensus-protocol.md:131-138) and approaches zero as scores converge. A convergence test (delta < epsilon) is the correct stopping rule for a decreasing-returns sequence; a flat N either overspends past convergence or halts a still-improving sequence. The 15/17 convergence observation (section 7) is empirical evidence that independent reviewers do converge, making an epsilon-test well-defined rather than speculative.
outcome_shape: PR rewriting consensus-protocol.md's cycle-structure and after-3-cycles sections to a convergence stopping rule with a configurable epsilon and a hard max-iterations backstop, plus a simulation test over synthetic score trajectories asserting early-stop on convergence and backstop-halt on divergence; verified by the test covering a converged sequence (stops at cycle 2) and a stuck sequence (halts at ceiling).

title: Extract consensus as a Raft-style reusable module (consensus_spec.py)
idea: In distributed systems, Raft succeeded precisely because it was designed as an *understandable, extractable* consensus module that etcd, Consul, and TiKV all vendor rather than re-deriving Paxos per project. The fleet has the opposite: consensus lives only as prose in team-execution's consensus-protocol.md while saga's /code-review, /doc-review, and /founder-review each hand-roll their own scoring narrative. Extract the scoring/verdict/iteration state machine into a saga-side primitive `plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py` (a peer of execution_spec.py) that takes a panel of scored dimensions and returns {reached, blocking, re-run-set} deterministically. team-execution's consensus-protocol.md and saga review skills both consume it instead of restating the 9.0/re-run/3-cap logic. The primitive is pure and unit-testable, killing the drift where each surface's threshold wording quietly diverges.
