basis: Raft (Ongaro & Ousterhout, 'In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm', 2014) was explicitly built to be reused as a library module across etcd/Consul/TiKV rather than reimplemented; the design goal was extraction. Fleet counterpart: consensus lives as prose in plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md:17,40,74 (thresholds/iteration cap) with no shared code, while grounding brief §3 item 2 records team-execution consensus catching defects green suites missed — the primitive worth extracting.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/consensus_spec.py (pure scoring/verdict/re-run state machine) + tests/test_consensus_spec.py; consensus-protocol.md rewritten to cite the primitive; version/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json bumps for saga + team-execution. Verified by unit tests asserting identical verdicts to the current prose rules on a fixture score matrix (all>=9.0 pass; any dim<7.0 forced re-run; 3-cap terminal).

title: Authority gradient: typed gating|advisory participant field (flight-deck PIC model)
idea: Aviation cockpit resource management runs a strict authority gradient: the first officer and every automated advisory (TCAS traffic callouts, EGPWS) can and must speak, but the Pilot-in-Command holds final command authority and a subordinate voice can never *execute* a clearance. Port that structurally into the extracted consensus primitive: every panel participant carries `authority: gating | advisory`, and the state machine mechanically refuses to let any advisory score move the reached/blocking outcome — advisory scores are surfaced and reconciled by Claude, never summed into the gate. This makes {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split} a *typed invariant that survives porting* to any consumer, rather than a convention re-explained per plugin. A guard test asserts that flipping an advisory participant's score from 10 to 0 never changes the gate verdict.
basis: Binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283, grounding brief §2): 'Claude is verifier-of-record for every gated decision; codex/agy = generator/advisory-reviewer/non-gated worker only. Structurally enforced.' This idea IS the structural enforcement mechanism and its revisit-when ('team-execution gains an external-engine worker slot') is exactly what a typed authority field prepares for safely. Alignment note §2: 'issue text must be explicit that consensus participation is advisory-only.'
outcome_shape: PR adding an `authority` enum field to the consensus_spec.py participant schema + a guard test (test_consensus_authority_invariant.py) proving advisory-score perturbation cannot change the gate; consensus-protocol.md and external-engine-workers.md updated to mark external engines authority=advisory. Verified by the invariant test + a metadata drift test that every external-engine reviewer entry is authority=advisory.

title: SPC-style consensus profiles: control limits derived per work-class, not hardcoded
idea: Statistical process control never uses one universal control limit; the UCL/LCL are set per process from its own capability, and a tighter limit is chosen where defects are costlier. The consensus protocol instead freezes 9.0/7.0/5.0 and max-3-iterations as global constants, so a docs typo pass and a security-critical change face identical gates. Introduce named `consensus-profiles` (e.g. `strict` 9.5/8.0/2-cap, `standard` 9.0/7.0/3-cap, `advisory` 7.0/none/1-cap) selected by work-class at invocation, replacing the magic constants with a profile lookup in consensus_spec.py. The profile is an operator-choosable input, honoring the intake's 'plugins encode the question, not a hardcoded mandate' posture, and each profile ships with a documented rationale for its limits.
basis: Hardcoded constants: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3'), :40 ('ACCEPT >= 9.0'), :72 ('< 7.0 BLOCKING'), :232 ('< 5.0 severe'); execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP=7 is the only other consensus-shaped constant and is already a named tunable, establishing the pattern. Intake brief resolved-tension 1: 'plugins encode the question, not a hard-coded mandate.' Analogy: SPC control limits (Shewhart control charts) are process-derived, not universal.
outcome_shape: PR adding a CONSENSUS_PROFILES table to consensus_spec.py (or a consensus-profiles.md registry) + profile-selection param threaded through consensus-protocol.md; tests asserting each profile's gate math and that removing a profile fails a drift guard. Verified by unit tests per profile + CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bumps.

title: Diversity-floor panel composition + external advisory synthesis (wisdom-of-crowds)
idea: Scott Page's Diversity Prediction Theorem proves a crowd's collective error falls as the *diversity* of its members' models rises — accuracy alone is not enough, cognitive diversity is a first-class ingredient. The current reviewer roster is a fixed set (Devil's Advocate, Security, Architecture, Infra) with no measure of lens overlap, and the mined 15/17 Claude+Codex independent-synthesis convergence is unused machinery. Add a panel-composition step that (a) scores lens overlap across the selected reviewers against a diversity floor, warning when the panel is redundant, and (b) optionally seats one external-engine participant (Codex/DeepSeek) that produces an *independent* synthesis reconciled by Claude — advisory-only, never gating. This operationalizes the 15/17 prior art as a repeatable divergence-check, not a one-off.
basis: Scott Page, 'The Difference' (2007) Diversity Prediction Theorem: collective error = average individual error minus prediction diversity — diversity mathematically reduces error. Fleet prior art: grounding brief §7 records 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converged 15/17, hand-reconciled.' Crosses {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) — engaged by keeping the external participant authority=advisory, reconciled by Claude as verifier-of-record, matching its revisit-when for a team-execution external-engine slot; and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318) second-opinion→opus/high dispatch shape.
outcome_shape: PR adding a panel-diversity check + optional external advisory synthesis slot to consensus-protocol.md and reviewer-registry.md, with the external slot marked authority=advisory (depends on T5-F5-2's typed field); a lens-overlap heuristic doc + test. Verified by a test that a redundant panel (two near-identical lenses) trips the diversity warning and that the external synthesis never enters the gate denominator.

title: Byzantine-tolerant quorum: survive one miscalibrated reviewer without weakening the gate
idea: Byzantine fault tolerance in distributed consensus assumes some participants may be arbitrarily wrong or adversarial and still reaches a correct decision with a 3f+1 quorum. The consensus protocol today demands unanimity (ALL reviewers >= 9.0), so a single miscalibrated or stuck reviewer — the Devil's Advocate is *designed* to be adversarial — can pin the panel at the 3-cycle cap even when the substance is sound. Add a quorum mode where, above a panel size, the gate tolerates up to f dissenting reviewers *provided Claude (verifier-of-record) explicitly adjudicates each dissent* — the tolerance never hands the gate to an advisory engine, it only lets Claude discount a demonstrably-miscalibrated lens with a logged justification. This keeps the gate Claude-owned while stopping one outlier from forcing a false 3-cap failure.
basis: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (Lamport, Shostak, Pease, 'The Byzantine Generals Problem', 1982; Castro & Liskov PBFT 1999): 3f+1 quorum reaches correct consensus despite f arbitrarily-faulty nodes. Fleet counterpart: consensus-protocol.md:74 requires unanimity ('ALL >= 9.0') and :17 caps at 3 cycles, so one stuck reviewer forces the documented 3-cap degrade (:161-172). Does NOT contradict {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} because adjudication stays with Claude — dissent-discounting is a Claude judgment with logged cause, not a quorum handed to an engine.
outcome_shape: PR adding an optional quorum-with-adjudication mode to consensus_spec.py/consensus-protocol.md: above panel-size K, up to f dissents may be Claude-adjudicated with a mandatory logged justification appended to the completion report. Verified by tests that adjudication requires a recorded cause and that f=0 (default) preserves today's unanimity behavior exactly.

title: Risk-based panel underwriting: size the panel to change exposure
idea: Insurance underwriting sets coverage and scrutiny proportional to expected loss — you don't run a full actuarial review on a trivial policy, and you never skip it on a catastrophic one. Consensus currently spawns the whole reviewer panel regardless of blast radius, so a one-line docs fix and a payments-path change both pay full-panel token cost. Add a consensus-worthiness pre-gate in consensus_spec.py that reads cheap risk signals already available (diff line count, files touched, security/auth path hits, public-API surface) and recommends a panel size — a single Devil's Advocate for low-exposure changes escalating to the full diverse panel plus strict profile for high-exposure ones. The recommendation is surfaced as an operator-choosable lever (never a silent downgrade), and the existing VERIFY_N_CAP=7 bounds the top end.
basis: First-principles: consensus cost scales with panel size x iterations x token-per-reviewer, yet review value is non-uniform — grounding brief §7 flags '350-450k recon' spend and §6 item 6 records operator pain that 'xhigh-Opus on everything wasteful.' execution_spec.py:114 VERIFY_N_CAP=7 already bounds panel size, proving panel-size-as-a-tunable is legitimate; no mechanism yet *chooses* within that bound by risk. A risk-proportional selector converts a flat cost into an expected-value-weighted one, and being operator-surfaced it honors intake tension 1 (no silent spend change).
outcome_shape: PR adding a risk-signal panel-size recommender to consensus_spec.py + consensus-protocol.md Step B3a, surfaced as an operator prompt with a documented low/standard/high mapping. Verified by unit tests mapping fixture diffs (docs-only, mixed, security-path) to recommended panel sizes and asserting the recommendation is advisory (operator can override upward).

title: Acceptance-sampling review: inspect a risk-stratified sample of hunks, not every line
idea: Manufacturing quality control abandoned 100% inspection decades ago for acceptance sampling (MIL-STD-105 / AQL): inspect a statistically-sized sample sized to lot size and acceptable quality level, and reject the lot if sample defects exceed the acceptance number. On large diffs the panel currently reasons over the whole change (or an artifact-pointer to it), and cost grows with lot size. Add an acceptance-sampling mode where reviewers are directed to a risk-stratified sample of hunks (all security/auth/public-API hunks always in-sample; the remainder sampled by an AQL-style plan sized to diff magnitude), with an explicit acceptance number — if sampled defects exceed it, the whole diff is kicked back to full review. This bounds review cost sub-linearly in diff size while keeping high-risk regions fully covered.
basis: MIL-STD-105E / ISO 2859-1 acceptance sampling: sample size and acceptance number are functions of lot size and Acceptable Quality Level; full inspection is reserved for failed lots. Fleet counterpart: consensus-protocol.md:28,190-198 already passes reviewers a full diff or artifact-pointer with no size-scaling, and grounding brief §7 records large-diff review cost as a spend driver. Stratification (security/auth always in-sample) borrows the same risk-tiering as T5-F5-6, keeping governance intact since gating still rides on Claude's read of sampled findings.
outcome_shape: PR adding an acceptance-sampling review mode to consensus-protocol.md + a hunk-sampler helper (risk-stratified, AQL-sized) with an acceptance-number escalation-to-full-review rule; tests. Verified by tests that all security/auth hunks are always in-sample, that exceeding the acceptance number triggers full-diff re-review, and that sample size grows sub-linearly with diff size.

title: Consensus replay log: append-only score ledger (event-sourced, Raft-log style)
idea: Raft's correctness rests on a replicated *append-only log* — every state transition is an immutable, ordered, replayable entry, which is also what makes the cluster auditable and recoverable. Consensus today emits only a transient score table per cycle and a final prose summary; once the run ends, the per-reviewer, per-iteration score trajectory is gone, so nobody can mine reviewer calibration drift or prove chain-of-custody on a gate decision. Emit an append-only consensus ledger (one entry per reviewer per iteration: score, verdict, fix-request digest, authority, adjudication cause) written by consensus_spec.py alongside the completion report. This makes consensus decisions replayable and audit-grade, and feeds the fleet's dark learning-mining loop (theme 10) with structured reviewer-calibration data it currently lacks — directly answering the 'evidence-artifact chain-of-custody' gap.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:142-157 shows scores are rendered only as an ephemeral per-cycle table and :166-172 keeps just a final prose note — no durable per-iteration record. Grounding brief §7 names 'probe script overwriting FAIL evidence artifact later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)' as a real integrity gap, and §3 item 5 records the promote/learning loop 'has never fired' for lack of substrate. An append-only ledger is the substrate. Reinforces theme 10 (provenance discipline) from the consensus side.
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only consensus-ledger writer to consensus_spec.py (JSONL: run-id, iteration, reviewer, authority, score, verdict, fix-digest, adjudication-cause) + consensus-protocol.md wiring + tests. Verified by a test that a 3-iteration run produces a complete, ordered, immutable ledger and that re-running does not rewrite prior entries; CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bumps.

title: One consensus kernel: extract the scoring contract from prose+frontmatter into a single versioned spec
idea: Flip the constraint 'every reviewer re-declares the pass rule' to its extreme: exactly ONE place in the fleet may state a consensus threshold. Today the 9.0/7.0/5.0 rule is written five+ times — consensus-protocol.md lines 17/70-74 plus each agent body (architecture-reviewer.md:120, devils-advocate-reviewer.md:62, security-reviewer.md:64) — a guaranteed drift surface. Create a machine-readable consensus-contract.json (accept>=9.0, revise-band 7.0-8.9, blocking<7.0, severe<5.0, max_iterations=3, denominator=applicable-dimensions) that consensus-protocol.md and every reviewer agent reference by anchor instead of restating numerically. Add a drift-guard test asserting no agent body contains a bare numeric threshold literal that disagrees with the contract. The practical kernel even if 'single source' is dogmatic: kill the copy-paste threshold drift that already burned 343 cards in the validate_card_body incident (grounding brief §3).
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Each reviewer must achieve an overall score of >= 9.0/10') and :70-74 restate the threshold that is ALSO independently hardcoded in agents/architecture-reviewer.md:120, agents/devils-advocate-reviewer.md:62, agents/security-reviewer.md:64 — same rule, five authored copies, no shared source; grounding brief §3 ranks contract-mirror drift as the #1 cross-repo pain (validate_card_body stale hand-copy, 343 cards).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-contract.json + a tests/test_consensus_contract_drift.py that greps every agents/*.md and consensus-protocol.md for numeric threshold literals and fails on any that disagree with the JSON; CHANGELOG + plugin.json version bump. Verified: intentionally editing one agent's 9.0 to 8.5 turns the test red.

title: Portable consensus-verdict artifact: a JSON envelope any plugin emits and any plugin can honor
idea: Flip 'consensus lives inside team-execution's B3 loop' to the extreme where consensus is a free-floating artifact no single plugin owns. Define a consensus-verdict schema (run-id, per-lens scores, overall, verdict, gated-bit, iteration, unresolved-fixes, produced-by) that team-execution's Step B3 emits and that saga /code-review, /outcome leaf gates, and /qa can all read without re-running the panel. The kernel: consensus results today are trapped in a session transcript and a completion report; making the verdict a durable typed artifact (mirroring the artifact_pointer.py pattern already in this plugin) lets a downstream gate cite an upstream consensus instead of re-spending tokens on it, and lets the gated-bit travel with the verdict rather than being re-derived.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/artifact_pointer.py already establishes a typed JSON pointer artifact pattern in this exact plugin (CLAUDE.md notes team-execution is now hybrid because of it); consensus-protocol.md:161-172 shows the verdict currently dies as free-text in a completion report with no schema, so no downstream consumer can honor it.
outcome_shape: PR adding references/consensus-verdict-schema.md + a snapshot/deref helper in artifact_pointer.py (or a sibling script) that serializes B3 scores; consensus-protocol.md Step B3d/After-3-Cycles updated to emit the envelope; unit test round-trips a verdict and asserts the gated-bit and applicable-denominator survive serialization. Verified by the round-trip test.

title: Everything-advisory flip: make gated-vs-advisory a bit that rides the verdict, not a saga-side routing accident
idea: Flip to the extreme where ZERO consensus ever gates — every verdict is advisory. That world is wrong (loses the whole point of team-execution gates), but running the flip exposes the kernel: the gated/advisory distinction currently lives only saga-side in lifecycle_state.py consensus_is_gated and operator-choice.md routing, NOT in the consensus protocol itself, so a team-execution verdict carries no self-description of whether it was meant to block. Port the governance-split bit INTO the consensus artifact so any consumer knows a verdict's standing without re-reading saga's router. This explicitly preserves {#gated-vs-advisory-consensus-is-a-governance-split}: the bit is not erased, it is made portable so the split survives when consensus is consumed outside saga's /plan flow (the anchor's whole intent — that a verdict must 'need to stick' — is exactly what a portable bit encodes).
basis: operator-choice.md:81-95 defines the split entirely as a backend-routing decision (consensus_is_gated=True default in lifecycle_state.py:133-area); the split is decided in saga/plan §5.2 KTD4 and never re-expressed inside team-execution's consensus-protocol.md — the verdict artifact is governance-blind, so porting consensus out of saga would silently drop the gated meaning the anchor #gated-vs-advisory... exists to protect.
outcome_shape: PR adding a required 'gated' field to the consensus-verdict envelope (from T5-F6-2), wiring saga lifecycle_state.py to stamp it at B3 emit-time, and a doc-review note in operator-choice.md that the bit is now verdict-resident not router-resident; test asserts an advisory verdict never sets the merge-block flag and a gated one always does. Verified by the paired test.

title: Plan-declared threshold profiles: flip the hardcoded 9.0/7.0/5.0 to a per-outcome consensus stringency dial
idea: Flip the constraint 'the bar is always 9.0' to its two extremes — a hotfix that only needs 5.0-to-ship, and a security-critical release that demands a clean 10.0. Neither extreme is a fixed global, which is the point: the stringency should be an operator/plan choice, not a constant baked into prose. Introduce named threshold profiles (e.g. strict=9.0/7.0/5.0, standard=8.0/6.0/4.0, ship-fast=7.0/5.0/3.0) selectable in the saga /plan unit table alongside the existing tier palette, defaulting to strict. The kernel survives even if operators never touch it: profiles turn the magic numbers into a declared, greppable, testable config instead of five hand-copied literals, and make 'why did this pass' auditable.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 and :70-78 hardcode 9.0/7.0/5.0 and max-iterations=3 as universal constants with no operator lever; saga/plan/SKILL.md already carries the ONE existing per-unit stringency table (the tier palette, plan/SKILL.md:296-352 per grounding brief §1), which is the natural host for a consensus-profile column — a lever seam that already exists.
outcome_shape: PR adding threshold-profiles to consensus-contract.json (from T5-F6-1) + a profile-selector column in plan/SKILL.md's unit table + KTD4 interrogation asking stringency when consensus is chosen; drift test asserts every profile keeps accept>=revise>=blocking>=severe ordering. Verified by the ordering test and a plan-render fixture showing the column.

title: Infinite-iterations flip: replace the max-3 cap with plateau-detection convergence
idea: Flip 'max 3 iterations, then ship best version' to unbounded iteration, then mine the kernel. Unbounded is unaffordable and can loop forever, but the fixed cap of 3 is equally arbitrary — it can stop one fix short of consensus, or waste a cycle when scores have already plateaued. Add plateau-detection: stop early when the round-over-round score delta for all still-open reviewers falls below an epsilon (no meaningful movement = a real disagreement a fourth cycle won't resolve), and surface that as 'converged-stuck' rather than the current silent 'proceeded with best version'. Keep 3 as the hard ceiling but let convergence end it sooner and label WHY it ended. This makes the termination reason a portable, honest signal instead of an opaque cap.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:17 ('Maximum iterations: 3. After 3 cycles, proceed with the best available version regardless of scores') and :161-172 (After 3 Cycles) treat 3 as a magic constant and the exit as undifferentiated. First-principles: a cap conflates two distinct terminal states — 'still improving but out of budget' vs 'stuck, scores not moving'. These warrant different operator actions (grant another cycle vs escalate the disagreement), so a single cap that cannot tell them apart discards decision-relevant information at exactly the moment consensus fails.
outcome_shape: PR updating consensus-protocol.md Step B3/After-3-Cycles with a plateau-epsilon rule + a 'termination_reason' field (consensus-reached | converged-stuck | cap-reached) on the verdict envelope; a small helper computing round-delta with a unit test over score sequences that plateau vs still-climbing. Verified: fixture where cycle-2→3 delta < epsilon reports converged-stuck, a climbing sequence reports cap-reached.

title: External advisory lens: seat Codex as a displayed-but-uncounted reviewer in the consensus panel
idea: Flip 'the reviewer roster is Claude-only subagents' toward '100 heterogeneous reviewers including other engines' and pull back to the one defensible seat: an external engine (Codex) reviewing the same diff as a SHADOW lens whose score is displayed in the cycle table but never enters the pass denominator or the fix-routing gate. The 15/17 independent-synthesis convergence is direct evidence the second engine catches real things; seating it advisory-only harvests that signal without letting it gate. This explicitly engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283) revisit-when: it does NOT add an external-engine gating slot — it is the chaperone-dispatch 'second-opinion→opus/high' shape from #318 applied to review, an advisory participant whose verdict Claude, the verifier-of-record, may adopt or discard. The score column is annotated 'advisory, not counted' so the governance boundary is legible in the artifact itself.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons + §3 finding 2: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled' — named prior art living in the session-mining synthesis (wf_7e5d77a2-5c0); the chaperone-dispatch second-opinion shape already exists at plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/external-engine-workers.md, giving a home for an advisory-review worker without inventing a new executor kind.
outcome_shape: PR adding an 'advisory reviewer' row-type to consensus-protocol.md's score-display + Step B3 (explicitly excluded from the >=9.0 denominator and re-review routing) and an external-engine-workers.md entry for a second-opinion review worker; test asserts an advisory reviewer's score never changes the consensus verdict. Verified by a fixture where a 4.0 advisory score leaves an otherwise-passing panel PASS.

title: Diff-shaped lens selection: port saga /code-review's judgment-selected lenses into team-execution's fixed roster
idea: Flip the fixed 5-dimension reviewer roster to the '100 possible lenses' extreme and mine the routing intelligence. team-execution spawns a static reviewer set regardless of what the diff touches (a pure-docs diff still summons the security and infra reviewers, who then score inert dimensions), while saga /code-review already selects lenses by judgment against the actual diff. Port that selection: a lens-selection step that reads the diff shape from the reviewer-registry and seats only applicable reviewers, recording the excluded ones as 'not-seated' with a cause — the same static-non-applicable vocabulary consensus-protocol.md already uses for excluded dimensions, lifted from dimension-granular to reviewer-granular. Consensus membership becomes portable and diff-appropriate rather than a fixed list, and the denominator honesty the protocol already prizes extends to who is even in the room.
basis: consensus-protocol.md:82-108 already defines 'static-non-applicable' exclusion but ONLY dimension-granular within one reviewer, explicitly noting a whole-lens exclusion path (':93-94, a reviewer whose entire lens is non-applicable is excluded WHOLE'); reviewer-registry.md exists as the seat roster and saga/code-review/SKILL.md already does judgment-selected lenses against the diff — the selection intelligence exists in one plugin and is absent in the other.
outcome_shape: PR adding a lens-selection step to consensus-protocol.md Step B3a keyed to reviewer-registry.md diff-shape tags, emitting a 'not-seated (static-non-applicable)' line per excluded reviewer; test asserts a docs-only diff seats no code-surface reviewers and the consensus denominator reflects only seated lenses. Verified by a docs-diff fixture producing a reduced, honestly-named panel.

title: Consensus-worthiness gate: a $0-consensus flip that decides when the panel is worth its tokens
idea: Flip the token budget to $0: if consensus could never spend a token, what would you still run? A single-reviewer smoke pass. That extreme exposes that team-execution today runs the full multi-reviewer 3-cycle panel unconditionally, even on a one-line typo fix — the 350-450k-tokens-in-20-min recon number shows how fast fan-out spend compounds. Add a consensus-worthiness predicate that sizes the panel to the change: below a diff-size/risk floor, run a single consolidated reviewer (or skip to advisory) and escalate to the full gated panel only when risk signals (security/auth/infra/cross-repo touch, or diff above a threshold) fire. The escalation ladder is the kernel — it makes 'when is consensus worth it' an explicit, tuned decision rather than an always-on cost, and it reuses the exact risk signals the governance-split router already computes.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)' quantifies fan-out cost; operator-choice.md:97-104 already computes the risk signals (has_security, has_infra, cross_repo, deployment_sensitive) that would key the escalation floor — the inputs exist, they are just never used to right-size the consensus panel, which always runs full per consensus-protocol.md Step B3.
outcome_shape: PR adding a consensus-worthiness section to consensus-protocol.md (Step B3-pre) keyed to the existing risk signals + a diff-size floor, defining single-reviewer / advisory / full-gated-panel tiers with escalation triggers; test asserts a sub-floor no-risk diff routes to single-reviewer and any security-touch diff forces the full panel. Verified by paired fixtures (trivial docs diff vs auth-touching diff).

title: Step B8 — team-execution teardown & reclamation gate
idea: team-execution's orchestration protocol runs Step B0 through B7 (Completion) and then simply stops — no phase reclaims the resources the run created. Add a Step B8 that, on both success and abort, removes worker worktrees, deletes merged/abandoned unit branches, signals resident chaperone-dispatch engines to release, and clears validator run-state from the git-ignored location. It fires at run END only (residency during the run is untouched), so warm-worker caching within the run is preserved. This closes the exact asymmetry where saga /work already tears down but team-execution silently leaks.
basis: team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md steps end at 'Step B7: Completion' (SKILL.md:403) with no B8; saga /work already does 'unlock, git worktree remove, git branch' cleanup at plugins/saga/skills/work/references/execution-strategy.md:97. This is complementary to {#worker-cache-scheduling} (reside team-side) rather than contradicting it: B8 reclaims at run-completion, the natural end of residency, not mid-run — so the caching window that decision protects stays intact.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a 'Step B8: Teardown & Reclamation' section to team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md plus references/teardown-checklist.md, with plugin.json + marketplace.json version bump and CHANGELOG entry. Verified by a drift-guard test asserting the B8 header exists and that the checklist enumerates worktree-remove, branch-delete, resident-release, and validator-state-clear items.

title: Fleet-wide orphan-worktree reaper (unregistered-worktree sweep)
idea: saga /outcome already has git-as-liveness-oracle sweeps in outcome_worktrees.py, but they only reconcile worktrees the /outcome DAG registered. Abandoned /work and team-execution worktrees are registered nowhere, so nothing ever reaps them — which is exactly how 15 stale worktrees accumulated in context-library and inflated the repo 10x. Build a standalone reaper that lists `git worktree list` + `.worktrees/`, cross-checks each path against every active saga/outcome registry and lease, and reports orphans (no owning registry, base branch merged, older than a threshold) with --dry-run as the default and an explicit --prune to act.
basis: Grounding brief §4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ → direct evidence for theme 6'; the three-sweep derive-on-read pattern already exists but is registry-scoped at plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_worktrees.py:300. Distinct from the direct-to-candidate 'worktree/background write routing' item, which is about Edit failing after removal, not reclaiming orphans.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/reap_worktrees.py (or a /saga reclaim command) plus tests/test_reap_worktrees.py exercising a fixture repo seeded with planted orphans and one live registered worktree, asserting the live one is spared and orphans are reported/pruned. Plugin.json + CHANGELOG updated.

title: Coordinator re-ping protocol for idle-without-delivering subagents
idea: Session mining caught subagents going idle without delivering an artifact and coordinators staring at stale idle notifications — reproduced live in the very session that mined it. Interactive /work parallel fan-out and team-execution reviewer fan-out have no idle detection at all. Define a lightweight re-ping protocol: the coordinator records each dispatch, and if a subagent returns no artifact within a per-lens budget, it re-pings ONCE with an explicit 'deliver your artifact or name your blocker' prompt before declaring the member stalled and routing around it. This is prose/protocol, not new machinery — a checklist step the coordinator follows.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 9: 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications — coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session).' Note: NOT the struck AskUserQuestion facet — this is subagent-liveness, in scope. Port source is /outcome's record_heartbeat/harvest_liveness (plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_liveness.py) reduced to a one-shot re-ping.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding references/liveness-reping.md to team-execution and a re-ping checklist step wired into Step B2 (Reviewers Reach Consensus) plus saga /work execution-strategy.md, with a drift-guard test asserting the reviewer fan-out step references the protocol. CHANGELOG + version bump.

title: Shared liveness oracle: port /outcome heartbeat/stalled to team fan-out
idea: /outcome carries a genuinely mature liveness harvester — heartbeat_seconds/timeout_seconds budgets, a `stalled` terminal that pages once and cascades, git as the liveness oracle. That machinery is trapped inside the /outcome DAG. team-execution reviewer fan-out and /work parallel subagents dispatch unbounded and unmonitored, so a hung member just hangs the whole run. Generalize harvest_liveness into a shared liveness module that both the /outcome dispatcher and the team-execution coordinator consume, giving fan-out members budgeted heartbeats and a deterministic stalled-reclaim path.
basis: plugins/saga/CHANGELOG.md:497-499 documents harvest_liveness reclaiming a stalled leaf on heartbeat/timeout breach; grounding brief §1 says the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP=7 and team fan-out is 'unbounded'. This crosses {#worker-cache-scheduling}, whose revisit-when is 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue' — this idle-poll harvester is precisely that justification, so the PR must land the shared queue/poll seam the decision anticipated rather than a bolt-on.
outcome_shape: Merged PR extracting plugins/saga/scripts/liveness.py (shared harvester) consumed by both outcome_liveness.py and a new team-execution coordinator hook, with tests/test_liveness_shared.py proving a heartbeat breach reclaims a fan-out member in both consumers. Marketplace + both plugin.json versions bumped.

title: Mid-run tier pause-and-adjust checkpoint
idea: Operators have directly asked for mid-run model-change pauses, but agent frontmatter hardcodes model with no dispatch-time override anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern — so today the only way to change tier mid-run is to abort and restart. Add a documented pause checkpoint between orchestration phases (e.g. after Step B1 workers, before B2 reviewers in team-execution; between execution waves in /work) where the coordinator re-reads the tier table for the REMAINING units, letting the operator downgrade or escalate the rest of the run without discarding completed work.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 6: 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses'; §1: 'no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern.' Crosses {#operator-choice-framework} (operator-choice = doc-only, CLI-driven /work), whose constraint I honor by making the checkpoint a documented re-read of the CLI tier table, NOT a new interactive gate primitive. Distinct from the QUEUED per-teammate-effort seed, which sets STATIC plan-time effort; this adjusts effort mid-RUN.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a 'Mid-run tier checkpoint' subsection to saga/skills/work/SKILL.md and team-execution SKILL.md Phase B, defining where the coordinator re-reads the remaining-unit tier table, with a drift-guard test asserting the checkpoint step and its remaining-units scoping. CHANGELOG + version bump.

title: Park & resume a running team across sessions
idea: A team-execution run is effectively all-or-nothing B0 through B7 within one session — there is no verb to pause a run partway, park its orchestration position, and resume it later on a fresh session or a different model. saga already proves cross-session durable resumption with its /outcome DAG. Add `park` (snapshot the current step, per-member status, reviewer consensus progress, and validator run-state to a durable location) and `resume` (restore that snapshot and re-enter at the parked step), so a long run can survive a session boundary, a rate-limit wall, or an operator stepping away.
basis: team-execution already writes validator run-state at Step B0a (team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md:286) but exposes no park/resume verb; saga /outcome demonstrates the durable cross-session model — 'a concurrent, durable DAG across sessions, worktrees' (plugins/saga/skills/outcome/SKILL.md:9). This extends existing state, so it does not add a new plugin and carries no {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} burden.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding park/resume steps to team-execution SKILL.md, a documented park-state schema under references/, and tests/test_team_park_resume.py asserting a parked run restores to the same step with member status intact. Plugin.json + marketplace + CHANGELOG updated.

title: fleet ps — one-shot inventory of what is running, held, and leaked
idea: No single command answers 'what is live across the fleet right now?' The knowledge is scattered: /outcome coordinator leases, the outcome_worktrees registry, saga's state.json tick index, and team-execution validator state each live in their own silo. Build a read-only aggregator that reads all four, cross-checks live worktrees against git (the liveness oracle), and prints a point-in-time table: held leases, active saga ticks, live worktrees, and orphan candidates flagged. It is diagnosis, not a daemon — a snapshot an operator runs to see leaks before they compound into 15 stale worktrees.
basis: Three siloed state stores are directly evidenced: coordinator lease at plugins/saga/skills/outcome/SKILL.md:75, the volatile state.json index at plugins/saga/skills/loop/references/drive-and-resume.md:107, and the worktree registry at plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_worktrees.py. Distinct from the QUEUED pulse-live-telemetry-component seed, which is a streaming/live telemetry surface; this is a one-shot read-only ps snapshot with leak flagging, no streaming.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_status.py (read-only, no mutation) plus tests/test_fleet_status.py feeding fixtures with a held lease, an active tick, a live worktree, and a planted orphan, asserting each renders in the correct column. CHANGELOG + plugin.json bump.

title: Teardown leak-ledger — reclamation as a verified invariant
idea: Even with a Step B8 teardown, reclamation done as best-effort repeats the fleet's most-recorded failure mode: the silent no-op that reports success without persisting. Make teardown falsifiable by emitting a leak-ledger at run close: dispatched N workers / reclaimed N worktrees / released N leases / remaining leaked = 0, asserted rather than assumed. A nonzero remainder surfaces loudly and names the specific leaked path or lease, turning 'we cleaned up' from a claim into evidence.
basis: Grounding brief §6 pattern 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring ... any bridge/delegation idea needs "did it actually run/persist" verification.' Teardown is exactly such an action; the ledger applies that verification discipline to reclamation. Complements (does not duplicate) T6-F1-1: that idea adds the teardown STEP, this adds the closing assertion artifact the step emits.
outcome_shape: Merged PR wiring a leak-ledger emission into the Step B8 teardown (team-execution) and /work cleanup, with a machine-checkable 'remaining leaked = 0' assertion and tests/test_leak_ledger.py proving a planted un-reclaimed worktree forces a nonzero, named remainder. CHANGELOG + version bump.

title: Step B8: non-skippable run-exit Teardown & Reclaim contract
idea: team-execution ends at Step B7 (Completion = report only); there is no step that shuts down resident workers, removes owned worktrees/branches, or proves nothing leaked. Invert teardown from a step-you-can-forget into an exit invariant: add Step B8 'Teardown & Reclaim' that TaskStops every named resident teammate, runs git worktree remove + branch -d for every worktree the run created, and writes a teardown manifest listing what it reclaimed. Then remove the possibility of skipping it: the run may not report completion (mirroring B7's missing-output block) until the reclamation ledger is empty or every residual is explicitly operator-accepted. R11 shedding only covers mid-run segment boundaries, so a clean run that never crossed a shed still leaks its last resident worker and worktree.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md:403 (Step B7 is the terminal step, report-only) and :311 (R11 Context Shedding fires only 'at its segment boundary', not at run exit) — no run-exit teardown exists; the missing-output completion-block at :418-421 is the exact enforcement pattern to reuse for reclamation.
outcome_shape: PR adding Step B8 to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md + new references/teardown-reclamation.md, with plugin.json/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json version bump; verified by a drift-guard test asserting Step B8 exists, enumerates worker-shutdown + worktree-removal + teardown-manifest, and that B7 completion refuses exit on a non-empty reclamation ledger.

title: Worktree reaper: automate away manual git worktree remove
idea: Fifteen abandoned saga worktrees inflated infiquetra-context-library 10x+ because cleanup depends on someone remembering to run git worktree remove. Remove the manual step entirely: ship a reaper script that lists worktrees, joins each against live signal (any live teammate holding it, the owning saga's terminal-or-absent state, and an age threshold), and prunes the ones that are provably abandoned. Dry-run is the default so it is safe to run in CI or a cron; --apply performs the removal and logs a reclamation record. This is distinct from the direct-to-candidate write-routing bug — that is about Edit failing after removal; this is about the worktrees never being removed at all.
basis: Grounding brief section 4, lines 86-88: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ -> direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8.'
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/worktree_reaper.py (dry-run default) + a saga skill/command entry that surfaces it, tests, and CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that seeds fake stale worktrees with terminal/absent sagas and asserts the reaper flags exactly those and leaves live-held ones untouched.

title: Segment-boundary tier re-derivation: change model mid-run without restart
idea: Today the only way to change a run's model/effort after dispatch is to abort and restart, because the (segment+agent+tier) tuple is derived once at start. Automate the operator's mid-run model-change ask by making the shed boundary an adjust-point: at each segment boundary — where R11 already sheds the resident worker and cache warmth is already surrendered — the run re-reads a small operator-writable tier-override and re-derives the tuple for the next segment before spawning its worker. No mid-segment interruption, no cache penalty beyond the shed that was already happening. The operator gets 'switch the next segment to opus/high' for free at the exact seam where a fresh worker is spawned anyway.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 6, lines 133-134: 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos)'. Crosses {#worker-cache-scheduling} (tuple derived saga-side); engages its revisit-when because the adjust-point rides the EXISTING R11 shed boundary (SKILL.md:311) rather than introducing a new mid-segment interruption or a formal wave queue — the tuple is still derived saga-side, only its input (the override file) becomes readable at the already-cache-cold seam, so cache economics are unchanged.
outcome_shape: PR adding a segment-boundary override read to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md Step B1 (+ saga /work execution-strategy.md), a documented override-file contract, CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that writes an override between segments and asserts the next segment's worker spec reflects the new tier while the current segment's is unchanged.

title: Plan-declared pause points replace the frantic async interrupt
idea: Because reliable async operator interruption of a background run is a harness-level problem (and AskUserQuestion reliability is out of scope), the reliable way to pause is one the run checks itself at a deterministic boundary. Invert reactive interruption into a pre-declared pause: /plan's unit table gains an optional pause_after marker, and team-execution/`/work` deterministically halts at that segment boundary for operator adjustment. The operator declares the intent to pause once, at plan time, instead of racing to catch a running agent. This removes the entire class of 'I tried to interrupt but it had already moved on' failures without touching the gate primitive.
basis: First-principles: an async interrupt of a background teammate is a race against the harness's message delivery, which grounding section 7 (patterns 2 and 9) shows is unreliable; the only pause the run can guarantee to honor is a flag it reads at a boundary it controls. Declaring that flag at plan time converts a race into a scheduled read, which is deterministic and testable — and it stays entirely clear of the struck AskUserQuestion primitive because the halt is a state check, not a question.
outcome_shape: PR adding pause_after to plugins/saga/skills/plan/references/plan-sections.md schema and a halt-check in team-execution SKILL.md Step B1, CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that a plan with pause_after=<segment> halts the run at exactly that boundary and resumes on a continue signal.

title: Coordinator liveness sweep with automatic single re-ping
idea: Subagents go idle without delivering and the operator is the one who notices — a pattern reproduced live in the very session that produced the grounding brief. Remove the human poll: the coordinator runs a deterministic liveness sweep where each resident teammate must emit a progress token by a per-segment deadline; on a miss the coordinator auto re-pings exactly once via SendMessage, and on a second miss it escalates (re-dispatch or surface as blocked) rather than waiting forever. 'Are you still working?' becomes machinery, not an operator chore. The single-re-ping-then-escalate ladder prevents both silent stalls and infinite polling.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 9, lines 139-140: 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications; coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session).' Crosses {#worker-cache-scheduling}; engages its revisit-when directly because that decision names 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue' as the revisit trigger, and this live-reproduced idle-without-delivery pattern is exactly that trigger firing — so a bounded idle-poll is now warranted rather than deferred.
outcome_shape: PR adding references/liveness-protocol.md and a Step B1 liveness-sweep loop to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md (progress-token deadline, single re-ping, escalation), CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test simulating a teammate that emits no progress token and asserting exactly one re-ping then escalation is recorded.

title: Positive delivery token: abolish the concept of 'idle'
idea: Idle-detection is inherently ambiguous — a quiet worker might be thinking or might be dead — and stale idle notifications are the noise that ambiguity generates. Remove idle as a concept entirely: a worker is not complete until it writes a delivery token to its manifest, and the coordinator recognizes only two states, delivered and not-delivered. This reuses team-execution's own missing-output rule, which already treats a required validator's absent evidence at exit as a completion block rather than a silent pass. Extending that same positive-evidence contract to worker delivery means 'stale idle notification' has no referent left to be stale about — there is only an unmet delivery token, which the liveness sweep or Step B8 teardown acts on deterministically.
basis: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md:418-421 — the existing rule that 'A required, non-skipped validator whose evidence record was never written is a missing-output omission, not a silent pass ... treat its absent evidence at process exit as a completion block' — is the in-file prior art to generalize from validator evidence to worker delivery.
outcome_shape: PR adding a delivery-token field to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/worker-manifest.md and delivered/not-delivered checks in Step B1 and Step B7, CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that a worker exiting without a delivery token blocks completion identically to a missing validator evidence record.

title: Derived-on-read 'fleet ps': reconstruct running/held/leaked from ground truth
idea: There is no single answer to 'what is running, held, or leaked right now' — the operator infers it from scattered signals and misses leaks (hence 15 orphaned worktrees). Invert trust-a-status-field into derive-on-read: a ps-style command reconstructs the live picture from ground truth — git worktree list, saga terminal states, the resident-teammate registry, and the background task list — and cross-joins them to flag held-but-abandoned and leaked resources. Nothing is a committed status field, so it cannot go stale. This is not the pulse live-telemetry widget (a streaming component); it is an on-demand reconciliation query whose whole purpose is leak detection at the join of those four sources.
basis: Grounding brief section 2, the /outcome campaign binding decision: 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields'. This idea engages that decision favorably — it is a pure read-side reconciliation that commits no status — and is grounded in the section 4 leak evidence (15 stale worktrees) that a derived ps would have surfaced immediately.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_ps.py + a saga command/skill entry and references/state-visibility.md, tests, CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that seeds a leaked worktree whose owning saga is terminal and asserts fleet_ps flags it as leaked while a live-held worktree is reported as running.

title: Reclamation-debt CI guard: the repo refuses to accumulate leaked state
idea: Teardown that depends on memory gets skipped — the 15 leaked worktrees are the proof. Remove the reliance on memory by making leaked runtime state a build-breaking condition: a CI guard scans the tree for committed .worktrees/ contents, orphaned saga state, and stranded resident-worker artifacts, and fails the check when it finds them. The best teardown is one CI will not let you merge past. This copies the org's already-proven pattern — context-library's validate.yml runs check_docs.py to schema-validate hygiene in CI — and points the same enforcement locus at runtime-state leakage instead of doc frontmatter. It is distinct from the QUEUED marketplace-ci-guard seed, which guards registry integrity, not leaked worktree/saga state.
basis: Prior art in infiquetra-context-library: grounding brief section 4, lines 77-80 — 'validate.yml CI runs check_docs.py (schema/frontmatter/link lint + promotion-ledger checks) + context_census.py --check' — the established schema-validate-in-CI enforcement pattern this idea redirects at runtime-state leak hygiene.
outcome_shape: PR adding a .github/workflows reclamation-debt guard job + plugins/saga/scripts/reclamation_debt_check.py and tests, CHANGELOG/marketplace bump; verified by a test that a tree containing a committed .worktrees/ payload or orphaned saga artifact fails the check and a clean tree passes.

title: Ephemeral resources are leases with a reaper, not run-owned cleanup steps
idea: The fleet treats cleanup as the run's last imperative action, so the one free-the-resource step is exactly the step that gets skipped whenever a run dies before its end. Reframe one level up: every ephemeral resource (git worktree, resident worker, run branch) is created as a LEASE — an owner id plus TTL written to a `.leases/` manifest at the creation site — and a standalone `lease_reaper.py` reclaims expired or owner-dead leases. Invoke the reaper at the top of every saga and team-execution entry (git-worktree-prune style), so reclamation is ambient and idempotent rather than a terminal courtesy. Ownership flips from the run to a lease registry, which is what the 15 orphaned worktrees actually are: leases with no living owner and nobody enumerating them.
basis: team-execution SKILL.md:403-421 (Step B7 is report-only, no reclamation) and grounding brief §4 '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+'. Crosses {#worker-cache-scheduling} which settles residency architecture but is silent on terminal reclamation; its revisit-when 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient' is satisfied — 15 leaked residents/worktrees are residency's cleanup proving insufficient, so a reaper complements (not contradicts) the scheduling model.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/lease_reaper.py + lease-manifest writes at worktree/resident-worker creation sites + a reaper call at saga/team-execution entry; verified by a pytest that seeds an expired lease and an orphan worktree, runs the reaper, and asserts both reclaimed and `git worktree list` shows zero orphans post-run.

title: Step B8 teardown barrier — completion means reclaimed, not merely reported
idea: team-execution defines completion as 'reported' (Step B7), never as 'reclaimed'. Attack that default directly: add Step B8 'Teardown & Reclamation' that asserts every resident worker named in the worker-manifest has been shed/stopped, every run-scoped worktree removed, and emits a reclamation record. A resident still alive at B8 becomes a leak-block exactly the way a never-written validator record is a missing-output completion block at B7 — same disease, same enforcement shape, applied to resources instead of evidence. This reuses the manifest machinery already present and closes the loop the Context-Shedding rule leaves open (R11 sheds at segment boundaries mid-run, but nothing confirms all residents are down at process exit).
basis: team-execution SKILL.md:311 (Context Shedding fires only at segment boundary), SKILL.md:308 (residents are run_in_background persistent teammates that outlive the run), SKILL.md:403-421 (B7 report-only; B8 absent). Intake brief states 'no Step B8 in team-execution'.
outcome_shape: PR editing plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md (add Step B8) + worker-manifest.md (add `reclaimed` disposition field) + plugin.json/CHANGELOG version bump; verified by a marketplace/drift-guard test asserting SKILL contains Step B8 and a dry-run that flags a leftover background task as a completion block.

title: Quiesce primitive — operator-raised pause via sentinel, not author-baked checkpoints
idea: The only places a run can pause today are where its author baked a prompt, so an operator with a new instruction must wait for the next scripted checkpoint or kill the run. Reframe the pause surface one level up: the operator raises a pause at any moment via a control-plane sentinel (a `.saga/pause` flag or saga-state field); the orchestrator polls it at each safe unit boundary and enters a QUIESCE state — stop dispatching new frontier work, let in-flight leaves drain, then surface a resume point. This is deliberately NOT AskUserQuestion (struck): it is a separate, file-based operator-interrupt channel with explicit drain semantics, so silence is never mistaken for consent and the pause is durable across a background dispatch that loses harness notifications.
basis: grounding brief §7 pattern 6 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos)' and pattern 9 (idle/notification fragility reproduced live). Aligns with {#outcome-campaign} HALT-not-degrade: quiesce is a clean HALT at a unit boundary, derived-on-read from the sentinel, never a committed status field — no revisit needed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a pause/resume sentinel protocol block to saga /work and /outcome SKILLs plus a saga_pause.py boundary-check helper; verified by a test that raises the sentinel mid-frontier and asserts no new leaf dispatches while one in-flight leaf drains, then a resume point is surfaced.

title: Late-bound tier — model/effort re-read per unit, defeating 'can't change model after spawn'
idea: 'You can't change a subagent's model after spawn' is true for one Agent call and false for an orchestrated run that spans many spawns. So the lifecycle mechanism, not the harness, is what makes mid-run model change impossible: the tier is authored once and never re-read. Reframe: resolve model/effort at each unit boundary from a mutable `.saga/run-tier.json`, so an operator editing that file during a quiesce sees the NEXT unit pick up the new tier with zero harness change. This is the lifecycle plumbing (re-resolve-at-boundary), leaving the tier-palette vocabulary itself to its own theme; here the win is that a frozen-at-dispatch property becomes a live, operator-adjustable one at unit granularity.
basis: grounding brief §1 'Every agent frontmatter hardcodes model:, zero effort fields, no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern'; plan/SKILL.md:296-352 tier table is authored-once. Crosses {#tier-vocab-ordering} (tiers are ordered escalation ladders): late-binding respects ordering by letting the operator step up or down the same ladder between units — revisit-when not tripped, the ladder semantics are preserved.
outcome_shape: PR adding a per-unit tier-resolve step reading `.saga/run-tier.json` into saga /work execution-strategy plus a `resolve_run_tier()` in execution_spec.py; verified by a test that seeds an override file, dispatches two units, and asserts unit 2 resolves the changed tier.

title: Typed liveness state machine + watchdog re-ping, replacing the ambiguous 'idle' signal
idea: A single 'idle' notification conflates four states — working-quietly, blocked-awaiting-input, delivered-awaiting-pickup, and dead — so the coordinator cannot act on it, and a silently-stuck worker looks identical to a finished one. Reframe: workers write a typed liveness state plus a heartbeat timestamp to the worker-manifest; the coordinator runs a watchdog that on stale heartbeat re-pings via SendMessage and after N missed pings escalates (declares dead, reclaims the slot). Under the standing concurrency cap of 3, a silently-idle worker holds a full third of fleet capacity, so cheap, crisp liveness detection has outsized value precisely because the cap makes a leaked slot expensive.
basis: grounding brief §7 pattern 9 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications; coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session)'; intake brief concurrency cap = 3. No binding decision opposed.
outcome_shape: PR adding a heartbeat + typed-liveness field to worker-manifest.md, a coordinator re-ping/escalation protocol block in team-execution SKILL Step B1, and a liveness.py staleness checker; verified by a test simulating a stale heartbeat and asserting a re-ping then an escalation-to-dead with slot reclamation.

title: Delivery = a named artifact pointer exists; 'idle-without-delivering' becomes computable
idea: Idle-without-delivering persists because 'delivered' is never given a crisp, machine-checkable definition — the coordinator hopefully awaits an unbounded completion with no done-signal it can test. Reframe delivery as producing a named artifact pointer: bind each worker/leaf's completion to a required deliverable pointer, so 'delivered' means 'the pointer exists' and 'idle-without-delivering' becomes the computable predicate 'past deadline AND no pointer'. team-execution already snapshots changed files as Layer-1 tree pointers via artifact_pointer.py at review epochs; extend that from a review-epoch artifact to a per-worker completion contract, turning a silent hang into an observable, actionable breach.
basis: First principles: an await with no testable completion predicate has exactly one failure mode — a human eventually notices — which is precisely the failure the session-mining pattern 9 records. Giving 'delivered' a truth-value that the coordinator can evaluate without the worker's cooperation (does the named pointer exist?) converts an unbounded, un-actionable wait into a bounded check with a defined breach action. The predicate is cheap, requires no new primitive (artifact_pointer.py exists), and is robust to a dead worker because it reads the filesystem, not the worker.
outcome_shape: PR adding a required per-worker `deliverable_pointer` to the worker-manifest contract + a coordinator breach predicate (deadline crossed and no pointer) with a re-ping/reassign ladder in team-execution SKILL; verified by a drift-guard test asserting the field is required and a dry-run where a missing pointer past deadline triggers the ladder.

title: Fleet doctor — one derived-on-read view of running / held / leaked
idea: Leaked resources are invisible because state is scattered across git worktrees, saga state files, and the harness task table with no unified read, so a leak only surfaces once it has inflated the repo 10x. Reframe: make leaks loud with a single `saga doctor` / `team doctor` command that reads all three sources and reports what is RUNNING (live background tasks), HELD (worktrees, leases, resident workers), and LEAKED (orphans with no living owner) — derived entirely on read, never a committed status field. Borrow the shape of `docker system df` and `git worktree list --porcelain`/`git fsck`: resource inventory becomes a first-class, always-available query instead of an archaeology dig after the fact.
basis: Prior art: `docker system df` and `docker system prune` (Docker CLI docs) expose dangling/leaked resources as a queryable inventory; `git worktree list --porcelain` and `git fsck` (Git docs) do the same for worktrees/objects. Aligns with {#outcome-campaign} derived-on-read (view is computed, never persisted). Motivating symptom: grounding brief §4's 15 orphaned worktrees that no command currently enumerates.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_doctor.py + a doctor command section in saga and team-execution SKILLs; verified by a test that stages a live task, a held worktree, and an orphan, then asserts the doctor classifies each into running/held/leaked correctly.

title: Shared reclamation-ledger primitive: register-on-spawn, idempotent reclaim_all
idea: Add a single session-scoped reclamation ledger (`plugins/saga/scripts/reclaim.py` + `references/reclamation.md`) that every durable-resource spawn writes to on creation: resident-worker id, background task handle, worktree path, and any `shared_install_ref`. Expose one idempotent `reclaim_all(session)` that shuts down residents, kills background tasks, and reaps worktrees, refactoring saga /outcome's existing `worktree_processor` reap path (outcome_worktrees.py) to route through it rather than owning bespoke logic. team-execution's new teardown (see T6-F4-2) and /work both call the same `reclaim_all`. The compounding return: any future spawn site gets teardown for free the moment it registers, instead of each surface re-deriving cleanup. Ledger is derive-on-read reconcilable against `git worktree list` so an out-of-band removal never strands the ledger.
basis: Grounding brief §1 confirms VERIFY_N_CAP=7 is the ONLY orchestration-level cap and that team-execution/`/outcome`/bridges have no shared teardown; saga CHANGELOG U7 already ships `worktree_processor` reap + 'git is the liveness oracle' detection (outcome_worktrees.py) as one-off /outcome machinery. Crosses `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` (residency teardown): engages its revisit-when only additively — this ledger adds reclamation over existing residency, it does NOT introduce a formal wave queue, so the settled derive-saga/reside-team boundary is untouched.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/reclaim.py`, `references/reclamation.md`, and a refactor of `outcome_worktrees.py` to call `reclaim_all`; verified by a new `tests/test_reclaim.py` asserting register→reclaim is idempotent and that a live worktree present in `git worktree list` is never double-reaped.

title: team-execution Step B8: Team Teardown wired to the shared reclaim primitive
idea: Add the missing terminal Step B8 ("Team Teardown & Reclamation") to team-execution's SKILL.md immediately after the last B-step, closing the gap where resident workers spawned with `run_in_background` (Step B1, R3) are never explicitly shut down and their worktrees never reaped. Rather than author standalone cleanup prose, B8 is a thin call into the shared `reclaim_all` primitive (T6-F4-1), so team-execution inherits saga's git-oracle reaping instead of reinventing it. B8 also asserts a post-condition check ('did every resident actually stop, is every worktree actually gone') to satisfy the repo's silent-no-op discipline. This is the surface the theme's teardown-gap evidence points directly at.
basis: team-execution SKILL.md Step B1 (lines ~303-312) spawns persistent `run_in_background` residents and sheds at segment boundary (R11) but the step sequence ends with no B8 teardown — the exact gap named in the theme axis ('no Step B8 in team-execution'). Grounding brief §6.1 requires bridge/delegation work carry a 'did it actually run/persist' post-condition, which B8's assertion satisfies.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `## Step B8: Team Teardown` to `plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md`, plus a version-bump surface update (plugin.json + CHANGELOG + marketplace.json per CLAUDE.md step 6); verified by a SKILL-lint/drift-guard test asserting B8 exists and references `reclaim_all`.

title: Extract outcome_liveness into a fleet-shared heartbeat/stalled engine
idea: Promote saga /outcome's `outcome_liveness.py` (harvest_liveness / record_heartbeat / `stalled` terminal, heartbeat_seconds+timeout_seconds budgets) from an /outcome-only unit into a shared liveness engine consumed by team-execution resident workers and /work background subagents. Each subagent emits a heartbeat; the coordinator's harvest pass reclaims any that breach budget as `stalled` and triggers a re-ping (see T6-F4-4). The compounding return: one liveness clock powers idle-detection everywhere, so the 'subagents idle without delivering' failure that currently reproduces live stops being re-solved per surface. Budgets stay `null`=untimed for attended leaves, preserving the existing /outcome semantics.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 9 ('subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications; coordinator must detect and re-ping', 2 repos + reproduced live this session); saga CHANGELOG U9 already ships `outcome_liveness.harvest_liveness`/`record_heartbeat`/`stalled` as /outcome-scoped. Crosses `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` whose revisit-when names 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue' — the live-reproduced idle-without-delivering IS that trigger firing; this engages it by shipping idle-poll reclamation WITHOUT a wave queue, the lighter branch the decision invites first.
outcome_shape: Merged PR relocating liveness into a shared module (e.g. `plugins/saga/scripts/liveness.py`) imported by both `outcome_dispatcher.py` and a new team-execution hook, with `tests/test_liveness_shared.py` asserting a breached-budget resident is harvested as stalled from a team-execution context; existing `test_outcome_liveness.py` stays green.

title: Delivery-gated re-ping protocol keyed on the typed artifact pointer
idea: Define a re-ping protocol for team-execution residents that treats liveness as 'delivered', not merely 'alive': a resident that signals done but produced no typed artifact pointer (the existing `artifact_pointer.py` contract) is classified idle-without-delivering and re-pinged via `SendMessage`, escalating to reclaim+respawn after N misses. This closes the specific failure mode where a stale idle notification masks a worker that never actually handed off. The compounding lever is reusing the artifact-pointer schema as the single 'did it deliver' oracle rather than trusting free-text 'done' claims, so every future worker type inherits a machine-checkable delivery gate.
basis: team-execution already ships `plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/artifact_pointer.py` (typed artifact-pointer passing, DECISIONS `{#artifact-pointer-ktds-291}`, PR #291/#324); grounding brief §7 pattern 9 names the re-ping need and §6.1 demands persistence verification over silent no-ops. One basis: the artifact-pointer contract exists and is the natural delivery oracle to gate liveness on.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `references/re-ping-protocol.md` + Step B1 amendment in team-execution SKILL.md, plus an `artifact_pointer.py` helper `has_delivered(worker_id)`; verified by a test asserting a done-signal-without-pointer worker is flagged idle and re-pinged before respawn.

title: Segment-boundary re-tier: mid-run model/effort adjust at the natural shed point
idea: Turn the segment boundary — where team-execution already sheds the resident worker (R11, cache-TTL horizon) — into a first-class operator adjust point: before the next segment's resident is spawned, the tier (model+effort) is re-derived saga-side, letting an operator's mid-run 'switch to opus/high' or 'drop to sonnet/medium' take effect on the very next spawn with zero warm-context loss. Because a shed already happens there, no in-flight work is disturbed. The compounding return: one adjust-point convention (re-derive at shed boundary) generalizes to context-budget and reviewer-set changes too, building beyond the static plan-dictated per-teammate-effort seed toward dynamic mid-run adjustment.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 6 ('operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses', 3 repos); team-execution SKILL.md R11 already sheds the resident at the segment boundary. Crosses `{#worker-cache-scheduling}` ('derive (segment+agent+tier) saga-side, reside team-side'): this adjust point re-derives tier saga-side at the shed boundary, which is exactly the decision's derive-side, so it extends rather than contradicts it. Builds beyond QUEUED `{#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}` (static, plan-time) by making the tier mutable mid-run.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a re-derive-tier hook at the Step B1 segment-shed boundary (SKILL.md + the saga-side tier derivation script) reading an operator-supplied override; verified by a test that a tier override set between segments changes only the next resident's spawn tier, not the current one.

title: Adjustment-envelope control file: one polled durable surface for all mid-run operator directives
idea: Ship a single durable, operator-editable control file (`.claude/team-execution/adjust.json`, git-ignored, derive-on-read) that a running team or /outcome polls at each pause boundary (segment shed, ready-frontier gap) for out-of-band directives: re-tier, drain-and-pause, cancel-a-segment, add-a-reviewer, or abort-with-clean-teardown. This is deliberately a file+poll surface, NOT a prompt primitive — sidestepping the struck-out AskUserQuestion reliability concern entirely while giving the operator a reliable mid-run steering wheel. The compounding meta-lever: every future mid-run adjustment lands in one schema-versioned envelope instead of ad-hoc bespoke prompts, and 'abort-with-clean-teardown' reuses the T6-F4-1 reclaim primitive.
basis: First-principles: a mid-run adjustment must persist across the pause and be read deterministically at a known boundary; the minimal durable surface with those properties is a polled, versioned control file, and it composes with the fleet's recurring derive-on-read-over-committed-state preference (grounding brief §6.5). A prompt primitive cannot satisfy this because it is synchronous and, per the Gate-B strike, unreliable — so a poll surface is the only path that respects the theme's out-of-scope constraint while still delivering pause-adjust. This is a written argument, not the AskUserQuestion primitive it explicitly avoids.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `references/adjustment-envelope.md` (schema + poll-boundary contract) and a parser in team-execution scripts, gitignore entry, and CHANGELOG/plugin.json bump; verified by a test that a directive written mid-run is honored at the next poll boundary and an unknown directive fails closed (no silent proceed).

title: Live run-inventory: the keystone manifest that teardown, liveness, and pause all read
idea: Generalize redis-channel's session presence pattern (registry HSET + heartbeat) from cross-session presence to an intra-run resource inventory: one session-scoped, derive-on-read manifest of everything currently held — resident workers, background tasks, worktrees, `shared_install_ref` installs, held leases — answerable via `saga status --live` / `team-execute --inventory`. This is the keystone primitive of the whole theme: the same manifest that answers 'what is running/held/leaked' is what T6-F4-1's reclaim iterates, what T6-F4-3's harvest scans, and what T6-F4-6's adjust boundary reconciles against. Build it once and the other three axes get their substrate for free.
basis: Prior art lives in-repo: `plugins/redis-channel/server/presence.py` (registry HSET + 10s heartbeat + lazy stale-entry GC) and ARCHITECTURE.md already implement exactly the register/heartbeat/GC pattern for sessions; this idea ports that proven shape to intra-run durable resources. Respects the `/outcome` campaign's derived-on-read / never-committed-status rule by deriving the manifest against `git worktree list` and live task handles rather than persisting a status field.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a run-inventory module + a `--live`/`--inventory` read command across saga and team-execution; verified by a test asserting the inventory correctly lists a spawned resident+worktree and drops it after reclaim, reconciled against `git worktree list`.

title: Leak-doctor: cross-fleet audit of held vs leaked resources with reclaim suggestions
idea: Ship a `--doctor` audit that reads the run-inventory (T6-F4-7) plus the git oracle and reports leaked resources across the fleet: stale worktrees (git worktree list minus live owners — the 15-stale-worktree disease), orphaned background tasks, resident workers past cache-TTL, and held leases whose owner session is dead. Each finding carries a one-line reclaim suggestion routed through `reclaim_all`. The compounding return: this is the standing verification the repo's silent-no-op theme demands — it makes 'did teardown actually happen' a runnable check instead of an assumption, and it doubles as the drift guard that would have caught the context-library worktree inflation before it hit 10x.
basis: Grounding brief §4 'Hygiene find: 15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in `.worktrees/` inflating the repo 10x+ — direct evidence for theme 6', plus §6.1 silent-no-op delegation theme requiring a runnable 'did it actually run/persist' check. One basis: the 15-worktree leak is the concrete failure a doctor audit surfaces and prevents.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `doctor` subcommand (saga scripts) that lists leaked worktrees/tasks/leases with reclaim suggestions; verified by a test seeding a stale worktree + dead-owner lease and asserting the doctor flags both and proposes reclaim without auto-mutating.

title: TTL-after-finished worktree reaper (Kubernetes / Janitor Monkey)
idea: Borrow Kubernetes' TTLAfterFinished Job controller and Netflix's Janitor Monkey: a garbage collector that reaps a resource once its owning work is terminal, after a grace TTL. Ship a `saga worktree-reap` script that scans `.worktrees/`, derives each worktree's liveness from saga/git state (branch merged? saga terminal? last-touched older than TTL?), and reclaims the orphans — dry-run by default, `--apply` to remove, never touching a worktree whose saga is still active. The reaper writes a reclamation-evidence record so the deletion has chain-of-custody. This is the standing janitor the fleet lacks: today nothing owns the lifespan of a worktree after its saga ends.
basis: Source domain: cluster orchestration. Kubernetes `TTLAfterFinished` controller (kubernetes/pkg/controller/ttlafterfinished) auto-deletes Jobs a set time after completion; Netflix Janitor Monkey (Netflix/SimianArmy) reaps unreferenced cloud resources on a schedule. Maps directly onto the grounded 15 stale abandoned saga worktrees inflating infiquetra-context-library 10x (grounding brief section 4) — same disease, and no controller owns worktree end-of-life.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `plugins/saga/skills/*/scripts/worktree_reap.py` (or a shared saga tool) + `tests/test_worktree_reap.py`; verified by a fixture repo seeded with terminal-saga and active-saga worktrees where `--apply` removes exactly the terminal orphans and leaves actives, plus a manual run against context-library reducing 15 stale worktrees to 0.

title: Apoptosis Step B8 — programmed self-teardown at run exit
idea: Biology solves 'work is done, now cleanly disappear' with apoptosis (programmed cell death) and Unix solves 'a finished child must not linger' with init reaping zombies. team-execution has neither at run exit: Step B7 only reports. Add Step B8 'Teardown & Reclamation' — at run completion the coordinator SendMessage-shuts-down every resident worker it spawned, confirms exit, removes any worktrees it created, and emits a reclamation manifest listing each spawned identity and its settled/leaked disposition. Completion is blocked (like a hard-failing validator) if any spawned resident has no exit confirmation, so a leaked background worker cannot pass silently.
basis: Source domain: biology (apoptosis) / Unix zombie reaping. Direct gap: team-execution Step B7 'Completion' is report-only (SKILL.md:403-416); resident workers are spawned with `run_in_background` (SKILL.md:308) and are shed only at segment boundaries by R11 (SKILL.md:311) — there is no exit-time reap, so a run that ends off a segment boundary leaks its residents with no completion check.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding 'Step B8: Teardown & Reclamation' to team-execution/SKILL.md + a `reclamation-manifest` evidence lane in references/validator-evidence-state.md + a drift-guard test asserting Step B8 exists and that an un-reaped resident blocks completion; verified by the existing evidence-absence test pattern.

title: Phi-accrual failure detector for subagent liveness
idea: Distributed systems moved past binary alive/dead: the phi-accrual failure detector outputs a continuous suspicion level from the history of inter-heartbeat intervals, so a slow-but-alive node is not falsely killed and a truly-dead one is caught fast. Apply it to resident workers and subagents: the coordinator records each worker check-in timestamp, computes phi from the interval distribution, and at a threshold escalates re-ping → re-dispatch, instead of the current all-or-nothing 'idle' guess.
