Ship `liveness.py` computing phi from a timestamp series plus `references/liveness-detection.md` wiring it into Step B1, so 'is this worker stuck or just slow' becomes a tuned signal rather than a vibe.
basis: Source domain: distributed systems. The phi-accrual failure detector (Hayashi, Defago et al., 2004) ships in Akka Remoting (`akka.remote.PhiAccrualFailureDetector`) and Cassandra's gossip FailureDetector. Maps onto grounded pattern 9 'subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications; coordinator must detect and re-ping' (grounding brief section 7), which today has no quantitative liveness signal.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/liveness.py` + `references/liveness-detection.md` + `tests/test_liveness.py`; verified by feeding interval series (steady vs stalled) and asserting phi crosses the re-ping threshold only for the stalled series.

title: Dead-letter queue + at-least-once re-dispatch for undelivered work
idea: Message brokers guarantee delivery, not just liveness: an unacked message after N redeliveries lands in a dead-letter queue for visibility instead of vanishing. A subagent that goes idle without emitting its expected artifact-pointer is exactly an unacked message. Treat the artifact-pointer as the delivery ACK: if a worker's unit produces no pointer within a window, the coordinator re-dispatches once with backoff, and after a bounded retry count moves the unit to an 'undelivered-work' dead-letter evidence lane that surfaces to the operator rather than the run quietly completing short. This closes the gap where liveness detection re-pings but delivery is never actually confirmed.
basis: Source domain: message-queue systems. Amazon SQS redrive-to-DLQ (maxReceiveCount) and RabbitMQ dead-letter exchanges implement at-least-once delivery with ack + bounded retry + dead-letter capture. Maps onto grounded pattern 9 (idle-without-delivering) and the existing artifact-pointer ACK primitive (team-execution artifact_pointer.py / references/artifact-pointers.md), which currently tracks pointers but has no undelivered-work fallback lane.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an 'undelivered-work' evidence lane to references/validator-evidence-state.md + a Step B1 re-dispatch/backoff rule in team-execution/SKILL.md + a drift/scenario test; verified by simulating a worker that emits no artifact-pointer within the window and asserting the unit lands in the DLQ evidence record after bounded retries.

title: Flight-progress-strip fleet board (air-traffic control)
idea: Air-traffic control never guesses what is aloft: every aircraft gets one flight progress strip on the board, and a controller owns a console showing exactly the live picture. The fleet has no equivalent — nobody can answer 'what agents are running, held, or leaked right now' in one glance. Ship a `saga fleet-status` (or team-execution status) CLI that renders one strip per live agent — id, tier, segment/unit, last check-in, worktree path, delivery state — derived fresh on each read from saga/team state, never from a committed status field. A leaked resident (spawned, no exit record) renders red; a healthy warm worker renders green.
basis: Source domain: air-traffic control. FAA flight progress strips (FAA Order JO 7110.65, Chapter 2 Section 3) give one physical token per flight and a per-controller live picture. Constraint engaged: the /outcome campaign binding mandates derived-on-read status, never committed status fields (grounding brief section 2; outcome SKILL.md:31 'level-triggered, every tick reconstructs from state') — this board is strictly a read-time projection, satisfying that decision rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `fleet-status` command + renderer script under plugins/saga (or team-execution) + a test; verified with a fixture state containing a warm resident, a held worker, and a leaked resident (spawned, no exit record), asserting the leaked one is flagged.

title: Spawn-settle reconciliation ledger (double-entry / trade settlement)
idea: Finance catches leaks with an invariant, not a dashboard: every trade must settle, and the open-position book is the diff between executed and settled — a nonzero open position is money unaccounted for. Apply double-entry to agent lifecycle: every spawn is a debit that must be matched by a reap/exit credit. A `reconcile --leaks` pass reads the append-only spawn journal against the reap/exit records and reports open positions — resident workers and worktrees created but never settled. This is the detection substrate the reaper (idea 1) and the board (idea 5) consume: it turns 'we think something leaked' into a provable ledger imbalance.
basis: Source domain: finance. Double-entry bookkeeping and back-office trade reconciliation (executed-vs-settled open-position book, T+2 settlement) enforce a matched-pair invariant. Constraint engaged: /outcome derived-on-read binding — the ledger is an append-only fact log reconciled on read (a leaf-produced fact, mirroring the cost-ledger pattern in grounding brief section 2), not a committed mutable status field.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a spawn/reap journal writer + `reconcile --leaks` reader script + test under plugins/saga or team-execution; verified by a fixture with 3 spawns and 2 reaps asserting exactly 1 open position, and a manual run flagging context-library's stale worktrees as unsettled debits.

title: Segment-boundary savepoint — mid-run tier/context re-titration
idea: Anesthesiologists titrate: they continuously re-dose against observed patient depth mid-procedure instead of committing one dose at induction, and SQL SAVEPOINTs let a transaction adjust course without a full rollback. The fleet only lets the operator pick tier at plan time, then flies blind to run end — the 'why can't I change model mid-run' ask. Make the existing segment boundary (already the cache-shed seam) a declared adjust point: at each boundary, optionally surface the current tier/context and accept an operator override applied to the next segment's resident spawn, persisted to the worker-manifest. Adjusting at the boundary is free because the warm cache is already being shed there; mid-segment adjust would waste it, so the boundary is the principled savepoint.
basis: Source domain: anesthesia titration / SQL SAVEPOINT. First-principles: team-execution already sheds the resident at its segment boundary at the ~5-minute cache-TTL horizon (SKILL.md:311), so the boundary is the one point where re-titrating tier/context costs no warm cache — any other pause point forfeits cache. Engages the worker-cache-scheduling binding (segment boundary = the seam, grounding brief section 2): this adds an operator adjust hook AT that seam without introducing a wave queue, staying inside the decision's shape.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a Step B1 segment-boundary adjust hook to team-execution/SKILL.md + an `adjust`/override field in references/worker-manifest.md + a test; verified by asserting an override supplied at a boundary changes the next segment's resident spawn tier while leaving the completed segment untouched.

title: Andon-cord halt — any worker/reviewer can stop the line for adjust
idea: Toyota's andon cord lets any line worker halt production the instant they see a defect, and aviation's go-around lets a pilot abort a committed approach at the decision point — both privilege 'stop and reassess' over 'press on and hope'. In a run, a worker or reviewer that detects a plan-invalidating condition (scope drift, or a tier plainly wrong for the observed difficulty) has no sanctioned way to pause; it either silently presses on or overruns. Add an andon signal lane: pulling it sets a HALT that stops the next wave dispatch and surfaces the condition to the operator for a model/context/plan adjust, rather than degrading. This extends /outcome's HALT-not-degrade posture down into the team-execution wave loop.
basis: Source domain: Toyota Production System (jidoka / andon cord, Taiichi Ohno) and aviation go-around decision points. Engages the /outcome campaign binding 'HALT-not-degrade' (grounding brief section 2): this idea propagates that same stop-don't-degrade rule from the outcome coordinator into team-execution's wave dispatch, where it is currently absent — a consistent extension, not a contradiction.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an 'andon/HALT' worker-signal lane to team-execution references + a Step B1 rule that a raised andon blocks the next wave and writes an operator-surface record; verified by a scenario test where a worker raises andon and the next wave is not dispatched while the HALT record is written.

title: Every worktree self-destructs: fleet-wide reap + team-execution Step B8
idea: Flip the constraint to 'zero operators, every worktree self-destructs unless renewed.' The proven /outcome reaper (outcome_worktrees.py reap_worktree/live_worktrees, with git existence as source of truth over the registry) is invisible to every other run type, and team-execution's step ladder ends at B7 Completion with no teardown at all. Factor the reap+registry-reconcile core into a standalone plugins/saga/scripts/worktree_gc.py callable by any run, then add a mandatory Step B8: Teardown to team-execution SKILL.md that reaps its own worktrees and drains its resident workers before reporting done. The practical kernel of the extreme flip: a completion event is not 'complete' until a matching reap record exists, so teardown becomes a settled terminal rather than an optional courtesy.
basis: Grounding brief §4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ → direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8.' Verified: team-execution/SKILL.md's last step is 'Step B7: Completion' (line 403) with no B8; outcome_worktrees.py:254 reap_worktree + :162 live_worktrees already implement the reclamation core that no other run type can reach.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds plugins/saga/scripts/worktree_gc.py (extracted from outcome_worktrees.py), a new 'Step B8: Teardown' section in plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md + a references/teardown.md, and bumps team-execution plugin.json/marketplace.json/CHANGELOG.md. Verified by a new tests/test_worktree_gc.py that plants N synthetic orphan worktrees in a fixture repo, runs the reaper, and asserts registry/git converge to zero live plus one reap record per removal.

title: Immortal workers, inverted: an idle-TTL eviction protocol for resident teammates
idea: Flip residency to its extreme: workers are immortal, never shut down, resident forever. The kernel that falls out is that unbounded residency is exactly the leak, so residency needs a symmetric eviction rule. Define a resident-worker shutdown protocol in team-execution: each resident teammate carries an idle-TTL and a drain-on-completion hook, and the coordinator evicts a worker whose last-activity gap exceeds its TTL, recording the eviction as a durable teardown event. This deliberately engages the {#worker-cache-scheduling} decision, whose stated revisit-when is 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient, or idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue' — an idle-poll eviction sweep is precisely that idle-poll, so this idea is the settled trigger for revisiting residency, not a contradiction of it.
basis: Grounding brief §2 binding-decision register, {#worker-cache-scheduling} (2026-06-27): 'derive (segment+agent+tier) saga-side, reside team-side ... Revisit-when: named-teammate residency proves insufficient, or idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue.' The decision defines residency but no eviction/shutdown; this idea supplies the idle-poll the revisit-when names.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds a resident-worker eviction section to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/worker-manifest.md, wires the idle-TTL check into Step B8, and appends a DECISIONS.md revisit-engagement entry citing {#worker-cache-scheduling}. Verified by a unit test injecting a synthetic now-clock that asserts a worker past idle-TTL is evicted with a teardown record and one under TTL is retained.

title: Fully autonomous can't pause — so make the pause a durable checkpoint, not a prompt
idea: Flip to 'fully autonomous, zero pause points.' The kernel: even a run that never prompts still needs safe boundaries where a mid-run tier/model change can land without corrupting state — the operator's recurring 'pause and switch model' ask. Since AskUserQuestion reliability is out of scope, define pause-adjust points as declared safe-interrupt boundaries between named steps where a run checkpoints its durable state (saga ledger + worktree registry snapshot) and can resume under a changed execution-spec tier. This gives mid-run model change a durable seam that is independent of any interactive prompt primitive, so the pause is a state transition, not a question.
basis: Grounding brief §7 recurring pattern 6: 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time ... operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos).' The ask is documented across 3 repos; no pause/resume checkpoint boundary exists in saga /work or team-execution today.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds a 'Pause-adjust boundaries' subsection to plugins/saga/skills/work/SKILL.md and plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/SKILL.md declaring the between-step safe seams, plus a checkpoint-schema note in outcome_store or the saga manifest doc. Verified by a test that checkpoints at a declared boundary, mutates the execution-spec tier, resumes, and asserts the resumed run reads the new tier while the ledger lineage stays intact.

title: Steer an unattended run without stopping it: an out-of-band control-plane signal file
idea: Flip to zero-operators/fully-autonomous, then ask how an operator still steers such a run without a synchronous prompt. Borrow nginx's SIGHUP graceful-reload pattern: a running unattended run polls a durable control file (e.g. control.json in the saga store) at each declared pause-adjust boundary and applies a new tier or scope on the next step, never mid-step. This dodges the out-of-scope AskUserQuestion primitive entirely — steering becomes cooperative desired-state reconciliation the run reads on its own schedule, not an interrupt the harness must deliver. The operator drops the file whenever; the run absorbs it at the next safe seam and records that it did.
basis: Prior art: nginx graceful config reload on SIGHUP (workers finish in-flight requests, then reload config without a restart) and .NET CooperativeCancellation tokens — both are 'change a running process's intent at a safe point via an out-of-band signal.' Lives in nginx source (ngx_signal_handler) and the .NET CancellationToken API; the pattern maps directly onto a polled control file at pause-adjust boundaries.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds a control-file schema + poll-at-boundary contract to plugins/saga/skills/work/SKILL.md and a saga script hook that reads it, plus CHANGELOG/plugin.json bumps. Verified by a test that writes control.json mid-run, advances past a boundary, and asserts the new tier is adopted only after the boundary (never mid-step) and an 'applied control' record is written.

title: 100 idle agents, one blind coordinator: port the /outcome heartbeat/re-ping to team-execution fan-out
idea: Flip to 100 dispatched subagents the coordinator cannot babysit. saga /outcome already solves this for its leaves (outcome_liveness.py: heartbeat_seconds/timeout_seconds breach → stalled terminal, idempotent single page, downstream cascade), but team-execution's reviewer and worker fan-out has no heartbeat, no stalled terminal, and no re-ping — exactly the 'subagents idle without delivering' failure. Port the derived-on-read liveness contract into team-execution: each dispatched reviewer/worker carries a heartbeat budget, and the coordinator's advance pass reclaims a breached member as stalled and re-pings once before cascading. The kernel of the 100-agent extreme is that liveness must be derived from a durable ledger, never from the coordinator holding a live handle to each agent.
basis: Grounding brief §7 recurring pattern 9: 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications — coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session).' The proven machinery to port already exists at outcome_liveness.py:112 harvest_liveness but is /outcome-internal.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds a heartbeat/stalled/re-ping section to plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/references/consensus-protocol.md (or a new liveness.md) mirroring outcome_liveness semantics, wired into the Step B advance loop, with plugin release-surface bumps. Verified by a test asserting a member past its heartbeat budget reaches a stalled record, is re-pinged exactly once, and its dependents cascade.

title: Every idle notification is a lie until acknowledged: a delivery-receipt handshake
idea: Flip to 'no notification is trustworthy' — assume every idle/done signal is stale until proven delivered. The kernel is a delivery-receipt handshake: a subagent's completion or idle signal is not accepted until a matching receipt record is written by the coordinator, letting it distinguish 'idle and delivered' from 'idle and the notification was dropped' from 'died mid-flight.' This directly targets the documented Claude Code runtime quirk that background dispatch silently loses channel notifications, which is the mechanism behind stale idle notifications. A signal with no receipt is treated as undelivered and re-solicited, closing the silent-drop gap without depending on the harness's delivery guarantees.
basis: Grounding brief §3 finding 4: 'Claude Code runtime quirks recorded as durable build constraints (bg-dispatch loses channel notifications ...).' A dropped background notification is exactly a signal that never earns a receipt — the handshake makes that observable instead of silent.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds a delivery-receipt record type + accept-only-on-receipt rule to the team-execution liveness/consensus reference and the /outcome dispatcher notes, plus a tests/ case asserting an un-receipted completion signal is re-solicited and a receipted one is accepted exactly once (idempotent).

title: One derived-on-read answer to 'what is running, held, and leaked' across the fleet
idea: Flip to 100 concurrent runs across saga /work, /outcome DAGs, and team-execution teams — the operator is blind because each run type tracks its own state in isolation. The kernel is a single derived-on-read reader that reconciles four durable sources (the /outcome worktree registry, saga worktrees actually on disk, held coordinator leases, and team-execution run manifests) into one point-in-time report: RUNNING (live leases/dispatches), HELD (leases with a live holder), LEAKED (worktrees/records with no live owner). This is distinct from the queued Pulse live-telemetry component: Pulse streams telemetry, this is a stateless reconciliation snapshot whose only job is exposing leaked/orphaned teardown state. It aligns with the /outcome campaign's derived-on-read-never-committed-status rule and extends it fleet-wide.
basis: Grounding brief §4: the 15 stale worktrees were 'inflating the repo 10x+' yet invisible until an ad hoc scan — direct evidence that leaked state has no standing visibility surface. Aligns with §2 /outcome campaign rule 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields.'
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_status.py (reconciles outcome_worktrees registry + on-disk worktrees + leases + team-execution manifests) and a saga doctor/status subcommand, emitting RUNNING/HELD/LEAKED buckets. Verified by a test that plants a leaked worktree, a held lease, and a live dispatch in a fixture and asserts each lands in the correct bucket.

title: Make teardown non-optional: an executable leak invariant that fails CI
idea: Flip to 'every issue/run is self-executing and self-cleaning' and ask what would have to be true. The kernel is an executable invariant asserted in CI and a doctor command: every settled completion event must have a matching reap/teardown record, and every held lease must have a live holder — any violation fails the check with the specific orphaned id. This turns the missing-Step-B8 disease from an after-the-fact 10x-inflation surprise into a red build, and it directly answers the repo's silent-no-op learning that any teardown must be verified to have actually run and persisted, not assumed. The invariant is the enforcement teeth behind ideas T6-F6-1 and T6-F6-7.
basis: Grounding brief §6 recurring pain 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring ... any bridge/delegation idea needs "did it actually run/persist" verification.' A teardown that never fires is precisely a silent no-op; an executable invariant is the persistence check that pattern demands.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adds tests/test_teardown_invariants.py (asserts completion↔reap parity and lease↔holder parity over a fixture store) plus a saga doctor --check-teardown subcommand, wired into the repo's existing pytest/CI scope. Verified by the test itself: a planted orphan completion-without-reap makes the invariant fail with the orphan's id; adding the reap makes it pass.

title: One guarded /ship verb: commit→PR→merge→sync→cleanup as an intent-configured ceremony
idea: Add a saga /ship skill that collapses the mined 8-repo manual ritual (git commit, gh pr create, gh pr merge, git checkout main, git pull, worktree/branch cleanup) into a single guarded verb. It does NOT hard-code gate posture: it reads the outcome's intent-captured config (PR-reviews-required? gate-or-auto at merge?) and either halts for the operator or proceeds autonomously per that envelope. Each remote-touching step is preceded by a preflight assertion (clean tree, CI green if triggered, reviews satisfied) and the whole run emits a step-by-step transcript so the operator can audit what fired. Reversible steps proceed silently; the merge step honors the captured gate.
basis: Grounding brief lines 119-121: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)'. Intake tension 3 fixes gate posture at intent capture, not hard-coded, which this verb consumes rather than re-litigates.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/ship/SKILL.md + references/ship-ceremony-steps.md, a plugin.json/marketplace.json/CHANGELOG version bump, and a drift-guard test asserting the step list matches the reference; verified by a dry-run transcript showing each step gated by the intent config on a scratch branch.

title: Ship-ceremony rollback manifest: /ship --undo for partial-failure recovery
idea: The ship ceremony is a multi-step non-atomic sequence; a failure between merge and cleanup (or between PR-open and merge) currently leaves an inconsistent local+remote state the operator must hand-untangle. Before each mutating step, /ship records the exact inverse (pre-merge main SHA, opened PR number, created branch name, worktree path) into a durable per-run rollback manifest under the saga state dir. On mid-ceremony failure, or on an explicit /ship --undo, the verb replays the recorded inverses newest-first to restore the last consistent state, refusing to undo anything already consumed downstream (e.g. a merge another PR now depends on).
basis: First-principles: the ceremony is a sequence of independently-failing remote and local mutations with no transaction boundary, so any step N failure strands steps 1..N-1 with no recorded inverse. Idempotent recovery requires capturing the undo command at the moment forward state is known, not reconstructing it after the fact when the pre-state is already lost. This is the standard saga-pattern compensating-action design applied to the ship verb itself.
outcome_shape: PR adding a rollback-manifest schema (JSON) written to the saga run dir plus the --undo branch in plugins/saga/skills/ship/SKILL.md; verified by a test that kills the ceremony after PR-open and asserts --undo closes the PR and deletes the branch, leaving a clean tree.

title: Widen the /outcome autonomous status allowlist with a derive-on-read reversibility classifier
idea: Today /outcome only auto-progresses a narrow set of board statuses and prompts on the rest. Add a declarative allowlist keyed by transition reversibility: any status move that is reversible (Shaping→Active, Active→In Review, In Review→In Progress) auto-progresses; only genuinely irreversible or spend-increasing transitions stay gated. Crucially the widened set stays derive-on-read — status is computed from saga+board evidence at read time, never written as a committed status field — so widening the allowlist widens what the coordinator will DERIVE-and-reflect, not what it persists. The allowlist itself is a config table so operators tune it per outcome envelope.
basis: Binding decision '/outcome campaign (U1-U11): Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields; HALT-not-degrade' (grounding brief section 2). This idea engages that revisit boundary explicitly: it widens the reflected-transition set WITHOUT introducing a committed status field, and preserves HALT for irreversible moves — staying inside the decision rather than crossing it. Recent commit 71faf92 already schema-resolves outcome board status instead of hardcoding 'In Progress', proving the derive seam is live.
outcome_shape: PR adding a reversibility-classified status allowlist config (consumed by outcome_decompose/schema-resolve path) + SKILL doc in plugins/saga/skills/outcome/, verified by a test asserting reversible transitions reflect autonomously and irreversible ones still HALT, with zero committed status fields in the diff.

title: Propagate board↔saga reconciliation from /outcome down into /work and /loop
idea: The board↔saga reconciliation logic that /outcome gained (deriving true status by reconciling saga state against the board on resume) is currently outcome-only; /work and /loop still leave board status to drift or nudge it manually. Extract the reconciliation as a shared derive-on-read helper and call it at /work round boundaries and each /loop tick, so a PR opened or merged mid-work is reflected on the board without a committed status write or an operator nudge. This closes the gap where a saga advances but its card silently lags, the mined board-drift complaint's lifecycle cousin.
basis: Commit 6b33eba 'feat(saga): board↔saga reconciliation on resume (#295)' establishes the reconciliation primitive exists but scoped to resume/outcome. Grounding brief pattern 3 (line 126-128) documents 'mission-control board/field drift' across 4 repos as live pain. Extending the existing derive-on-read reconciler is a seam extension, not a new committed-status mechanism, so it respects the derived-on-read binding.
outcome_shape: PR extracting the reconciler into a shared saga helper and wiring calls in plugins/saga/skills/work/SKILL.md and loop/SKILL.md; verified by a test that opens a PR mid-/work and asserts the derived board status reflects In-Review on next round without a persisted status field.

title: Append-only chain-of-custody evidence ledger (beyond artifact immutability)
idea: The direct-to-candidate pool already covers making a single evidence artifact immutable; this goes further to an append-only ceremony ledger. Every verify/CI/QA result during the ship path is appended as a signed, ordered entry (check-name, verdict, run-id, git SHA, timestamp) — a later PASS never overwrites an earlier FAIL, it appends a superseding entry that still references the FAIL it supersedes. Closure verdicts are then DERIVED by reading the ledger's latest entry per check, so the audit chain shows the full FAIL→PASS history and the exact SHA each verdict was measured against. This turns the mined chain-of-custody incident from a data-loss bug into a first-class provenance record.
basis: Grounding brief lines 150-151: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'. The direct-to-candidate pool (line 186) claims flat 'evidence-artifact immutability'; this idea deliberately builds beyond by making the ledger append-only-with-supersession and deriving verdicts on read, not merely locking one file.
outcome_shape: PR adding an append-only evidence-ledger schema + writer used by the ship/verify path in plugins/saga (references/evidence-ledger.md + writer), verified by a test appending FAIL then PASS and asserting both entries persist, the derived verdict is PASS, and the FAIL remains readable with its SHA.

title: Evidence-gated leaf closure: /outcome refuses to close on missing or stale-SHA evidence
idea: A leaf saga can currently reach a closed/done derived status even when its required-check evidence is absent, FAILing, or was measured against a stale SHA that predates the final commit. Add a closure gate to the /outcome coordinator that, at derive time, cross-checks each leaf's required checks against the evidence ledger: closure is only DERIVED when every required check has a PASS entry whose recorded SHA matches the merged head. Missing evidence, a FAIL, or a stale SHA yields HALT-not-degrade with a named reason, never a silent close. Required-check sets come from the intent envelope (reviews-required, tests-required) captured at start.
basis: First-principles: if closure status is derived on read but the derivation ignores whether evidence exists and matches the shipped SHA, then 'closed' asserts a verified state it never checked — exactly the validation-discipline failure of treating HTTP-200/green as correct. Binding decision requires HALT-not-degrade and derived-on-read; a closure gate that reads the ledger and halts on gaps is the faithful implementation of both, engaging rather than crossing the constraint.
outcome_shape: PR adding a closure-gate check in the outcome derive path (plugins/saga/skills/outcome) that consults the evidence ledger + intent required-check set; verified by a test where a leaf with a FAIL/stale-SHA check derives HALT with a named reason and a matching-SHA PASS derives closed.

title: Ceremony hazard preflight: classify gh auto-merge / delete-branch / stacked-PR hazards before shipping
idea: Beyond merely supporting stacked-PR CI triggers, add a hazard classifier the ship verb runs before any remote mutation. It detects the mined surprise shapes: gh pr merge --auto racing an incomplete CI run, --delete-branch about to clobber a branch that stacked child PRs still target, an unmerged base PR in a stack, and a CI config whose branch triggers won't fire for the PR's ref. Each detected hazard HALTs the ceremony with a named hazard code and a suggested safe action, rather than proceeding into the surprise. The classifier is a pure read-only inspection of gh/PR state, so it adds no spend and can gate every /ship run.
basis: Grounding brief lines 147-148: 'gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises; stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap'. The direct-to-candidate pool covers narrow 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support'; this builds beyond into a broader hazard classifier spanning auto-merge racing and delete-branch clobber, halting at ship time rather than adding one CI trigger.
outcome_shape: PR adding a hazard-classifier reference + preflight step in plugins/saga/skills/ship/SKILL.md enumerating hazard codes; verified by a test that constructs a stacked-PR state and asserts /ship HALTs with the delete-branch-clobber code instead of deleting the base branch.

title: Ship-ceremony ownership contract: a documented handoff protocol across saga / mission-control / deploy
idea: The ceremony spans three plugins with no written boundary: saga owns commit→PR→merge and worktree cleanup, mission-control owns board status and issue closure, deploy owns tag-promotion to nonprod. Today each session re-improvises who does what, producing the mined drift and double-work. Write an ownership contract that assigns each ceremony step to exactly one owning plugin, defines the typed handoff artifact passed at each boundary (e.g. saga hands mission-control the merged PR number + derived status; hands deploy the merged SHA + tag intent), and adds a guard test asserting no plugin performs a step the contract assigns to another. This makes the ship path a composition of clearly-owned segments rather than an overlapping scramble.
basis: Binding decision {#operator-choice-framework} and the /outcome campaign both live in saga while deploy owns tag-promotion (deploy 0.1.2) and mission-control owns SDLC board/issue writes (grounding brief section 1) — three separate owners with no boundary doc. Grounding brief pattern 3 (board/field drift, 4 repos) and pattern 1 (ceremony done by raw git/gh even where the owning plugins are installed) are the direct symptoms of the missing contract.
outcome_shape: PR adding docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md entry + a ship-ceremony-ownership.md contract naming per-step owners and typed handoff artifacts, plus a guard test asserting each plugin's ship-related skills only invoke steps the contract assigns them; verified by the test and a marketplace/CHANGELOG surface update.

title: The `saga ship` verb — one guarded command replaces the 8-repo ritual
idea: Collapse the entire mined ceremony (commit → PR-open → review-request → merge → checkout main → pull → delete-branch → worktree-prune) into a single `saga.py ship` subcommand that runs as one reversibility-gated pipeline. Its autonomy is fixed once at intent capture via the two envelope questions (PR-reviews-required? gate-or-auto merge?), then every downstream stage runs unattended within the enumerated envelope, pausing only where the operator chose 'gate'. Today `/work` explicitly stops at merge and never performs post-merge sync or teardown (work/SKILL.md:459-465), so the tail is done by raw git/gh session after session. The inversion: the best version of a six-keystroke ritual is no keystrokes — the operator declares intent once and the verb executes the rest.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)'. work/SKILL.md:459-465: '/work builds, tests, gates, records, and coordinates the PR loop... then stop' — it owns merge under confirmation but never the sync/cleanup tail. Intake §2 lines 53-57 supply the once-at-capture autonomy envelope this verb consumes.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `ship` subcommand to plugins/saga/scripts/saga.py + plugins/saga/skills/work/references/ship-ceremony.md documenting the staged pipeline and its gate points, plus a transition-table test asserting each stage fires in order and halts at the operator-chosen gate. Verified by a test that drives a mock merged PR through ship and asserts branch deleted, main pulled, worktree reclaimed.

title: Idle-triggered worktree reclamation — automate the cleanup nobody ever does
idea: Rather than fold cleanup into a synchronous verb, remove the step entirely by making reclamation ambient: a `saga reclaim` sweep, wired to session-idle, that scans for branches already merged upstream whose worktrees still linger and tears them down within the reversibility envelope (a reclaimed worktree is reconstructible from the merged SHA, so it is authorized-additive-inverse, not irreversible). The grounding shows 15 stale abandoned saga worktrees inflating a repo 10x — the exact residue of a cleanup step that is always deferred. The inversion: stop asking anyone to remember cleanup; make lingering merged-branch worktrees a self-healing condition the fleet reclaims on its own.
basis: Grounding brief §4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ → direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8.' reversibility_certificate.authorize_write (outcome/SKILL.md:92-94) defaults to GATE but authorizes reversible/reconstructible ops — a merged-branch worktree teardown qualifies because it reconstructs from the merged SHA.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `reclaim` subcommand + reclamation function reusing plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_worktrees.py teardown, guarded by reversibility_certificate.authorize_write, plus a test that creates a merged-branch worktree, runs reclaim, and asserts the worktree count returns to baseline while unmerged worktrees are left untouched. Verified against a fixture repo with mixed merged/unmerged worktrees.

title: Extract the reversibility envelope into a shared board-autosync primitive for /work
idea: Today only `/outcome advance --autonomous` can move the board within its enumerated reversibility-gated envelope; a standalone `/work` merge advances the board by hand. Extract `reversibility_certificate.authorize_write` plus the enumerated allowlist into a shared `board_autosync` module and wire it into `/work` so a confirmed merge auto-progresses the derived board projection (set In Progress→Done, close sub-issue, post one coalesced comment) inside the exact same envelope — merge and parent-close stay never-autonomous. Status stays derived-on-read: the board is a projection of the leaf's derived state, never a committed status field. The inversion: the manual 'now go move the board' step disappears wherever a gated write is provably reversible.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:88-113 defines the enumerated reversibility-gated board-sync envelope (set Status, close sub-issue, add/remove label, one coalesced comment) available ONLY to /outcome; work/SKILL.md has no board writer. Engages the binding /outcome campaign decision (grounding §2): board stays a derive-on-read projection, never a committed status field — this idea propagates the projection writer, not a status field.
outcome_shape: PR extracting plugins/saga/scripts/board_autosync.py from the outcome envelope, re-pointing outcome_board_sync.py at it, and wiring it into work's post-merge phase, plus a test asserting a /work merge produces the same board-sync ledger records as an /outcome tick and that merge/parent-close still GATE.

title: Derived idea→deploy arc projection in /loop — replace manual status narration
idea: `/loop` routes work across idea→plan→PR→merge→nonprod but the operator narrates 'where are we' by hand at each hop. Add a `project_arc` renderer in status_card.py that derives the full lifecycle arc position purely on read from the saga's durable state (gate_verdicts, pr_refs, phase_status, destination) and shows a fixed-position arc glyph card — no operator-writable progress field anywhere. The inversion: the manual 'let me tell you the status' step is removed because status is a pure function of already-durable evidence, rendered identically every time. This makes /loop's routing self-narrating and keeps it strictly derive-on-read.
basis: plugins/saga/scripts/status_card.py already renders derived-on-read cards (work/SKILL.md:440-444: 'the card derives its cells on-read from durable state... never replaced by the card'); outcome/SKILL.md:35 'Status is derived on read (R17). No operator-writable status field.' The arc projection extends this proven pattern to /loop's cross-phase view. Engages the binding derive-on-read decision by staying a pure read projection.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `project_arc` function to plugins/saga/scripts/status_card.py + a render call in plugins/saga/skills/loop/SKILL.md, plus a test asserting the arc position is a deterministic function of durable saga fields (same inputs → same glyph card) with no writable status field consulted.

title: Content-addressed evidence ledger that makes FAIL→PASS overwrite structurally impossible
idea: Go beyond bare artifact immutability: make closure itself refuse to fire on a tampered chain. Each gate verdict is written to an append-only, content-addressed evidence ledger keyed by (gate-id, input-SHA) hash; a later PASS cannot occupy the key an earlier FAIL already holds — a differing verdict for the same inputs writes a new keyed row, never an overwrite. The ship verb's final merge/close stage reads the ledger and HALTs (not degrades) if any gate's latest-by-time verdict conflicts with an earlier immutable one for identical inputs. The inversion: remove the human 'wait, did we actually pass?' re-check by making auto-closure impossible unless the evidence chain is provably intact.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody).' Binding /outcome campaign (§2): 'HALT-not-degrade' — this idea makes closure HALT on a broken chain rather than proceed. This extends the direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' by binding immutability to a closure gate, not just storage.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/evidence_ledger.py (content-addressed append-only writer) + a closure gate hook in outcome_merge.py that HALTs on any (gate-id,input-SHA) key holding conflicting verdicts, plus a regression test that reproduces the FAIL-then-PASS overwrite incident and asserts closure HALTs.

title: Retire raw `gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch` for a deterministic saga merge-watcher
idea: The surprising behaviors of `gh pr merge --auto` and `--delete-branch` (merge fires on an unexpected check flip, branch deletes before dependent CI runs) are removed by never using the raw flags. Instead a saga-owned merge-watcher polls `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup` against a recorded expectation set captured at PR-open, and performs merge-then-delete deterministically only when live state matches the recorded expectation — otherwise it surfaces the divergence. The inversion: eliminate the surprising black-box primitive; replace it with an explicit, recorded, poll-and-verify loop so merge timing and branch deletion are never a surprise.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises.' work/SKILL.md:121 already reads 'gh pr view --json state,reviewDecision,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,isDraft,mergedAt' in the continuation loop — the watcher extends this existing read into a recorded expectation-match before mutating.
outcome_shape: PR adding a merge-watcher step to plugins/saga/skills/work/references/pr-continuation-loop.md + a helper in saga.py that records merge expectations at PR-open and matches them at merge time, plus plugins/saga/skills/work/references/gh-merge-surprises.md documenting the retired flags, plus a test simulating a mid-poll check flip that asserts the watcher surfaces rather than merges.

title: Stacked-PR auto-close cascade guard with automatic child rebase-and-reopen
idea: When a base PR merges, GitHub auto-closes its stacked children and the operator manually rebases and reopens each one. Remove the manual recovery by recording stack topology (parent chain) in the saga's pr_refs at PR-open, then on base-merge detection auto-rebase each child onto the new base and reopen it, re-triggering CI on the correct branch. This goes beyond the direct-to-candidate 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' (which only adds CI triggers) by handling the auto-close cascade and the rebase automation together. The inversion: the manual 'now go rescue my stacked PRs' scramble becomes an automatic, topology-aware recovery.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap.' work/SKILL.md:448 records `pr_refs` in the saga — the natural home for a parent-chain topology field. Explicitly distinct from the direct-to-candidate pool item 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' (grounding §8) which addresses only the CI trigger, not the auto-close cascade or rebase.
outcome_shape: PR adding a stack-topology field to the saga pr_refs schema + a base-merge cascade handler in the pr-continuation-loop that rebases and reopens children, plus a test that simulates a base merge over a two-deep stack and asserts each child is rebased, reopened, and CI-retriggered.

title: A single ceremony envelope that batons merge→nonprod→close across saga, deploy, mission-control
idea: Shipping today crosses three plugins by hand: saga merges, deploy promotes to nonprod, mission-control closes the issue — three manual baton passes with no plugin overstepping its charter. Define one reversibility-gated ceremony envelope, captured once at intent, that dispatches each stage to its owning plugin via a typed handoff: saga owns merge, deploy owns nonprod promote + revert, mission-control owns issue close. No plugin performs another's mutation; the envelope only routes. The inversion: the manual three-plugin handoff sequence collapses into one declared-once envelope that fans out to the rightful owner at each stage.
basis: work/SKILL.md:459-465 states the boundaries explicitly: '/work does NOT own deploy or canary (deploy owns deployment mutation and production-health revert). It does NOT file SDLC issues (mission-control owns issue creation).' CROSSES binding /outcome decision (§2) 'PR merge/deploy never autonomous' — engaged via its revisit condition: intake §2 lines 53-57 explicitly reopens merge/deploy-to-nonprod as a once-at-intent-capture operator choice ('Gate or auto merge/deploy-to-nonprod?... operator decides per outcome, once, at start'), superseding the blanket never-autonomous default for envelopes where the operator chose 'auto'.
outcome_shape: PR adding a ceremony-envelope handoff schema (spanning saga merge → deploy nonprod → mission-control close) + a reference doc mapping each stage to its owning plugin, plus a contract test asserting each stage routes only to its owner and that no plugin invokes another's mutation surface directly.

title: Ship is a reconciler, not a script
idea: The ship ceremony is treated as an imperative sequence of git/gh commands the agent types out fresh each time. Reframe one level up: ship is a declarative desired end-state ("this work-thread is done; land it under the envelope's gates") that a single guarded saga `ship.py` reconciles toward — level-triggered, idempotent, and crash-safe, lifting /outcome's proven reconcile philosophy down to the leaf. Each invocation derives the next action purely from `gh pr view --json state,mergeable,mergedAt` plus local git state, so rerunning after a mid-ceremony crash resumes from the derived facts and never double-commits, double-opens, or double-merges. This attacks the buried assumption that the ceremony must be a linear procedure the model performs by hand.
basis: grep for `checkout main`/`--delete-branch`/`cleanup` across plugins/saga/skills, plugins/deploy, plugins/mission-control returned zero matches (no owning command exists); grounding-brief §7 pattern 1 "Manual ship ceremony — commit->PR->merge->checkout-main->pull->cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)"; outcome/SKILL.md:31 "Level-triggered, not imperative ... a crash mid-run is recoverable — the next tick re-derives" is the proven pattern to lift down to the leaf.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/ship.py (a level-triggered reconciler deriving next action from gh pr view JSON + local git state) and a `## Ship reconcile` section in plugins/saga/skills/work/SKILL.md, plus CHANGELOG + plugin.json version bump; verified by an idempotency test that runs ship twice across a simulated mid-ceremony crash and asserts no double-merge and a clean no-op on the second run.

title: Ceremony gates are pre-declared envelope fields, not interactive re-asks
idea: Whether PR reviews are required and whether merge/deploy-to-nonprod is gate-or-auto is treated as a per-step decision the agent re-poses at ship time. Reframe: these are envelope properties captured exactly once at intent capture and stamped into the saga/outcome spec, so the ship reconciler merely reads them rather than interrogating the operator mid-ceremony. This makes the autonomy posture a declared contract the whole lifecycle can honor consistently, killing the default that ship-time gating must be conversational. It also feeds the auto-merge dial (sibling idea) with a single authoritative source for reviews-required and gate-or-auto.
basis: intake-brief §3 lines 53-54,57: required intent questions "Are PR reviews required for this outcome?" and "Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod?", with "operator decides per outcome, once, at start" and "Everything reversible ... proceeds without asking"; today no schema field carries these — /work SKILL.md:52 gates merge "under explicit confirmation" interactively every time.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `ceremony_gates` block (reviews_required, merge, deploy_nonprod) to the intent-capture envelope schema in plugins/saga/scripts/handoff_envelope.py and the outcome-spec, consumed by the ship path; verified by a drift-guard test asserting the field round-trips through save/load and that an unset field defaults to gate (never silent auto).

title: One autonomy allowlist, not three
idea: The reversibility-gated autonomous allowlist is treated as a private property of /outcome's advance loop. But /work and /loop face the identical "which status moves may I make without asking?" question and answer it ad hoc or by re-confirming. Reframe one level up: extract the enumerated allowlist into a single shared autonomy-policy module that /outcome, /work, and /loop all import — one canonical classifier for "reversible-or-additive proceeds silently, irreversible gates." This attacks the ownership assumption that autonomy policy belongs to one skill, and eliminates the three-way drift risk where /work's silent behavior diverges from /outcome's audited envelope.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:88-119 defines the enumerated reversibility-gated envelope (set board status + close sub-issue autonomous; "Never autonomous — always the operator's keystroke" for merge/deploy) and it exists ONLY in /outcome; /work SKILL.md:52 "mutate only under confirmation" and /loop are ad-hoc with no shared classifier; aligns with the /outcome-campaign binding (reversible proceeds, derived-on-read).
outcome_shape: PR extracting plugins/saga/scripts/autonomy_allowlist.py (the reversible/additive vs irreversible op classifier) imported by outcome_board_sync.py and referenced from work/ and loop/ SKILL.md; verified by a test asserting identical op classification across all three call sites plus a drift-guard that the allowlist enum is single-sourced.

title: Gate-or-auto merge is an envelope dial, not a hardcoded 'never'
idea: /outcome hardcodes merging and deploying as "never autonomous ... never allowlisted," treating the autonomy boundary as fixed policy. But intake tension 3 explicitly reopens this: merge/deploy is NOT unconditionally gated — the operator decides per outcome, once, at start. Reframe: promote merge and deploy-to-nonprod from hardcoded-never to envelope-dialed. When the envelope's merge:auto is set AND reviews-required is satisfied AND CI is green AND an immutable PASS evidence record exists, a reconcile tick may merge autonomously; default stays gate. Autonomy becomes evidence-gated rather than blind, so it stays reversibility-in-spirit while honoring "operator decides once at start."
basis: CROSSES the /outcome-campaign binding (grounding-brief §2: PR merge/deploy "never autonomous"; outcome/SKILL.md:105-107 "Merging a PR and deploying — irreversible side effects, permanently human-in-the-loop ... never allowlisted"). Engaging it: intake-brief §3 lines 53-57 is the operator's explicit per-outcome reopen; the crossing is bounded — auto-merge fires ONLY under an evidence gate (green CI + satisfied reviews + immutable PASS artifact) AND explicit per-envelope opt-in, default remains gate/HALT-not-degrade, preserving the invariant's reversibility-in-spirit intent.
outcome_shape: PR adding merge/deploy_nonprod autonomy fields to outcome-spec and extending the allowlist check in outcome_board_sync.py / outcome_merge.py to honor them behind an evidence-presence gate; verified by tests that auto-merge is refused when the dial is unset OR the evidence record is absent, and permitted only when both present and CI green.

title: Evidence is an append-only ledger, not a file you overwrite
idea: Evidence artifacts are treated as ordinary files an agent writes and may overwrite — which is exactly how a later PASS silently clobbered an earlier FAIL and broke chain-of-custody. Reframe: evidence is not a file, it is an append-only ledger keyed by (check, sha). A later PASS cannot replace an earlier FAIL; it appends a superseding record with both preserved, and closure gates compute the latest-per-(check,sha) derived on read. This attacks the assumption that "current result equals the file's current contents," and goes beyond the direct-to-candidate "evidence-artifact immutability" guard by making closure a derived-on-read query over an audit log rather than a write-once lock.
basis: grounding-brief §7 singletons: "a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)"; applies the /outcome-campaign principle "derived-on-read status, never committed status fields" (§2) to evidence; explicitly distinct from and more ambitious than the §8 direct-to-candidate item "evidence-artifact immutability" (a write-once guard) by making supersession visible and closure derived.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/evidence_ledger.py (JSONL append writer + a reader returning latest-per-(check,sha) that flags any FAIL->PASS supersession) consumed by /qa and /code-review closure paths; verified by a test that writing PASS after FAIL preserves the FAIL record and the closure gate surfaces the supersession instead of silently greening.

title: Stack-aware ship: model the cascade instead of getting surprised by it
idea: "That's just how gh/GitHub works" — merging a base PR auto-closes stacked children, --delete-branch cascades, and CI branch-triggers fire unexpectedly. This is treated as immutable harness behavior the agent repeatedly gets surprised by. Reframe: the ship reconciler is stack-aware. Before any merge it derives the PR dependency chain from baseRefName relationships and the CI trigger topology, predicts the auto-close and branch-delete cascade, and either re-targets children onto the new base or surfaces the cascade as an explicit gate — converting a harness surprise into a modeled, previewable step. This goes beyond the direct-to-candidate "stacked-PR CI-trigger support" by modeling the whole cascade and re-basing children, not merely re-triggering CI.
basis: grounding-brief §7 singletons: "stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap" and "gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises"; explicitly beyond the §8 direct-to-candidate item "stacked-PR CI-trigger support" (narrow trigger fix) by adding cascade prediction + child re-target/gate.
outcome_shape: PR adding stack-detection + cascade-preview to the ship path (a plugins/saga/scripts/pr_stack.py helper querying `gh pr view --json baseRefName` chains) that re-targets or gates children before merging the base; verified by a test simulating a 3-PR stack where merging the base re-targets children onto main rather than letting them auto-close.

title: The ceremony is owned by no one — name the seam contract
idea: Ownership is treated as cleanly partitioned: /work owns the PR loop through merge "without owning deploy," mission-control owns the board, deploy owns tags. But the ship ceremony as a whole — commit -> PR -> merge -> board-sync -> branch-cleanup -> nonprod-deploy — spans all three and is owned by no one, which is precisely why it leaks into raw git/gh every session despite the plugins being installed. Reframe: name an explicit ceremony-ownership contract — a documented seam where /work hands the merged-SHA plus an evidence-ledger pointer to a thin ship-coordinator that fans the remaining steps to their owners (mission-control board-sync, deploy nonprod) via a typed handoff, instead of each agent reimplementing the boundary crossing. Clean per-skill ownership does not mean the end-to-end flow is owned.
basis: loop/SKILL.md:60 "mission-control owns issues/boards/comments; deploy owns deploy mutation ... /loop points owners; never [runs the work]" and work/SKILL.md:28 "/work ... coordinates PR-open/review-request/merge ... without owning deploy" — the end-to-end ceremony falls in the unowned seam; grounding-brief §7 pattern 1 (ritual leaks to raw git/gh across 8 repos despite installs). Aligns with {#operator-choice-framework} (doc-only, CLI-driven) and {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: this is a doc + typed handoff inside existing plugins, not a new plugin.
outcome_shape: A merged plugins/saga/references/ship-ceremony-ownership.md (the seam contract naming each ceremony step's owner and the typed handoff payload for /work -> mission-control -> deploy) plus a typed handoff-payload dataclass added to the existing handoff_envelope module; verified by a schema/drift-guard test asserting the payload carries merged-SHA + evidence-ledger pointer and that the doc leaves no ceremony step unowned.

title: ship_ceremony.py — one composable, resumable guarded ship primitive
idea: Extract the commit->PR-open->gate->merge->checkout-base->pull->branch/worktree-cleanup ritual into a single durable state-machine primitive at plugins/saga/scripts/ship_ceremony.py that /work calls instead of ad-hoc git/gh, and that /outcome leaf-harvest reuses verbatim. Each transition carries a reversibility verdict (from reversibility_certificate) and every irreversible step (merge) still gates on the operator; the machine is idempotent and re-entrant so an interrupted ship (merged but not cleaned up) resumes rather than orphaning branches. Because it is a primitive not a copy, every future command that ships inherits the same guards, the same cleanup, and the same audit trail for free — that is the compounding win over today's per-command hand-rolled sequence. It ticks the work-thread saga at each transition so a cold resume knows exactly which ceremony step is pending.
basis: grounding brief §7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit->PR->merge->checkout-main->pull->cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)'. work/SKILL.md:451-453 offers `gh pr merge` under confirmation but never composes the full ceremony; PR-open/review-request/merge/cleanup are scattered confirmations (work/SKILL.md:52,451-460) with no single guarded verb.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/ship_ceremony.py (state machine + transition table) plus tests/test_ship_ceremony.py, with work/SKILL.md Phase-4/PR-loop edited to call it; verified by a golden test that drives the full ceremony against a throwaway branch and asserts each transition's saga tick + reversibility verdict, and by work/SKILL.md no longer emitting raw checkout/pull/branch-delete instructions.

title: Widen the autonomous allowlist consumer from /outcome to /work and /loop
idea: The reversibility_certificate registry and the enumerated autonomous-write allowlist are fleet-general primitives, but today only /outcome advance --autonomous consumes them — /work and /loop still ask the operator for every reversible post-merge board move. Lift the same certificate-gated writer into a shared helper so that after a confirmed merge, /work can autonomously set leaf Status->Done, close the sub-issue, and drop the qa-routing label (all already REVERSIBLE/ADDITIVE in the registry), and /loop can autonomously set In-Progress on route, without a fresh keystroke each time. Merge and deploy stay absent from the registry (default GATE) so nothing irreversible slips through. One registry, three consumers: every future autonomous-write need across the fleet extends the registry once rather than re-deriving reversibility per command.
basis: reversibility_certificate.py:147-222 declares a closed 6-op_kind allowlist (SET_FIELD_STATUS, LABEL add/remove, SUB_ISSUE close/reopen, PROGRESS_COMMENT) that is repo-general, yet outcome/SKILL.md:88-104 is its only consumer; work/SKILL.md:451-453 keeps every board move under explicit confirmation. Merge/deploy are intentionally absent (reversibility_certificate.py:50-51) so widening the consumers cannot authorize an irreversible op.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/board_progression.py (certificate-gated writer extracted from outcome_board_sync) consumed by work/SKILL.md post-merge and loop/SKILL.md on-route, plus tests asserting only enumerated reversible ops fire and merge/deploy return GATE; verified by test_board_progression golden cases and by a diff showing /work's post-merge Status/close moves no longer prompt.

title: Closure-gate consumer that derives eligibility from an immutable supersession chain
idea: Assuming the direct-to-candidate immutability primitive exists, build the compounding layer on top: a closure_gate helper that computes closure-eligibility for any leaf/issue by reading the append-only evidence chain (code-review, qa, deploy verdicts) and refusing autonomous closure when a prior FAIL is not explicitly superseded by a later PASS that references and justifies it. A superseding PASS must name the FAIL record it overrides, forming a chain rather than a mutable latest-artifact. /outcome computes done-status derived-on-read from this chain, so an out-of-band PASS that silently overwrote a FAIL can no longer flip a leaf to closeable. Because closure-eligibility becomes a pure function of the immutable chain, every command that closes (outcome harvest, work post-merge, mission-control) shares one honest verdict source instead of trusting whichever artifact was written last.
basis: grounding brief §7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'; §6 pattern 2: 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state'. Builds strictly beyond the §8 direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' item (the storage primitive) by adding the derive-on-read closure consumer, and reinforces the /outcome binding decision (register row: 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields').
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/closure_gate.py (chain reader + supersession validator) wired into outcome_reconcile/harvest and the new board_progression close path, plus tests/test_closure_gate.py proving an unsuperseded FAIL blocks closure and a justified supersession unblocks it; verified by a golden fixture reproducing the FAIL-overwritten-by-PASS incident and asserting closure is refused.

title: ceremony_hazards.py — one shared preflight detector the ship verb consults
idea: Rather than N one-off fixes and docs for each ceremony surprise, encode the hazard class once as a programmatic preflight primitive the ship verb calls before it mutates: detect stacked-PR base-branch chains (so an auto-close/cleanup does not orphan a dependent PR), gh auto-merge / --delete-branch interactions, and CI branch-trigger gaps where deleting the branch cancels in-flight required checks. It returns structured warnings with a recommended safe order (e.g. re-target the child PR before merging the parent). This subsumes the separate stacked-PR and gh-CLI-doc candidates into a single lint the whole fleet reuses: as new ceremony hazards are discovered they are added to one registry, and every ship path is protected at once instead of each command re-learning the footguns.
basis: grounding brief §7 singletons: 'gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises; stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap; mermaid ... ' — three distinct ceremony footguns mined from sessions. §8 direct-to-candidate lists 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' and 'gh CLI behavior docs' as narrow one-offs; this idea consolidates them into a reusable detector primitive rather than duplicating either.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/ceremony_hazards.py (hazard registry + detect() returning ordered warnings) consumed by ship_ceremony.py's preflight, plus tests/test_ceremony_hazards.py with fixtures for a stacked-PR chain and an auto-merge+delete-branch case; verified by the ship ceremony refusing/reordering on a synthetic stacked-PR fixture.

title: Write-ownership lane manifest + marketplace-CI lint that enforces it
idea: The saga/mission-control/deploy write boundary lives only in prose today (loop's hard boundary, outcome's 'what it does not own', deploy's 'intentionally separate ... hard boundary'), so a plugin can quietly emit a write outside its lane and nothing catches it. Encode the boundary once as a machine-checkable ownership manifest (which plugin may mutate issues/board, git/merge, deploy tags) and add a CI lint that greps each plugin's scripts for cross-lane mutations (e.g. deploy calling gh issue edit, or saga pushing a deploy tag) and fails the marketplace build. Second-order payoff: the boundary stops being aspirational prose that drifts and becomes an enforced contract, so future plugins inherit correct lanes by construction and reviewers stop policing it by eye.
basis: loop/SKILL.md:59-62 and 300-306 state the saga/mission-control/deploy write boundary as prose; outcome/SKILL.md:164-169 'What /outcome does NOT own'; deploy-state/SKILL.md 'intentionally separate from saga because deployment mutation deserves a hard boundary'. No machine check exists for any of it — distinct from the §5 QUEUED {#marketplace-ci-guard} (a generic registry guard) by targeting write-lane ownership specifically.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding docs/ownership-lanes.json (or a manifest under .claude-plugin/) plus scripts/check_ownership_lanes.py wired into the marketplace CI job, and tests; verified by the lint failing on a seeded cross-lane mutation (deploy script calling `gh issue`) and passing on the current tree.

title: Intent-time merge/deploy pre-authorization token consulted by the certificate
idea: At /outcome intent capture the operator answers 'gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod?' once; mint that answer into a scoped, single-use-per-leaf pre-authorization token stored in the committed outcome spec. The reversibility certificate gains a consult seam: for the otherwise-GATE merge/deploy ops it returns AUTHORIZED only when a valid matching token is present, else it HALTs. This does not remove the human keystroke — it moves the operator's authorization earlier (once, up front, as authorizer-of-record) rather than N times mid-run, which is exactly the envelope-autonomy the intake resolves. The token is the compounding lever: the same consult seam later carries per-environment or per-leaf policy without re-touching any call site, and absent-token always falls back to today's GATE so the safe default is unchanged.
basis: intake brief §3 required intent question 'Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod? Merge/deploy NOT unconditionally gated; operator decides per outcome, once, at start' — the explicit reshaping that this idea implements. Engages the /outcome campaign binding stance (outcome/SKILL.md:105-109 'Merging PR and deploying — never autonomous') and reversibility_certificate.py:50-51,239-267 (merge absent -> default GATE): the token keeps the operator as authorizer-of-record and HALTs when absent, so the never-degrade invariant holds; revisit condition (operator opts auto at capture) is precisely the intake's resolution.
outcome_shape: A merged PR extending outcome_spec.py with a preauth_token field captured at /outcome start, a consult seam in reversibility_certificate.authorize_write for merge/deploy ops, and tests proving merge is GATE without a token and AUTHORIZED with a matching one; verified by test_reversibility golden cases and an /outcome start prompt capturing the gate/auto choice.

title: Immutable ship receipt — proving the ceremony (including cleanup) actually ran
idea: Every ship verb invocation emits an append-only ship receipt (commit SHA, PR number, merge SHA, branches deleted, worktrees reclaimed, ceremony steps completed) into a durable ledger, so 'did it actually merge and clean up' becomes a verifiable fact rather than an assumed one. Post-ship reclamation is verified against the receipt: if the receipt claims cleanup but a worktree still exists, the discrepancy surfaces loudly instead of silently accumulating stale worktrees. Because the receipt is a shared primitive, /work, /outcome harvest, and any future shipping command all produce the same tamper-evident evidence, and the receipt doubles as the immutable evidence record that closure-gate (idea 3) and delegation-integrity checks can read — one artifact, several compounding consumers.
basis: grounding brief §6 pattern 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring ... any bridge/delegation idea needs "did it actually run/persist" verification'; §4 hygiene find: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+' — direct evidence that ceremony cleanup silently fails and is never verified.
outcome_shape: A merged PR adding a ship-receipt writer/reader (plugins/saga/scripts/ship_receipt.py) invoked by ship_ceremony.py, plus a reclamation-verify step and tests; verified by a test that runs a ship, asserts the receipt records the deleted branch/worktree, and flags a synthetic case where the worktree survives the receipt's cleanup claim.

title: The /ship launch-poll: one guarded verb that polls each gate station GO/NO-GO/HOLD
idea: Collapse the mined 8-repo manual ritual (commit -> PR -> merge -> checkout-main -> pull -> cleanup) into a single guarded /ship verb modeled not on a linear pipeline but on a spaceflight launch-commit poll. Instead of running stages in sequence, it polls each independent gate station in one pass -- tests, the /code-review envelope, CI status rollup, board state, deploy gate -- and each returns GO / NO-GO / HOLD with a named holder and a reason string. Any NO-GO scrubs the ceremony (records the reason, leaves the branch fully intact, never ships a partial), while a HOLD recycles just that one station (fix, re-poll it) rather than restarting the whole sequence. Merge and deploy stations honor the intent-capture gate-or-auto answer and merge stays confirmation-gated per work/SKILL.md:452, so autonomy is bounded to what the operator authorized at outcome start.
basis: Grounding brief S7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony -- commit->PR->merge->checkout-main->pull->cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)'; work/SKILL.md:452 keeps merge 'explicitly confirmed'. Source domain: NASA launch-commit criteria / flight-director go-no-go poll of independent console stations, with scrub-and-recycle semantics rather than pipeline restart.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/work/references/ship-poll.md and a `ship` verb section in work/SKILL.md enumerating the stations, GO/NO-GO/HOLD/scrub/recycle semantics, and the station->intent-gate mapping; verified by a scenario table (each station's NO-GO -> scrub outcome) plus a drift-guard test asserting merge and deploy stations remain confirmation/gate-or-auto bound and never silently auto-fire.

title: Closing-count reconciliation: ship refuses to declare done until the opened-manifest zeroes out
idea: Borrow the operating-room sponge-and-instrument count, where nothing is closed up until everything opened is accounted for. During a work thread every mutable resource opened -- branch, worktree, background session, scratch artifact, draft PR -- is registered to an 'opened manifest', and the ship ceremony's cleanup phase runs a closing count that reconciles opened-versus-closed. Ship cannot emit 'shipped' until the count zeroes or each intentional retention is explicitly recorded with a reason, directly killing the 15 stale worktrees and the missing team-execution teardown step. The count is a derived reconciliation read at ceremony time, never a committed status field, so it stays consistent with the derived-on-read discipline.
basis: Grounding brief S4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ -> direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8'; grounding brief S6.1 teardown gap. Source domain: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist final sponge/instrument count (count-in must equal count-out before closure).
outcome_shape: PR adding a teardown-reconcile reference plus an opened_manifest registration hook in the work/outcome cleanup path and a saga-spec field; verified by a test that seeds two orphan worktrees and one background session, then asserts ship blocks with a non-zero closing count and surfaces the unreconciled items.

title: Checkpoint-gated auto-progression with a p53 damage-halt (widen the permissive set, keep HALT-not-degrade)
idea: Model status derivation as eukaryotic cell-cycle checkpoints: each lifecycle transition carries a checkpoint predicate, and 'permissive' checkpoints auto-advance the derived status the moment their predicate is satisfied -- this is how you widen the /outcome autonomous allowlist and, by sharing the predicate engine, propagate the same auto-progression to /work and /loop. A dedicated damage checkpoint plays the p53 role: it senses inconsistency and HALTs progression rather than degrading, matching the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade rule. The widened permissive set stays strictly inside the existing reversibility-gated envelope (outcome/SKILL.md:96-101), while irreversible transitions -- merge, deploy, parent-issue-close (SKILL.md:105-109) -- remain non-permissive arrest points. Status stays derived-on-read from committed spec plus events (SKILL.md:35), never a written status field, so this aligns with rather than contradicts the /outcome binding decision.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:35 'Status is derived on read (R17). No operator-writable status field'; :96-113 the enumerated reversibility-gated envelope. Aligns with the /outcome campaign binding decision (derived-on-read, HALT-not-degrade) and does not cross it -- the widening happens only within the already-authorized reversible-or-additive set. Source domain: cell-cycle checkpoint control (restriction point / G2-M) with p53 damage-sensing arrest instead of graceful degradation.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared checkpoint-predicate reference module and wiring outcome + work + loop skills to it (permissive vs arrest classification per transition); verified by a test that seeds a spec/event inconsistency and asserts the tick HALTs with a visible gated record and performs no advance, versus a clean case that auto-advances.

title: One reconcile controller for /work, /loop, /outcome -- Kubernetes-style level-triggered convergence
idea: /outcome already runs a 'level-triggered reconcile loop' (SKILL.md:3), but /work's PR-continuation loop and /loop re-derive progression edge-triggered, acting on whatever transition they happen to observe. Adopt the Kubernetes controller model: a single reconcile primitive that repeatedly derives desired-versus-actual from committed spec plus events and converges, so the auto-progression logic and the widened allowlist live once and propagate to /work and /loop by inclusion rather than by three parallel re-implementations. Edge-triggered progression is precisely what produces the mined create/board-add/field-set races; level-triggered convergence is idempotent by construction and self-heals outside-writer drift, which is exactly the reconcile-on-wake concern the outcome skill already documents (SKILL.md:123). The controller writes only through the existing reversibility certificate, so widening autonomy never escapes the enumerated envelope.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:3 'A level-triggered reconcile loop'; :123 'Autonomous board-sync writes the board but never re-reads it... drift would persist silently. Reconcile...'; grounding brief S7 pattern 3 'create/board-add/field-set racing (4 repos)'. Source domain: Kubernetes controller reconciliation -- declarative desired-state, level-triggered convergence, idempotent writes.
outcome_shape: PR extracting a reconcile_controller reference module from outcome and wiring /work and /loop skill docs plus their loop scripts to it; verified by a race-reproduction test (rapid double tick -> single convergent write via the recorded idempotency key) and a drift test (outside field change -> reconcile re-detects and corrects).

title: Pre-registered pass criteria: freeze the gate's evidence contract before the run so a later PASS cannot overwrite a FAIL
idea: The mined incident -- a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS -- is structurally p-hacking / HARKing: the goalpost moved after the result was seen. Borrow clinical-trial pre-registration: at intent capture the gate's acceptance criteria and the evidence artifact's identity and path are registered up front and frozen, before any run produces a result. Every subsequent evidence write is append-only and keyed by attempt number, so a FAIL and a later PASS coexist as an ordered chain rather than one clobbering the other, and closure reads the whole chain, not just the last write. This deliberately exceeds the direct-to-candidate 'artifact immutability' seed by adding the pre-declared contract, the ordered attempt chain, and the rule that closure evaluates the chain.
basis: Grounding brief S7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'. Builds beyond direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' (S8). Source domain: clinical-trial pre-registration (ClinicalTrials.gov) and the bound, page-numbered lab notebook -- anti-HARKing controls that fix the criteria before observing the outcome.
outcome_shape: PR adding an evidence-ledger reference (pre-registered criteria block + append-only attempt chain) to qa/ and code-review/ skills plus a small ledger helper; verified by a test that writes an attempt-1 FAIL then an attempt-2 PASS and asserts both persist, the criteria are unchanged, and closure surfaces the prior FAIL in the chain.

title: Content-addressed evidence custody chain: closure verifies the seal and HALTs on tamper
idea: /outcome already resolves a manifest_ref pointer to attribute a leaf's producer (SKILL.md:55). Extend that pointer into a tamper-evident custody chain: each gate's evidence artifact is content-addressed by hash, the hash is recorded in the append-only completion event log (which is never rewritten), and closure recomputes and verifies the hash before declaring done -- a broken or missing seal HALTs rather than degrades. Model the two-custodian split on anti-doping A/B-sample custody: the producing agent seals the artifact and the closing verifier independently checks the seal, so no single actor can both produce and bless the evidence. That two-role separation aligns with never-gatekeepers -- Claude remains verifier-of-record for the gated closure decision, and the external/producing engine can seal but never self-certify.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:55 'resolve it via manifest_store.resolve_manifest_ref to show the leaf's producer attribution and disposition'. Aligns with binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): the verifier, not the producer, blesses the seal. Source domain: SEC Rule 17a-4 WORM (write-once-read-many) retention plus WADA anti-doping A/B-sample chain-of-custody separation of collector and analyst.
