outcome_shape: PR extending manifest_store to content-hash-seal evidence artifacts and adding a closure-time verify step in outcome/ and qa/; verified by a test that seals an artifact, mutates its bytes, and asserts closure HALTs with a tamper record rather than passing, plus a test that a producer cannot self-certify without the verifier role.

title: Merge interlocking: a route-locking pre-merge check that prevents stacked-PR auto-close and strand surprises
idea: The mined singletons -- stacked-PR auto-close, gh pr merge --auto and --delete-branch behavior surprises, CI branch-trigger gaps -- are all conflicting-route hazards. Borrow railway signalling interlocking, where a route cannot be set if it conflicts with an already-set route. Before any merge or auto-merge is authorized, build the PR dependency graph (which PRs base on which) and apply interlock rules: a child PR's merge route is locked until its base merges; --delete-branch is blocked while a dependent PR still bases on that branch; an auto-merge that would auto-close a stacked sibling is flagged as a conflicting route and gated. The interlock is surfaced advisorily at /work's merge-confirmation step (SKILL.md:452), informing the operator rather than silently overriding, so it goes beyond the direct-to-candidate 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' by adding the conflicting-route safety logic itself.
basis: Grounding brief S7 singletons: 'gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises; stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap'. Extends beyond direct-to-candidate 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' (S8). Source domain: railway signalling interlocking -- route locking and conflicting-route prevention on shared track.
outcome_shape: PR adding a merge-interlock reference and a pre-merge PR-dependency-graph check invoked at /work's merge offer; verified by a test with a stacked pair A<-B asserting B's auto-merge and branch-delete are blocked/flagged while A is open, and cleared once A merges.

title: Positive handoff protocol at the saga <-> mission-control <-> deploy boundary -- no dropped batons
idea: Ownership of a work item passes across three plugins -- saga (build to merge), mission-control (board and issue state), deploy (tag promotion) -- but today those transfers are implicit and race. Borrow air-traffic control's positive handoff and the naval bridge transfer 'you have the con': the releasing plugin does not drop ownership until the receiving plugin explicitly acknowledges (the 'radar contact' ack), recorded as an ack token in the saga. The saga->deploy edge is the sharp one, since /work owns the PR loop to merge but explicitly does not own deploy (SKILL.md:28); the handoff makes that boundary an acknowledged transfer, and the intent-capture gate-or-auto answer travels inside the handoff envelope so deploy knows whether it is authorized to auto-promote or must gate. This engages the /outcome rule that merge/deploy is never coordinator-autonomous by moving the authority decision to deploy explicitly rather than leaving it implicit at the boundary.
basis: work/SKILL.md:28 '/work answers: Build it -- and owns the PR loop to merge (this engine)' and its description 'without owning deploy'; grounding brief S7 pattern 3 create/board-add/field-set racing. Aligns with /outcome campaign (merge/deploy never coordinator-autonomous) and {#operator-choice-framework}. Source domain: FAA ATC positive/radar-contact sector handoff and naval bridge conning-authority transfer ('you have the con').
outcome_shape: PR adding a handoff-ack envelope (ack token + gate-or-auto payload) to saga/handoff and the deploy skill docs, plus a saga field recording the acknowledged transfer; verified by a test asserting ownership is not released until an ack is recorded and that the gate-or-auto answer propagates into the deploy-side authorization decision.

title: /work ship — one guarded verb for commit→PR→merge→sync→cleanup
idea: Flip the constraint to its extreme: the operator NEVER issues a raw git or gh command for the ship ceremony again — a single `/work ship` verb runs the whole ordered ritual (stage+commit, push, PR-open, request-review, merge, checkout main, pull, delete-branch, prune worktree). The unrealistic part is 'never touch git'; the practical kernel is that the five steps are one recorded, resumable transaction with a single confirmation surface instead of five, so a crash mid-ceremony re-derives the remaining steps from saga state rather than leaving a half-shipped branch. Merge stays explicitly gated unless an intent-capture envelope pre-authorized it (tension-1 attended rule), and every step writes an ordered ledger entry so `resume` can replay the tail. It supersedes the ad-hoc `commit-push-pr` + `clean_gone` pairing by making sync+cleanup first-class members of the same transaction rather than two disconnected commands the operator remembers to run.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos).' work/SKILL.md:52-53 confirms /work today treats PR-open, review-request, and merge as three separate explicitly-confirmed ops and does NOT own sync/cleanup at all.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/skills/work/references/ship-ceremony.md` + a `ship_ceremony.py` transaction script + a `/work ship` verb block in work/SKILL.md, with plugin.json/CHANGELOG/marketplace.json version bump. Verified by an integration test driving the ordered plan in dry-run against a throwaway repo, asserting each step emits a saga ledger entry and that an injected mid-ceremony abort resumes from the exact next step.

title: Envelope-authorized merge in the /outcome autonomous allowlist
idea: Flip 'merge is permanently human-in-the-loop' to its opposite extreme — zero operator keystrokes, the coordinator merges. The unrealistic pole (silent unattended merge) is tamed to a practical kernel: a new `AUTONOMOUS_UNDER_ENVELOPE` write class in `reversibility_certificate.authorize_write` fires a merge ONLY when a durable, revocable, intent-captured `merge_policy=auto` token exists for that outcome, and only after the leaf's own gates (green CI + fresh approval + passing QA evidence) are all satisfied on read. Pre-authorization is not silence: the merge is recorded in the board-sync ledger with the envelope id that authorized it, and a single revocation flips every future tick back to GATE. This deliberately reopens the 'never allowlisted' merge rule because intake §3 explicitly makes merge operator-choosable once at start rather than unconditionally gated.
basis: Crosses `/outcome campaign` register row + outcome/SKILL.md:105-107 ('Merging a PR ... never allowlisted'). Engaged via its revisit condition in intake §3 lines 53-57: 'Are PR reviews required...? Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod? Merge/deploy NOT unconditionally gated; operator decides per outcome, once, at start.' Derived-on-read is preserved — no status field is committed; the envelope token is a consent record, not a status.
outcome_shape: PR touching `plugins/saga/scripts/reversibility_certificate.py` (new write class + envelope check), outcome/SKILL.md allowlist section, and the board-sync ledger schema, plus CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bump. Verified by a certificate unit test: merge is DENIED with no token, AUTHORIZED with a valid token + all-gates-green, and re-DENIED after revocation, with each authorized merge carrying the authorizing envelope id in the ledger record.

title: Autonomous board-sync propagated down into /work and /loop
idea: Flip 'only /outcome propagates status to the board' to the extreme where EVERY lifecycle transition anywhere auto-projects to the operations board with zero manual mission-control moves. Today /work and /loop write `phase_status`/`status` onto the saga but never touch the board, so a standalone /work run leaves the board stale until someone hand-moves the card — exactly the board/field-drift pain. The kernel: extract /outcome's `advance --autonomous` writer (reversibility certificate + idempotent board-sync ledger + reconcile-on-wake) into a shared library that /work and /loop call on each confirmed phase transition, so the board is a derived projection of saga state fleet-wide, not an outcome-only feature. This stays inside derived-on-read — the board is an external projection, no committed status field is introduced — and it reuses the same reconcile drift-hold so an outside writer is still detected.
basis: loop/SKILL.md:264-269 shows /loop ticks set `--phase-status`/`--status`/`--destination` with no board write; outcome/SKILL.md:90 states the autonomous board writer exists ONLY behind `advance --autonomous`. Grounding §7 pattern 3 documents mission-control board/field drift across 4 repos as the recurring cost of that gap.
outcome_shape: PR extracting `board_sync.py` (certificate + ledger + reconcile) from the outcome path into a shared module imported by work/SKILL.md and loop/SKILL.md transition steps, with CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bump. Verified by a test that a simulated /work phase transition emits the same idempotent ledger write and reconcile drift-hold that an /outcome tick would, and that a repeated tick is a no-op under the same key.

title: Closure blocked by an unresolved FAIL in a content-addressed evidence ledger
idea: Flip 'evidence files are mutable paths' to the absolute: nothing is ever overwritten — every QA/review evidence artifact is written to a content-addressed, append-only object keyed by (acceptance-predicate, content-hash). Immutability alone is already a direct-to-candidate item, so the novel kernel here is the CLOSURE GATE built on top: a ship/close is DENIED whenever the ledger holds an unresolved FAIL object for the same acceptance predicate, and the ship verdict must reference the specific evidence hash it is trusting so a later PASS cannot silently supersede an earlier FAIL. The verdict is derived on read by walking the predicate's object chain — latest state wins only if every prior FAIL carries an explicit resolution object — which turns the audit chain-of-custody from a filename convention into an enforced predicate. This directly answers the incident where a probe overwrote a FAIL artifact with a later PASS.
basis: Grounding §7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody).' qa/SKILL.md:288 shows /qa writes evidence to a reusable mutable path `docs/qa/<file>.md` with `--evidence-link`, the exact overwrite surface. Builds beyond the §8 direct-to-candidate 'evidence-artifact immutability' by adding the derived closure-blocking predicate, not just immutable storage.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/evidence_ledger.py` (content-addressed append-only store + `resolve_verdict(predicate)` walker), rewiring qa/SKILL.md Phase 5 emit to write objects + reference a hash, and a closure-gate check in the ship path. Verified by a test: write FAIL object, then write PASS object for the same predicate — closure stays DENIED until an explicit resolution object is appended, and the FAIL object remains readable by hash.

title: Stacked-PR-aware ship preflight with topological merge ordering
idea: Flip to the extreme where EVERY PR is stacked on another — design the ship ceremony as if the default case is a deep stack, then keep the kernel for the common case. A ship preflight walks each open PR's base ref, detects when a base is itself another open PR (a stack), computes the safe topological merge order, and refuses `--delete-branch` on any branch that still has a live descendant PR based on it. It also flags the gh auto-merge + CI-branch-trigger footguns: a base-branch merge that would auto-close descendants or fire branch-triggered CI on a retargeted base. Beyond mere 'stacked-PR CI-trigger support' (a direct-to-candidate item), the novel piece is the retarget-and-reorder planner that emits a diffable merge sequence and blocks the branch-delete that would strand a descendant.
basis: Grounding §7 singletons: 'stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap' and 'gh pr merge --auto/--delete-branch behavior surprises.' These are recorded ceremony footguns with no current tooling; work/SKILL.md's merge path (line 452) treats a PR as standalone with no base-chain awareness.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/scripts/ship_preflight.py` (base-chain detection + topological order + retarget plan) and a stacked-PR section in `references/ship-ceremony.md`, with CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bump. Verified by a test constructing a 3-PR stack (C→B→A) that asserts the emitted merge order is A,B,C, that deleting A's branch is refused while B is open, and that a base-retarget plan is produced for B and C.

title: One declared ship-ownership contract across saga / mission-control / deploy
idea: Flip the boundary two ways — collapse all three plugins into one omniplugin (rejected: portfolio-groom burden) versus total separation — and mine the kernel from the failure of both: a single declared ownership matrix that names exactly which plugin owns each ceremony mutation (commit/PR/merge = saga /work; board Status + issue open/close = saga board-sync + mission-control; tag-promotion/deploy = deploy) with a drift-guard test asserting no two plugins claim the same mutation. Today the boundary is prose scattered across three SKILLs ('/work does NOT own deploy', deploy owns tag-promotion) with no machine-checkable contract, which is how release-surface and handoff drift creep in. This is a contract module, not a new plugin, so it reduces boundary confusion without adding to the portfolio. The matrix becomes the single source the ship verb, board-sync, and deploy hand-offs all read to know where a mutation legally lives.
basis: work/SKILL.md:460-461 ('does NOT own deploy ... deploy owns deployment') + deploy-state/SKILL.md:37-45 (deploy owns tag-promotion) define the boundary only in prose. Engages `{#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}`: this adds a contract file, not a plugin, so it carries no consolidation debt and instead shrinks cross-plugin ambiguity — satisfying rather than crossing the decision.
outcome_shape: PR adding `plugins/saga/references/ship-ownership.md` (the matrix) + a `ship_ownership.py` machine-readable table + a boundary drift-guard test, with CHANGELOG/marketplace bump. Verified by a test asserting every ceremony mutation maps to exactly one owning plugin and that a synthetic duplicate-claim fails the guard.

title: Self-shipping issue — an executable ship policy authored at intent capture
idea: Take the F6 'every issue self-executing' flip literally: at issue-creation time in mission-control, the operator answers the two envelope questions (PR-reviews-required? merge/deploy gate-or-auto?) once, and those answers are stored on the issue as an executable ship-policy envelope that travels with it. The unrealistic pole is fully hands-off shipping; the kernel is that the ceremony's autonomy is decided at the moment of intent, not re-litigated at every step, so /outcome advance simply reads the envelope to know whether to gate or fire each ceremony step. On green CI + fresh review + passing evidence the issue self-progresses to its authorized ceiling (PR, merge, or nonprod) and pages the operator only on exception — the envelope is the single revocable consent that ideas T7-F6-2 and T7-F6-3 both consume. This closes the loop where autonomy posture is asked ad hoc mid-run instead of captured as a durable, auditable field at intake.
basis: Intake §3 lines 53-57 name the two required intent questions and state the operator decides autonomy 'once, at start'; grounding §8 theme 7 frames this as 'envelope autonomy.' No ingestion path exists today — grounding §1 correction (h) confirms `outcome_decompose.py` does not ingest from an existing GitHub Objective and 'No ingestion path confirmed', so the envelope has no authoring home yet.
outcome_shape: PR adding a ship-policy envelope schema + the two intent questions to `plugins/mission-control/skills/issues` (or a `ship_envelope.py`), an issue-body/field carrier, and an envelope-reader in outcome advance, with CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace bump. Verified by a test that a captured `{reviews: required, merge: auto, deploy: gate}` envelope round-trips onto an issue and that outcome advance reads it to gate deploy while authorizing merge.

title: Wire the existing sub-issue reader into `/outcome start --from-objective`
idea: The ingestion primitive already exists but is orphaned: `discover_subissues.py` fetches a parent issue plus its linked sub-issues (number/title/state/url/labels/assignees) via GraphQL, yet `/outcome start` accepts only a free-text objective and always emits the hardcoded 2-node design->build starter (`_starter_nodes`). An operator who did the disciplined thing in mission-control (filed an Objective, linked capability/defect sub-issues) gets zero leverage and must hand-redraft the whole DAG. Add `start --from-objective <owner/repo#N>` that calls `fetch_subissues`/`normalize`, maps `parent.title` to the objective, each sub-issue to a node (kind inferred from label: capability/defect->code, exploration/context-update->non-code), seeds each node's `github` pass-through map with the sub-issue ref so board-sync and reconcile bind immediately, marks closed sub-issues as pre-completed seeds, then hands the drafted DAG straight to the existing U7 review-before-dispatch gate. This turns a real GitHub Objective tree into a validated seed DAG in one command instead of a manual retype.
basis: discover_subissues.py:42-86 already returns parent+subissues with labels/state; outcome.py:270-274 `_starter_nodes()` hardcodes design->build; grounding brief §1(h): '`/outcome start` = 2-node starter DAG ... not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.'
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome.py (new `--from-objective` arg + objective->DAG seeder fn), a thin importer of discover_subissues.py, plugins/saga/skills/outcome/SKILL.md (start-verb row), references/outcome-spec.md, and the release surfaces (plugin.json/marketplace.json/CHANGELOG). Verified by new tests/test_outcome_command.py cases feeding a fixture GraphQL payload and asserting the produced spec `validate()`s and each node.github binds to its sub-issue.

title: Ingest-provenance + `reconcile --from-objective` structural drift guard
idea: Once an outcome is seeded from an Objective, the GitHub tree keeps moving — someone adds a sub-issue, closes another, retitles a third — and the outcome-spec DAG silently diverges from the Objective it was born from. This is the exact disease #295 reconcile solves for status, but one altitude up: today's `outcome_reconcile` scope is strictly 'board Status and issue open/closed', so an ADDED or REMOVED sub-issue on the parent is invisible. Stamp each ingested node and the spec with an `ingest_source` provenance record (parent ref + the spec_revision at ingest), and add `outcome reconcile <id> --from-objective` that re-fetches the sub-issue tree and surfaces added/removed/retitled sub-issues as `structure-drift` records the operator resolves via the existing lazy_grow/prune paths — never auto-mutating, because R20 approval is recorded per spec_revision and any structural edit re-closes the gate. This keeps a long-running campaign honest against the Objective without a second writer.
basis: references/outcome-spec.md:170 fixes reconcile's saga-owned field class to 'board Status and issue open/closed' only — structural additions are out of scope; discover_subissues.normalize returns `totalCount`; grounding brief §3 pattern 3 records board/field drift as a top-3 recurring pain.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_reconcile.py (new `structure-drift` detector reading discover_subissues vs spec nodes), outcome_spec.py (ingest_source provenance field + round-trip), outcome.py (reconcile `--from-objective` flag), SKILL.md reconcile section, and release surfaces. Verified by tests/test_outcome_reconcile.py asserting an added-sub-issue fixture yields a structure-drift record that resolves through lazy_grow and bumps the revision.

title: Canonical `intent` envelope: capture the mandated start-time posture questions once
idea: `start()` persists only outcome_id, objective, and nodes — the intake brief's mandated 'required intent questions' (Are PR reviews required? Gate or auto merge/deploy-to-nonprod? decomposition posture serial-vs-throughput? external-LLM posture per stage?) have literally nowhere to land, so they are re-answered ad hoc mid-run or silently defaulted, which is the documented silence-as-consent fury pattern. Add a canonical `intent` object to OutcomeSpec alongside `objective`/`decision_trail`, captured once at start via a structured dialog, encoding `merge_gate`/`deploy_gate`/`reviews_required`/`decompose_posture`/`external_llm_posture`. `advance` reads `intent` each tick instead of hardcoded defaults, and the autonomous board-sync allowlist is intersected with it (merge/deploy stay permanently HITL, but `reviews_required` decides whether a leaf can reach `done` without a review-artifact). Crucially this is posture config — a committed decision field like `objective`, NOT a node status field — so derived-on-read is preserved: live node state is still computed each read, only the operator's once-settled posture is stored.
basis: intake brief §3: 'Required intent questions: Are PR reviews required ... Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod? ... operator decides per outcome, once, at start'; outcome.py:261-263 start writes only {outcome_id, objective, nodes}; OutcomeSpec field list outcome_spec.py:365-369 has no posture field. Engages the /outcome campaign binding 'never committed status fields' by explicitly scoping intent as posture, not status.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_spec.py (new `intent` dataclass + validate + from_dict/to_dict), outcome.py (start-time dialog + intent-aware advance), references/outcome-spec.md top-level shape table, SKILL.md, and release surfaces. Verified by tests/test_outcome_spec.py round-trip + validation cases and a test_outcome_command.py case asserting reviews_required gates a leaf's `done` transition.

title: `start --preview`: confirm intent + derived DAG before any branch/spec/store is written
idea: `start()` immediately writes the spec, materializes the store, and (via the campaign) commits to an `outcome/<slug>` branch, and it refuses to re-start once a spec exists — so a mistyped objective or a wrong posture answer leaves a branch-local artifact you must manually tear down before retrying. There is no dry-run. Add `outcome start --preview` that runs the full intent dialog and renders the resulting intent envelope, the seeded/derived starter DAG, and a one-glance posture summary through the existing `status_card` renderer WITHOUT writing any file. The operator confirms once, then the real `start` proceeds; a rejected preview costs nothing and creates no zombie branch. This is the antidote to the silence-as-consent gate pattern at the single most expensive-to-undo moment of the campaign.
basis: outcome.py:257-266 `start` writes spec + `_store` immediately and raises 'already started; use resume' if a spec exists; grounding brief §7 pattern 2 documents operator fury at gate primitives that treat silence as consent — a no-write preview is the mitigation.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome.py (`--preview` no-write path reusing status_card.project_outcome), SKILL.md start-verb row, and release surfaces. Verified by a tests/test_outcome_command.py case asserting `--preview` produces rendered output and leaves zero files under docs/outcomes/<id>/.

title: `outcome draft`: refine a raw brain-dump into a clarity-checked objective + node skeleton
idea: `start` demands a crisp objective string and the `outcome_clarity` rubric (output-vs-outcome, measurability, direction+threshold) is only ever applied downstream in /spec — so an operator with a messy paragraph, a pasted spec, or a Slack blob either hand-crafts a clean objective (friction) or feeds an activity-phrased objective that only fails the clarity lens much later. Add `outcome draft <raw-file-or-stdin>` that runs the raw text through the `outcome_clarity` rubric to produce a candidate measurable `objective` (rewriting 'we'll build X' into 'X moves metric M past threshold T') plus a proposed node skeleton, presents both for operator edit, and then feeds the existing U7 approval gate before `start`. Claude is the drafter and verifier-of-record; if an external engine is used to draft the rewrite it is advisory-only and Claude reconciles — the never-gatekeepers decision holds because no gated decision is delegated. This closes the gap SKILL.md itself flags: 'Authoring the graph from scratch ... a later unit.'
basis: references/rubrics/spec/core/outcome_clarity.md exists (output-vs-outcome, measurability) but is wired only into /spec; SKILL.md:166 lists 'Authoring the graph from scratch — /plan + decompose flow (a later unit)' as NOT owned by /outcome today. Engages {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): the draft rewrite is advisory, Claude is verifier-of-record, so the revisit-when is not tripped.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome.py (new `draft` verb), a new references/outcome-draft.md wiring the clarity rubric, SKILL.md verb table, and release surfaces. Verified by a test feeding an activity-phrased raw string and asserting the drafted objective carries a measurable direction+threshold and the skeleton `validate()`s.

title: Derive a per-leaf `step_profile` from kind + risk instead of assuming the full lifecycle
idea: Every leaf implicitly runs the full native /plan->/work->/code-review->/qa, and the starter is always design->build, so a one-line changelog (non-code, low-risk) carries the same ceremony as a gated destructive capability. The Node already carries `kind` plus `gated`/`risky`/`destructive` flags, but nothing derives WHICH lifecycle steps a leaf should actually run from them. Add a pure `step_profile(node)` function that maps (kind, risk flags, has-PR-contract) to a recommended lifecycle-verb set — skip /plan+/doc-review for a trivial non-code leaf, force /qa plus a second review for a destructive one — surfaced in the `attend` handoff and the `graph` render so the operator sees the tailored path per leaf. This never enables any backend (the menu stays off-by-default, host-conditional), and if a step the profile requires has no available capability the tick HALTs rather than silently skipping the step — HALT-not-degrade applied to step selection, not just backend selection.
basis: references/outcome-spec.md:48 Node carries `kind` + `gated/risky/destructive` risk flags; outcome.py:270-274 hardcodes design->build; SKILL.md:22-23 `attend` hands a native /resume with no per-leaf step tailoring. Engages the /outcome campaign binding 'HALT-not-degrade; backend menu off-by-default' by stating the derivation enables nothing and HALTs on missing step capability.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts (new outcome_steps.py pure fn or an outcome_spec.py helper), attend/graph rendering in outcome.py, SKILL.md, and release surfaces. Verified by a tests/test_outcome_spec.py table over (kind, risk-flags) -> expected verb set and an attend-handoff snapshot test.

title: `outcome repost`: change campaign posture mid-run as an audited, re-approving spec bump
idea: Intent is settled 'once, at start', but outcomes run for hours across sessions and session-mining recorded operators asking for mid-run model-change pauses — today flipping a posture (reviews-required off, merge-gate to auto) means hand-editing the committed spec with no sanctioned, audited path and no guarantee the next tick re-derives from it. Add `outcome repost <id> --set merge_gate=auto` (etc.) that mutates the intent envelope atomically using the established redirect_dependency shape: mutate a snapshot, validate, and only then bump `spec_revision` and append a `decision_trail` 'why' record. Because approval is recorded per spec_revision, a repost that LOOSENS a gate automatically re-closes the frontier approval gate until the operator re-confirms — so you can never silently auto-merge by flipping a flag mid-flight, and every posture change is a first-class append-only audit record the next tick re-derives behavior from.
basis: outcome_decompose.py module docstring: 'approval is recorded per spec_revision ... any structural edit (which bumps the revision) re-closes the gate'; outcome_spec.py:382-395 bump_revision appends append-only decision_trail; grounding brief §7 pattern 6: 'operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses'. Engages derived-on-read: posture change bumps the revision, node status stays derived each tick.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome.py (new `repost` verb), outcome_spec.py (atomic intent mutation with validate-then-bump), SKILL.md verb table, and release surfaces. Verified by tests/test_outcome_spec.py cases asserting a rejected repost leaves spec_revision/decision_trail untouched and a gate-loosening repost re-closes frontier approval.

title: `/outcome ingest <owner/repo#N>` — seed the DAG from an existing parent Objective instead of re-authoring it
idea: Add an `ingest` verb that replaces the manual node-drafting step entirely: point it at an existing GitHub parent Objective issue and it seeds the whole starter DAG from that issue's sub-issues. `discover_subissues.py` already fetches the parent + every sub-issue (number, title, state, labels, url, assignees) via GraphQL, but nothing consumes it — `start()` ignores GitHub and stamps the fixed design→build pair. `ingest` maps each open sub-issue to one Node: `subplot_id` from issue number, `title` from issue title, `kind` derived from the SDLC type label (capability/enhancement/defect → code; exploration/context-update/objective → non-code), and `node.github={"issue": ref}` pre-wired so no U8 sub-issue is regenerated for work that already exists. The result is a draft spec routed straight into the U7 R20 approval gate, so a mis-mapped graph is still operator-reviewed before any dispatch.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (h): "outcome_decompose.py (U7) is the real decomposition path — just not at start-time and not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed." discover_subissues.py exists and returns exactly the sub-issue fields needed (number/title/state/labels) but is unwired to outcome.py `start()` (outcome.py:260-274 defaults to `_starter_nodes()` and never reads GitHub). This is the theme's named-missing code path, not a redesign of a working one.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding `ingest_objective()` to outcome.py (or a new `outcome_ingest.py`) that calls discover_subissues.normalize and emits node_dicts, an `ingest` CLI verb + SKILL.md verb-table row, and unit tests asserting kind-from-label mapping and github-ref pre-wiring; verified by a fixture GraphQL payload producing a spec whose nodes 1:1 match the sub-issues and whose frontier is gated pending R20 approval.

title: Auto-derive `depends_on` edges from GitHub blocked-by/tracked-by relationships — remove hand-drawn ordering
idea: The painful manual step in any ingest is drawing the dependency edges; invert it by reading the ordering GitHub already knows. Extend the GraphQL in `discover_subissues.py` to also pull each sub-issue's `trackedIssues`/`trackedInIssues` (task-list references) and timeline `blocked_by`/`blocks` cross-references, then translate those into `depends_on` edges when seeding the DAG. Edges that would form a cycle or a dangling target are dropped-with-report rather than crashing the ingest, because `add_dependency`/`lazy_grow` in outcome_decompose.py already validate-then-bump atomically and reject cycles. What GitHub cannot express (a genuinely implicit ordering) stays a manual edge the operator adds at the same R20 review — so the automation removes the mechanical 80%, not the judgment.
basis: First-principles: `start()`/`_starter_nodes()` seed edges only from the hardcoded design→build pair, and `discover_subissues.GRAPHQL_QUERY` fetches labels/assignees but NOT issue relationships, so an ingested multi-issue Objective lands as N disconnected nodes with zero ordering — every edge would be hand-drawn. GitHub's sub-issue/tracked-issue graph is the authoritative ordering source the operator would otherwise transcribe by eye; reading it is strictly cheaper and less error-prone than re-typing it, and outcome_decompose's atomic cycle-rejecting edge adds make bad derived edges safe to attempt.
outcome_shape: Merged PR extending discover_subissues.GRAPHQL_QUERY with trackedIssues/timeline cross-refs, a pure `edges_from_relationships()` mapper, and integration with the ingest seeder; unit tests asserting a blocked-by pair becomes a `depends_on` edge and a cycle-forming pair is dropped-and-reported; verified against a two-fixture payload (linear chain + a cyclic pair).

title: Capture PR-review + merge/deploy posture once at `start`, as committed intent config every leaf inherits
idea: Today `start(repo_root, outcome_id, objective, ...)` asks nothing — posture is implicit and re-decided per leaf. Remove the per-leaf re-litigation by capturing the two required intent questions exactly once at start and committing them as an `intent` block on the spec (not a status field): `reviews_required: bool` and `merge_deploy: gate|auto`. Every leaf's derived step chain and every autonomous board-sync write then reads this one block, so no leaf ever re-asks and no dispatch silently assumes a posture. Because posture is authoring-time declared config (a sibling of `nodes`/`objective`, revision-bumped like any structural edit), it does NOT violate derived-on-read — that rule governs live status, and the `never-autonomous merge/deploy` allowlist in SKILL.md still holds regardless of what `auto` selects downstream of the human keystroke.
basis: Intake brief §3: required intent questions are verbatim "Are PR reviews required for this outcome?" and "Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod?" … "operator decides per outcome, once, at start." outcome.py `start()` (:244-267) takes only `objective` and has no intent parameter or spec field; OutcomeSpec (outcome_spec.py:352-372) carries objective/nodes/decision_trail/cost_rollup but no posture. Engaging the `/outcome`-campaign binding decision (derived-on-read): posture is committed *intent* config, not derived *status*, so it is stored like `objective`, not computed on read.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding an `intent: OutcomeIntent` field to OutcomeSpec.from_dict/to_dict + schema_version bump, an `intent` arg threaded through `start()`, a SKILL.md start-dialog section, and drift-guard/version tests; verified by round-tripping a spec with `{reviews_required, merge_deploy}` through save/load and asserting a non-code leaf's derived chain reads the block.

title: Ask nothing the host already forces — suppress the deploy-gate question when no deploy target exists
idea: The best posture question is the one you never have to answer. When the start-time intent dialog reaches the merge/deploy-gate question, first probe the host: if the backend menu is off (default) and no deploy target/credentials resolve for this repo, the deploy leg is unreachable, so pin `merge_deploy` to `gate` and skip asking — recording the suppression in the decision trail with the reason, never silently. Same for the reviews question if the repo has no PR-review capability wired. This inverts the dialog from 'ask every question' to 'ask only the ones the environment leaves genuinely open,' shrinking start friction while staying auditable.
basis: Binding constraint on this theme (grounding brief §2, `/outcome` campaign row): "backend menu off-by-default with host-conditional degrade." Engaging its revisit/tension with HALT-not-degrade: a *suppressed question whose answer is forced by the host* is a legitimate host-conditional degrade only if it is recorded and surfaced (decision_trail entry), never a silent default — which is why this idea writes the suppression reason rather than defaulting quietly. SKILL.md already classifies merge/deploy as never-autonomous, so pinning to `gate` on an unreachable target is the safe direction.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `probe_host_capabilities()` helper and a `suppressed` list to the intent-capture path that pins forced answers + appends a decision_trail reason; SKILL.md note on host-conditional question suppression; tests asserting a no-deploy-target host yields `merge_deploy=gate` with a recorded suppression and never prompts.

title: `/outcome draft` — turn a raw brainstorm blob into a reviewable node DAG, removing hand-authored node_dicts
idea: outcome_decompose.py assumes the operator already has structured `node_dicts` in hand — `add_node`/`lazy_grow`/`elaborate` all take dicts. The manual step being removed is composing those dicts. Add a `draft` path that takes a small raw input (a pasted spec paragraph, a bullet list, a Slack dump) and, via a single readonly drafter agent, refines it into a candidate node list (subplot_id/title/kind/depends_on) that flows straight into the existing atomic `lazy_grow` + R20 approval machinery. The drafter is a *generator*, never a gatekeeper: it proposes, the operator approves at the unchanged R20 gate, and a bad draft rolls back exactly like any rejected batch. This is the `/plan`+decompose authoring the SKILL says outcome does not own — so it ships as a thin drafting seam that hands structured dicts to decompose, not as decompose logic itself.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md "What `/outcome` does NOT own": "Authoring the graph from scratch — `/plan` + decompose flow (a later unit)." outcome_decompose.py functions (`add_node` :79, `lazy_grow` :120, `elaborate` :177) all require pre-built `node_dict`s — the text→dict step is the confirmed gap. Binding decision `{#external-engines-never-gatekeepers}`: the drafter must be advisory/generator only, satisfied here because output still passes the R20 human approval gate before any dispatch.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `draft` verb wiring a readonly drafter subagent (saga:readonly-verifier-class spawn per CLAUDE.md sandbox rule) whose structured output feeds `lazy_grow`, plus SKILL.md verb row and a test that a raw-text fixture produces node_dicts landing in the gated frontier; verified end-to-end from paste → gated DAG.

title: Derive each leaf's lifecycle step chain from node kind + posture — stop running full /plan→/work→/code-review→/qa on every leaf
idea: The SKILL states every leaf 'runs the usual /plan → /work → /code-review → /qa,' but a non-code exploration or context-update leaf has a different completion contract (no merged PR) and gains nothing from /code-review or a PR-review gate. Remove the fixed chain: derive the step set per leaf from `Node.kind` plus the committed intent posture. A `non-code` leaf resolves to plan→work→(qa if it has verifiable output), skipping code-review; a `code` leaf with `reviews_required=false` drops the review *gate* (still may run advisory review) but keeps merge human-gated. The chain becomes a pure function of (kind, posture), computed on read like every other derived fact — no stored step field.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md line 20: "leaf subplot normal linear saga runs usual `/plan → /work → /code-review → /qa`" — a single fixed chain. outcome_spec.py:54 comment: "A subplot is code-bearing (its completion contract is a merged PR, R11) or non-code" — the contract already differs by kind, so a uniform step chain over-processes non-code leaves. Engaging derived-on-read: the step set is computed from committed kind+intent, never persisted as a status field.

title: `/outcome repost` — change posture mid-run, re-gating pending leaves and HALTing any leaf the change tightens
idea: Posture is captured once at start, but reality shifts (a risky Objective mid-run needs reviews turned on). Rather than force a teardown-and-restart, add a `repost` verb that mutates the committed `intent` block through the same atomic snapshot→validate→bump-revision path decompose uses for structural edits. Because the R20 dispatch gate is keyed per `spec_revision`, bumping the revision automatically re-closes the frontier so newly-stricter posture is re-approved before any further dispatch — the gate machinery already does the hard part. For an already-dispatched leaf whose posture *tightened* (reviews now required on a leaf that dispatched under auto), the tick HALTs that leaf and surfaces it rather than letting it merge under the old posture: HALT-not-degrade, not silent grandfathering.
basis: outcome_decompose.py `make_dispatch_gate`/`approve_frontier` (:337-368): approval is keyed by `spec_revision` and "a structural edit bumps the revision and re-closes the gate." A posture edit reusing `bump_revision` (outcome_spec.py:381) inherits that re-gating for free. Engaging the `/outcome`-campaign HALT-not-degrade binding: a tightened-posture in-flight leaf must HALT-and-surface, not silently continue under the prior posture — the idea's explicit design point.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `repost` verb calling an atomic `set_intent()` on OutcomeSpec (validate→bump), a tick rule that HALTs in-flight leaves whose posture tightened, SKILL.md verb row, and tests asserting revision-bump re-closes the R20 gate and a tightened in-flight leaf HALTs; verified by a two-tick scenario.

title: Read the Objective issue body's acceptance criteria to pre-fill posture + kinds — turning prose into a proposed intent envelope
idea: When ingesting an existing parent Objective, the issue body already encodes intent in prose: a 'Definition of Done' mentioning 'must pass review' implies `reviews_required=true`; 'deploy to nonprod' implies the deploy leg is in scope; acceptance-criteria bullets hint at kinds. Instead of asking the operator every question from a blank slate, parse the Objective body into a *proposed* intent envelope and step-selection defaults, presenting them pre-filled for one-keystroke confirm-or-edit. This removes the cold-start blank dialog while keeping the operator as the deciding authority — the parse is a suggestion the start dialog seeds, never a silently-applied posture.
basis: First-principles: idea T8-F2-1 ingests sub-issues but discards the parent Objective's body text, and idea T8-F2-3 still asks the two posture questions from scratch — yet the Objective body an operator wrote to define the outcome is the highest-signal source of that exact intent. Parsing prose into a *pre-filled, operator-confirmed* envelope strictly dominates a blank dialog: worst case the operator edits it (same cost as answering fresh), best case they confirm in one keystroke. It stays a suggestion feeding the T8-F2-3 dialog, so it neither gatekeeps nor commits posture silently.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a `propose_intent_from_body(objective_body) -> OutcomeIntent` heuristic parser feeding the start/ingest dialog's defaults, SKILL.md note that proposed posture is operator-confirmed, and tests over fixture Objective bodies (review-mentioning vs silent) asserting the proposed envelope and that nothing is applied without confirm.

title: First-class intent envelope on the OutcomeSpec (posture is not implicit)
idea: Today `start(root, outcome_id, objective)` writes only `{outcome_id, objective, nodes}` (outcome.py:262) and `OutcomeSpec.validate` requires only a non-empty objective string (outcome_spec.py:449-450) — the intake's required intent answers (reviews-required, gate-vs-auto merge, gate-vs-auto deploy, spend posture) have literally no home in the canonical spec, so posture is silently re-derived ad hoc every session. Reframe the objective from 'a bare string' to 'a settled intent envelope': add a top-level `intent` block to the spec schema captured by a one-time start-time dialog, committed to the spec on the outcome branch like every other canonical field. The dispatcher and the `advance --autonomous` reversibility envelope read posture from this block instead of re-asking. Because it is a settled input (like `objective`), not a live-computed value, it does not violate derived-on-read — status stays derived; intent is a committed decision, and the schema comment should say so explicitly to pass the campaign's no-writable-status guard.
basis: outcome.py:262 `{"outcome_id": outcome_id, "objective": objective, "nodes": node_dicts}` and outcome_spec.py:449-450 validate only the objective — no posture field exists. Intake tension 3 requires intent settled 'once, start'. Campaign binding (grounding brief section 2) forbids operator-writable STATUS; intent is a settled input not status, engaged in-idea.
outcome_shape: PR touching outcome_spec.py (new `intent` dataclass field + validate + to_dict/from_dict), outcome.py `start` signature + skills/outcome/SKILL.md `start` row + references/outcome-spec.md schema doc; verified by a round-trip test (start writes intent, resume rebuilds it) and a schema drift-guard test asserting intent is read-only-after-start, not a status field.

title: Intent dialog renders blast-radius, not abstract yes/no
idea: The default assumption is that intent capture is a list of yes/no questions answered blind. Reframe one level up: an intent answer is a grant of an autonomy envelope, so the dialog should show the operator exactly what each posture authorizes before they commit. Add `outcome start --preview` that maps each posture answer onto the concrete `advance --autonomous` allowlist (SKILL.md:96-113): reviews-required=no + merge=auto renders 'N code leaves will auto-merge with no human gate'; the ALWAYS_OPERATOR set (merge, deploy, parent-close) renders as permanently-gated regardless of answers. This attacks the default that consent is captured as answers rather than as a previewed, reversibility-classified blast radius — turning the reversibility_certificate from an internal guard into the operator-facing surface of the intent dialog.
basis: SKILL.md:96-113 enumerates the exact authorized-vs-ALWAYS_OPERATOR envelope and cites `reversibility_certificate.authorize_write`; the mapping from posture to this envelope is what the preview renders. Intake tension 3 names the two required questions verbatim.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `--preview` path to outcome.py `start` that renders the posture→envelope table via the existing reversibility certificate, plus a SKILL.md subsection; verified by a snapshot test asserting the preview lists exactly the SKILL.md-enumerated ALWAYS_OPERATOR items as gated under every posture combination.

title: Ingest an existing GitHub parent Objective + sub-issues as a seed DAG
idea: The fixed assumption is that a subplot DAG is always freshly *authored* via /plan + decompose. But a GitHub parent Objective with linked sub-issues is already a latent DAG — mission-control:flow already links `#43 as a sub-issue of #42` and tracks blocked-by relations, and Node already carries a `github` dict (outcome_spec.py:219). Add `outcome ingest <objective-issue-ref>`: read the parent Objective and its sub-issues through outcome_github.py, map each sub-issue to a Node (populating `github.sub_issue`), map GitHub tracked 'blocked-by' / 'depends-on' relationships to `depends_on` edges, and emit a draft spec that enters the SAME R20 approval gate (`approve_frontier`) before anything dispatches. This closes the confirmed gap that `outcome_decompose.py` decomposition 'is not from an existing GitHub Objective — no ingestion path confirmed.'
basis: Grounding brief section 1 correction (h): '/outcome start = 2-node starter DAG, outcome_decompose.py is the real path — just not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' Node.github field at outcome_spec.py:219; approve_frontier at outcome_decompose.py:337-355; mission-control:flow sub-issue linking in skill roster.
outcome_shape: New PR adding `outcome ingest` verb to outcome.py + an ingestion mapper in outcome_github.py (Objective+sub-issues → node_dicts + edges), a SKILL.md verb-table row, and outcome-spec.md provenance note; verified by a test fixture (a mocked parent Objective with three sub-issues and one blocked-by edge) asserting the produced spec passes validate and its frontier requires approval before dispatch.

title: Structural-drift reconcile for ingested outcomes (GitHub as a second structure source, surface-only)
idea: Principle 4 (SKILL.md:39) fixes the ownership boundary: 'committed spec = canonical structure; GitHub = completion; cache holds nothing canonical.' For an outcome INGESTED from a GitHub Objective, that boundary is a choice, not a law — the Objective keeps evolving (sub-issues added/removed on GitHub after ingest). Reframe: extend the existing reconcile loop (#295, SKILL.md:123-155), which already re-reads saga-owned fields and surfaces drift for operator resolution, with a new *structural* drift class that detects added/removed sub-issues on the source Objective and SURFACES them as operator-gated lazy-grow / prune suggestions — never auto-applied. This engages the campaign binding 'committed spec canonical structure' via its revisit condition: canonicality is preserved (the spec still only changes through an operator-approved decompose edit), HALT-not-degrade holds (drift halts that node's ops, never silently degrades), and human-in-the-loop is intact.
basis: SKILL.md:39 (principle 4 canonical-spec boundary) and SKILL.md:123-155 (reconcile re-reads saga-owned fields, surfaces divergence, --resolve applies operator decision, silent unless diverged). Crosses campaign binding 'committed spec canonical structure' — engaged by keeping GitHub structure surface-only + operator-gated, never a silent writer.
outcome_shape: PR extending outcome_reconcile.py with a structural-drift detector for ingested outcomes (diff current source sub-issue set vs ingested node set) that emits lazy-grow/prune suggestions into the existing --resolve surface, plus SKILL.md reconcile-section update; verified by a test where a sub-issue added post-ingest surfaces as a lazy-grow suggestion and is applied only via an explicit --resolve action.

title: Refine a raw brain-dump before falling back to the fixed 2-node starter
idea: `start` unconditionally builds a fixed 2-node DAG regardless of how rich the input is (outcome.py:262) — a one-line objective and a pasted multi-paragraph Slack thread both collapse to the same skeleton, discarding structure the operator already gave. Reframe the 2-node starter from 'the shape' to 'the fallback': when the objective argument is a rich raw dump, route it through a lightweight refinement pass that extracts a crisp objective plus candidate node seeds, scored against the existing outcome-clarity rubric (references/rubrics/spec/core/outcome_clarity.md), and present that as the draft — still entering the R20 approval gate. Only genuinely thin input falls through to the 2-node skeleton. This makes intake input-shape-adaptive instead of one-size-fits-all.
basis: outcome.py:262 builds a fixed 2-node DAG from the objective string with no input-richness branch; the outcome-clarity rubric file exists at plugins/saga/references/rubrics/spec/core/outcome_clarity.md (confirmed by find). R20 approval gate = approve_frontier (outcome_decompose.py:337).
outcome_shape: PR adding an input-richness branch to outcome.py `start` (rich raw text → refinement into objective + seed node_dicts scored by outcome_clarity, else 2-node fallback) + SKILL.md note; verified by two tests — a thin one-liner still yields the 2-node skeleton, a multi-paragraph dump yields >2 approval-gated seed nodes.

title: Derive each leaf's lifecycle step-set from its work shape (uniform /plan→/work→/code-review→/qa is a default, not a law)
idea: The skill fixes that every leaf subplot 'runs the usual /plan → /work → /code-review → /qa' (SKILL.md:20). That uniform chain is a default: a context-update or docs-only leaf has no runtime surface for /qa, an exploration/spike does not need the /code-review merge gate, an ingested defect may skip /plan. Reframe: derive a per-Node `lifecycle_profile` from the leaf's work shape (mission-control's 6-type issue taxonomy — capability / enhancement / defect / exploration / context-update / objective — is already a work-shape classifier available at ingest/draft time) and let the dispatcher hand each leaf the right native-verb chain. The profile is rendered in the R20 approval preview so the operator sees which steps were selected and can override — no gate is ever silently dropped; this is step-selection, not degradation, so HALT-not-degrade is untouched.
basis: SKILL.md:19-23 states every leaf runs the usual /plan→/work→/code-review→/qa on its own branch. Mission-control's 6-type taxonomy (capability/enhancement/defect/exploration/context-update/objective) is documented in mission-control:issues skill + repo CLAUDE.md as an existing work-shape classifier. HALT-not-degrade engaged: profile is operator-visible at approval, gates never silently dropped.
outcome_shape: PR adding a `lifecycle_profile` field to Node (outcome_spec.py) + a shape→profile deriver keyed on issue type, consumed by outcome_dispatcher.py to select the native-verb chain, surfaced in the approval preview + SKILL.md; verified by a test asserting a context-update leaf's profile omits /qa while a capability leaf keeps the full chain, and both remain approval-gated.

title: Repose verb: posture is renegotiable at a revision boundary, not frozen at start
idea: Intake tension 3 settles posture 'once, at start' — a deliberate guard against re-asking every tick. But 'frozen forever' and 'asked every tick' are not the only options; 'once' is a choice the harness can widen safely. Reframe: model a posture change as an explicit operator verb `outcome repose <id>` that mutates the committed intent block, bumps `spec_revision`, re-closes the R20 dispatch gate exactly like a structural graph edit, and appends to the decision_trail (outcome_decompose.py:337-368 already makes approval consumed by a revision bump). This engages the 'asked once at start' binding through its own logic: the runner still never auto-re-asks — renegotiation is operator-initiated only, and it inherits the exact safety net (re-approval before the new frontier dispatches) that already governs mid-flight graph edits. Attended runs re-preview blast-radius (idea T8-F3-2) before the repose commits.
basis: Intake tension 3: intent settled 'once, start' (the binding this crosses). outcome_decompose.py:337-368: approval is per spec_revision and consumed by a structural edit's revision bump — the exact re-gate mechanism reused here. Revisit engaged: never auto-re-asks; operator-initiated, re-approval-gated like R33 edits.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `outcome repose` verb to outcome.py that edits the intent block, bumps spec_revision, and re-closes the dispatch gate via approve_frontier, plus SKILL.md verb-table row + decision_trail entry; verified by a test asserting a repose re-closes the frontier gate (no dispatch until re-approval) and records the posture change in the decision trail.

title: A HALT is a latent renegotiation point, not just a dead stop
idea: HALT-not-degrade means a leaf that hits an unsatisfiable barrier or a gate the current posture cannot clear stops and pages the operator (SKILL.md principle 3: paged only on gates, unsatisfiable barriers, ambiguity, parent-close). The fixed framing is that a HALT is a terminal 'stuck' signal. Reframe one level up: many HALTs are caused by the start-time posture being wrong for this branch of the graph (e.g. a leaf needs an auto-merge the operator gated globally). So when a leaf HALTs, offer a *scoped* posture amendment as one of the ranked resolution options in the attention consolidator — never auto-applied, always an explicit keystroke routed through `repose`. This keeps HALT-not-degrade intact (nothing silently proceeds at lower quality) while turning a class of dead-stops into a one-line decision, closing the loop between the halt surface and the intent envelope.
basis: First-principles: HALT-not-degrade forbids silent lower-quality continuation but says nothing about *offering the operator a scoped, explicit posture change* at the halt — that is still a deliberate human decision, which the constraint permits. SKILL.md principle 3 enumerates the halt causes (gates/unsatisfiable barriers/ambiguity/parent-close); a posture-caused gate halt is resolvable by an explicit scoped repose, not by degrading. The argument: a global posture answer cannot be right for every branch, so binding it globally guarantees avoidable halts.
outcome_shape: PR extending the attention consolidator / halt-surface in outcome_orchestrator.py to attach a scoped-repose resolution option to posture-caused gate halts (routed through the repose seam, operator-keystroke only), plus SKILL.md interaction-method note; verified by a test where a leaf gated by global posture surfaces a scoped-repose option and does not proceed until the operator selects it.

title: IntentEnvelope: a single committed posture primitive every consumer derives from
idea: Today `start()` takes only an `objective` string and `_starter_nodes()` hard-codes a 2-node design->build DAG with no home for the intake's required intent questions (PR-review-required? gate-or-auto merge/deploy? time-vs-money posture?). Introduce one `IntentEnvelope` dataclass on `OutcomeSpec` (`outcome.intent`), captured ONCE at start and committed to the branch spec as authoring-time config (not a status field, so derived-on-read is untouched). Make it the SHARED source of truth: Node defaults for `gated`, `degrade_policy`, and backend eligibility derive from the envelope rather than being re-decided per node. The compounding win is one schema that step-selection (T8-F4-3), renegotiation (T8-F4-5), and even leaf-saga defaults all read, so future posture knobs land in one place instead of scattering across the Node fields.
basis: outcome.py:270-274 `_starter_nodes()` returns only design+build with no posture; SKILL.md:53 intent questions have no capture home; intake brief §3 lists required questions 'Are PR reviews required outcome?' / 'Gate or auto merge/deploy-to-nonprod?' asked once at start. Engages U1-U11 derived-on-read constraint: intent is committed authoring-time config like `Node.state` declared value, never an operator-writable live-status field.
outcome_shape: PR adds `IntentEnvelope` dataclass + `intent` field to plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_spec.py (round-trip to_dict/from_dict), wires capture into outcome.py `start()`, documents the intent gate in outcome/SKILL.md. Verified by a round-trip test and a test asserting Node `gated`/`degrade_policy` defaults derive from the envelope.

title: GitHub Objective -> DAG seed ingestor riding the existing nodes= seam
idea: `start()` already accepts an optional `nodes=` list, but nothing produces one from an existing parent Objective and its sub-issues — grounding §1(h) confirms no ingestion path exists. Add `outcome_ingest.py` that reads a parent Objective issue plus its linked sub-issues through the `outcome_github` seam and emits a starter node-dict list: each sub-issue becomes a node, `kind` inferred from labels (capability/defect->code, context-update/exploration->non-code), and `depends_on` edges derived from sub-issue 'blocked-by' links or task-list ordering. It plugs straight into the existing `nodes=` parameter, so no new dispatch machinery is needed. Compounding: every mission-control Objective already carries the sub-issue graph, so this turns months of manually-linked backlog into a one-command DAG and makes the whole /outcome layer reachable from existing SDLC artifacts.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (h): '/outcome start = 2-node starter DAG ... not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' outcome.py:248,260 shows `start(nodes=...)` accepts a caller-supplied node list that defaults to `_starter_nodes()` only when None — the injection seam already exists.
outcome_shape: PR adds plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_ingest.py + `outcome.py start --from-objective <repo#N>` wiring through the existing nodes= param, plus outcome/SKILL.md surface note. Verified by a fixture Objective with 3 sub-issues (one blocked-by edge) producing a validated 3-node DAG with the correct single edge.

title: Lifecycle step-profile registry: input shape -> which steps a leaf runs, as data not code
idea: Every leaf runs the fixed `/plan -> /work -> /code-review -> /qa` regardless of shape (SKILL.md:20), so a doc-only or already-planned leaf still pays for a full ladder. Add a declarative `step_profiles` registry (a JSON table beside `execution_spec.py`) mapping input-shape signals — `kind=non-code`, has-existing-plan, risk flags, PR-review-required from the IntentEnvelope — to an ordered SUBSET of lifecycle steps, and derive a `step_profile` per node on read. Because the tuples are ordered escalation ladders, a lighter profile is a prefix of the full one, never an arbitrary set. Compounding: the same registry is consumed by both /work and /outcome dispatch, and adding a new profile (e.g. 'hotfix: work->qa') is a data edit, not a code change — the future cheapening is a one-line registry row.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:20 'A leaf subplot is a normal linear saga that runs the usual /plan → /work → /code-review → /qa' — fixed ladder, no shape-derived selection. Engages binding decision {#tier-vocab-ordering}: profiles are ordered escalation ladders (each lighter profile a prefix of the full ladder), honoring the 'ordered, not just closed sets' constraint rather than treating steps as an unordered menu.
outcome_shape: PR adds a step-profile registry (JSON) + resolver in plugins/saga/scripts/, a derived `step_profile` on the outcome Node, and SKILL.md docs. Verified by resolver unit tests mapping each input-shape fixture to its expected ordered step list, including a prefix-ladder assertion.

title: Raw-paragraph refiner that compiles prose into draft nodes through the existing R20 approval gate
idea: An operator pastes a paragraph ('ship auth v2: schema, endpoints, migration, docs') and wants structure without hand-authoring node-dicts. Add a refiner entrypoint that compiles the prose into draft node-dicts, then routes them through the ALREADY-BUILT decompose path — `add_node`/`lazy_grow` under `validate()` plus `approve_frontier` — so nothing dispatches until the operator approves the drafted frontier (R20). The refiner is just another `nodes=` producer; the safety net is reused, not rebuilt. Compounding: the same refinement primitive backs objective-ingestion (T8-F4-2) and any future raw-input source, and a malformed LLM draft fails `validate()` at the source before any dispatch, inheriting the mis-drafted-graph safety net for free.

The refiner reuses this exact gate rather than adding a parallel one. Slug/validate guard at outcome_spec.py:245-248 already rejects a mis-drafted LLM-authored id before dispatch.
outcome_shape: PR adds a refine entrypoint in plugins/saga/scripts/ that emits node-dicts consumed by outcome_decompose.add_node/lazy_grow + approve_frontier, with an outcome/SKILL.md usage note. Verified by a test feeding malformed refined output and asserting it fails validate() and never records a dispatch.

title: Posture renegotiation riding the spec_revision re-approval rails already built for graph edits
idea: Operators need to change posture during a run — flip auto-merge to gated, tighten a degrade policy — but there is no mechanism today. Rather than build new gating, treat a posture change as a spec facet edit that bumps `spec_revision` and RE-CLOSES the dispatch gate exactly like a structural edit: undispatched leaves pick up the new posture, in-flight leaves are untouched (the same state-aware rule that governs `elaborate`/`prune`). This is pure F4 leverage — the graph-versioning + R20 re-approval machinery already exists; renegotiation just becomes another producer of a revision bump. Compounding: any future posture knob added to the IntentEnvelope automatically inherits the re-approval discipline with zero new gating code.
basis: outcome_decompose.py:19-22 / 337-368: 'approval recorded per spec_revision, any structural edit bumps revision re-closes gate until new frontier's edges re-approved' and the state-aware in-flight rule (`_IN_FLIGHT = frozenset({'dispatched'})`, line 47). Renegotiation reuses `bump_revision` + `approve_frontier`. Engages U1-U11 HALT-not-degrade: an in-flight leaf under a posture change is HALTED for operator re-approval, never silently degraded to the new posture mid-flight.

title: Start-time host capability probe: enabled-backend set captured once, HALT on absence
idea: The constraint is 'backend menu off-by-default with host-conditional degrade,' and SKILL.md:84-86 notes the backends (team-execution, cc-workflows-ultracode, /goal, ...) are 'wired in later units.' Probe host capability ONCE at intent time — which backends this host can actually reach — and record the enabled set in the IntentEnvelope, off-by-default until the probe confirms availability. The dispatcher reads that set instead of re-probing per tick. Critically, if a leaf's declared backend is not in the enabled set, the tick HALTs and pages rather than silently degrading to inline (HALT-not-degrade). Compounding: one probe result is reused across every dispatch across the whole run and every resume, and the enabled-backend registry becomes the single seam future backends register into.
basis: outcome/SKILL.md:84-86 'execution backends ... are wired in later units; the dispatch seam and the reconcile loop are the contract.' Binding decision /outcome campaign (U1-U11): 'backend menu off-by-default with host-conditional degrade' and 'HALT-not-degrade' — this idea makes both concrete at intent-capture time (menu off until probe enables; HALT on unavailable declared backend rather than silent inline fallback).

title: Ingestion provenance stamps that make reconcile and board-sync fire for free
idea: Objective ingestion (T8-F4-2) can do more than seed structure: if each ingested node stamps `node.github = {repo, issue, sub_issue}` at seed time, the ALREADY-BUILT reconcile-on-wake loop (#295) and the autonomous board-sync envelope automatically track those issues with zero extra wiring — external closes get detected, Status fields get moved, progress comments get coalesced. This is the second-order F4 payoff: ingestion is not just a convenience, it wires the provenance that turns saga's existing board-sync machinery from theoretical to end-to-end for real backlog. Compounding: the same github-stamp contract also lets a lazy-grown node later mint its own tracking sub-issue through the same field shape, closing the ingest<->emit loop.

Composes with T8-F4-2 but is a distinct provenance-wiring artifact. Honors derived-on-read: stamps are structural provenance, not a live-status field.

title: BOM-explosion ingestion: parent Objective + sub-issues to a routed DAG seed
idea: Manufacturing MRP 'explodes' a Bill of Materials (parent assembly + child parts) and then applies a routing that defines part precedence; a flat parts list without routing cannot be scheduled. Today discover_subissues.py already fetches a parent GitHub issue plus its sub-issues via GraphQL, but returns a FLAT node list with zero dependency edges (a BOM with no routing) and is wired into nothing. Build outcome_ingest.py + a `start --from-objective <repo#num>` path that maps each sub-issue to an OutcomeSpec Node, then runs a routing-inference pass that parses issue-body 'blocked by #N' / 'depends on #N' and label-tier ordering into drafted depends_on edges. The drafted edges never auto-dispatch: they land as a spec_revision that must clear the existing R20 approve_frontier gate (decompose.py:337), exactly the mis-drafted-graph safety net.
basis: discover_subissues.py fetches parent+subIssues(first:50) as a flat list (GRAPHQL_QUERY, lines 11-32) with no edge data; grounding brief §1 correction (h): '/outcome start = 2-node starter DAG... not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' start() defaults to _starter_nodes() (outcome.py:260,270-274). The R20 gate that would guard the draft already exists: decompose.approve_frontier (outcome_decompose.py:337).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_ingest.py + a `start --from-objective` branch in outcome.py, a section in references/outcome-spec.md, and tests/test_outcome_ingest.py that ingests a fixture parent-with-subissues payload and asserts (a) one Node per sub-issue, (b) inferred depends_on edges from a 'blocked by' body, (c) the seed is gated, not dispatched. Verified by pytest + a manual `start --from-objective` dry-run printing the drafted Mermaid graph.

title: Goods-receipt reconciliation: ingesting an already-in-flight Objective idempotently
idea: A warehouse goods-receipt process reconciles a packing manifest (what was ordered) against goods actually received (some already delivered) using a three-way match, so it never re-orders what has already arrived. An Objective ingested today is rarely greenfield: some sub-issues are closed, some have open PRs. Naive ingestion would seed every node as `pending` and resurrect completed work. Instead, ingestion should seed structure from the spec but derive each node's INITIAL live state from GitHub reality at ingest time (closed sub-issue -> done, open+linked-PR -> in-flight) by reusing the outcome_github harvest, honoring the derived-on-read binding rather than writing a status field. Re-ingesting the same Objective is then idempotent: arrived goods are not re-scheduled.
basis: Binding decision '/outcome campaign (U1-U11)': 'Derived-on-read status, never committed status fields' (grounding brief §2). discover_subissues.py already returns each sub-issue's `state` (open/closed) in normalize() (lines 63-90), so the reconciliation input exists but is discarded. Node.state defaults to 'pending' (outcome_spec.py:203) regardless of GitHub truth.
outcome_shape: PR extending outcome_ingest to pass sub-issue state through a state-derivation function (closed->done, open->pending/in-flight per PR link) feeding the existing derive_states path, plus tests/test_outcome_ingest_reconcile.py asserting a closed sub-issue ingests as derived `done` and a second ingest is a no-op. Verified by pytest on fixtures covering closed / open / open-with-PR.

title: Filed flight plan: a one-time intent envelope that governs the whole run
idea: In air-traffic control a pilot files a flight plan and receives clearance ONCE before pushback; the plan then governs the entire flight and is read at every handoff but never re-negotiated ad hoc. `/outcome start` today takes only a free-text objective string and asks nothing, yet the intake brief mandates required intent questions ('Are PR reviews required?', 'Gate or auto-merge/deploy?', spend posture) answered once per run. Add a persisted `intent` block to OutcomeSpec capturing those answers at start as the run's filed flight plan, read on every reconcile tick (does this leaf's completion contract require a review? may this leaf auto-merge?) but never re-asked. HALT-not-degrade governs the dialog itself: an unanswered mandatory posture question HALTs start rather than silently defaulting to a permissive value.
basis: Intake brief tension 3: 'Required intent questions: Are PR reviews required outcome? Gate or auto merge/deploy-to-nonprod?... operator decides per outcome, once, start.' start() signature (outcome.py:244-267) accepts only objective:str with no posture capture; Node carries per-node gated/risky flags (outcome_spec.py:205-207) but there is no outcome-level intent envelope. HALT-not-degrade is a binding '/outcome campaign' constraint (grounding §2).
outcome_shape: PR adding an `intent` dataclass to outcome_spec.py (reviews_required, merge_posture, deploy_posture) with round-trip from_dict/to_dict, a start-time dialog in the outcome SKILL/outcome.py, and tests asserting (a) schema round-trip stability, (b) start HALTs when merge_posture is absent. Verified by pytest round-trip + a HALT-on-missing-posture test.

title: ER triage acuity: input shape derives which lifecycle steps run
idea: Emergency-department triage scores each arrival's acuity (e.g. the five-level Emergency Severity Index) and that score selects the pathway and resources: chest pain gets the full cardiac protocol, a sprain gets fast-track with steps deliberately skipped. `/outcome` today has only NODE_KINDS = ('code','non-code') and nothing consumes kind to decide which lifecycle steps a leaf runs; every leaf implicitly implies the full plan->work->review->qa. Add a derived `step_profile` function keyed on kind + labels: a code leaf -> plan/work/code-review/qa; a non-code doc leaf -> skip qa; a hotfix-labeled leaf -> work/review only. Derived on read (never stored), so re-classifying a node when its labels change is automatic, matching the derived-on-read binding.
basis: outcome_spec.py:56 NODE_KINDS = ('code','non-code') with the only consumer being validate() (line 249) — no step-selection logic anywhere. SKILL.md:20-23 states a leaf 'runs the usual /plan -> /work -> /code-review -> /qa' uniformly with no per-node step subset. Derived-on-read is a binding '/outcome campaign' constraint (grounding §2).
outcome_shape: PR adding a step_profile derivation to outcome_spec.py (or a small outcome_steps.py), a mapping table in references/outcome-spec.md, and tests/test_step_profile.py mapping fixtures (code, non-code doc, hotfix-labeled) to expected step sets. Verified by pytest over the fixture matrix.

title: Morphogenesis: a raw one-liner differentiates into a coarse skeleton, then elaborates on evidence
idea: In developmental biology a single cell does not receive a top-down blueprint; it progressively differentiates via staged commitment, a coarse body plan forming first (gastrulation) and fine structure emerging later as signaling gradients arrive. Structure is never fully specified up front. `/outcome` already has the two lazy mechanisms for this (lazy_grow appends a later layer 'as evidence arrives', elaborate splits an oversized undispatched node in place) but no FRONT DOOR that turns a raw one-line objective into the first coarse skeleton. Add a `refine` step: a raw string -> an LLM-drafted 2-4 milestone gastrula skeleton -> operator approval via the R20 gate -> each milestone then lazily elaborates as its predecessor's evidence lands. The refinement ladder makes the existing growth machinery reachable from unstructured intent.
basis: decompose.lazy_grow docstring: 'Append a later layer as evidence arrives (R21 lazy growth)' (outcome_decompose.py:120-124); elaborate splits an undispatched node in place (lines 177-196); both are gated by approve_frontier (line 337). Yet start() only accepts free text and drops to the hardcoded _starter_nodes() (outcome.py:260,270-274) — no raw-text refinement path feeds these mechanisms.
outcome_shape: PR adding an `outcome refine <id>` verb (draft coarse milestones from the objective string, land as a gated spec_revision via approve_frontier) + a 'differentiation ladder' section in the outcome SKILL, and a test asserting a raw string produces a validated coarse skeleton that stays gated until approved. Verified by pytest + a dry-run showing the drafted milestone graph.

title: Raft joint consensus: an overlap-safe mid-run posture amendment
idea: Raft never swaps cluster configuration atomically; a membership change transitions through a joint (old+new) consensus so the system is never split-brain, and no decision is ever made under two conflicting configs. Mid-run posture change in `/outcome` (operator flips auto-merge -> gate-merge, or raises the review requirement, halfway through) has the same hazard: a leaf already dispatched under the old posture must not be retroactively re-judged. Model a posture amendment as a versioned bump of the intent envelope (an `intent_revision`, mirroring spec_revision's re-close-the-gate pattern) that applies ONLY to not-yet-committed leaves; in-flight leaves finish under the posture they were dispatched with (the joint-consensus overlap window). HALT-not-degrade: if an amendment would strand an in-flight irreversible op (a merge already authorized), HALT and surface rather than silently applying.
basis: Raft joint consensus for configuration change — Ongaro & Ousterhout, 'In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm' (ATC '14), §6 'Cluster membership changes', where the two-phase C_old,new overlap prevents two disjoint majorities. The re-close-the-gate mechanism to mirror already exists locally: approve_frontier is 'keyed by revision, consumed by the next structural edit' (outcome_decompose.py:337-350).
outcome_shape: PR adding intent_revision to OutcomeSpec + an `outcome intent-amend <id>` verb and a pre-dispatch check that reads the intent_revision effective at dispatch time, with tests/test_intent_amend.py asserting an in-flight leaf keeps its dispatch-time posture while a pending leaf picks up the amended one, and that an amendment stranding an authorized merge HALTs. Verified by pytest over the overlap and HALT cases.

title: Pre-authorized credit line: a spend envelope set once, step-up auth on overage
idea: A payment card carries a pre-authorized limit set once; transactions under it clear silently, but a charge that would exceed it (or a flagged category) triggers step-up authentication before it clears. The intake brief's asymmetric approval rule wants exactly this shape: capture a spend posture once at run start, then let cache-tight dispatches proceed silently while any spend-increasing choice (tier escalation, parallel fan-out) requires an explicit operator yes. Encode a spend-envelope block in the start-time intent (a tier ceiling + a per-tick or per-run cost ceiling); the outcome_dispatcher checks each ready leaf's projected dispatch against it, clearing silently when under and HALTing for step-up authorization when a dispatch would escalate tier or exceed the ceiling. The cost ledger (a binding leaf-produced fact) is the transaction log the check reads against.
basis: Intake brief tension 1: unattended -> 'cache-tight serial; may proceed silently'; attended -> 'any spend-increasing choice (parallel fan-out, cache churn, tier escalation) always requires explicit operator yes... Asked once per run start.' Binding '/outcome campaign': 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (grounding §2). outcome_costs.py exists (cost rollup) but no start-time ceiling gates dispatch; start() captures no posture (outcome.py:244-267).
outcome_shape: PR adding a spend_envelope to the intent block + a pre-dispatch authorization check in outcome_dispatcher.py that reads outcome_costs, with tests asserting an under-ceiling dispatch clears silently and a tier-escalating / over-ceiling dispatch HALTs with a step-up prompt (never silent degrade). Verified by pytest over under/over/escalate cases.

title: Committed intent block on the spec, captured once (zero-operator default flip)
idea: Flip the operator to zero: imagine /outcome start asked NO questions and every posture (PR-reviews-required, merge-gate, deploy-gate, spend posture) was inferred from repo defaults. Mining the kernel: today start() takes only a free-text objective and the spec carries no posture at all, so the intake's mandatory intent questions have nowhere to live.
