Add a typed `intent` object to outcome_spec.OutcomeSpec (reviews_required, merge_gate, deploy_gate, spend_posture) validated like `objective`, populated once at start via a single confirm-or-edit surface with mode-based defaults (unattended->cache-tight, attended->ask on spend-increasing choices). Because it is committed spec structure and not a derived status field, it survives cache wipe and rides R26/R27 durability. This is the anchor the other T8 ideas attach to.
basis: outcome.py:244-262 start() accepts only (outcome_id, objective, nodes) — no posture; grep of outcome_spec.py returns zero intent/posture/reviews_required/merge fields. Intake brief lines 53-54 name the mandatory intent questions ('Are PR reviews required outcome?' / 'Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod?') with 'operator decides per outcome, once, start' — a captured-but-unhoused requirement. Engages derived-on-read: intent is committed config (like objective), NOT a derived status field, so no contradiction.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_spec.py (new Intent dataclass + validate + to_dict/from_dict), outcome.py start(), skills/outcome/SKILL.md (start verb row), references/outcome-spec.md field table; verified by a new tests/ round-trip test asserting intent survives save->load->resume and by CHANGELOG/plugin.json/marketplace.json version bump per CLAUDE.md step 6.

title: start --from-objective: 100 existing sub-issues self-seed the DAG (self-executing-issue flip)
idea: Flip 'every issue self-executing' to the extreme: point /outcome at an existing GitHub parent Objective with 100 linked sub-issues and have all 100 become leaf nodes with zero re-authoring. Mining the kernel below the unrealistic 100: build outcome_ingest.py that reads a parent Objective + its sub-issue list (via the mission-control sub-issue-link primitive), emits node_dicts (subplot_id from issue number, kind inferred from issue type label — capability/enhancement/defect -> code, exploration/context-update -> non-code), and hands them to start() as the seed graph instead of the 2-node starter. This is the ingestion path the grounding brief flags as nonexistent. After the one-time seed the committed spec is canonical (R26) and sub-issues remain generated-from/synced-to spec — no ongoing bidirectional authority.
basis: Grounding brief line 30: '(h) NUANCE: outcome_decompose.py (U7) is the real decomposition path — just not at start-time and not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' SKILL.md:168 lists 'Filing SDLC issues (mission-control)' as out-of-scope, confirming the seam is a bridge not a merge. Engages binding R26 (spec is structural source of truth): ingestion produces the canonical spec once, sub-issues stay generated-from-spec afterward, so no derived-status or dual-authority violation.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/outcome_ingest.py + `start --from-objective <owner/repo#N>` arg in outcome.py + SKILL.md verb doc; verified by an offline test feeding a captured GitHub sub-issue-list fixture and asserting the emitted spec validates and node count == sub-issue count, plus release-surface bump.

title: Fully-autonomous edge inference: sub-issue cross-references become depends_on edges
idea: Flip to fully-autonomous topology: imagine the operator draws ZERO edges and the DAG's dependency structure is inferred entirely from what sub-issues already say. Mining the kernel: sub-issue bodies routinely contain 'depends on #123' / 'blocked by #456' / task-list references; an edge-extraction pass over ingested sub-issues (companion to T8-F6-2) turns those into depends_on edges, then validate() catches cycles/dangling exactly as it does for authored graphs. Because validate is dispatch-state-blind and atomic, a bad inferred edge simply fails the seed rather than corrupting anything. Operator still reviews the drafted graph at the R20 approval gate before any dispatch — inference proposes, the gate disposes.
basis: External prior art: the mission-control `flow` skill already owns the sub-issue parent/child link primitive ('Link #43 as a sub-issue of #42') and card-body validation (card_validator.py), living in plugins/mission-control — the reverse read (extracting existing links/refs) reuses that same relationship graph rather than inventing one. Engages R20: inferred edges enter as a *drafted* frontier requiring operator approval before dispatch (outcome_decompose.py:329 approval gate), so autonomy is bounded to proposal.
outcome_shape: PR adding an edge-inference function to outcome_ingest.py (regex/ref-extraction over issue bodies -> depends_on) + a --infer-edges flag; verified by a test where a fixture with 'blocked by #X' produces the correct edge and a fixture with a circular ref is rejected by spec.validate().

title: $0 zero-LLM parser: markdown checklist/headings -> node draft, HALT on ambiguity
idea: Flip the refinement budget to $0: no model call is allowed to turn a raw paragraph into structure. Mining the kernel: a small raw input (a pasted markdown checklist, a heading tree, a numbered list) already encodes latent nodes and often latent order; a deterministic parser lifts '- [ ] item' / '## heading' into candidate node_dicts with no LLM, and when the input is genuinely ambiguous (prose with no list structure) it HALTs and surfaces 'I cannot structure this deterministically — decompose via /plan' rather than degrading to a hallucinated guess. This makes the cheapest, safest ingestion path the default and reserves the model spend for genuinely unstructured prose, aligning start-time capture with the campaign's HALT-not-degrade posture.
basis: First-principles: the campaign mandates HALT-not-degrade, so the correct failure mode for structuring is refusal, not a plausible fabrication. A deterministic parser has exactly two outcomes — confident lift or explicit HALT — with no hallucination surface, which is strictly safer AND $0 versus an LLM pass that cannot signal 'I'm unsure' reliably. Markdown checklists/heading trees are already a serialized tree, so extracting them needs no inference; only the ambiguous residue justifies model spend. This makes zero-budget the honest default and model spend the deliberate escalation.
outcome_shape: PR adding a parse_structured_input() to outcome_ingest.py (checklist/heading -> node_dicts, else raise a HALT signal) + a `start --from-notes <file>` path; verified by tests: a checklist fixture yields N nodes, a prose fixture raises the HALT sentinel (no partial spec written).

title: Per-node step profile: input shape picks which lifecycle steps run (all-steps vs 1-step flip)
idea: Flip to both extremes and mine the middle: what if EVERY leaf ran the full /plan->/work->/code-review->/qa ceremony (max cost), versus every leaf running exactly ONE step? Neither is right, which reveals the missing lever: a per-node step_profile derived from node.kind plus the captured intent (T8-F6-1). A code leaf under reviews-required intent -> plan+work+code-review+qa; a non-code leaf -> a lighter work-only or spec-only profile; a doc/context leaf -> author+doc-review. Today `kind` only fixes the completion contract (merged-PR vs closed-issue), not which steps the leaf spends on. Deriving the step set at seed time from (kind x intent) makes ceremony proportional to the work and is itself derived-on-read from committed inputs, never a stored mutable status.
basis: outcome_spec.py:54 — 'A subplot is code-bearing (its completion contract is a merged PR, R11) or non-code' — kind governs the completion contract ONLY. SKILL.md:21-22 states a leaf 'runs the usual /plan -> /work -> /code-review -> /qa' uniformly, with no shape-driven selection. So the step set is currently uniform-by-convention, not derived. Engages derived-on-read: step_profile is a pure function of committed kind+intent, computed on read, not an operator-writable field.
outcome_shape: PR adding derive_step_profile(kind, intent) to outcome_spec.py or a new outcome_steps.py, surfaced in the graph/status card per node; verified by a table-driven test mapping (kind, intent) tuples to expected step sets and a status-card render assertion.

title: Zero-step leaves: an already-merged PR / closed sub-issue seeds as a terminal node
idea: Flip step count to zero: some ingested work is already DONE — a sub-issue closed as completed, a PR already merged before the outcome was framed. Mining the kernel: ingestion (T8-F6-2) should not re-run any lifecycle step on such a node; it should seed it directly as a terminal `done` node so the ready frontier starts already reduced and downstream dependents unblock immediately. The reconcile path already treats a contract-satisfying completed close as the harvester's sanctioned completion, so seeding a terminal node from that same signal is consistent, not a new authority. A `not_planned` close instead seeds nothing (advises prune), preserving the existing drift semantics.
basis: SKILL.md:138-140 — 'a completed close that satisfies a non-code leaf's completion contract is the harvester's sanctioned path and stays silent; a not_planned close ... is drift.' outcome_spec.py TERMINAL_STATES includes 'done' (line ~67 region). So a closed-completed sub-issue already maps to a sanctioned terminal signal; seeding it as a terminal node reuses that contract rather than inventing status. Engages derived-on-read: the node seeds with its completion as an event/contract fact, not an operator-written status scalar.
outcome_shape: PR extending outcome_ingest.py to classify closed sub-issues (completed->seed terminal node with a completion event; not_planned->skip+advise prune) + a test asserting a closed-completed fixture yields a done leaf that does not enter the dispatch frontier.

title: outcome intent set: renegotiate posture mid-run, atomic revision bump + R20 re-gate
idea: Flip 'posture is immutable once set' to 'renegotiable at any tick': mid-run the operator realizes reviews should now be required, or spend posture should tighten. Mining the kernel: an `outcome intent set <field> <value>` verb mutates the committed intent block through the exact atomic snapshot->validate->bump_revision->re-close-approval-gate seam that decompose edits already use, so a posture change re-opens the R20 gate for the affected frontier before anything dispatches under the new posture. Crucially, the merge_gate and deploy_gate can only move TOWARD more gating — they can never be renegotiated to autonomous, because PR-merge and deploy are permanently ALWAYS_OPERATOR. This gives live posture control without ever eroding the campaign's never-autonomous invariant.
basis: outcome_decompose.py:20-22 — 'any structural edit bumps revision) re-closes gate until new frontier's edges re-approved' and _commit() (lines 68-71) does validate->bump_revision->trail atomically; approve_frontier records approval per spec_revision (line 337+). Engages the /outcome campaign binding 'PR merge/deploy never autonomous': intent-set explicitly forbids moving merge/deploy toward autonomy (SKILL.md:105-109 classifies parent-close/merge/deploy as ALWAYS_OPERATOR), so the renegotiation lever cannot cross that invariant.
outcome_shape: PR adding set_intent(spec, field, value) to outcome_decompose.py (atomic, revision-bumping, re-gating) + `intent set` CLI verb in outcome.py + SKILL.md verb row; verified by a test asserting the edit bumps spec_revision, re-closes the approval gate, and rejects any merge/deploy->autonomous transition.

title: Capture backend + degrade posture once, host-conditional, HALT when unsatisfiable
idea: Flip the backend menu to 'always fully autonomous, pick anything': imagine start silently chose the richest execution backend (team-execution, ultracode) for every leaf. Mining the kernel against the campaign's own guardrails: capture a backend/degrade posture in the intent block ONCE at start — which backends the operator permits and whether host-conditional degrade is allowed — with the menu OFF by default. At dispatch, if the chosen backend's host prerequisites are absent, the leaf HALTs and surfaces the gap rather than silently degrading, unless the captured posture explicitly permits a one-rung degrade (mirroring the #287 sandbox-degrade axis: an autonomous pre-side-effect leaf may drop one rung; else none). This turns backend selection from an every-dispatch improvisation into a once-captured, HALT-safe posture.
basis: outcome_spec.py:95 — 'an autonomous pre-side-effect leaf may drop one rung; none — no degrade constraint' (the #287 sandbox-capability degrade axis already models bounded degrade). SKILL.md:84-86 lists the backend menu (inline/fork/subagent/team-execution/ultracode/goal/manual) as a dispatch seam wired later with no posture capture. Engages the theme/campaign binding 'backend menu off-by-default with host-conditional degrade' AND 'HALT-not-degrade': default off, degrade only when the captured posture and host both permit, otherwise HALT and surface.
outcome_shape: PR extending the Intent dataclass (T8-F6-1) with backends_permitted + degrade_policy fields, consumed at the dispatch seam in outcome.py/outcome_dispatcher.py to HALT-or-degrade per host check; verified by a test where an unmet host prerequisite HALTs by default and degrades one rung only when posture permits.

title: Standards preflight injected into mission-control:issue drafting
idea: Today an operator drafts an SDLC issue with zero awareness of the context-library standard that governs the work, so issues silently contradict required conventions and the drift is caught only downstream in review. Add a 'standards preflight' step to plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md that fetches the 1.4KB context-library llms.txt whole and injects it into the issue-drafting prompt, then requires the generated body to name the applicable standard (testing/delivery/security) with its authority tier. Because llms.txt is self-describing and byte-tiny, injection is cache-cheap and always current — no vendored copy to rot. Verified by a fixture issue-draft run that asserts the body carries a 'Standards' line resolving to a real llms.txt anchor.
basis: Grounding brief section 4, line 82: 'Absent: pull library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation'. llms.txt confirmed 1.4KB whole-injectable with authority-tiered Core/Standards/Optional sections (read from infiquetra-context-library/llms.txt).
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md (+ a small fetch helper) and its CHANGELOG/plugin.json version bump; verified by a fixture issue-draft test asserting the drafted body cites a resolvable llms.txt anchor.

title: Archetype-scoped standards lens in saga:plan
idea: saga:plan interrogates HOW work gets built but never consults the org standards for the archetype it is planning, so plans omit the testing/security gates the library mandates and /work discovers them late. Add a plan-creation lens that inspects the plan's touched paths, derives the repo archetype, and loads only the matching per-topic context-library README (8-12KB, on demand per the documented consumption shape) — not the whole library — then appends an 'Applicable Standards' section to the plan artifact with each standard tagged by authority tier. This honors the self-describing-index consumption model rather than blob injection. Verified by planning a fixture change under two archetypes and asserting different standards sections resolve.
basis: Grounding brief section 4, lines 82 and 84-85: 'Absent: pull library into ... saga:plan creation' and 'per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md adding the standards lens, plus release-surface bump; verified by a two-archetype fixture plan run asserting archetype-correct standards sections.

title: Fleet-local self-describing standards index (plugins-repo llms.txt)
idea: The plugin fleet has no self-describing map of which org standards each plugin must honor, so an agent editing team-execution has no cheap whole-injectable pointer to the standards that bind it — it must guess or crawl. Mirror the context-library pattern inward: add a ~1-2KB fleet standards-index (llms.txt-shaped) at repo root mapping each of the 8 plugins to its authority-tiered obligations and the exact context-library anchors, plus a context_census-style --check in CI that fails when the index drifts from the actual plugin roster. This extends schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index outward exactly as the theme constraint requires, no new paradigm. Verified by CI: adding a plugin without indexing it fails the census check.
basis: Grounding brief section 4, lines 78-80: 'context_census.py --check (keeps llms.txt honest). org convention is schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index'. context_census.py confirmed to carry scan/check_content_floor machinery reusable for a fleet index.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding /llms.txt (or standards-index.md) at plugins-repo root + a CI job invoking a census --check; verified by a red-then-green test where an unindexed plugin fails CI.

title: Three-way checkable classification field in the standards schema
idea: Enforcement today is all-or-nothing: check_docs.py hard-fails on lint but there is no declared boundary between what a script can mechanically verify, what needs a review lens's judgment, and what is merely advisory — so judgment-class standards either get ignored or get bolted into brittle regex checks that produce false failures. Add a required 'enforcement' enum field (machine-checkable | judgment-checkable | advisory) to the standards schema / section-contract in check_docs.py, so the index self-declares how each standard is enforced; CI hard-fails only machine-checkable, review lenses (saga:code-review, doc-review) pick up judgment-checkable, advisory is surfaced-not-gated. Verified by a schema-validation test that rejects a standard missing the enforcement tag.
basis: First-principles: check_docs.py already runs check_section_contracts (line 334) and check_status_and_authority (line 249) — a self-describing index that does not declare enforcement modality forces every consumer to re-derive whether a rule is CI-gateable, which is precisely why judgment-class rules leak past the machine gate or get faked into brittle regex. A single declared enum makes the split machine-readable and routes each rule to the right locus. No binding decision crossed.
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching context-library scripts/check_docs.py section-contract schema + the standards frontmatter, adding the enforcement enum and a validation branch; verified by a test rejecting an untagged standard.

title: Make mermaid render a non-opt-in CI gate (close the 13-diagram blind spot)
idea: check_docs.py already has check_mermaid (line 203) but it is opt-in behind --mermaid because it spins headless Chrome per block, so CI runs without it and 13 broken diagrams shipped — the plain linter passing says nothing about whether a diagram renders. Close it by adding a fast static mermaid pre-parse (grammar-only, no browser) that runs unconditionally in CI to catch the common breakage classes, keeping the heavy mmdc render as a nightly/opt-in deep pass, and wire the same guard into the plugins repo which itself ships mermaid (redis-channel/ARCHITECTURE.md). Verified by committing a deliberately broken diagram and watching the fast gate fail on the normal CI path.
basis: check_docs.py:203-207 and :433 confirm check_mermaid exists but is opt-in ('--mermaid ... because mmdc spins up headless Chrome per block. The plain doc-linter passing says nothing about whether a diagram renders'); grounding brief axis note '13 broken diagrams shipped past check_docs.py'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR touching context-library scripts/check_docs.py (add fast static mermaid check + always-on CI wiring) and a mirrored guard in the plugins-repo CI; verified by a broken-diagram fixture failing the default CI path.

title: Pagination-exhaustion assertion for mission-control list fetches
idea: mission-control item-list fetches silently truncate at 200 items, so board and metrics reads present a partial picture as complete and operators make decisions on missing cards. Add a shared fetch guard in the mission-control board/flow/metrics scripts that, on any paginated GraphQL/REST fetch, asserts the cursor was exhausted (hasNextPage == false) before returning — and hard-errors, loud, when a page boundary is hit without exhaustion rather than returning the truncated slice. This is the schema-validate-in-CI discipline applied to runtime data completeness. Verified by a mocked >200-item response test asserting the guard raises instead of silently returning 200.
basis: Grounding brief session-mining finding 3, lines 126-128: 'mission-control board/field drift — ... item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 ... (4 repos)'; theme T9 axis names '200-item pagination truncation' explicitly.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a paginate-or-raise helper used across plugins/mission-control/skills/{board,flow,metrics}/scripts, plus a unit test with a mocked >200-item response asserting the raise; release-surface bump.

title: Live-vs-assumed project field/option schema drift guard
idea: mission-control assumes project fields and option aliases that no longer exist (hardcoded aliases, nonexistent fields), so field-set operations fail mid-flow or write to the wrong field. Vendor a project-schema snapshot (fields + option ids per board) and add a CI/preflight check that diffs the assumed schema baked into mission-control against a live GraphQL field-discovery pull, failing when an assumed field or option alias has drifted — the same self-describing-index-plus-CI-validate pattern the context library already uses for docs, applied to board schema. Verified by mutating the snapshot to reference a stale field and watching the drift check fail.
basis: Grounding brief session-mining finding 3, lines 126-128: 'mission-control board/field drift — nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases ... create/board-add/field-set racing (4 repos)'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a vendored project-schema snapshot + a drift-check script wired into mission-control preflight/CI; verified by a stale-field fixture failing the check.

title: Authority-model stop-and-surface enforced inside saga/team-execution flows
idea: authority-model.md defines a priority order and an explicit 'stop and surface conflict' rule, but nothing enforces it inside plugin flows — when a plan or team run hits two standards that collide (a required rule vs a recommended one, or a plan step contradicting a required gate), the agent silently picks one and proceeds, defeating the whole authority model. Encode the stop-and-surface as a shared flow primitive: when saga:plan or team-execution detects a standards conflict at the same or ambiguous authority tier, it HALTs and surfaces the conflict to the operator (mirroring the /outcome HALT-not-degrade posture) instead of resolving silently. Verified by a fixture with two colliding standards asserting the flow emits a surfaced-conflict halt rather than a silent choice.
basis: Grounding brief section 4, line 81: 'authority-model.md defines agent priority order incl. "stop surface conflict"'; the /outcome binding decision (section 2, line 48) establishes HALT-not-degrade as the sanctioned posture, so this extends an existing decision rather than crossing it.
outcome_shape: Merged PR adding a stop-and-surface conflict primitive referenced from plugins/saga/skills/plan and team-execution SKILL flows + a references doc; verified by a colliding-standards fixture asserting a surfaced halt.

title: Auto-inject llms.txt at issue and plan creation (remove the go-read-the-standards step)
idea: Today an author must remember to consult the context library before drafting an issue or plan; the manual step is 'go read the standards.' Invert it: the ~1-2KB llms.txt index is fetched and injected automatically at the top of mission-control:issue and saga:plan creation flows, so the standards arrive at the author instead of the author hunting them. The index is whole-injectable by design (1.4KB verified on disk), so cost is trivial and it stays honest via context_census. The author never has to know the library exists; the relevant per-topic READMEs are surfaced as on-demand links from the injected index.
basis: Grounding brief §4: 'Absent: pull library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation' and 'llms.txt (~1-2KB) whole-injectable'; verified on disk llms.txt is 1.4K at ~/workspace/infiquetra/infiquetra-context-library/llms.txt.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/mission-control/skills/issues (creation prompt) and plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md to fetch+inject llms.txt at creation start, plus a drift-guard test asserting the injected index is present and byte-current; verified by the test and by a dry-run issue/plan showing the index block.

title: Standards manifest that splits machine-checkable from judgment-checkable so CI automates the checkable subset
idea: Every standard today is prose a human must interpret; there is no ADR-to-code-pattern lint. Add a standards-manifest.json in the context library tagging each standard with checkable ∈ {machine, judgment, advisory}. F2 automates away human review of the machine-checkable subset: check_docs.py grows a lint pass that enforces exactly those, judgment ones become auto-generated review lenses, advisory ones stay reference-only. This extends the existing schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index convention outward rather than inventing a runtime-injected blob, and it makes the enforcement locus explicit and testable per standard.
basis: Grounding brief §4: 'Absent: any ADR↔code-pattern lint' and org convention is 'schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index'; check_docs.py exists (15.3K) at context-library/scripts/.
outcome_shape: PR adding docs/standards-manifest.json (one row per standard with a checkable field) + a check_docs.py lint pass enforcing machine-checkable rows + test_check_docs.py cases; verified by CI failing a seeded violation of a machine-checkable standard.

title: Validator-coverage census: fail CI when a doc artifact type ships unchecked (kill the mermaid-class blind spot)
idea: The mermaid gap (13 broken diagrams shipped past check_docs.py) was not a missing rule but a missing meta-guarantee: nobody proved every artifact type in the docs had a validator. Invert the discovery order — instead of finding blind spots after breakage, a coverage census enumerates artifact kinds present in the corpus (mermaid fences, tables, code fences, cross-links, front-matter blocks) and fails CI when any kind has no registered validator. This is the context_census self-describing pattern turned on the validators themselves, not on the content. It generalizes beyond the specific mermaid fix (which is already a direct-to-candidate) to guarantee no future artifact type ships silently unchecked.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'mermaid syntax never validated by check_docs.py (13 broken diagrams shipped)'; distinct from the direct-to-candidate mermaid-validator fix — this is a coverage meta-check over validators.
outcome_shape: PR adding a validator-coverage census to scripts/ (registry of artifact-type→validator) wired into validate.yml, with a test proving an unregistered artifact type fails CI; verified by removing a validator registration and seeing red.

title: Machine-readable authority-model priority block so plugins stop re-interpreting prose
idea: authority-model.md encodes the required/recommended/reference priority order and the stop-and-surface rule as prose every agent must re-read and re-interpret. Remove the interpretation step: add a structured priority block (YAML front-matter or a fenced table) to authority-model.md that plugins load and apply deterministically, with context_census --check keeping the prose and the block in lockstep. The human-parse step becomes a lookup. This is the smallest extension of the self-describing-index convention and makes the authority order a value plugins can resolve, not a paragraph they must understand.
basis: Grounding brief §4: 'authority-model.md defines agent priority order incl. "stop surface conflict"'; context_census.py exists (10.8K) and already keeps llms.txt honest.
outcome_shape: PR adding a structured priority block to docs/governance/authority-model.md + a context_census.py check asserting block↔prose consistency + test; verified by census failing when the block and prose disagree.

title: Automated stop-and-surface: plan/issue flows halt when a draft contradicts an injected standard
idea: The authority-model's 'stop and surface conflict' rule currently depends on a human noticing the contradiction. Automate the vigilance: once the standards index is injected (idea 1), saga:plan and mission-control:issue run a lightweight conflict check that halts and surfaces when a draft proposes something contradicting a machine-checkable standard, rather than silently proceeding. It surfaces derived-on-read (no committed conflict state), matching the derive-on-read binding decision — the check recomputes against current standards every run, never persisting a stale verdict. The manual 'did anyone catch this' step disappears; conflicts stop the flow at authoring time, not at review.
basis: Grounding brief §4: authority-model.md 'stop surface conflict' rule + 'Absent ... inside plugin flows'; engages binding decision Derive-on-read (§2 /outcome campaign 'derived-on-read status, never committed status fields') by recomputing per run rather than persisting a conflict flag.
outcome_shape: PR adding a conflict-surfacing lens to plugins/saga/skills/plan and mission-control issue creation that halts+surfaces on a machine-checkable-standard contradiction, with a test driving a contradicting draft to a HALT; verified by the seeded draft stopping the flow.

title: Live-derived board schema census: remove hand-maintained field maps and the 200-item truncation
idea: mission-control drift (nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases, list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items) all stems from hand-maintained assumptions about the board schema. Invert it: derive a board-schema.json snapshot directly from the live GitHub Projects API (fully paginated, no 200 cap) via a board_census.py that mirrors context_census.py, and diff the committed snapshot in CI so any field/alias drift fails the build. The manual step of trusting hardcoded field maps is removed — the schema is regenerated from truth and drift is caught mechanically. This extends the schema-validate-in-CI convention to the board surface without a new plugin.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 3: 'mission-control board/field drift — nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases, item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items'.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/.../board_census.py + a committed board-schema.json + a full-pagination fix + CI diff step; verified by CI failing on a mutated snapshot and by the census returning >200 items on a 375-item board.

title: Generate review lenses from the standards manifest so hand-authored checklists can't drift
idea: saga:code-review and doc-review carry hand-authored review lenses that will drift from the ADRs they are supposed to enforce — the same contract-mirror drift disease that produced 343 falsely-clean cards when validate_card_body went stale. Remove the hand-authored checklist entirely: generate the judgment-checkable review lenses from the standards manifest (idea 2) at build time, so the review lens is always a projection of the current source of truth, never a copy that rots. A drift-guard test asserts the generated lenses match the manifest, killing the copy-drift failure mode at its root.
basis: First-principles: hand-authored review lenses are copies of ADR intent and copies drift from source (grounding brief §3.1 records exactly this failure — stale validate_card_body passed 343 cards a live contract rejected, #222). Generating lenses from the manifest makes the copy structurally impossible, closing the drift loop rather than re-checking it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a lens-generation script that emits review-lens fragments from standards-manifest.json, consumed by saga code-review/doc-review SKILL.md, plus a test asserting generated-lens↔manifest parity; verified by CI failing when a manifest edit is not reflected in the generated lens.

title: Topic-keyed on-demand standards resolver: remove the which-doc-do-I-need decision
idea: The library's consumption shape is a ~1-2KB always-resident index plus 8-12KB per-topic READMEs loaded on demand, but nothing lets a plugin request a topic by key — the author still decides which doc to open. Automate that decision: add a standards_resolve.py that takes a topic key (e.g. issue-taxonomy, board-schema, authority-order) and returns the matching per-topic README, backed by a topic-key field added to llms.txt so the index is the routing table. Plugins request standards by need; the whole-library-injection problem (platform-specs dominates) is avoided because only the keyed topic loads. The manual 'find the right file' step is replaced by a resolver lookup.
basis: Grounding brief §4: 'per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible (platform-specs dominates)' and llms.txt is the self-describing index (1.4K verified on disk).
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/standards_resolve.py (topic-key → README) + a topic-key field in llms.txt + a context_census check that every topic key resolves to an existing README; verified by the census failing on a dangling key and the resolver returning the correct doc for a known key.

title: Standards preflight at issue-authoring time, not just library CI
idea: The theme treats 'enforcement lives in the context-library's own CI' as fixed; the reframe is that the authoring moment is itself an enforcement locus that is currently blind. Wire a standards-preflight step into mission-control:issue (and saga:handoff) that, before an issue body finalizes, whole-injects the ~1-2KB llms.txt index and lazily loads the one relevant per-topic README, then surfaces any binding DECISION whose revisit-when the drafted work would trip (e.g. a body proposing a new plugin surfaces {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}). This is the check_docs.py schema-validate convention pushed outward to the consumer, not a new paradigm. It never blocks reversibly-authored text; it annotates the draft with the standards it must engage.
basis: plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md:68/245/354 route authoring only through a local references/issue-types.md decision tree; grounding brief §4: 'Absent: any pull of the library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation.' No cross-repo boundary or binding decision is tripped (extends existing plugins; proposes no new plugin per {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/scripts/standards_preflight.py + a wire-in edit to skills/issues/SKILL.md + references/standards-preflight.md; verified by a mission-control test asserting a draft mentioning 'new plugin' surfaces the {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} anchor and its revisit-when.

title: Review lenses auto-derived from the binding-decision register
idea: The closed enum of review lenses in saga:code-review / saga:doc-review is treated as hand-authored and fixed; the reframe is that the binding-decision register is a lens generator. Every binding DECISION carrying a revisit-when is mechanically a review lens ('does this diff trip {#worker-cache-scheduling}?'). Generate an adr-lenses manifest from the DECISIONS.md anchors flagged binding, inject it into the judgment-selected lens pool, and add a parity check that the set of binding anchors equals the set of derived lenses so a new binding decision cannot land without its review lens. This extends the self-describing-index convention (context_census.py keeps llms.txt honest) to keep the review surface honest against the ADR set.
basis: docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md:12 defines the '> ### title (hash) {#slug}' + '**Revisit when.**' schema; 95 {#anchor} entries exist with live cross-refs like {#saga-docs-source-model}; grounding brief §2 enumerates 8 binding anchors as an active register but no artifact ties them to review lenses.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/code-review/references/adr-lenses.md (generated) + a generator script + a parity test asserting binding-register anchors == derived lenses; verified by adding a stub binding anchor and watching the parity test go red until the lens is regenerated.

title: llms.json sidecar: make the index a machine-readable consumption contract
idea: The theme treats llms.txt as a passive ~1-2KB prose blob that consumers whole-inject and then load topics on demand by feel. The reframe: the whole-inject-vs-lazy-load boundary is a choice that every consumer currently re-hardcodes. Extend context_census.py to emit an llms.json sidecar (topic -> byte-size -> authority-rank -> load-policy: whole-inject|on-demand|never) so any plugin deterministically decides what to inject rather than guessing, and ship a thin standards_index reader in this repo's shared scripts that plugins call. The index stops being something an agent interprets and becomes a contract it executes.
basis: grounding brief §4: 'llms.txt (~1-2KB) whole-injectable; per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible (platform-specs dominates)' — the load policy is real but implicit; context_census.py --check already owns keeping the index honest, so the sidecar is the same convention with a machine-readable payload. Cross-repo (touches context-library) but crosses no binding decision.
outcome_shape: PR (context-library) adding llms.json emission to context_census.py + (this repo) plugins/_shared/scripts/standards_index.py reader + a test that the reader's whole-inject set stays under a 2KB budget; verified by census --check failing when llms.json drifts from llms.txt.

title: Authority-order as an executable resolver, not trusted prose
idea: authority-model.md's priority order is treated as a doc agents are trusted to follow in-context; the reframe is that read-time precedence is a deterministic function, not a judgment call. Ship an authority_resolve primitive that, given a fact contested across sources (plan artifact vs repo CLAUDE.md vs context-library standard), returns the winning source per the documented order. This makes 'which source is authoritative here' answerable without spending reasoning tokens and gives the conflict-surfacing layer (T9-F3-8) a precise input: the resolver decides precedence, the surfacer decides when disagreement is material enough to HALT. The order table stays the source of truth; the resolver is generated from it and parity-checked.
basis: grounding brief §4: 'authority-model.md defines the agent priority order incl. stop and surface conflict' — the order exists as prose with zero executable form anywhere in the fleet. No binding decision governs read-time precedence.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/_shared/scripts/authority_resolve.py generated from authority-model.md's order + a golden-case test table (repo-override-wins, library-standard-wins, plan-wins) + a parity check that the resolver's order equals the doc's; verified by the golden table.

title: check_journal.py — schema-validate the ADRs themselves
idea: The org convention is schema-validate-in-CI everywhere except its own decision records: DECISIONS.md entries are free prose held together by {#slug} and **Revisit when.** conventions with no validator, so a cited anchor can dangle and a binding decision can ship with no revisit-when. The reframe attacks 'an ADR is human prose, not a validatable artifact.' Mirror check_docs.py with a check_journal.py that lints anchor uniqueness, cited-anchor existence (the 95 anchors reference each other), presence of revisit-when + commit hash for DECISIONS, and requires each entry to self-declare checkable: machine|judgment|advisory. This is the same schema-validate-in-CI pattern, turned on the standards that everything else is validated against.
basis: docs/engineering-journal/DECISIONS.md:3-17 specifies the ADR schema in prose (rationale + tradeoff + revisit-when + commit hash); 95 {#anchor} entries with live cross-refs (e.g. line 221 cites {#saga-docs-source-model}); no validator exists — check_issue_contract_parity.py proves the repo already runs this class of CI gate.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/check_journal.py + a CI job wiring it + a docs/engineering-journal frontmatter schema; verified by intentionally breaking one cross-ref anchor and one missing revisit-when and watching CI go red.

title: Enforcement-coverage classifier: surface binding-but-unenforced decisions
idea: The machine/judgment/advisory split is treated as a property a standard is born with and keeps; the reframe is that it is a migration ladder and that a 'binding' decision with neither a CI checker nor a review lens is advisory-in-disguise. Tag every binding-register anchor with an explicit enforcement field naming its enforcer (a CI check id, a named review lens, or 'operator-judgment'), then run a meta-check that any anchor claiming machine-checkable maps to a real, existing check id — so deleting a checker flips the decision to unenforced-drift and fails CI. The one-time triage of the 8 register decisions produces a ranked backlog of advisory standards ready to climb the ladder to machine-checkable.
basis: First principles: grounding brief §2 lists 8 binding decisions, some annotated 'structurally enforced' and some not, with no field distinguishing an enforced decision from an aspirational one. A decision labeled binding with no checker and no lens is indistinguishable at runtime from advice; only an explicit enforcer field + a coverage meta-check makes the split observable and prevents silent decay when a checker is later removed.
outcome_shape: PR extending the binding-register table (a machine-readable enforcement-registry.yaml) with an enforcement field per anchor + scripts/check_enforcement_coverage.py + a test that a machine-checkable anchor pointing at a nonexistent check id fails; verified by deleting a referenced check id and observing red.

title: Checkable-surface census — guard the blind spot, not just mermaid
idea: 13 broken mermaid diagrams shipped green not because mermaid is special but because check_docs.py's checkable surface was hand-drawn to silently exclude an entire renderable class. The reframe attacks 'green check_docs = sound docs': the real defect is that no inventory exists of embedded renderable/executable content the linter does not validate (mermaid, json fences, yaml frontmatter examples, runnable bash snippets, cross-repo anchor refs). Build a checkable-surface census (mirroring context_census.py's self-describing pattern) that enumerates every embedded content class across docs, marks each validated|unvalidated, and fails CI when a new unvalidated class appears — a drift-guard on the guard itself. This builds past the narrow mermaid candidate to close the meta-blind-spot that let it through.
basis: grounding brief §7 singleton: 'mermaid syntax never validated by check_docs.py (13 broken diagrams shipped).' The direct-to-candidate pool (§8) already holds the narrow mermaid fix; this idea deliberately generalizes to the unenumerated checkable surface, which no seed covers.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/checkable_surface_census.py + a committed checkable-surface.json manifest + CI wire; verified by introducing a novel fenced-block class in a doc and watching the census flag it as unvalidated-drift until it is either validated or explicitly waived.

title: Stop-and-surface as an invokable primitive inside plugin flows
idea: authority-model.md already carries a 'stop and surface conflict' rule, but it lives as prose the agent is trusted to honor and is invisible at the moments conflicts actually occur (plan says X, repo CLAUDE.md says Y, library standard says Z). The reframe: conflict adjudication is not something to leave to in-context judgment — make it a standards_conflict_check primitive that saga:plan and mission-control:issue call, which takes the drafted artifact plus the resolved standards (fed by T9-F3-4) and, on a material conflict, HALTS for operator adjudication rather than letting the agent quietly pick a side. This mirrors the /outcome HALT-not-degrade posture and turns a passive doc rule into wired machinery.
basis: grounding brief §4: 'authority-model.md defines the agent priority order incl. stop and surface conflict' and §4 lists it as absent from any plugin flow. Crosses {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): explicitly engaged — the conflict arbiter is Claude/CI-side, never an external engine, and it surfaces to the operator rather than auto-resolving, so Claude remains verifier-of-record; the decision's revisit-when (read-only-sandbox profile ships) is not required to move.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/_shared/scripts/standards_conflict_check.py + wire-ins to saga:plan/SKILL.md and mission-control:issues/SKILL.md + a HALT-path test asserting a seeded plan-vs-CLAUDE.md conflict halts for operator input instead of silently resolving; verified by the halt test.

title: Library-index-backed validation of the issue 'Context library links' field
idea: mission-control:issue already requires a 'Context library links' field for Hermes readiness but treats it as free text with an `_none_` escape hatch, so the field is a decoration nobody checks. Add a resolver step in the issues skill (and its sdlc_manager validate path) that reads the vendored context-library `llms.txt` index and offers the operator the real topic anchors matching the issue type/target repo, then validates any entered link against that index so a stale or invented path fails card validation. This turns a manual box into a governed injection point: every issue born after it carries a real, resolvable standards pointer. The same resolver is reusable by saga:plan's issue handoff, so one seam feeds two producers.
basis: issues/SKILL.md:83-89 makes 'Context library links' a required Hermes field but says 'use `_none_` when no context applies' (unvalidated free text); grounding brief §4: 'Absent: any pull of the library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation.'
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md + plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py (validate_card_body path) + a new tests/test_context_link_validation.py; verified by a red/green test where an issue body citing a non-index path fails validation and one citing a real llms.txt anchor passes.

title: Vendor the 1.4KB llms.txt as a SHA-pinned artifact on the existing parity registry
idea: The fleet has no offline copy of the standards index, so any plugin flow that wants the whole-injectable ~1.4KB `llms.txt` needs a cross-repo checkout it never does. Vendor `llms.txt` into plugins/mission-control/config/generated/ beside a pinned `.sha256`, and add it to the `VENDORED_ARTIFACTS` tuple in check_issue_contract_parity.py — which by its own design 'extends the gate with no other change.' Now every plugin flow can whole-inject the index at zero cross-repo cost, and CI proves it has not drifted from the source library exactly the way it already proves the issue-contract copies. This is pure leverage: one tuple entry reuses an entire drift-proof mechanism, and it establishes the pattern for vendoring future small standards surfaces (authority priority order, ADR index).
basis: check_issue_contract_parity.py:38-46 'Adding a future vendored artifact here extends the gate with no other change'; measured `wc -c llms.txt` = 1463 bytes (whole-injectable, matches §4's ~1-2KB claim).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/generated/llms.txt + llms.txt.sha256, one line in VENDORED_ARTIFACTS, and a sync note in CLAUDE.md step 6; verified by the existing CI parity job failing on a deliberate one-byte edit and passing on the pinned copy.

title: standards-manifest.json: classify each convention machine/judgment/advisory and route it
idea: Today a context-library convention is either wired into a CI schema check (machine-hard) or invisible to the fleet (nothing enforces it); there is no middle tier for 'a human reviewer should weigh this.' Author a `standards-manifest.json` registry that lists each convention with a `checkability` tag (machine-checkable | judgment-checkable | advisory) and a `locus` pointer, then have two thin consumers read it: CI iterates the machine-checkable rows and asserts each maps to a live check, while saga:/code-review loads the judgment-checkable rows as a review-lens menu. The compounding win is that adding a new standard becomes a single registry row that automatically lands in the right enforcement locus, instead of a hand-wired decision each time. This is the check_docs schema-validate-in-CI convention extended outward: the manifest is itself schema-validated and self-describing.
basis: First-principles: enforcement effectiveness = matching a rule to a locus that can actually judge it. Grounding §4 shows only two loci exist (CI-hard inside the library, or nothing in the fleet); a rule that is judgment-shaped has nowhere to live, so it silently goes unenforced. A checkability-tagged registry is the minimal structure that lets each rule find its correct locus and makes the routing decision reusable rather than re-litigated per rule.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/standards_manifest.json + a schema + scripts/check_standards_manifest.py (asserts every machine-checkable row resolves to a live check) wired into ci.yml validate job; verified by CI failing when a machine-checkable row points at a missing check and by /code-review surfacing the judgment-checkable rows as lenses.

title: Check-coverage meta-guard: fail CI when a registered validator check is never invoked
idea: The 13-broken-diagram escape happened because check_docs.py defines a real `check_mermaid` behind an opt-in `--mermaid` flag that even prints 'skipping mermaid render check' — and CI never passes the flag, so a whole check silently no-ops forever. Rather than just flipping mermaid on (the narrow direct-to-candidate fix), build a class-level meta-guard: a `check_coverage.py` that discovers every `check_*` function a validator module registers and asserts each is actually reachable from the CI invocation, failing when a check is defined-but-dark. Ship it first against this repo's own validators (scripts/validate_plugins.py, marketplace/validator) and make it portable to the library's check_docs. The compounding return: every future opt-in or forgotten check is auto-caught, so the mermaid class of blind spot cannot recur anywhere the guard runs.
basis: check_docs.py:433-444 — `--mermaid` is opt-in and prints 'note: --mermaid requested but mmdc not on PATH; skipping mermaid render check'; validate.yml runs `python3 scripts/check_docs.py` with no `--mermaid`, so check_mermaid is dark. §7 singletons: 'mermaid syntax never validated by check_docs.py (13 broken diagrams shipped).'
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/check_coverage.py + a manifest of expected-invoked checks + ci.yml step; verified by the guard failing on a seeded defined-but-uninvoked check function and passing once it is wired into the CI command line.

title: Pagination-completeness lint over GitHub list-call sites
idea: The python sdlc_manager paginates GraphQL correctly (first:100 + cursor loop), but agent-authored `gh project item-list` calls rely on a manual `--limit`, and the operator doc itself warns the default '--limit of 30 silently truncates' a 400+ item board — the exact mechanism behind the 200-of-375 truncation pattern. Add a `check_pagination.py` drift guard that scans plugin scripts and agent docs for GitHub list calls (`gh project item-list`, `gh api ... items`, `items(first:`) and fails any site lacking either a cursor loop or an explicit `--limit 1000` guard, driven by a small registry of recognized list-call shapes. The leverage is a self-extending call-site registry: every new board/list call is enforced for completeness at author time, so the truncation class stops shipping instead of being caught by an operator noticing missing rows.
basis: plugins/mission-control/agents/sdlc-operator.md:305 'the default --limit of 30 silently truncates'; §7 pattern 3: 'item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items.' sdlc_manager.py:772/906 shows the correct cursor loop exists, proving the drift is between the guarded python path and the unguarded CLI/agent path.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/check_pagination.py + a call-site allowlist/registry + ci.yml lint step; verified by the guard failing on an unguarded `gh project item-list` in an agent doc and passing once a `--limit 1000` or cursor guard is present.

title: authority-conflict: a shared stop-and-surface primitive for plugin flows
idea: The library's authority-model.md defines the agent priority order and a 'stop and surface conflict' rule, but nothing in this fleet actually invokes it — when a plan says X and an ADR says not-X, agents silently pick one. Extract a small reusable `authority_conflict` primitive (a saga/mission-control shared helper) that flows call when they detect an instruction crossing priority tiers: it halts, names both sources and the priority order that governs them, and surfaces the conflict for an operator decision rather than degrading silently. This directly inherits the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade posture, so it aligns with an established binding pattern rather than crossing it. The compounding return is one conflict-surfacing seam reused by /plan, /work, and /code-review, so every lifecycle stage gets consistent conflict behavior for free as new standards arrive.
basis: grounding §4: 'authority-model.md defines the agent priority order incl. "stop and surface conflict"' and 'Absent: any reference to the library from this repo's CI.' Aligns with binding /outcome campaign decision (§2): 'HALT-not-degrade' — this idea reuses that posture rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared scripts/authority_conflict.py (or saga references helper) + wiring one call site in saga:plan's conflict check + tests; verified by a test where a plan/ADR contradiction triggers a HALT+surface envelope instead of a silent pick.

title: Per-topic on-demand standards loader keyed off the llms.txt index
idea: Whole-library injection is infeasible (platform-specs dominates), so the intended shape is: whole-inject the ~1.4KB index, then load one 8-12KB per-topic README on demand — but no helper does the routing, so agents guess paths and drift. Add a thin `standards resolve <context>` helper (hosted in existing mission-control/saga tooling, not a new plugin) that maps a work context (issue type, touched plugin dir, ADR id) to the correct per-topic doc via the vendored llms.txt index and returns only that doc's path/content. To respect the plugin-portfolio-groom binding decision, this ships as a script beside existing skills, carrying no new-plugin footprint. The compounding win: as the library grows new topics, the index update propagates to every consumer automatically, and agents stop hardcoding library paths that go stale.
basis: grounding §4: 'per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible (platform-specs dominates).' Engages binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} (§2, 'new plugin ideas carry a consolidation burden of proof') by hosting the helper inside an existing plugin's scripts/ rather than adding a plugin — its revisit-when for new plugins is not triggered.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/scripts/standards_resolve.py (reads vendored llms.txt, returns topic doc path) + a reference in the issues/plan skills + tests; verified by a test mapping a sample context to the expected per-topic doc and failing on an index miss.

title: ADR-to-code-pattern review lens on the saga /code-review lens registry
idea: There is no ADR-to-code-pattern lint anywhere, so decisions like adr-0002 (standardize engineering journals) are enforced only by memory. Add an `adr-patterns` review lens to saga:/code-review that, given the merge-base diff, reads the vendored ADR index and checks touched files against a small registry of ADR-derived pattern assertions (e.g., a repo of consequence touching docs/engineering-journal/ must carry a dated LEARNINGS/DECISIONS entry per the journal ADR), surfacing advisory findings rather than blocking. Because the lens reads an ADR-pattern registry, adding a new enforceable ADR is a registry row, not new lens code — the leverage compounds as the ADR corpus grows. This is the review-lens injection point that closes the 'ADR-code-pattern lint absent' gap while keeping ADR judgment advisory, matching the checkable-split posture.
basis: grounding §4: 'Absent: ... any ADR-code-pattern lint'; check_docs.py REQUIRED_FILES pins 'docs/governance/adrs/adr-0002-standardize-engineering-journals.md' as a real ADR anchor to key patterns off. CLAUDE.md engineering-journal section already mandates same-commit journal entries, giving a concrete first pattern to assert.
outcome_shape: PR adding an adr-patterns lens entry to saga /code-review (skills/code-review references + an adr_patterns.json registry) + tests; verified by /code-review emitting an advisory finding on a journal-touching diff that omits a dated entry, and staying silent when the entry is present.

title: Poka-yoke standards fixture at issue/plan creation
idea: Toyota Production System poka-yoke mistake-proofs at the assembly fixture: a part physically cannot seat wrong, so defects are prevented at the point of work rather than inspected out later. Apply the same locus shift to standards: inject the context-library llms.txt index (~1-2KB, whole-injectable per section 4) directly into the mission-control:issue and saga:plan creation flows as a required-read block, so the operative standards are present at the exact moment an issue body or plan is authored — not discovered at review. This closes the grounding-brief 'Absent: pull library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation' gap. The fixture is the injection wiring plus a rendered assertion that the block was actually surfaced, mirroring context_census keeping llms.txt honest — extend that self-describing-index convention outward into the two creation surfaces rather than inventing a new blob mechanism.
basis: Grounding brief section 4: 'Absent: pull library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation' and 'llms.txt (~1-2KB) whole-injectable'. Confirms both the gap and the injectable index size.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md and plugins/saga/skills/plan/SKILL.md that adds an llms.txt-index injection step at creation, plus a drift-guard test asserting the injected standards block is present in generated issue/plan scaffolds. Verified by the new test passing in CI and a rendered example.

title: Gene-expression resolver: transcribe only the topic READMEs the work needs
idea: A cell holds its whole genome but transcribes only the operons its current state demands; the genome index (regulatory regions) is cheap and always present, while full gene products are synthesized on demand. Map this to consumption shape from section 4: llms.txt is the always-injected genome index (~1-2KB), and the 8-12KB per-topic READMEs are transcribed only when the active work touches that topic — whole-library injection is infeasible because platform-specs dominates, exactly like a cell never transcribing its entire genome at once. Build a standards_resolver that reads llms.txt, detects which topics the current issue/plan/review actually implicates (from labels, changed paths, or plan sections), and loads only those READMEs. This extends the self-describing-index convention (the index declares what is loadable) into a runtime lazy loader rather than a static blob dump.
basis: Grounding brief section 4: 'Consumption shape: llms.txt (~1-2KB) whole-injectable; per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible (platform-specs dominates).' Directly specifies index-plus-on-demand mechanics this resolver implements.
outcome_shape: PR adding a standards_resolver.py (in mission-control or saga scripts) plus SKILL.md wiring in the plan/issue flows, with a unit test asserting that a given topic-set loads exactly the matching READMEs and never the whole library. Verified by test coverage of the topic-detection-to-README mapping.

title: Schema-registry ETags: llms.txt as a staleness-detecting manifest with per-topic hashes
idea: Confluent Schema Registry and HTTP conditional-GET (ETag / If-None-Match) let a consumer hold a manifest of content hashes and skip re-fetching anything unchanged, while loudly detecting when a held copy has gone stale against the registry. The grounding brief's recurring pattern 7 ('Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact') is precisely a missing staleness check on consumed standards. Extend context_census.py so llms.txt carries a per-topic content hash (the registry role), and give the consumption-side resolver an If-None-Match style check: a plugin flow that quotes a standard records the topic hash it read, and a CI/preflight guard flags any cached or asserted standard whose recorded hash no longer matches the live llms.txt. This keeps the authority-model priority order honest over time and extends the self-describing index (it now describes freshness), not a new paradigm.
basis: Grounding brief section 4 ('context_census.py --check keeps llms.txt honest') plus section 7 recurring pattern 'Stale memory/doc claims asserted as fact, caught only by operator recall'. The ETag manifest attacks exactly that staleness gap on the existing census mechanism.
outcome_shape: PR to the context-library context_census.py adding per-topic hashes to llms.txt output, plus a consumer-side hash-check guard in a fleet plugin preflight; verified by a test that mutates a topic README and asserts the guard flags the now-stale recorded hash.

title: Cockpit-checklist enforcement classes: do-verify vs challenge-response vs advisory
idea: Aviation checklists are formally taxonomized by enforcement mode: 'do-verify' items are mechanically confirmed, 'challenge-response' items require a second human's judgment call-out, and briefing items are advisory. The theme's checkable-split axis is the same taxonomy applied to ADRs/standards. Add an enforcement_class field to each ADR/standard's frontmatter (machine-checkable | judgment-checkable | advisory) and have check_docs.py route on it: machine-checkable rules become CI lint failures, judgment-checkable rules become mandatory saga:code-review lenses, advisory rules are surfaced but never block. This makes the enforcement locus explicit per rule instead of every rule defaulting to unenforced prose, and extends the existing schema-validate-in-CI convention by giving check_docs.py a class-driven routing table rather than a new engine.
basis: External prior art: FAA/Boeing cockpit checklist taxonomy (do-verify vs challenge-response vs read-and-do), documented in Boeing 'Operational Use of Flight Path Management Systems' and NASA checklist-design literature. The three modes map onto machine/judgment/advisory enforcement classes.
outcome_shape: PR adding an enforcement_class frontmatter field to the context-library sdlc-schema.json and ADR template, plus check_docs.py routing (fail on machine-checkable violations, emit review-lens list for judgment-checkable). Verified by a schema-validation test and a fixture ADR of each class exercising each route.

title: Known-good-die burn-in: actually compile-render mermaid, don't lint its text
idea: Semiconductor fabs do not ship a die because it passed visual inspection; they burn it in and functionally exercise it, because 'test escapes' (defects that pass a shallow gate) are the expensive failures. The 13 broken mermaid diagrams that shipped past check_docs.py are textbook test escapes: the gate lints diagram text but never renders it, so syntactically-broken diagrams pass. Add a real render step (mermaid-cli / mmdc compile to SVG in a throwaway step) to check_docs.py so a diagram must actually compile to pass — functional exercise, not text inspection. This is a direct extension of the schema-validate-in-CI convention: the diagram is now validated by execution the way the schema is validated by parse.
basis: Theme T9 enforcement-drift-guarding axis states the 'mermaid blind spot: 13 broken diagrams shipped past check_docs.py'. The render gate closes exactly that documented escape.
outcome_shape: PR to the context-library check_docs.py (and its validate.yml CI) adding a mermaid compile-render assertion, with a fixture broken diagram that the new gate must fail on and a valid one it must pass. Verified by CI red-then-green on the fixtures.

title: Consumer-driven contract test for the live project-board field schema
idea: Pact-style consumer-driven contract testing and Avro schema-registry compatibility checks prevent a producer from silently changing a schema the consumer depends on: the consumer publishes the shape it assumes, and CI fails the moment the live schema drifts from it. mission-control's board/field drift (nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases, per grounding-brief pattern 3) is an unguarded consumer contract, and sdlc_manager.py hardcodes fields(first: 30) / fieldValues(first: 20) caps that can silently truncate a project's real field set. Add a contract test that queries the live GitHub Projects field schema and diffs it against a checked-in field-contract manifest, failing loud on any assumed-but-absent field or any project whose field count exceeds the hardcoded first: N cap. This extends schema-validate-in-CI outward from docs to the board API surface.
basis: plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py:820 'fields(first: 30)' and :791 'fieldValues(first: 20)' are hardcoded caps; grounding-brief section 7 pattern 3: 'mission-control board/field drift — nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases'. Both verified this session.
outcome_shape: PR adding a field-contract manifest and a contract test in tests/ that queries a live/mocked project schema and fails on drift or on field-count exceeding the first:N caps in sdlc_manager.py. Verified by the test failing against a drifted fixture schema.

title: Kafka consumer-offset completeness guard against silent 200-item truncation
idea: A Kafka consumer that stops reading before the log's high-water mark silently loses records with no error; the discipline is to assert you consumed up to the committed end-offset. mission-control's item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items (grounding-brief pattern 3) is the same class of bug: pagination stops but nothing asserts the log was fully drained. sdlc_manager.py already loops on pageInfo.hasNextPage in some queries but the drift shows not every list path does. Add a completeness guard: any list operation must either exhaust hasNextPage or explicitly declare a cap and fail loud (or annotate the result as truncated) when hasNextPage is still true — never return a silently-partial list. This extends the schema-validate-in-CI ethos to result-completeness as a first-class invariant.
basis: Grounding-brief section 7 pattern 3: 'item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items'; corroborated by sdlc_manager.py:907/1586 hasNextPage loops existing on some but not all list paths (verified this session).
outcome_shape: PR to plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py adding a shared paginate-to-exhaustion helper (or explicit truncation flag) applied to all item-list queries, plus a test asserting a >200-item mocked project returns all items or a loud truncation marker. Verified by the test.

title: TCAS resolution advisory: authority-model stop-and-surface as a plugin primitive
idea: TCAS (Traffic Collision Avoidance System) in air-traffic control does not silently pick a heading when two aircraft converge; it detects the conflict and issues a Resolution Advisory that forces the crew to act on a surfaced, explicit conflict. The context-library authority-model.md already defines a priority order including a 'stop and surface conflict' rule, but section 4 shows it is never invoked inside plugin flows. Implement stop-and-surface as a reusable primitive: when a plan/issue creation flow finds two standards sources giving conflicting guidance (e.g., an ADR vs a topic README, or two priority-adjacent rules), it HALTs and surfaces the conflict to the operator with both sources quoted, rather than silently resolving by guess. This honors the grounding-brief HALT-not-degrade posture from the /outcome campaign and the never-gatekeepers decision (Claude surfaces, operator decides — no external engine adjudicates).
basis: Grounding brief section 4: 'authority-model.md defines agent priority order incl. stop surface conflict' and 'Absent: pull library into ... creation'. The primitive activates an already-authored-but-unused rule; aligns with /outcome campaign 'HALT-not-degrade' (section 2).
outcome_shape: PR adding a conflict-detection-and-surface routine invoked in saga:plan and mission-control:issue creation (quoting both conflicting sources, halting for operator choice), plus a test with two contrived conflicting standards asserting the flow halts rather than auto-picks. Verified by the halt-path test.

title: Required-and-checked context-library field at issue creation (flip optional link to hard gate)
idea: Flip the constraint that context-library standards are an OPTIONAL card decoration to the extreme: no SDLC card may be created unless the governing standard is resolved, injected, and cleared. mission-control:issue fetches the ~1-2KB llms.txt index at creation, resolves which per-topic standard applies to the card's type/repo, injects a distilled clause into the card body, and extends validate_card_body with a lens that fails the card when its text asserts something the resolved standard forbids. The extreme (every card blocked pending standard) is impractical, but the kernel is: turn issues/SKILL.md:277's dangling optional 'Context library links' into a resolved, machine-checked field so 343-clean-cards-fail-live-contract (#222) drift cannot recur at the standards layer.
basis: plugins/mission-control/skills/issues/SKILL.md:277 'Ask for optional Notes / conventions and Context library links when they would...' -- the library is already named at the injection point but never pulled or validated; grounding brief §4 confirms 'Absent: any pull of the library into mission-control:issue / saga:plan creation'.
outcome_shape: PR touching plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py (validate_card_body lens), skills/issues/SKILL.md (required field), and config/sdlc-schema.json (standards-topic key); verified by a new case in plugins/mission-control/tests/test_card_validator.py asserting a card that violates a resolved standard is rejected.

title: One review lens per ADR (flip single general lens to 100 auto-attached standards lenses)
idea: Flip 'saga review runs a handful of judgment-selected lenses' to the extreme of one lens per ADR/standard in the library. The impractical extreme (100 lenses on every diff) yields the kernel: a generated lens-manifest, derived from the library's llms.txt topic map, that lets /code-review and /doc-review auto-attach ONLY the standards-lenses whose owning topic matches the touched file globs. This closes the grounding-named gap of 'no ADR-to-code-pattern lint' without a new paradigm: the manifest is regenerated from the self-describing index, exactly the context_census pattern pointed outward at review time.
basis: grounding brief §4: 'Absent: ... any ADR↔code-pattern lint; any reference to the library from this repo's CI' and 'per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand' -- a topic→file-glob lens manifest is the missing binding between the two.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/skills/code-review/references/standards-lenses.md plus a generated lens-manifest (topic→glob→lens-prompt) built from llms.txt, wired into doc-review/code-review lens selection; verified by a parity test asserting the manifest topic set equals the llms.txt topic set.

title: Authority-ordered token-budgeted library loader (flip to always-inject-everything, mine the budgeted kernel)
idea: Flip the consumption constraint to 10x budget: whole-inject the entire library into every plugin flow, always. Since platform-specs dominates and that's infeasible, the kernel is a shared context_lib_resolve.py helper that whole-injects only the ~1-2KB llms.txt at flow start, then lazily fetches a per-topic README only when a flow cites a need, resolving each fetch through the same GitHub-main→vendored→local ladder sdlc_manager already uses for the schema. The authority-model priority order becomes the loader's resolution order, so the most-authoritative topic wins when two topics both claim a rule. No new plugin — one shared script any plugin imports.
basis: plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py:291 _resolve_sdlc_schema 'Resolve sdlc-schema.json via GitHub main → vendored → local fallback' is the proven resolution ladder to reuse; grounding brief §4 fixes the budget shape ('llms.txt (~1-2KB) whole-injectable; per-topic READMEs (8-12KB) load on demand; whole-library injection infeasible').
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared scripts/context_lib_resolve.py (index whole-inject + authority-ordered on-demand topic load + GitHub/vendored/local ladder), adopted by one caller (mission-control:issue), with unit tests covering the fallback ladder and authority-order tie-break.

title: Vendored SHA-pinned llms.txt snapshot with census-parity gate (flip to $0/offline, nothing-cached)
idea: Flip to the zero-network extreme: the library index does not exist at run time and every flow must survive with $0 remote fetches. The kernel is to vendor a snapshot of llms.txt into THIS repo beside a pinned SHA256 manifest — exactly the vendoring the plugin already does for sdlc-schema.json — so rate-limited or offline flows still get a deterministic index, while a census-parity CI gate recomputes the hash and fails when the snapshot silently drifts from source. This makes the self-describing index honest across the repo boundary, not just inside the library, and hardens the standards layer against the same silent-copy drift that produced #222.
basis: plugins/mission-control/config/generated/check_issue_contract_parity.py:1-25 'each vendored module ... PLUS a pinned SHA256 fingerprint ... recomputes the SHA256 ... any hand-edit ... fails the gate' — the exact parity mechanism to extend to a vendored llms.txt.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/mission-control/config/vendored/llms.txt + llms.txt.sha256 and a parity check invoked from .github/workflows/ci.yml; verified by an intentional-drift test (edit snapshot → gate exits 1).

title: Three-lane standards manifest (flip to every-rule-machine-checkable, mine the honest split)
idea: Flip to the extreme where every standard is machine-checkable with zero judgment. That extreme lies (it manufactures the mermaid-style false confidence — a rule believed linted that no linter covers), so the kernel is an honest three-lane self-describing manifest tagging each standard machine-checkable | judgment-checkable | advisory. Tooling then routes by lane: machine rules become check_docs-style CI assertions, judgment rules become review-lens prompts (feeds T9-F6-2), advisory rules are inject-only. The lane tag makes 'we think CI covers this' a checkable claim rather than an assumption, which is precisely how 13 broken diagrams shipped past a checker everyone trusted.
basis: First-principles: a blind spot is invisible precisely when a rule is assumed machine-covered but is not (mermaid: 13 diagrams shipped past check_docs.py). If every rule carries an explicit enforceability lane, the set 'believed-linted ∩ actually-unlinted' becomes empty by construction — the false-confidence class is closed at the manifest, not per-instance. This is context_census's honesty invariant applied to the rule taxonomy rather than the index.
outcome_shape: PR adding a standards-lanes manifest (rule-id→lane→enforcer-ref) generated alongside llms.txt, plus a generator + a test asserting every machine-lane rule names a live enforcer and no rule is unlaned.

title: Checker coverage-ledger (flip to check_docs validates EVERYTHING, mine the self-describing gap map)
idea: Flip to the extreme where the docs checker validates every artifact type that exists. It cannot, so the kernel is a coverage meta-check that emits, from the checker's own rule registry, the artifact types it DOES and does NOT validate — turning the mermaid blind spot from an invisible gap into a self-describing coverage ledger that FAILS when a new unvalidated artifact type appears in the tree. This is distinct from simply adding a mermaid rule (already a direct candidate): it guards the whole class of future blind spots by making 'what the checker ignores' an explicit, reviewed, drift-gated artifact rather than tacit silence.
basis: grounding brief §7 singletons: 'mermaid syntax never validated by check_docs.py (13 broken diagrams shipped)' — evidence the gap is invisible because the checker's non-coverage is undeclared; the fix targets the undeclared-coverage class, not the one diagram type in the direct-to-candidate pool.
outcome_shape: PR adding a check_coverage manifest (artifact-type→validated? →rule-ref) + a CI step that diffs discovered artifact types against the manifest and fails on an unlisted type; verified by a test that introduces a novel artifact type and asserts the gate trips.

title: Live-field + pagination-completeness HALT guard before any board write (flip to nothing-assumed)
idea: Flip to the extreme where the fleet assumes nothing about GitHub schema and verifies every field and every page live before acting. The kernel is a pre-write guard in sdlc_manager that (a) diffs assumed project field names against a live GraphQL field probe and HALTs on any nonexistent/aliased field rather than writing blind, and (b) asserts pagination completeness — fetched N must equal the reported total, failing loudly instead of silently truncating at 200 of 375. This extends the existing cursor-paginated queries into a completeness contract and applies the /outcome HALT-not-degrade posture to the standards/schema-drift surface.
basis: grounding brief §7.3: 'nonexistent fields assumed, hardcoded aliases, item-list pagination silently truncating at 200 of 375 items' (4 repos); the cursor loop already exists at plugins/mission-control/scripts/sdlc_manager.py:772 'items(first: 100, after: $cursor)' — completeness just needs asserting. Engages binding /outcome 'HALT-not-degrade' as the model rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a field-existence probe + pagination-completeness assertion in sdlc_manager (guard raises a typed exception on drift/truncation), wired ahead of board-add/field-set writes; verified by tests in test_typed_exceptions.py / test_board_add_multi_project.py simulating a missing field and a truncated page.

title: Machine-readable authority precedence with deterministic detect + mandatory surface (flip to fully-autonomous resolution)
