idea: Flip the authority-model's stop-and-surface rule to the extreme of fully-autonomous silent resolution: encode the agent priority order as a machine-readable precedence table and let a flow auto-pick the winner when two injected standards conflict. Full autonomy violates the operator-choice posture, so the mined kernel keeps the deterministic DETECT-and-PICK machinery but forces a stop-and-surface: the flow shows the precedence-resolved choice AND the overruled alternative, and proceeds only on operator acknowledgement. This makes authority-model.md's prose 'stop and surface conflict' executable inside saga:plan and mission-control:issue instead of aspirational.
basis: grounding brief §4: 'authority-model.md defines the agent priority order incl. "stop and surface conflict"' — a defined-but-uncoded rule. Engages binding {#operator-choice-framework} (surface, never auto-decide) and derive-on-read (conflict derived at read, no committed verdict) rather than contradicting them.
outcome_shape: PR adding an authority-precedence manifest (topic/rule→rank) + a shared surface-conflict helper that detects overlapping-rule conflicts and emits a resolved-vs-alternative prompt, adopted in saga:plan standards injection; verified by a test feeding two conflicting standards and asserting the helper surfaces both with the precedence-correct pick flagged.

title: Consent-receipt protocol: gates refuse to proceed without a captured operator answer artifact
idea: Gate-B struck AskUserQuestion reliability as harness-level and out of scope, but the operator pain (silence treated as consent, gates firing before answers are captured) is fixable plugin-side without touching the primitive: stop trusting it. Every gate step in saga and team-execution writes a consent receipt — a small artifact containing the operator's literal answer text, the options offered, and a timestamp — before the gated action runs, and the action step verifies the receipt exists and is non-empty. A timeout, an error, or an empty answer produces no receipt, and no-receipt is HALT-not-degrade, never proceed. This converts every gate from 'the primitive said yes' to 'here is what the operator actually said', and makes rubber-stamp bypass auditable after the fact.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 2: 'AskUserQuestion silently auto-proceeds on timeout treating silence as consent (documented operator fury), fires before answers are captured, errors outright' (6 repos). The Gate-B resolution in §8 theme 6 struck the primitive itself as harness-level out of scope — this idea explicitly engages that strike by working around the primitive at the plugin layer instead of fixing it, which the strike does not foreclose. Consistent with the /outcome campaign decision's HALT-not-degrade constraint (§2).
outcome_shape: Merged: shared consent-receipt convention reference doc + gate steps in saga (/work merge gate, /outcome attend gates) and team-execution validator gates updated to write-then-verify receipts, with a drift-guard test that greps gate steps for receipt verification.

title: Dispatch manifest + casualty reconciliation: every fan-out must account for its dead
idea: The recurring rate-limit pain is not the absence of a concurrency knob — it is that 6 of 7 agents can die and the run keeps going as if nothing happened. Define one shared contract: every fan-out site (team-execution reviewer dispatch, /outcome frontier dispatch, workflow emitters) writes a dispatch manifest (N expected, IDs, expected deliverables) at spawn time, and its collector reconciles delivered-vs-manifest and emits a structured casualty report (delivered, rate-killed, silent-no-op, idle). Casualty rate above a threshold is HALT-not-degrade at the next gate rather than silent quality erosion. This deliberately sidesteps /optimize's removed max_concurrent knob — it adds zero throttling machinery, only accounting and refusal to pretend.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting'; 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery' (3 repos). Engages the /optimize shed-knob decision explicitly: verified today that optimize/SKILL.md:17-19 sheds max_concurrent fan-out by design — this idea proposes detection+halt, not a knob, so it does not re-litigate the shed. Extends the only existing cap precedent, VERIFY_N_CAP=7 (execution_spec.py:114), from prevention to reconciliation.
outcome_shape: Merged: manifest/casualty-report schema in a shared reference + reconciliation steps wired into team-execution Step A7 fan-out and /outcome advance, with tests that a shortfall produces a HALT fact.

title: Liveness derived from artifact-pointer appearance, not agent chattiness
idea: Idle-without-delivering subagents are detected today by coordinators noticing silence and re-pinging — a polling-the-vibes protocol. The just-merged typed artifact-pointer seam (#324, artifact_pointer.py) makes a structural alternative possible: every spawn declares its expected deliverable pointer at dispatch time, and the coordinator derives liveness from whether the pointer target exists and is growing, never from status messages or stale idle notifications. An agent that chats but produces no pointer is dead; an agent that is silent but whose artifact is materializing is alive. This is derive-on-read (the campaign's own recurring rejected-alternative winner) applied to agent liveness.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 9: 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications — coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session)'. The seam exists: plugins/team-execution/skills/team-execution/scripts/artifact_pointer.py verified present today (merged in #324). Aligned with the /outcome campaign binding decision 'derived-on-read status, never committed status fields' (§2).
outcome_shape: Merged: dispatch-time expected-pointer declaration added to the artifact-pointer contract + coordinator liveness check in team-execution and /outcome attend that reads pointer existence/mtime, replacing chat-based idle detection.

title: Never-fired detector: lifecycle machinery must prove it has ever produced output or face sunset
idea: The promote pipeline has existed across the whole measurement window and has promoted exactly zero learnings — the operator pays maintenance cost on machinery that has never fired, and nothing in the fleet would ever notice. Generalize the repo's own dead-wiring learnings to the lifecycle itself: a fired/never-fired ledger records each time a piece of gated machinery (promote, fallback ladders, HALT paths, degrade branches) actually executes its payoff path, and /retro flags any machinery with zero firings over N runs with a forced three-way proposal: lower its trigger threshold, fix its wiring, or sunset it. Uncomfortable on purpose — some of the fleet's proudest safety machinery may turn out to be decoration.
basis: Grounding brief §3 item 5: 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine ≥3-repo transcendent cluster. The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.' Combined with §6 item 1: silent no-ops and dead wiring are this repo's top journal pain (5+ learnings) — this idea is that pattern turned on the lifecycle's own plumbing.
outcome_shape: Merged: firing-ledger append hooks in promote/retro/fallback code paths + a /retro audit step that emits sunset-or-fix proposals for never-fired machinery, with the promote pipeline as the first adjudicated case.

title: Chaperone-emitted engine-agnostic session skeletons: fix mining darkness at the write side
idea: 219 codex sessions sit dark because the mining substrate is Claude-session-shaped and nobody wants to build a codex-format parser per engine. Invert it: provenance is a write-side obligation of the bridge, not a read-side archaeology problem. The chaperone that already wraps every external-engine dispatch (per the chaperone-dispatch decision) emits a neutral session-skeleton record — task, prompts, deliverable pointers, outcome verdict — in the same format the Claude mining pipeline consumes, at the moment of delegation. Every future engine added to the router registry inherits minability for free, and the 219-session class of gap becomes structurally impossible rather than perpetually backfilled.
basis: Grounding brief §7: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap, feeds theme 10.' Engages the binding {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} decision (§2) constructively rather than contradicting it: the chaperone is retained as the single dispatch point and gains one emit obligation; no new executor kind or residency is introduced.
outcome_shape: Merged: skeleton-emit spec + implementation in the codex and agy bridge chaperone paths + promote_scan/retro substrate acceptance of chaperone-emitted skeletons, with a test that a delegated task yields a minable record.

title: Content-addressed, append-only evidence: verification artifacts that cannot be quietly rewritten
idea: A probe script overwrote a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS — the audit trail was mutable, so the gate that read it was retroactively fooled. Make evidence artifacts append-only and content-addressed: verification writers (qa probes, code-review envelopes, verify-panel outputs) name files by content hash, verdict records reference evidence by hash, and any gate consuming evidence re-verifies the hash before trusting it. A later run produces a new artifact beside the old one, never over it; the FAIL stays in the record forever. Cheap to implement, and uncomfortable in what it implies: today every gate in the fleet trusts whatever bytes currently sit at a well-known path.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)', reinforced by §6 item 2 ('provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state', 4 learnings). Also listed in §8 direct-to-candidate as 'evidence-artifact immutability' — this idea is the structural class-level version (content addressing + hash-verified consumption), not just a dont-overwrite rule.
outcome_shape: Merged: evidence-immutability convention reference + hash-addressed write helpers in saga /qa and /code-review artifact paths + gate-side hash verification, with a test that an overwrite attempt is rejected.

title: Tier-precedent ledger: tier choices cite measured priors instead of being re-derived every run
idea: Operators and planners burn attention re-deriving the same tier judgments run after run ('xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful', hand-built per-unit tier tables in 3 repos), and each derivation is a fresh guess with no memory of what the last identical shape actually cost. Record every tier decision as a replayable fact: unit shape, tier chosen, measured token cost, and outcome verdict. /plan's tier table — currently the fleet's one operator-facing lever — then cites precedent lines ('last 3 read-only recon fan-outs at this shape cost 350-450k; sonnet delivered') alongside its recommendation, and /retro appends actuals. This turns intake tension 4's 'recommendation plus cheaper fallback' rule from taste into evidence.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 6: 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos)', plus the measured anchor '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs'. Builds on the existing lever at plan/SKILL.md:296-352 (§1) rather than inventing a new one, and respects {#tier-vocab-ordering}: precedents are cited against the ordered escalation ladder.
outcome_shape: Merged: tier-precedent ledger schema + /plan tier-table step that reads and cites it + /retro append step recording actual cost/verdict per unit.

title: Forbid contract mirrors: consumers exec the source-of-truth validator, and a lint bans hand-copies
idea: The 4-repo drift pain (343 'clean' cards failing the live contract because validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of card_validator.py) is usually answered with sync automation or drift-guard CI — which keeps the copies and polices them forever. The uncomfortable structural fix is to abolish the copies: mission-control exposes card_validator.py (and the sdlc schema) as a stable, versioned CLI contract, consumer repos rewrite their checks to exec the installed plugin's validator at check time, and a lint in the context-library validate suite bans locally-implemented validation of contracts that have a canonical owner. Drift becomes impossible instead of detected, at the cost of a runtime dependency on plugin installation — a tradeoff worth surfacing explicitly.
basis: Grounding brief §3 item 1: 'validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract, → #222), re-vendored sdlc-schema.json' — 4 independent repos, the top-ranked consumer-side pain. Named issue anchor: #222.
outcome_shape: Merged: versioned CLI validator entrypoint in mission-control + at least one consumer repo's check rewritten to exec it + a no-local-mirror lint rule, with the removed hand-copy as proof.

title: Basis-anchor decay: stale open issues re-verify their own grounding or close themselves
idea: The intake brief's own first pre-mortem is backlog rot — this very ideation process will generate faster than the fleet executes, and wave-tagging only orders the rot, it does not drain it. Since every issue in this backlog carries a basis with concrete anchors (file:line, decision anchors, quoted evidence), make that basis a liveness contract: a periodic cheap-tier pass re-verifies the anchors of issues untouched for N days against current code and journal state. Anchors that moved or evidence that has since been fixed produce an automated 'basis decayed' comment and a close-as-stale proposal at the next board review; anchors that hold re-stamp the issue as still grounded. The backlog becomes self-pruning by the same provenance discipline that created it.
basis: Intake brief 'Pre-mortems recorded' item 1: 'Backlog rot — generation outpaces execution bandwidth; the fleet churns under open issues. Mitigation: wave tagging, wave-1 bandwidth multipliers' — the recorded mitigation orders execution but contains no pruning mechanism, which is the gap this fills. Reinforced by grounding brief §6 item 2 (provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state, 4 learnings).
outcome_shape: Merged: basis-anchor re-verification script + scheduled mission-control pass that comments/labels decayed issues and surfaces close proposals at board review.

title: Rubber-stamp telemetry: measure whether each gate ever changes the path before deciding auto-progression
idea: Auto-progression debates (which steps of the ship ceremony may proceed without asking) are currently settled by taste at intent capture. Instrument gates instead: record for every gate firing whether the operator's answer diverged from the recommended default. A gate answered 'proceed as recommended' in 100% of its last N firings is empirically a rubber stamp — surface it as an auto-progression candidate with its own history as the argument; a gate that regularly redirects work has proven its rent and stays. This gives the intake's envelope-autonomy dialog a data-backed menu instead of a blank questionnaire, and it will be uncomfortable when beloved gates turn out never to have changed anything.
basis: First-principles argument: the 8-repo manual-ship-ceremony pattern (grounding §7 pattern 1) shows operators route around installed lifecycle tooling, and gate friction is the standing hypothesis for why — but no measurement exists either way, so both gate-removal and gate-keeping arguments are currently unfalsifiable. The intake's tension 3 makes gating operator-configurable per outcome, which requires the operator to predict which gates pay rent with zero data. Recording answer-vs-default divergence is the minimal observable that makes both the bypass hypothesis and each per-gate decision testable; it is spend-neutral, reversible, and does not itself remove any gate, so it cannot contradict the never-autonomous merge/deploy posture — it only informs the dialog that posture already mandates.
outcome_shape: Merged: gate-firing telemetry appended to saga state (gate id, default offered, answer given, divergence bit) + a /retro report ranking gates by divergence rate with auto-progression candidates flagged.

title: Undo-ledger: replace pause points on reversible mutations with act-log-inverse-notify
idea: Invert the gate model for the reversible class of operations: instead of pausing to ask, every plugin mutation that has a computable inverse (board status move, label apply, issue close, branch create, PR open, review run) executes immediately and appends an inverse-operation entry to a shared undo ledger (JSONL in the saga dir, plus a `/undo` skill that replays inverses newest-first). The gated set shrinks to exactly the operations with no inverse (merge, deploy, delete-with-data), which stays consistent with the /outcome campaign's 'merge/deploy never autonomous' line. This also reduces fleet dependence on the unreliable AskUserQuestion primitive (struck from scope as harness-level) without touching the harness: fewer questions asked at all. Ledger entries are leaf-produced facts, matching the derived-on-read posture rather than committed status.
basis: Intake brief lines 56-57: 'Everything reversible (status moves, issue closures, labels, branches, PRs opened, reviews run) proceeds without asking.' The fleet currently has no mechanism that makes reversibility real — nothing records the inverse, so skills gate defensively anyway. Grounding brief section 7 item 2 documents gate-primitive unreliability across 6 repos (struck as harness-level); shrinking the number of gates is the plugin-side lever that remains in scope.
outcome_shape: Merged: shared `undo_ledger.py` helper + ledger-write adoption in mission-control board/label/issue mutations and saga branch/PR steps + a `/undo` command that replays inverses, with tests proving round-trip for each registered operation type.

title: Presumed-dead delegation: process-level provenance receipts required by every bridge
idea: Invert the trust default in delegation: a bridge result is presumed to be a silent no-op or fallback until a wrapper-captured receipt proves otherwise. The wrapper (not the LLM text channel) records ground truth at dispatch time — resolved binary path, `--version` output, exit code, wall-clock, engine-reported model id, and a per-dispatch nonce that must be echoed in the output — into a receipt file beside the result. Consumers (team-execution worker table, saga verify steps, agy envelope handling) hard-fail on missing or mismatched receipts instead of accepting plausible-looking text. This converts the entire silent-no-op class from 'detect after the damage' to 'structurally impossible to accept', because the fallback path cannot forge process-level evidence it never generated.
basis: Grounding brief section 6 item 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings: agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter mismatch) — any bridge/delegation idea needs did-it-actually-run/persist verification.' Every listed failure shares one mechanism: trust placed in the text channel, which the fallback also produces. Only evidence captured outside the text channel discriminates.
outcome_shape: Merged: `delegation_receipt.py` (emit + verify) + receipt emission added to the codex and agy bridge wrappers + receipt verification wired into team-execution result-ingest and saga external-engine consumption, with a test that simulates a silent fallback and proves rejection.

title: Ship ceremony moved to time zero: branch + draft PR minted at /work start, ship = flip-ready
idea: Remove the end-of-session ship ritual by running it before the work exists: when /work begins executing an approved plan, it immediately mints the branch, pushes an empty scaffold commit, and opens a draft PR carrying the plan link and intent envelope. Shipping then degenerates to 'mark ready for review' plus (only when the run-start intent answered auto-merge yes, per the intake's per-outcome intent questions) enabling merge-on-green; checkout-main/pull/branch-cleanup moves to a reaper that runs on merge webhook or session start rather than in the shipping session. Second-order payoff: every push to the draft PR triggers CI, so the hand-in gate can read CI status as the only verifier — dissolving the local-vs-CI parity gap (theme 11) as a side effect. The design must explicitly absorb the documented `gh pr merge --auto`/`--delete-branch` behavior surprises and the stacked-PR CI-trigger gap rather than rediscovering them.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos).' The 8-repo recurrence despite installed tooling shows automating the same end-of-session sequence is not enough — the step must stop existing at the end. Merge stays under the intake section 3 per-outcome operator decision ('Gate or auto merge... operator decides per outcome, once, start'), so this does not contradict the /outcome campaign's never-autonomous merge posture.
outcome_shape: Merged: /work SKILL.md step change (branch+draft-PR at execution start, intent-envelope-conditional auto-merge enablement), a merge/session-start cleanup reaper script, and CHANGELOG/version bumps; verified by one full plan→PR→merge pass using the new flow.

title: Recon demand elimination: CI-maintained repo fact index makes read-only fan-outs a cache hit
idea: The cheapest recon fan-out is the one that never launches. Extend the org's existing 'schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index' convention (context library llms.txt pattern) to code repos: a post-merge CI job regenerates a structured fact index (plugin inventory, agent frontmatter matrix, script entry points, registry/vocabulary tuples, test map) as a committed artifact. Recon-class steps in saga and workflow emitters are required to read the index first and fan out agents only for questions the index cannot answer — turning a 350-450k-token pattern into a file read plus targeted misses. This is demand elimination, not scheduling, so it composes with rather than contradicts the settled worker-cache-scheduling architecture (which governs how residual agent work is scheduled, not whether it is needed).
basis: Grounding brief section 7 singletons: '350–450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)', combined with section 4: 'the org convention is schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index, not runtime-injected blobs.' The number quantifies pure re-derivation of facts that are deterministic functions of the repo tree at a given commit — exactly what a CI-refreshed index precomputes. Binding decision {#worker-cache-scheduling} is engaged: its revisit-when (residency insufficient / idle-poll cost) is untouched because this idea removes demand upstream of that architecture.
outcome_shape: Merged: `scripts/generate_fact_index.py` + CI job committing `docs/fact-index/` on merge + an index-first instruction landed in the saga recon/scan step guidance, with a before/after token measurement on one real recon task recorded in LEARNINGS.md.

title: Producer-push contract propagation: the source repo opens the refresh PRs, hand-copying abolished
idea: Invert the ownership of contract mirrors: today consumers hand-copy (validate_card_body, re-vendored sdlc-schema.json) and drift is discovered by incident. Instead, the source repo carries a consumer registry (repo, path, transform) beside each published contract, and a CI job on contract-change merge dispatches refresh PRs to every registered consumer; consumer CI independently fails if vendored bytes differ from registry-declared generated bytes. Drift becomes impossible to create silently in either direction — a human never hand-copies, and an unregistered copy is flagged by a workspace-wide sweep that greps for known contract fingerprints. This is structurally different from the obvious 'add drift-guard tests' because the guard lives with the producer, who is the only party that knows a change happened at time zero.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 1: 'Rename/vocabulary churn + contract-mirror drift (4 repos): ... validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract, → #222), re-vendored sdlc-schema.json.' The 343-card incident shows consumer-side vigilance failed precisely because the consumer had no signal a change occurred; only the producer has that signal at the moment of change.
outcome_shape: Merged: `contracts/consumers.json` registry + a dispatch workflow in this repo (source of card_validator/sdlc vocab) that opens refresh PRs on contract change + one consumer repo converted to registry-declared generated vendoring as the reference implementation.

title: Liveness-by-lease: one TTL-lease primitive replaces every teardown step and idle-detection loop
idea: Delete teardown steps and coordinator idle-polling by making persistence itself require active renewal: every long-lived artifact or actor — saga worktrees, resident team workers, background sessions, dispatched subagents — writes a lease file (owner id, TTL, renewal timestamp) at creation and must renew it to stay alive. A single generic reaper (session-start hook plus optional cron) reclaims anything whose lease expired: removes the worktree, tears down the worker, marks the subagent dead and eligible for respawn. Nothing anywhere needs a 'remember to clean up' step (the missing team-execution Step B8 becomes unnecessary rather than implemented), and 'idle without delivering' converts from a condition the coordinator must actively detect into a state that self-expires. Engages {#worker-cache-scheduling} explicitly: leases govern reclamation, not scheduling, so the settled residency architecture stands; if lease-renewal telemetry later shows idle-poll cost dominating, that is precisely the decision's named revisit trigger for a formal wave queue.
basis: Grounding brief section 4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10×+ → direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8', plus section 7 pattern 9: 'Subagents idle without delivering; stale idle notifications — coordinator must detect and re-ping (2 repos; also reproduced live in this very session).' Both are the same failure class — cleanup as a remembered step — and remembered steps demonstrably do not get remembered.
outcome_shape: Merged: `lease.py` primitive (create/renew/check) + lease emission in saga worktree creation and team-execution worker spawn + a generic reaper wired as a session-start hook, with a test suite covering expiry, renewal, and reap of each resource kind.

title: Knobless admission control: an ambient AIMD semaphore every spawn site acquires, no per-skill caps
idea: Agree with /optimize's deliberate removal of its max_concurrent knob and generalize the reasoning: per-skill concurrency knobs rot into 'aspiration, not machinery'. Instead, concurrency becomes ambient infrastructure — a tiny shared admission gate (file-lock semaphore in a well-known path, redis-backed when available) that every spawn site (team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, workflow emitters, engine bridges) acquires before dispatch and releases on completion; callers queue rather than fail. The window adapts by additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease: any 429 or rate-limit kill observed by a holder shrinks the window immediately, sustained success grows it back — so the cap tracks the real limit without anyone configuring anything. VERIFY_N_CAP remains as a domain-specific panel-size rule; this governs the orthogonal question of simultaneous in-flight agents fleet-wide.
basis: Grounding brief section 1 concurrency paragraph: 'the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7 ... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded. Notably, /optimize deliberately removed a max_concurrent knob (optimize/SKILL.md:18) — ideation on theme 13 must engage why', plus section 7 pattern 4: 'the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery.' The engagement: the knob was rightly removed because knobs are aspiration; the fix is a mechanism no skill has to encode or remember, which is the only shape consistent with both findings.
outcome_shape: Merged: `admission_gate.py` (acquire/release, AIMD window, 429 feedback hook) + adoption at the three named unbounded spawn sites + a LEARNINGS entry with a measured fan-out run showing zero rate-limit kills at previously failing widths.

title: Retire the promotion ceremony: cross-repo learning as a query-time join at /plan and /investigate
idea: The promote loop has never fired once — treat that as evidence the push-and-curate architecture is dead weight, not evidence it needs more discipline. Invert direction: leave learnings where they are written and make consumption a query-time join — a cheap `journal_query.py` that greps/indexes every workspace repo's LEARNINGS.md and DECISIONS.md, wired as a mandatory low-cost step in /plan and /investigate ('has any repo already learned about X?'). The 0-promotions ledger stops being a failure because promotion stops being the mechanism; genuinely transcendent clusters, if they ever appear, surface as repeated query hits — an observable trigger — rather than requiring a curation ceremony nobody performs. /promote is demoted to an optional archival pass or deleted outright, which also pays the plugin-sprawl consolidation dividend that {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} demands new work respect.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 5: 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine ≥3-repo transcendent cluster. The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.' Plus section 7 pattern 7 (stale claims caught only by operator recall) — a query-time join at plan time is exactly the moment a stale claim would be cross-checked. No binding decision in the grounding brief section 2 register protects the promote architecture, so the retirement is in bounds.
outcome_shape: Merged: `journal_query.py` cross-repo index/search tool + a mandatory consult step landed in /plan and /investigate SKILL.md + /promote marked deprecated-pending-signal in its SKILL.md with the query-hit-cluster trigger documented as its resurrection condition.

title: Ask-once intent envelope: capture autonomy answers on the issue, so /outcome start never re-interrogates
idea: The intake mandates the intent questions be asked 'per outcome, once, start' — so make every later ask a bug by persisting the answers at the earliest moment they exist. mission-control issue creation and saga /handoff write a machine-readable intent block into the issue body (per the card_validator schema family): reviews-required, merge posture, deploy-to-nonprod posture, spend posture. /outcome start reads the block and skips the interview entirely for issues that carry it, interrogating only bare issues; this simultaneously becomes the missing Objective-ingestion path the grounding brief confirms does not exist. Committed intent is operator input, not derived status, so the /outcome campaign's derived-on-read constraint is engaged and respected: status stays derived, intent is legitimately an input fact.
basis: Intake brief lines 53-55: 'Required intent questions: Are PR reviews required outcome? Gate or auto merge / deploy-to-nonprod? ... operator decides per outcome, once, start', combined with grounding brief section 1 correction (h): '/outcome start = 2-node starter DAG... not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' The questions are already answered at issue-shaping time in practice; the only missing piece is a durable, schema-validated place for the answers and a reader.
outcome_shape: Merged: intent-envelope block added to the issue-body schema (card_validator + templates) + mission-control /issue and saga /handoff writing it + /outcome start reading it with interview-skip logic, covered by a drift-guard test tying the three surfaces to one schema.

title: Zero-bridge provider onboarding: one OpenAI-compatible HTTP bridge, providers become pure registry rows
idea: The intake's settled router shape says 'each provider registry entry + bridge script' — invert the second half: for the entire class of OpenAI-compatible providers, ship exactly one generic `openai_compat_bridge.py` (base_url, model, api-key env var, all read from the registry row) and zero per-provider scripts. Ollama serves /v1/chat/completions natively and DeepSeek's API is OpenAI-compatible, so the two named targets — the $0 offload target and the cheap second opinion — onboard as registry entries alone, and every future API-key provider is a one-line diff instead of a script plus review plus release-surface bump. Per-provider scripts remain reserved for genuinely non-compatible CLIs (codex, agy), which already exist. This extends the existing engine_resolver/engine_registry seam rather than adding a plugin, respecting the consolidation burden of proof.
basis: Named prior art: the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API as de facto multi-provider standard — Ollama exposes it natively (ollama.com/blog/openai-compatibility, /v1/chat/completions), DeepSeek documents OpenAI SDK compatibility (api-docs.deepseek.com), and LiteLLM (github.com/BerriAI/litellm) proxies 100+ providers behind this one interface, proving a single adapter covers the provider class. Engages the intake section 5 resolved shape explicitly: the registry-driven single-router decision is preserved; only the per-provider-script assumption is dropped for the compatible class.
outcome_shape: Merged: `openai_compat_bridge.py` + registry schema extension (base_url/model/key-env fields) + Ollama and DeepSeek registry entries + an integration test against a local Ollama endpoint, with release surfaces bumped in the same PR.

title: Semantic tier roles in agent frontmatter: stop hardcoding model names, dispatch by work shape
idea: Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes a concrete model name (opus/sonnet/haiku) and zero effort fields, so a model generation change (opus 4.8 -> fable 5) means ~25+ frontmatter edits and fable/xhigh stay unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary. Break the assumption that the model name is the currency: agents declare a semantic tier role ('judgment', 'mechanical', 'survey', 'adversarial-review'), and one fleet-level role->model/effort mapping file resolves it at dispatch time. The mapping preserves the ordered-escalation-ladder semantics of {#tier-vocab-ordering} (roles map into positions on the MODELS/EFFORTS ladders, not around them), so escalation/fallback logic is untouched. One mapping edit re-tiers the whole fleet; a drift-guard test asserts no agent file carries a raw model literal.
basis: Grounding brief section 1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution)... fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary.' Verified today: MODELS=("fable","opus","sonnet","haiku") / EFFORTS=(...,"xhigh") at plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:52-53 with the strongest-first/weakest-first ordering comment. Engages binding decision {#tier-vocab-ordering}: roles are an indirection layer over the ordered ladders, not a replacement of them.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: fleet tier-role mapping file + resolver helper, all agent frontmatters converted from model literals to roles, drift-guard test that fails on any raw model literal in agents/*.md, CHANGELOG/marketplace bumps.

title: Cross-session admission control: the rate limit is shared across sessions, so the cap cannot live inside any one skill
idea: Every existing and proposed cap (VERIFY_N_CAP=7, the intake's batches-of-3 rule) governs a single run inside a single session, but the Anthropic rate limit is one shared resource across every concurrent Claude Code session, /loop timer, and cron routine on the host. Three sessions each honoring 'max 3' still produce 9 concurrent agents. Reframe concurrency as a host-level leased resource: a token-lease ledger that all spawn sites (team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, workflow emitters, engine bridges) acquire from before spawning, with lease expiry for crashed holders. The redis-channel plugin already maintains a live cross-session presence registry, giving a ready substrate; a file-lock fallback covers hosts without Redis. This engages /optimize's deliberate removal of its max_concurrent knob head-on: that removal was correct evidence that a per-skill knob is the wrong locus, and this idea completes the move by placing governance above all skills instead of restoring it inside one.
basis: Grounding brief section 1: 'the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7 (execution_spec.py:114)... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded. Notably, /optimize deliberately removed a max_concurrent knob (optimize/SKILL.md:18) — ideation on theme 13 must engage why.' Both anchors re-verified today. Section 7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting; the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery.' redis-channel 0.5.0 session registry confirmed in fleet map.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: a shared admission-control module (lease ledger with redis-channel and file-lock backends) + adoption in at least two unbounded spawn sites (team-execution fan-out, /outcome dispatch), with a liveness/expiry test.

title: Gates are durable approval records with pluggable transports, not AskUserQuestion widgets
idea: Gate-B struck AskUserQuestion reliability as harness-level and out of scope — but the fleet's deeper assumption is that a gate IS the widget. Reframe: a gate is a durable pending-approval record (saga-state artifact with question, options, requestor, deadline policy) whose satisfaction can arrive over any transport — terminal prompt, Discord button ({#discord-button-approval} seed), redis-channel reply. The skill blocks on the record, never on a widget timeout, so silence is structurally never consent regardless of what any primitive does on timeout. This does not fix the primitive (respecting the Gate-B strike); it removes the primitive from the trust chain entirely, and as a bonus makes gates survivable across session restarts and answerable from a phone during unattended /outcome runs.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 2: 'AskUserQuestion silently auto-proceeds on timeout treating silence as consent (documented operator fury), fires before answers are captured, errors outright; agents fall back to plain-text questions (6 repos).' Section 8 theme 6 Gate-B resolution: 'AskUserQuestion primitive reliability struck — harness-level, out of scope' — engaged explicitly: this idea routes around the primitive rather than repairing it. Seed {#discord-button-approval} in QUEUED.md (grounding section 5) supplies the second transport.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: gate-record contract + reference implementation in saga (write/poll/satisfy helpers), one alternate transport wired (redis-channel or Discord), and a never-timeout-to-consent test.

title: Content-addressed recon cache: grounding scans keyed by git tree hash, reused instead of re-spawned
idea: Read-only recon fan-outs burned 350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes, and the same surveys (plugin inventory, agent-frontmatter census, seam verification) are re-run from scratch every session because the fleet assumes recon is a per-run expense. Reframe recon output as a derived artifact with an invalidation key: each survey writes its distilled result to a cache keyed by the git tree hash of the paths it read; a later run with an unchanged tree hash reuses the artifact for zero agent spawns. This is orthogonal to the settled {#worker-cache-scheduling} architecture — that decision governs prompt-cache/worker residency (segment+agent+tier); this memoizes the outputs of read-only derivations, a different layer, so no revisit-when is triggered.
basis: Prior art: Bazel remote caching and Nix content-addressed derivations (bazel.build/remote/caching; nixos.org content-addressed store) — build outputs keyed by input digests, rebuilt only when inputs change. Same shape applies to read-only agent surveys whose inputs are file trees. Grounded need: grounding brief section 7 singleton '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: a recon-cache helper (key = sorted-path tree hash + survey id, store under saga scratch or .saga/cache) + adoption in at least one recurring survey path, with a cache-hit/invalidation test.

title: Execution attestation receipts: no bridge output is admissible without provenance
idea: The fleet keeps re-fixing silent no-ops one bridge at a time (agy silent Claude-fallback, dead producer+consumer wiring, fake-adapter mismatch). The assumption to break: bridges are trusted narrators of their own execution. Invert it — every delegation bridge (agy, codex, external-engine workers, workflow emitters) must emit a structured receipt alongside its output: engine identity, model actually used, token counts, exit status, output digest, wall time. One shared validator checks receipt presence and shape before any consumer treats the output as real; a missing or Claude-self-identified receipt on an external-engine call is a hard fail, not a silent fallback. This converts 'did it actually run' from a per-bridge test-writing discipline into a single fleet contract, and it strengthens {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} by making advisory-only participation provable rather than asserted.
basis: Prior art: SLSA provenance and in-toto attestations (slsa.dev, in-toto.io) — supply-chain security's answer to the identical problem: artifacts are inadmissible without a signed predicate stating who built them, from what, and how. Grounded need: grounding brief section 6.1 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings: agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter mismatch)'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: receipt schema + shared validator module + receipt emission wired into the agy and codex bridges, with a test that a fallback-to-Claude execution is rejected loudly.

title: Ship ceremony lives in the git surface, not the conversation: the 8-repo finding is an adoption verdict, not a feature gap
idea: Session mining shows the commit->PR->merge->checkout-main->pull->cleanup ritual done by raw git/gh in 8 repos even where saga and mission-control are installed. The obvious response is 'add a /ship skill' — but the evidence says skills that must be remembered lose to git muscle memory, so the assumption to attack is that the plugin's surface is the Claude conversation. Instead, meet the operator in the shell: a saga-installed gitconfig alias pack / thin git wrapper where finishing moves on a saga-tracked branch (push of a work branch, merge of its PR) trigger the ceremony — board move, branch/worktree cleanup, saga close — with the conversation-side skill as one caller among several. Not a new plugin (respecting {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}); it is saga growing a shell-side limb. Uncomfortable on purpose: it concedes that for this workflow the terminal, not the model, is the reliable trigger point.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit->PR->merge->checkout-main->pull->cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos).' The 'even where installed' clause is the load-bearing evidence that the conversation surface is the wrong locus. Consolidation burden per {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} engaged: ships inside saga, no new plugin.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: saga ship-ceremony script callable from both a slash command and an installable git alias/hook pack, plus install/uninstall tooling and docs.

title: Executable checks manifest: kill the hand-maintained CI mirror in CLAUDE.md
idea: This repo's own CLAUDE.md carries the fossil of a past parity bug: 'Run type checking (match CI scope — CI checks plugins/ scripts/ tests/, not just plugins/)' — a hand-written prose mirror of CI config that already drifted once and was patched with a warning parenthetical instead of a structural fix. Reframe local-vs-CI parity as a contract with a single executable source: a checks manifest (one small file listing each check's command and scope) that CI workflows consume and a local runner executes, so 'run what CI runs' is mechanical and the CLAUDE.md section becomes generated or reduced to 'run the manifest'. This is the same contract-mirror-drift disease as the 4-repo T14 evidence, caught living inside the fleet's own instruction file.
basis: CLAUDE.md:126 (verified today): '# Run type checking (match CI scope — CI checks plugins/ scripts/ tests/, not just plugins/)' — prose mirroring CI scope, i.e. a hand-copy of a machine contract. Pattern match: grounding brief section 3.1 'contract-mirror drift... validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract)' and section 7 pattern 10 'Local-vs-CI verification parity gaps — CI red on checks local runs passed (2 repos)'.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: checks-manifest file + local runner script + CI workflow refactored to consume the manifest + CLAUDE.md quality-checks section replaced by the single runner invocation, with a drift test asserting CI and manifest agree.

title: Enforcement-locus inversion: the context library's CI audits the fleet's vendored mirrors, not the other way around
idea: The obvious T9 ideas inject library content into plugin prompts at runtime — fighting the org's own convention, which is schema-validate-in-CI plus a self-describing index, explicitly not runtime-injected blobs. Invert the direction of consumption instead: the fleet already knows exactly which contracts get hand-copied and drift (vendored sdlc-schema.json, validate_card_body vs card_validator.py, vocab tuples), so add a census job — living in the library's CI, which already runs check_docs.py and context_census.py — that walks consumer repos' known mirror sites, diffs them against source of truth, and opens drift issues automatically. Enforcement fires where the authority lives, on the cadence of the authority changing, with zero prompt-token cost. Merges T9 and T14 at their shared root.
basis: Grounding brief section 4: 'Enforcement already exists inside the library: validate.yml CI runs check_docs.py... + context_census.py --check... The org convention is schema-validate-in-CI + self-describing index, not runtime-injected blobs' and 'Absent: ... any reference to the library from this repo's CI.' Drift evidence: section 3.1, four independent repos, including the 343-card validate_card_body incident (#222).
outcome_shape: Merged PR (cross-repo): mirror-site registry file in this repo + census job extension in infiquetra-context-library CI that diffs registered mirrors and files drift issues via mission-control.

title: Subject-scoped promotion: the >=3-repo transcendence bar is why zero learnings have ever promoted
idea: The promote loop has fired zero times, and the reflex diagnosis is coverage (219 dark codex sessions). Attack the bar instead: recurrence-counting assumes the same lesson gets independently re-learned and identically worded in 3+ repos, but one shared operator plus shared tooling means a harness quirk is learned once, documented once, and never recurs — exactly the 1-repo/4-quirks Claude Code runtime constraints that bind every repo yet can never clear a 3-repo bar. Rekey promotion eligibility by the learning's SUBJECT: if the subject is fleet-shared infrastructure (Claude Code harness behavior, gh/uv semantics, plugin contracts, org conventions), a single well-evidenced learning is already transcendent; repo-local subjects keep the recurrence bar. The /promote pass stays manual, gated, and agent-judged — only the eligibility predicate changes.
basis: Grounding brief section 3.5: 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster. The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.' Counterexample in the same document, section 3.4: 'Claude Code runtime quirks recorded as durable build constraints (bg-dispatch loses channel notifications; agents/*.md not auto-loaded; protocol byte-identity) — 1 repo, 4 distinct quirks' — universally binding constraints structurally unable to satisfy the recurrence bar.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: promote_scan.py / promote skill gains a subject-scope classifier (fleet-shared vs repo-local) and dual eligibility rules, plus the first actual promotion of the 4 runtime-quirk learnings as validation.

title: Revisit-when conditions become checkable predicates: decisions re-open on evidence, not memory
idea: The binding-decision register is the backbone of this whole ideation process, and every row carries a revisit-when clause — yet nothing anywhere evaluates those clauses; they are prose dead letters that depend on someone remembering them at the right moment. That is the same disease as the journal's stale-claim learnings (provenance must be re-verified against current state). Make revisit-when machinery: DECISIONS.md entries carry an optional machine-checkable predicate (a grep, a file-exists, a version threshold, a registry lookup), and a /retro-time (or CI) sweep evaluates them and flags decisions whose revisit condition has come true — e.g. {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} auto-flags the day a read-only-sandbox profile ships, and {#worker-cache-scheduling} flags when idle-poll telemetry crosses its stated threshold. First-principles argument: a constraint whose release condition is unmonitored converges to a permanent constraint, so the fleet silently ossifies around decisions whose premises have expired; cheap predicate evaluation is strictly better than relying on human recall across dozens of decisions and months of drift.
basis: Argument: (1) the grounding brief's own rule — 'ideas contradicting one must engage its revisit-when' (section 2 header) — makes revisit-when clauses load-bearing gates for all future work; (2) every listed clause ('read-only-sandbox profile ships', 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient', 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue') is a testable world-state, yet no process, CI job, or skill step evaluates any of them; (3) the journal independently records 4 learnings that unverified stale claims persist until lucky operator recall (grounding section 6.2) — the identical failure mode. Therefore unmonitored revisit conditions guarantee either ossification (constraint outlives its premise) or accidental violation (someone forgets the constraint exists); a predicate sweep eliminates both at near-zero cost.
outcome_shape: Merged PR: DECISIONS.md entry schema gains an optional revisit-check field + a sweep script wired into /retro (and optionally CI) that evaluates predicates and emits a came-true report, with existing register entries backfilled where checkable.

title: Fleet capability registry that GENERATES its mirrors instead of guarding them
idea: Invert the drift-guard posture: instead of writing reactive tests for each producer/consumer mirror pair (tier tables, engine-worker tables, agent rosters), define one machine-readable fleet-registry (tiers, engines, intents, agent roster, caps) from which the mirrored surfaces are rendered — the /plan unit-tier table, the team-execution Step A7 worker table, and future ENGINE_INTENTS consumers all become generated blocks with a render script and a CI check that rendered output matches source. Every future vocabulary change (a new model, a new intent, a rename) becomes a one-file edit plus regen, and every new mirror is drift-proof by construction. Drift-guard tests themselves become auto-enumerated from the registry's declared producer/consumer pairs rather than hand-written per incident. Preserves {#tier-vocab-ordering}: the registry stores ordered ladders, and the renderer emits them in ladder order.
basis: Grounding brief §1 correction (c): ENGINE_INTENTS is a hand-mirrored producer/consumer pair — 'authored in /plan (plan/SKILL.md:303-304), rendered in team-execution Step A7 worker table (team-execution/SKILL.md:229-233)'. Grounding §3 finding 1: contract-mirror drift recurred in 4 independent repos, including validate_card_body's stale hand-copy that failed 343 'clean' cards (#222). Recent commit 46b7001 shipped yet another one-off 'registration drift guard' — the incident-driven guard pattern is already recurring in this repo.
outcome_shape: Merged fleet/registry.json + scripts/render_registry.py + CI check, with at least the /plan tier table and the team-execution engine-worker table converted to generated blocks and one auto-enumerated drift-guard test replacing a hand-written one.

title: One dispatch-time tier resolver instead of 24 frontmatter edits
idea: The obvious fix for fable/xhigh unreachability is adding model/effort fields to every agent frontmatter — which creates 24 new hardcoded surfaces that drift. The leverage move: generalize saga's readonly-verifier per-call override pattern (the fleet's only existing dispatch-time lever) into a shared tier_resolver primitive that any spawn site calls with (work-shape, run-mode, operator-override) and gets (model, effort) back, reading defaults and ladders from the fleet registry. Frontmatter model fields demote to last-resort fallback; tier-policy changes become one edit; new plugins inherit the lever for free instead of re-deciding tiering per agent. This also gives the intake's asymmetric spend-approval rule (attended vs unattended) exactly one enforcement point instead of N prompt paragraphs.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model: (opus/sonnet/haiku), zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution), no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga's readonly-verifier per-call pattern' and 'fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary.' The per-call pattern is a verified working seam to generalize, not a greenfield invention. Compatible with {#operator-choice-framework} (doc-only, CLI-driven): the resolver is machinery under the existing doc-driven choice, not a new choice surface.
outcome_shape: Merged tier_resolver helper (saga scripts or shared lib) + adoption at three named spawn sites (team-execution worker dispatch, saga verify-panel, workflow emitter docs) with frontmatter demoted to fallback.

title: Resource lease broker: one primitive for concurrency slots AND worktree/teardown reclamation
idea: Do not extend VERIFY_N_CAP into a global constant — constants govern one spawn site each and teach nothing. Instead ship a tiny file-based lease broker: any spawner (team-execution reviewer fan-out, workflow emitters, /outcome leaf dispatch, engine bridges) acquires a lease before spawning; leases carry TTLs and name the resources held (agent slot, worktree path). Expiry drives two second-order wins for free: rate-limit governance (max-3 becomes a broker policy, not per-script discipline) and stale-resource reclamation (the 15 abandoned worktrees are exactly expired leases nobody swept). The broker's ledger is also free telemetry — who spawns what, when 429s hit — feeding cache-economics and tier decisions later. Engages the binding /optimize shed explicitly: optimize/SKILL.md deliberately sheds its own max_concurrent fan-out and stays serial-by-default; the broker does not re-add a local knob to /optimize — it governs the fleet-level shared resource, and the revisit trigger has fired: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting' and 'KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery' show per-skill discipline does not compose.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7 (execution_spec.py:114)... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded'; verified today: execution_spec.py comments say the cap 'directly guards rate-limit overcorrection (R3: 22/23-judges panel)'. Grounding §4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+'. Grounding §7 pattern 4 (3 repos): rate-limit fan-out kills. Intake added constraint: max 3 concurrent, currently enforced only by workflow-script convention.
outcome_shape: Merged concurrency_lease.py (acquire/release/TTL/sweep) + a reclamation sweep command + adoption in team-execution fan-out and saga verify-panel, with the max-3 policy expressed as broker config.

title: Fleet-wide cost-fact ledger so tier recommendations cite priors instead of re-reasoning
idea: Session mining shows tier reasoning is re-derived ad hoc every run, and the one hard cache-economics number the fleet owns (350-450k tokens in under 20 minutes for read-only recon fan-out) was captured by luck. Generalize the /outcome campaign's 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' rule fleet-wide: an append-only JSONL ledger any unit writes (unit shape, tier used, tokens, wall time, outcome), plus a reader that /plan's tier table and the intake's spend-lever prompt query for priors ('last 5 recon fan-outs on sonnet averaged N tokens'). Compounding: every run makes the next run's tier recommendation cheaper and more defensible, the spend-approval dialog quotes real numbers, and cache-first-vs-throughput stops being a vibes debate. Extends, not contradicts, the /outcome U1-U11 decision — same fact-shape, wider producers.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 6 (3 repos): 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses.' §7 singleton: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)'. §2 binding register, /outcome campaign: 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' — this idea widens the producer set under the same rule.
outcome_shape: Merged ledger schema + writer helper + /plan tier-table step that surfaces ledger priors when recommending unit tiers.

title: Execution receipts: one append-only integrity envelope every bridge must emit
idea: Silent no-ops keep recurring because each bridge (agy, codex, engine bridges, workflow emitters) invents its own success signal, and 'ran' is inferred from absence of error. Define ONE receipt contract — a small append-only JSON envelope the delegated side must write (engine identity, exit evidence, artifact hashes, timestamps) — plus one shared checker the dispatching side runs. New bridges inherit integrity for free instead of re-learning the agy-silent-fallback lesson; the checker also closes the evidence chain-of-custody hole (a PASS can never overwrite a FAIL because receipts are append-only and hash-linked). This converts five separate journal learnings from 'be careful' prose into a structural impossibility, which is the compounding: verification cost per new bridge drops to adopting a schema.
basis: Grounding brief §6 item 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings: agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter mismatch) — any bridge/delegation idea needs did-it-actually-run/persist verification.' §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody).' Two independently-mined failure families, one shared root cause: no common execution-evidence contract.
outcome_shape: Merged receipt schema doc + receipt.py writer/checker + two existing bridges (agy delegate, one engine bridge) converted, with a test that a missing receipt fails the dispatch.

title: Decision tripwires: make every DECISIONS.md revisit-when machine-checkable
idea: The binding-decision register is governance prose: every entry carries a revisit-when condition that no process ever evaluates, so decisions silently outlive their premises (the /optimize shed's revisit conditions arguably already fired via the rate-limit findings, and nobody noticed until this ideation). Add a tripwire convention: DECISIONS.md entries may carry a machine-checkable probe (a shell/python one-liner: count stale worktrees, count 429 failures in the ledger, check promote-ledger emptiness), and a decision_tripwires runner — invoked by /retro or CI — evaluates them and surfaces 'this decision is now revisitable' signals. Second-order effect: the journal stops being write-only memory and becomes a live governor; every future ideation round starts with an automatically-current binding register instead of a hand-rebuilt one, and the cost of maintaining decision hygiene drops toward zero.
basis: Grounding brief §2: every binding decision in the register carries an explicit 'Revisit-when' clause (e.g. worker-cache-scheduling: 'named-teammate residency proves insufficient, or idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue'), yet §6 item 2 records 4 learnings that 'provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state' — the fleet has documented evidence that unevaluated standing claims rot, and revisit-when clauses are exactly such standing claims. This idea engages the register itself rather than any single decision: it operationalizes revisit-when instead of contradicting anything.
outcome_shape: Merged tripwire frontmatter convention in the engineering-journal practice + decision_tripwires.py runner + /retro step that reports fired tripwires, with 3 existing decisions backfilled with probes.

title: Fix the never-fired promote loop by moving clustering cost to capture time (learning slugs)
idea: The promote pipeline has never promoted anything — not because the machinery is broken but because clustering freeform prose across 19 repos after the fact is expensive and lossy, so no ≥3-repo cluster ever surfaces. Change the economics: learnings get tagged at capture with topic slugs from a small controlled vocabulary (drawn from the fleet registry of H-F4-1, so vocabulary has one home), making cross-repo clustering a grep and the ≥3-repo transcendence threshold machine-checkable. The 219 dark codex sessions become minable into the same slug space instead of requiring bespoke synthesis. Compounding: every learning written after the convention lands makes the next /promote pass cheaper, converting a dead loop into one whose marginal cost falls with use.
basis: Grounding brief §3 item 5: 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine ≥3-repo transcendent cluster. The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.' §7: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap.' A loop that exists but never fires is an economics problem, not a missing-feature problem; the fix belongs at the capture margin where cost is near zero, not the scan margin where it is maximal.
outcome_shape: Merged slug vocabulary + journal-entry frontmatter convention (updated shared practice doc) + promote_scan.py slug-clustering mode + a backfill pass over this repo's LEARNINGS.md.

title: Confirmed-gate wrapper: fleet-owned silence-is-HALT gating above the unreliable harness primitive
idea: Gate B struck AskUserQuestion reliability as harness-level and out of scope — correct for fixing the primitive, but it leaves every gate in every skill still DEPENDING on a primitive documented to auto-proceed on timeout, treating silence as consent. The fleet-side move is in scope: one thin confirmed-gate wrapper (skill reference + tiny helper) that requires an affirmative artifact (an answer token or file the operator's response produces) before proceeding, and treats absence as HALT — aligning with the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade rule rather than contradicting anything. Compounding: every gate in every skill inherits silence-is-HALT from one adoption point, and when the harness primitive eventually improves, only the wrapper changes. Uncomfortable on purpose: it asserts the fleet should stop trusting a harness primitive it cannot fix, rather than waiting.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 2 (6 repos): 'AskUserQuestion silently auto-proceeds on timeout treating silence as consent (documented operator fury), fires before answers are captured, errors outright; agents fall back to plain-text questions.' §8 Gate-B resolution struck only the harness-primitive fix ('harness-level, out of scope'); a fleet-owned wrapper is plugin machinery, squarely in scope, and extends the binding /outcome rule 'HALT-not-degrade' to attended gates.
outcome_shape: Merged confirmed_gate reference doc + helper + adoption at two named gates (/work merge confirmation, /outcome pause points), with a test that timeout/silence yields HALT.

title: Provider registry entries carry cost/latency metadata so routing changes reprice the whole fleet
idea: The intake already commits to one registry-driven router plugin. The compounding extension an obvious pass will miss: make each provider registry entry carry cost-per-token and latency-class metadata, and have the tier resolver (H-F4-2), the spend-lever prompt, and /plan's offload recommendations all read prices from that single registry. Then adding Ollama at $0 automatically reshapes offload defaults everywhere without touching a single skill prompt; a DeepSeek price change is a registry edit, not a prompt archaeology expedition. The registry becomes the fleet's price oracle — one write point, N read points — which is the difference between a router that routes and a router that governs spend. Stays inside {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} and {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}: pricing informs offload/second-opinion selection, never gate participation.
basis: Intake brief §Resolved tensions 5 names the seam ('one router plugin, registry-driven — extend the existing engine-registry seam (engine_resolver.py / engine_registry.py); each provider is a registry entry + bridge script') and §4 requires every Fable-tier line to carry 'a recommendation plus a cheaper fallback.' First-principles: a cheaper-fallback recommendation is only honest if the system knows relative prices; without price metadata in the registry, every skill that recommends a fallback must hardcode its own price beliefs, recreating the exact mirror-drift disease §3 documents. Therefore price metadata belongs at the single point providers are already being registered — the marginal cost is a few JSON fields, and every downstream lever inherits currency.
outcome_shape: Merged registry schema extension (cost/latency fields on engine entries) + one consumer converted (/plan offload recommendation reads registry prices) + doc note in the router plugin.

title: Token-bucket + circuit-breaker admission control for all fan-out bridges
idea: Borrow the token-bucket rate limiter and Hystrix-style circuit breaker from resilient distributed-systems / API-gateway design. Instead of a static concurrency cap of 3, ship a shared admission-control library (`concurrency_governor.py`) that every fan-out site imports: team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, workflow emitters, and engine bridges each request a token before spawning. On a 429 the breaker trips open for that provider, sheds load, and half-opens with exponential backoff — turning 'aspiration, not machinery' into a real shared meter. The bucket refill rate is the operator's spend/rate lever, not a hard-coded 3.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded' and only VERIFY_N_CAP=7 exists (execution_spec.py:114); §7 pattern 4 '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery'. Engages theme-13 seed and /optimize's deliberately-removed max_concurrent (optimize/SKILL.md:18) by making the cap a refillable meter, not a fixed knob.
outcome_shape: Merged `plugins/saga/scripts/concurrency_governor.py` (token-bucket + per-provider circuit breaker) plus adoption diffs at the three named fan-out sites and a drift-guard test asserting no unbounded spawn loop remains.

title: Dead-man's switch / heartbeat watchdog for delegated bridges
idea: Aviation and industrial control use a dead-man's switch: a worker must periodically assert liveness or the system assumes failure and acts. Apply it to delegation integrity — every bridge dispatch (agy, codex, engine workers, /outcome leaves) writes a heartbeat token to a known path on start and on each progress checkpoint; a lightweight watchdog in the coordinator treats missing heartbeats past a deadline as a silent no-op and re-pings or fails loud, rather than accepting a Claude-fallback as success. This directly attacks 'subagents idle without delivering' and 'agy silent Claude-fallback'.
basis: Grounding brief §6 pattern 1 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (agy silent Claude-fallback...)' and §7 pattern 9 'Subagents idle without delivering... coordinator must detect and re-ping (also reproduced live in this very session)'. Aligns with never-gatekeepers: watchdog is advisory liveness, not a gate decision.
outcome_shape: Merged heartbeat-token contract doc + `bridge_watchdog.py` helper and integration at agy/codex/engine dispatch sites, with a test that a stalled worker is flagged rather than reported complete.

title: Chain-of-custody evidence ledger with content-addressed immutability
idea: Forensic evidence handling and blockchain both solve 'prove this artifact was not silently overwritten' via content-addressing and an append-only custody log. The grounding brief records a probe overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS — a chain-of-custody break. Ship an evidence-ledger helper that hashes each verification artifact (content-addressed filename), refuses in-place overwrite, and appends {hash, producer, timestamp, verdict} to an immutable ledger. Saga verify/qa/code-review write through it, so provenance claims are re-derivable from hashes instead of trusted memory.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singletons: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS (audit chain-of-custody)'; §6 pattern 2 'Provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state'. Reinforces derive-on-read (§6 pattern 5) by making evidence content-addressed rather than mutable.
outcome_shape: Merged `evidence_ledger.py` (content-addressed write + append-only custody log) wired into saga qa/verify artifact writes, with a test proving a second write of the same logical artifact cannot clobber the first.

title: Byzantine-quorum weighting for cross-engine consensus review
idea: Distributed consensus (PBFT / weighted quorum) tolerates faulty nodes by weighting votes and requiring a supermajority, not naive unanimity. Consensus review currently reconciles Claude+Codex by hand (15/17 convergence). Formalize a portable quorum protocol: each reviewer emits typed findings with a confidence weight; agreement above a quorum threshold auto-confirms, disagreements surface as the reconcile set for Claude (verifier-of-record) to adjudicate. This makes the 15/17 hand-reconciliation mechanical and portable across engines while keeping external engines advisory-only.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' and §3 finding 2 (consensus catching defects green suites missed). Engages binding decision {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} — quorum is advisory input; Claude adjudicates the disagreement set, preserving verifier-of-record.
outcome_shape: Merged consensus-quorum protocol spec + reference implementation in team-execution that emits an auto-confirmed set and a Claude-adjudication set, with a fixture reproducing the 15/17 split.

title: Working-set / LRU cache-line reasoning for worker-tier reuse
idea: CPU cache design reasons about working sets, cache lines, and eviction (LRU) to maximize hit rate under a fixed budget. Cache economics currently derives (segment+agent+tier) saga-side with segment = plugin directory. Add a working-set analyzer that, given a plan's unit graph, computes the (segment,tier) reuse profile and reorders/batches units to maximize warm-worker hits — the same way a compiler schedules to reduce cache misses — and reports a projected hit-rate before the run. The 350–450k-token recon number becomes a measurable baseline to beat.
basis: Binding decision {#worker-cache-scheduling}: derive (segment+agent+tier) saga-side, segment boundary = plugin directory; revisit-when 'idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue'. This idea stays inside that architecture — it adds a scheduling/ordering analyzer over the existing derivation, engaging the revisit condition by treating batch ordering as a wave-queue precursor. Number from §7 singletons: 350–450k tokens in <20 min recon fan-outs.
outcome_shape: Merged `worker_working_set.py` analyzer producing a projected warm-hit-rate + suggested unit batch order, with a test on a multi-segment plan fixture.

title: Consumer-driven contract tests (Pact-style) for vocabulary propagation
idea: Microservice teams stop schema drift with consumer-driven contract testing (Pact): each consumer publishes the contract it expects, and the provider's CI fails if it breaks any consumer's expectation. The fleet has the exact disease — validate_card_body was a stale hand-copy of card_validator.py, 343 'clean' cards failed the live contract. Ship a contract-broker convention: each contract copy (card validators, sdlc-schema, tier vocab) declares its source-of-truth provider; a CI guard fetches the provider and fails on byte/semantic drift, so a rename in the source breaks the consumer's build loudly instead of silently.
basis: Grounding brief §3 finding 1 'validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract, → #222)' and finding 3 'contract copies drifting from source of truth'; theme 14. External prior art: Pact consumer-driven contract testing (pact.io).
outcome_shape: Merged contract-manifest format + CI guard script that diffs each declared consumer copy against its provider and fails on drift, seeded with the card_validator/sdlc-schema pairs.

title: Power-grid economic dispatch for provider/model routing
idea: Electricity grids solve economic dispatch: meet demand by stacking generators cheapest-first up a merit order, subject to each unit's capacity and ramp limits. Model the provider router the same way — registry entries carry (marginal cost, latency, capacity/rate-limit, capability floor); the resolver builds a merit-order stack and dispatches each unit to the cheapest provider that clears its capability floor and has headroom, spilling to the next when a provider saturates (429). Ollama sits at $0 baseload; DeepSeek is cheap mid-merit; Opus/Fable are peakers reserved for judgment units.
basis: Intake brief §5 'one router plugin, registry-driven — extend engine_resolver.py / engine_registry.py; Ollama → $0 offload target; DeepSeek → cheap second opinion'. Stays inside the registry-seam decision. Engages {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} by keeping merit-order dispatch to worker/offload roles, not executor residency. External prior art: power-system economic dispatch / merit-order stacking.
outcome_shape: Merged merit-order fields in engine_registry entries + a dispatch function in engine_resolver that selects provider by cost-under-capability-floor with 429 spillover, plus a routing-decision test matrix.

title: Manufacturing andon-cord + poka-yoke for the ship ceremony
idea: Toyota's production system uses poka-yoke (mistake-proofing so a step physically cannot be done wrong) and the andon cord (any worker halts the line on a defect). The 8-repo manual ship ceremony (commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup by raw git) is an un-mistake-proofed hand assembly. Ship a single ceremony command that encodes the whole sequence as a poka-yoke checklist — each step gated on the prior's verified success, stacked-PR CI-trigger and branch-cleanup handled — with an andon halt: any failed step stops and surfaces rather than half-completing. HALT-not-degrade, matching the /outcome campaign posture.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 1 'Manual ship ceremony ... done by raw git/gh in session after session, even where saga/mission-control is installed (8 repos)'; singletons on stacked-PR auto-close + CI branch-trigger gap and gh pr merge --auto surprises. Honors {#outcome-campaign} HALT-not-degrade. External prior art: Toyota Production System poka-yoke + andon cord.
outcome_shape: Merged saga ship-ceremony command that runs the commit-through-cleanup sequence as gated poka-yoke steps with andon halt-on-failure, covering stacked-PR CI trigger and branch cleanup, plus a dry-run test.

title: Currency-exchange fungibility layer for the model/effort tier palette
idea: Money markets make heterogeneous currencies fungible via a common exchange with published rates and convertibility everywhere. Today fable/xhigh are legal tender only in saga's /plan vocabulary; every agent frontmatter hardcodes model with zero effort field. Introduce a tier-exchange layer: a single canonical (model,effort) tuple type that any dispatch site can hold, plus resolvers that convert a plan-authored tier into a dispatch-time override for agent spawns — making fable/xhigh spendable currency fleet-wide, honoring the ordered-escalation-ladder semantics rather than a flat enum.
basis: Grounding brief §1 'fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary', '0 of 24 effort fields in team-execution', 'no dispatch-time override lever anywhere except saga readonly-verifier'. Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} 'tuples are ordered escalation ladders' by preserving ladder order across the exchange. QUEUED seed {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort}.
outcome_shape: Merged canonical tier-tuple type + a dispatch-time resolver that lets a plan-authored tier drive agent spawn model/effort, with team-execution consuming it and a test proving xhigh reaches a spawned worker.

title: Garbage-collection reachability sweep for stale worktree reclamation
idea: Runtime garbage collectors reclaim memory by tracing reachability from live roots and sweeping the unreachable. The repo has 15 stale abandoned saga worktrees inflating it 10x, same disease as team-execution's missing teardown (Step B8). Ship a mark-and-sweep reclaimer: enumerate live roots (active sagas, open PRs, running teams), mark their worktrees reachable, and sweep the rest — with a grace generation (like a nursery) so freshly created worktrees aren't collected mid-flight. Run at ceremony end and as an on-demand /reclaim, turning teardown from a forgotten manual step into a periodic sweep.
basis: Grounding brief §4 'Hygiene find: 15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+ → direct evidence for theme 6 (teardown/reclamation), same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8'. External prior art: tracing (mark-sweep) garbage collection with generational nursery.
outcome_shape: Merged `worktree_reclaim.py` mark-and-sweep with a grace-generation guard + a /reclaim entry point and ceremony-end hook, with a test that live-rooted worktrees survive and stale ones are swept.

title: Tier shadow audit: sampled counterfactual replay one tier down turns tier tables from vibes into evidence
