idea: Flip: with 10x Fable budget you would replay every unit at every tier and know exactly what each tier buys. The practical kernel at 1x: sample 1-in-N completed units (plan units, review lenses, verify panels) and silently re-run the same unit one rung lower on the ordered MODELS/EFFORTS ladder, diff the outputs, and log sufficient/insufficient to the cost ledger. Over weeks this produces an empirical per-stage tier-value dataset, so the tier line in every plan carries a measured recommendation instead of ad hoc reasoning re-derived each session. Sampling is spend-increasing, so per intake tension 1 it is off in attended mode without explicit operator yes and budget-capped in unattended mode. Engages {#tier-vocab-ordering} directly: 'one tier lower' is only well-defined because the tuples are ordered escalation ladders (execution_spec.py:52-53).
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 6: 'Ad hoc tier reasoning every time — xhigh-Opus on everything is wasteful; manual per-unit tier tables; operator asking for mid-run model-change pauses (3 repos)'. Intake tension 4 requires every tier line to carry a recommendation plus cheaper fallback — but no mechanism anywhere in the fleet produces evidence for that recommendation; MODELS/EFFORTS ordering verified at plugins/saga/scripts/execution_spec.py:52-53.
outcome_shape: Merged: a shadow-audit sampling hook in saga /work + team-execution, a tier-evidence ledger schema, and a report script that renders per-stage tier sufficiency rates consumed by /plan's tier table.

title: The promote loop is dead wiring: treat 0-promotions-ever as a silent no-op defect, not a high bar
idea: Uncomfortable cross-cut of T15 into T10: the fleet's own dead-wiring lens (producer exists, consumer exists, nothing ever flows) applied to /promote condemns the cross-repo learning pipeline itself — it has existed for months and produced zero output, exactly the signature the journal warns about in bridges. Flip 'promotion is rare and precious' to 'promotion is mandatory': every /retro must either promote or emit a machine-readable why-not record. Practical kernel: promote_scan emits near-miss clusters (2-repo, not just >=3-repo) into a decaying candidate ledger, and a quarterly promotion-or-postmortem check fails loudly if the ledger only ever decays — forcing a diagnosis of whether the threshold, the journal vocabulary mismatch across repos, or the scan itself is the blocker. Keeps /promote manual and gated; adds pressure and instrumentation, not autonomy.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 5: 'Promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted; no genuine >=3-repo transcendent cluster. The cross-repo learning loop exists but has never fired.' Combined with section 6 item 1: 5+ learnings on silent no-ops and dead wiring ('dead-wiring producer+consumer') — the promote pipeline matches that defect signature exactly.
outcome_shape: Merged: promote_scan near-miss cluster mode + candidate-decay ledger + a promotion-or-postmortem check wired into /retro guidance, with the first postmortem record explaining the 0-promotion history.

title: Zero-token fire drill: run one canonical lifecycle loop entirely on the $0 registry entry and publish the irreducibility map
idea: Flip Fable budget to $0: everything must run on the Ollama registry entry. Most of the fleet has never been exercised this way, so nobody actually knows which lifecycle stages degrade gracefully, which produce garbage, and which structurally cannot be de-Clauded (gated decisions, where never-gatekeepers makes Claude the verifier-of-record by decision, not by cost). The kernel: a repeatable drill — scripted canonical loop (spec -> plan -> work -> review on a toy change) forced through the router's $0 provider — whose output is a per-stage 'minimum viable tier' map committed as a reference doc. The map is the missing empirical floor under both the router plugin's offload defaults and every cheaper-fallback line intake tension 4 requires. Re-run the drill when the registry gains a provider; the diff is the provider's real value.
basis: Intake brief section 'Resolved tensions' item 5 (Provider reach): 'one router plugin, registry-driven... Ollama -> $0 offload target' — the $0 target is named but no mechanism validates what $0 can actually carry. Constrained by {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} (#283): gated decisions stay Claude regardless of budget, which is precisely what the drill's irreducibility map documents rather than contradicts.
outcome_shape: Merged: a drill script + fixture change in the router plugin's test surface, and a references/minimum-viable-tier-map.md updated per drill run.

title: Execution receipts: one nonce-challenge receipt contract for every bridge, missing receipt = hard fail
idea: Flip trust to zero: assume every delegation bridge (agy, codex, workflow emitters, Task spawns, engine bridges) silently no-ops until proven otherwise. The kernel is a single fleet-wide receipt contract instead of per-bridge ad hoc checks: the caller mints a nonce; the delegate must return a receipt containing the nonce echo plus a runtime fingerprint that only the real runtime can produce (provider model id, actual token counts, engine version string), and the caller validates before consuming any result. agy's silent Claude-fallback becomes structurally impossible — a Claude fallback cannot forge a codex/gemini runtime fingerprint. One schema, one validator script, adopted bridge by bridge; a drift-guard test enumerates known spawn sites and fails when a bridge lacks receipt wiring, converting 'did it actually run' from a per-incident learning into an enforced invariant.
basis: Grounding brief section 6 item 1: 'Silent no-ops in delegation & dead wiring (5+ learnings: agy silent Claude-fallback, dead-wiring producer+consumer, test-shape-masks-dead-wiring, fake-adapter mismatch) — any bridge/delegation idea needs did-it-actually-run/persist verification.' Aligned with {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch} (#318): receipts strengthen chaperone dispatch by proving which runtime the chaperone actually reached.
outcome_shape: Merged: receipt schema + shared validator script + receipt wiring in the agy and codex bridges first, plus a spawn-site enumeration drift-guard test.

title: Operator-absence contract: every gate declares its machine-readable no-answer behavior, linted fleet-wide
idea: Flip to zero operators for two weeks: every gate in the fleet either halts forever, guesses, or silently auto-proceeds — and today nobody can say which gates do which. Kernel: a declared absence-behavior field for every gate site (HALT / safe-default-with-record / escalate-to-channel), stated in the skill text next to the gate and enumerable by a lint that walks all plugins and fails on any undeclared gate. Default posture is HALT, matching the /outcome campaign's HALT-not-degrade decision; silence-as-consent becomes impossible to ship accidentally because the lint forces the author to write the word. This deliberately does NOT touch the AskUserQuestion primitive itself (struck at Gate B as harness-level): it is plugin-layer policy about what the surrounding skill does when no answer arrives, which is entirely this repo's locus.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 pattern 2: 'AskUserQuestion silently auto-proceeds on timeout treating silence as consent (documented operator fury)... (6 repos)' plus the Gate-B resolution striking primitive reliability as out of scope — this idea occupies the in-scope remainder. Engages the /outcome campaign binding decision's HALT-not-degrade as the mandated default absence behavior.
outcome_shape: Merged: an absence-behavior convention doc, declarations added to all saga/team-execution gate sites, and a gate-inventory lint in CI that fails on undeclared gates.

title: Shed, don't cap: a 429-driven preemption supervisor with a requeue ledger instead of static concurrency knobs
idea: Flip to 100 concurrent agents against real rate limits: static admission caps are the wrong shape because the limit is a moving external signal, not a known constant — which is plausibly why /optimize deliberately removed its max_concurrent knob rather than tuning it. Kernel: govern reactively. Every fan-out tags spawns with a shed-priority; a lightweight supervisor watches for 429/limit signals and, on pressure, kills the lowest-priority in-flight agents and writes them to a requeue ledger for serial replay after backoff, so a rate-limit storm degrades to slower instead of '6 of 7 agents failed'. VERIFY_N_CAP stays as the panel-size sanity bound it was born as; this adds the runtime layer that caps structurally cannot provide. The intake's cap-of-3 becomes just the most conservative shed-priority profile rather than a hand-enforced rule in workflow scripts.
basis: Grounding brief section 1: 'the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded. Notably, /optimize deliberately removed a max_concurrent knob (optimize/SKILL.md:18) — ideation on theme 13 must engage why' — verified: optimize/SKILL.md sheds max_concurrent fan-out by design, re-entering only via operator escalation. Plus section 7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting; the emitter has no concurrency knob... KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery.' The shed design honors /optimize's removal (no new static knob) while fixing the unbounded-fan-out deaths.
outcome_shape: Merged: shed-priority tagging convention + a requeue-ledger schema and supervisor loop in the workflow emitter path, with team-execution reviewer fan-out as first adopter.

title: Recon memoization: tree-hash-keyed committed survey artifacts so 400k-token recon fan-outs run once per tree state
idea: Flip to nothing-cached and the 350-450k-token read-only recon fan-outs become intolerable, exposing that recon is an expensive pure function of the git tree being recomputed from scratch every session. Kernel: memoize it — survey outputs (plugin inventory, agent-frontmatter maps, spawn-site enumerations) become committed artifacts keyed by the git tree hash of their input paths; a cache-check helper returns the stored artifact on key match and only dispatches the fan-out on miss. This engages the derive-on-read decision rather than contradicting it: derive-on-read exists because committed state goes stale, but a tree-hash key makes staleness structurally impossible (any input change changes the key, forcing a miss) — so the rejected-alternative rationale does not apply. Orthogonal to {#worker-cache-scheduling}, which governs prompt-cache residency in workers; this is artifact-level reuse across sessions where no worker survives.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 singletons: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)', combined with section 6 item 5 ('Derive-on-read over committed state — recurring rejected alternative') whose staleness rationale is explicitly engaged via content-addressed keying, and {#worker-cache-scheduling}'s scope (worker residency, segment=plugin dir) which this does not touch.
outcome_shape: Merged: a recon-cache helper script + convention doc in saga, with one high-traffic survey (agent-frontmatter/model inventory) converted as the proving case.

title: The marketplace is the contract bus: distribute shared contracts as plugin surface, making drift a version check
idea: Flip vendoring to its extreme opposite — no repo ever copies a contract; everything resolves from the source of truth at use time. The practical kernel: the fleet already operates a distribution channel with versioning, installation, and update mechanics — the plugin marketplace itself. Shared contracts (sdlc-schema.json, card_validator logic, tier vocabulary) ship inside the plugin that owns them (mission-control, saga) and consumer repos call the installed plugin's script instead of a hand-copied validate_card_body; the 343-cards-failed class of drift collapses into 'your installed plugin is version X, upstream is Y', which existing version-drift guards already know how to check. No new plugin (satisfying the groom-17-to-7 burden of proof) — this is a re-homing of contract copies into plugins that are already installed in the 8 repos where the ship-ceremony mining found saga/mission-control present.
basis: Grounding brief section 3 item 1: 'validate_card_body stale hand-copy of the real card_validator.py (343 clean cards failed the live contract, -> #222), re-vendored sdlc-schema.json' — 4-repo recurrence. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: no new plugin is created; contract copies consolidate into existing installed plugins.
outcome_shape: Merged: card_validator exposed as a callable contract surface of mission-control with a documented consumer pattern, plus removal of one downstream hand-copy and a consumer-side version-pin check.

title: Issues as execution envelopes: mission-control emits a machine-readable intent block that /outcome ingestion can run
idea: Flip: every GitHub issue, once created, is executable by a dispatcher with no human interpretation. The kernel that survives realism: issue bodies gain a structured execution-envelope section — tier recommendation with cheaper fallback, backend posture, gate answers ('PR reviews required?', 'gate or auto merge?'), budget note — written at creation time by mission-control:issue / saga:handoff and validated by the same card_validator surface. This gives the confirmed-missing /outcome Objective-ingestion path a typed input contract instead of prose archaeology: ingestion parses envelopes, not paragraphs. It is intent capture, not committed status, so it stays inside the /outcome campaign decisions — derived-on-read status untouched, backend menu remains off-by-default (the envelope recommends, the dispatcher still confirms), and the intake's per-outcome gate questions get a durable home instead of evaporating with the session that asked them.
basis: Grounding brief section 1 correction (h): 'outcome_decompose.py (U7) is the real decomposition path — just not at start-time and not from an existing GitHub Objective. No ingestion path confirmed.' Plus intake tension 3's required intent questions ('Are PR reviews required?', 'Gate or auto merge/deploy-to-nonprod?... operator decides per outcome, once, start') which currently have no persistence surface. Engages the /outcome campaign binding decision explicitly: envelope = input intent, never committed status; backend menu stays off-by-default.
outcome_shape: Merged: an execution-envelope schema in card_validator, emission in mission-control:issue and saga:handoff, and an /outcome ingestion parser that builds a starter DAG from an Objective's enveloped sub-issues.

title: Consensus elasticity: shrink panels where measured reviewer agreement is high, backed by sampled spot-checks
idea: Flip consensus to zero — one reviewer everywhere — and ask where that is actually safe. The uncomfortable answer: nobody knows, because the fleet never measures reviewer agreement; panel sizes are set by convention, and the operator-praised defect catches may be concentrated in a minority of lens/file-type combinations while the rest is over-provisioned ceremony. Kernel: team-execution records per-review agreement (findings overlap between panel members, echoing the hand-reconciled 15/17 Claude+Codex convergence) into a ledger; where a lens shows sustained near-unanimity, panel size drops to one with a sampled second reviewer as a spot-check, and any spot-check disagreement snaps the lens back to full panel. Gated decisions remain Claude-verified throughout, so never-gatekeepers is untouched — this resizes Claude-internal panels, not the advisory/gated split.
basis: Grounding brief section 7 singleton: 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' — an 88% agreement rate measured once by hand is exactly the signal proposed for systematic capture; section 3 item 2 (consensus review catching defects green suites missed, 2 repos, operator-praised) supplies the counter-pressure the spot-check snap-back mechanism answers. {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} engaged: elasticity applies only to Claude-internal panel sizing.
outcome_shape: Merged: an agreement-ledger written by team-execution's consensus step plus a documented panel-sizing policy consuming it, with snap-back rules and an initial report from historical review artifacts.

title: Model Palette Compiler
idea: Create a single fleet-wide model/effort vocabulary file and generate every agent frontmatter model field, command option, and plan-tier table from it, so fable/xhigh stop being aspirational in one plugin and become compile-time-checked currency everywhere; any plugin hardcoding a stale model or omitting an allowed effort tier fails contract tests.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: operator-facing model control only matters if the vocabulary is reachable at every dispatch point.
outcome_shape: PR adding contracts/model-palette.yaml, a generator, and test_model_palette_drift.py across the plugin fleet

title: Delegation Flight Recorder
idea: Every bridge invocation should emit a signed-ish receipt: requested engine, resolved engine, actual command/API called, transcript hash, working directory, artifacts touched, and verifier-of-record; the receipt becomes mandatory input to any lifecycle gate that claims external work happened, so a silent fallback either contradicts the claim or is missing.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: "delegated" should become an auditable evidence type, not a narration style.
outcome_shape: PR adding delegation_receipts.py, bridge adapters, and receipt validation in saga/team-execution gates

title: Rate-Limit Air Traffic Control
idea: Replace per-skill fan-out with a small local lease broker that all skills must ask before spawning reviewers, workers, outcome leaves, or external engines; leases encode provider, model, effort, expected tokens, priority, and lifecycle phase, with backpressure instead of burst failure, and the broker can deliberately serialize low-value review panels while preserving concurrency for high-value blockers.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: concurrency must be governed at the fleet level because rate limits fail at the fleet level.
outcome_shape: PR adding fleet_dispatch_broker.py, dispatch-policy.yaml, and adapters for team-execution, saga /outcome, and external-engine bridges

title: Consensus Treaty Files
idea: Extract consensus rules into portable "treaty" profiles covering quorum, independence requirement, allowed providers, disagreement handling, confidence scoring, and gate/advisory behavior, so team-execution, saga review, Codex rescue, and external reviewers all consume the same profile rather than carrying hardcoded thresholds; historical Claude+Codex convergence becomes calibration data instead of folklore.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: consensus is a protocol; burying it inside one plugin prevents reuse and calibration.
outcome_shape: PR adding consensus-profiles.yaml, consensus_runner.py, and migration tests for existing team-execution thresholds

title: Bridge Lie-Detector Tests
idea: Add negative-control tasks that an external engine can pass only by actually running, e.g. requiring Antigravity-specific transcript structure, Ollama local model metadata, or a DeepSeek API response header to appear in the receipt; the test fails if Claude answers plausibly but the external proof signature is absent.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: silent no-op failures need adversarial tests, not happy-path mocks.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/delegation_integrity/ with bridge-specific sentinel fixtures and CI smoke coverage

title: Provider Passports
idea: Treat Ollama, DeepSeek, Claude, Codex, Antigravity, and API-key providers as registered providers with passports (capabilities, credential lane, privacy class, rate limits, cost/speed rank, supported lifecycle roles, preflight command, proof parser); routing then asks for capability plus constraints, not a hardcoded CLI engine name, letting local models handle cheap ideation while API providers stay reserved for hard reasoning.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: provider routing should be capability-based, not tool-name based.
outcome_shape: PR adding providers.yaml, provider_registry.py, and resolver tests for CLI, local, and API-key providers

title: Warm Worker Hotel
idea: Build a reusable worker pool for expensive engines and repo clones instead of launching fresh disposable workers for every unit; workers get leases, TTLs, cache namespaces, and teardown receipts so reuse is intentional rather than sticky hidden state, saving both wall time and context setup cost for repeated Ollama or external-engine jobs.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: cache economics require first-class worker lifetime management.
outcome_shape: PR adding worker_pool/, worker-leases.jsonl, and bridge support for lease acquire/release

title: Ship Ceremony Compiler
idea: Make every implementation plan emit a machine-readable closeout thunk: intended branch, commit paths, PR metadata, merge policy, post-merge checkout/pull/cleanup, and verification commands; a fleet command executes the thunk with readbacks after each step and stops on ambiguity, turning the manual git/gh ceremony into something generated, reviewable, and repeatable.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: repeated manual ceremony is workflow debt with an obvious compilation target.
outcome_shape: PR adding ship_thunk.schema.json, ship_ceremony.py, and saga /work emission of closeout thunks

title: Lifecycle Autopilot With A Brake
idea: Add an opt-in lifecycle controller that advances idea -> plan -> work -> review -> ship -> retro when evidence gates are satisfied, but requires a visible brake file or approval marker at risky boundaries; it should not decide quality, only notice that the next stage is mechanically unblocked, turning "what now?" into state-machine progression.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: humans should approve risk, not remember every mechanical next step.
outcome_shape: PR adding lifecycle-autopilot.yaml, lifecycle_state_machine.py, and dry-run output for saga commands

title: Objective Ingestion Inbox
idea: /outcome should first capture an Objective artifact before dispatching leaves, covering intent, non-goals, repo scope, acceptance signals, budget, allowed providers, and pause points; it can ingest from a user prompt, GitHub issue, plan doc, or branch diff, but must normalize all of them into the same object so leaf dispatch operates from a stable Objective instead of a loose prompt.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: better intent capture reduces downstream agent drift and accidental scope expansion.
outcome_shape: PR adding objective.schema.yaml, /outcome ingest, and tests that issue/doc/prompt inputs produce equivalent Objective objects

title: Standards Lockfile
idea: Move ADR and standards enforcement to a versioned lockfile generated from the context library; plans and reviews cite the exact standards version they used, and violations require explicit waivers with expiry and rationale, making standards enforcement a compiler pass before work rather than a reviewer's memory test after work.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: standards only scale when the enforcement locus is explicit and versioned.
outcome_shape: PR adding standards.lock, standards_resolver.py, and plan/review checks for missing or stale standards versions

title: Learning Seismograph
idea: Build a miner that scans retros, review findings, failure notes, and ship receipts for repeated failure signatures across repos, only opening a promote candidate when it has 3+ repo provenance, direct snippets, and a proposed context-library patch, so the promote loop fires from evidence pressure instead of operator memory.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: cross-repo learning needs a detection system, not a button nobody presses.
outcome_shape: PR adding learning_miner.py, learning-signatures.yaml, and generated promote-candidates/*.md

title: Agent Death Certificates
idea: Every multi-agent team gets a lifecycle record: created, assigned, heartbeat, paused, completed, failed, abandoned, and teardown result; stale agents become visible dead letters with enough context to resume or kill cleanly, applied equally to team-execution panels, /outcome leaves, and external-engine workers.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: long-running agent systems need tombstones as much as launch commands.
outcome_shape: PR adding team_lifecycle.py, agent-runs.jsonl, and liveness checks in team-execution and saga

title: Prompt Contract Auditor
idea: Add a static auditor that reads every agent prompt, frontmatter field, command doc, and script contract across all 8 plugins, flagging claims about tools, models, efforts, consensus behavior, or bridge wiring that are not backed by executable code or tests, catching dead wiring before a user discovers it during real work.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: prompt drift is production drift in a skills-based plugin fleet.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugin_contract_audit.py, prompt schema fixtures, and CI output grouped by plugin

title: Effort Escrow
idea: Make /plan allocate model/effort budget as spendable escrow per unit: cheap units can refund unused budget, risky units can request escalation, and the operator sees a ledger before execution, with external providers, local models, and Claude tiers all drawing from the same abstract budget, giving fable/opus/sonnet/haiku/xhigh operational meaning without exposing every backend detail.
basis: codex (GPT) proposal: a model/effort lever becomes useful when it controls spend, escalation, and routing across the whole lifecycle.
outcome_shape: PR adding effort_ledger.py, effort-policy.yaml, and plan/work integration that records actual versus planned effort

title: One leaf-produced run-fact ledger spine serving spend, cache, engine, and delegation telemetry
idea: Four themes independently invented the same artifact: T12 wants an estimate-then-reconcile spend envelope on the cost ledger, T4 wants a cache-economics ledger (cached-vs-fresh tokens), T2 wants a dispatch-fed engine-usage ledger, and T15 wants an append-only cross-bridge chain-of-custody ledger. Build ONE ledger contract instead of four: a versioned, append-only, leaf-produced fact record (run id, spawn site, model/effort tier, tokens by cache class, engine/bridge identity, receipt hash, wall time) written at every spawn exit, with per-consumer derived views (spend reconciliation, residency benefit, provider staleness, delegation audit). Each parent idea becomes a view over the spine rather than a parallel ledger that will drift (theme 14's disease).
basis: Convergent independent invention is the strongest signal in the pool: parents T12-F4-5, T4-F3-5, T2-F4-6, T15-F2-8, and H-F4-4 all specify an append-only leaf-produced fact ledger with ~70% overlapping fields. Shipping them separately creates four mirrored record schemas — exactly the contract-mirror drift T14 documents (grounding brief §3 finding 1). The binding /outcome decision 'cost ledger = leaf-produced fact' (grounding §2, U1–U11 row) already names the write locus, so the spine extends settled architecture rather than inventing a new one.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/run_ledger.py (versioned record schema + append-only writer) plus derived-view helpers, wired into the /work spawn exit and team-execution teammate exit; verified by a schema test, an append-only immutability test, and one derived view (spend estimate-vs-actual) rendered in a real run artifact.

title: TTL-lease broker: concurrency slots, worktree reclamation, and orphan write-fencing are one primitive
idea: H-F4-3 spotted that concurrency caps and teardown are both resource leases; T6-F3-1 wants ephemeral resources modeled as leases with a reaper; T15-F5-6 wants fencing tokens so a stale orphan's late write is rejected; T13-F1-4 wants a fleet-wide lease file so co-running workflows cannot sum past the cap. Merge all four: a single file-backed lease broker where every spawn acquires a lease that IS the concurrency slot, carries a fencing token that every write path checks, names the worktree/branch it holds, and expires on TTL — expiry simultaneously frees the slot, arms the reaper for the worktree, and invalidates the token so the orphan cannot clobber a retry's evidence. Three fleet diseases (rate-limit fan-out kills, 15 stale worktrees, orphan clobbering) become one invariant: no resource exists outside a live lease.
basis: Grounding brief §4: '15 stale abandoned saga worktrees in .worktrees/ inflating the repo 10x+'; §7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting'; §7 singleton: 'a probe script overwriting a FAIL evidence artifact with a later PASS'. Parents H-F4-3, T6-F3-1, T15-F5-6, T13-F1-4 each solve one facet with the same lease mechanic; the hybrid is the shared primitive they all presuppose. Engages the worker-cache-scheduling revisit-when ('idle-poll justifies a formal wave queue') rather than contradicting it: leases are the accounting layer under any future queue.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared lease_broker.py (acquire/renew/release, fencing token, TTL reap) consumed by the saga workflow emitter's parallel batches and by worktree creation in /work; verified by a test where an expired lease's write is rejected and its worktree is reaped, plus a two-process test proving summed acquisition never exceeds the cap.

title: /ship ends in Step B8: the guarded ship verb whose final gate is verified reclamation
idea: The ship-ceremony ideas (T7-F4-1 ship_ceremony.py, T7-F4-4 hazard preflight) and the teardown ideas (T6-F2-1 Step B8, T6-F1-2 orphan-worktree reaper) describe the same run-exit moment from two sides. Hybrid: the ship verb's state machine is commit→hazard-preflight→PR→merge-watch→sync→RECLAIM, where the final state is a verified teardown (worktree removed, branch pruned, scratch cleared, lease released) and the ship receipt is only minted when reclamation proves clean. This kills the reason teardown never happens — it is nobody's step today — by making it the exit condition of the verb operators already want for the 8-repo manual ritual. Cleanup stops being hygiene and becomes the definition of shipped.
basis: Grounding brief §7 pattern 1: 'Manual ship ceremony — commit→PR→merge→checkout-main→pull→cleanup done by raw git/gh in session after session (8 repos)' — note 'cleanup' is already the ritual's last verb; §4: 15 stale saga worktrees prove the cleanup half is the part that gets dropped, 'same disease as team-execution's missing Step B8'. Parents T7-F4-1/T7-F4-4 build the verb without reclamation; T6-F2-1/T6-F1-2 build reclamation without a trigger moment. Merge/deploy gating stays operator-decided per intake tension 3 (ship verb asks once at start, per the asymmetric approval rule).
outcome_shape: PR adding a guarded ship ceremony skill/script to saga whose terminal state is verified reclamation and whose receipt records it; verified by an end-to-end dry-run artifact showing HALT when a worktree survives, and a CHANGELOG/marketplace bump per release-surface policy.

title: One committed IntentEnvelope from issue handoff to every spend and autonomy gate
idea: T8-F4-1 defines an IntentEnvelope on the OutcomeSpec; H-F6-9 has mission-control issues carry a machine-readable intent block; T4-F4-1 wants a shared execution_posture primitive every fan-out site imports; T12-F6-7 wants a mode-aware tier recommender; T7-F3-2 wants ceremony gates pre-declared as envelope fields. Hybrid: one envelope schema (PR-review posture, merge/deploy gating, attended/unattended mode, spend posture, tier ceiling, backend set) authored ONCE — at issue handoff or /outcome start — then read by the tier resolver, the spend-asymmetry gate, the ship ceremony, and fan-out posture decisions. The intake's 'asked once per run start' rule becomes a single schema with a single writer and many readers, instead of five skills each re-asking or hardcoding.
basis: Intake brief tension 3 mandates the start-time questions ('Are PR reviews required?', 'Gate or auto merge/deploy?') asked 'per outcome, once, at start', and tension 1 makes spend posture 'asked once per run start, mode-based recommendation' — two once-asked postures with no named home today. Parents T8-F4-1, H-F6-9, T4-F4-1, T12-F6-7, T7-F3-2 each build a partial envelope; unmerged they yield five posture surfaces that re-interrogate the operator, violating the ask-once mandate they each cite.
outcome_shape: PR adding an intent_envelope schema module in saga plus producer wiring in /outcome start and mission-control prepared-issue drafting, and consumer reads in the tier table and spend gate; verified by a round-trip test (issue block -> envelope -> consumer reads) and a drift-guard asserting no consumer re-prompts for a field the envelope carries.

title: Dispatch-time tier resolver: single palette source, effort field, because+fallback, priors from the ledger
idea: Fuse the tier-currency stack into one seam: T3-F4-1's shared palette module (kill the literal-string scatter), H-F4-2's dispatch-time resolver (instead of 24 frontmatter edits), T3-F2-3's effort-injection shim generalizing the readonly-verifier per-call pattern, T12-F3-2's requirement that every recommendation emit a 'because' plus a cheaper fallback, and H-F4-4's cost-fact priors so the 'because' cites measured history instead of re-reasoned vibes. The resolver takes (role_kind, work_shape, envelope tier ceiling) and returns (model, effort, because, cheaper_fallback), reading the run-fact ledger for precedent. This makes fable/xhigh reachable everywhere, retires hardcoded model: fields incrementally, and satisfies the never-silent-expensive rule structurally.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'The fleet's ONE operator-facing model/effort lever: saga /plan's unit tier table... Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:, zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution)... fable/xhigh unreachable outside saga plan vocabulary' — plus QUEUED seed {#team-execution-per-teammate-effort} (§5). Parents H-F4-2, T3-F4-1, T3-F2-3, T12-F3-2, H-F4-4 partition the fix; separately they leave either the vocabulary scattered, the effort field dead, or the recommendation unjustified. Respects {#tier-vocab-ordering}: the resolver's fallback is one rung down the ordered ladder.
outcome_shape: PR adding tier_resolver.py beside execution_spec.py (palette imported, not copied), an effort-injection spawn shim, and first consumer wiring in team-execution's A7 worker table; verified by unit tests for resolution + fallback ordering and a drift-guard failing on any new hardcoded palette literal.

title: One vendored-artifact parity registry covering contracts, the standards index, and release surfaces
idea: T14-F4-1 proposes a generic vendored-contract parity primitive; T9-F4-2 independently proposes vendoring llms.txt 'as a SHA-pinned artifact on the existing parity registry'; T14-F4-3 wants a release-surface version tri-lock (plugin.json == marketplace.json == CHANGELOG head); T11-F1-8 wants a four-surface release-parity CI guard. These are all the same machine: a registry of (source-of-truth ref, local mirror path, coupling policy pin/float, guard) rows, one CI job iterating it. The hybrid ships the registry once and lands three row families on day one — cross-repo contract mirrors (sdlc-schema.json, validate_card_body-class copies), the vendored context-library index, and this repo's own release surfaces — turning three guard-writing habits into data entry.
basis: Grounding brief §3 finding 1: rename/contract-mirror drift in 4 repos including 'validate_card_body stale hand-copy... 343 clean cards failed the live contract (#222)' and 're-vendored sdlc-schema.json'; §6 finding 3: 'Release-surface drift persists despite CLAUDE.md step 6 — room for automation.' Parent T9-F4-2 explicitly names riding 'the existing parity registry' — proof the pool already implies one registry, while T14-F4-1, T14-F4-3, and T11-F1-8 would otherwise ship it three times.
outcome_shape: PR adding a vendored-artifact registry (YAML) + one parametrized CI check consuming it, with initial rows for sdlc-schema.json, llms.txt, and per-plugin release-surface tri-locks; verified by a red-test demonstrating each row family catching an injected drift.

title: fleet doctor: one derived-on-read audit of leaked resources, dead wiring, and receiptless delegations
idea: T6-F2-7's derived-on-read 'fleet ps', T6-F4-8's leak-doctor, H-F1-4's never-fired detector (machinery must prove it has ever produced output), and T15-F6-8's continuous delegation-integrity monitor are all read-only reconciliations of claimed state vs ground truth. Hybrid: a single read-only `fleet doctor` command with three lenses over the same evidence base (lease/ledger files, worktrees, saga stores, receipt ledger): (1) running/held/leaked resources, (2) lifecycle machinery that has never fired (the promote loop, dead seams), (3) delegations lacking receipts or with silent-fallback signatures. One evidence-gathering pass, three reports, zero writes — the diagnostic complement to the lease broker and receipt contract, and the tool that would have surfaced the 15 stale worktrees, the never-fired promote loop, and the agy silent fallback before an operator stumbled on them.
basis: Three grounded diseases share one detection shape — state was claimed but ground truth disagreed: 15 stale worktrees (grounding §4), 'promote ledger: 0 learnings ever promoted' (§3.5), 'agy silent Claude-fallback' + dead-wiring learnings (§6.1). Parents T6-F2-7, T6-F4-8, H-F1-4, T15-F6-8 each build a one-lens scanner; the expensive part (enumerating ground truth across worktrees, stores, ledgers) is common, so one pass with three lenses dominates three scanners. Derive-on-read is the house posture (grounding §2 /outcome row, §6.5), so a read-only doctor fits binding decisions exactly.
outcome_shape: PR adding a fleet-doctor script + skill surface producing a three-section report artifact; verified by fixture tests seeding a leaked worktree, a never-fired seam, and a receiptless delegation record, each surfaced in the correct section.

title: Ambient AIMD admission control with a requeue ledger — cap, backoff, and shed as one governor
idea: H-F2-7's knobless ambient semaphore, T13-F5-3's AIMD governor (start at 3, multiplicative backoff on 429, additive probe up), and H-F6-6's shed-don't-cap preemption supervisor with a requeue ledger combine into one admission-control layer every spawn site acquires from: static cap 3 as the ceiling (intake constraint), AIMD adjusting the effective width below it on observed 429s, and any killed/rejected dispatch landing in a durable requeue ledger that the next advance re-picks (T13-F2-4's resume-on-429 for free). T13-F4-5's move — encoding /optimize's deliberate serial=1 as a first-class exception row, not a re-added knob — resolves the binding tension with the shed max_concurrent decision. No per-skill knobs anywhere; the governor is the only concurrency authority.
basis: Intake brief added constraint: 'Maximum 3 concurrent agents at any moment, across all phases' with enforcement currently 'workflow scripts chunk every fan-out' — aspiration, not machinery. Grounding §1: 'the only orchestration-level cap is VERIFY_N_CAP = 7... team-execution reviewer fan-out, /outcome leaf dispatch, and engine bridges are unbounded'; §7 pattern 4: '6 of 7 agents failed on rate-limiting'; 'KTD6 was aspiration, not machinery'. Engages /optimize's deliberately-removed max_concurrent (grounding §1) via parent T13-F4-5's exception-registry treatment rather than contradicting it.
outcome_shape: PR adding a shared admission-control module (acquire with AIMD width + requeue ledger) consumed by the saga workflow emitter and the verify-panel spawner, with an exceptions registry carrying /optimize serial=1; verified by a simulated-429 test showing width backoff, requeue, and re-pick, plus a drift-guard over fan-out sites.

title: Tree-hash recon memoization with $0 local-model cache-miss filling
idea: H-F6-7 keys committed recon/survey artifacts by git tree hash so 400k-token read-only fan-outs run once per tree state; T2-F6-4 lands Ollama as the $0 keyless local offload row; T4-F2-7 collapses N cold repo reads into one shared context pack. Hybrid: the recon layer becomes cache-first AND cheap-on-miss — a warm tree-hash hit costs zero tokens, and a cold miss is dispatched to the $0 local offload lane (mechanical read-only summarization is exactly the WEAK-capability-tolerant work shape local models fit), with Claude consuming only the distilled pack. The two ideas multiply: memoization bounds how often recon runs, the $0 lane bounds what a run costs, and the shared context pack is the artifact both produce/consume. Read-only offload also never touches the never-gatekeepers boundary.
basis: Grounding brief §7 singleton: '350-450k tokens in <20 min for read-only recon fan-outs (cache-economics number)'. Intake §5: 'Ollama -> $0 offload target'. Parents H-F6-7, T2-F6-4, T4-F2-7 attack cost frequency, unit price, and redundancy separately; combined, the recon bill approaches zero for unchanged trees and near-zero for changed ones. Advisory-only summarization respects {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} — no gated decision consumes raw engine output.
outcome_shape: PR adding tree-hash-keyed recon-artifact storage + lookup in the grounding/recon spawn path and an offload route to the Ollama registry row for cache misses; verified by a repeat-run test showing zero re-mining on identical tree hash and a receipt-bearing local-engine dispatch on miss.

title: Portable consensus kernel: typed gated/advisory bit, worthiness entry gate, and a non-scoring external seat
idea: Extract the consensus machinery once with its three strongest amendments built into the contract rather than bolted on: T5-F6-1's single versioned scoring spec (consensus_spec.py, deleting prose-as-source-of-truth and the ~24 hand-copied threshold constants), T5-F4-3's gated-vs-advisory governance bit stamped on every verdict artifact so porting cannot leak the boundary, T5-F6-8's consensus-worthiness entry gate so a panel must earn its convene, and T5-F4-4's external-engine advisory seat — displayed, never counted — making the 15/17 Claude+Codex convergence a repeatable membership mode. Shipping the kernel without these three would immediately generate the amendment PRs; shipping them as contract fields makes /work and /outcome consumers correct by construction.
basis: Prior art: grounding brief §7 singleton — 'Claude+Codex independent syntheses converging 15/17, hand-reconciled (theme 5 prior art)' — a measured instance of the external advisory seat's value, living in this repo's session-mining synthesis (workflow wf_7e5d77a2-5c0 journal). Consumer-side signal §3.2: consensus review 'catching defects green suites missed (2 independent repos, operator-praised)' motivates portability. Parents: T5-F6-1, T5-F4-3, T5-F4-4, T5-F6-8. The non-scoring seat satisfies {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} structurally: the external verdict cannot move the score that sets the gate.
outcome_shape: PR adding consensus_spec.py (thresholds, cycle policy, governance bit, worthiness pre-gate, advisory-seat slot) with team-execution reviewers refactored to import it; verified by a contract test proving an advisory seat's score cannot change the gate outcome and a drift-guard against re-inlined threshold literals.

title: Checkable liveness for decisions AND backlog: revisit-when tripwires and basis-decay share one predicate engine
idea: H-F4-6/H-F3-10 make every DECISIONS.md revisit-when a machine-checkable predicate; H-F1-9 makes stale open issues re-verify their own grounding basis or close themselves; T10-F5-4 instruments where promotion candidates die. All three need the same engine: a registry of (artifact anchor, predicate, evidence probe, action-on-fire) rows evaluated by a scheduled read-only pass that surfaces — never auto-executes — fired tripwires. The hybrid matters doubly for THIS ideation campaign: the intake's pre-mortem #1 is backlog rot, and every surviving idea carries a basis that decays; wiring basis-decay into the same machinery that watches revisit-whens means the backlog this process generates is born self-auditing, and the binding-decision register stops depending on human memory to reopen.
basis: First-principles: the grounding brief's binding-decision register (§2) lists seven revisit-when conditions, all checked today by nothing but recall — and §6.2 records four learnings of 'provenance/status claims must be re-verified against current state'. Meanwhile intake pre-mortem 1 names backlog rot as the top failure mode of this very campaign. A predicate over evidence is the same object whether its subject is a decision anchor or an issue basis; two engines would be theme-14-style parallel houses. Parents: H-F4-6, H-F3-10, H-F1-9, T10-F5-4. Read-only surfacing keeps the /promote write gate and operator authority intact.
outcome_shape: PR adding a tripwire registry format + a read-only evaluator script and a scheduled digest artifact, with initial rows for two real revisit-whens from DECISIONS.md and a basis-decay row template for wave-tagged issues; verified by a fixture test firing one tripwire and asserting surface-not-execute.

title: Close the mining loop: codex substrate in, durable findings ledger, pattern-to-drafted-issue out
idea: The mining ideas ship a pipeline in fragments: T10-F2-1 lights up the 219 dark codex sessions as substrate, T10-F1-4 adds an incremental watermark so re-mining stops, T10-F4-4 writes mined findings somewhere durable instead of a workflow journal that evaporates, and T10-F4-7 institutionalizes the mined-pattern-to-prepared-issue move this very campaign performed by hand. Individually each leaves the loop open (substrate without writeback evaporates; writeback without an emitter accumulates; an emitter without codex substrate misses half the evidence). The hybrid is the closed loop as one deliverable: substrate adapters (claude + codex) -> watermarked incremental mining -> durable findings ledger with lineage -> N-repo recurrence threshold -> prepared-issue draft through the existing mission-control write gate. Nothing writes to GitHub without the gate; everything upstream is read-only and resumable.
basis: Grounding brief §7: '219 codex sessions in-window with no mining substrate — grounded gap' and '175 findings -> 10 recurring patterns' produced by a one-off manual workflow; parent T10-F4-4's own framing: 'stop letting 175 mined findings evaporate into a workflow journal'. §3.5: the promote loop 'has never fired', showing open-loop learning machinery is the norm, not the exception. Parents: T10-F2-1, T10-F1-4, T10-F4-4, T10-F4-7.
outcome_shape: PR adding a codex substrate adapter + watermark store to the /retro mining path, a findings-ledger format with per-finding lineage, and a threshold-triggered prepared-issue emitter targeting mission-control's draft flow; verified by an end-to-end fixture run producing a draft issue from two seeded repos' recurring finding.

title: One agent-file CI lint: frontmatter schema, tier/effort fields, prompt rubric, and cache-prefix stability
idea: Three themes each propose a CI pass over the same ~34 agent .md files: T11-F2-4/T11-F4-1 lint prompt quality against a rubric and a shared agent-spec registry, T3-F4-6 lints tier/effort frontmatter fleet-wide, and T4-F3-4 lints prompt prefix stability (no volatile token ahead of stable prose, since cache economics is set at authoring time). Run separately these are three CI jobs, three file walkers, and three places to forget a new plugin. The hybrid is one agent-file lint suite with pluggable rules — frontmatter schema (validates against the shared palette from G-hybrids-5), required effort declaration, deterministic rubric checks, prefix-stability ordering — plus an advisory-only LLM rubric lane kept out of the blocking path. Every future agent-file invariant becomes a rule, not a job.
basis: Grounding brief §1: 'Every agent frontmatter across all 8 plugins hardcodes model:... zero effort: fields (0 of 24 in team-execution)' — a fleet-wide authored-surface defect with no current guard; the worker-cache-scheduling decision (§2) makes prompt-prefix structure economically load-bearing, so prefix ordering is a lintable correctness property, not style. Parents T11-F2-4, T11-F4-1, T3-F4-6, T4-F3-4 all iterate the identical file set; unification is the same move CLAUDE.md's mypy note already teaches (match CI scope once, centrally).
outcome_shape: PR adding an agent-lint script (rule registry + walkers over plugins/*/agents and skill-referenced agent defs) wired into ci.yml, with frontmatter-schema, effort-presence (warn-then-block staged), and prefix-order rules; verified by red-fixture tests per rule and a clean pass over the current fleet or an explicit baseline waiver file.

title: One fleet intent envelope: merge the five parallel per-theme posture envelopes into a single shared schema and a single run-start interview
idea: Nineteen pool ideas independently invent an 'envelope' — T8's IntentEnvelope (T8-F4-1) for /outcome posture, T12-F3-3's budget envelope for spend, T7-F2-8/T7-F3-2's ceremony envelope for ship gates, T4-F4-1's run-posture primitive for cache economics, T1-F5-8's run-start intent manifest for engine choice, T6-F4-6's adjustment-envelope control file. Shipped separately these produce five run-start interrogations and five uncoordinated schemas the operator must answer for the same run. The unwritten meta-move: one shared intent_envelope.v1 schema (module in saga, consumed fleet-wide) with named sections — tier posture, spend asymmetry, engine intents, ship/merge gating, concurrency posture, attended/unattended mode — captured in ONE composed run-start interview, persisted on the spec/issue, and read by every consumer that today plans its own ask. Each theme's envelope idea becomes a section of this schema rather than a sibling artifact; a per-run interrogation budget falls out for free because the asks are co-scheduled.
basis: Gap in pool: jq census finds 19 envelope-titled ideas spanning T1/T2/T4/T5/T6/T7/T8/T12 (T8-F4-1, T12-F3-3, T7-F2-8, T4-F4-1, T8-F1-3, H-F2-9, ...) — every theme wrote its own envelope, none wrote the merge, and no idea addresses the combined interrogation load of shipping them all. Intake brief 'Resolved tensions' 1–4 mandates asking these postures 'once per run start' — a promise only a unified envelope can keep once five themes each add their own ask. Compatible with the /outcome campaign decision (committed intent config is explicitly allowed; derived-on-read applies to status, not operator posture).
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/intent_envelope.py (schema + composed-interview renderer) plus consumption shims referenced from /outcome start, /work, /plan tier table, and team-execution run-start; drift-guard test asserting no consumer defines a posture question outside the envelope registry; merged sibling envelope issues re-pointed at sections of this schema.

title: One append-only ledger substrate under the pool's 45 ledgers and 19 receipts
idea: The pool proposes ~45 ledger ideas and ~19 receipt ideas — cost ledger (T2-F4-6), cache-economics ledger (T4-F3-5), consensus replay log (T5-F5-8), delegation chain-of-custody (T15-F2-8), tier-regret ledger (T12-F4-7), reclamation ledger (T6-F4-1), evidence custody chain (T7-F5-6), dispatch-casualty manifest (H-F1-2). Every one independently re-solves the same four problems: append-only storage, content addressing/tamper evidence, where the file lives relative to worktree blast radius (T15-F3-8), and how /retro queries it. Nobody wrote the substrate: a single fleet ledger primitive — one JSONL append-only, hash-chained, worktree-external store with a typed 'kind' column and a tiny reader API — that every per-theme ledger becomes a row-kind of, not a bespoke file format. Without this, convergence ships a dozen incompatible ledgers and the {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} sprawl concern reproduces itself at the artifact layer.
basis: Gap in pool: jq census over pool.json — 45 titles matching 'ledger', 19 matching 'receipt', zero ideas proposing a shared substrate they instantiate. Binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} (grounding brief §2) puts a consolidation burden of proof on new machinery; shipping 10+ bespoke ledger formats is the exact sprawl it names. The /outcome campaign decision already fixes one design point ('cost ledger = leaf-produced fact'), which the substrate must honor: leaves append, coordinators read.
outcome_shape: PR adding plugins/saga/scripts/fleet_ledger.py (append/verify/query, hash-chained JSONL, worktree-external path resolution) + a references/ledger-kinds.md registry; two existing ledger consumers (cost ledger, verify evidence) migrated as proof; conformance test that a later PASS row cannot mutate an earlier FAIL row.

title: Name the import mechanism: where cross-plugin shared primitives actually live and how a plugin gets them
idea: At least 28 pool ideas say 'shared primitive every plugin/fan-out site imports' (tier palette T3-F4-1, concurrency resolver T13-F4-1, consensus kernel T5-F6-1, liveness engine T6-F4-3, reclaim primitive T6-F4-1, delegation receipt T15-F4-1, posture primitive T4-F4-1). None answers the load-bearing question: plugins are independently installed marketplace artifacts with no shared Python package path — cross-plugin import is not currently a thing. H-F6-8 circles it for contracts ('the marketplace is the contract bus') but stops short of code. The missing idea: decide and build the fleet-commons distribution mechanism — either (a) a fleet-core plugin whose scripts/ is the canonical home, with sibling plugins resolving it via marketplace-installed path discovery plus a vendored-fallback shim, or (b) a real Python package published from this repo that CLI plugins declare as a dependency. Without this decision, all 28 'shared primitive' survivors silently degrade into copy-paste mirrors — recreating exactly the T14 contract-drift disease the pool is trying to cure.
basis: First-principles: grounding brief §1 lists 8 independently versioned plugins; the marketplace installs each in isolation, so 'X.py every plugin imports' has no resolvable import path today — verified by the repo layout (each plugin's scripts live under its own skills/ tree, tests import via repo-root paths that do not exist at install time). 28 pool ideas (jq census on 'shared primitive'/'imports') depend on this unnamed mechanism; if unresolved, each ships as a hand-copy, which the 4-repo contract-mirror-drift evidence (grounding §3 finding 1) shows will drift. Engages {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7}: a fleet-core home is consolidation, not sprawl — it deletes future copies rather than adding a surface.
outcome_shape: A DECISIONS.md entry choosing the distribution mechanism (with rejected alternative recorded) plus the first PR implementing it: fleet-core resolution shim + one real consumer (tier palette or concurrency resolver) imported through it from two different plugins, with an install-time integration test proving resolution works outside the repo checkout.

title: Route around the rate limit: 429 pressure sheds offloadable work to the $0/external provider lane instead of queueing it
idea: T13's fifty-three ideas all treat 429s as a throttling problem — backoff (T13-F1-3), AIMD (T13-F5-3), requeue (H-F6-6), leases (T13-F1-4). T2's fifty-two ideas treat providers as a cost problem — Ollama as $0 offload, DeepSeek as cheap second opinion. Nobody wrote the intersection: external providers do not consume the Anthropic rate budget, so under sustained 429 pressure the correct move for offload-class units (mechanical, non-gated, chaperone-verifiable per {#external-engine-chaperone-dispatch}) is not to wait — it is to reroute to the registry's local/external lane, expanding effective concurrency at zero marginal Anthropic tokens. Concretely: the shared backoff wrapper (T13-F4-3's primitive) gains a reroute branch that consults engine_resolver for an eligible offload row when a unit is tagged offloadable, HALTing (not degrading) for gated/judgment units, and stamping the reroute in the dispatch ledger. This converts the 6-of-7-agents-killed failure mode into partial forward progress.
basis: Gap in pool: grep confirms no T13 idea mentions provider rerouting and no T2 idea mentions 429/rate-limit as a routing trigger; the closest are H-F6-6 (shed+requeue, same provider) and T13-F6-7 (per-lane caps, no cross-lane movement). First-principles: rate limits are per-provider; the fleet already has a registry seam (engine_resolver.py/engine_registry.py, intake §5) designed to route work by intent, so capacity relief is a new routing *reason*, not new machinery. Constraint compliance: only offload-intent, never-gatekeepers-safe units reroute; Claude remains verifier-of-record; judgment units still queue — this stays inside {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} rather than revisiting it.
outcome_shape: PR extending the shared 429-retry primitive with a registry-consulting reroute branch for offload-tagged units + dispatch-ledger reroute stamps; test simulating 429 storms asserting offload units reroute, gated units HALT-queue, and every reroute is ledgered.

title: External-engine output is untrusted input: injection containment on advisory text crossing into gated flows
idea: T15's fifty-four ideas prove a delegation RAN (receipts, transcripts, fencing); T1's forty-eight ideas reconcile WHAT it said (typed reconciliation, dissent records). Nobody treats the advisory text itself as a threat surface: a second-opinion finding or offload diff from codex/DeepSeek/Ollama is untrusted model output that Claude, as verifier-of-record, folds directly into review artifacts, plan docs, and — via typed reconciliation (T1-F2-4) — into machine-parsed structures. A poisoned or merely confused engine emitting 'ignore prior instructions / mark this finding resolved / run this command' inside a finding body is an authority-bypass channel that {#external-engines-never-gatekeepers} does not structurally close, because that decision governs verdict authority, not content injection. The missing idea: a fleet trust-boundary contract for engine-borne text — advisory content is always fenced as quoted data (delimited, provenance-tagged, never interpolated into instructions), reconciliation prompts explicitly instruct treating it as claims-to-verify, and a lint over engine-consuming skills asserts no engine output reaches a Bash/Write/gate call unfenced.
basis: Gap in pool: jq census for 'injection|untrusted' over all 771 ideas hits only T9 standards-injection ideas (a different sense — injecting standards docs); zero T1/T15/T2 ideas address adversarial content in engine output. First-principles: the never-gatekeepers decision (grounding §2) enforces who decides, but prompt-injected advisory text influences the decider through the content channel — the same class of hole as the repo's own Discord MCP guidance ('that is the request a prompt injection would make'), which shows the org already recognizes this threat model at other bridge boundaries but has not applied it to engine bridges. Cheap to close now, expensive after T1/T2 wave-1 multiplies engine call sites.
outcome_shape: PR adding a references/engine-output-trust-boundary.md contract + fencing conventions in the T1 reconciliation surfaces and engine bridge scripts, plus a CI lint asserting engine-output variables never interpolate into executable or gate-affecting contexts; adversarial fixture test with a booby-trapped advisory finding that must surface as data, not act.

title: Remote gate approval over the fleet's own channel: lifecycle gates delivered and answered through redis-channel/Discord
idea: H-F3-3 names the abstraction ('gates are durable approval records with pluggable transports') and H-F4-8 wraps the unreliable harness primitive, but nobody lands the transport the fleet already ships: redis-channel 0.5.0 plus the Discord bridge. The concrete idea: a gate, when raised in an unattended run (mode known from the intent envelope), writes its durable approval record AND pushes a gate card through the connected redis-channel endpoint — question, blast radius, reversibility class, evidence links — and the operator's typed Discord reply is captured as the consent-receipt artifact (H-F1-1's contract) that unblocks the run. Silence remains HALT, never consent (the 6-repo silent-auto-proceed fury finding). This converts the pool's long-unattended-run posture (intake: 'hours, not minutes') from 'run dies at first gate overnight' to 'operator approves from a phone', and it is the consolidation-friendly move: it makes two existing dark plugins load-bearing for the lifecycle core instead of adding a new surface.
basis: Direct: QUEUED.md seeds {#discord-button-approval} and {#proactive-notifications} (grounding brief §5) are exactly this ask and were flagged 'carry into Phase D', yet jq census shows only 8 pool ideas even mention redis-channel/Discord and none proposes gate delivery over it — the pool circled the abstraction (H-F3-3, H-F4-8, H-F6-5 operator-absence contract) without landing the named transport. Session-mining pattern 2 (gate-primitive unreliability, 6 repos) supplies the HALT-on-silence requirement; Gate-B struck fixing AskUserQuestion itself as out of scope, which makes an out-of-band transport the remaining in-scope path.
outcome_shape: PR adding a gate-transport seam to the confirmed-gate wrapper (durable approval record + redis-channel push + reply-to-consent-receipt capture), a references/gate-transport.md contract, and an end-to-end test faking the channel round trip; silence-times-out to HALT with a resumable gate record.

title: Execute the skills: an end-to-end lifecycle regression harness on a fixture repo, because the pool only ever lints prompts as text
idea: T11's entire quality apparatus treats SKILL.md and agent prompts as static artifacts — rubric linters (T11-F1-1), frontmatter lints (T11-F6-4), scorecards (T11-F4-2), prompt-contract audits (X-codex-14). The fleet's actual behavior — does /plan emit a valid spec, does /work's gate hold, does the emitted workflow chunk its waves — is never executed anywhere before release. Meanwhile the pool proposes hundreds of SKILL.md edits. The missing idea: a behavioral regression harness — a committed fixture repo plus a small suite of canonical lifecycle scenarios (plan a toy change, run the ship ceremony dry, raise and answer a gate) executed headlessly on the cheapest tier in scheduled CI, asserting on artifact shapes (spec JSON validates, saga appended, gate record present, worktree reclaimed) rather than on prose. H-F6-3's zero-token fire drill is the closest neighbor but is a one-shot irreducibility probe, not a standing regression gate. This is the safety net every other wave-1 idea silently assumes exists.
basis: Gap in pool: jq census for 'fixture repo / execute the skill / behavioral regression' returns zero hits across 771 ideas; all T11 coverage is static analysis. First-principles: the repo's tests cover Python scripts, but skills are prompt-programs whose only test today is production use — the same 'test shape masks dead wiring' disease this repo's own journal records (grounding §6 pain 1), applied one level up. Every high-churn wave (this backlog) multiplies untested prompt edits; a scenario harness converts 'we changed 30 SKILL.md files' from faith to a green check. Cost is bounded by running haiku/sonnet-tier on a toy fixture, matching the unattended cache-tight posture.
outcome_shape: PR adding tests/lifecycle-fixture/ (toy repo) + a scheduled CI job running 3–5 canonical scenarios headlessly at cheap tier with artifact-shape assertions, plus a contributing note requiring a scenario touch when a lifecycle skill's contract changes.

title: Backlog admission governor: pace issue materialization against measured execution throughput, so wave tagging is machinery instead of hope
idea: The intake brief's pre-mortem #1 is backlog rot — 'generation outpaces execution bandwidth; fleet churns under open issues' — mitigated only by static wave tags. The pool's nearest ideas are H-F1-9 (stale issues re-verify their basis or self-close — a decay valve at the tail) and mined-pattern-to-issue pipelines (T10-F2-7) that make generation FASTER. Nobody wrote the admission-control front: a governor that reads mission-control flow metrics (throughput, WIP age — machinery that already exists in the metrics skill) and gates wave-N materialization on wave-(N-1) drain: issues beyond a WIP-derived open-issue budget stay in a prepared-draft parking lane rather than landing as open GitHub issues. Combined with H-F1-9 this closes the loop at both ends — admission control at the front, basis decay at the back — and it is the only idea class that protects the fleet from this very ideation program's own success.
basis: Direct: intake brief 'Pre-mortems recorded' #1 names backlog rot and offers only wave tagging as mitigation — a label, not machinery. Gap in pool: jq census for backlog/throughput/admission returns cache-posture and concurrency ideas plus H-F1-9's tail-side decay; zero ideas govern the materialization rate itself. The metrics substrate (mission-control:metrics — cycle time, throughput, WIP age over Operations/Asgard/CAMPPS) already exists to derive the budget from, so the governor is a consumer of existing telemetry, not new instrumentation.
outcome_shape: PR adding a materialization-budget check to the Gate-F/handoff path (mission-control prepared-issue lane holds drafts beyond a flow-derived open-WIP budget, with an operator override) + a docs/plans policy note; verified by a dry run over this backlog's own wave plan showing the computed admission schedule.

title: The fleet control-surface census: one generated, always-current map of every operator lever, gate, and envelope across all plugins
idea: The pool adds on the order of a hundred new operator-facing controls — tier dials, spend envelopes, engine intents, concurrency caps, ship postures, consensus profiles, gate policies. Exactly one idea inventories any of them, and only for tiers (T12-F4-2's lever-site registry, mirroring sandbox-spawn-sites.md). Nobody wrote the fleet-wide version: a generated control-surface census — every skill's operator questions, every envelope field, every registry dial, every gate and its no-answer behavior — extracted from the skills/registries themselves into one legible reference (a 'what can I even configure, and where does it live' page), drift-guarded so a new lever cannot ship without appearing on the map. Without it, the wave-1 fleet becomes spectacular machinery the operator cannot hold in his head, and every 'ask once' promise is unauditable because nobody can enumerate the asks.
basis: Gap in pool: T12-F4-2 proves the pattern is wanted (an inventory registry for ONE lever class, explicitly modeled on the existing sandbox-spawn-sites.md precedent) but no idea generalizes it fleet-wide, while the pool simultaneously multiplies lever count by an order of magnitude. First-principles: legibility is the binding constraint on operator-in-the-loop designs — the asymmetric approval rule (intake tension 1) requires the operator to recognize spend-increasing choices, which requires knowing the choice set; and the repo already accepts the census-as-drift-guard pattern (sandbox-spawn-sites.md + registration drift guard, commit 46b7001), so this extends a proven house idiom rather than inventing one.
outcome_shape: PR adding scripts/control_surface_census.py (extracts levers/gates/envelope fields from skill frontmatter + registries into docs/references/fleet-control-surface.md) + a CI check failing when a lever exists off-census; first generated census committed.

title: Baseline before the wave: freeze today's pain metrics so 'the fleet got better' is a measurement, not a vibe
idea: The pool instruments the FUTURE fleet exhaustively (45 ledgers, telemetry everywhere) but no idea captures the BEFORE picture: manual ship ceremonies per week (8-repo finding), 429 fan-out kill rate ('6 of 7 agents failed'), tokens per recon fan-out (350–450k), stale-worktree count (15), gate silent-auto-proceed incidents, promote-loop firings (0). Without a frozen baseline, every wave-1 issue closes as 'shipped' with no way to say whether the ship ceremony verb actually reduced manual ceremonies or the concurrency governor actually cut kill rates — precisely the validation-discipline failure the operator's global instructions prohibit ('no speed/cost claims without measurement from the actual run'). The idea: a one-time, committed baseline document deriving each number from the same substrate the grounding brief used (session mining, journals, git evidence), each metric paired with its re-measurement recipe, and a /retro hook that re-runs the recipes after each wave lands.
basis: Direct: the operator's own validation discipline (global CLAUDE.md: 'Do NOT state anything about performance without verifying it from a direct, current source') applied to the program itself; the grounding brief already contains the raw numbers (§4: 15 stale worktrees; §7: 8-repo ship ritual, 6-of-7 rate-limit kill, 350–450k recon tokens, 0 promotions ever) but they live in a point-in-time brief with no re-measurement recipe. Gap in pool: per-theme telemetry ideas measure the new machinery's own operation; none measures the delta against the pre-wave world, so program success is currently unfalsifiable.
outcome_shape: A committed docs/plans/2026-07-plugin-fleet-baseline.md with ~8 numbered metrics, each carrying its evidence source and an executable re-measurement recipe (script or documented query), plus a /retro checklist line re-running them per wave; verified by re-deriving two metrics from scratch and matching the brief.

title: The dark half of the fleet: an explicit in-or-out verdict and primitive-parity pass for deploy, home-lab-ops, unifi, and redis-channel
idea: The grounding brief maps 8 plugins; the 15 themes and ~771 ideas concentrate almost entirely on saga, team-execution, mission-control, and agy. jq census: 7 ideas mention unifi/home-lab-ops, 8 mention redis-channel/discord — under 2% of the pool for half the fleet. A 'turn the fleet spectacular' backlog that silently ignores four plugins either believes they are fine (unverified) or out of scope (undeclared). The missing meta-move: a deliberate per-plugin verdict pass — for each dark plugin, decide (a) it adopts the wave-1 fleet primitives where its shape matches (deploy gains ledger/receipt evidence and ship-ceremony integration per T7-F2-8's baton; redis-channel becomes the gate transport of G-negative-space-6; home-lab-ops portal gates adopt the consent-receipt contract), or (b) it is declared lifecycle-peripheral in DECISIONS.md with a revisit-when — engaging {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} honestly instead of by omission. Either verdict is fine; the absence of a verdict is the defect.
basis: Direct: grounding brief §1 fleet map lists 8 plugins (deploy 0.1.2, home-lab-ops 1.2.0, redis-channel 0.5.0, unifi 1.1.0 among them) while the §8 theme roster derives every theme from saga/team-execution/mission-control/agy evidence; pool census confirms <2% idea coverage of the other four. Binding decision {#plugin-portfolio-groom-17-to-7} makes sprawl an active concern that cuts both ways — plugins kept in the portfolio should either participate in fleet primitives or have their peripheral status recorded; today neither is true, which is the same undeclared-scope disease the pool's own contract-census ideas (T14-F4-7: 'every contract must declare a guard') attack at the contract layer.
outcome_shape: A DECISIONS.md entry per dark plugin (participate-with-listed-primitives or peripheral-with-revisit-when) produced by one read-only survey pass, plus follow-on issues only for the 'participate' verdicts; the decision entries are the merged artifact, wave-tagged behind the primitives they depend on.

title: Fold this ideation program's architecture back into /ideate: blind hunters, gap synthesis, basis contract, and capped batching as reusable skill machinery
idea: This program is running a hand-built pipeline — 12-theme grounding, ~72 Opus frame agents, 6 blind Fable novelty hunters, gap synthesis reading the merged pool, a basis-type contract ('ideas without a supporting basis are killed'), concurrency-capped batching, and an anti-anchoring rule (hunters blind, only gap-synthesis reads the pool). None of that lives in saga:ideate; it lives in two dated plan docs and a bespoke workflow, and will evaporate when this backlog ships. No pool idea proposes capturing it: the 17 /ideate-adjacent hits are all engine-lane offers into /ideate, not upgrades of /ideate's own architecture. The idea: promote the proven elements into /ideate as declared modes — a grounding-brief stage, a basis_type contract on every emitted idea, an optional blind-hunter lane, a terminal gap-synthesis pass, and cap-aware batch dispatch — so the next big divergence run is an invocation, not a two-day pipeline build.
basis: Direct: the intake brief's Phase D table (Opus wide net + blind Fable hunters + gap synthesis + convergent critique, with the anti-anchoring pre-mortem #4 rationale) exists only as a plan document for this one run — quoted structure at intake brief lines 66–76 and 143–151; saga:ideate's registered description ('multi-agent divergent→convergent engine') claims the genus but demonstrably lacks these mechanisms or this program would not have needed the bespoke pipeline. Gap in pool: jq census shows every /ideate mention is an engine-offer surface idea (T1-F1-2 etc.), zero propose back-porting this program's architecture. This is also the house engineering-journal norm (capture the mechanism in the same effort that proved it) applied at skill scale.
outcome_shape: PR upgrading plugins/saga/skills/ideate/SKILL.md + references/ with the staged architecture (grounding stage, basis contract fields, blind-hunter lane, gap-synthesis pass, cap-aware batching), citing this program's artifacts as the evidence run; CHANGELOG/version bump per release-surface rules; verified by a scaled-down invocation producing contract-conformant ideas.
